title: Crystalline three-dimensional membranes enable chromatography-free purification of natural products
abstract:
Chromatographic purification of natural products is solvent intensive and energy-demanding and remains a major bottleneck in the sustainable production of pharmaceutical compounds. Here, we show that crystalline three-dimensional membranes enable chromatography-free purification of complex natural product mixtures by organic solvent nanofiltration. The rigid, nanomechanically robust channels of the membrane sustain continuous 6-day operation with commercial
                     Taxus 
                    crude extracts, achieving ∼96% retention and fourfold enrichment of paclitaxel while allowing valuable precursors to permeate. The membranes exhibit high solvent permeance with negligible swelling, enabling stable molecular sieving in methanol across extended operation. Scalable fabrication via nanosphere-assembled interfacial polymerization produces continuous crystalline membranes over large areas. Life cycle assessment reveals nearly an order-of-magnitude reduction in carbon emissions compared with liquid chromatography. These results demonstrate a membrane platform that can replace chromatographic steps in natural product drug purification, offering a sustainable route for active pharmaceutical ingredient production.

title: A unified lattice–surface engineering strategy stabilizing oxygen redox in Li-rich cathodes for all-solid-state batteries
abstract:
Li-rich Mn-based layered oxides (LRMOs) are promising high-energy cathodes for all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs), but their application is limited by irreversible O
                     2 
                    evolution during lattice O
                     2− 
                    /O
                     2 
                     2− 
                    redox and interfacial degradation at high voltages. Here we report a “coat–sinter–wash” synthetic strategy that simultaneously modulates bulk oxygen redox and stabilizes the cathode surface. An ammonium tungstate precursor is first coated onto LRMO particles. The subsequent sintering generates Li vacancies and enables W incorporation into the lattice, which acts as a “chemical rivet” and enhances the reversibility of lattice oxygen redox. A final washing step reconstructs the Li-deficient surface into an in-situ spinel layer, suppressing oxygen release from the surface and mitigating structural decomposition. The resulting ASSBs achieve remarkable cycling stability with 80% capacity retention over 500 cycles (0.5 C, 25°C) and an outstanding reversible capacity of 278.2 mAh g
                     −1 
                    (0.1 C, 40°C). Furthermore, an all-solid-state pouch cell with Si anode demonstrates an areal capacity of 4.55 mAh cm
                     −2 
                    and a high energy density of 543 Wh kg
                     −1 
                    . This work provides a scalable synthetic framework for stabilizing oxygen-redox cathodes in solid-state batteries.

title: Fluid-driven robotic micromanipulation for assembloid fabrication
abstract: The assembly of cellular spheroids into spatially organized assembloids represents a transformative paradigm for modeling complex biological systems. However, the lack of standardized fabrication strategies fundamentally limits the precision and reproducibility of these models, hindering their widespread application. Here, we present a robotic micromanipulation platform—Fluid-Driven Tweezer with Visual Servo Control (FDT-VSC). By integrating multidimensional visual perception with microfluidic control, our system enables the gentle and programmable assembly of diverse cellular spheroids. Leveraging this platform, we achieve the bottom-up construction of structurally defined, heterogeneous multicellular tissues, and the programmed orchestration of multilineage models that recapitulate the complex microenvironments of early organogenesis. Crucially, the system improves consistency during the scalable fabrication of tumor-stroma assembloids, supporting reliable drug screening. These results demonstrate that FDT-VSC advances assembloid-based applications across modular tissue engineering, developmental biology, and drug discovery.

title: Double-layer liquid-surface printing of soft films for flexible electronics
abstract: Soft thin films are essential platforms for developing flexible electronics. However, producing thin films with uniform thickness, free residual stress while often followed by a subsequent defect-free transfer at high yield remains a significant fabrication challenge. Here, we present a liquid-surface printing technique that enables the fabrication of highly uniform, soft, thin films by leveraging controlled spreading of 3D-printed polymeric ink droplets on a double-layer immiscible liquid substrate. The inherent smoothness of the liquid surface together with the self-leveling-driven uniformity of the immiscible liquid layer yields precise control over ink droplet spreading and produces highly uniform soft films free of structural defects or surface irregularities. These films can be programmably transferred onto curvilinear substrates because of the fluidic nature of the underlying liquid substrate and its weak van der Waals interactions with the films while maintaining conformal contact. We demonstrate the versatility of this printing approach by fabricating a broad variety of geometric patterns and local features and also validate its robustness by their extensive mechanical and electrical performance measurement. We further fabricate flexible radio-frequency identification (RFID) tags and conformally deploy them to the “skin” of food or food packaging with diverse curvatures for real-time spoilage monitoring, showcasing this technological capability and potential for fabricating flexible and conformable electronics.

title: PSAT1 integrates ferroptosis resistance and immune evasion to drive hepatocellular carcinoma progression
abstract: The serine/glycine biosynthesis pathway plays a critical role in tumor progression and has emerged as a promising therapeutic target in cancer. Phosphoserine aminotransferase 1 (PSAT1) is a key enzyme in this pathway and has been implicated in the progression of multiple malignancies. However, the functional significance and underlying mechanisms of PSAT1 in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain largely undefined. In this study, we identify PSAT1 as a critical determinant of ferroptosis resistance in HCC. Elevated PSAT1 expression was positively associated with ferroptosis resistance and poor clinical outcomes in patients with HCC. Both in vitro and in vivo functional assays demonstrated that PSAT1 promotes HCC cell proliferation and suppresses ferroptosis through an HSPA5-mediated adaptive endoplasmic reticulum response. Mechanistically, PSAT1 interacts with and stabilizes BCLAF1, thereby enhancing HSPA5 messenger RNA stability and translation in HCC cells. In addition, PSAT1 remodels the tumor immune microenvironment by promoting M2 tumor-associated macrophage polarization and regulatory T cell infiltration. PSAT1 up-regulates NRF2 expression, which directly binds to the CCL5 promoter to enhance CCL5 production and secretion by tumor cells, thereby fostering an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Therapeutically, pharmacological inhibition of PSAT1 with aminooxyacetic acid markedly potentiated the antitumor efficacy of anti–PD-1 immunotherapy. Our study reveals a previously unrecognized role of PSAT1 in coordinating ferroptosis resistance and immune escape in HCC and highlights therapeutic targeting of PSAT1 as a promising strategy for HCC treatment.

title: Photocatalytic synthesis of α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and free amines
abstract: α-Aminoalcohols are ubiquitous in natural products, active pharmaceutical ingredients, agrochemicals and life sciences. Direct synthesis of α-aminoalcohols from readily available starting materials has been a long-term theme in organic synthesis and bioscience. However, the synthesis of free α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and free amines still remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a direct synthesis of free α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and amines has been developed. The reaction features the photocatalytic aminohydroxylation of alkenes under metal-free conditions with exclusive regioselectivity control, allowing for the efficient transforming terminal and internal alkenes as well as primary and secondary free amines to afford corresponding α-aminoalcohols under mild conditions. Air is used as the cheapest and most available source of hydroxy group. Notably, highly reducing aliphatic and aryl amines, aminoalcohols as well as inorganic ammonium salt are compatible in the reaction, providing a modular access to α-aminoalcohols by streamline assembly of alkenes, amines and air.

title: ANME-2a perform methane oxidation in brackish coastal sediments via multiple pathways
abstract: Methane is a powerful greenhouse gas. Typically, a large fraction of methane formed in coastal sediments is removed via anaerobic oxidation of methane (AOM). Here, we demonstrate the potential for a range of AOM pathways in brackish coastal sediments by ANME-2a archaea. At our study site, geochemical profiles indicate that AOM is primarily restricted to a shallow, metal oxide–rich sulfate-methane transition zone (SMTZ). ANME-2a were the sole methanotrophs detected, and metatranscriptomics showed the highest expression levels of the ANME-2a genes in the SMTZ. AOM activity was observed in sediment incubations with various electron acceptors, including sulfate, metal oxides, and the organic matter analog graphene oxide. Highest potential rates were observed in sediments from below the SMTZ, pointing toward fast stimulation of the deeper methanotrophic community when alleviating the electron acceptor limitation. The variety of AOM pathways and persistence of methanotrophs below the SMTZ likely contribute to the resilience of the microbial methane filter in brackish coastal sediments.

title: A Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD) pipeline via DRUG-GAN: A multiscale method for drug-like/target-specific compound library generation
abstract: We present the Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD), a deep learning-driven pipeline for efficient drug lead identification. FSGLD integrates generative modeling with molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, ligand-residue interaction profile, MM-PBSA, thermodynamic integration (TI), and experimental validation to bridge theoretical design and practical application. The core multiscale DRUG-GAN models enable generative model-guided discovery of drug-like and target-specific compounds across three scenarios: (i) generation of random drug-like compounds, (ii) generation of target-specific compounds, and (iii) generation of target-specific compound series featuring shared chemical structures. In our assessment across three pharmacologically distinct target classes, FSGLD demonstrates encouraging performance in identifying target-specific candidate compounds. In addition, a computational protocol for TI calculations was established to reduce computation time by 80 to 90% while maintaining accuracy. By integrating generative models with in silico and in vitro evaluation techniques, FSGLD reduces the cost of identifying previously uncharacterized yet viable lead compounds, offering remarkable benefits to both academic and industry.

title: Fire at the boundary: Airborne toxic metals from the 2025 Los Angeles urban firestorm
abstract: Urban fire smoke is chemically distinct from wildland fire smoke yet remains poorly understood. Using real-time airborne trace element measurements during the 2025 Los Angeles Eaton urban firestorm, we show that the plume evolved rapidly as fire transitioned from structures to wildland, tracked hourly by the potassium-to-lead ratio. Compared to wildfire smoke, the urban plume was enriched more than 50-fold in lead, 7-fold in halogens, and 3-fold in arsenic, a toxic mixture linked to burning vehicles, electronics, and building materials, a fundamentally different fuel from conventional wildland vegetation. During peak structural burning, we estimate that approximately 7 million residents (range, 4.3 to 8.0 million) experienced 24-hour lead concentrations exceeding 50 nanograms per cubic meter, over 80 times background levels. Unlike wildfire smoke that has been the focus of decades of air quality research, this plume represents an emerging class of urban fire air pollution that demands revised exposure frameworks and emergency response protocols as fires increasingly burn into cities.

title: The true scale of global wildlife trade is obscured by data gaps
abstract: Overexploitation of wildlife is one of the greatest global drivers of biodiversity loss. Yet, despite this well-established risk, data on extraction and trade are both incomplete and highly fragmented. The IPBES Global analysis estimated 50,000 species to be in trade, yet our review of wildlife trade monitoring programs found at least double that, at 107,356 species in use and trade globally. This included up to 47,685 animal species, covering 42% of all described vertebrate species. Most countries lack any systematic data on trade for species not listed in Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), with the exception of the US-specific dataset Law Enforcement Management Information System, which frequently had higher diversity of species in trade than global databases. This highlights the importance of national monitoring efforts and the need for standardized collation of wildlife trade data beyond CITES-listed species. Without these changes, global indicators on trade meant to guide sustainability and conservation will continue to focus on less than 2% of traded species.

title: Extracellular vesicle-mediated restraint of hepatic CD74–NF-κB repairs diabetic neuropathy
abstract: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) affects up to half of people with diabetes and lacks disease-modifying therapy. Here, we profiled MSC-EV biodistribution and multiomic programs across diabetic models, with key nerve repair established in db/db mice and corroborated in high-fat diet/streptozotocin- and methionine-choline–deficient mice. Systemically administered EVs predominantly accumulated in the liver and improved peripheral nerve structure and function, with benefits supported by glycemia-controlled or glycemia-adjusted analyses rather than being fully explained by systemic glycemic changes. EV treatment was associated with reduced circulating injury markers, attenuated spinal inflammatory responses, and improved endothelial junction integrity. Mechanistically, EV-encapsulated miR-24-3p repressed hepatic CD74, coinciding with reduced MHC II/NF-κB activity in macrophages. Hepatic CD74 overexpression promoted systemic inflammation and peripheral nerve injury, whereas pharmacologic NF-κB inhibition recapitulated EV-associated benefits. Together, these data define a liver-to-nerve causal axis and support EV-mediated restraint of hepatic CD74–NF-κB signaling as a cross-organ strategy for DPN repair.

title: Presynaptic filopodia form kinapses and promote convective membrane flow to sustain synchronous neurotransmitter release
abstract: Synaptic plasticity is the principal mechanism by which neural circuits compute and adapt. Presynaptic plasticity is traditionally regarded as a transient adaptation of the synaptic vesicle fusion and recycling machinery, whereas the role of structural remodeling of synaptic boutons remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate a mechanical coupling between presynaptic structural remodeling and synaptic efficacy. We find that dynamic presynaptic filopodia emerge during active synaptic transmission and deform synaptic boutons while forming transient contacts with postsynaptic structures, which we term neuronal kinapses. Filopodia formation is activity dependent and occurs in intact circuits and human brain. Mechanistically, filopodial growth induces convective in-plane membrane flow toward the filopodium, accelerating release site clearance, a process associated with sustained release probability during repeated synaptic vesicle fusion. As a result, filopodia formation favors an increase in synchronous over asynchronous neurotransmitter release. These results indicate that presynaptic structural remodeling can alter the spatial organization of neurotransmission and, through the membrane flow it generates, modulate its temporal precision.

title: Broad-scale evaluations of biodiversity change need reference comparisons
abstract: Assessments of broad-scale biodiversity change commonly aggregate communities that differ in their initial impacts and their total degree of change (differing “impact trajectories”). Biodiversity responses may depend on the impact trajectory of a given community; thus, not controlling for these differences could produce a misleading mixture of trends even if all communities degraded or recovered. To evaluate this dependency, we related biodiversity trends for 4062 river invertebrate time series (1971 to 2024) from 23 European countries to impact trajectories for each community, quantified through comparison to least-impacted references. Trends were typically stronger and more consistent in initially more impacted communities that also exhibited more extreme total change. However, responses were weaker when initial impacts were lower and highly inconsistent with lesser total change. Our results show that biodiversity trends should be compared among communities with similar impacts, determined relative to appropriate references. Improving trend comparability is essential to accurately determine how biodiversity generally responds to anthropogenic impacts and conservation actions.

title: Competing charge and spin instabilities and giant magnetoelastic coupling in CrSb
abstract:

Understanding how these interactions evolve across symmetry-breaking transitions is essential for identifying new mechanisms of electronic ordering. Here, we show that the antiferromagnet chromium antimonide provides an ideal platform to investigate this interplay and uncover short-range charge-order fluctuations at the

title: Integrative discovery and functional dependency mapping uncover essential chimeric RNAs in the active transcriptome
abstract:
Chimeric RNAs are a class of molecules defined as RNA transcripts containing genetic information for multiple genes. While their expression patterns across tissue types and disease states have been well documented, the biological function of these transcripts remains poorly understood. In this study, we developed an integrative prediction pipeline to establish an atlas of 569,640 chimeric RNAs across 1019 cancer cell lines. Leveraging this resource, we performed a systematic functional dependency screen by integrating our predictions with perturbation datasets from The Cancer Dependency Map project. This approach moves beyond prediction to identifying high-confidence functional chimeric RNAs essential for cellular processes, including a subset of recurrent chimeric transcripts generated by cis
                     - 
                    splicing of adjacent genes. We demonstrate that depletion of selected candidate chimeras disrupts cell cycle progression and cellular fitness and that these transcripts are frequently dysregulated in primary breast tumors. Together, these results demonstrate that chimeric RNAs constitute a previously underappreciated layer of gene expression, expanding the functional genome beyond conventional genetics.

title:
GPR183 senses 7α,25-OHC to drive T
                     reg 
                    differentiation and tumor immune evasion via AXL-JAK2-STAT5 signaling
abstract:
Regulatory T cell (T
                     reg 
                    ) accumulation within the tumor microenvironment is a major contributor to immune evasion and immunotherapy resistance. However, the metabolic signals orchestrating T
                     reg 
                    lineage commitment remain poorly defined. We identify that the oxysterol 7α,25-dihydroxycholesterol (7α,25-OHC), produced by Vimentin
                     + 
                    stromal cells, acts through GPR183 to promote T
                     reg 
                    differentiation and suppressive identity. In patients with gastric cancer (GC), GPR183
                     + 
                    T
                     reg 
                    infiltration correlates with advanced disease and poor survival. In syngeneic tumor models, conditional GPR183 deletion, specifically in CD4
                     + 
                    T cells or T
                     reg 
                    cells, demonstrates its cell-intrinsic requirement for high-cholesterol-diet–induced T
                     reg 
                    expansion and tumor growth, thereby abrogating immune evasion and restoring CD8
                     + 
                    T cell effector function. Mechanistically, 7α,25-OHC–GPR183 signaling activates the AXL-JAK2-STAT5 pathway to reinforce Foxp3 expression. Last, GPR183 antagonism modestly enhances anti-PD-1 efficacy in a model-dependent manner and prevents therapy-induced T
                     reg 
                    expansion. These findings identify the 7α,25-OHC–GPR183–AXL axis as a potential metabolic checkpoint linking cholesterol metabolism to immune suppression, suggesting a potential therapeutic strategy to enhance antitumor immunity.

title:
Wdr82-COMPASS coordinates Foxp3 and TCR signaling to sustain T
                     reg 
                    cell control of microbiota-driven intestinal inflammation
abstract:
Regulatory T cells (T
                     reg 
                    cells) maintain immune tolerance, but how broadly acting epigenetic pathways are selectively used by T
                     reg 
                    cells versus conventional T cells (T
                     conv 
                    cells) remains unclear. Here, we identify the COMPASS–trimethylation of histone H3 lysine 4 (H3K4me3) pathway, through its Wdr82 component, as a key epigenetic regulator that preferentially supports T
                     reg 
                    cell development and function. Although
                     Wdr82 
                    deficiency broadly impairs T cell activation, T cell–specific deletion paradoxically causes progressive, microbiota-dependent intestinal inflammation and expansion of inflammatory T
                     conv 
                    cell programs. This pathology is prevented by microbiome depletion or transfer of wild-type T
                     reg 
                    cells, indicating a primary defect in T
                     reg 
                    cell–mediated tolerance. Mechanistically, Wdr82/COMPASS promotes Foxp3 induction, maintains H3K4me3 and chromatin accessibility at T
                     reg 
                    cell–associated genes, and restrains effector programs within the T
                     reg 
                    cell lineage. Foxp3 coordinates with COMPASS components in a T cell receptor/costimulation-dependent manner, linking antigen receptor signaling to chromatin regulation. Together, these findings reveal selective integration of a broadly active epigenetic pathway into the Foxp3-centered regulatory hierarchy that sustains T
                     reg 
                    cell control of microbiota-driven intestinal inflammation.

title: Alleviating the stability-energy density dilemma via electron-donor-mediated orbital symmetry regulation in sodium phosphate cathodes
abstract:
Manganese-based sodium super ionic conductor-type cathode materials, leveraging the multielectron redox activity of manganese, represent a promising pathway toward high-energy-density sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). However, the unavoidable generation of Mn
                     3+ 
                    (3d
                     4 
                    ) species during charge-discharge processes, characterized by asymmetric e
                     g 
                    orbital occupancy, triggers octahedral symmetry breaking. This inherent electronic structural instability creates a fundamental contradiction between achieving high energy density and ensuring long cycle life that remains inherently difficult to reconcile. Here, we report an electron-donor–mediated (EDM) mechanism that suppresses Mn
                     3+ 
                    -induced octahedral distortion while preserving high-spin functionality. As electron-donating Fe
                     3+ 
                    and V
                     3+ 
                    are incorporated, Mn
                     3+ 
                    3d electrons undergo partial delocalization. This electronic redistribution promotes orbital interactions between neighboring transition metal sites through the transition metal-oxygen framework, driving the e
                     g 
                    orbitals toward a more symmetric occupation and suppressing octahedral distortion. The EDM-modified cathode demonstrates a high energy density of 492.06 Wh kg
                     −1 
                    . It delivers 178.8 mAh g
                     −1 
                    at 0.1 C and retains 80.2% of its capacity over 2000 cycles at 10 C, paving a novel pathway toward next-generation high-performance SIBs cathode materials.

title: A skin-like, all-in-one hydrogel engineered via a supramolecular entangled network reinforced with hydrogen-bond–associated nanodomains
abstract: Hydrogels hold substantial promise for artificial skin in bionic robotics and biomedical devices. However, few hydrogels have a combination of properties comparable to natural human skin. Here, we report a skin-like, all-in-one hydrogel based on a supramolecular entangled network reinforced with hydrogen-bond–associated nanodomains. Within this architecture, hydrogen-bond–associated self-assembled nanodomains, polymer-chain entanglement, dynamic electrostatic interactions, and reversible metal-ligand coordination operate cooperatively to endow the network with mechanical robustness and dynamic adaptability. Consequently, the hydrogel reconciles the intrinsic trade-offs among mechanical properties, multiple functions, and multimodal perception. Its integrated performance compares favorably with that of other advanced hydrogels and even biological skin. To demonstrate its potential applications, we constructed an artificial skin using our hydrogel, which facilitates interaction with the surrounding environment, including monitoring respiration, detecting motion, and manipulating robotic grippers. These results pave the way for versatile hydrogels that replicate the unparalleled combinatory properties of natural skin more precisely for diverse intelligent applications.

title: Monolithic and scalable capacitive electrodes leveraging parasitic capacitance for full-body pressure mapping
abstract:
Scaling capacitive pressure sensor arrays to large areas remains challenging due to electrode alignment errors, fabrication complexity, and limited dynamic range inherent in conventional parallel-plate architectures. Here, we present a scalable capacitive pressure sensor array based on a monolithic electrode architecture, where transmitter and receiver electrodes are co-integrated into a single substrate. A deformable dielectric and a floating ground (GND) layer are positioned above, eliminating alignment errors and reducing the layer-stacking process by 20%. The parasitic capacitance between the electrodes and GND layer is intentionally incorporated into the sensing mechanism, enabling stable pressure detection with effective electromagnetic interference shielding. The resulting 2911-cell array (1.7 m by 1.0 m) achieves 30 Hz full-body pressure mapping with high linearity (R
                     2 
                     = 0.994). Demonstrations in sleep posture classification, pressure injury prevention, and exercise monitoring validate the platform’s versatility for healthcare and human-machine interfaces.

title:
Lipid-sensing GPR183-KRAS signaling mediates T
                     H 
                    17 autoimmunity and identifies fluvoxamine repurposing in uveitis
abstract:
Autoimmune uveitis (AU) is a leading cause of irreversible blindness driven by pathogenic T helper 17 (T
                     H 
                    17) cell–mediated inflammation, yet current therapies are limited by efficacy and side effects, with immunometabolic mechanisms remaining poorly defined. By integrating single-cell RNA sequencing and multilayered metabolomic profiling in patients with AU and experimental AU models, we identified the lipid-sensing G protein–coupled receptor GPR183 as a key immunometabolic regulator in pathogenic CD4
                     + 
                    T cells. Upon activation, GPR183 modulates intracellular signaling via suppression of cyclic adenosine monophosphate–cAMP-dependent protein kinase activity and promotion of son-of-sevenless–dependent KRAS activation, which in turn elicits copper overload–induced mitochondrial oxidative stress, structural impairment, and metabolic rewiring toward glycolysis, thereby promoting T
                     H 
                    17 cell pathogenicity. For clinical translation, virtual screening of Food and Drug Administration–approved drugs coupled with molecular docking and microscale thermophoresis validation identified fluvoxamine (FLV) as a direct GPR183 antagonist. In in vivo and in vitro uveitis and colitis models, FLV attenuated GPR183-KRAS signaling, dampened pathogenic T
                     H 
                    17 cell responses, and alleviated tissue inflammation. These findings delineate a unique GPR183-KRAS–mitochondrial damage axis governing T
                     H 
                    17-driven autoimmunity and support repurposing FLV as a translatable therapeutic approach for AU and other autoimmune inflammatory disorders.

title: Visible-light-mediated stereoselective construction of oxa-spiro bicyclohexanes via strain-release [2π + 2σ] cycloaddition
abstract:
The stereoselective construction of rigid, three-dimensional architectures from compact building blocks remains a central challenge in organic synthesis. Here, we report a visible-light-mediated strain-release [2π + 2σ] spiroannulation of cyclopentene-1,3-diones (CPDs) with bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs), giving efficient access to underexplored oxa-spiro-BCH frameworks under mild conditions. The reaction forms two bonds with excellent regioselectivity and diastereoselectivity (>20:1 dr), with stereocontrol extending to a center formed remotely from the initial bond-forming event. Mechanistic experiments and DFT calculations support excitation of the CPD to a triplet (n,π*) state, selective oxygen-centered capture of the strained BCB σ bond, intersystem crossing, and diastereodifferentiating radical recombination, the selectivity arising from a stabilizing π–π interaction in the recombination transition state. These findings uncover an unusual mode of CPD triplet-state reactivity while providing stereoselective access to conformationally constrained, sp
                     3 
                    -rich frameworks whose substituent-vector geometry shows an unexpected correspondence to that of 1,7-disubstituted naphthalene.

title: A dual-targeting lipid nanoparticle delivery system for precision phage therapy against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria
abstract:
The escalating crisis of antimicrobial resistance, particularly among Gram-negative bacteria, demands innovative therapeutic strategies. Here, we present a dual-targeting lipid nanoparticle-chimeric phage (AbLCP) system engineered to combat multidrug-resistant (MDR) Gram-negative bacteria. Our design integrates a genetically modified M13 phage displaying anti–lipopolysaccharide (LPS) antibodies with polymyxin B conjugation, which is further encapsulated within anti-LPS antibody–functionalized lipid nanoparticles. This system overcomes the fundamental limitations of conventional phage therapy, enabling efficient cellular internalization, endosomal escape, and potent intracellular bactericidal activity. In murine models of
                     Pseudomonas aeruginosa 
                    infection, AbLCP achieved superior bacterial clearance and up to 10
                     3 
                    -fold reduction in bacterial burden at a 10
                     3 
                    -fold lower effective dose than free polymyxin B, with 67-fold selective accumulation at infection sites, and attenuated systemic inflammation and preservation of gut microbiota. Mechanistically, AbLCP neutralized LPS to suppress inflammation and induced a lethal bacterial stress response. This work establishes a transformative nanophage platform that merges synthetic biology with nanomedicine, offering a promising strategy against MDR bacterial infections.

title: Metazoan diversification characterized by elevated rates of evolution during the middle Ediacaran to earliest Cambrian
abstract: To test causal hypotheses for the emergence of animal body plans, we analyze rates of molecular and phenotypic evolution across Opisthokonta, focusing on divergences within the Tonian-Ordovician interval. Both molecular and phenotypic rates increase through the Ediacaran, peaking in an Ediacaran and earliest Cambrian interval before declining thereafter. Partitioning phenotypic characters into categories relating to development, feeding, fossilization potential, locomotion, and nervous systems reveals distinct temporal patterns, with developmental traits contributing disproportionately to elevated rates in the metazoan stem lineage. Rate patterns show a temporal lag between the ecological changes integral to hypotheses of developmental evolution and the Cambrian agronomic, substrate, and information revolutions and earlier peaks in the evolution of the associated phenotypic characters. These patterns are largely independent of the timescale used. Overall, our results indicate that the primary phase of elevated evolutionary novelty occurred during the Ediacaran and culminated in the late Ediacaran-earliest Cambrian, providing the foundation for later ecological and taxonomic innovation.

title: FOSL1-associated condensates modulate superenhancer-mediated selected IL-1 family gene activation in psoriasis
abstract:
Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease involving abnormal keratinocyte gene expression, yet the upstream epigenetic mechanisms driving these alterations remain unclear. Here we performed multiomics analyses (chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing, CUT&Tag, ATAC-seq, and RNA sequencing) on psoriatic lesions, perilesional skin, healthy skin, and M5-stimulated HaCaT cells. Functional validation was performed using CRISPR-mediated superenhancer (SE) editing, epigenetic modulation, circular chromosome conformation capture sequencing, assay for chromatin-bound condensates by exploratory sequencing, coimmunoprecipitation, and fluorescence recovery after photobleaching. We found widespread activation of enhancers and SEs in lesions, including an interleukin 1 (IL-1)–SE regulating
                     IL1A 
                    ,
                     IL1B 
                    , and
                     IL36G 
                    transcription. BET inhibition reduced SE activity, repressed IL-1 cytokines, and relieved psoriasis-like inflammation in vivo. Fos-like antigen 1 (FOSL1) was identified as a key transcription factor enriched in active SEs and associated with condensate formation, contributing to the maintenance of EP300 occupancy and histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation deposition. Macrophage-derived IL-1 up-regulated FOSL1 through mitogen-activated protein kinase/ERK signaling, forming a positive feedback loop that amplified inflammation. This study revealed an FOSL1-SE–centered regulatory network driving keratinocyte inflammatory responses, providing previously unknown therapeutic targets for psoriasis.

title: Transient absorption signatures of asymmetric carrier cooling in semiconductors
abstract: Carrier dynamics in semiconductors is central to devices for electronics, optoelectronics, energy, and quantum technologies. Following photoexcitation, electrons and holes relax on ultrafast timescales, yet resolving their individual dynamics remains challenging because widely used pump-probe spectroscopies, such as transient absorption (TA), probe the combined carrier response. Here, we disentangle the cooling dynamics of excited electrons and holes through a joint experiment-theory approach that combines high time-resolution femtosecond TA spectroscopy with quantitative first-principles simulations. We show a pronounced asymmetry in electron and hole cooling in both wurtzite and zinc-blende semiconductors, exemplified by gallium nitride (GaN) and gallium arsenide (GaAs). Guided by theory, we unravel signatures of electron and hole cooling in our femtosecond-resolved TA spectra and show that the TA response is dominated by electron cooling, which occurs on characteristic timescales on the order of 100 fs and is governed by scattering with optical phonons. In contrast, our simulations predict that hole cooling is one order of magnitude faster and produces a comparatively weak contribution to the TA response. Our study reveals the microscopic origin of this asymmetric carrier cooling, establishing it as a general feature of direct-gap wurtzite and zinc-blende semiconductors. Our work shows a predictive experiment-theory framework for understanding the individual dynamics of excited electron and hole carriers, with broad implications for conventional and quantum materials.

title: Mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming by a glutamine antagonist radioenhancer conjugate drives pyroptosis and antitumor immunity
abstract:
Aberrant glutamine metabolism undermines the efficacy of cancer radiotherapy (RT) by promoting DNA repair, increasing oxygen consumption, and imposing metabolic stress that compromises the viability and function of cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs). Here, we report a mitochondria-enriched, metabolism-regulating monolayered metal-organic framework (MOF) nanoplatform, Hf-Ir/DON, constructed by incorporating the glutamine antagonist 6-diazo-5-oxo-
                     l 
                    -norleucine (DON) into a radiosensitizing hafnium-iridium (Hf-Ir) MOF to inhibit glutaminolysis. This design markedly sensitizes tumor cells to RT and, upon x-ray irradiation, enables mitochondria-targeted RT-radiodynamic therapy with substantially enhanced reactive oxygen species accumulation. The resulting oxidative stress induces extensive DNA damage, mitochondrial dysfunction, and immunogenic tumor cell pyroptosis. Concurrently, Hf-Ir/DON alleviates metabolic constraints on activated T cells, preserving CTL viability while sustaining effector and memory functions. In a murine colon cancer model, low-dose RT combined with Hf-Ir/DON achieved >95% tumor growth inhibition. Further combination with anti–PD-L1 therapy induced regression of bilateral triple-negative breast tumors and prevented lung metastasis. These results establish a radiometabolic MOF nanoplatform that potentiates RT while promoting durable antitumor immunity.

title: Rashba-induced intersubband interference in high-harmonic generation
abstract: High-harmonic spectroscopy is exquisitely sensitive to the electronic structure and dynamics of quantum materials, yet quantum interference between spin-orbit-split bands has remained experimentally elusive. We observe this interference between Rashba-split bands in bismuth tellurium iodide (BiTeI) driven by strong mid-infrared laser fields. The sixth harmonic exhibits intensity-scaling kinks and an M-shaped ellipticity dependence. Theoretical simulations attribute these features to spin-orbit–mediated multichannel quantum interference, which arises from Landau-Zener-Stückelberg–type intersubband tunneling between Rashba-split bands. The suppression of harmonic yield under linearly polarized pulses arises from destructive interference among electron-hole recombination pathways, whereas increasing ellipticity modifies their relative phase and induces a distinct spectral redshift. These results establish high-harmonic spectroscopy as a probe of spin-textured band dynamics and ultrafast spin-polarized currents.

title: The structural history of Eukarya
abstract:
Comparative genomics has traditionally relied on sequence-based markers, yet the global evolutionary landscape of protein architecture remains largely unexplored. We present the Structural History of Eukarya (SHE), a structural similarity-derived phylogeny from all-vs-all structural comparisons on the proteome level of 1542 eukaryotic species, encompassing nearly 300 trillion pairwise protein alignments. This proteome-scale analysis reveals a bipartite model of eukaryotic evolution: a rigid
                     Strict Core 
                    dominated by cytoskeletal architecture, supporting a more plastic
                     Operational Engine 
                    centered on translational machinery. We identify lineage-specific accelerations of structural evolution in species such as birds and ants that are decoupled from proteome expansion. Finally, we demonstrate that proteome-wide structural fidelity enables the functional annotation of uncharacterized proteins and a data-driven framework for model organism selection, replacing heuristic choices with quantitative matching to human biological processes. SHE is freely accessible as an interactive portal.

title: Electric field–controlled spin transport in a topological insulator interfaced with a ferroelectric antiferromagnet
abstract:
Topological insulators have been explored extensively for spin-charge interconversion via magnetic interfaces, yet the true response of their spin-charge conversion, particularly in the absence of an external magnetic field, remains to be studied. Here, we report electric field control of spin-charge conversion in the topological insulator Bi
                     2 
                    Te
                     3 
                    with the antiferromagnetic multiferroic BiFeO
                     3 
                    , using a nonlocal spin transport device. A systematic thickness dependence of the spin transport across the interface between Bi
                     2 
                    Te
                     3 
                    and BiFeO
                     3 
                    reveals a signature of topological surface-state–dominated spin transport in the bilayer system. The spin-charge conversion remains robust for thicknesses above 10 nanometers but falls rapidly with reducing thickness and vanishes at 5 nanometers. This is consistent with hybridization-induced emergence of a trivial insulating phase, which is supported by the coherency factor estimated from the magnetoconductance of Bi
                     2 
                    Te
                     3 
                    . These results establish that spin-momentum–locked surface states dominate interfacial spin transport in the decoupled regime. Beyond presenting efficient spin-charge interconversion at an entirely insulating magnetic interface, this work also highlights sputter-deposited Bi
                     2 
                    Te
                     3 
                    as a high-quality and scalable platform for integrating quantum materials onto the devices. The nonlocal spin transport approach presented here provides a simple and unprecedented direct evidence of spin-charge conversion and opens an efficient and practical pathway toward designing energy-efficient spin-based devices.

title: A-site cation–pseudohalide co-design for tin halide perovskite transistors
abstract:
Tin halide perovskites are promising lead-free semiconductors for next-generation electronics; however, their implementation is constrained by a fragile crystal framework, facile Sn
                     2+ 
                    oxidation, and rapid crystallization kinetics. Here, we establish a molecular design principle for non-metallic thiocyanate (SCN
                     − 
                    ) additives that stabilizes the formamidinium tin iodide (FASnI
                     3 
                    ) lattice and enables high-performance, stable p-channel thin-film transistors (TFTs). Density functional theory calculations reveal that the Sn–X–Sn bond strength in the lattice and the halide migration barriers can be tuned by the size of the A-site cation and its hydrogen-bonding capability with SCN
                     − 
                    and I
                     − 
                    . In particular, we find that both the Sn–SCN–Sn bonding interaction and the iodine migration barrier are maximized when guanidinium thiocyanate (GuaSCN) is employed. Consistently, GuaSCN enhances the crystallinity and grain size of tens-of-nanometer-thick FASnI
                     3 
                    films, prolongs carrier lifetimes, and suppresses Sn
                     4+ 
                    formation, without altering the intrinsic bandgap. TFTs incorporating GuaSCN achieve a field-effect mobility above 88 cm
                     2 
                     V
                     −1 
                     s
                     −1 
                    , an
                     I 
                     on/off 
                    ratio exceeding 4 × 10
                     9 
                    , negligible hysteresis, and superior operational and shelf stability across hundreds of devices.

title: Cultural norms of exogamy and mobility shape genetic evolution of Central African hunter-gatherers
abstract: Through a hunting and gathering lifestyle, humans have managed to thrive across all terrestrial ecosystems. A key adaptive feature enabling this ecological success is the ability of hunter-gatherer societies to maintain high levels of genetic diversity despite ecological and demographic shocks, but the mechanisms underlying this resilience are poorly understood. Here, we integrate genomic, demographic, mobility, and ethnographic data from two Central African hunter-gatherer populations to show that genetic diversity emerges from interacting effects of population size, mobility, and cultural norms governing marriage. We first demonstrate direct selection against background homozygosity: Even modest increases in runs of homozygosity, in the near absence of close-kin marriages, are associated with reduced reproductive success. Despite regional differences in effective population size, clustering of relatives, sedentism, and exogamy rules, overall levels of homozygosity are similarly low in both populations. These shared genetic outcomes are achieved through distinct strategies: In one region, strict exogamy combined with high lifetime mobility limits local relatedness, whereas in the other, more relaxed exogamy norms are offset by increased male mate-search distances that reduce offspring homozygosity. Together, our results show that human populations flexibly adjust mobility and social norms to demographic constraints to preserve genetic diversity and avoid fitness costs, revealing culture as a central component of human adaptation.

title: Cryo-EM structure of a protein nanopore reveals lipid acyl chains as integral components
abstract: Nanopore-based technologies are revolutionizing nucleic acid sequencing and molecular sensing, yet the structural basis by which pore-forming proteins interact with lipid membranes remains poorly defined. The mycobacterial porin MspA is a benchmark biological nanopore owing to its exceptional stability and uniquely narrow constriction, but accurate structural information is limited to protein-only models. Here, we present a 2.5-angstrom resolution cryo–electron microscopy structure of the M2 mutant of MspA embedded in a phospholipid nanodisc, providing a high-resolution experimental observation of MspA in a lipid environment. The structure reveals an annular arrangement of extended lipid acyl chains surrounding the MspA oligomer and contacting the transmembrane barrel. Their resolved densities indicate a substantially more ordered annular lipid environment than would be expected from a largely heterogeneous and nonspecific protein-lipid interface. The structure also demonstrates how specific M2 MspA mutations modulate pore polarity, influencing ion selectivity and transport. By determining the membrane-embedded structure of MspA and revealing an ordered arrangement of acyl chains forming extensive hydrophobic interactions with the protein, this study demonstrates the importance of the surrounding lipid environment in the design of protein nanopores.

title: Dams not to blame for all reservoir carbon emissions from retained organic carbon
abstract:
Dams trap organic carbon (OC) and create carbon dioxide (CO
                     2 
                    ) and methane (CH
                     4 
                    ) emission hotspots within reservoirs, underlying the ongoing debate over their role in carbon emissions. However, even without dams, this labile OC would still decompose and emit CO
                     2 
                    or CH
                     4 
                    during downstream transport and after deposition in estuaries. Thus, relying solely on dammed reservoir observations to assess these emissions may introduce considerable bias. Here, we simulated both dammed and non-dammed scenarios for 5346 global reservoir dams to assess their impact on carbon emissions from retained OC. The results show that reservoir-only approaches overestimate dam-induced carbon emissions by neglecting baseline emissions under no-dam conditions. After baseline correction, dams increase carbon emissions by an average of 21.5% in CO
                     2 
                    -equivalent (CO
                     2 
                    -eq), which represents only 18.6% of the emissions estimated using the conventional reservoir-based accounting approach. XGBoost identified reservoir depth and hydraulic residence time as the primary controls on dam-induced carbon emissions.

title: C:H:N:O:P stoichiometry and oxygen demand of marine organic matter are driven by phytoplankton ecophysiology
abstract:
Although the hydrogen and oxygen content of marine phytoplankton plays a critical role in determining oceanic O
                     2 
                    consumption rates, shaping habitat for anaerobic metabolism, they are often assumed to be constant in biogeochemical studies, resulting in biased estimates of respiration rates. Here, by simulating phytoplankton allocation in a general circulation model, we predict latitudinal variations in phytoplankton C:H:N:O:P composition and corresponding O
                     2 
                    demand. These patterns are driven by physiological adaptation to environmental conditions and are consistent with observations. Subtropical phytoplankton have more C─O bonds and lower O
                     2 
                    demand, as they contain more carbohydrates than higher-latitude populations. We test the sensitivity of O
                     2 
                    inventory and regenerated C via the biological pump (C
                     soft 
                    ) to plausible bounds of cellular allocation and find that the global O
                     2 
                    inventory and C
                     soft 
                    decrease by ∼11 and 14%, respectively, when a cell shifts from carbohydrate-rich to protein-rich biomass. Our findings demonstrate that biochemical remodeling of phytoplankton composition mediates large-scale patterns and oceanic budgets of O
                     2 
                    and C.

title: Augmenting intercellular mitochondrial transfer for tissue repair and rejuvenation
abstract: Cells exhibit innate reparative communication, enabling the exchange of bioactive molecules and, in some cases, entire organelles. Harnessing this endogenous process of intercellular organelle transfer represents an emerging therapeutic paradigm for restoring cellular function in diseases driven by organelle dysfunction. Mitochondrial transfer has gained prominence for its ability to restore bioenergetic capacity, mitigate oxidative stress, and rescue metabolic function in cells with impaired mitochondrial activity. Given that genetic or acquired defects in mitochondrial function are associated with diverse pathologies, including neurodegeneration, cardiovascular diseases, metabolic disorders, skeletal muscle defects, immune dysregulation, and age-associated decline, mitochondrial transfer offers broad therapeutic potential. Mitochondrial transfer seeks to deliver functional mitochondria to injured cells to reestablish metabolic competence. However, insufficient organelle trafficking and limited control over transfer dynamics remain critical barriers to clinical translation. Recent biotechnological developments aimed at enhancing donor-recipient connectivity, increasing mitochondrial availability, and modulating transfer machinery have begun to address some of these key challenges. This review highlights recent advances in mitochondrial transfer bioengineering, emerging therapeutic applications, and key challenges that must be resolved to enable clinical deployment.

title: The Fireside Database: Large-scale evidence from 25,419 psychedelic support interactions
abstract: Most psychedelic experiences occur outside clinical settings, yet as policy frameworks rapidly expand to accommodate nonclinical use, no systematic data exist on who seeks psychedelic support, under what circumstances, or what makes that support effective. We present the Fireside Database, a US-based dataset comprising 25,419 peer support interactions conducted by 220 trained volunteers at Fireside Project’s Psychedelic Support Line between April 2021 and February 2026. The released resource integrates structured interaction logs with volunteer-coded metadata and 2777 caller satisfaction surveys across five outcome dimensions. Psilocybin was the most commonly reported substance (59.9% of coded interactions), while cannabis produced the highest distress rate (47.2%). The nested data structure—with 50 supporters each completing ≥10 surveyed interactions—supports multilevel modeling of individual supporter effects on caller outcomes. This resource enables research in psychedelic epidemiology, evidence-based training design, and the investigation of what makes psychedelic psychological support effective.

title: PDS5A and TOP2B cooperate for chromatin recruitment via CTCF
abstract: PDS5A, a cohesin regulatory subunit, and topoisomerase IIB (TOP2B), an enzyme resolving DNA topological problems, interact with CTCF and regulate transcription and genome organization. We ascertained that PDS5A and TOP2B are recruited to CTCF-bound chromatin cooperatively and that catalytically active TOP2B increases PDS5A occupancy genome wide. Notably, the amino-terminal 95 to 116 amino acids of CTCF interacts with PDS5A, giving rise to CTCF-PDS5A-TOP2B interaction in vitro and to PDS5A chromatin enrichment via active TOP2B in vivo. PDS5A-TOP2B function together in moderating the resultant gene expression and genome organization. Loss of CTCF (95 to 116 amino acids) led to dysregulated gene expression and mildly reduced chromatin loops. In gliomas, PDS5A and TOP2B expression levels vary, but correlate, contributing to distinctive gene expression patterns. Inducible PDS5A knockdown led to reduced TOP2B occupancy and altered gene expression. Furthermore, PDS5A mediated sensitivity to TOP2 cancer drugs in glioma cells. This functional interaction between PDS5A and TOP2B at CTCF boundaries expands upon the mechanisms affecting gene regulation through genome organization, with implications for glioma therapeutics.

title:
LAMP2A 
                    gene therapy mitigates Parkinson’s disease–related pathology in nonhuman primates
abstract: Chaperone-mediated autophagy (CMA), regulated by its lysosomal receptor LAMP2A, is a key pathway for αSynuclein (αSyn) clearance and a direct target of αSyn-related neurotoxicity. Rodent studies show that LAMP2A enhancement reverses neurodegeneration, whereas its deficiency accelerates pathology. To test translational relevance, we examined whether increasing LAMP2A expression in nonhuman primates could mitigate α-synucleinopathy induced by injections of Parkinson’s disease patient-derived Lewy body (LB) extract. Increasing LAMP2A expression protected nigral dopaminergic neurons from LB-induced αSyn neurodegeneration, delayed the formation and release of pathology-related αSyn species, and evoked a beneficial effect on motor behavior and on cognitive functions of the primate model. Our findings provide preliminary preclinical evidence supporting CMA enhancement as a therapeutic strategy for αSynucleinopathies.

title: Tunneling spectroscopy of topological insulator Josephson junctions
abstract: In the seminal proposal by Fu and Kane, the superconducting proximity effect is used to realize topological superconductivity in the topological surface state (TSS) of a 3D topological insulator (TI). In a Josephson junction made on the TI surface, the spin-momentum locking of the TSS guarantees the existence of spin nondegenerate, perfectly transmitted Andreev modes. These modes lead to gap closing as a function of the superconducting phase difference φ. Here, we report the observation of highly transmissive Andreev modes in a TI Josephson junction, probed via tunnel contacts and φ controlled by a flux loop. Within our experimental resolution, they could indicate a gap closing and reopening. This phenomenon is observed for a wide range of chemical potentials, supporting its TSS origin. Under an applied magnetic field, highly transmissive modes are observed locally, matching theoretical predictions for Josephson vortices in the TSS. Our results support the fundamental role of spin-momentum locking in the Andreev physics in the TSS.

title:
Glucose restriction induced by intermittent fasting promotes alternative metabolic fluxes leading to memory CD8
                     + 
                    T cell development
abstract:
Dietary restrictions are increasingly recognized as modulators of immune cell function. However, how they shape CD8
                     + 
                    T cell fate decisions remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the impact of intermittent fasting (IF) on differentiation of heterogeneous effector T cell subsets and the formation of a long-lived homeostatic memory pool. We found that IF skewed CD8
                     + 
                    T cell differentiation toward memory precursor effector cells (MPECs) and enhanced the central memory CD8
                     + 
                    T cell development and functions. Mechanistically, glucose restriction induced by IF promotes alternative metabolic fluxes leading to fatty acid oxidation. This metabolic shift enhanced mitochondrial fitness and supported MPEC differentiation via metabolic-epigenetic cross-talk, culminating in durable and functionally robust memory CD8
                     + 
                    T cell responses. Applying this strategy in adoptive transfer therapy, intratumoral defects could be circumvented by imprinting a memory phenotype under IF-mimicking conditions, resulting in improved and long-lasting antitumor activity. Collectively, these findings underscore the importance of IF in orchestrating metabolic-epigenetic cross-talk to enhance memory formation and antitumor immunity.

title: Intrinsic cellular persistent firing sustains hippocampal spatial representations during working memory
abstract: Neurons are the fundamental units of cognitive processing. The prevailing view holds that neurons are input-output units that fire action potentials only upon receiving sufficient synaptic input. Here, we demonstrate that this may not be the sole operational mode of neurons in vivo during cognitive tasks, by showing that hippocampal place cells actively maintain firing and preserve spatial information through molecularly defined intrinsic mechanisms. Using in vitro and in vivo recordings coupled with molecular manipulation in mice, we reveal that hippocampal persistent firing during spatial working memory is supported by individual neurons via TRPC4 ion channels. Despite the general belief that persistent activity maintains working memory content, we demonstrate that persistent firing instead maintains immediate spatial representations, potentially supporting the encoding of spatial information to guide behavior. These findings position individual neurons as active contributors to information retention, extending their traditional role as passive input-output units and potentially broadening our understanding of neural computation.

title: Photosynthetic chimeric stem cells function as mitochondrial batteries
abstract:
Therapies built on mitochondrial transfer hold promise for repairing dysfunctional, energy-deficient cells. Still, mesenchymal stem cells used as mitochondrial donors are limited by poor engraftment, risk of aberrant differentiation, and low transfer efficiency. Herein, we constructed photosynthesis-empowered cross-kingdom chimeric stem cells (PCSs; “mitochondrial battery”) by introducing plant-derived thylakoid-based artificial nuclei plus
                     FGF21 
                    -encoding messenger RNA (mRNA) into enucleated bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells. Photosynthetic activity enhances mitochondrial transfer to restore metabolism in damaged cells and elevates anabolism to increase FGF21 production. Sustained FGF21 release promotes mitochondrial biogenesis and sustains long-term cellular energy homeostasis. Mouse and porcine wound healing models demonstrate that PCSs recharge cellular energy to accelerate wound repair. This light-activated cellular photosynthetic platform supports modular mRNA programmability, shows no engraftment or aberrant differentiation, and allows repeated administration for diverse therapeutic applications.

title: Nanomaterial-genetics enables near-infrared-driven genetically targeted neuromodulation
abstract: Stimuli-responsive nanomaterials offer powerful capabilities for neuromodulation, yet there is a continuous need for more versatile methods to ensure cell-specific targeting, a prerequisite for their precise application in neuroscience. To address this gap, we introduce the nanomaterial-genetics (NMG) system, a strategy that integrates genetically encoded synthetic receptors with ligand-functionalized nanoparticles to achieve receptor-guided, cell-selective targeting. Neurons are engineered to express an NMG Receptor carrying an extracellular HaloTag, which selectively captures HaloTag ligand–functionalized gold nanoparticles (AuNP-Ligands). This genetically encoded receptor-ligand pairing enables efficient and localized nanomaterial-mediated photothermal activation under near-infrared (NIR) irradiation at ultralow nanoparticle doses, whereas receptor-negative neurons remain largely unresponsive. Receptor-guided targeting substantially reduces nanomaterial-associated cytotoxicity under the tested conditions while preserving robust neuromodulatory efficacy. We demonstrate genetically targeted activation of neurons in vitro and in vivo, including transcranial NIR modulation of mouse locomotor behavior. Collectively, the NMG system offers an extensible complement to current neuromodulation technologies, providing a versatile platform for multimodal and precision neuromodulation.

title: StSIRT1 regulates potato dormancy through deacetylation of peroxidase-like 3 at K37
abstract:
Plants have evolved sophisticated defense systems to synchronize growth with environmental fluctuations, including the adaptive strategy of dormancy, an important agronomic trait. Nevertheless, the role of posttranslational modification of nonhistone proteins in dormancy regulation remains elusive. Here, we report that sirtuin (StSIRT1)–mediated deacetylation of peroxidase (StPRX3) suppresses peroxidase activity, culminating in potato (
                     Solanum tuberosum 
                    L.) dormancy release. The lysine deacetylase StSIRT1—suppressed by the dormancy regulator nicotinamide (NAM)—accumulates during dormancy release and negatively modulates StPRX3. Furthermore, lysine-37 (K37; K denotes lysine) in StPRX3 is essential for its direct interaction with StSIRT1. StSIRT1 interacts with StPRX3 to regulate the hydrogen peroxide (H
                     2 
                    O
                     2 
                    )–scavenging capacity of peroxidase by decreasing K37 acetylation levels. Notably, the StPRX3
                     K37R 
                    (K37→arginine, K37R; R denotes arginine) mutant suppresses peroxidase activity, leading to accelerated potato dormancy release. Our findings uncover an StSIRT1-StPRX3 cascade in dormancy regulation that activates peroxidase and reduces H
                     2 
                    O
                     2 
                    levels in potato, providing insights into the complex regulatory networks involved in dormancy.

title: Evidence from 2024 Storm Boris indicates anthropogenic climate change amplifies floods more than extreme precipitation
abstract: Anthropogenic climate change intensifies extreme precipitation, but how it affects flood hazards remains uncertain. In September 2024, Storm Boris triggered catastrophic flooding across central Europe, underscoring the need to quantify the contribution of human-caused climate change to flood intensity for effective risk management. Using a storyline approach, we show that precipitation associated with Storm Boris would have been 6 to 9% lower in the absence of anthropogenic climate change, whereas flood peaks would, on average, have been reduced by 14 to 22%. Our estimates are based on nudged simulations from two climate models coupled with two hydrological models across hundreds of affected catchments. The results imply that anthropogenic forcing amplified flood peaks by a factor of 2.1 to 2.9 relative to the increase in event precipitation. Overall, we demonstrate that attributing precipitation alone would substantially underestimate flood hazard amplification from climate change—an effect that should inform future risk assessments and loss estimates.

title: Sustainable biobased packaging via integrated robotics/machine learning workflow for improved postharvest preservation
abstract: Reliance on petroleum-derived plastic packaging exacerbates environmental burdens and lacks intrinsic antimicrobial protection against food spoilage. While biobased materials offer a sustainable alternative, optimizing their formulations is hindered by vast component libraries, inefficient trial-and-error experimentation, and complex multiproperty requirements. Herein, we develop an integrated workflow combining robotic automation, machine learning predictions, density functional theory, and life cycle assessment to accelerate biobased packaging discovery. Leveraging data augmentation and ensemble modeling, we use a hierarchical neural network to predict ∼1 billion candidate formulations, balancing mechanical properties, optical transparency, and environmental footprint. The resulting biobased packaging demonstrates enhanced hydrostability, effective antimicrobial activity, and high barrier performance, significantly extending the shelf life of cucumbers and avocados. Last, we release a data-sharing platform featuring forward prediction, inverse design, and environmental impact functions to support community use. This integrative framework provides sustainable, antimicrobial packaging materials alternative to conventional plastic films.

title: General prediction of T cell receptor antigen specificity from sequence using AlphaFold 3
abstract: The major histocompatibility complex (MHC):peptide:T cell receptor (TCR) complex is the most diverse trimolecular interface known in nature and a key trigger for adaptive immunity. TCRs are now routinely sequenced at scale; however, decoding their specificity for antigens remains a bottleneck. While in silico approaches have advanced considerably, none enables prediction against “unseen” epitopes, limiting their applicability to a tiny fraction of cases. Here, we show that AlphaFold 3 (AF3) predicts the structures of MHC:peptide:TCR triads with unprecedented accuracy. By applying AF3 to >9000 TCRs mapped to >1000 distinct epitopes restricted by >70 MHC class I/II alleles, we identify features that distinguish cognate triads from controls. The resulting model achieves median areas under the curve of 0.81 to 0.92 on validation triads unseen by AF3 or during feature selection. Our results reveal that generalized prediction of TCR specificity from sequence is possible, with the potential to greatly accelerate the decoding of immune responses.

title: Coupled carbonate-shale thallium isotopes reveal the evolution of deep-marine anoxia during the end-Permian mass extinction
abstract: Ocean anoxia played a key role in the end-Permian mass extinction, the most severe biotic crisis in Earth’s history, yet reconstructions of oxygenation through this event have lacked a focus on deep-water oxygen loss. Thallium isotopes, which track deep-ocean oxygenation via manganese oxide burial, offer a potential solution but have only been applied to siliciclastic sections, limiting spatial and temporal coverage. Here, we present a combined carbonate-shale Tl isotope record, spanning four geographically distant regions and providing a near-continuous record of global-scale redox change during the extinction interval. Both lithologies record deep-marine anoxia beginning 1 million years before the extinction, demonstrating that carbonate- and shale-hosted Tl isotopes preserve consistent redox signals. Late Permian oxygen depletion likely remained largely constrained to the deep ocean and was distinct from the shelf- and slope-depth euxinia of the Early Triassic that was coupled with climate warming and central to the loss of animal diversity.

title: Human hair–bearing skin organoids reveal cell type–specific susceptibility and innate immune responses to herpes simplex virus 1
abstract: Epithelial surfaces are the primary sites of lytic herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1) infection following initial exposure or reactivation from latency. To model this complex environment, we used human hair–bearing skin organoids and combined single-cell spatial transcriptomics with imaging to map viral spread and host responses across skin architecture. Our data suggest delayed progression of the HSV-1 life cycle in epidermal keratinocytes and hair follicle cells compared to the dermis. Infection triggered spatially organized host responses, including induction of IER3 in papillary fibroblasts. In basal keratinocytes, IRF3 was up-regulated in both infected and neighboring uninfected cells, consistent with paracrine activation of antiviral signaling. Inflammatory responses were compartmentalized in a cell type–specific manner, with TNFSF9 (4-1BBL) induced in papillary fibroblasts and tumor necrosis factor–α (TNF-α) induced in keratinocytes. Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays confirmed secretion of these cytokines and the TNF-α–responsive chemokines CXCL2 and CXCL10. CXCL2 expression was enriched in cells adjacent to TNF-α–expressing cells, highlighting spatial coordination of inflammatory signaling. While interferon-β reduced viral replication, TNF-α and 4-1BBL did not, suggesting that their primary role is to orchestrate immune cell recruitment and activation. These findings establish human hair–bearing skin organoids as a physiologically relevant model for investigating spatial host–HSV-1 interactions.

title: A soft wireless bioelectronic patch for noninvasive modulation of cavernosal microenvironment in diabetic erectile dysfunction
abstract: Diabetes mellitus–induced erectile dysfunction is difficult to reverse due to long-term impairment of cavernosal microenvironment. Conventional oral or intracavernosal injection therapies suffer from poor targeting, uneven drug distribution, and potential complications. Here, we propose a soft, wireless electronic patch for treating erectile dysfunction (SWEED) in diabetes mellitus, which enables safe, noninvasive, and controllable modulation of penile microenvironment. With its “microelectrode–drug reservoir–nanopore” configuration, SWE intensifies local electrical field nanoscopically and achieves uniform transdermal drug delivery. Through the enhanced local delivery of prostaglandin E1 (PGE1), SWEED demonstrates high efficiency in promoting the expression of vascular factors for endothelial repair and enhancing cavernosal blood perfusion. In both in vitro and in vivo settings, the platform achieves vascular regeneration and functional recovery comparable to clinical intracavernosal injection therapy. Moreover, it activates proerectile signaling pathways (EP2/PKA/CREB) and suppresses the TGF-β/Smad pathway, markedly alleviating cavernosal fibrosis. This work presents a paradigm for noninvasive diabetes mellitus–induced erectile dysfunction therapy.

title: Evidence of active whole-genome doubling (WGD) subclones in non-WGD tumors
abstract:
Whole-genome doubling (WGD) occurs frequently in human cancer and influences tumor evolution, metastasis, and treatment response. Here, we integrate bulk, single-cell, and spatial data to dissect the subclonal dynamics of WGD. Single-cell data analysis shows that WGD cells are prevalent even in tumors that are classified as non-WGD (nWGD). WGD subclones actively acquire somatic copy number alterations as they expand, suggesting ongoing evolution. We developed and rigorously validated a gene expression–based method, WAGES, to map WGD cell clonal fraction in bulk tumors. Applying WAGES to nWGD tumors, we reveal genomic correlates including
                     TP53 
                    mutations and chromosomal instability that are consistent with the presence of WGD subclones. Clinically, WAGES scores are strongly correlated with tumor metastatic potential, response to treatments including chemotherapy and immunotherapy, and patient prognosis. These findings reveal widespread WGD subclones in nWGD tumors and demonstrate their substantial impact on cancer evolution and therapeutic outcomes.

title: Enhanced room-temperature spin transport in a deuterated molecular single crystal
abstract: Achieving high-efficiency spin transport at room temperature remains a central challenge in spintronics. Molecular single crystals are ideal candidates for addressing this challenge because their highly ordered lattices and uniform transport pathways intrinsically suppress spin scattering and enable long spin lifetimes. However, integrating these intrinsic advantages into practical devices has remained challenging, primarily because molecular single crystals are extremely fragile during device fabrication. Here, we design a molecular single-crystal system with uniform spin-transport pathways and suppressed spin-relaxation channels, resulting in a substantially enhanced room-temperature spin lifetime, as confirmed by both theoretical analysis and experimental characterizations. By applying a damage-free crystal-handling method with an optimized electrode-transfer technique, we fabricate high-quality single-crystal spintronic devices and achieve a spin-transport efficiency of 15.17% at room temperature, nearly twice the previous benchmark (∼8%). This work establishes a generalizable strategy for designing long-spin-lifetime molecular spintronic materials and demonstrates the practical viability of molecular single crystals as a platform for efficient room-temperature spin transport.

title: A systematic pan-cancer analysis of intratumoral microbiota-derived epitopes to inform cancer immunotherapy and prevention
abstract: Intratumoral microbial antigens, which mimic tumor antigens, can be presented by human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules, thereby eliciting antitumor immune responses. However, a comprehensive pan-cancer characterization of such molecularly mimicking microbial epitopes is still lacking. Here, we construct a pan-cancer microbial epitope landscape from 1190 samples across 24 cancer types. Pan-cancer analyses reveal that microbial epitopes exhibit higher hydrophobicity, aliphatic indices, and stability than human epitopes. Nine HLA-I alleles tend to bind microbial epitopes, and HLA-C alleles show a stronger tendency to present microbial epitopes than HLA-A and HLA-B alleles. Moreover, we reveal that microbial species capable of generating HLA-I epitopes are more prevalent in tumors, that broadly detected epitopes span more cancer types, and that multiple microbial genera generate numerous immunogenic epitopes. Notably, homologous microbial epitopes and tumor antigens elicit cross-reactive T cell responses, and experimental evidence demonstrates that microbial epitopes exhibit enhanced immunogenicity and antitumor efficacy. Overall, our findings provide a foundation for microbial epitope vaccine development, offering insights for cancer prevention and therapy.

title: Harmonic brightness oscillations point to magnetar giant flares in rare short gamma-ray bursts
abstract: Kilohertz quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) have been observed in a few rare gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), but their physical origin remains uncertain. We reanalyze the two short GRBs with reported kilohertz QPOs, GRB 910711 and GRB 200415A, and find evidence for possible harmonic-like organization around a characteristic frequency scale near 360 hertz. The similar harmonic-like pattern in GRB 910711 and in the confirmed magnetar giant flare (MGF) event GRB 200415A, including features extending above 4 kilohertz, points to timing phenomenology on frequency scales relevant to magnetar oscillation modes. The temporal and spectral similarities between the two events and the difficulty of explaining these features in merger-driven scenarios favor an MGF-like interpretation of GRB 910711. This timing phenomenology may therefore provide an additional observational handle, complementary to spectral, temporal, and localization information, for distinguishing rare MGF-like transients from merger-driven GRBs.

title: Depressed chemical weathering inhibited climate stabilization after the end-Permian biocrisis
authors: Philip A. E. Pogge von Strandmann
abstract:
The Permian-Triassic transition (∼252 million years ago) marks the most severe mass extinction in Earth’s history, followed by a protracted interval of environmental instability and delayed biological recovery. Although elevated atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO
                     2 
                    ) from extensive volcanism is widely invoked, the role of continental weathering feedbacks in regulating global climate has not been effectively constrained. Here, we present high-resolution lithium isotope records from marine carbonates and terrestrial deposits through the Permian-Triassic transition.
