title: Targeting Mitochondrial Redox Signaling Promotes Neuroregeneration and Functional Recovery in a Multiple Sclerosis Model
authors:
Yuki Narushima, 
Joshua Saylor, 
Shun Saito, 
Jinyan Zhou, 
Haruka Kawano, 
Shehata Anwar, 
Haruki Oba, 
Rachel Huezo, 
Miyu Okano, 
Haruki Matsuda, 
Makoto Kawatani, 
Kaori Honda, 
Hiroyuki Osada, 
Yuta Kikuchi, 
Masahito Ohue, 
Masami Ishibashi, 
Takayoshi Arai, 
Makoto Inoue, 
Midori A. Arai
abstract:
Modulation of mitochondrial redox signaling by furapyrrodole activates CYB5R3 and suppresses Notch signaling, unlocking the regenerative potential of endogenous neural progenitor cells. This approach promotes neurogenesis, oligodendrogenesis, and remyelination, thereby improving neuronal function in a mouse model of multiple sclerosis and identifying mitochondrial redox signaling as a potential therapeutic target for neuroregeneration in neurodegenerative diseases.








ABSTRACT
Neurodegenerative diseases, including multiple sclerosis (MS), are characterized by progressive neuronal loss and limited regenerative capacity. To stimulate in vivo neurogenesis and oligodendrogenesis by harnessing the untapped regenerative potential of endogenous neural progenitor cells (NPCs) that are upregulated in the CNS under disease conditions, we developed a novel compound that targets Notch signaling, a pathway known to suppress neuronal differentiation of NPCs. Furapyrrodole, which was identified by screening a natural product‐like synthetic chemical library, binds to and activates the mitochondrial reductase CYB5R3, which naturally downregulates Notch signaling downstream of γ‐secretase. The in vivo efficacy of furapyrrodole was evaluated in mice with experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE), a mouse model of MS. Furapyrrodole treatment after the peak of EAE disease significantly improved motor function and promoted recovery of motor neurons and myelination by stimulating endogenous NPC‐derived neurogenesis and oligodendrogenesis. In addition, furapyrrodole supresses neuroinflammation in the CNS. Collectively, these findings indicate furapyrrodole is a promising therapeutic candidate for MS by harnessing endogenously upregulated NPCs and inducing anti‐inflammation. Our study demonstrates for the first time that modulation of mitochondrial redox signaling promotes neuroregeneration and remyelination without causing severe adverse effects.

title: A Multi‐Structural Radiomic Digital Phenotyping Framework for Deciphering Preclinical Evolution of Degenerative Meniscal Tears
authors:
Shengfa Li, 
Hao Liu, 
Yanbin Zhu, 
Hang Zhang, 
Qifeng Tao, 
Wenbo Zhao, 
Xin Miao, 
Shanshan Yang, 
Tianyu Chen, 
David Hunter, 
Changhai Ding, 
Ting Wang, 
Juan Wang, 
Wei Chen
abstract:
Subclinical matrix disruption precedes degenerative meniscal tears across the knee joint. A spatial compartmental radiomics model utilizing 3D-DESS MRI captures early osteochondral destabilization, accurately predicting incident tears up to four years pre-collapse. Feature attributions uncover coordinated chondral and osseous alterations, advancing non-invasive risk profiling to guide timely, personalized joint-preserving interventions.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Degenerative meniscus tears (DMTs) are pivotal in knee osteoarthritis progression, yet conventional MRI often fails to capture the subvisual alterations preceding macroscopic failure. We developed a multi-structural digital risk stratification framework (MSC-RM) that integrates standardized radiomic signatures from six knee structures (femur, tibia, cartilages, and menisci) derived from 3D double-echo steady-state MRI with baseline clinical risk profiles. Utilizing a longitudinal cohort ( n  = 674), our framework decoded complex degeneration patterns, achieving superior 4-year predictive performance (AUC 0.871). Survival analysis revealed that high-risk individuals had a 6.12-fold greater hazard of developing DMTs than the low-risk group. Furthermore, a reader test with five resident surgeons demonstrated that MSC-RM significantly enhanced diagnostic consistency (Kappa increased from 0.38 to 0.55), effectively bridging the expertise gap. By shifting the paradigm from reactive lesion detection to proactive risk management, this framework provides a scalable strategy for precision preventive medicine and establishes digital biomarkers as critical tools for optimizing musculoskeletal health in aging populations.

title: Illumination‐Dependent Interfacial Recombination in Perovskite Photovoltaics Driven by Trap States in Metal Oxide Electron Transport Layers
authors:
Tianhao Lan, 
Joel Luke, 
Oskar J. Sandberg, 
Charlie Henderson, 
Ying Sun, 
Katherine Stewart, 
Ji‐Seon Kim
abstract:
Changes in light intensity impact trap states introduced at the metal oxide/perovskite interface. Comparing SnO 2 , TiO 2  and ZnO electron transport layers reveals high interfacial trapping and recombination under high-light, while bulk defects become more dominant under low-light. These findings provide important device design rules required for different illumination conditions.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) now exceed 27% power conversion efficiency (PCE); however their performance under varying illumination conditions remains strongly influenced by interfacial charge carrier dynamics. Although bulk defects have been substantially reduced through perovskite compositional engineering, trap states in metal oxide electron transport layers (ETLs) can still capture carriers and promote non-radiative recombination, with effects that depend strongly on photon flux. Here, we investigate trap-assisted interfacial recombination in metal oxide ETLs using a Low-High-Low (LHL) illumination protocol, which probes device behavior from low-light (1000 lux) to 1 Sun and back. We find that interfacial trap states have only a minor effect under low-light but become highly detrimental under 1 Sun illumination, where they dominate interfacial recombination and reduce the open-circuit voltage (V OC ). This effect is particularly pronounced for metal oxides with higher densities of surface trap states, such as TiO 2 . Upon returning to low-light after 1 Sun exposure, devices show a marked V OC  decrease followed by slow recovery, consistent with gradual charge release from interfacial traps and the subsequent suppression of recombination. These findings reveal the strongly illumination-dependent role of metal oxide trap states and provide design guidance for optimizing PSCs for both outdoor and indoor photovoltaic applications.

title: Multi‐Omics Analyses Identify Candidate Genes Associated With Stage‐Specific Quality Formation in Mulching‐Treated Moso Bamboo Shoots
authors:
Bo Wang, 
Yanbin Wang, 
Chunyue Wang, 
Zishan Ahmad, 
Peixin Teng, 
Huijing Ni, 
Qiang Wei, 
Muthusamy Ramakrishnan
abstract:
Organic mulching reprograms Moso bamboo shoot development, enhancing yield and nutritional quality. This multi-omics study reveals that coordinated metabolic, transcriptional, and post-transcriptional regulation drives stage-specific quality formation, offering comprehensive insights into how this agricultural practice improves crop performance and palatability.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Bamboo shoots are nutrient-rich edible resources, and organic mulching promotes earlier shoot emergence and increases yield. However, the molecular mechanisms regulating mulching-treated shoot (MtS) development remain unclear. Field experiments across three Moso bamboo forests, combined with biochemical profiling, metabolomics, and transcriptomics, examine MtS development. Mulching induces stage-specific shoot quality formation (MtS1-MtS4) and increases shoot size, yield, biochemical traits, and market value compared with spring shoots (SS) and winter shoots (WS). MtS increases soluble sugars, phenolics, tannins, and alkaloid-related metabolites and reduces water content and antioxidant capacity. Metabolite profiling identifies 2029 metabolites and reveals stage-dependent shifts in amino acid, carbohydrate, lipid, flavonoid, tricin-related, and cell-wall modification pathways. Transcriptome analysis identifies 13 691–18 038 differentially expressed genes across SS vs MtS comparisons. KEGG enrichment highlights sugar metabolism, lignin and cellulose synthesis, and hormone signalling. Transcription factor families, including bHLH, MYB, NAC, bZIP, C2H2, and SPL, show stage-dependent expression. O2PLS analysis reveals covariance between metabolite and transcriptome profiles. WGCNA identifies 16 stage-associated modules and candidate genes, including  SPL18 ,  NID1 ,  PIF3L6 ,  ATH1L , and  TOM6 . Alternative splicing indicates widespread post-transcriptional regulation. Protein-protein interaction analysis reveals interactions among AS-O2PLS-prioritised genes. These results show that mulching reshapes stage-specific shoot quality formation through coordinated physiological, metabolic, transcriptional, and post-transcriptional changes.

title: Variation in hypoxia tolerance is driven by evolutionary changes in gene regulation in the eastern oyster
authors: Eaton, K. M., Vaidya, R. V., La Peyre, J., Pollack, J. B., Sirovy, K. A., Kelly, M.
abstract: Understanding the genomic basis of stress tolerance is crucial for predicting biological responses to environmental change. Here, we investigated the genomic basis of divergence in hypoxia tolerance between two populations of eastern oyster (Crassostrea virginica) from Louisiana and Texas, USA. We combined low-coverage whole-genome sequencing data with previously generated transcriptomic evidence to understand the mechanisms underlying population-specific variation in hypoxia tolerance. Genome-wide analyses revealed substantial population differentiation (global FST = 0.21), indicative of a clear genetic break between our study populations. We combined estimates of genomic differentiation (FST) with diversity metrics to generate a set of exploratory candidate regions showing signatures consistent with recent selection. Several candidate genes identified through this approach were associated with the maintenance of homeostasis under environmental stress. We additionally tested whether genes previously identified as differentially expressed (DE) under hypoxia exhibit elevated genomic divergence between populations. While these hypoxia DEGs did show higher than expected between-population differentiation, this pattern also holds for other environmentally responsive genes. This suggests that transcriptomically responsive genes in general may generally show elevated divergence among populations, possibly due to a weaker effect of purifying selection. Furthermore, we found that hypoxia DEGs did not show an enrichment of nonsynonymous fixed differences (p = 0.9155, as compared to the genome-wide background), suggesting that the elevated divergence seen in these genes is not driven by rapid protein-coding evolution. Together, our results support a model in which population-scale differences in hypoxia tolerance occur primarily through evolution of gene regulation acting on environmentally responsive pathways.

title: Characterisation of cis-regulatory elements and genome wide enhancer prediction in Heliconiini butterflies
authors: Ritchie, A. D., Cicconardi, F., Montgomery, S. H.
abstract: The large-scale annotation and spatiotemporal characterisation of cis-regulatory promoters and enhancers remain limited in many non-model organisms, largely due to fragmented availability of multiomic datasets across species and developmental conditions. Heliconius butterflies, which have been used to investigate wing development and patterning, have provided key insights into the genetic architecture underlying morphological diversification and adaptive pigmentation. Despite this, we are limited in what we understand of how cis-regulatory dynamics drive phenotypic wing patterning variation. Here, by re-analysing and re-evaluating available data, we present a comprehensive new description of a cis-regulatory atlas for Heliconius wing development by integrating chromatin accessibility dynamics (ATAC-seq) with histone modification profiling (H3K27ac, H3K4me3). High-confidence peak sets enabled robust annotation of promoters and enhancers, revealing regulatory distributions consistent with canonical regulatory organisation. Promoters displayed comparatively higher conservation of transcription factor motifs, whilst enhancers exhibited greater sequence diversity, broader genomic distributions and more variable motif repertoires. Comparative analysis revealed cis-regulatory divergence to be primarily temporal, with substantial chromatin remodelling and differential histone enrichment across development, while regulatory dynamics were highly conserved between forewing and hindwing tissues. Extending these experimentally characterised regulatory landscapes, a convolutional neural network was trained for sequence-based enhancer prediction, achieving test AUROC and AUPRC values of 0.909 and 0.913, respectively. Predictions across 34 Heliconiini assemblies displayed significant enrichment within independently characterised accessible chromatin and conserved non-exonic elements (CNEEs), supporting their putative regulatory function. Overall, this study provides a large-scale characterisation of cis-regulatory dynamics and extends enhancer annotation across Heliconiini, providing a foundation for comparative investigations of regulatory conservation and diversification.

title: MutQA: A Cross-Validated Q&A Dataset for Genetic Mutations
authors: McCourt, R., Arredondo, D., Macaulay, O., Poshiya, S., Edeh, O., Virupakshappa, K., Nguyen Bach, M., Almeida Ruiz, E., Hu, Y., Tafoya, L. E., Hudgens, D. P., Kundnani, D., Sahu, A.
abstract: We introduce MutQA, a dataset of 330,387 citation-grounded question-answer (QA) pairs linking genetic mutations to their functional consequences as described in the biomedical literature. Each record pairs a protein-coding mutation with a natural-language question and an evidence-backed answer anchored to sentences in one of 27,442 open-access PubMed Central articles, spanning 6,620 genes and 125,593 gene-variant pairs. The dataset is constructed using CrossValQA, a framework that enforces information isolation between independent LLMs: one model generates QA pairs from an article, a second model answers the same question without access to the first model's response, and a third model judges whether each model's rationale supports the other's answer, so that retained QA pairs are reproducible from the source text rather than hallucinated. Of 401,406 audited QA pairs, 82.7% pass both directions of this cross-validation; those with a recoverable reference protein sequence form the released benchmark. In a 999-pair stratified audit, two expert annotators agree exactly on 86.4% of cross-validated QA pairs (95% CI 83.7-89.0; n = 638), a tier in which about 90% of ratings are "correct". Individual LLM judges agree with individual annotators at a comparable 87.0% on this tier but far less on QA pairs that fail cross-validation. Fine-tuning MutaPLM on MutQA nearly doubles its mean LLM-judge score for question-conditioned mutation-effect answering (1.45 to 2.82 on a 0-5 scale) and improves mutation-recovery accuracy from effect descriptions from 19.4% to 32.1%. Providing variant-matched MutQA retrieval context, without fine-tuning, improves strict answer accuracy across four LLM families by 20.0-28.6 percentage points, demonstrating the framework's ability to improve the reliability of LLM answers. We also apply CrossValQA to proteomics, providing a proof of concept for its use beyond mutation-specific QA. We release the dataset, construction framework, and evaluation code.

title: Shared genomic signatures of Arctic adaptation among distantly related plant lineages
authors: Elphinstone, C., Sandler, M., Stone, P., Torres Jimenez, M. F., Henn, J. J., Zhang, X., Birkeland, S., Brochmann, C., Henry, G. H. R., Todesco, M., Bacon, C. D., Rieseberg, L. H.
abstract: Extreme environments impose strong selection pressures that can drive convergent adaptation among distantly related species. Arctic plants survive low temperatures, 24-hour light in summer and darkness in winter, short growing seasons, limited precipitation, nutrient-poor soils, and extreme seasonal variation. To test if these conditions are associated with shared genomic signatures, we generated a chromosome-level genome assembly for Oxyria digyna and compared it with existing reference genomes for three distantly related Arctic species (Cochlearia groenlandica, Draba nivalis, Dryas octopetala) and for 16 non-Arctic species from the same families. We identified 214 orthogroups with signatures of positive selection in all Arctic species, 1.6 times the number shared among the non-Arctic species. Although no gene ontology (GO) categories remained significantly enriched after multiple-testing correction, descriptive annotations included genes involved in general functions including protein folding, glycolysis, transcription, and oxidative-stress responses. Orthogroups showing copy number variation were associated with biotic interactions, sexual reproduction, and nutrient acquisition, suggesting that species may respond to biotic and nutrient stresses by shifts in gene copy number. Arctic and alpine genomes contained lower proportions of some repetitive elements, including terminal inverted repeats, and smaller regions of centromeric repeats than non-Arctic genomes. Overall, we see shared genes under positive selection, similar functions of genes with high copy number variation, and lower counts of some repetitive elements in the Arctic plant genomes. Our findings reveal a shared genomic signature of Arctic adaptation across deeply diverged plant lineages, suggesting that evolution in extreme environments repeatedly targets similar genomic features.

title: Taxonova: Deep learning enables fast and confidence-aware microbiome species-level amplicon classification
abstract:
by Kardokh Kakabra, Shriram Patel, Andriy Temko, Marcus J. Claesson 

Accurate species-level taxonomic classification of microbial amplicon sequences remains challenging due to the difficulty of resolving subtle variations within conserved ribosomal regions. Traditional similarity-based methods struggle with short amplicons and sequences with poor database representation. No existing method performs robustly across the full spectrum of amplicon lengths, limiting applicability across diverse sequencing platforms and variable-region targets. We present Taxonova, a deep learning framework for both short- and long-read ribosomal amplicons. Evaluated across physical and biome-simulated mock communities representing seven biomes (via the accompanying benchmark tool Taxobench), Taxonova attains species-level F-measures of 0.76–1.00 (median 0.94) for short-read and 0.82–0.99 (median 0.97) for long-read amplicons spanning 250 bp to 4,900 bp, reduces the species-level abundance-estimation error (L1 norm) by a median of 0.52 to 1.50 depending on amplicon region, and has a species-level false-positive rate that is a median of 16.2 × 10 −4  lower than that of the other classifiers. Species-level assignment is expected to be most reliable for well-characterised communities, such as human-associated microbiomes. To demonstrate real-world applicability, we also compared amplicon-derived taxonomic profiles to paired shotgun whole-genome sequencing from gut, soil and vaginal microbiomes; Taxonova achieves the strongest species-level concordance (Jaccard) in all three studies, with a species-level Jaccard index 0.009 to 0.022 higher than that of the next-best classifier across both high- and low-complexity communities. Taxonova runs at a throughput of roughly 100 sequences per second on a single CPU core, making it suitable for routine deployment in research settings.

title: From 16S rDNA-seq count data to microbial interactions: A comprehensive benchmark of co-occurrence network inference methods
abstract:
by Piero Mariotto, Matteo Baldan, Barbara Di Camillo, Giacomo Baruzzo 

The study of the ecological interactions within microbial communities is crucial for gaining deeper insights into community ensemble and evolution, enabling targeted modification of the community’s functionality. Many inference approaches have been developed to derive ecological associations. Here, we focus on co-occurrence computational methods, in which associations are inferred from metagenomic abundance data by measuring the statistical dependence between species counts across different sampled populations. The limitations in culture-based experiments have hindered the ability to assess these methods’ validity, leading to scarce application in metagenomics studies. To provide a comprehensive assessment of network inference method performance, we benchmark 18 different computational approaches across a broad spectrum of experimental scenarios. We use synthetic 16S rDNA-seq count data generated from known underlying interaction networks, enabling systematic and controlled evaluation. The benchmark spans scenarios varying in numbers of species and samples, sample richness, sequencing depth, and interaction network structure. We evaluated the performance of the methods both in terms of accuracy of the inferred network, using various metrics from binary classification theory and metrics coming from network science, and in terms of computational burden. We found that methods have valid results only in a restricted, and often unrealistic, field of application, whereas their effectiveness diminishes with more realistic simulation parameters. Our findings highlight the limits of the co-occurrence-based approach and the need for further development in microbial ecological association inference.

title: Cd47 deficiency in mouse brain under excitotoxic stress
abstract:
CD47, a transmembrane protein with well-established immune and neurodevelopmental roles, was recently identified as an abundant presynaptic protein in humans, non-human primates, and mice. To investigate how
                     Cd47 
                    influences neuronal stress and injury, we performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing of hippocampi from wild-type (WT) and
                     Cd47 
                    knockout (KO) mice exposed to kainic acid (KA) at convulsive (KA25; 25 mg/kg) or subconvulsive (KA3; 3 mg/kg) doses. Integrating cell-type annotations with Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA) revealed distinct neuronal and glial gene modules whose co-expression structure differed by genotype and by KA exposure. Notably, certain modules showed KA-associated changes in co-expression structure only in
                     Cd47 
                    -deficient cells. Enrichment analyses of these modules highlighted translational, bioenergetic, and synaptic gene sets. Comparing transcriptome-wide distributions using Wasserstein distance demonstrated that vehicle-treated KO cells most closely resembled WT cells exposed to KA3, of all fifteen pairwise comparisons. These findings suggest that
                     Cd47 
                    loss shifts the hippocampal transcriptome toward a state resembling mild excitotoxic stress, implicating
                     Cd47 
                    as a candidate regulator of neuronal stress adaptation and providing a hypothesis for testing that role.

title: Telomere-to-telomere genome of a dodecaploid desert shrub  Prunus pedunculata  reveals polyploidy-driven arid adaptation
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Background 
                     
                      Geographical imbalance in extremophile plant genomics has left the Mongolian Plateau underexplored.
                       Prunus pedunculata 
                      , a desert shrub endemic to this arid region, provides an ideal system for understanding woody plant adaptation to extreme drought, yet its genomic architecture remains unknown.
                     
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     
                      Here we present a telomere-to-telomere genome assembly for
                       P. pedunculata 
                      , a dodecaploid (2n = 12 × = 96) with the highest ploidy level among sequenced woody perennials. Its 1.38 Gb genome is resolved into 48 chromosomes, and telomeric repeats are detected in each. Evolutionary analysis confirms an autopolyploid origin with > 80% subgenome consistency and no evidence of hybridization. The most recent whole-genome duplication dates to approximately 3.49 million years ago, coinciding with the uplift of the Tibetan Plateau and the intensification of Asian interior aridity. Ancestral karyotype reconstruction using six
                       Prunus 
                      species spanning diploid to dodecaploid genomes and three inflorescence types reveals an eight chromosome ancestor and post polyploidization chromosomal rearrangements. Organ specific transcriptomics under progressive drought uncovers a coordinated division of labor that integrates ABA,
                       CLE25 
                      ,
                       BES1 
                      /
                       BIN2 
                      , and auxin signaling modules to orchestrate growth cessation and stress survival. Drought induced genes significantly overlap with expanded gene families, demonstrating functional recruitment of polyploidy derived redundancy.
                     
                   
                   
                     Conclusions 
                     
                      This work confirms an autopolyploid origin for
                       P. pedunculata 
                      and links this polyploidization event to the aridification of the Asian interior. Duplicated genes have been repurposed for drought stress, and a multi-component signaling network coordinates organ responses and enhances survival under water scarcity, offering leads for crop improvement.

title: In-cell structures visualize human pre-ribosome assembly in the nucleolus
abstract: In eukaryotes, ribosome biogenesis initiates within the nucleolus, a hallmark multilayered compartment of the nucleus. Structures of pre-ribosomes have been characterized ex situ, but their assembly pathways within human nucleoli have not been described. Here, we used cryogenic correlative light and electron tomography to visualize molecular landscapes within HeLa cell nucleoli and obtained in-cell structural snapshots of both ribosomal subunit precursors, the small subunit processome and the pre-60S. These recapitulate major states resolved previously ex situ and reveal additional critical interaction partners, including the RNA exosome, rixosome, and nuclear export receptor CRM1-RanGTP. We further show how pre-ribosome assembly landscapes are altered upon RNA polymerase I inhibition. Our study combines molecular structures with cellular context to elucidate the spatiotemporal assembly pathway of the human ribosome.

title: The delocalized nature of chemical bonding at a catalytic metal surface
abstract: Adsorbate bonding at metal surfaces requires hybridization of localized molecular orbitals with delocalized electronic bands of the metal; hence, the electronic wave function involved in bonding may extend far beyond the adsorption site. We revealed the consequence of this delocalization by determining the distance over which structural variations of the metal surface influence the molecule-metal bond strength. Velocity-resolved kinetics provided adsorption energies for three molecules bound at atomic steps of platinum (Pt), each exhibiting bond-strength changes of up to 0.2 electron volts as the step-step distance varied over 100 angstroms. We observed molecule-specific behavior reflecting the hybridization of molecule-specific orbitals with symmetry-selected orbital bands of the metal that respond differently to structural modifications of the solid. We discuss implications of these observations for adsorption on Pt nanoparticles.

title: Data-driven discovery and rapid, direct synthesis of MXenes
abstract: MXenes are a rapidly expanding family of two-dimensional transition metal carbides and nitrides, yet scalable synthesis routes remain limited and historical reports suggest a broader, largely unexplored chemical space. We used machine learning–assisted database mining to uncover hidden multilayer MXenes. Screening reveals 33 previously synthesized but unrecognized MXene candidates. Guided by these findings, we synthesized seven multilayer MXenes using a rapid, scalable self-propagating high-temperature method that requires no sustained external heating and completes within minutes. We further realized 11 previously unexplored rare earth–based MXenes (M = praseodymium, neodymium, samarium, gadolinium, terbium, holmium, and thulium). Experiments and modeling suggest semiconducting behavior and diverse magnetic states across this family. Together, these results expand the MXene family and demonstrate a data-driven strategy for accelerating materials discovery through sustainable methods.

title:
Papaver 
                    self-incompatibility is controlled by two multiallelic idiomorphs
abstract:
Self-incompatibility (SI) prevents self-fertilization through highly polymorphic genetic recognition at the
                     S 
                    locus with multiple alleles. In
                     Papaver rhoeas 
                    , the
                     S 
                    determinants were previously identified as
                     PrpS 
                    and
                     PrsS 
                    . However, we found that
                     PrpS-PrsS 
                    was absent in many
                     S 
                    haplotypes. In this work, we report the identification of an alternative pair of polymorphic
                     S 
                    genes,
                     S locus oligopeptide transporter 
                    (
                     SOPT 
                    ) and
                     S locus glycine-rich protein 
                    (
                     SGRP 
                    ), segregating at the
                     S 
                    locus when
                     PrpS-PrsS 
                    is absent.
                     SOPT 
                    and
                     SGRP 
                    display hallmark
                     S 
                    determinant features and confer SI when heterologously expressed in
                     Arabidopsis thaliana 
                    . Therefore, instead of having allelomorphs with homologous variants, the
                     Papaver 
                    SI system is determined by two multiallelic idiomorphs sharing no obvious common ancestry. This discovery of a dual-idiomorph system reveals a distinct genetic basis for polymorphism, with implications for the evolution of allorecognition mechanisms.

title:
Whole-body single-cell atlas of an adult vertebrate,
                     Danionella cerebrum
abstract:
A complete cell type transcriptome atlas of a vertebrate could promote understanding of animal cell type composition, organization, and evolution. The miniaturized, transparent, and regenerative teleost
                     Danionella cerebrum 
                    brings whole-vertebrate single-cell profiling experiments within reach. We performed region-stratified single-cell RNA sequencing across the adult
                     Danionella 
                    body and mapped cell types and gene expression at single-cell resolution using spatial transcriptomics. We delineated spatially distinct neural cell types on the basis of their regional gene expression signatures. The body-wide atlas elucidated cell types harboring adult molecular positional memory, uncovered paedomorphic features, and revealed conserved body-region and appendage-specification programs in adult connective tissue. Comparative analyses revealed conserved neural cell types, and regeneration datasets uncovered expression dynamics during telencephalon regeneration. This whole-vertebrate transcriptome atlas yields a comprehensive resource for myriad questions in biology and neuroscience.

title: Western Pacific double subduction drives Gulf of California rifting
abstract: Continental rifting reflects the balance between tectonic forces and lithospheric strength, yet the mechanisms of breakup remain debated. Rapid rifting of the Gulf of California oblique rift (GOCOR) ~6 million to 8 million years ago is a key example; it may have resulted from the lithosphere responding to external kinematics or acceleration of long-lived extension. The dynamics of either scenario remain incompletely understood. In this study, we highlight that the rapid rifting of the GOCOR coincides with the initiation of Western Pacific double subduction. Using three-dimensional geodynamic models, we show that such subduction reorganization can transmit extensional stresses of ~5 to 15 megapascals across the Pacific plate, loading the GOCOR and the southern San Andreas fault. Subduction reorganization may represent the missing driver for the initiation of rapid GOCOR rifting within a preconditioned lithosphere and may be an overlooked tectonic force behind other rifting events.

title: Genomic erosion across avifauna in a biodiversity hotspot sounds a conservation alarm
abstract: Loss of biodiversity can have a hidden dimension—the cryptic erosion of genetic diversity even in the face of apparent species resilience. We quantified changes in genetic diversity by comparing historical and modern genomes of 62 songbird species from the Gaoligong Mountains, a biodiversity hotspot in southwestern China. We identified genomic loss averaging between 43 and 49%; and, unexpectedly, common species were disproportionately affected. We argue that this loss was driven primarily by habitat fragmentation (and mitigated by dispersal ability) and show that it exceeds prior estimates and conservation policy thresholds. Species identified as having lost diversity continue to be listed as “Least Concern” on the International Union for Conservation of Nature’s Red List of Threatened Species, exposing a blind spot in extinction risk monitoring. We call for genomic metrics to be rapidly integrated into global conservation frameworks.

title: A commensally regulated immune rheostat fine-tunes skin barrier fitness
abstract:
At the skin’s surface, the epidermis must balance stem cell renewal with barrier maintenance to withstand environmental stress and shield against pathogens. In this study, we identify a microbial-immune-epithelial feedback mechanism that integrates environmental information into stem cell regulation in mice. Specifically, we show that Langerhans cells (LCs), an intraepithelial macrophage population, orchestrate this circuit by producing prostaglandin E
                     2 
                    , which restrains stem cell proliferation, promotes epidermal differentiation, and maintains barrier integrity during homeostasis. Upon pathway disruption, stem cells become overactivated, hindering terminal differentiation and weakening barrier function. Upstream, LC activity is tuned by the local microbial environment in a rheostat-like fashion, coupling commensal sensing to stem cell dynamics. Our findings provide a general framework for how barrier tissues achieve adaptive homeostasis amid continual external fluctuations.

title: Spatial coordination in the codevelopment of the human urogenital system during organogenesis
abstract: The human urogenital system originates from a common embryonic domain, yet the mechanisms guiding its spatiotemporal coordination remain understudied. Here, we combined high-resolution spatial transcriptomics with single-cell multiomics to profile human embryos from Carnegie stages 15 to 23, capturing the codevelopmental dynamics of the urogenital system. We revealed mesonephros- and adrenal primordium–derived signals that promote gonadal specification and enable efficient in vitro generation of cells resembling early gonadal lineages. We also uncovered a possible mesonephric origin of gonadal supporting cells through rete testis or ovarii linking the mesonephros. Finally, we delineate three transcriptionally distinct steroidogenic lineages differing in cholesterol sourcing, cortisol synthesis, and sex hormone production that together orchestrate sex differentiation. These findings deepen our understanding of urogenital system assembly and guide the exploration of coordinated multiorgan development.

title: Stimulated protein degradation to promote mitochondrial function and neuronal survival
abstract:
Targeted protein degradation is a promising modality to treat cancer or inflammation, but whether it can provide a similar benefit for disorders caused by pervasive protein dysregulation is unclear. We describe stimulated protein degradation (SPD) as a strategy that leverages agonists of stress-responsive E3 ubiquitin ligases to simultaneously eliminate multiple pathogenic factors. Specifically, we show that activators of the reductive stress response E3 CUL2
                     FEM1B 
                    boost degradation of multiple physiological substrates to improve mitochondrial import and electron transport chain assembly. In this manner, CUL2
                     FEM1B 
                    agonists preserve mitochondrial function and neuronal survival in models of neurodegenerative COX deficiency syndrome and Friedreich’s ataxia. By activating E3 ligases that evolved to safeguard cellular integrity, SPD expands the use of compound-induced protein degradation to complex pathologies of high unmet need.

title:
Altermagnetism revealed by polarized neutrons in MnF
                     2
abstract:
Altermagnets are compensated magnets with symmetry-enforced spin split bands. Direct spectroscopic evidence for their existence has been reported in several materials. For example, inelastic neutron scattering (INS) has recently been used to witness a splitting of magnon bands in MnTe that is compatible with altermagnetism. Here, we present polarized INS results on MnF
                     2 
                    showing that it is altermagnetic. Our data reveal a splitting coming from the long-range dipolar coupling. Furthermore, using a domain-biased sample, the data reveal a nonzero chirality in the neutron scattering cross section that reverses the sign between the two magnon modes. It is this feature that clearly demonstrates altermagnetism in MnF
                     2 
                    . This finding highlights the potential for polarized INS to characterize altermagnets through its sensitivity to fine structure in magnon spectra.

title: Intrinsic gestational timing governs human cerebellar development after preterm birth
abstract: Intrinsic programs shape brain maturation; however, which of these programs are perturbed by prematurity as well as the molecular pathways involved remain unknown. The human cerebellum serves as a paradigm of extrauterine development—its accelerated growth and circuit formation align with the third trimester, a period disrupted by preterm delivery. Using multimodal datasets encompassing in vivo neuroimaging and neurodevelopmental outcomes with postmortem spatial-transcriptomic and histopathological profiling, we show that prematurity diverts the cerebellar developmental trajectory. Cerebellar growth and functional outcomes scaled with gestational age, despite modifying perinatal exposures. Spatially resolved developmental programs underlying macroscopic trajectories were marked by incomplete granule cell maturation and impaired Purkinje cell structural refinement, which indicate lineage-specific developmental asynchrony. Thus, prematurity constitutes biologically displaced maturation, in which infants of equivalent postmenstrual age occupy divergent developmental states.

title: The global geography of threats to freshwater biodiversity
abstract: Human activities are eroding biodiversity, especially in freshwater systems. Despite major advances in quantifying species vulnerability and threats, we still lack a crucial understanding of where threats are affecting freshwater species globally. Here, we produced a species-centered spatial assessment of threats, mapping the impact of 45 threats across 21,490 freshwater species of amphibians, fish, mammals, odonates, and reptiles. We found that species in highly developed and water-managed regions are strongly affected by multiple overlapping threats. Although threats vary across taxa and regions, increasing threat probabilities elevate extinction risk and population declines, with freshwater species experiencing greater threat intensity and distinct spatial patterns than terrestrial species. Our findings establish a spatially explicit baseline for targeting the most urgently needed freshwater conservation and management interventions.

title: A Martian meteorite that formed ≳4.1 billion years ago samples Mars’ early crust and mantle
abstract:
Martian meteorites provide a record of the planet’s geological history. However, most are geologically young samples that are not representative of Mars’ surface, which is dominated by ancient rocks. We describe the Martian meteorite Teghaza 001 (Teg 001), a slowly cooled igneous rock that formed at least 4.1 billion years ago. Its composition, mineralogy, and texture are distinct from other Martian meteorites. We determine that Teg 001 is a sample of ancient crust, which formed from a geochemically distinct mantle source with primordial composition. The presence of aqueously altered minerals, combined with bulk and mineral-specific oxygen isotope measurements, indicate that Teg 001 experienced reactions with fluids enriched in
                     18 
                    O, before ejection into space by an impact.

title: Rapid longitudinal flights cause time shifts and Sun compass error
Emergence of Chern metal in a moiré Kondo lattice
abstract:
A Chern metal is a two-dimensional metallic state of matter carrying chiral edge states. We report the observation of a Chern metal at the onset of the magnetic Kondo breakdown in a frustrated moiré Kondo lattice--angle-aligned MoTe
                     2 
                    /WSe
                     2 
                    bilayers. The state is compressible and is manifested by a nearly quantized Hall resistance and a finite longitudinal resistance arising from a bad metallic bulk. We demonstrate the presence of a chiral edge state by nonlocal transport measurements and current-induced quantum anomalous Hall breakdown. Magnetic circular dichroism measurements further reveal a magnetization plateau for the Chern metal before a metamagnetic transition at the Kondo breakdown. Our results open an opportunity for moiré engineering of exotic quantum phases through the interplay between band topology and Kondo interactions.

title: Chiral altermagnon in MnTe
abstract:
Altermagnetism has been recognized as a magnetic phase that bridges the properties of ferro- and antiferromagnetism. The momentum-dependent spin splitting observed in these materials reflects their distinctive symmetry characteristics, which also establish the conditions for chiral magnons to emerge. Here we provide direct experimental evidence for a chiral magnon in the altermagnetic candidate manganese telluride (MnTe) revealed by circular-dichroism resonant inelastic x-ray scattering. This mode, which we term chiral altermagnon, exhibits a distinct momentum dependence of its spin polarization consistent with the altermagnetic
                     g 
                    -wave symmetry of MnTe. Our polarization-resolved data corroborate the existence of a discrete class of magnetic excitations, demonstrating how altermagnetic order shapes spin dynamics and paving the way for advances in spintronic and quantum technologies.

title: Pervasive patterns in bird songs resemble those in human speech and song and are independent of vocal learning
abstract: Bird songs are often described as analogs to human speech and songs, but expansive comparisons are necessary to determine analogy and mechanistic substrates. By analyzing global corpora consisting of 367 bird species (>74,500 vocal elements from ~5900 songs) within two clades of vocal learners (oscines and hummingbirds) and related nonlearners (suboscines and nightjars) and 52 human languages (>15,000 elements in >800 speech or song phrases), we revealed common patterns in bird songs that resemble prevalent patterns in human speech and song with variation in resemblance to speech or song. Vocal learning did not systematically affect acoustic patterning or similarity to human vocalizations. These data underscore the deep analogies between bird and human vocalizations and convergent motor mechanisms shaping communication.

title: Deciphering the molecular basis of maize cold tolerance via integrative regulatory network analysis
authors:
Tianshuo Li, 
Wei Wang, 
Chuang Jiang, 
Jinkui Cheng, 
Fei Yi, 
Liusheng Duan
abstract:
SUMMARY 
                   
                    Maize (
                     Zea mays 
                    L.) is a globally critical but cold‐sensitive crop. Understanding the temporal organization of cold‐responsive, circadian‐associated, and hormone‐associated transcriptional programs is essential for deciphering how plants balance growth and survival under cold stress to ensure food security. We performed high‐resolution time‐series RNA‐seq on 108 maize seedling samples across 14 time points (0–36 h cold stress and 24 h recovery). Coronatine (COR) was utilized as a defined JA‐associated chemical perturbation to probe hormone‐associated transcriptional responses during cold stress. We identified 12 986 cold‐responsive and 2259 recovery‐responsive genes, revealing a recovery‐associated transcriptional transition characterized by suppressed photosynthesis‐related processes and enrichment of genes associated with lipid catabolism, accompanied by transient physiological stress during early recovery. Cold stress induced widespread phase shifts and reduced oscillation amplitudes among circadian‐associated transcripts, while COR identified distinct hormone‐associated transcriptional modules and candidate network‐associated genes, including
                     ZmWRKY71 
                    and
                     ZmHSP28 
                    , whose roles were further supported by molecular and genetic analyses. This study establishes a temporally resolved transcriptional framework for maize cold stress and recovery, integrating transcriptional dynamics, physiological responses, and experimentally supported regulatory nodes.

authors:
Jinghui Gao, 
Houyin Xia, 
Yajun Wu,

Jiawen Peng,

abstract:
SUMMARY 
                   
                    Alfalfa (
                     Medicago sativa 
                    ), an autotetraploid species, is a globally important forage crop. Traditional genetic transformation methods predominantly rely on leaf‐derived callus, a process that is complex, inefficient, and particularly challenging to generate stable transgenic lines in polyploid plants. To address these limitations, we developed an efficient transformation system that bypasses callus induction by directly exploiting stem regeneration. Our protocol enables the generation of stable gene‐edited alfalfa plants from shoot tips. It accommodates stem explants from various developmental stages and significantly reduces the time required. Moreover, this approach was effective across multiple alfalfa cultivars, and preliminary proof‐of‐concept experiments in
                     Nicotiana tabacum 
                    and
                     Solanum lycopersicum 
                    suggested potential transferability beyond alfalfa. This study represents a substantial advancement in perennial plant transformation and provides a robust and practical platform for optimizing stem regeneration‐based genetic modification systems.

title:
Correction to “
                     GT1 
                    regulates maize sex determination by affecting the jasmonate pathway”

Single‐cell transcriptome atlas reveals a
                     
                       WRKY33 
                     
                    ‐
                     
                       HSP81 
                     
                    regulatory module that orchestrates phenylpropanoid‐mediated defense against
                     
                       Sclerotium rolfsii 
                     
                     in
                     
                       Dendrobium officinale
authors:
Lingli Li, 
Ye Xu, 
Wei Liu, 
Zhitao Niu, 
Qingyun Xue, 
Xiaoyu Ding
abstract:
SUMMARY 
                   
                    Plants employ cell‐type‐specific transcriptional programs to defend against pathogens, yet the cellular heterogeneity of immune responses in the medicinal orchid
                     Dendrobium officinale 
                    Kimura et Migo remains largely unexplored. A single‐cell transcriptomic atlas of the
                     D. officinale 
                    stem base upon
                     Sclerotium rolfsii 
                    infection was constructed, profiling over 20 000 cells across 12 and 24 h post‐infection. A total of 21 cell clusters were resolved into 6 major cell types—epidermal, ground tissue parenchyma, proliferating, xylem, phloem, and vascular bundle parenchyma cells—with identities validated by fluorescence
                     in situ 
                    hybridization. Cell‐type‐specific analyses revealed that epidermal and phloem cells mounted early defense responses, while xylem cells exhibited the most extensive transcriptional reprogramming at 24 hpi, coinciding with the activation of lignin biosynthesis pathways.
                     WRKY33 
                    was identified as a central transcriptional activator that directly binds W‐box motifs in the promoters of lignin biosynthetic genes
                     C4H 
                    and
                     HCT 
                    , promoting lignin deposition and enhancing disease resistance. Conversely, the nuclear‐localized chaperone
                     HSP81 
                    physically interacts with
                     WRKY33 
                    and functions as a broad regulator of multiple transcription factors via co‐factor sequestration, thereby compromising defense when overexpressed. These findings uncover a
                     WRKY33 
                    ‐
                     HSP81 
                    regulatory module that orchestrates phenylpropanoid‐mediated defense in
                     D. officinale 
                    , providing a high‐resolution cellular framework for understanding plant immunity and offering potential targets for improving disease resistance in this economically valuable species.

title: Lessons from the past: resurrecting an ancestral strigolactone receptor

Nuclear importin α1
                     AtIMPA1 
                    regulates stomatal reopening to defend against
                     Pst 
                     DC3000 
                    by orchestrating
                     ABA 
                    signaling
authors:
Ting Zhang, 
Kang Wang, 
Yi Guan, 
Jingao Zhang, 
Charles Tetteh, 
Chenxi Liu, 
Cheng Zhang, 
Pinyuan Jin, 
Sheng Luo, 
Yiling Wang, 
Huajian Zhang
abstract:
SUMMARY 
                   
                    Importin α family proteins serve as essential carriers for transporting specific disease‐resistant proteins into the nucleus, enabling these proteins to function properly. However, whether importin α proteins are involved in plant immunity remains unclear. Here, we characterized a guard cell‐expressed protein importin α1 AtIMPA1, which contributed to resistance against
                     Pseudomonas syringae 
                    pv.
                     tomato 
                    DC3000 (
                     Pst 
                    DC3000). When dip‐inoculated with
                     Pst 
                    DC3000, the
                     impa1 
                    mutants exhibited increased susceptibility, along with significant stomatal reopening induced by the phytotoxin coronatine (COR) secreted by
                     Pst 
                    DC3000; while overexpression of
                     AtIMPA1 
                    enhanced resistance to
                     Pst 
                    DC3000 with compromised stomatal reopening induced by COR. Notably, following syringe‐infiltration of
                     Pst 
                    DC3000, the
                     impa1 
                    mutants showed increased resistance, whereas overexpression lines were more susceptible to
                     Pst 
                    DC3000, indicating that COR‐triggered stomatal reopening is a primary determinant in AtIMPA1‐mediated disease resistance. Further investigations revealed that AtIMPA1 regulated COR‐triggered stomatal reopening is linked to abscisic acid (ABA) signaling. Mutation of
                     AtIMPA1 
                    attenuated the ABA‐mediated inhibition of root length and seed germination, and disrupted the ABA‐induced protein abundance and localization of the ABA‐responsive protein, supporting its role in regulating the ABA response. These findings shed light on the functional significance of AtIMPA1 in COR‐triggered stomatal reopening and provided new insights into how importin α proteins orchestrate ABA signaling to regulate plant immunity.

title: Sorghum Metabolic Atlas: A fluorescent protein‐based subcellular localization resource for sorghum enzymes
authors:
Purva Karia, 
William P. Dwyer, 
Ava Kloss‐Schmidt, 
Charles Hawkins, 
Bo Xue, 
Daniel Ginzburg, 
Maxine L. Gutierrez, 
Ritesh Mewalal, 
Ian Blaby, 
David W. Ehrhardt, 
Seung Y. Rhee
abstract:
SUMMARY 
                   
                    Plant metabolism drives traits essential for productivity and resilience, yet understanding metabolic networks requires subcellular, cellular, and tissue‐level spatial context that remains limited, particularly in crop species. Experimentally derived subcellular localization data for enzymes are sparse, constraining analyses of metabolic organization in the cell. We developed a high‐throughput protoplast transformation and fluorescent protein (FP) tagging system optimized for
                     Sorghum bicolor 
                    , a climate‐resilient C
                     4 
                    crop. Using this platform, we experimentally determined the subcellular localization of 234 metabolic enzymes spanning 184 pathways. The sorghum enzymes we characterized localize to 12 subcellular compartments. Comparison with computational predictions highlights variable accuracy across compartments, and cross‐species comparison with
                     Arabidopsis thaliana 
                    shows partial agreement with available experimental data. All data are accessible through the Sorghum Metabolic Atlas (
                     www.sorghummetabolicatlas.org 
                    ) web platform, enabling search, visualization, and download. This study presents a large‐scale experimental dataset of enzyme localization in sorghum, providing a resource for studies of plant metabolic organization and comparative analyses.

title: Trait‐based plant ecology: some history and some future
authors:
Mark Westoby, 
Sandra M. Díaz, 
Hans Lambers, 
Ian J. Wright
abstract:
Schematic of plant species range boundaries, some mechanisms that might set them, and some traits that might explain them.
 
 
 Summary 
 Since around the year 2000, trait-based ecology has become self-aware as a strand of research within ecology. How did this happen? What is trait-based ecology now? And where might it go in future? This paper offers selective answers to those questions. We first outline the history leading up to the emergence of trait-based plant ecology during the 1990s. Second, we assess briefly what has been achieved up to mid-2020s. Third, we discuss two challenges (among many) for trait-based plant ecology over the next 25 yr. One is about the boundaries of species ranges along temperature gradients. Some of these boundaries may be decided by thermal tolerance, others by biotic interactions such as competition or pathogens. How can we identify which applies to which species? Which traits, feasible to measure across many species, might help with this? A second major challenge is about the global zonation of vegetation physiognomy or biome types. How well can we explain this in terms of traits, and from first principles, meaning via eco-evolutionary models for why different trait values should be competent and competitive in different settings? First-principle rules for how ecosystems are constructed should be central to ecology as a discipline. 
 Resumen 
 Desde aproximadamente el año 2000, la ecología basada en caracteres funcionales se consolidó como una línea de investigación autoconsciente y distintiva. ¿Cómo surgió, qué representa actualmente y hacia dónde avanzaría? Este artículo ofrece algunas respuestas selectivas. Primero, resumimos los antecedentes históricos que condujeron al desarrollo de la ecología vegetal basada en caracteres funcionales en los años 1990. Segundo, evaluamos los logros en la década de 2020. Tercero, examinamos dos desafíos (entre los muchos que existen) para los próximos 25 años. El primer desafío se refiere a los límites de distribución de las especies a lo largo de gradientes térmicos. Algunos pueden estar determinados por la tolerancia térmica y otros por interacciones bióticas, como la competencia o los patógenos. ¿Cómo podrían distinguirse estos mecanismos y qué caracteres, factibles de ser medidos en muchas especies, podrían ayudar? El segundo desafío involucra la zonación global de las fisonomías de vegetación y los biomas. ¿Hasta qué punto pueden explicarse mediante caracteres funcionales y primeros principios, es decir modelos eco-evolutivos, cuáles valores de caracteres deberían ser competentes y competitivos en diferentes ambientes? Las reglas fundamentales que explican a partir de primeros principios cómo se construyen los ecosistemas deberían ocupar un lugar central en la ecología.
