By integrating TabPFN baseline comparison, training‐experience assessment, and model‐consistency analysis, the framework identifies boundary and extrapolative samples that require priority refinement. Our predictions for W‐doped and Sc‐doped M‐type hexaferrites successfully reproduce key experimental occupancy trends. This work offers a practical data‐driven strategy to generate physically plausible occupancy hypotheses and assign refinement priorities for partially occupied oxide systems.

title: Lactate Drives Pathological Browning of White Adipose Tissue to Aggravate Sepsis‐Associated Metabolic Disorders in a GPR81‐Dependent Manner
authors:
Chunliang Zheng, 
Xiaohua Li, 
Shuo Li, 
Chungen Xing, 
Chun Cao
abstract:
Sepsis-triggered lactate accumulation induces pathological white adipose tissue browning. Lactate activates adipocyte GPR81 to sequentially upregulate CTRP6-p38 signalling and UCP1 expression. This cascade exacerbates sepsis-associated metabolic disorders.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Lactate serves as a prognostic biomarker for sepsis, yet its adipose-centered signaling pathway driving persistent metabolic disorders remains unclear. We reveal that lactate accumulation triggers browning of white adipose tissue (WAT) via GPR81 to aggravate sepsis-induced hypermetabolism, muscle wasting, and insulin resistance. Septic patients exhibit hyperlactatemia and WAT browning, with lactate concentrations correlated with fat and muscle loss. Genetically deleting UCP1 substantially attenuates LPS-induced hypermetabolism, muscle wasting, and insulin resistance, confirming WAT browning as a major mediator of sepsis-associated metabolic disorders. Lactate supplementation and pharmacological interventions using glycolysis or lactate dehydrogenase inhibitors identify lactate as the upstream pathogenic trigger. Using siRNA screening, global GPR81 knockout, and AAV9-mediated adipose-specific GPR81 knockdown, we identify GPR81 as the lactate receptor mediating UCP1 upregulation. Mechanistically, GPR81 activation induces CTRP6 and p-p38 to upregulate UCP1. AAV9-mediated overexpression of CTRP6/MKK6 in GPR81 −/−  mice, together with pharmacological downregulation of CTRP6 or inhibition of p-p38, supports the involvement of this pathway in WAT browning. Taken together, evidence from clinical data, gene-knockout mice, and primary adipocyte experiments demonstrates that lactate drives WAT browning in a GPR81-dependent manner to aggravate sepsis-associated metabolic disorders, identifying potential targets for therapeutic investigation in metabolic disorders unresponsive to conventional anti-infective and nutritional support treatments.

title: An Infusible Decellularized Extracellular Matrix Material Binds to Vasculature in Infarcted Myocardium and Induces Pro‐Reparative Gene Expression Following Acute Myocardial Infarction Through Inherent Avidity and Bioactive Signaling
authors:
Michael B. Nguyen, 
Alexander Chen, 
Quincy Lyons, 
Van K. Ninh, 
Maxwell C. McCabe, 
Colin Luo, 
Benjamin D. Bridgelal, 
Connor Uhre, 
Julian Cheng, 
Kate E. Reimold, 
Selena Cao, 
Kirk C. Hansen, 
Kevin R. King, 
Karen L. Christman
abstract:
To better characterize an infusible extracellular matrix (iECM) material, we applied size‐based fractionation to separate out components into two major fractions. We characterized these fractions to understand how material properties such as composition, morphology, and biochemical properties affect bioactive effects in the context of acute myocardial infarction, providing insight into further development of infusible, targeting biomaterials.








ABSTRACT
To treat acute myocardial infarction (MI), we previously engineered an infusible decellularized extracellular matrix (iECM) biomaterial that reduces vascular permeability and exerts immunomodulatory and pro‐reparative effects. To probe the heterogenous contents of iECM and its contribution to infarct localization and downstream biological function, we separated iECM into high and low molecular weight (MW) components. Though mass spectrometry showed similar compositions, biochemical analysis and transmission electron microscopy revealed higher sGAG content within the nanofibrillar high MW, while the globular low MW had more exposed functional groups. These differences translated to a higher binding efficiency of the high MW to ECM proteins and cell surface receptors under flow, while the low MW drove the reduction in vascular permeability. Neither component alone achieved the infarct retention levels of complete iECM, showing that the two components exhibit dependent infarct localization and both are necessary for iECM's overall function. Via single‑nucleus RNA sequencing, both components elicited comparable immunomodulatory and pro‑reparative transcriptional profiles, suggesting that the similarity in composition likely drives the transcriptional response. These findings elucidate the material properties of an intravascularly deliverable ECM biomaterial and how those properties relate to downstream biological behavior, enabling future work investigating nanomaterial mimicry and improvements in material processing and potency.

title: Fuyuan Huoxue Decoction Promotes Lumbar Interbody Fusion in Rats: Role of Macrophage‐Driven Inflammation and the TLR9/NF‐κB Pathway
authors:
Hongwei Gao, 
Han Wu, 
Shaorong Li, 
Weijian Wang, 
Yijian Guo, 
Shuai Cheng, 
Jiayi Sun, 
Jilong An, 
Wei Zhang
abstract:
Fuyuan Huoxue decoction improves lumbar interbody fusion in rats while reducing inflammatory macrophage activity and supporting bone‐forming stem cells. Experiments implicate extracellular DNA and TLR9/NF‐κB signaling in early responses. These findings point to coordinated control of inflammation and osteogenesis as a potential route to stronger spinal fusion.








ABSTRACT
Delayed union and pseudarthrosis remain complications of lumbar interbody fusion. We investigated Fuyuan Huoxue decoction (FY) in a rat extreme lateral interbody fusion model. FY improved bone mineral density and trabecular architecture. Reduced inflammatory macrophage infiltration and nuclear factor kappa B (NF‐κB) activation at 4 weeks were accompanied by improved bony bridging at 8 weeks. Transcriptomic and network analyses nominated Toll‐like receptor 9 (TLR9)/NF‐κB signaling for functional investigation. FY‐medicated serum reduced macrophage inflammatory markers and extracellular double‐stranded DNA (dsDNA), promoted bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell (BMSC) osteogenesis, and attenuated impairment induced by inflammatory macrophage‐conditioned medium. DNase treatment reduced this medium's inhibitory effects, whereas a separate exogenous dsDNA challenge impaired osteogenesis and was attenuated by a TLR9 antagonist. TLR9 agonist and antagonist experiments in BMSCs and a 2‐week in vivo agonist intervention supported pathway involvement. Human nonunion single‐cell data showed increased phospholipid scramblase 1 and interleukin‐6 expression in myeloid cells. These findings support complementary pro‐osteogenic and anti‐inflammatory actions of FY and identify TLR9/NF‐κB as a candidate pathway contributing to fusion repair.

title: Co‐Design Insights for Mechanically Active Flexible Printed Circuit Boards Through the CurveQuad Origami Robot
authors:
Xuelin Wu, 
Daniel Feshbach, 
Satviki Vasireddy, 
Louis Beardell, 
Bao To, 
Yuliy Baryshnikov, 
Cynthia Sung
abstract:
This paper presents the process of integrating electronics directly into the body sheet of CurveQuad, a small origami robot that can self‐fold, crawl, and steer with a single actuator. The authors design a flexible printed circuit board for the body sheet: the key challenge is to navigate how embedding electronics affects the mechanical properties and thus the robot's functionalities.








ABSTRACT
Folding flexible printed circuitboards (FPCBs) into origami patterns offers a route to fabricating robots with actuation, sensing, and control fully integrated into the robot body. However, integrating electronics into origami robots introduces a coupled electrical and mechanical design problem since the circuit layout affects the local stiffness and mass distribution and therefore the deformation mechanics. We explore this problem in the context of the FPCB CurveQuad, a centimeter‐scale curved‐crease origami quadruped. The robot body is fabricated as a folded double‐sided FPCB that contains the crease pattern, copper routing, sensors, local stiffening features, and electrical interfaces. A single servomotor drives tendons on the underside of the body, enabling the sheet to self‐fold from a planar state and twist for crawling and steering. The resulting robot is 60 mm ×$\times$ 65 mm ×$\times$ 50 mm in the folded state and weighs 10.9 g. It crawls at 16.8 mm s−1${\rm s}^{-1}$ (0.259 body lengths s−1${\rm s}^{-1}$), steers by shifting the actuator oscillation range, and is capable of feedback control. We present our design process for this robot, illustrating strategies for addressing electromechanical co‐design with complex bending requirements, enabling folded FPCBs to function as robotic mechanisms rather than simply as passive electronics substrates.

title: SpaCut: Transcript‐Aware Morphology Fusion for Robust Cell Segmentation in Subcellular Spatial Transcriptomics
authors:
Yongheng Li, 
Fangfang Zhu, 
Wenwen Min
abstract:
Subcellular spatial transcriptomics enables high-resolution mapping of gene expression within tissues, but accurate cell segmentation is essential for assigning transcripts to individual cells. We present SpaCut, a deep learning framework that integrates transcriptomic features with nucleus-guided morphological information to precisely delineate cell boundaries. Across diverse spatial transcriptomics datasets, SpaCut improves segmentation accuracy and transcript assignment, enabling more reliable single-cell analysis of tissue architecture.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Subcellular Spatial Transcriptomics (SST) offers unprecedented opportunities to decipher tissue architecture at subcellular resolution. Consequently, accurate cell segmentation is a fundamental prerequisite for analyzing SST data, as precise transcript assignment is essential for downstream single-cell interpretation. Existing methods often overlook the spatial organization of transcripts, rely on simplified geometric priors, or struggle to coordinate transcript-derived features with morphology-derived spatial guidance. This limitation restricts their adaptability to irregular cell shapes, often leading to transcript misassignment. To address this, we propose SpaCut, a unified deep learning framework designed to effectively integrate transcriptomic feature learning with dynamic morphological guidance. SpaCut comprises a Gene-Wise Attention (GWA) module and a Nuclei-Guided Attentive Fusion (NGAF) module. GWA encodes the high-dimensional transcript map and aggregates features across multiple depths. NGAF uses the encoded transcript features to modulate distance-based nuclear softmasks and refine nucleus-anchored cell boundaries through progressive training. Extensive evaluations across seven datasets from diverse platforms (including Xenium, CosMx, MERSCOPE, and Stereo-seq) demonstrate that SpaCut significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both segmentation accuracy and consistency with single-cell reference data. The source code is available at  https://github.com/wenwenmin/SpaCut .

title: A Programmable Braided Silk‐Glass Fiber Ligament Promoting Rapid Motoric Recovery
authors:
Changbo Lu, 
Daming Liu, 
Haoxin Zhang, 
Zhiwei Qiao, 
Qiuming Gao, 
Jia Meng, 
Hongyin Yue, 
Songkai Li, 
Shuo Zhang, 
Tao Yuan, 
Yun Xue, 
Hui Jiang, 
Zhenguo Liu, 
Yibo Wang, 
Nirong Bao, 
Yuli Chen, 
Xiaojiang Yang
abstract:
A scalable three‐dimensional braiding strategy integrates silk and glass fibers into customizable artificial ligaments with programmable “J‐shaped” nonlinear mechanics. The silk‐rich architecture supports osseoligamentous integration, while glass fibers provide mechanical reinforcement and biomimetic mineralization cues, enabling strain‐adaptive load transfer, accelerated tendon‐bone healing, and functional motor recovery within 4 weeks after rabbit ACL reconstruction.








ABSTRACT
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction and related soft‐hard tissue repairs remain challenged by grafts that either lack the characteristic “J‐shaped” stress–strain profile or sacrifice compliance for stiffness while also offering poor biological integration. Here, we report a silk‐glass fiber (SF‐GF) hybrid ligament fabricated by scalable three‐dimensional braiding, combining industrially available glass fibers with biocompatible silk. By tuning the braiding angle (15∘$15^\circ$–45∘$45^\circ$), the grafts exhibit programmable nonlinear mechanics and viscoelasticity. This design closely replicates the strain‐stiffening response and long‐term creep resistance of native ligaments. Silk‐rich domains promote osseoligamentous integration and osteogenic differentiation, while glass fibers provide high strength and bases for biomimetic mineralization. In rabbit ACL reconstruction, the angle‐optimized SF‐GFs facilitated prompt tendon‐bone healing and restored functional jumping ability within 4 weeks. Finite element modeling rationalizes the strain‐dependent load transfer from silk to glass fibers, underlying the characteristic “J‐shaped” response. Importantly, this material‐structure co‐design leverages mass‐producible components and a manufacturable braiding process, facilitating translational potentials beyond ACL reconstruction toward diverse soft‐hard tissue repairs.

title:
HADHA
                     K406 
                    Lactylation Regulates Metabolic Reprogramming and Suppresses Immune Responses in Gastric Cancer
authors:
Maoxiao Feng, 
Qinlian Jiao, 
Jiankang Zhu, 
Yidan Ren, 
Xiaoyu Teng, 
Xin Su, 
Zigan Li, 
Yuxuan Cai, 
Xiaoyan Liu, 
Yunshan Wang, 
Guangyong Zhang
abstract:
HADHA K406 lactylation fuels fatty acid β-oxidation and HMGCR-dependent cholesterol biosynthesis, fostering immunosuppressive MDSCs and exhausted CD8 +  T cells in gastric cancer. Loss of this modification blocks cholesterol production, remodels the tumor microenvironment, and tumor growth is suppressed via combined inhibition of HMGCR and LDHA.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Gastric cancer (GC) represents a substantial global health challenge and is among the most prevalent and deadly malignancies worldwide. Emerging evidence suggests that protein lactylation plays a pivotal role in the progression of various cancers. However, the specific levels and regulatory mechanisms of protein lactylation in GC remain poorly understood. In this study, we detected elevated pan-lactylation modification levels in GC tissues. Notably, lactylation at the K406 site of hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase (HADHA) was significantly upregulated in GC tissues. This site-specific lactylation modification enhanced GC progression. Disrupting lactylation at the HADHA  K406  site markedly reduced its enzymatic activity, thereby mitigating GC progression by impairing fatty acid β-oxidation and glycolysis. Furthermore, inhibiting HADHA  K406  lactylation (HADHA K406la) suppressed the HMG-CoA reductase (HMGCR)-mediated cholesterol synthesis pathway, which, in turn, improved the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment in GC. Finally, combining an HMGCR inhibitor with a lactate dehydrogenase A (LDHA) inhibitor effectively enhanced the immune response against GC and inhibited tumor progression. In conclusion, this study demonstrated that HADHA K406la regulates GC progression through its impact on metabolic pathways, suggesting its potential as a therapeutic target for GC treatment.

title: Toward Practical Zn‐Ion Batteries Through Separator/Electrolyte Co‐Design
authors:
Gao Wang, 
Ze He, 
Rui Wang, 
Jiajing Wang, 
Shaowen Cao, 
Michael De Volder, 
Qinyou An
abstract:
A hybrid organic–aqueous electrolyte enables thin commercial polypropylene separators to replace bulky glass-fiber separators in practical Zn-ion batteries. This electrolyte/separator co-design improves wettability, promotes uniform Zn plating/stripping, and suppresses hydrogen evolution, resulting in 4360 h of symmetric-cell cycling and stable Zn//NVO full cell operation at 4.4 mAh cm −2  while increasing pouch-cell energy density by over 2.5-fold.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 While substantial research effort has been paid to address short-circuits and parasitic hydrogen evolution reactions (HER) in Zn-ion batteries (ZIBs), a remaining challenge that is often overlooked is ZIB separators. Currently, thick glass fiber (GF) separators are used, which unnecessarily reduce the volumetric cell performance and lead to non-uniform Zn plating/stripping. Unfortunately, separators optimized for Li-ion batteries are intrinsically hydrophobic and therefore incompatible with aqueous ZIB systems. Here, we propose using a hybrid organic-aqueous electrolyte which is compatible with thin polypropylene (PP) separators developed for Li-ion batteries. The hybrid electrolyte, together with the PP separator, enables uniform Zn plating and suppresses HER. Combined, these effects allow for stable cycling for 4360 h at 1 mA cm −2  and 3 mAh cm −2  in a Zn symmetrical cell. Further, replacing the currently used 350 µm-thick GF separator with our proposed 23 µm PP separator can increase the energy densities of multi-layer pouch cells by over 2.5-fold. Finally, Zn//NVO full cells using our hybrid electrolyte and separator demonstrate stable cycling performance for over 200 cycles at a high areal capacity of 4.4 mAh cm −2 , demonstrating that electrolyte/separator co-design is an overlooked strategy toward practical ZIBs.

title: Passive Color Imaging Through Macroscopic Strong Scattering Media
authors:
Renrui Wang, 
Xiaoyu Wang, 
Jianyu Wang, 
Zhiyu Yang, 
Xiangyang Ji
abstract:
Light reflected from distant targets is severely attenuated and scattered by dense fog. A color‐channel‐simulated, independently exposed sCMOS array (CISA), combined with a passive colorful de‐scattering pipeline (PCDP), captures and reconstructs extremely weak target signals. Clear color images are recovered under strong scattering, demonstrating a practical route toward passive long‐range imaging in challenging environments.








ABSTRACT
De‐scattering imaging seeks to recover target information from the scattered images, which has increasingly garnered attention due to its wide‐ranging applications across various fields. Scattering media such as fog and turbid water can severely degrade imaging quality, thereby obstructing the accurate recovery of important details for identifying targets. Existing methods struggle to maintain de‐scattering performance in practical complex strong scattering media. To address this challenge, we propose an sCMOS array detection system that utilizes color channel simulation and independent exposure adjustment mechanisms. Our system significantly extends the dynamic range and enhances the signal‐to‐noise ratio of raw scattering data. By introducing a passive colorful de‐scattering pipeline, we achieve high‐quality reconstruction in strong scattering conditions that preserves the target's chromatic identity. Experiments in outdoor foggy conditions demonstrate the system's effectiveness in recovering target's shape and color. Further validation in aquaculture setting indicates the generalization of our method. This work paves the way for outdoor passive imaging applications under challenging scattering conditions.

title: Genome‐Wide and Multi‐Omics Analysis Identified DNA‐Interacting Circular RNA circFOXK2 as MLL1 Regulator for Histone H3K4 Methylation in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma
authors:
Chi Hin Wong, 
Jessica Jazmin Peña‐Paladines, 
Sum Yin Valerie Leung, 
Ka‐Fai To, 
Kenneth Siu Ho Chok, 
Yangchao Chen
abstract:
Circular RNA circFOXK2 is frequently upregulated in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma to promote tumor heterogeneity, growth, and metastasis. Through circRNA‐DNA interaction at different genomic locations, circFOXK2 removes the PPIE inhibitory effects on MLL1 for gene‐activating H3K4 methylation of the oncogenes. This highlights the importance of circRNAs in gene regulation through circRNA‐DNA interaction and uncovered the novel therapeutic direction targeting circFOXK2‐DNA interaction.








ABSTRACT
Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is one of the most devastating malignancies with high lethality despite the current therapeutic interventions. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) play important roles in many biological processes and disease development. However, the underlying mechanism remains largely unexplored. To identify novel druggable targets, we aimed to elucidate the mechanisms contributing to the critical roles of circRNAs in PDAC. We performed a genome‐wide and multi‐omics investigation on the circFOXK2‐DNA interaction in PDAC progression. Single‐cell ATAC‐sequencing analysis using the publicly available dataset revealed the importance of the circFOXK2‐DNA interaction network in intratumoral heterogeneity. Through circRNA‐DNA interaction by complementary base pairing, circFOXK2 recognizes targets at different genomic locations: enhancer, promoter, and intragenic region. CircFOXK2 forms a docking pocket by intramolecular base pairing for the N‐terminal RNA‐recognition motif of PPIE, disrupting the PPIE‐MLL1 interaction. This removes the PPIE inhibitory effects on MLL1 for gene‐activating H3K4 methylation. Specifically, circFOXK2 promotes TMSB15B and BCAS1 expressions by enhancing H3K4me3 at the promoter. At the gene body, circFOXK2 facilitates transcription elongation of TRIO and LAMA4 by intragenic H3K4me3. At the distal intergenic enhancer, circFOXK2 promotes H3K4me1 of CYP26A1 and TCP11 for gene activation. These results highlight the importance and therapeutic potential of circRNA‐DNA interaction in gene regulation.

title: Scalable variant-to-function screens using prime editing perturb-seq
authors: De Jonghe, J., Armas Reyes, M., Jamieson, C., Christensen, J. B., Opzoomer, J. W., Taylor-King, J. P.
abstract: Linking genetic variants to their functional consequences at scale remains a major challenge in human genetics. Perturb-seq is limited in the variants it can install, while prime editing has largely been restricted to simpler mechanistic readouts. Here, we introduce prime editing perturb-seq (PEP-seq), which links programmed mutations to transcriptomic states. We designed 2,164 prime editing guides targeting common expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs), premature termination codons, and position-matched synonymous controls, generating 749,110 time-resolved single-cell transcriptomes. PEP-seq precisely detected nonsense-mediated decay, while probe-based junction measurements suggested depletion of mature RNAs. For eQTLs, a locus-size-corrected specificity metric showed that the intended target was frequently the most affected transcript within a 1 Mb window, with effects also associated with open chromatin near the edit site. These results establish PEP-seq as a scalable platform for direct, endogenous variant-to-function mapping.

title: Engineered Tn5 Variants Enhance CUT&Tag Fidelity for Transcription Factors
authors: Piper, L., Baird, E., Ashbaugh, H. J., Pentecost, O. A., Nowinski, S., Janssens, D. H.
abstract: The CUT&Tag method performs exceptionally well for profiling histone modifications, but mapping sequence-specific transcription factors (TFs) is complicated by intrinsic Tn5 activity at accessible DNA, and the high-salt washes used to suppress this activity can destabilize TF-chromatin interactions. We engineered the Tn5 DNA-binding channel to attenuate target-DNA engagement by replacing individual positively charged amino acids with neutral amino acids. We identified a "Goldilocks" variant (K160A) with intermediate attenuation that improved recovery of GATA2 motif-containing sites under low-salt CUT&Tag and KCl-based DynaTag conditions. A second variant (K249A) had improved performance for profiling CTCF over less accessible sites characterized by sharply focused short-fragment enrichment. By comparing the K160A and K249A variants, this TF-CUT&Tag assay provides a physical readout of the local chromatin environment at TF binding sites. Applying K160A TF-CUT&Tag to pluripotency-associated TFs in mouse embryonic stem cells increased recovery across their genomic binding landscapes while preserving factor-specific motif architectures. During skeletal muscle differentiation, TF-CUT&Tag improved recovery of MyoG and Pax7 occupancy relative to standard CUT&Tag, revealing strongly motif-enriched MyoG binding and a shift in Pax7 binding from CpG-rich promoters in progenitors toward Pax7 motif-enriched sites during differentiation. Together, these results show that TF-CUT&Tag captures distinct modes of TF-chromatin interaction, including motif-directed binding sites and more salt-sensitive sites that may depend on lower-affinity DNA recognition or protein-protein interactions and are difficult to predict from DNA sequence alone.

title: A 4,000-year genomic history of Bantu speakers from the Congo rainforest
authors: Parasayan, O., Roux, M., Mendisco, F., Prado-Martinez, J., Liu, D., Laval, G., Harmant, C., Pemonge, M.-H., Pomilla, C., Young, L., Hurles, M., Sandhu, M., Massilani, D., Chak, B., Barreiro, L. B., Hombert, J.-M., Mouguiama-Daouda, P., Kacki, S., Grollemund, R., Deguilloux, M.-F., de Saulieu, G., Oslisly, R., Quintana-Murci, L., Patin, E.
abstract: The Congo rainforest was the heartland of the Bantu Expansion, yet its demographic history remains partially understood. We inferred past population dynamics using genomes from 960 sub-Saharan Africans, including four newly sequenced ancient individuals from Iroungou cave and 176 present-day individuals from Gabon. Bantu-speaking populations began differentiating ~4,000 years ago, preceding explosive population growth by a millennium. Distinct southward dispersals contributed to the ancestry of Bantu speakers in Gabon and elsewhere in sub-Saharan Africa, with the ~700-year-old Iroungou individuals providing the closest genetic proxies for the latter. Both Bantu speakers and hunter-gatherers from the Congo rainforest experienced a major demographic crisis ~1,500 years ago, coinciding with an archaeological hiatus. These findings illuminate early Bantu dispersals and the subsequent, unexplained collapse of rainforest populations.

title: 3D-genome impacts of TAD-boundary-disrupting ultra-rare structural variants identified in schizophrenia
authors: Porras, L. M., Farrell, M., Rodriguez-Lausell, I., Iglesias-Maldonado, G. A., Tuliao, E. V., Wright, E., Kreiman, A., Ancalade, N., Stoddard, C., Szatkiewicz, J., Giusti-Rodriguez, P.
abstract: Schizophrenia is a complex and multifactorial brain disorder that impacts ~1% of the U.S. population. The genetic architecture of schizophrenia includes 10 large rare structural variants (SVs) ~10 exonic variants, and over 250 common variants. Previously we combined whole genome sequencing (WGS) with brain-specific epigenomic data and found an excess of ultrarare SVs in schizophrenia localizing to the boundaries of topologically associated domains (TADs). Alterations in TAD boundaries (TAD-b) may lead to disarrangement of enhancer-promoter contacts and dysregulation of gene expression and have been associated with several human diseases. Our study sought to functionally characterize two of these TAD-b SVs using chromatin conformation capture (e.g., Hi-C) and RNA sequencing, to unveil mechanistic insight into the effects of these variants on 3D-genome organization and gene expression. To achieve this, we genetically engineered these two TAD-b SVs in isogenic induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) using CRISPR/Cas9. iPSCs were differentiated into neuronal precursor cells, excitatory glutamatergic neurons, and medium spiny neurons. We found that these TAD-boundary-disrupting SVs could reshape the 3D-genome and transcriptional networks in a cell-type-specific manner.

title: NicheCorr: Identifying Niche-Specific Differential Gene Co-Expression in Spatial Transcriptomics
authors: Yang, S., Ho, Y.-Y., Fan, D.
abstract: Cell-cell communication is central to biological processes such as immune responses and tumor progression, yet the role of spatial proximity between distinct cell types in shaping gene co-expression remains poorly understood. Existing approaches primarily identify differences in average gene expression across tissue regions, often overlooking how local cellular microenvironments reshape gene-gene interactions within cells. To address this gap, we introduce NicheCorr, a statistical procedure that identifies cell type-specific niche-associated gene co-expression changes within distinct spatial niches. In simulations, NicheCorr attained the highest power for detecting niche-dependent co-expression. It was also the only method evaluated that maintained Type I error control when mean expression varied nonlinearly with the niche, a setting in which CS-CORE, scHOT without mean adjustment, and the Pearson test all exhibited inflated false positive rates. Furthermore, NicheCorr integrates ligand-receptor (LR) inference, enabling a comprehensive view of spatially structured signaling interactions. We applied the framework to the CosMx SMI Human Liver FFPE Dataset and the Xenium Human Pancreatic Cancer Dataset, identifying 52 gene pairs in liver tumor cells whose co-expression changes with T-cell niche composition and 48 gene pairs in pancreatic cancer whose fibroblast niche-dependent co-expression differs between tumor and CFTR- tumor cells, and uncovering potential LR interactions that may underlie these differential co-expression patterns.

title: Individualised electrophysiological neural field models for the assessment of thalamocortical function in disorders of consciousness: A multicentre study
authors: Glenn J. M. Van der Lande
abstract:
by Lín Cóngyǔ, Prejaas Tewarie, Naji L. N. Alnagger, Iván Mindlin, Glenn J. M. Van der Lande, Laouen Belloli, Steven Laureys, Lionel Naccache, Benjamin Rohaut, Aurore Thibaut, Jitka Annen, Olivia Gosseries, Pablo Núñez, Jacobo D. Sitt 

Understanding the neural mechanisms underlying disorders of consciousness (DoC) remains a major challenge, particularly in distinguishing limited awareness in minimally conscious state (MCS) and complete unawareness in unresponsive wakefulness syndrome, also coined vegetative state (UWS/VS). In this multicentre study, we fitted a biophysically informed corticothalamic neural field model to high-density EEG data from two large independent datasets, comprising 203 UWS patients, 270 MCS patients and 74 healthy controls. We then used the fitted parameters to simulate EEG time series on a per-subject basis and compared empirical and simulated complexity metrics. The model reliably captured the spectral features across different states of consciousness and revealed reduced corticothalamic integrity in DoC patients that was more pronounced in UWS than in MCS, supporting the mesocircuit hypothesis. Furthermore, the simulated EEG reproduced the complexity patterns of the empirical recordings, with permutation entropy emerging as a sensitive marker capable of distinguishing between MCS and UWS for both real and simulated time series.

title: The evolutionary advantage of replacers in the Moran process
abstract:
Evolution occurs in populations of reproducing individuals. In stochastic descriptions of evolutionary dynamics, such as the Moran process, individuals are chosen randomly for birth and for death. If the same type is chosen for both steps, then the reproductive event is wasted, because the composition of the population remains unchanged. Here we introduce a new phenotype, which we call a
                     replacer 
                    . Replacers are efficient competitors. When a replacer is chosen for reproduction, the offspring will always replace an individual of another type (if available). We determine the selective advantage of replacers in well-mixed populations and on one-dimensional lattices. We find that being a replacer substantially boosts the fixation probability of neutral and deleterious mutants. In particular, fixation probability of a single neutral replacer who invades a well-mixed population of size
                     N 
                    is of the order of
                     
                       
                         
                         
                           
                             1 
                             / 
                             
                               N 
                             
                           
                         
                       
                     
                    rather than the standard 1/
                     N 
                    . Even more importantly, replacers are much better protected against invasions once they have reached fixation. Therefore, replacers dominate the mutation selection equilibrium even if the phenotype of being a replacer comes at a substantial cost: curiously, for large population sizes and small mutation rates, the relative reproductive rate of a successful replacer can be as low as 1/
                     e 
                    .

title: Early vs late fusion of qMIDS with machine learning based classifiers for oral cancer diagnosis from gene expression data
abstract:
by Ferid Ben Ali, Iosif Mporas, Vaishnavi Balaji, Dickson Ibaranyanakaye, Barbara Carey, Muy-Teck Teh, Sola Adeleke 

Different fusion architectures of the quantitative Malignancy Index Diagnostic System (qMIDS) method with machine learning classifiers for oral cancer diagnosis from gene expression data are investigated. The proposed fusion architectures are tested on geographically and ethnically diverse datasets and the evaluation results showed performance improvements with late fusion, which significantly outperformed early fusion in more matched model configurations than the reverse in every cohort, although at the best-performing configuration the two architectures were statistically indistinguishable in most cohorts. Inter-dataset analysis showed robustness of the proposed architectures when the training/test samples are from different populations.

title: Modeling reaction–diffusion processes in simplified to complex astroglial branchlet geometries using different simulation tools
abstract:
by Laura Keto, Saana Seppälä, Derek Ndubuaku, Annika Mäki, Tuomo Mäki-Marttunen, Marja-Leena Linne, Tiina Manninen 

Computational modeling of spatial biochemical processes in neuroscience is increasingly important as advances in experimental and imaging techniques provide detailed insights into cellular organization. Reaction–diffusion models are commonly used to study the diffusion and interactions of ions and molecules within neuronal cells, and multiple open-access simulation platforms have been developed to support such analysis. However, a comprehensive analysis of commonly used simulation tools, including MCell, STEPS, NeuroRD, and NEURON, remains lacking, particularly for realistic glial cell geometries, as these tools were originally developed for neurons. Here, we present a systematic analysis of these four simulation environments by implementing equivalent calcium diffusion and calcium–calmodulin reaction–diffusion models across a range of spatial domains. These include simplified geometries (cylinders and rectangular cuboids) as well as biologically realistic astroglial morphologies derived from electron microscopy data, including mouse Bergmann glia and mouse and human cortical astrocytes. Using matched kinetic parameters and diffusion constants, we examine simulation outputs and morphological variations across platforms under comparable conditions. We find that all tools produce overall consistent results for the systems considered, indicating that each can reliably capture diffusion and reaction–diffusion dynamics in simplified and complex geometries. At the same time, we show that the structural heterogeneity of branchlets from human astrocytes and mouse Bergmann glia gives rise to distinct calcium signaling, demonstrating that fine-scale morphology critically shapes astroglial dynamics and must be accurately captured by simulation frameworks. In addition, notable differences emerge in geometry representation, implementation strategies, computational aspects, and usability of the tools. By highlighting key trade-offs between geometric fidelity, flexibility, and computational cost in modeling intracellular biochemical processes, these findings provide practical guidance for selecting appropriate simulation tools. More broadly, our results support the use of reaction–diffusion modeling in morphologically realistic astrocytic environments and contribute to enabling mechanistic studies of localized signaling events at synaptic and perisynaptic sites.

title: On real-time calibrated prediction for complex model-based decision support in pandemics: Part 1
abstract:
by Daniel Williamson, Trevelyan J. McKinley, Xiaoyu Xiong, James M. Salter, Robert Challen, Leon Danon, Ben Youngman, Doug McNeall 

Infectious disease models are used to predict the spread and impact of outbreaks of a disease. Like other complex models, they have parameters that need to be calibrated, and structural discrepancies from the reality that they simulate that should be accounted for in calibration and prediction. Whilst Uncertainty Quantification (UQ) techniques have been applied to infectious disease models before, they were not routinely used to inform policymakers in the UK during the COVID-19 pandemic. In this paper, we will argue that during a fast moving pandemic, models and policy are changing on timescales that make traditional UQ methods impractical, if not impossible to implement. We present an alternative formulation to the calibration problem that embeds model discrepancy within the structure of the model, and appropriately assimilates data within the simulation. We then show how UQ can be used to calibrate the model in real-time to produce disease trajectories accounting for parameter uncertainty and model discrepancy. We apply these ideas to an age-structured COVID-19 model for England and demonstrate the types of information it could have produced to feed into policy support prior to the lockdown of March 2020.

title: Chemogenomic profiling of diverse  Saccharomyces cerevisiae  strains using the novel CRISPR-Cas9 markerless barcoded library BarMix
abstract:
Background
                      Natural populations are rich reservoirs of genetic variation, and incorporating this diversity into functional genomic screens can reveal the genetic and phylogenetic determinants underlying trait differences. Genetic barcoding is a powerful tool for yeast functional genomics, enabling scalable fitness profiling and high-throughput gene-trait interaction mapping. Nevertheless, few barcoded libraries capture the natural diversity of  Saccharomyces cerevisiae . 
                  
                     Results
                      Here, we introduce BarMix, a novel barcoded library of diverse  S. cerevisiae  strains designed and validated for high-throughput fitness profiling. Using CRISPR-Cas9, we integrate distinct markerless genetic barcodes into the genomes of 262 strains representing multiple phylogenetic clades of wild, domesticated, and admixed origins. To evaluate its utility for genotype–phenotype mapping, we quantitatively profile the pooled library by barcode-sequencing against 33 small-molecule compounds with diverse bioactivities and identify 281 chemogenomic interactions through genome-wide association analysis. Chemical fitness signatures differ between domesticated and wild clades, particularly under stresses affecting ergosterol biosynthesis, DNA alkylation, microtubule depolymerisation, TORC1 inactivation, and membrane permeability. We validate seven associated alleles through allele-swap experiments, including variants in genes that modulate multidrug export (Yrr1), tRNA-specificity (ArgRS), and small-molecule methylation (Crg1). Several alleles display variable penetrance across strains, suggesting a complex genetic basis for trait variation. Importantly, including admixture into the genome-wide association design enhances variant detection in  S. cerevisiae . 
                  
                     Conclusions
                      These results establish BarMix as a powerful platform for genotype–phenotype discovery with diverse applications in functional genomics and biotechnology, and highlight the value of incorporating natural variation into model-systems biology.

title: Cell-type-specific explainable spatial features extracted from digitized H&E slides explain gene expression variability beyond cell-type composition
abstract: Cell-type composition and tissue architecture jointly influence gene expression patterns. Although single-cell and spatial transcriptomic technologies can characterize both factors, their cost limits widespread use. Bulk RNA deconvolution estimates cell-type composition but lacks spatial context. In contrast, routine H&E whole-slide images provide a scalable source of explainable cell-type-specific spatial features describing tissue architecture. However, the extent to which the spatial features explain gene expression variability beyond cell-type composition remains largely unknown, and in this study, we aim to address this gap. The study leveraged a dataset of 471 normal prostate tissue samples with bulk RNA gene expression and paired WSIs. The WSIs are processed for nuclei segmentation and cell-type classification to extract cell-type-specific proportions ( n  = 7) and spatial features ( n  = 38) reflective of local neighborhood and tissue architecture. We model the gene expression as a function of cell-type-specific features to assess their contribution to gene expression variability, and evaluate the incremental explanatory effect of spatial features over the cell type compositions. Likelihood ratio testing comparing the full model (cell-type-specific spatial and proportion features, with the proportions-only model serving as the null model) to the proportions-only model identified 2330 of 24,075 genes with significantly improved model fit after adjustment for multiple testing (FDR-adjusted p-value < 0.05). Among significant genes, the full model shows the highest ability to explain gene expression variability (median adjusted $$\:{R}^{2}$$ = 0.195 [IQR 0.122, 0.289]), compared to the spatial features only model (0.176 [0.109, 0.263]), and the proportions only model (0.068 [0.031, 0.128]). Finally, gene expression was modelled using XGBoost with cell-type-specific features. Feature importance analysis identified nine distinct, biologically relevant gene clusters and confirmed the regression-based results, with cell-type-specific spatial features contributing substantially to gene expression variability beyond cell-type composition. These findings demonstrate that explainable cell-type-specific spatial features derived from routine H&E slides capture transcriptionally relevant tissue architecture that is not reflected by cell-type composition alone. Such features provide a scalable and cost-effective approach for explaining gene expression variability in bulk tissue samples.

title: Preference-guided CT projection correction for surface-based feather morphometrics
abstract:
Background
                      Traditional imaging pipelines often optimize for human-readable images and generic quality metrics, but algorithm-facing morphometric workflows require preservation of the information used by downstream measurement. Acquisitions that appear overexposed or visually nonstandard may therefore be appropriate when they expose subtle structures to an analysis algorithm. We developed a task-aligned projection-correction framework for reducing morphology-relevant CT motion artifacts without relying on human visual interpretability as the final quality standard. 
                  
                     Results
                      Using CT-based feather morphometry as a motivating example, we treated a previously published feather-growth computer-vision workflow as the downstream task to be protected during correction. A residual denoising autoencoder defined a bounded projection-correction space, and an expert human-preference ranker scored candidate residual corrections for preservation of task-relevant morphology. In a five-scene synthetic proof-of-concept benchmark comprising four development seeds and one fully held-out seed, rank-weighted evolution-strategy updates optimized latent corrections under projection-preservation, latent-bound, and angular-smoothing constraints. The development-inclusive five-scene summary showed 67.9% lower reconstruction RMSE and 72.0% lower density-map RMSE than motion-corrupted data, with the fully held-out seed showing the same direction and similar magnitude of improvement. Preference-guided correction also outperformed a feed-forward residual-autoencoder baseline (reconstruction RMSE 0.00260 ± 0.00013; density-map RMSE 0.0500 ± 0.0021), whereas TomoPy joint reprojection alignment changed the principal morphology-error endpoints by approximately 1% or less under the local non-rigid feather-motion benchmark. Clean-data controls produced only small perturbations when no motion correction was needed. In two illustrative real-data case studies, the same framework reduced visible feather ghosting and improved downstream crest-density mapping and agreement with manual reference masks when inserted upstream of the published morphometric workflow. 
                  
                     Conclusions
                      These results support task-aligned projection correction as a route toward CT imaging workflows optimized for downstream biological measurement rather than generic visual image quality alone. The study provides proof-of-concept evidence that expert preference signals can guide bounded projection-domain correction for surface-based biological morphometrics.

title:
Natural Variation in
                     CYCLIC NUCLEOTIDE‐GATED ION CHANNEL 16 
                    Controls Fruit Weight in Tomato
authors:
Xiang Wang, 
Yixuan Huang, 
Huaiqi Miao, 
Ying Dai, 
Youwei Wang, 
Ziyuan Ding, 
Nanyi Li, 
Gang Wu
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Fruit weight is a crucial agronomic trait influencing yield and quality in tomato domestication. Although numerous quantitative trait loci (QTLs) controlling fruit weight have been reported, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain largely unresolved. Here, we identify natural variation in the promoter region of
                     CYCLIC NUCLEOTIDE‐GATED ION CHANNEL 
                    16 (
                     CNGC16 
                    ) associated with both fruit weight and gene expression differences via genome‐wide association study (GWAS) in tomato accessions. Geographical and subpopulation analyses reveal that the large‐fruit
                     CNGC16 
                    haplotype was selectively favoured during domestication and may contribute to local environmental adaptation. Functional assays demonstrate that
                     CNGC16 
                    regulates fruit weight by promoting cell division and maintaining cytosolic Ca
                     2+ 
                    homeostasis in fruit cells. Mechanistically, CNGC16 physically and genetically interacts with calmodulin 6 (CaM6) to mediate calcium signalling that controls fruit size. These findings uncover a novel calcium‐dependent pathway regulating tomato fruit weight and propose
                     CNGC16 
                    and
                     CaM6 
                    as promising molecular targets for crop improvement.

title:
DNA 
                    ‐Barcoded Polysaccharide Specific Monoclonal Antibodies Facilitate Sensitive and Multiplexed Detection of Cell Wall Polymers
authors:
C. Frankie Griffith, 
Michael G. Hahn, 
Ian S. Wallace
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Plant cell walls are polysaccharide‐rich extracellular matrices composed of multiple complex carbohydrate polymer networks, including cellulose, hemicelluloses, pectins, and glycosylated proteins. Polysaccharide deposition critically impacts cell wall structure, and structural microheterogeneity within cell wall glycans also influences polymer rigidity and polymer‐polymer interactions. Collections of monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) have been developed to target unique carbohydrate epitopes within cell wall polysaccharides and to investigate how these structural changes impact cellular and plant development. Here, we implement generalizable methods to attach unique DNA barcodes to mAbs that recognize major cell wall polysaccharide classes. By applying these mAbs individually to polysaccharide standards, we demonstrate that bound DNA barcoded antibody abundance can be measured via quantitative PCR. Additionally, we demonstrate that DNA‐conjugated antibodies can be pooled to quantitatively analyze polysaccharide epitope composition of polysaccharide standards and fractionated cell wall material by amplifying their unique barcodes via qPCR. These results demonstrate that barcoded polysaccharide‐directed mAbs offer sensitive, quantitative insights into cell wall polysaccharide composition and facilitate multiplexed profiling of cell wall polysaccharide abundance. This approach will also enable multiple future high‐throughput applications, such as glycome profiling, spatial glycomics, and glycan interaction measurements, that will further our understanding of cell wall compositional impacts on plant physiology.

title:
Spatiotemporal Transcriptomics Reveals That a ZF‐HD–
                     GmCWINV4 
                    Module Controls Carbon Partitioning and Seed Size in Soybean
authors:
Di Wu, 
Yiran Ding, 
Yang Tao, 
Xiaoyi Fu, 
Bing Han, 
Juan Song, 
Tianquan Yang, 
Tingshuang Yi, 
Wei Xu
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Seed size and oil content are key determinants of agronomic productivity in soybean (
                     
                       Glycine max 
                     
                    ). Although the ultrastructure and cellular composition of soybean seeds have been well characterised, the spatiotemporal expression patterns of genes governing sucrose transport and catabolism across distinct cell types remain poorly understood. Here, we present a high‐resolution spatiotemporal transcriptomic atlas of early soybean seed development, spanning the globular, heart, and cotyledon stages. We delineated 17 distinct cell types and identified 249 cell‐type marker genes. We further characterised the phloem region of the seed coat, a key compartment associated with sucrose transport and metabolism. Systematic profiling of sugar‐related genes revealed cluster‐specific and developmental stage‐dependent transcriptional patterns. We functionally characterised GmCWINV4, a phloem‐specific cell wall invertase that hydrolyses sucrose into glucose and fructose. Overexpression of
                     GmCWINV4 
                    substantially increased seed size, weight, and oil content in soybean. We also identified two zinc finger homeodomain (ZF‐HD) transcription factors, GmZF‐HD27 and GmZF‐HD36, that directly activate
                     GmCWINV4 
                    transcription by binding to ‘ATTA’ cis‐elements in its promoter. Moreover, we demonstrated that sucrose acts as an upstream signal that induces
                     GmZF‐HD36 
                    transcription in a dose‐dependent manner. Collectively, these findings provide a comprehensive spatiotemporal transcriptomic resource for studying soybean seed development and reveal a previously unreported ZF‐HD–
                     GmCWINV4 
                    regulatory module that modulates post‐phloem sucrose metabolism, thereby contributing to increased seed size and oil content. These findings offer mechanistic insights and potential targets for improving seed yield and nutritional quality in soybean.

title:
Lessons From
                     CABBI 
                    : Advancing Vegetative Oil Production in
                     
                      C
                       4 
                     
                    Crops Through a Vertically Integrated
                     DBTL 
                    Framework
authors:
Daniel Lunn, 
Kiyoul Park, 
Narendra Naik Deshavath, 
Jia Dong, 
Kankshita Swaminathan, 
Jeremy Guest, 
Andrew D. B. Leakey, 
Nathaniel M. Butler, 
Jorg Schwender, 
Vijay Singh, 
John Shanklin, 
Fredy Altpeter, 
Edgar B. Cahoon
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    The global demand for renewable liquid fuels and biobased chemicals has intensified interest in engineering high‐biomass C
                     4 
                    grasses to accumulate triacylglycerol (TAG) in vegetative tissues. Achieving this goal requires coordinated solutions across molecular biology, crop science, chemical engineering, and life cycle assessment, disciplines that rarely operate within a single research program. The Center for Advanced Bioenergy and Bioproducts Innovation (CABBI) was established to provide this integration through a Design–Build–Test–Learn (DBTL) framework applied to three C
                     4 
                    feedstocks: saccharum (
                     Saccharum 
                    spp. hybrids), sorghum (
                     
                       Sorghum bicolor 
                     
                    ), and miscanthus (
                     Miscanthus 
                     × 
                     giganteus 
                    ). Through iterative DBTL cycles, CABBI has produced transgenic saccharum and sorghum lines with substantially elevated levels of vegetative TAG, with multi‐location field trials having confirmed stable trait heritability and lipid yields. We have also leveraged our integration to develop a dual system biorefinery that co‐recovers vegetative lipids with fermentable sugars at levels sufficient to achieve industrial ethanol titres. Importantly, this fully integrated cross‐disciplinary data integration model has highlighted the key constraints currently preventing TAG‐rich vegetative oil from achieving commercial viability as: (i) active lipid turnover, (ii) photosynthetic trade‐offs, (iii) spatial misexpression, and (iv) bioprocessing challenges. CABBI uses emerging technologies, including biofoundry‐enabled construct screening, precision genome editing, and machine‐learning‐assisted regulatory design, to further accelerate DBTL cycles. More broadly, this work illustrates how integrative centre‐scale research that unites diverse expertise can accelerate discovery and translation, positioning these systems to expand agricultural markets and contribute to a more secure and resilient bioeconomy.

title: From fire injury to tree death: insights into the physiological mechanisms of postfire tree mortality
authors:
Raquel Partelli Feltrin, 
Daniel M. Johnson
abstract:
Conceptual framework linking fire injury to immediate and delayed physiological effects and postfire tree outcomes.







Summary
Fire injury can cause immediate tree death, but it can also initiate physiological changes that affect a tree's ability to recover and survive. The mechanisms linking these injuries to postfire recovery or mortality remain poorly understood. Fire‐induced injuries can disrupt tree carbon balance by reducing carbon acquisition, impairing carbohydrate transport, and increasing demands on nonstructural carbohydrates needed for recovery. Fire has also been hypothesized to cause mortality through hydraulic failure, although evidence for this mechanism in fire‐exposed trees remains limited. Emerging evidence suggests that interactions between carbon balance and water transport may jointly influence postfire tree outcomes. Here, we synthesize current understanding of how fire affects tree carbon balance and water transport and offer pathways for future research.

title:
A
                     RIN 
                    ‐
                     SlJMJ6 
                    transcriptional–epigenetic module activates carotenoid biosynthesis through
                     H3K27me3 
                    demethylation in tomato
authors:
Zhiwei Li, 
Yijie Zhou, 
Yahan Wang, 
Hanzhi Liang, 
Jiechun Peng, 
Hui Yang, 
Jing Zeng, 
Lu Xiao, 
Guoxiang Jiang, 
Keqiang Wu, 
Yueming Jiang, 
Xuewu Duan
abstract:
Summary 
                   
                     
                       
                         Fruit ripening involves extensive transcriptional and epigenetic reprogramming, yet how chromatin modifiers are targeted to specific genomic loci in coordination with transcription factors remains unclear. 
                       
                       
                         
                          Here, we show that the histone H3K27me3 demethylase SlJMJ6 physically and functionally associates with the master ripening regulator RIPENING INHIBITOR (RIN) to regulate carotenoid biosynthesis in tomato (
                           Solanum lycopersicum 
                          ) fruit.
                         
                       
                       
                         
                          Genetic and transcriptional analyses demonstrated that SlJMJ6 and RIN cooperatively promote carotenoid accumulation and activate key biosynthetic genes, including
                           PSY1 
                          ,
                           DXS1 
                          and
                           ZISO 
                          . Genome‐wide analyses revealed that SlJMJ6 preferentially binds promoter regions enriched in CArG motifs and extensively co‐occupies ripening‐associated genes with RIN. Epigenomic analyses showed that SlJMJ6 association correlates with reduced H3K27me3 enrichment at co‐targeted loci, whereas loss of either
                           SlJMJ6 
                          or
                           RIN 
                          increases H3K27me3 enrichment and reduces expression of ripening‐related genes. Furthermore, SlJMJ6 occupancy at representative target loci is markedly reduced in the
                           rin 
                          mutant, indicating that RIN facilitates SlJMJ6 chromatin association.
                         
                       
                       
                         Together, our findings reveal a cooperative RIN‐SlJMJ6 regulatory module linking RIN‐dependent transcriptional regulation with locus‐specific H3K27me3 dynamics, providing a mechanistic framework for chromatin‐mediated activation of metabolic genes during fruit ripening.

title: Root saprotropism: A tropism guided by environmental pH sensing
abstract: In saprotropism, roots perceive fungal‐derived acidic pH gradients via the RGF‐RGFR module to trigger asymmetric abscisic acid signaling, reorient microtubules, and drive root bending away from decay. Extracellular pH is a key convergence mode that mediates diverse plant‐microbe interactions.

title: The CsBLH9-CsOVATE module regulates heat tolerance via chlorophyll degradation in cucumber
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Heat stress has become a primary environmental factor that severely threatens crop yield and quality. Despite many genes having been identified to participate in heat response, natural alleles of heat response genes that can be utilized in crop breeding are scarce, and the underlying mechanisms remain enigmatic. In this study, we identified a BEL1-like Homeodomain (BLH) transcription factor CsBLH9, through genome-wide association study (GWAS), and demonstrated its positive role in heat response. The natural variants of CsBLH9 exhibit different levels of heat tolerance and differential response to gibberellin (GA) treatment. Knockout of CsBLH9 resulted in sensitive heat response and reduced chlorophyll levels. CsBLH9 can directly bind to the promoters of chlorophyll catabolic genes stay-green (CsSGR) and pheophorbide a oxygenase (CsPAO) to inhibit their expression. Furthermore, we identified CsOVATE as an interacting partner of CsBLH9 that also functions as a positive regulator of heat tolerance. Csovate mutants showed phenotypes similar to Csblh9 mutants under heat stress, and CsOVATE enhanced the CsBLH9-mediated inhibition of CsSGR and CsPAO expression. Therefore, our findings suggested that CsBLH9-CsOVATE acts as a module that regulates heat tolerance via chlorophyll degradation in cucumber, and the natural alleles of CsBLH9 provide new targets for crop improvement under heat stress.

title:
Trichoderma 
                    elicitor CP3 induces phosphorylation and nuclear export of SRP to enhance tomato resistance to gray mold
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Beneficial Trichoderma fungi enhance plant immunity, but the molecular mechanisms of elicitor-mediated immune priming are still not well defined. Here, we identified a cerato-platanin (CP) family elicitor, CP3, from T. asperellum that enhances tomato resistance to Botrytis cinerea. CP3 is secreted and localizes to the host nucleus, where it interacts with the tomato protein SRP. This interaction recruits casein kinase 1 to phosphorylate SRP at Ser-185, thereby triggering its nuclear export to the plasma membrane. Subsequently, SRP binds the ubiquinone biosynthesis protein COQ9, forming a signaling module that activates reactive oxygen species production and jasmonate/ethylene defense pathways to establish induced systemic resistance. Genetic disruption of CP3, SRP, or COQ9 abolishes CP3-induced resistance, confirming their essential roles. Our findings reveal a complete CP3–SRP–COQ9 signaling axis through which a beneficial fungal elicitor reprograms host nucleocytoplasmic trafficking to activate tailored immunity, offering new molecular targets for engineering disease-resistant crops.

title: Multi-omics profiling reveals common and specific molecular responses to butenolide perception
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Strigolactones (SLs) and Karrikins (KARs) are butenolide compounds that have been characterized to act like phytohormones. While SLs are synthesized endogenously in plants from carotenoids, KARs are a known constituent of wildfire smoke emanating from the combustion of carbohydrates in burning plant tissues. Despite their different sources of origin, they have similar chemical structures and are perceived through similar receptor complexes. However, the compound-specific molecular pathways downstream of these two signalling molecules remains to be elucidated. Hereby, we adopt an integrated approach combining transcriptome, proteome, proteogenome and metabolome profiling to compare the molecular responses of seeds and seedlings to the synthetic strigolactone analog, rac-GR24 and to the karrikinolide, KAR1 in Arabidopsis seeds or seedlings. This multi-omics approach allowed us to delineate the key conserved, and compound-specific, regulators such as transcription factors, splicing-related proteins, and primary metabolites that could play important functional roles in establishing the signaling response to these butenolides. Correlational analysis suggested differential splicing and metabolite regulation in response to rac-GR24 and KARs suggesting potential molecular targets including the TCA cycle. Treatment of mutants of key enzymes of energy metabolism, identified in the above studies, revealed that these mutants showed altered metabolic responses to butenolide treatment. In summary, our integrative dataset reveals strong associations between butenolide treatment and TCA cycle related changes across multiple molecular levels, and provides a foundation for generating testable hypotheses on how these signals interface with energy metabolism.

title: The Plant Ubiquitin System: From Identification of E2 and E3 enzymes to Molecular Mechanisms and Biological Function
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Ubiquitination is an essential post-translation modification involved in almost every cellular process and is critical for proper functioning of eukaryotic cells. The modification involves the covalent attachment of ubiquitin, a small, conserved peptide, to select proteins. One or more ubiquitin molecules may be attached in varying configurations, leading to a range of possible outcomes that regulate protein function, including changes in location, stability, and activity. Components of the ubiquitin system are highly expanded in plants relative to other eukaryotes and play major roles in almost all aspects of plant growth and development, from phytohormone perception and signalling, to maintaining nutrient homeostasis in the face of fluctuating environmental conditions. 
                   We begin this Centennial Review by highlighting two Plant Physiology papers that contributed to the identification and characterisation of ubiquitin enzymes. We then provide an update on our understanding of how plants use the ubiquitin system to link environmental change with plant growth and development. We first focus on recent advances in understanding how the structure and function of ubiquitin ligases are modulated by phytohormones and nutrient status. We then highlight emerging knowledge linking components of the ubiquitin system with biomolecular condensates, including stress granules, and discuss the potential functional implications.

title: Class III chitinases in Medicago truncatula facilitate arbuscular mycorrhizal symbiosis with Rhizophagus intraradices
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Plant chitinases are important defense enzymes in plant-microbe interactions and also participate in nodule symbiosis between legumes and nitrogen-fixing rhizobia. However, the roles of chitinases in arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) symbiosis remain incompletely defined. In this study, we characterized two class III chitinase genes in the legume Medicago truncatula (ecotype R108), namely MtCHIT3e and MtCHIT3f. Heterologous expression in Nicotiana benthamiana confirmed hydrolytic activity toward colloidal chitin, a fluorogenic chitooligosaccharide substrate, chitooligosaccharides, and lipo-chitooligosaccharides. In M. truncatula roots inoculated with AM fungi, transcripts of the two genes were significantly upregulated. Analysis of M. truncatula hairy roots transformed with promoter–β-glucuronidase constructs indicated strong induction of MtCHIT3e and MtCHIT3f promoter activity in response to applied chitooligosaccharide and lipo-chitooligosaccharide signals. Furthermore, fluorescent protein fusions localized the chitinases predominantly to the apoplast of host cells during AM colonization. Tnt1 insertion mutants in the chitinase genes exhibited reduced AM colonization, whereas nodule formation induced by Sinorhizobium meliloti was unaffected. Together, these results support a role for class III chitinases in promoting AM symbiosis and provide genetic evidence that they are required for optimal root colonization by AM fungi.

title: Maize endonuclease NOB1 couples ribosome biogenesis with translational regulation during kernel development
abstract:
Abstract 
                   NOB1-mediated cleavage of 20S pre-rRNA represents a critical quality-control step during cytoplasmic maturation of the eukaryotic 40S ribosomal subunit, yet its developmental significance in crops remains largely unexplored. Here, we identified two highly conserved maize NOB1 paralogs, ZmNOB1a and ZmNOB1b, both exhibiting RNA-binding and endonuclease activities and associating with pre-40S ribosomal particles. Genetic analyses demonstrated that the two paralogs function redundantly, but with unequal contributions, to support gametophyte viability and kernel development. Simultaneous disruption of ZmNOB1 activity resulted in severely impaired male gametophyte transmission, markeldly reduced female gamete viability, and profound defects in embryo and endosperm development. Molecular analyses further revealed widespread disruption of pre-rRNA maturation, including defective D-site cleavage, accompanied by impaired ribosome assembly and reduced translational capacity. Consistent with these molecular defects, mutant kernels exhibited decreased starch and storage protein accumulation, together with elevated levels of free ribosomal subunits and reduced 80S monosomes and polysomes. Moreover, ZmNOB1 exhibited co-sedimentation and directly interacted with the translation initiation factor eIF4A, implying a potential functional coordination between late ribosome maturation and translation initiation. Collectively, our findings establish ZmNOB1-mediated pre-rRNA processing as a key determinant of translational competence, reproductive fitness, and seed filling in maize.

title:
Promoter variation in
                     BraHDAC1 
                    modulates stomatal regulation and thermotolerance in
                     Brassica rapa
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Heat stress severely limits the productivity of Brassica rapa, a key vegetable crop worldwide. Deciphering the genetic basis of thermotolerance is essential for developing climate-resilient cultivars. By integrating genome-wide association studies (GWAS) with bulked segregant analysis (BSA), we identified two single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP1 and SNP2) in the promoter of the histone deacetylase gene BraHDAC1, which underlies natural variation in heat tolerance. These SNPs create a functional ABRE-CE cis-regulatory module exclusively in thermotolerant haplotypes (Hap1 and Hap3), enabling heat-induced transcription via binding of the transcription factor BraAREB1. Enhanced BraHDAC1 activity in turn represses the pectin methylesterase (PME) gene BraPME1 through histone H3K9/K14 deacetylation at its promoter. This repression, together with the coordinated regulation of additional PME and pectin methylesterase inhibitors (PMEI) genes, is associated with altered total PME activity and broader changes in pectin methylesterification, which may contribute to temporal stomatal regulation. This regulation involves early stomatal opening and increased transpiration associated with lower leaf temperature, consistent with enhanced transpirational cooling, followed by later closure to conserve water. Our findings define a BraAREB1-BraHDAC1 regulatory module in which BraPME1 is one functionally validated downstream target, illustrating how a cis-regulatory variation coordinates transcriptional, epigenetic, and cell wall modification responses to heat stress. The SNP and its associated regulatory module provide direct targets for marker-assisted breeding and genetic improvement of thermotolerant B. rapa.

title: Low ambient temperatures regulate Arabidopsis abscisic acid signaling and seed germination via CBFs–ABI3/ABI5–ICE1 interactions
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Seed germination is profoundly influenced by diverse environmental stimuli (e.g., temperatures), but the associated underlying molecular mechanisms remain largely uncharacterized. In this study, we demonstrated that low ambient temperatures, such as 16°C, suppress Arabidopsis thaliana seed germination, with endogenous abscisic acid (ABA) signaling revealed as a critical part of the underlying mechanism. The germination suppression and ABA response regulation by low ambient temperatures require ABSCISIC ACID INSENSITIVE3 (ABI3) and ABI5, two indispensable transcriptional activators in the ABA signaling pathway. In-depth analyses demonstrated physical associations between ABI3/ABI5 and low-temperature-responsive C-REPEAT BINDING FACTOR1 (CBF1), CBF2, and CBF3 (i.e., CBFs). Genetic evidence confirms that CBFs are essential for low-temperature- and ABA-mediated germination repression. Furthermore, CBFs and ABI3/ABI5 synergistically mediate the inhibitory effects of both low temperatures and ABA on germination. Mechanistically, these factors reciprocally enhance each other's transcriptional activities and promoter enrichment at downstream target genes. Notably, CBFs also directly bind INDUCER OF CBF EXPRESSION1 (ICE1), establishing an antagonistic regulatory axis with ABI5. Collectively, our findings underscore the critical modulatory effects of low ambient temperatures on ABA signaling and seed germination, thereby elucidating the mechanism by which the CBFs–ABI3/ABI5–ICE1 module functions as a signal transducer that converts environmental stimuli into endogenous hormone signals.

title: A polymer-embedded molecular fuse for safer high-nickel lithium batteries
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Thermal runaway in high-energy lithium batteries is driven by autocatalytic radical reactions and flammable gas accumulation, posing a critical safety bottleneck for next-generation energy storage. Here we report a cathode-integrated polymeric molecular fuse enabling thermally responsive safety control without compromising electrochemical performance. By tuning inductive and hyperconjugative effects of phosphonate side chains, the dissociation energy of sacrificial P–C bonds is regulated, yielding an ∼10°C shift in activation temperature, as supported by density functional theory and in situ variable-temperature Raman spectroscopy. Upon activation, P-centered radicals suppress exothermic chain reactions, achieving a 76% reduction in heat release and delaying thermal runaway in LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 cathodes and 0.6 Ah Li-metal pouch cells. Notably, the activation threshold exceeds typical cathode processing temperatures, preventing premature radical generation during fabrication while enabling on-demand safety activation. This work establishes a substituent-regulated molecular fuse that couples fabrication-compatible stability with triggerable intrinsic safety, transforming battery thermal management from passive suppression to controllable molecular-level reaction pathways.

title: Photocatalytic harvesting of oxygen atoms from carbon dioxide
scEvoSel maps evolutionary selection signals onto single-cell transcriptomic atlases to reveal selection-relevant cellular contexts
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Selection is a core driving force of evolution. Although genome-wide scanning can identify numerous genomic regions affected by selection, it remains challenging to further reveal the specific cellular contexts in which these selection signals act. To address this issue, we developed scEvoSel, an analytical framework that integrates population-level selection signals with single-cell RNA sequencing data to identify selection-relevant cell types. We calculated DCMS scores based on the population variation data from wild boars and domestic pigs and mapped them to the single-cell atlas of skeletal muscle from wild boars and Duroc pigs. The results showed that scEvoSel accurately identified fibro-adipogenic progenitors (FAPs) and myocytes, which exhibited significant changes in cell proportions, as well as lymphoid cells, which showed breed-associated transcriptional divergence. Moreover, we also calculated DCMS scores derived from population variation data of red junglefowl and Leghorn chickens and mapped them to the single-cell atlas of the liver of Leghorn chicken. Hepatocytes, endothelial cells, Kupffer cells and B cells were identified by scEvoSel as the primary selection-relevant cell types. Additionally, scEvoSel enables the analysis of key genes and functional pathways affected by selection within the corresponding cellular contexts. Overall, scEvoSel provides a framework for resolving population selection signals at single-cell resolution, expands the research dimensions for functional interpretation of selection signals, and offers a methodological tool for investigating cellular contexts associated with selection-driven evolutionary processes and complex trait formation.

title: Genome shock in a migratory songbird hybrid zone
abstract:
Abstract 
                   The genome shock hypothesis proposes that hybridization destabilizes genome regulation, leading to increased chromatin accessibility, derepression of transposable elements (TEs), and potential reductions in hybrid fitness, contributing to speciation. While extensively studied in plants, evidence in vertebrates is limited. Here, we tested this hypothesis in a hybrid zone between two subspecies of Swainson’s thrushes (Catharus ustulatus). We quantified genome-wide TE proportions, TE expression, and chromatin accessibility during both the migratory and non-migratory state using whole genome resequencing, RNA-seq, and ATAC-seq data from two migration-associated brain regions. Hybrids exhibited greater TE proportions, expression, and chromatin accessibility than parental lineages, providing the first direct evidence for genome shock in a wild avian system. TE expression and chromatin accessibility were positively correlated in all states and brain regions, but the strength of these patterns differed between states and tissues indicating that genome shock is context-dependent. Signatures of shock were localized in regulatory regions and associated with differential transcript factor binding sites linked to retinoic acid receptor signaling, a key pathway for seasonal and photoperiodic responses. Overlap between open chromatin, upregulated TEs and previously identified transgressively expressed genes in these hybrids suggest that genome shock extends beyond TE activation to directly affect gene expression. Our results motivate further investigation into genome shocks’ effects on genomic incompatibilities, hybrid fitness, and speciation.

title: Profile of Barbara Sherwood Lollar
abstract: In a laboratory nearly 2.4 kilometers under the Canadian Shield, geochemist Barbara Sherwood Lollar has tracked the sustained release of enough hydrogen gas from Earth’s crust to produce 4.7 million kilowatt-hours of energy per year. Elected to the National Academy of Sciences in 2022, Sherwood Lollar revisited the Kidd Creek Mine in Ontario, Canada where, in 2013, her explorations found that waters flowing from deep fractures were 1.6 billion years old. Reported in her Inaugural Article, the findings, aided by studies of noble gases in the samples, pushed the age of Earth’s oldest waters back by hundreds of millions of years.

title: Toward holistic reform of researcher assessment and incentives at US academic institutions
Quantifying ancient architecture: Stone-level machine learning reveals architectural variation and settlement growth at Shivta
abstract: Built environments provide durable evidence for how ancient settlements were organized, expanded, and transformed over time. Yet quantitative approaches to documenting architectural variability are generally labor-intensive, limited to individual structures, or dependent on aggregate volumetric estimates. We present a scalable, machine-learning-based framework that shifts the unit of analysis to the individual building stone and combines two complementary datasets: low-altitude drone imagery of surface remains and close-range photographs of standing walls. Applied to the Late Antique settlement of Shivta in the Negev Desert, the method automatically digitized approximately 235,000 surface stones and 12,000 stones in 604 walls, quantifying stone size, shape regularity, and masonry arrangement across walls, households, insulae, and the settlement as a whole.
