title: PHGDH‐Mediated Serine Metabolism in Nucleus Pulposus Cells Is a Potential Therapeutic Target for Intervertebral Disc Degeneration
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is a major cause of low back pain, driven largely by nucleus pulposus cell (NPC) senescence under chronic hypoxia and nutrient stress. Serine metabolism regulates senescence, but its role in IVDD remains unclear. Here, transcriptomic profiling reveals that the glycine–serine–threonine pathway is downregulated in senescent NPCs, with marked reduction of the serine synthesis rate limiting enzyme PHGDH. This is confirmed by single cell RNA sequencing of human discs, aged rat tissues, and degenerated human samples, accompanied by decreased intracellular serine. PHGDH silencing or serine deprivation inhibits NPC proliferation, induces senescence, and suppresses matrix anabolism. Mechanistically, PHGDH deficiency lowers α ketoglutarate, impairing histone demethylation and increasing H3K27me3 occupancy at the Rap1b promoter, which silences Rap1b and activates mTORC1, thereby blocking autophagic flux. Additionally, serine starvation depletes glutathione, elevates ROS, and promotes apoptosis. In vivo, AAV mediated PHGDH overexpression alleviates puncture induced IVDD, while a serine deficient diet exacerbates degeneration. Collectively, we uncover a PHGDH/Rap1b/mTORC1/autophagy cascade linking serine deprivation to NPC senescence, and propose that restoring PHGDH or serine availability may be a viable strategy to combat age related disc degeneration.

title: Stroke‐Heart Syndrome: Mechanisms, Temporal Phenotypes, and Diagnostic Reasoning
authors:
Fa Lin, 
Jian Lyu, 
Yanci Liu, 
Zhiyuan Feng, 
Jie Bao, 
Wenxiong Song, 
Bingcheng Zhu, 
Minghao Liu, 
Jionghao Xue, 
Jiadi Weng, 
Jiani Zhang, 
Jizong Zhao, 
Xiaolin Chen, 
Bin Dong
abstract:
Stroke‐heart syndrome describes new or worsened cardiac abnormalities after acute stroke. This Review defines its clinical boundaries, traces autonomic, inflammatory, endothelial, and supply‐demand mechanisms across time, and proposes provisional phenotypes that integrate lesion location, premorbid cardiac substrate, serial biomarkers, electrocardiography, and imaging. The framework supports safer differentiation from primary cardiac disease and more individualized monitoring and management.








ABSTRACT
Stroke‐heart syndrome (SHS) encompasses new or worsened cardiac abnormalities that arise after acute stroke, most often within the first 30 days and with an early peak. Its spectrum includes acute myocardial injury, electrocardiographic changes, arrhythmia, ventricular dysfunction, Takotsubo syndrome, and heart failure, but similar findings may reflect antecedent cardiac disease or systemic illness. This Review defines the accepted clinical boundaries of SHS and integrates central autonomic network disruption, neuroendocrine stress, inflammation, endothelial and microvascular dysfunction, oxygen supply‐demand imbalance, and premorbid substrate into a time‐resolved framework. Eight provisional, non‐mutually‐exclusive phenotypic domains are proposed to organize current evidence without implying validated endotypes. A diagnostic approach based on symptom chronology, prior cardiac data, serial troponin and electrocardiography, rhythm monitoring, echocardiography, selective coronary assessment, and cardiac magnetic resonance is presented to distinguish stroke‐triggered injury from recent myocardial infarction, pre‐existing atrial fibrillation, chronic myocardial injury, and established heart failure. No syndrome‐specific treatment is validated; care should prioritize recognized cardiac emergencies, correction of reversible stressors, and coordinated stroke‐cardiology decision‐making. Prospective studies with documented premorbid status, standardized time points, and blinded adjudication are needed to validate the proposed phenotypes and determine whether they improve outcomes.

title: A Bi‐Adjuvant Senolytic Nanovaccine Modulating Dendritic Cell Senescence Ameliorates Aging‐Related Metabolic Dysfunction
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Senolytic vaccines hold promise for eliminating senescent cells, but their efficacy is limited by poor seno‐antigen immunogenicity and age‐related dendritic cell (DC) dysfunction. Here, we engineered an active biomaterial‐enabled bi‐adjuvant senolytic nanovaccine (CK5‐GC‐NV) by co‐assembling CpG oligodeoxynucleotide with a fusion protein of the seno‐antigen Gpnmb and a cationic spider silk protein variant (CK5). Beyond antigen delivery, the CK5 scaffold acts as an intrinsic senomodulator associated with the downregulation of mitotic kinases Aurka/b and a concomitant decrease in senescence‐associated PI3K/AKT phosphorylation in DCs. This intervention attenuates aged DC phenotypes, restores antigen cross‐presentation, and synergizes with CpG to elicit potent cytotoxic T‐lymphocyte responses against senescent targets. Across multiple aging mouse models, CK5‐GC‐NV immunization orchestrated targeted clearance of Gpnmb
                     + 
                    senescent adipocytes, profoundly ameliorating metabolic dysfunction and extending lifespan. This multifunctional biomaterial platform integrates seno‐antigen immunogenicity enhancement with the restoration of aged DC function, providing a promising proof‐of‐concept for antigen‐directed gerotherapeutics.

title: ReLink: Reliable Deep Learning for Microscopic Motion Tracking
authors:
Yuan Jiang, 
Xiaochen Feng, 
Hongda Wei, 
Hao Sha, 
Hongpeng Wang, 
Min Zhang, 
Sanyang Han, 
Yongbing Zhang
abstract:
ReLink enables reliable trajectory linking in single‐particle tracking by integrating physics‐informed motion statistics with confidence‐based adaptive filtering. Across diverse simulated and experimental conditions, ReLink robustly reconstructs trajectories and preserves the fidelity of downstream analyses, enabling accurate characterization of microscopic dynamics from physically verifiable free diffusion to complex intracellular anomalous diffusion.








ABSTRACT
Single‐particle tracking (SPT) serves as a fundamental technique for deciphering complex microscopic dynamics in biological and physical systems by resolving trajectories of individual particles. However, linking localizations into trajectories remains challenging in realistic experiments, where crowding, blinking, and localization errors lead to linking ambiguity. Both statistical and deep‐learning approaches have been explored in these conditions, yet reliable link selection that generalizes across varying data distributions remains elusive. Here, we propose ReLink, a general deep‐learning framework for reliable trajectory linking in SPT. By integrating physical priors into geometric representations and leveraging confidence‐based adaptive filtering at inference, ReLink enables automated selection of trustworthy linkages, thereby preserving the fidelity of downstream trajectory‐based analyses. Across challenging simulated scenarios spanning broad experimental conditions and motion regimes, ReLink consistently outperforms representative statistical and deep learning‐based trajectory linking methods in both edge‐level and trajectory‐level evaluation metrics, leading to markedly improved downstream inference on public benchmarks. We further validate ReLink on diverse real‐world experiments, from free diffusion systems to crowded intracellular environments, demonstrating its practical significance for quantitative interpretation of microscopic dynamics and its promise for next‐generation trustworthy and automated SPT.

title: A Mechanistic Dissection of Multifaceted Complement Attack in Age‐Related Macular Degeneration Reveals the Superiority of C3 Inhibition
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Age‐related macular degeneration (AMD) is the leading cause of irreversible central vision loss in the elderly, and geographic atrophy (GA) represents its advanced atrophic form. While C5 and C3 inhibitors have shown efficacy in slowing GA progression, the precise pathogenic roles of individual complement effectors and the optimal inhibition strategy remain subjects of ongoing debate. This study employs an in vitro model using A2E‐laden retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) cells and normal human serum to systematically investigate complement‐mediated RPE degeneration and compare the protective effects of different complement‐targeting strategies. We demonstrate that C5 blockade, while preventing lytic cell death caused by the membrane attack complex (MAC), fails to fully restore mitochondrial function or prevent phagolysosomal damage. Crucially, these C5‐independent pathologies involve C3 activation products. In contrast, upstream C3 inhibition comprehensively protects RPE cells by ameliorating these diverse pathological processes. Our findings provide a detailed mechanistic understanding of complement‐driven RPE degeneration and support a mechanistic rationale for an upstream C3‐targeting strategy in GA secondary to AMD.

title:
Interface‐Confined Cavitation at an MXene/TiO
                     2 
                    Schottky Heterointerface for Non‐Thermal Juice Preservation
authors:
Xiaoge Wu, 
Yunxiao Zhu, 
Nan Qin, 
Zhaoli Zhang, 
Qi Zhang, 
Yang Tao
abstract:
This work establishes an MXene/TiO 2  Schottky heterointerface for non-thermal sonocatalysis. Interface-confined cavitation and dynamic Ti 3 
 + /V₀ shuttles drive charge transport and reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. The platform achieves 3-log pathogen reduction while retaining heat-labile nutrients in complex food matrices, redefining sonocatalyst design.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Non-thermal food preservation demands catalytic platforms that achieve potent antimicrobial efficacy without compromising heat-labile nutrients. Yet whether a sonocatalyst merely seeds bubble nucleation or actively channels transiently concentrated acoustic energy into chemical work has remained unresolved, and the violent, opaque nature of cavitation further precludes operando observation of catalyst surfaces. Herein, an MXene/TiO 2  Schottky heterointerface is engineered with the aim of localizing cavitation collapse at the catalyst-liquid boundary through three cooperatively acting determinants: a built-in electric field for charge separation, hierarchical surface roughness for energy focusing, and pre-existing oxygen vacancies for dynamic defect modulation. A convergent multi-proxy evidence chain, comprising passive cavitation imaging, single-bubble computational fluid dynamics, chronoamperometry, quasi-in situ spectroscopy, and ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), supports a working model of this interface-confined cavitation regime. Under 40 kHz ultrasound without external heating, the interface delivers 3-log inactivation of the tested indicator bacteria ( E. coli  and  S. aureus ) at the laboratory scale, while preserving 82% of vitamin C and 88% of total anthocyanin content in juice. This work thus proposes interface-confined cavitation as a transferable design rationale for sonocatalytic interfaces, with operando validation of the active interface as the decisive next step.

title: Single‐Nucleus RNA Sequencing Identifies CREM as a Brake on Myofiber Hypertrophy in Chickens
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Myofiber hypertrophy is central to economically important agricultural traits and vertebrate development, yet the underlying cellular and molecular programs remain elusive. Chickens have undergone substantial divergence in muscle growth following decades of artificial selection, making them a unique model for dissecting these mechanisms at single‐cell resolution. Here, we performed singlenucleus RNA sequencing on 91 144 nuclei from postnatal chicken pectoralis major. Eight major conserved cell populations were resolved, with temporal dynamics exhibiting divergence between fast‐growing broilers and slow‐growing layers. A novel terminally differentiated myocyte subpopulation (
                     AK1 
                     + 
                    myocytes) was markedly enriched in slow‐growing birds. Analysis revealed that accelerated myoblast expansion and delayed terminal differentiation are primary drivers of myofiber hypertrophy, supported by a pro‐growth niche involving IGF‐signaling FAPs and macrophage‐myogenic crosstalk. Further comprehensive analyses identified CREM as a master repressor of myofiber hypertrophy. Mechanistically, CREM directly binds and transcriptionally activates the
                     JUN 
                    promoter, and both factors cooperatively sustain the expression of growth inhibitors MSTN, FBXO32, and TRIM63. In vivo and in vitro functional validation confirmed that CREM deletion promotes myofiber hypertrophy, increasing pectoralis major weight and percent by 29.96% and 20.50%, respectively. This study uncovers CREM as a novel brake on myofiber hypertrophy, offering fundamental insights into vertebrate skeletal muscle development.

title: STRIDE: A Sequencing Depth Robust Metric for Sparse Chromosome Conformation Capture Data Comparison
authors:
Bingxiang Xu, 
Xiaomeng Gao, 
Weichu Tao, 
Zhihua Zhang, 
Feifei Li
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   High‐throughput chromatin conformation capture technologies, such as Hi‐C and its derivatives, have revolutionized the study of 3D genome organization. However, the robustness of contact‐frequency‐based analyses to sequencing depth remains a major challenge, particularly for sparse datasets such as single‐cell Hi‐C. To overcome this challenge, we present a novel computational framework that employs the mean first passage time (MFPT) from Markov chain theory to convert chromatin contact matrices into a graph‐based effective distance representation. We demonstrate that the MFPT representation is empirically more robust to sequencing‐depth reduction and supports reliable downstream 3D genomic analyses, including TAD and chromatin loop detection, differential chromatin contact analysis, as well as the imputation and representation of sparse single‐cell Hi‐C data. Building on this representation, we developed STRIDE (spatial topological representation of interaction distance evaluation), a library similarity metric that does not require dataset‐specific parameter optimization. STRIDE is robust to sparse and noisy data and shows improved resilience to technical variation, thereby facilitating accurate identification of cellular states and developmental trajectories in the datasets analyzed. Together, the MFPT representation and STRIDE provide a robust computational framework for sequencing‐depth‐resilient analysis of 3D genome organization.

title: Disrupted Top‐Down Modulation as a Mechanism of Impaired Multisensory Processing in Autistic Children
Propofol Modulates Fear Memory Reconsolidation by Inhibiting D2 Receptor‐Expressing Neurons in the Medial Prefrontal Cortex
authors:
Jie Li, 
Yi‐Ge Guo, 
Xing Xu, 
Gui‐Lin Meng, 
Han Li, 
Liu‐Wei Chu, 
Xin‐Yuan Chen, 
Xiao‐Yun Guo, 
Tao Xu, 
Ti‐Fei Yuan, 
Ji Hu, 
Xiao‐Na Zhu
abstract:
This study shows that propofol modulates fear-memory reconsolidation in mice. It works by suppressing D2 receptor-expressing neurons within the medial prefrontal cortex and their connections to the basolateral amygdala. D2-receptor agonists reproduce this fear-reducing effect, offering potential non-anesthetic therapeutic strategies for trauma-related fear disorders.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Fear memory reconsolidation provides a temporal window for modifying established fear memories, yet the underlying cellular and neural circuit mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Using in vivo fiber photometry and chemogenetic approaches in freely moving mice, we show that propofol modulates fear memory reconsolidation by inhibiting D2 receptor-expressing neurons in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC). These neurons exhibit heightened activity during fear memory reconsolidation and project prominently to the basolateral amygdala (BLA). Notably, local pharmacological activation of D2 receptors in the mPFC recapitulates the fear-attenuating effect of propofol when administered during the reconsolidation window. Circuit-level investigations further show that propofol suppresses the reconsolidation-associated enhancement of the mPFC D2 -BLA synaptic transmission, and chemogenetic activation of this projection counteracts the effect of propofol on fear memory reconsolidation. Moreover, selective knockdown of D2 receptors in BLA-projecting mPFC neurons diminishes the effect of propofol, supporting a critical role for D2 receptor signaling within this projection-defined circuit. Together, these findings identify the mPFC D2 -BLA circuit as a key neural substrate through which propofol modulates fear memory reconsolidation and highlight prefrontal D2 receptor signaling as a potential target for reconsolidation-based interventions aimed at maladaptive fear memories.

title: DUSP26 Regulated by YY1 Lactylation Couples Osteogenesis and Angiogenesis by Dephosphorylating PMPCB at Y141 and Activating Mitophagy in BMSCs
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) support bone formation through osteogenic differentiation and pro‐angiogenic paracrine activity, but the mechanisms coordinating these functions remain incompletely understood. Here, we identified dual‐specificity phosphatase 26 (DUSP26) as a regulator of BMSC osteogenesis and mitochondrial homeostasis. DUSP26 expression increased during osteogenic differentiation and was reduced in osteoporotic femoral tissues. p300 gain‐ and loss‐of‐function experiments, together with analysis of the Yin Yang1(YY1) K183R mutant, supported the conclusion that p300‐regulated YY1 lactylation contributes to DUSP26 transcriptional activation. DUSP26 interacted with the mitochondrial processing peptidase subunit beta(PMPCB) and reduced its tyrosine phosphorylation, with mass spectrometry and mutational analyses implicating Y141 as involved in this regulation. Functional assays supported a model in which DUSP26 limits mitochondrial processing peptidase (MPP)‐mediated PTEN‐induced kinase 1 (PINK1) processing and promotes PINK1‐dependent mitophagy, thereby supporting mitochondrial homeostasis. DUSP26 enhanced osteogenic differentiation and the pro‐angiogenic activity of BMSC‐conditioned medium(CM), whereas its knockdown impaired bone formation and reduced type H vessels in vivo. Furthermore, BMSC‐derived exosomes carrying a runt‐related transcription factor 2 (RUNX2) promoter‐driven DUSP26 plasmid produced preferential transgene expression in osteogenic‐lineage cells and attenuated ovariectomy‐induced bone loss in mice. These findings link lactylation‐associated transcriptional regulation to mitochondrial protein processing and support further preclinical evaluation of DUSP26‐directed approaches for osteoporosis.

title: Phase‐Programmed Microneedles Enable Sequential Hydrogen and Quercetin Release for Scar‐Reduced Regeneration of Burn Wounds
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Burn wounds complicated by bacterial infection and fibrotic scarring remain a major clinical challenge, demanding therapeutics capable of coordinated infection control, inflammation modulation, and tissue regeneration. Here, we report a phase‐programmed microneedle (MN) patch (QR/AB‐MNs) that enables spatiotemporally controlled release of ammonia borane (AB) and quercetin (QR) to achieve synergistic antimicrobial and anti‐fibrotic therapy. The MNs comprise a poly (lactic‐co‐glycolic acid) (PLGA) shell encapsulating QR and a sulfobutylether‐β‐cyclodextrin (SBECD) core loaded with the H
                     2 
                    ‐releasing prodrug AB. Upon exposure to the mildly acidic wound microenvironment, the system triggers sustained generation of hydrogen (H
                     2 
                    ) and AB degradation products, effectively eliminating bacteria and biofilms while mitigating oxidative stress. Subsequently, gradual PLGA degradation ensures prolonged QR release, suppressing fibroblast hyperproliferation and TGF‐
                     β 
                    mediated collagen deposition, thereby preventing hypertrophic scarring. In murine and rabbit burn models, QR/AB‐MNs markedly accelerated wound closure, reduced inflammation and bacterial burden, restored skin appendages, and yielded scar‐reduced regeneration with native‐like collagen architecture. Transcriptomic profiling further revealed that QR/AB‐MNs orchestrate a broad anti‐fibrotic transcriptional program, concurrently attenuating pro‐fibrotic signaling, cell‐extracellular matrix interactions, and collagen synthesis. Collectively, this programmable MN platform integrates redox modulation, anti‐infective therapy, and matrix remodeling to achieve comprehensive, scarless‐like healing of infected burn wounds.

title: Lactate Homeostasis Disruption Potentiates TACE‐Immunotherapy in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Developing strategies that simultaneously overcome chemoresistance and immune suppression remains a major challenge for improving transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Inspired by clinically used CaCO
                     3 
                    microspheres in TACE, we propose an “extracellular buffering‐intracellular metabolic disruption” strategy to precisely regulate lactate homeostasis for targeted therapy. Herein, we engineered multifunctional embolic microspheres (SDCa‐MSs) co‐loaded with calcium carbonate nanoparticles (CaNPs), syrosingopine (Syr), and doxorubicin (DOX) for TACE application. Within the acidic tumor microenvironment, SDCa‐MSs buffer extracellular acidity while disrupting intracellular lactate metabolism, thereby simultaneously remodeling extracellular and intracellular pH homeostasis. This coordinated regulation enhances DOX efficacy, induces calcium dyshomeostasis and immunogenic cell death, and ultimately stimulates robust antitumor immunity. In multiple murine HCC models, SDCa‐MSs markedly suppress tumor growth, remodel the tumor immune microenvironment, and synergistically enhance the therapeutic efficacy of anti‐PD‐L1 immunotherapy. By integrating metabolic regulation, chemotherapy, and immune activation into a single embolic platform, this work establishes an acid–base homeostasis‐regulating strategy for potentiating TACE and provides a conceptual framework for improving locoregional cancer immunotherapy.

title: Ischemic Postconditioning Protects Aged Myocardium Against Ischemia/Reperfusion Injury by Regulating Mitochondrial Dynamics via piR‐4913
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Ischemic postconditioning (IPostC) mitigates myocardial ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury, but its regulation of mitochondrial dynamics in the aged heart remains unclear. This study investigates the underlying mechanisms by evaluating PIWI‐interacting RNA (piRNA) expression profiles after I/R injury. Functional assays using piR‐4913 silencing assess its impact on infarct size, mitochondrial ATP production, and oxidative stress. Mechanistic analyses identify that piR‐4913, a cardiac‐enriched piRNA markedly upregulated in aged hearts following I/R injury, is effectively suppressed by IPostC. Silencing piR‐4913 confers cardioprotection by limiting infarct size, enhancing ATP production, and reducing oxidative stress. Mechanistically, piR‐4913 acts as a key facilitator that promotes the recruitment of OGT to Drp1, thereby catalyzing the O‐GlcNAcylation modification of Drp1 at Thr604. This modification promotes Drp1 mitochondrial translocation and Fis1 interaction, driving excessive mitochondrial fission and dysfunction. In vivo validation using a Drp1‐T604A mutant demonstrates profound resistance to I/R injury, confirming the critical role of Thr604 O‐GlcNAcylation in age‐related cardiac damage. Collectively, IPostC exerts cardioprotection in the aging heart by restraining the piR‐4913/OGT/Drp1 axis, thereby restoring mitochondrial proteostasis and dynamics. This pathway represents a promising therapeutic target to improve clinical outcomes in elderly patients with myocardial infarction.

title: pH‐Responsive Nanoplatform‐Mediated Lipid Hijacking and Metabolic Collapse for Synergistic Starvation‐Immunotherapy
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Tumor starvation therapy is a promising metabolism‐targeting intervention, yet its efficacy is largely counteracted by lipid droplet (LD)‐driven compensatory metabolism in malignant cells. Existing LDs‐targeted approaches are further hampered by off‐target systemic metabolic disturbances and inherent immunosuppressive adverse effects. Here, we construct a zeolitic imidazolate framework‐8 (ZIF‐8)‐based nanomedicine loaded with 2‐deoxy‐D‐glucose (2‐DG) and surface‐decorated with copper‐tannic acid (Cu‐TA, ZIF‐8/2‐DG@Cu‐TA). This nanosystem reroutes intracellular LDs from tumor cells to adjacent cancer‐associated fibroblasts (CAFs) to realize synergistic tumor starvation and immunotherapy. In the acidic tumor microenvironment, the degradable Cu‐TA coating activates connexin 43 (Cx43) hemichannels on CAFs. After internalization by tumor cells, ZIF‐8/2‐DG releases 2‐DG to suppress glycolysis, while dissociated zinc ions disrupt mitochondrial bioenergetics and further trigger Cx43 hemichannels activation on tumor cells. Fully assembled Cx43 gap junctions mediate directional LDs trafficking from tumor cells to CAFs, restricting intracellular lipid energy pools sustaining malignant metabolic demands. Simultaneous blockade of glycolysis, mitochondrial respiration and lipid metabolism induces profound tumor‐cell metabolic collapse. The resulting metabolic stress strongly amplifies antitumor immunity and markedly suppresses both subcutaneous and orthotopic MOC1 tumors. Overall, this study establishes a gap‐junction‐driven triple metabolic starvation paradigm and offers mechanistic insights for next‐generation metabolic immunotherapies.

title: BRCA1 Mutation‐Recognizing Tetrahedral Framework Nucleic Acid Nanoplatform Enables Coordinated PARP/WEE1 Inhibition and STING‐Associated Antitumor Immunity in Ovarian Cancer
authors:
Chenyi Wang, 
Mengying Yao, 
Jinhui Xie, 
Dingjie Wang, 
Yashi Shi, 
Xiaodan Mao, 
Chunhua Lu, 
Pengming Sun
abstract:
BRCA1 mutation-responsive FBOA-tFNA selectively recognizes mutant transcripts and coordinates reduction-responsive intracellular delivery of olaparib and adavosertib, amplifying DNA damage and weakening G2/M checkpoint protection. These effects are accompanied by STING-associated immune activation and stronger antitumor immunity, while sequential anti-PD-1 treatment further improves tumor control and promotes memory-associated T-cell responses.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Improving therapeutic efficacy and antitumor immune responsiveness in BRCA1-mutant ovarian cancer remains challenging. Here, we developed a BRCA1 mutation-guided tetrahedral framework nucleic acid nanosystem, FBOA-tFNA, for coordinated intracellular delivery of the PARP inhibitor olaparib and the WEE1 inhibitor adavosertib. After folate receptor-mediated uptake, FBOA-tFNA recognizes BRCA1 mutant RNA through toehold-mediated strand displacement, enabling mutation-selective beacon activation, while drug release is independently regulated by reduction-responsive disulfide cleavage. Coordinated PARP/WEE1 inhibition amplified DNA damage, impaired G2/M checkpoint protection, and promoted tumor-cell killing in BRCA1-mutant ovarian cancer models. Resulting DNA damage-associated intracellular dsDNA signals activated STING-associated signaling, type I interferon responses, immunogenic cell death (ICD)-associated stress, dendritic-cell maturation, and CD8 +  T-cell activation. Engineered patient-derived ovarian cancer organoids expressing a BRCA1 2594delC -containing transcript further supported the mutation-selective recognition and therapeutic potential of FBOA-tFNA ex vivo. In vivo, FBOA-tFNA showed tumor-associated fluorescence accumulation, BRCA1 mutant-transcript recognition-associated beacon activation, enhanced antitumor efficacy, and preliminary repeated-dose tolerability. Moreover, FBOA-tFNA enhanced antitumor immune responses and improved the response to anti-PD-1 therapy, accompanied by increased effector and memory-like T-cell populations. This programmable DNA nanoplatform provides a personalized combination strategy for coordinated DNA-damage therapy and immunomodulation in BRCA1-mutant ovarian cancer.

title: XChrom: A Cross‐Cell Chromatin Accessibility Prediction Model Integrating Genomic Sequence and Cellular Context
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Single‐cell chromatin accessibility offers unique insights into transcriptional regulation beyond gene expression. However, paired datasets of these two modalities remain relatively scarce, and existing computational models cannot simultaneously predict chromatin accessibility for unseen genomic regions and cells. Here, we present XChrom, a deep learning framework for genome‐wide cross‐cell chromatin accessibility prediction that integrates genomic sequence and single‐cell transcriptomics‐derived cell identity into a unified model. Comprehensive evaluations show that XChrom consistently outperforms existing methods in cross‐region and cross‐cell predictions, and uniquely enables cross‐both predictions. It also supports cross‐sample prediction when batch effects are properly corrected. Cross‐species analyses demonstrate XChrom's robust performance and its ability to capture evolutionarily conserved regulatory rules. Applied to peripheral blood mononuclear cells from COVID‐19 patients, XChrom accurately identifies transcription factor activities in novel but related cell states and reveals pathogenesis‐associated regulatory alterations. XChrom is available as an open‐source Python package, facilitating single‐cell transcriptional regulation research.

title: Advances in Josephson Junction Materials and Processes Toward Practical Quantum Computing
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   The Josephson junction (JJ) is the fundamental nonlinear building block of superconducting quantum technologies. Its macroscopic quantum tunneling physics underpins superconducting quantum computing, sensing, and communication, but scaling these platforms to utility‐scale architectures places increasingly stringent demands on junction materials, interfaces, and fabrication. Practical quantum computing requires high reproducibility, low power consumption, tunability, a small device footprint, and resilience to noise and defects. This review surveys how advances in materials science, device characterization, and nanofabrication are addressing these challenges and redefining the figures of merit for next‐generation JJs. This review also examines the evolution of fabrication strategies, from conventional multi‐angle evaporation to foundry‐compatible superconducting processes and the integration of emerging junction materials. Progress along these directions will determine how rapidly JJs move from laboratory‐scale components to the foundation of industrial‐scale quantum processors.

title: Gapless Complete Genome and Multi‐Omics Illuminate Immune Adaptation and Host‐Virus Interactions in a Coronavirus Reservoir
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Bats are major reservoirs of emerging viruses, including severe acute respiratory syndrome‐related coronaviruses, yet they exhibit remarkable tolerance to viral infections with limited clinical manifestations‐a longstanding immunological paradox. Here, we generate a telomere‐to‐telomere (T2T) de novo genome assembly for
                     Rhinolophus sinicus 
                    (
                     R. sinicus 
                    ), designated T2T‐RSC1.0 (2.14 Gb), comprising 17 fully anchored autosomes and both sex chromosomes. This gapless assembly resolves 129.19 Mb of previously unresolved regions (PURs) and enables annotation of 848 previously unannotated genes, including 131 protein‐coding genes and five pseudogenes on the 33.75 Mb Y chromosome. Using 2.12 × 10
                     5 
                    newly identified single‐nucleotide polymorphisms within PURs, population genomic analyses resolve three major genetic groups and provide improved resolution of genome‐wide population structure. Comparative analyses further reveal population‐level associations between major histocompatibility complex polymorphism and viral diversity. Multi‐omics and functional analyses reveal a coordinated evolutionary remodeling of antiviral defense, antigen presentation, cytokine signaling, and inflammatory regulation in horseshoe bats. This study provides an unparalleled genomic resource for
                     R. sinicus 
                    and establishes an integrated framework for investigating immune evolution, long‐term host–virus coexistence, and mammalian adaptive evolution.

title: Macrophage GLUD1 is Essential for Redox Balance and Immune Homeostasis in Cardiac Injury
authors:
Tingting Jin, 
Chaojie Lai, 
Qingyan Zhou, 
Ruilin Wang, 
Yiping Tong, 
Wentao Chen, 
Nikola Rabrenovic, 
Tingyu Zhang, 
Xinrong Ren, 
Chengchen Huang, 
Jiawen Chen, 
Ran Li, 
Luyang Yu, 
Massimiliano Mazzone, 
Wenbin Zhang, 
Guosheng Fu, 
Min Shang
abstract:
Excessive free radical production and dysregulated immune responses are key contributors to myocardial ischemia-reperfusion (IR) injury. Macrophage GLUD1 activity safeguards against HIF-1α accumulation and maladaptive responses to IR-induced ROS production. Specifically, GLUD1 deficiency results in mitochondrial ROS accumulation due to reduced NADPH/NADP +  and GSH/GSSG ratios during IR injury. Elevated mitochondrial ROS inhibits PHD2 activity, leading to HIF-1α accumulation, while promoting IκBα degradation and NF-κB activation. This cascade triggers the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines, ultimately causing cardiomyocyte apoptosis and cell death during IR. Therapeutically, pharmacological activation of GLUD1 preserves cardiac function and mitigates IR injury. Figure created in BioRender, Shang, M. (2026) ntt54v1.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Excessive free radical production and dysregulated immune responses contribute to myocardial ischemia-reperfusion (IR) injury. However, the mechanisms by which macrophages regulate reactive oxygen species (ROS) homeostasis and orchestrate immune responses during IR injury remain elusive. Here, we show that glutamate dehydrogenase 1 (GLUD1) expression is induced in monocytes from patients with acute myocardial infarction after interventional therapy and in cardiac-recruited macrophages from mice subjected to IR injury. GLUD1-deficient macrophages exacerbate IR injury by increasing mitochondrial ROS accumulation and amplifying pro-inflammatory responses. Mechanistically, GLUD1 deficiency leads to mitochondrial ROS accumulation due to reduced NADPH/NADP +  and GSH/GSSG ratios during IR injury. Elevated mitochondrial ROS inhibits PHD2 activity, stabilizing HIF-1α and enhancing NF-κB signaling, promoting the release of pro-inflammatory factors and exacerbating myocardial damage. Systemic activation of GLUD1 or adoptive transfer of monocytes pre-treated with a GLUD1 activator preserved cardiac function and mitigated IR injury. These findings highlight macrophage GLUD1 as a critical regulator of redox balance and immune homeostasis, presenting a promising therapeutic target for alleviating IR injury and preserving cardiac function.

title: ALDH2 Suppresses Ferroptosis and Promotes Bortezomib Resistance in Multiple Myeloma Through the KEAP1‐NRF2 Feedback Loop
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Resistance to bortezomib (BTZ) represents a major obstacle that limits the therapeutic efficacy and worsens the prognosis of multiple myeloma (MM). Ferroptosis, a form of regulated cell death triggered by excessive lipid peroxidation, has garnered increasing attention for anticancer intervention, yet the mechanisms underlying ferroptosis in MM remain enigmatic. Here, we confirmed that ALDH2 is upregulated in MM patients and that its altered expression is closely associated with BTZ resistance and poor prognosis. Functionally, ALDH2 promoted the proliferation, BTZ resistance, and ferroptosis resistance of MM cells, suggesting its oncogenic role. Mechanistically, ALDH2 competitively bound to KEAP1 and stabilized NRF2 by preventing its ubiquitin‐proteasome‐mediated degradation, thereby promoting the nuclear translocation of NRF2 and subsequent upregulation of GPX4, and in turn regulating ferroptosis, proliferation, and BTZ resistance in MM. In parallel, NRF2 bound directly to the promoter region of ALDH2 and further enhanced ALDH2 transcription, thus forming a positive feedback loop. Collectively, our findings reveal that the ALDH2/KEAP1/NRF2‐GPX4 axis may serve as a key regulator of ferroptosis in MM and a promising therapeutic target for overcoming BTZ resistance.

title: Multiscale Interfacial Engineering Enables Robust Reconstituted Wood
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Development of sustainable, high‐performance structural materials capable of replacing traditional engineering plastics and lightweight alloys is critical to achieving carbon neutrality. However, engineering renewable wood into structural materials intrinsically relies on reconstitution and bonding, during which traditional polymer adhesives introduce compositionally and mechanically heterogeneous interfaces. These discontinuities produce stress concentrations under water‐induced swelling and shrinkage, undermining long‐term stability. Herein, we proposed a synergistic strategy integrating interfacial reconstruction and water‐induced regeneration to reconstruct heterogeneous interfaces into homogeneous ones with compositional and structural continuity. This approach enabled lap joints to achieve a high dry shear strength of 6.2 MPa, exceeding that of natural wood. Notably, this strategy utilized water to facilitate the regeneration and performance retention of the interface, allowing the material to retain 97% of its strength even after two boiling water cycles. Furthermore, the mechanical properties were optimized through pressure control, thereby yielding specific flexural strength (276.2 MPa cm
                     3 
                    g
                     −1 
                    ) and specific flexural modulus (24 000 MPa cm
                     3 
                    g
                     −1 
                    ) that were comparable or even superior to those of certain metals, construction materials, and engineering plastics. This work provides useful insights into the design of high‐performance, sustainable wood‐based structural materials suitable for outdoor environments.

title: Metasurface‐Based Multidimensional Light‐Field Manipulation: From Technologies to Applications
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Metasurfaces composed of subwavelength meta‐atoms provide an ultrathin and highly integrable platform for manipulating optical wavefronts and have reshaped the development of flat optics and meta‐optics. Beyond conventional single‐parameter phase engineering, recent advances have enabled coordinated control of multiple degrees of freedom of light, including phase, amplitude, polarization, wavelength, spatiotemporal mode, and orbital angular momentum (OAM). This review summarizes the physical principles, implementation strategies, and representative applications of metasurface‐based multidimensional light‐field manipulation. We first discuss the fundamental mechanisms of metasurface‐based light‐field manipulation, including generalized Snell's law, phase discontinuity, meta‐atom scattering, and the modulation of basic optical degrees of freedom. We then review major multidimensional design strategies, such as joint phase‐amplitude, phase‐polarization, phase‐wavelength, phase‐OAM, spatial‐polarization, temporal‐phase, and higher‐dimensional control. Representative applications in optical information processing, computational imaging, holographic and near‐eye display, optical communication, structured‐light generation, and optical manipulation are further discussed. Finally, we highlight current challenges associated with efficiency, bandwidth, crosstalk, dynamic reconfigurability, fabrication tolerance, scalable manufacturing, and system‐level integration, and outline future opportunities in metasurface‐based multidimensional light‐field manipulation.

title: Noninvasive Detection and Subtyping of Esophageal Cancer by Circulating Cell‐Free mtDNA Fragmentomics: A Multi‐Center Validation Study
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Esophageal cancer (EC) is highly lethal due to late diagnosis, and accurate non‐invasive tools for early detection and subtyping remain lacking. Circulating cell‐free mitochondrial DNA (ccf‐mtDNA) fragmentomics offers a promising biomarker source. In this large multi‐center study enrolling 1,260 participants spanning healthy control (HC), benign esophageal diseases (BED), precancerous lesions and EC patients, we developed two machine learning models based on plasma ccf‐mtDNA fragmentomic profiles: an EC detection (ED) model and a pathological subtyping prediction (PSP) model. The ED model achieved an AUC of 0.9706 (EC vs. non‐EC) in the training cohort, with high performance in internal (0.9762), external (0.9748), and Chinese minority (0.9668, Uyghur and Kazakh) validation cohorts. At the optimal cut‐off, it yielded 92.16% sensitivity for stage I EC in the combined validation cohort and correctly identified 93.10% of early EC cases missed by preoperative biopsy. It also discriminated high‐grade intraepithelial neoplasia from non‐EC with an AUC of 0.9597. The PSP model distinguished ESCC from EAC with 89.71% accuracy, improving to 90.74% after integrating key clinical parameters. In summary, ccf‐mtDNA fragmentomics provides a robust, non‐invasive platform for early EC detection, precancerous risk stratification, and histological subtyping, demonstrating strong potential to transform clinical management.

title: Laser‐Induced Rashba Spin‐Orbit Torques in Multiferroic Semiconductor (Ge,Mn)Te
authors:
Zeynab Sadeghi, 
Tomáš Ostatnický, 
Eva Schmoranzerová, 
Jozef Kimák, 
Dominik Kriegner, 
Helena Reichlová, 
Lukáš Nádvorník, 
Gunther Springholz, 
J. Hugo Dil, 
Juraj Krempasky, 
Petr Němec
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    The multiferroic semiconductor (Ge,Mn)Te exhibits ferroelectricity, strong Rashba spin‐orbit coupling, and carrier‐mediated magnetic order, making it a unique platform for exploring the interplay between electronic, structural, and magnetic degrees of freedom. In this study, we investigate the ultrafast magnetization dynamics of Ge
                     0.85 
                    Mn
                     0.15 
                    Te using time‐resolved magneto‐optical spectroscopy. By separating magnetic and nonmagnetic contributions in the transient response, we identify two distinct laser‐induced magnetic phenomena, both arising from a photoinduced effective spin‐orbit torque. Coherent magnetization precession is driven by a laser‐induced increase in hole concentration, which modifies the occupation of Rashba‐split, spin‐locked valence band states, and shifts the position of the magnetic easy axis. The transient change in magnetic properties, observed as variations in the amplitude and coercive field of the pump‐induced change in ellipticity hysteresis loops, is attributed to laser‐induced modifications of the ferroelectric sublattice displacement, which affect the ferroelectric polarization and the associated Rashba spin‐orbit interaction. While the first type of optical spin‐orbit torque has already been observed in the diluted magnetic semiconductor (Ga,Mn)As, the second effect is unique to the multiferroic Rashba semiconductor (Ge,Mn)Te, opening new opportunities for all‐optical manipulation of magnetic order and spin‐orbit torque generation in spin‐orbitronic devices.

title: An Environmental Stable Ionogel‐Based Smart Glove System for Integrated Underwater Communication and Safety Warning
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Flexible sensing technology based on hydrogel‐based smart gloves enables accurate gesture recognition in complex environments, but such gloves degrade in dry, high‐temperature, and underwater conditions, and their complex assembly limits practical usability. Here, a smart glove monitoring system is developed by integrating a poly(benzyl methacrylate‐co‐2‐hydroxyethyl acrylate)/ionic liquid (P(BZMA‐co‐HEA)/IL) ionogel sensing layer with a flexible printed circuit board (FPCB). The ionogel is constructed through a network‐constrained ionic soft‐space regulation strategy, where HEA‐rich segments strengthen the network, IL provides deformation‐adaptive ionic soft spaces, and BZMA‐rich hydrophobic segments suppress water penetration. The optimized ionogel combines stretchability (up to 1100%), weight retention (98.86% at room temperature and 95.25% at 65°C), favorable adhesion, anti‐swelling behavior, and stable sensing performance under multiple environmental conditions. The FPCB enables a detachable and reconfigurable sensor array, ensuring stable interfacial contact and wearing flexibility. By further combining multi‐channel signal acquisition, fully connected neural network (FCNN)‐assisted gesture classification, and real‐time alert feedback, the smart glove functions as an integrated sensing‐recognition‐warning platform, achieving 99.92% gesture recognition accuracy and enabling reliable underwater communication and safety warning. This work establishes an effective material design and integration strategy for environmentally adaptive smart gloves.

Corynoxine Inhibits Tumor Growth  
 The cover depicts corynoxine entering tumor cells and targeting NQO1 to weaken the NQO1-PTPA association, thereby facilitating PTPA association with PP2Ac and activating PP2A. This molecular switch disrupts tumor-promoting signals and ultimately suppresses tumor cell survival and proliferation. More details can be found in the Research Article by Linna Du, Xuan Cao, and co-workers (DOI:  10.1002/advs.77362 ).

title: Matrix Stiffness Enhances Odontogenic Differentiation of DPSCs through Membrane Curvature Protein Baiap2‐Modulated Exosome Release (Adv. Sci. 60/2026)

abstract:
Dental Caries  
 Matrix stiffness promotes odontogenic differentiation of dental pulp stem cells by enhancing exosome release. This process is mediated through PI3K-AKT-Baiap2 signaling that modulates membrane curvature, which also depends on mechanosensitive kinesin-1 and vesicular transport. These findings reveal a previously underappreciated mechanosensitive mechanism linking extracellular matrix stiffness to exosome secretion in deep caries pathogenesis. More details can be found in the Research Article by Jinsong Hu, Bo Cheng, Lin Niu, and co-workers (DOI:  10.1002/advs.76908 ).

abstract:
Molecular Transport in Tough Hydrogels  
 Hydraulic pressure enables programmable molecular transport in tough hydrogel membranes. The cover depicts molecular transport across a hydrogel membrane, where pressure-driven convection actively guides molecules through the polymer network in combination with passive diffusion. By tuning the convective flow, molecular transport can be dynamically regulated, providing a versatile platform for selective delivery and molecular separation. More details can be found in the Research Article by Xinyue Liu and co-workers (DOI:  10.1002/advs.77159 ).

abstract:
Quantitative SERS  
 A mesoporous-shell monolayer plasmonic architecture transforms stochastic Raman enhancement into reproducible molecular quantification. Ordered silver nanoparticles generate deterministic hotspots, while porous silica shells regulate molecular access and stabilize photosensitive drugs. Applied to therapeutic drug monitoring, the platform enables accurate serum analysis and SERS-guided chemotherapy dosing, maintaining antitumor efficacy while reducing systemic toxicity. title: A Robust Bio‐Supportive Hydrogel Patch for Full‐Thickness Repair of Gastroesophageal Defects
authors:
Xingqi Song, 
Zhewei Shuai, 
Weiyan Sun, 
Liang Chen, 
Yiwei Shen, 
Jiateng Hu, 
Yuanqi Ma, 
Jie Luo, 
Meilin Huang, 
Yan Luo, 
Yunlang She, 
Guangdong Zhou, 
Chang Chen, 
Dong Lei
abstract:
Gastroesophageal defect repair remains a formidable clinical challenge plagued by high leakage and life‐threatening complications. We develop a double‐disc, highly crystalline PVA‐based RBS hydrogel patch featuring suture‐free sealing, robust acid/enzyme resistance and mechanical durability. It achieves full‐thickness tissue regeneration across perforation and fistula models in multiple species, demonstrating promising clinical translation potential.








ABSTRACT
Surgical repair of gastroesophageal (GE) defects is a formidable clinical challenge, plagued by high leakage, fistula recurrence and life‐threatening complications due to gastric acid exposure and persistent mechanical stress. To address this unmet need, we developed a robust bio‐supportive (RBS) hydrogel patch for immediate fluid‐tight closure and full‐thickness tissue regeneration. Fabricated from highly crystalline polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) hydrogel, the RBS patch has a double‐disc architecture, inherent porous network and weakly bound water. The double‐disc design ensures effective sealing and deformation resistance; high crystallinity confers adequate mechanical strength and long‐term acid/enzyme resistance. Moreover, its porous microstructure and weakly bound water synergistically promote cellular adhesion, migration and tissue infiltration for functional repair. In rat and rabbit models, the RBS patch achieved remarkable healing of gastric perforations (GP), esophageal perforations (EP) and tracheoesophageal fistulas (TEF), with intact mucosal, submucosal and muscular layers regeneration. Its efficacy and safety were further validated in beagle dog models, highlighting clinical translation potential. This RBS patch serves as a versatile bio‐supportive technology for GE defects and a promising platform for tissue repair in dynamic physiological environments.

title: Single‐Cell Dissection of Microglial Dysfunction in Diabetes‐Associated Neurodegenerative Vulnerability
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    The molecular mechanisms linking type 2 diabetes to increased neurodegenerative risk remain poorly defined. Given the critical involvement of microglial dysfunction in neurodegeneration, we constructed a temporal single‐cell atlas integrating transcriptomic and epigenomic profiles of microglia from diabetic (db/db) and control (db/m) mice across the lifespan. We delineated a nonlinear, diabetes‐specific pathological trajectory characterized by early inflammatory activation, a mid‐stage inflection in neurodegeneration‐associated signaling and metabolic stress, and late‐stage dysfunction. Chromatin accessibility profiling revealed early and persistent epigenomic priming of neurodegeneration‐associated pathways, accompanied by stage‐specific enhancer rewiring. Pseudotime analysis identified a disease‐associated microglial (DAM) state as a candidate transition node, characterized by biased polarization and accelerated maturation under diabetic conditions. Targeted validation using freshly isolated microglia and primary microglial cultures further supported the early expansion of the DAM population, a bias toward homeostatic‐to‐DAM activation, and
                     Arhgap15 
                    ‐dependent regulation of phagocytic activity. Together, these findings identify microglial states and candidate regulatory pathways that may link diabetes to neurodegenerative vulnerability.

title: An Adipocyte MKK3–p38β Axis Preserves Insulin Responsiveness in Mice and Is Reciprocally Altered in Human Obesity
authors:
Edgar Bernardo, 
Nuria Matesanz, 
Jorge‐Luis Torres, 
Alba C. Arcones, 
Juan Ignacio Jiménez‐Loygorri, 
Alfonso Mora, 
Leticia Herrera‐Melle, 
Luis Leiva‐Vega, 
Maria Elena Rodriguez, 
Lourdes Hernández‐Cosido, 
Marta Leon, 
Paula Yong González, 
Teresa Durán, 
Tamara Parracho, 
Francisca Mulero, 
Rubén Nogueiras, 
J. Simon C. Arthur, 
Angel R. Nebreda, 
Roger J. Davis, 
Miguel Marcos, 
Guadalupe Sabio
abstract:
The adipocyte MKK3–p38β axis emerges as an adaptive stress-response pathway during obesity. Human visceral adipose tissue analyses, adipocyte-specific mouse models, and primary adipocytes show that the MKK3–p38β axis supports insulin responsiveness by restraining p70S6K-dependent inhibitory IRS1 feedback and preserving AKT–GLUT4 signaling. This pathway defines a selective adipose mechanism that may help preserve glucose handling under nutritional stress.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Obesity is a major risk factor for insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes. Adipocyte stress responses can either promote metabolic dysfunction or preserve insulin action, but the contribution of the p38 MAPK activator MKK3 to adipose tissue physiology remains poorly understood. Here, we show that adipose MKK3 expression increases early during high-fat feeding and is also elevated in human obesity. In human visceral adipose tissue, MKK3 expression was positively associated with body mass index and leptin and inversely associated with HbA1c in unadjusted analyses. Using germline, Fabp4-Cre, and Adipo-Cre Mkk3-deficient mice, together with p38β-deficient mice and primary adipocytes, we found that loss of adipocyte MKK3 impairs insulin responsiveness. Adipo-Cre;Mkk3 fl/fl  (Adipo Mkk3 ) mice displayed reduced insulin-stimulated glucose uptake selectively in subcutaneous white adipose tissue despite unchanged body composition and basal brown adipose tissue activity. Mechanistically, MKK3 or p38β deficiency increased p70S6K activity and inhibitory IRS1 Ser307 phosphorylation, reduced GLUT4 translocation and Akt activation, and these defects were partially rescued by rapamycin or the selective p70S6K inhibitor PF-4708671. Together, these findings identify an adipocyte MKK3-p38β-p70S6K axis that helps preserve insulin signaling during nutritional stress.

title: An extensible deep learning framework for multi-type chromatin interaction prediction through hierarchical adaptation strategies
abstract:
by Shuaibin Wang, Tong Chen, Weixu Liu, Xuejie Zheng, Zhongxin Yang, Zhen Liang, Yin Shen 

Three-dimensional chromatin interactions play essential roles in gene regulation, yet computational prediction of diverse interaction types remains largely dependent on specialized, single-task models. Here, we present UniLoopNet, a multi-task deep learning framework that predicts multiple types of chromatin interactions including enhancer–promoter interactions, enhancer–enhancer interactions, CTCF-mediated loops, and stripe-associated interactions from DNA sequences. UniLoopNet employs a shared encoder–decoder architecture with hierarchical adaptation strategies, integrating multi-task, transfer, and continual learning based on task semantic similarity. Comprehensive benchmarking across multiple cell lines demonstrates that UniLoopNet outperforms existing specialized and multi-task approaches, with AUROCs exceeding 0.90 in most tasks. Under stringent evaluation settings, including chromosome-matched, distance-matched, realistic imbalanced, and locus-disjoint tests, AUROCs range from 0.8934 to 0.9366. In the realistic 1:5 class-imbalance setting, the AUPRCs for enhancer–promoter and enhancer–enhancer interaction prediction are 0.7956 and 0.6935, respectively. Cross-cell-line transfer experiments further show that applying UniLoopNet to another cell line requires adaptation by supervised fine-tuning on target-cell-line data, after which performance is comparable to that of within-cell-line training. Notably, the framework exhibits data efficiency in experiments with substantially reduced training data. Interpretability analyses reveal that the learned sequence features are associated with known transcription factor binding sites and uncover differential regulatory effects of disease-associated variants. UniLoopNet provides a versatile and data-efficient framework for sequence-based prediction and interpretation of diverse 3D genome interactions, complementing existing sequence-to-map approaches while improving the understanding of sequence-encoded regulatory potential.

title: Evolutionary and dynamic constraints converge on a conserved coupling sector in thermally adapted GH1 β-glucosidases
abstract:
by Li-Ting Zheng, Yi Li, Xian He, Lian-Tao Yang, De-Rui Zhao, Meng-Ting Liu, Peng Sang, Li-Quan Yang 

How protein sequences evolve to maintain functional conformational dynamics under thermal stress remains an important question in molecular evolution. Thermophilic enzymes are often considered to achieve stability primarily through enhanced structural rigidity, yet thermal adaptation may also involve the preservation or reorganization of correlated motions across the protein scaffold. Here, we compared three glycoside hydrolase family 1 β-glucosidases—BsBgl1A, 9UPT, and LQBG8—that share a conserved (β/α) 8  TIM-barrel fold but display distinct optimal temperatures of approximately 45, 65, and 70 °C, respectively. By integrating comparative structural analysis, three independent 1 μs molecular dynamics simulations at 300, 325, and 350 K, neural relational inference of residue-level dynamic coupling, and family-level coevolutionary analysis, we identified distinct dynamic strategies associated with their thermal phenotypes. All three enzymes retained their global compactness and principal secondary-structure framework across the simulated temperatures, indicating that differences in RMSD and residue flexibility did not reflect large-scale unfolding. BsBgl1A showed the strongest temperature sensitivity, with increased structural deviation and residue mobility at 350 K. Its inferred interaction network exhibited a non-monotonic response, characterized by pronounced overcoupling at 325 K followed by reduced connectivity at 350 K. In contrast, 9UPT maintained relatively restrained residue dynamics and a highly reproducible coupling topology across temperatures. LQBG8 combined substantial local conformational flexibility with persistent long-range coupling and retained the highest directed network density at 350 K. Across the three enzymes, the βα5–βα7 region repeatedly emerged as a shared structural and dynamic center. Coevolutionary couplings were also enriched in TIM-barrel-associated regions that spatially converged on this sector. These findings indicate that thermal adaptation in GH1 β-glucosidases is not adequately explained by uniform structural rigidification. Instead, enzymes with the same conserved fold may adopt distinct organizations of correlated motion, while greater thermal adaptation is associated with the persistence or reorganization of a βα5–βα7-centered dynamic coupling pattern under elevated temperature. The correspondence between dynamic coupling and coevolutionary enrichment is consistent with long-term evolutionary constraint on this structural sector, although it does not establish direct selection on the network as an independent functional unit. Our results therefore provide a testable framework in which thermostability reflects a balance among local stabilization, regional flexibility, and the resilience of higher-order dynamic organization.

title: In silico  prediction of metabolic trait robustness in microbial cells
abstract:
Microbial strains undergo notable biomass expansion in industrial applications subjecting populations to Darwinian selection. The consequent adaptive evolution may threaten the often tediously developed desired metabolic traits of the strains, such as flavor or platform chemical production. Yet, it remains unresolved how to predict the evolutionary trait robustness. Here, we propose TRAEV (Trait Robustness Against EVolution), a computational framework for
                     in silico 
                    prediction of evolutionary robustness of metabolic traits and trajectories of desired traits in application environments. TRAEV uses constraint-based metabolic models for predicting environment-dependent trait-fitness dependencies and accounts for the stochasticity of adaptive evolution by using Monte Carlo-based perturbation analysis. First, TRAEV predicts the immediate metabolic phenotype in the new environment, and then, the subsequent evolutionary trajectories of fitness and desired trait. Metabolic trait robustness is quantified from the evolutionary trajectories as two scores: Robustness Score (RS) and Trade-off Score (TS). RS represents trait robustness and the overall trait level during evolutionary adaptation, whereas TS captures trait–fitness trade-offs. We validated TRAEV by predicting relative evolutionary robustness of heterologous pigmentation of two engineered
                     Saccharomyces cerevisiae 
                    strains and two desired aroma generation traits by multiple wine strains of
                     S. cerevisiae 
                    if they were developed via a laboratory selection process. Thus, we showed how TRAEV predictions could guide strain development. TRAEV can be integrated into computational strain design workflows across microbial strains, desired metabolic traits, and application environments. Ultimately, model-predicted evolutionary robustness of desired metabolic traits can guide both strain and process development and help enhancing the economic attractiveness of industrial applications using microbial cells.

title: KmerSignificance score: A discriminative and biologically informed framework for viral  k -mer prioritization
abstract:
Distinguishing closely related viral strains requires identifying genomic regions where subtle sequence differences carry biological significance. While
                     k 
                    -mer-based approaches offer computational efficiency for genome analysis, existing methods lack standardized frameworks for evaluating which
                     k 
                    -mers are most informative. Current selection strategies focus primarily on statistical discriminative power without integrating biological context. We introduce KmerSignificance Score (KSS), a
                     k 
                    -mer prioritization framework combining three components: an information-theoretic method measuring strain-distinguishing capacity, an optimized amino acid substitution matrix (MIYATA_EVO) for mutation impact assessment, and a protein characterization score derived from annotations and database cross-references retrieved through UniProt. All three component scores and the integrated KSS are bounded in [0,1] by construction, providing a common numerical scale for ranking positions within a dataset. The discriminative component achieved a mean F1 of 0.881, not significantly different from chi-squared (0.876), the strongest of eight baselines. Top-ranked selections from the discriminative component nonetheless differed from those produced by chi-squared, especially for SARS-CoV-2 and HIV-1. The MIYATA_EVO matrix, optimized using a genetic algorithm, increased the composite agreement score across eight amino acid characteristics by 28.4% over the original MIYATA matrix. Across 17,471 viral proteins, the protein characterization score tracked UniProt’s five-level annotation score closely (Kendall’s
                     
                       
                         
                         
                           
                             τ 
                             = 
                             0.775 
                           
                         
                       
                     
                    ), as expected for measures drawing on overlapping annotation content. Within each level, the continuous score provided finer numerical resolution among proteins. Literature cross-referencing on SARS-CoV-2 (278,738 sequences, 19 Pango-derived lineage labels), HIV-1 (12,223 sequences, 15 subtype labels), and human cytomegalovirus (HCMV; 399–646 sequences, 4–8 locus-specific genotypes) found that the top-ranked
                     k 
                    -mers reported here map to established variant-defining mutations, subtype-specific polymorphisms, and genotype markers. KSS provides a standardized framework for viral
                     k 
                    -mer prioritization with potential applications in variant surveillance, molecular epidemiology, and functional annotation. The tool is available at
                     https://github.com/bioinfoUQAM/KmerSignificanceScore 
                    .

title: The glutamine-aspartate metabolic tradeoff between fast growth and metabolic flexibility
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Background 
                     Cancer cells develop selective dependencies on nutrients, creating potential opportunities for therapeutic intervention. However, how metabolic rewiring enables cancer cells to sustain proliferation while adapting to nutrient limitation remains incompletely understood. 
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     We develop a systematic framework to investigate nutrient dependencies and apply it to extracellular glutamine dependence. By measuring metabolite exchange rates across 54 cancer cell lines with different degrees of glutamine dependence, together with metabolic profiling of human stem-cell differentiation, we identify tissue-associated differences in the use of glutamine and aspartate for glutamate biosynthesis. These differences are linked to a trade-off between rapid proliferation and metabolic flexibility. Time-resolved intracellular metabolomics following glutamine withdrawal reveal a common limitation in purine biosynthesis. However, this metabolic limitation alone is insufficient to explain glutamine dependency, suggesting that additional regulatory responses to glutamine deprivation contribute to growth arrest. 
                   
                   
                     Conclusions 
                     Our study provides a systematic framework for identifying metabolic features associated with nutrient dependence and shows how established functions of glutamine, aspartate and asparagine are coordinated across diverse cancer cell types. This approach may support the mechanistic characterization and pharmacological targeting of metabolic dependencies beyond glutamine addiction.

title: Mitigating bias in spatial transcriptomic pipelines via human feedback with CSDE
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Biological discovery from large-scale assays requires extensive preprocessing, during which raw outputs (e.g., images, sequences) are processed into structured forms amenable to analysis. In spatial transcriptomics, differential expression analysis depends on cell segmentation, gene expression quantification, and cell-type annotation, all prone to systematic errors. We introduce corrected spatial differential expression (CSDE), building on prediction-powered inference to leverage a small set of expert-validated cells to correct for preprocessing bias. Across three case studies, CSDE yields more reliable differential expression estimates than the prevalent approach neglecting preprocessing.

title: Attentive interpretable tabular learning (TabNet) for miRNA expression classification in cervical cancer and Alzheimer's disease
abstract:
Background and Objective
                      The classification of RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data presents a fundamental challenge in computational biomedicine: raw read counts are high-dimensional, over-dispersed, and heteroscedastic, requiring careful preprocessing before machine learning models can be applied. Existing deep learning approaches for RNA-seq classification have largely overlooked the tabular nature of genomic expression data and have offered limited embedded interpretability. This study proposes TabNet, an attentive interpretable tabular learning architecture, as a framework for miRNA-based disease classification and evaluates its performance and interpretability against three established baseline models. 
                  
                     Methods
                      Two publicly available miRNA expression datasets were examined: a cervical cancer cohort (58 samples, 714 miRNAs) and an Alzheimer's disease cohort (70 samples, 503 miRNAs). Raw count data were preprocessed following the MLSeq framework, encompassing DESeq median-ratio normalisation, near-zero variance filtering, supervised gene ranking based on DESeq differential expression analysis, and the DESeq variance-stabilising transformation (vst). Gene subsets corresponding to 5%, 10%, and 30% of the post-filtering feature space were evaluated. TabNet was benchmarked against eight baselines spanning four learning paradigms: a 1D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), a Long Short-Term Memory network (LSTM), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Random Forest, ElasticNet-regularised logistic regression, a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), the prior-fitted transformer TabPFN, and the inherently interpretable Explainable Boosting Machine (EBM). Each configuration was assessed over 50 independent random train/test splits (70%/30%) under a strict leakage-free protocol in which all preprocessing, hyperparameter selection, and early stopping relied exclusively on inner validation subsets of the training partitions; all metrics are reported as mean $$\pm $$ SD. 
                  
                     Results
                      Under the leakage-free protocol, a group of four methods reached a statistically indistinguishable accuracy ceiling: on the cervical cancer dataset, ElasticNet (95.06% $$\pm $$ 4.66), EBM (94.94% $$\pm $$ 4.60), TabPFN (94.71% $$\pm $$ 4.64), and Random Forest (94.35% $$\pm $$ 5.82); on the Alzheimer's disease dataset, TabPFN (70.86% $$\pm $$ 10.26), EBM (70.67% $$\pm $$ 12.67), and ElasticNet (70.48% $$\pm $$ 9.76) led. TabNet reached 85.18% $$\pm $$ 11.10 (cervical) and 64.38% $$\pm $$ 11.23 (Alzheimer's) at its respective best levels -- below the top tier, but with the distinctive property of producing sparse, instance-level attention explanations as part of its forward computation. Supplementary analyses showed that self-supervised pre-training conferred no significant benefit at these cohort sizes, that results were robust to the choice between supervised differential-expression and unsupervised variance feature ranking, and that instance-level attention patterns varied substantially across splits, supporting their use as illustrative rather than confirmatory evidence. 
                  
                     Conclusions
                      In rigorously leakage-controlled small-cohort miRNA classification, strongly regularised classical models, glass-box additive models, and prior-fitted transformers converge to the same accuracy ceiling, and no evaluated method -- including attention-based deep learning -- surpasses it. Within this landscape, TabNet remains distinctive as the only evaluated deep architecture whose sequential attention mechanism produces sparse instance-level miRNA attributions as an inherent part of prediction, offering a trade-off between embedded interpretability and a moderate accuracy cost that we quantify precisely. These results argue for protocol-first evaluation and calibrated claims when deep tabular models are applied to small transcriptomic cohorts.

title:
Genetic architecture of low‐temperature germinability in rice revealed by integrated maps of
                     SNPs 
                    and structural variation
abstract:
SUMMARY 
                   
                    Low‐temperature germinability (LTG) limits rice direct seeding, yet its genetic architecture and regulatory roles of structural variations (SVs) remain largely unclear. We evaluated LTG in 403 rice accessions at four temperatures (13°C, 15°C, 18°C, 21°C). Integrating SNP/SV–GWAS, RNA‐seq, gene editing, population genetics, and machine learning, we dissected the genetic basis of LTG and built a genomic selection (GS) prediction model. The panel showed extensive LTG variation, which was negatively correlated with origin latitude. SV‐ and SNP‐based GWAS for LTG detected 119 and 127 QTLs, respectively, with 25 loci overlapping between the two datasets. Combining GWAS and RNA‐seq, we screened 30 candidate genes and 48 favorable haplotypes, with high‐LTG favorable alleles enriched in low‐latitude
                     Xian 
                    (
                     Indica 
                    ) accessions. We identified a deletion in the
                     qLTG3‐1 
                    coding region that negatively regulated LTG, and gene editing (CRISPR/Cas9) confirmed
                     qLT11d 
                    is a key gene for LTG. Population genetic analysis identified 29 inter‐subspecies (
                     Xian–Geng 
                    ) and 37 intra‐
                     Xian 
                    divergent regions for LTG, implying shared selected regions across and within subspecies under low temperature. Using SNP and SV data, we built corresponding genomic selection (GS) models with the machine learning‐based MFGP method, achieving high prediction accuracy across all temperatures. All cross‐temperature prediction correlations exceeded 0.55, with optimal performance at 18°C. Our results clarify rice LTG genetic architecture and suggest potential regulatory roles for SVs that merit further investigation, providing candidate genes, favorable haplotypes, and a GS model for LTG genetic improvement in direct seeding rice.

title: Root hairs and mycorrhiza represent alternative phylogenetically conserved strategies for belowground absorptive surface maximization
authors:
Joana Bergmann, 
Tom Lachaise, 
Karla M. Barfuss, 
Emma Bretherick, 
Elsa Matthus, 
Mark van Kleunen, 
Matthias C. Rillig
abstract:
The phylogenetically conserved trade-off between the investment in root hairs and mycorrhization formation.
 
 
 Summary 
 
Plants take up nutrients from the soil while investing in absorptive root surface or mycorrhizal partners. Root hairs – a major structure for nutrient uptake and cheap to build – increase the absorptive root surface. As such, they are an important component of plant resource economics but largely neglected in root economic concepts so far.
This is mainly due to data scarcity, which we set out to overcome by measuring root-hair traits on 82 European grassland species in a glasshouse experiment. Using fluorescence and light microscopy, root-hair length and incidence were measured along with mycorrhizal colonization.
We found a phylogenetically conserved trade-off between plant investment into root hairs and mycorrhiza, which captures functional differences between obligatory and non-mycorrhizal plants as well as between grasses and legumes. This trade-off defines a novel dimension in fine-root trait variation.
We conclude that plants invest in root hairs as part of a ‘do-it-yourself’ strategy in absorptive surface maximization for soil exploration. These findings demonstrate that root hairs play a fundamental role in fine-root trait variation and need to be considered when studying belowground plant economic strategies.
 
 Zusammenfassung 
 
Um Nährstoffe aus dem Boden aufzunehmen, investieren Pflanzen in Wurzeloberfläche oder Mykorrhiza-Partner. Wurzelhaare – wichtige Strukturen für die Nährstoffaufnahme, die günstig gebildet werden können – vergrößern die absorbierende Wurzeloberfläche. Damit sind sie ein wichtiger Bestandteil der Ressourcenökonomie von Pflanzen, wurden jedoch in Konzepten der Wurzelökonomie bislang weitgehend vernachlässigt.
Dies ist hauptsächlich auf die geringe Datenverfügbarkeit zurückzuführen, die wir durch die Messung von Wurzelhaarmerkmalen an 82 europäischen Grünlandarten in einem Gewächshausexperiment ein Stück weit überwinden wollten. Mithilfe von Fluoreszenz- und Lichtmikroskopie wurden die Länge und das Vorkommen von Wurzelhaaren sowie die Mykorrhiza-Kolonisierung gemessen.
Wir fanden einen phylogenetisch konservierten Trade-off zwischen den Investitionen der Pflanzen in Wurzelhaare und Mykorrhiza. Dieser stellte funktionelle Unterschiede zwischen obligat mykorrhizalen und nicht-mykorrhizalen Pflanzen sowie zwischen Gräsern und Leguminosen dar und definierte eine neue Dimension der Merkmalsvariation von Feinwurzeln
Wir kommen zu dem Schluss, dass Pflanzen im Rahmen einer „Do-it-yourself“-Strategie zur Maximierung der absorbierenden Oberfläche für die Erschließung des Bodens in Wurzelhaare investieren können. Unsere Ergebnisse zeigen, dass Wurzelhaare eine grundlegende Rolle bei der Merkmalsvariation von Feinwurzeln spielen und bei der Untersuchung unterirdischer pflanzlicher Ressourcenstrategien berücksichtigt werden müssen.

title: Disentangling atmospheric and soil drought: a new stand‐level manipulation approach for mature forests
authors:
Marcus Schaub, 
Stefan Hunziker, 
Jonas Gisler, 
Giovanni Bortolami, 
Volodymyr Trotsiuk, 
Katrin Meusburger, 
Christian Hug, 
Andreas Rigling, 
Arthur Gessler, 
Charlotte Grossiord
abstract:
Design of the VPDrought experiment in a Scots pine ( Pinus sylvestris ) forest at the Pfynwald research platform.
 
 
 Summary 
 
Atmospheric and soil drought are major, yet typically confounded, drivers of tree stress. Rising vapor pressure deficit (VPD) may impair forest function independently of soil moisture decline, yet stand-scale experimental separation in mature forests has remained unresolved. We tested whether atmospheric demand can be manipulated independently of soil water supply and how such manipulation propagates through the soil–plant system.
We established a factorial field manipulation in a  c.  130-yr-old  Pinus sylvestris  forest that independently modifies canopy VPD and soil water input using fine-mist VPD reduction, irrigation (+600 mm), and throughfall exclusion (−50% precipitation). Atmospheric and soil conditions were continuously monitored across depths over two growing seasons.
The experiment specifically targeted periods of high atmospheric evaporative demand, reducing VPD by an average of 21% when ambient VPD exceeded its 90 th  percentile. Soil drying followed sustained high-VPD phases, beginning in the topsoil and progressively later at depth. Despite identical water inputs, reduced VPD particularly altered deeper soil water trajectories, indicating plant-mediated feedbacks.
Atmospheric drought propagates through the soil–plant–atmosphere continuum rather than acting solely as an aboveground stressor. Explicit integration of atmospheric demand into experiments and ecosystem models is essential for predicting forest resilience under rising atmospheric drought.
 
 Zusammenfassung 
 
Atmosphärische Trockenheit und Bodentrockenheit sind wesentliche, jedoch meist sich gegenseitig überlagernde Ursachen für Stress bei Bäumen. Ein steigendes Dampfdruckdefizit (VPD) kann die Funktionsfähigkeit von Wäldern unabhängig von einer Abnahme der Bodenfeuchte beeinträchtigen. Bisher ist es noch nicht gelungen, diese Einflussgrößen auf Bestandesebene in Altbeständen experimentell zu trennen. Wir untersuchten, ob sich das Dampfdruckdefizit unabhängig von der Bodenwasserversorgung manipulieren lässt und wie sich eine solche Manipulation auf das Boden-Pflanzen-System auswirkt.
