title: Adaptive Cellular Responsiveness to Electrical Stimulation at the Skin‐Electrode Interface
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Wearable electrical stimulation (ES) devices are emerging platforms for wound healing, where cellular responses at the skin‐electrode interface critically influence therapeutic outcomes. Here, we demonstrate that skin cells dynamically adapt to sustained ES by upregulating voltage‐gated calcium channels (VGCCs) and enhancing their sensitivity to electrical cues. Using a transparent indium tin oxide (ITO)‐based bioelectronic platform, we find that ES‐induced upregulation of the L‐type VGCC Ca
                     V 
                    1.3 amplifies intracellular calcium (Ca
                     2+ 
                    ) influx during subsequent stimulation. ES delivered through a skin‐conformal ITO‐based wearable device similarly increases Ca
                     V 
                    1.3 expression in mouse wound tissue, accompanied by accelerated wound healing, enhanced collagen deposition, vascular remodeling, and changes in the CD206/iNOS macrophage‐associated marker balance. Pharmacological inhibition of L‐type VGCCs with nifedipine suppresses Ca
                     V 
                    1.3 upregulation and attenuates these regenerative responses, supporting a functional contribution of VGCC‐mediated Ca
                     2+ 
                    signaling to ES‐assisted wound repair. Human skin cells further exhibit enhanced Ca
                     2+ 
                    responsiveness and coordinated transcriptional and proteomic remodeling following sustained ES. These findings identify adaptive VGCC‐associated Ca
                     2+ 
                    signaling as a key cellular mechanism underlying sustained ES responses at the bioelectronic interface.

title: Surface‐Selective Pt Enrichment for Stabilizing Ultrathin 2D PtCu Nanosheets Toward Durable Oxygen Reduction
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Ultrathin Pt‐based 2D alloy nanosheets are promising electrocatalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) due to their high surface‐to‐volume ratios and favorable facet‐dependent activity. However, their thermodynamic instability and susceptibility to transition metal dissolution present critical barriers to their practical application. While surface Pt enrichment could mitigate such degradation, constructing Pt‐rich surfaces on 2D nanosheets remains challenging, as conventional approaches often induce structural collapse or undesired thickening. Herein, we report a surface‐selective Pt enrichment strategy via galvanic replacement to stabilize ultrathin PtCu nanosheets (PtCu NS/C) while preserving their unique 2D integrity. PtCu@Pt NS/C features a Pt‐enriched outer region and an alloyed subsurface, which effectively suppresses Cu exposure while maintaining beneficial electronic interactions. PtCu@Pt NS/C delivers high ORR activity, outperforming commercial Pt/C. More importantly, PtCu@Pt NS/C exhibits remarkable durability, with 17.5% mass activity loss after 30 000 accelerated stress test cycles. Notably, in single‐cell PEMFC configurations, PtCu@Pt NS/C demonstrates outstanding voltage stability with a minimal loss of 4 mV at 0.2 A cm
                     −2 
                    , whereas PtCu NS/C and Pt/C suffer much larger losses of 41 and 38 mV, respectively. This work demonstrates that preferential near‐surface Pt enrichment effectively stabilizes PtCu nanosheets, offering a surface‐engineering approach for improving the durability of ultrathin 2D alloy electrocatalysts.

title: Gradient‐Oxidized Bacterial Cellulose for Self‐Sustained Soil Moisture Sensing
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Soil moisture monitoring is pivotal to precision agricultural irrigation. Conventional soil moisture sensors rely on external power supplies and suffer from poor environmental compatibility. The facile fabrication of hydrovoltaic devices with asymmetric film structures remains challenging, and related designs tailored for soil scenarios are still insufficient. Here, we report an in situ‐grown planar asymmetric encapsulated bacterial cellulose (AEBC) device for self‐powered soil moisture sensing. Graphene oxide (GO) and carbon nanotubes (CNT) are sequentially embedded on opposite sides of the growing cellulose network via gravity‐assisted in situ assembly, forming an oxygen‐functional gradient. A LiCl‐doped Ecoflex hygroscopic layer is further integrated to continuously provide mobile ions and stabilize moisture uptake. The 35 µm‐thick device delivers a volumetric power density of 211.37 µW·cm
                     −3 
                    and maintains stable operation for over 20 days across wide temperature and pH ranges. A wireless monitoring system integrating the AEBC with deep learning‐based signal recognition achieves accurate soil moisture detection. The bacterial cellulose matrix can be biodegraded in soil, and degradation residues exert no adverse effects on plant growth. This work provides an in situ fabrication strategy for asymmetric hydrovoltaic films, offering a promising sustainable platform for self‐powered agricultural monitoring.

title: Rational Surface Engineering Reduces Advanced Glycation End‐Product Adsorption and Improves Implant Integration
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Advanced glycation end‐products (AGEs) accumulate in metabolic diseases such as diabetes and are closely associated with poor outcomes following implantation. However, how these molecules influence events at the biomaterial interface has remained largely unknown. Here, we identify AGEs as critical biointerfacial modifiers that adsorb onto implant surfaces, reprogram immune responses, promote fibrotic encapsulation, impair angiogenesis, and compromise osseointegration. This suggests a potential mechanism by which metabolic disease disrupts biomaterial–tissue integration. By engineering titanium surfaces enriched with amine or carboxyl functionalities, we create AGE‐resistant biointerfaces that effectively suppress pro‐inflammatory M1 macrophage polarization, promote an anti‐inflammatory M2 macrophage phenotype, reduce fibrotic encapsulation, enhance angiogenesis, and improve osseointegration across ex vivo, in vitro, and in vivo diabetic models. These findings establish disease‐informed surface chemistry as a design paradigm for next‐generation implants intended for metabolically compromised and other high‐risk patient populations.

title: CircFAM65A/CANX Condensates Sequester FAM134B to Inhibit ER‐phagy and Suppress Hepatocellular Carcinoma Progression
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   ER‐phagy has been implicated in tumor progression; however, its regulatory mechanisms in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain largely unexplored. Here, we identified circFAM65A as a novel circRNA that is downregulated in HCC and its overexpression suppressed HCC progression. Mechanistically, circFAM65A interacted with CANX and attenuated the CANX‐mediated promotion of ER‐phagy and HCC progression. Specifically, circFAM65A promoted CANX condensate formation, and these condensates sequestered FAM134B, reducing the FAM134B‐LC3 interaction and suppressing ER‐phagy. Furthermore, a biomimetic membrane‐coated nanoparticle (PLGA/circFAM65A@M‐3E11) was designed to deliver circFAM65A, which effectively inhibited HCC growth in vivo. Together, these findings identify circFAM65A as a regulator of CANX‐mediated ER‐phagy and support its delivery as a potential therapeutic strategy for HCC.

title: Adaptive Active Illumination Via Translationally and Axially Tunable Cascaded Metasurfaces
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Active three‐dimensional sensing requires accurate light delivery and sufficient return‐signal strength, while complex scenes require a tunable balance between local power concentration and illumination coverage. Collimated beam illumination supports a longer maximum detectable distance by concentrating optical power, whereas expanded beam illumination improves angular sampling efficiency by increasing coverage per projection. Existing active‐illumination approaches typically use fixed illumination patterns or predefined scanning trajectories, making it difficult to balance local power concentration for maximum detectable distance with illumination coverage for sampling efficiency. Here we propose an adaptive active‐illumination method based on translationally and axially tunable cascaded metasurfaces (TATCMs). TATCMs control the beam output angle within the field of view (FoV) through lateral translation and tune illumination coverage through axial‐spacing tuning. At an operating wavelength of 905 nm, the implemented TATCMs demonstrate continuous beam‐output‐angle control across an approximately 70°×70° FoV under a ±300 µm lateral stroke, while increasing the interlayer spacing by 2.64 mm expands collimated beam illumination with a measured divergence of 0.06° to provide continuous coverage across the FoV. Adaptive three‐dimensional reconstruction further demonstrates the potential of TATCMs as a compact planar illumination platform for scene‐adaptive three‐dimensional sensing in autonomous vehicles, unmanned aerial vehicles, and industrial robotics.

title: Methanol‐Regulated Interfacial Polymerization of Fluorinated Polyamide Membranes Enables Rapid Liquid Hydrocarbon Separation
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Interfacially polymerized polyamide membranes have revolutionized industrial desalination, yet their intrinsically polar networks are poorly suited for molecular separations in nonpolar liquid hydrocarbons. Herein, classical polyamide chemistry is extended to hydrocarbon separations through the incorporation of a hydrophobic trifluoromethyl‐substituted diamine. Methanol was introduced as a cosolvent to overcome the limited aqueous solubility of the fluorinated monomer while regulating interfacial polymerization. Systematic investigation revealed how methanol‐mediated interfacial reaction kinetics and fluorination collectively govern polyamide network formation and membrane structure. The resulting fluorinated polyamide membrane exhibited a 12‐fold increase in toluene permeance and a 51‐fold enhancement in toluene/1,3,5‐triisopropylbenzene (TIPB) separation factor relative to conventional polyamide membranes. The membrane maintained 96%–98% TIPB rejection while sustaining a high average toluene permeance of 0.17 L m
                     − 
                     2 
                    h
                     − 
                     1 
                    bar
                     − 
                     1 
                    during 21 days of continuous operation. Beyond model solute systems, the membrane demonstrated effective molecular discrimination in application‐relevant hydrocarbon mixtures, enabling the fractionation of representative Fischer–Tropsch liquids, rapid enrichment of linear α‐olefins, and efficient separation of light linear/branched alkanes as well as near‐boiling hydrocarbon mixtures. This work establishes fluorinated polyamide membranes as a versatile platform for nonpolar liquid hydrocarbon separations and expands the scope of the highly scalable interfacial polymerization technology beyond aqueous applications.

title:
Potassium‐Impurity‐Modulated Self‐Trapped Excitons and Energy Transfer in Phase‐Separated, Mn
                     4+ 
                    ‐Doped Li
                     2 
                    HfF
                     6
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Self‐trapped excitons (STEs) play an important role in the luminescence of halide materials, yet their formation and manipulation in complex fluorides remain largely underexplored. Here, Mn
                     4+ 
                    ‐doped Li
                     2 
                    HfF
                     6 
                    phosphors were synthesized by room‐temperature coprecipitation to investigate impurity‐modulated STEs and their role in Mn
                     4+ 
                    sensitization. High‐resolution neutron powder diffraction reveals impurity‐associated phase separation into two closely related Li
                     2 
                    HfF
                     6 
                    lattices. Photoluminescence and cathodoluminescence measurements resolve two broad host‐emission components: STE1, assigned to intrinsic Li
                     2 
                    HfF
                     6 
                    , and redshifted STE2, associated with a K‐containing lattice. Under high‐energy cathodoluminescence excitation, enhanced Mn
                     4+ 
                    red emission correlates with STE2 emission but not with STE1 emission, supporting a selective STE2 → Mn
                     4+ 
                    energy‐transfer pathway. Density functional theory ΔSCF (self‐consistent field) calculations yield distinct relaxed STE1 and STE2 configurations, confirming the K‐induced redshift of the STE emission. These results identify K‐associated STE2 as a key sensitizing state for Mn
                     4+ 
                    luminescence, establishing impurity modulation as an effective strategy for tuning excitonic emission and host‐to‐activator energy transfer in complex fluoride phosphors.

title: Rapid Solidification Brings Ultralow Thermal Conductivity and Superior Thermoelectric Performance for Intrinsic GeTe Alloy
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Intrinsic GeTe suffers from excessively high carrier concentrations caused by Ge vacancies and limitations in phase regulation, which constrain further enhancement of its thermoelectric performance. In this work, rapid solidification with glass fluxing techniques is employed to achieve a large undercooling of Δ
                     T 
                    = 112–122 K in the GeTe alloy for the first time. By Ge enrichment, the carrier concentration is tuned to an optimal range of 5.7 × 10
                     20 
                    cm
                     −3 
                    and the carrier mobility is enhanced to 75.3 cm
                     2 
                    V
                     −1 
                    s
                     −1 
                    . The stoichiometric GeTe alloy retains a portion of the high‐temperature cubic phase at room temperature, forming a rhombohedral‐cubic (α+β) uniform dual‐phase structure with a specific crystallographic orientation. DFT calculations of the band structure, density of states, and phonon spectrum reveal the influence of the α+β structure on electrical transport and thermal diffusion. This unique microstructure combined with multiscale defect engineering enables a high figure of merit (
                     zT 
                    ) of 1.32 at 700 K for the Ge
                     1.03 
                    Te alloy, with a total processing time of less than 2 h, significantly improving the preparation efficiency. This work demonstrates that liquid undercooling technology is an efficient preparation method for effectively regulating the phase composition and microstructure of thermoelectric alloys.

title: Thirteen quick tips for bacteriophage genome annotation
abstract: by Bishoy Maher Zaki, George Bouras, Andrew M. Kropinski, Alice R. Wattam, Robert A. Edwards, Ramy K. Aziz

title: Calsequestrin localization at RyR2 clusters enables calcium wave propagation in ventricular myocytes
abstract:
by David Conesa, Blas Echebarria, Leif Hove-Madsen, Yohannes Shiferaw, Enrique Alvarez-Lacalle 

Intracellular calcium waves in cardiac myocytes propagate through a fire-diffuse-fire mechanism in which calcium released from one RyR2 cluster diffuses to neighboring clusters and triggers their activation. Yet propagation faces a fundamental physical difficulty: the calcium signal must cross distances of 1–2  μ m between Z-planes while being attenuated by cytosolic buffering and diffusion, and at the same time the release site depletes its local sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium store. How waves propagate efficiently despite these constraints has remained unclear. We developed a three-dimensional computational model of mouse ventricular myocytes at submicrometer resolution to address this question. Our central finding is that co-localization of calsequestrin2 (CASQ2) with RyR2 clusters is required for robust wave propagation. In a physiological model, where CASQ2 is concentrated at release sites as observed experimentally, calcium waves propagate reliably across the cell with velocities that match the experimental range. In contrast, when CASQ2 is distributed uniformly throughout the sarcoplasmic reticulum, keeping total CASQ2 unchanged, the wavefront stalls. These results identify CASQ2–RyR2 co-localization as a key structural requirement for effective calcium wave propagation in ventricular myocytes.

title: An integrative computational approach for obstacle avoidance during action selection
abstract:
by Shan Zhong, Nader Pouratian, Paul Schrater, Vassilios Christopoulos 

Action selection in cluttered environments, where individuals must simultaneously pursue goals and avoid obstacles, presents a significant challenge for the brain. To understand the underlying mechanisms of action selection in such contexts, we propose a computational model that extends stochastic optimal control theory through a novel framework for obstacle avoidance. The model decomposes action selection into a weighted combination of individual control policies, each generated for either target approach or obstacle avoidance. By integrating value information from goals, obstacles, and actions into a unified measure of “relative desirability”, the model dynamically determines the contribution of each policy to the overall action selection process. We evaluated the framework using simulated target-reaching tasks in cluttered environments based on previous human studies. The results showed that the model qualitatively captures key features of human motor behavior, including the influence of obstacle properties on movement trajectories and the transient tendency to initiate movements toward obstacles before avoidance. This work offers new insights into the dynamic interaction between approach and avoidance behaviors, providing a basis for future studies of action selection in more complex and naturalistic settings.

title: Urbanisation drives parallel genomic divergence across cities and bumble bee species
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Background 
                     Urbanisation imposes pervasive environmental change, yet it remains unclear whether evolutionary responses to cities are largely idiosyncratic or whether similar selective pressures across cities repeatedly generate predictable genomic outcomes. 
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     Here, we analyse whole-genome data from 524 individuals of three widespread bumble bee species sampled across nine independent urban–rural pairs in Central Europe to test whether urban environments drive parallel evolutionary responses across cities and species. Genetic diversity responded idiosyncratically to urbanisation, with two species showing no detectable urban–rural differences and one species exhibiting reduced diversity in cities, consistent with species-specific ecological traits and habitat requirements. Despite weak population structure and high gene flow in all species, we detected consistent and replicated genomic divergence associated with urban environments. Genome–environment association analyses revealed parallel allele-frequency shifts at the same loci across independent cities for each species, while selective sweep scans identified repeated signals of positive selection in urban populations. Across species, urban-associated divergence was highly polygenic and occurred predominantly in non-coding regions with potential regulatory roles. Although the specific genes involved were largely species-specific, functional enrichment analyses revealed strong convergence across species, particularly in pathways related to physiological stress responses, neurocognitive and behavioural processes, metabolism and immunity. 
                   
                   
                     Conclusions 
                     Together, these results suggest that urban environments can impose recurrent selective pressures, generating predictable and parallel genomic responses across cities and species despite ongoing gene flow. More broadly, our findings highlight polygenic, potentially regulatory adaptation as an important component of evolutionary responses to urban environments.

title: Mitonuclear control of transcription complexes regulates tRNA splicing
abstract:
Background
                      The human genome has hundreds of tRNA genes, a subset of which is intervened by short introns. Transcription of the latter genes by RNA polymerase (Pol) III generates precursor tRNAs that undergo splicing by the tRNA splicing complex, in addition to the removal of flanking sequences by RNase P and RNase Z. The former enzyme consists of tRNA splicing endoribonuclease complex and tRNA ligase complex. However, it was unknown how and where the human tRNA splicing complex executes its function in cells. 
                  
                     Results
                      We show that transcription complexes assembled on intron-containing tRNA genes possess a tRNA ligase complex and that this enzyme is regulated by a mitonuclear communication mechanism. A cytoplasmic, mitochondria-associated HSPC117, the catalytic subunit of the tRNA ligase complex, transiently relocates to the nucleoplasm in the S phase of the cell cycle to promote the second step of splicing, exon ligation, of select tRNAs. This nuclear localized RTCB-type ligase acts as an integral part of transcription complexes. Knockout of HSPC117 or expression of an inactive mutant of this enzyme leads to severe inhibition of transcription and exon ligation due to the assembly of deficient transcription complexes. Inhibition also brings to deficiency of the perinucleolar compartments, as a result of reduced expression of the H1 RNA essential to Pol III transcription in cells. 
                  
                     Conclusions
                      This study demonstrates that transcription complexes execute splicing of select intron-containing tRNAs and that this two-stage reaction is time-based on a mitonuclear communication mechanism that controls the tRNA ligase HSPC117 in human cells.

title: Sequence design for three-dimensional genome folding using Akita Semifreddo
abstract: DNA sequence directs genome folding, which in turn shapes enhancer-promoter communication and gene expression. How to design DNA sequences that produce desired folding patterns remains largely unexplored. Here we present Akita Semifreddo, which combines an efficient "half-frozen" version of the AkitaV2 genome folding model with the Ledidi sequence optimizer to design DNA sequences with desired folding in silico. We demonstrate that this framework enables design for major folding features – boundaries, dots, and flames – with desired positions and strengths. In short, Akita Semifreddo provides a platform for dissecting the sequence grammar of genome folding and engineering synthetic regulatory landscapes.

title: ReadsRatio: a facile method for cell type deconvolution with cross-platform applications
abstract: Existing methylation-based cfDNA deconvolution methods are sensitive to sequencing depth, reference quality, and platform variability. We develope ReadsRatio, an approach to estimate tissue proportions using the ratio of unmethylated reads within cell type-specific marker regions, without requiring reference methylation intensity signals. Compared to conventional methods, ReadsRatio detects specific tissue involvement in both simulations and clinical cohorts involving lupus, kidney transplantation, and COVID-19. It maintains accuracy across sequencing platforms and at reduced sequencing depths, enabling substantial cost savings in our preliminary estimations. ReadsRatio provides a versatile, cost-efficient framework for cfDNA deconvolution with broad research and clinical applicability.

title:
Natural variation in a
                     
                       FtMYB32 
                     
                    ‐
                     
                       FtCES18 
                     
                    module drives
                     Rhizoctonia solani 
                    resistance by reprogramming jasmonate and flavonoid metabolism in Tartary buckwheat
abstract:
SUMMARY 
                   
                    Tartary buckwheat
                     (Fagopyrum tataricum 
                    ) is renowned for its adaptability to complex growing conditions and stress tolerance. However, soil‐borne necrotrophic pathogens such as
                     Rhizoctonia solani 
                    frequently cause devastating diseases that severely compromise its yield and quality. In this study, through a genome‐wide association study (GWAS), we identified a carboxylesterase gene,
                     FtCES18 
                    , and demonstrated that it acts as a core positive regulator of disease resistance in Tartary buckwheat. Overexpression of
                     FtCES18 
                    significantly enhanced plant resistance, whereas virus‐induced gene silencing (VIGS) led to a highly susceptible phenotype. Further analyses revealed that FtCES18 efficiently catalyzes the hydrolysis of methyl jasmonate (MeJA) into free jasmonic acid (JA), which initiates downstream JA‐Ile signaling and rapidly promotes endogenous jasmonate accumulation upon pathogen infection. This JA signaling cascade reprograms host flavonoid metabolism, promoting the substantial accumulation of downstream defensive flavonoids (such as rutin and quercetin). Furthermore, we found that the transcription factor FtMYB32 directly binds to the MBS cis‐element in the
                     FtCES18 
                    promoter to activate its expression. Notably, evolutionary analysis revealed a domestication‐associated C‐terminal truncation in the cultivated FtMYB32 that impairs its transactivation capacity, explaining the compromised basal resistance in cultivated accessions compared to their wild ancestors. Crucially, a natural single‐nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) in the
                     FtMYB32 
                    promoter defines a superior haplotype (hapC) conferring enhanced basal transcriptional activity. This natural variation in promoter activity controls the expression abundance of the
                     FtMYB32 
                    ‐
                     FtCES18 
                    module via a “dosage fine‐tuning” effect, which is subsequently amplified by the downstream metabolic cascade, ultimately contributing to the natural variation in disease resistance among different Tartary buckwheat accessions. This study provides valuable genetic resources and a theoretical basis for breeding novel Tartary buckwheat varieties with high disease resistance.

title:
Reconstructing Cenozoic grasslands in North America and western Eurasia: evidence for cold‐season grasses from
                     3D 
                    phytolith morphology
authors:
Rosalie M. Hermans, 
Timothy J. Gallaher, 
William H. Brightly, 
Callie Zender, 
Christophe Snoeck, 
Caroline A. E. Strömberg
abstract:
Summary 
                   
                     
                       
                         Pooideae, the largest grass subfamily, radiated in the Northern Hemisphere from the Paleocene onward and today dominates cold‐season and high‐altitude grasslands. Fossil phytolith assemblages suggest pooid‐rich ecosystems during the Oligocene–Miocene, but the lack of quantitative phytolith identification has limited reconstruction of early grassland composition and ecology. 
                       
                       
                         We combined 3D geometric morphometrics of grass silica short‐cell phytoliths (GSSCPs) with machine‐learning classification and phylogenetically informed climate modelling. A dataset of modern GSSCPs was used to classify Eocene–Miocene phytoliths from Türkiye and the US Great Plains and reconstruct paleoclimate. 
                       
                       
                         3D GSSCP morphology distinguished modern grass subfamilies and tribes. Fossil assemblages contained mainly phytoliths assigned to Bambusoideae and Pooideae (including Poeae I and II). In modern grasses, Crenate and Polylobate phytolith dimensions correlated with temperature and precipitation. Fossil Crenates and Polylobates yielded climate estimates warmer and wetter than today. Ancestral state reconstructions indicated milder winter conditions at early Pooideae nodes, with cold tolerance arising early. 
                       
                       
                         Major temperate grass lineages (Poeae I and II) were established earlier than previously recognized, and Pooideae‐rich grasslands were present by the Oligo‐Miocene under warmer, wetter climates than today. These findings demonstrate the value of 3D phytolith morphometrics for interpreting early grassland evolution.

title: Defining membrane‐bound transcription factors in plant stress responses
authors:
Zhihong Zhu, 
Detao Yi, 
Jingrui Peng, 
Yiwei He, 
Chong Wang, 
Junjie Li, 
Qun Hu, 
Jing Zou, 
Jianguo Wu, 
Shuai Zhang
abstract:
This review explains how membrane-associated transcription factors become active through mechanisms involving water channels or changes in membranes and organelles. It examines whether these pathways overlap, how they affect growth and defense, and what remains uncertain for improving crop resilience.
  
 ABSTRACT 
 Biotic and abiotic stresses rapidly alter water and H 2 O 2  fluxes, membrane fluidity, organelle redox state, and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) proteostasis, affecting nuclear gene expression. Membrane-bound transcription factors (MTFs) and related membrane-associated pathways regulate the generation, localization, and activity of nuclear-competent forms of transcription factors through proteolysis, unconventional mRNA splicing, and post-translational regulation. This mini review examines ER-to-Golgi trafficking and proteolytic activation of bZIP17/28, IRE1-dependent splicing of bZIP60/OsbZIP50, the varied activation mechanisms of NAC/NTLs, and PIP-associated MYBs. PIP–MYB studies support transporter participation in MTF activation, although the contributions of transport activity and physical interaction remain difficult to separate. Most bZIP and NAC/NTL pathways respond to changes in ER, membrane, or organelle status. We discuss their roles in proteostasis, growth restraint, and immunity, and how pathogens exploit them. We also assess the evidence for direct transporter–MTF coupling and indirect regulation by membrane state. Their use in crops will depend on establishing how endogenous MTFs are activated and switched off, and whether the resulting responses improve yield across environments.

title:
Disruption of OsMAPKKK24 activation by the
                     Xanthomonas oryzae 
                    effector XopY leads to compromised disease resistance in rice
authors:
Lilan Chen, 
Yongming Chen, 
Wencai Xu, 
Xiaofang Wu, 
Shanshan Deng, 
Zhanchun Wang, 
Dingzhong Tang, 
Wei Wang
abstract:
The kinase OsRLCK55 phosphorylates OsMAPKKK24 to positively regulate rice resistance against  Xanthomonas oryzae . To compromise this defense, the effector XopY targets OsMAPKKK24 and suppresses its autophosphorylation and the transphosphorylation mediated by OsRLCK55, ultimately leading to reduced disease resistance.

  
 ABSTRACT 
 Mitogen-activated protein (MAP) kinase (MAPK) cascades are highly conserved signaling modules that play crucial roles in plant disease resistance. Emerging evidence shows that MAPK cascades are potential targets of plant pathogen effectors. Bacterial leaf blight (BLB), caused by  Xanthomonas oryzae  pv.  oryzae  ( Xoo ), is a devastating disease in rice.  Xoo  secretes multiple effectors into host rice plants to suppress immune activation. XopY is a conserved effector across diverse  Xoo  strains; however, how XopY manipulates disease resistance and what its host targets are in rice remain largely unknown. Here, we report that XopY from the  Xoo  strain PXO86 interacts with the MAPK kinase kinase OsMAPKKK24 and RECEPTOR-LIKE CYTOPLASMIC KINASE 55 (OsRLCK55). OsRLCK55 phosphorylates OsMAPKKK24, and both contribute to rice BLB resistance by positively regulating early immune responses. XopY suppresses the activation of OsMAPKKK24 by enhancing its intramolecular interaction between the N- and C-terminal regions. The association of XopY with OsRLCK55 and OsMAPKKK24 also interferes with their interaction and suppresses OsRLCK55-mediated transphosphorylation of OsMAPKKK24, ultimately inhibiting MAPK activation and subsequent disease resistance. Taken together, these findings not only reveal that OsRLCK55 and OsMAPKKK24 are crucial for BLB resistance but also uncover a mechanism by which XopY compromises disease resistance by manipulating OsMAPKKK24 activation in rice.

title: Integration-free and cluster-free detection of localized differential gene coexpression in single-cell data with DiCoLo
abstract: Detecting changes in gene coordination patterns between biological conditions and identifying the cell populations in which these changes occur are key challenges in single-cell analysis. Existing approaches often compare gene coexpression between predefined cell clusters or rely on aligning cells across conditions. These strategies can be suboptimal when changes occur within small subpopulations or when batch effects obscure the underlying biological signal. To address these challenges, we introduce DiCoLo, a framework that identifies genes exhibiting differential colocalization, defined as changes in coordinated expression within localized cell neighborhoods - subsets of highly similar cells in the transcriptomic space. Importantly, DiCoLo does not rely on cell clustering or cross-condition alignment. For each condition, DiCoLo constructs a gene graph using Optimal Transport distances that reflect gene colocalization patterns across the cell manifold. Then, it identifies differential gene programs by detecting changes in connectivity patterns between the gene graphs. We show that DiCoLo robustly identifies differential gene colocalization even under weak signals or complex batch effects, outperforming existing methods across multiple benchmark datasets. When applied to mouse hair follicle development data, DiCoLo reveals coordinated gene programs and emerging cell populations driven by perturbations in morphogen signaling that underlie dermal condensate differentiation. Overall, these results establish DiCoLo as a powerful framework for uncovering localized differential transcriptional coordinated patterns in single-cell data.

title:
Chromosome-scale genome assembly and annotation of
                     Octodon degus
abstract:
High-quality reference genomes are essential for comparative and functional genomics yet remain unavailable for many emerging model organisms. Here, we report OctDeg2.0, a chromosome-level genome assembly and annotation of the degu (
                     Octodon degus 
                    ), generated using PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing and Hi-C scaffolding from a single male individual.
                     Octodon degus 
                    is of growing interest as a natural animal model for aging and Alzheimer's disease research. The 3.4 billion base-pair assembly comprises 28 autosomes and both sex chromosomes, with markedly improved contiguity and completeness over the prior short-read assembly while maintaining high base accuracy. The new assembly provides substantially enhanced gene annotation, clearer resolution of chromatin architecture and
                     cis 
                    -regulatory element landscapes, with much improved characterization of repetitive and structurally complex regions, including centromeres and segmental duplications. We present a streamlined and reproducible pipeline for high-resolution de novo genome assembly and gene annotation applicable to other emerging model organisms. This work establishes a robust genomic resource for studying molecular and cellular mechanisms in health and disease in
                     Octodon degus 
                    .

title: Single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomics reveal dynamic cell differentiation and storage product accumulation in rice endosperm
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Rice (Oryza sativa) endosperm, a major food source worldwide, accumulates starch, proteins, and lipids. Understanding the cellular and molecular mechanisms that govern endosperm development and storage product accumulation is crucial for improving grain yield and quality. Through single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomic analyses of 177,820 nuclei and 60,003 spatial spots across four developmental stages of the rice caryopsis, we identified 12 distinct cell types and delineated seven precise anatomical regions, thereby establishing a spatially resolved single-cell transcriptomic atlas of the developing rice endosperm. Using these cell type annotations, we inferred the developmental trajectories of endosperm cells, uncovered gene regulatory networks underlying cell differentiation, and identified three key transcription factors that regulate aleurone cell-fate determination. Furthermore, we observed cellular heterogeneity in the aleurone layer and the starchy endosperm and showed how this heterogeneity coordinates nutrient transport and storage product biosynthesis during rice grain filling. This study establishes a comprehensive cellular foundation and genetic regulatory network for understanding rice endosperm formation and storage product accumulation.

title: Ultrastable 4.99 V Li rich Mn-based cathodes achieved by catalytic-shielded and strain-buffered interface engineering
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Lithium-rich manganese-based layered oxides (LROs) offer high theoretical capacity but are limited by irreversible oxygen redox, voltage fade, and structural degradation upon cycling. Herein, we develop a dual-interface engineering strategy for LRO cathodes, integrating a catalytic-shielded carbon coating and interface-confined discrete spinel domains. The carbon layer decouples electrolyte decomposition from lattice-driven catalysis, suppressing cathode-electrolyte interphase growth and oxygen release, while subsurface-confined spinel phases establish three-dimensional Li+ transport pathways and mitigate lattice strain. Ex-situ hard/soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy confirm enhanced anionic redox reversibility and stable charge compensation. Consequently, the optimized LRO achieves an initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 93.1% with a discharge capacity of 295 mAh g−1 at 0.1 C, compared with 267 mAh g−1 and 79.0% for the pristine counterpart. It maintains 88.9% capacity after 150 cycles at 4.99 V (vs. 29.4% for pristine after 80 cycles) and 79.2% after 200 cycles at 45°C. Remarkably, a 1.58 Ah Si/C||HV-LRO pouch cell delivers 307 Wh kg−1 energy density and retains 70.7% capacity after 100 cycles at 0.8 C, demonstrating practical viability for high-energy applications. This work establishes a paradigm for stabilizing high-voltage LRO cathodes through spatially decoupled interfacial catalysis and reinforcement.

title: Phylogenomics of Cypriniformes, the most diverse order of freshwater fishes: consensus, challenges and limitations
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Cypriniformes, the most species-rich order of freshwater fishes (∼5,000 species), represents a key lineage for understanding vertebrate diversification in freshwater ecosystems. This clade includes several highly miniaturized and understudied lineages whose phylogenetic placements have long remained contentious. Here, we present the first phylogenomic analysis of Cypriniformes with complete family-level representation and broad genus-level coverage, encompassing 316 species comprising approximately 30% of all described genera. Our dataset integrates 257 newly assembled genomes with publicly available resources and analyzes multiple sets of genome-wide markers using both concatenation-based and coalescent-aware approaches. The general concordance among analytical frameworks indicates that the backbone topology of Cypriniformes is now established, allowing clear identification of well-supported clades and regions of persistent conflict. Our results strengthen the evolutionary relationships of several miniaturized lineages, while identifying recalcitrant relationships shaped by both biological processes and model artefacts that can yield superficially similar patterns of phylogenetic conflict. Our study substantially expands genomic representation and establishes a phylogenomic foundation for future comparative, developmental, and evolutionary research in this freshwater radiation.

title: Recurrent tandem duplication of a conserved enhancer underlies parallel genetic origins of rumplessness in chickens
abstract: Abstract Congenital caudal body truncation in chickens—the rumpless phenotype—provides a powerful model for studying vertebrate axis elongation. This trait has been linked to misexpression of  IRX1  and  IRX2  in the embryonic tail bud, and breed-specific candidate mutations, including a deletion upstream of  IRX1  proposed for the Piao breed, have been reported, yet whether the various breeds share a common causal basis has remained unresolved. By combining whole-genome resequencing, long-read sequencing, and population genomic analyses of four geographically isolated rumpless breeds (Chinese Piao, Japanese Uzurao, Belgian Barbu de Grubbe, and Chilean Araucana), we identify distinct tandem duplications of the  IRX1 / IRX2  intergenic region that converge on a single ∼700 bp conserved noncoding element, which we designate  EnhRp . Haplotype and breakpoint analyses reveal that these duplications arose through at least two mutational events rather than a single shared origin. Functional assays in chicken embryos demonstrate that duplicating  EnhRp  acts as a hypermorphic gain-of-function mutation, elevating enhancer activity in the tail bud in a dose-dependent manner, consistent with the ectopic  IRX1 / IRX2  expression. Our findings support a model of parallel evolution in which distinct structural variants recurrently target a specific  cis -regulatory element across at least two independent lineages, highlighting the critical role of noncoding variation in shaping morphological diversity.

title: SSAlign: fast and sensitive protein structure search at scale
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Motivation 
                     Predicted protein structure resources now contain hundreds of millions of models, turning structural comparison from a pairwise alignment task into a database-scale retrieval problem. Exhaustive structural aligners are computationally impractical at this scale, whereas fast structural-alphabet searches may discard remote or low-complexity homologs during prefiltering. Database-scale search therefore requires methods that combine rapid retrieval with sensitivity to global structural similarity. 
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     We present SSAlign, a protein structure search method that integrates SaProt sequence-structure embeddings, entropy-reduced dense retrieval, an SS-score predictor, and two-stage alignment refinement. In benchmarks on the Swiss-Prot, SCOPe40, and AFDB50 datasets, SSAlign showed competitive alignment quality and returned more TM-align-supported hits than Foldseek in recall-oriented evaluations. On AFDB50, 1000 queries against 53.7 million structures completed in 3150 s on CPUs and 2290 s with GPU prefiltering, corresponding to 103-fold and 142-fold speedups over Foldseek, respectively. On SCOPe40, SSAlign increased the area under the curve (AUC) by 20.2% at family level and 33.3% at superfamily level. In simple-fold antimicrobial peptide case studies, SSAlign retrieved candidates that were not returned by Foldseek under the tested settings, indicating its utility as a fast candidate-generation tool for proteome-scale structural search. 
                   
                   
                     Availability and implementation 
                     The source code for SSAlign is publicly available at https://github.com/ISYSLAB-HUST/SSAlign. The software version and test data used in this study are archived on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23432919. Datasets and prebuilt indices can be downloaded from http://bioinfo.isyslab.info/ssalign/download/section/ssalign/.

Correction for Croke et al., Meta-analysis and public policy: Reconciling the evidence on deworming
Correction for Kawamura, Proof of the density threshold conjecture for pinwheel scheduling
Making unpaid breastfeeding count
Restructuring the nitrogen cycle and sparing cropland by feeding insect-derived protein to global livestock
Reading strong selection from modest GWAS hits
Rembrandt through the eyes of the machine: Toward explainable Human–AI collaboration in painting attribution
abstract: With questions that persist for centuries, art attribution is a complex detective effort that shapes cultural identity. Our goal is to complement human expertise, providing statistical and visual arguments that shed new light on discussions about great masters like Rembrandt and beyond, with long-term implications for art analysis and human–AI collaboration. We present an AI-driven explainable approach to assist painting attribution with up to 97.9% recall, 95.8% accuracy when highly confident, and methods that identify the most relevant areas. This work supports human–AI collaboration by incorporating expert guidance, expanding the outputs with explainable visualizations, tailoring settings to users’ needs, thorough calibrations to avoid overconfidence, and building a dataset that balances quality with quantity and focuses on comparable artists like a master’s pupils and teachers.

title: New molecular and historical evidence on ancient Egyptian embalming
abstract:
Mumia vera aegyptiaca 
                    was a mummy-derived medicinal substance widely used in medieval and early modern medicine, yet its material composition and biological activity remain poorly understood. Here, we integrate Egyptological and pharmaceutical-historical analysis of 41 textual sources with LC–MS/MS-based metabolomics, molecular networking, machine-learning-assisted annotation, and bioactivity testing to investigate ancient Egyptian embalming materials and historical
                     Mumia vera 
                    samples. We analyzed 24 objects from university and pharmacy museum collections, including historical
                     Mumia vera 
                    products, mummified body parts, embalming residues, bandages, and two mummified skulls. Comparative metabolomics revealed substantial heterogeneity among materials labeled as
                     Mumia vera 
                    , but also recurrent molecular signatures consistent with aged conifer resins, including oxidized abietane-type diterpenoids. Several samples contained
                     Aloe 
                    -associated metabolites, including aloeresin A/D- and aloin-related compounds. These data reveal
                     Aloe 
                    -associated metabolites in ancient Egyptian embalming-related materials and support the presence of
                     Aloe 
                    spp.-derived exudates in selected samples. The convergence of molecular and textual evidence further raises the possibility that a previously unresolved Egyptian term from the 2nd millennium BC may refer to
                     Aloe 
                    sp. or an
                     Aloe 
                    -derived product. Comparative metabolomics also linked an inconspicuous powder sample to a specific mummified head, although their curatorial association had not been securely documented. Finally, a historical
                     Mumia vera aegyptiaca 
                    extract modestly protected MDCK cells from influenza virus-induced cytopathic effects, whereas the isolated major compound 7-oxodehydroabietic acid was inactive on its own. Together, these findings show how integrating textual scholarship, pharmaceutical history, and molecular analysis can refine the interpretation of ancient Egyptian embalming practices, museum objects, and historical medicines.

title: Evaluation of possibly fabricated references in 500,000 science, engineering, and computing papers
abstract: References to nonexistent studies are well documented in biomedical research, but evidence outside biomedicine is limited. We analyzed a stratified random sample of 500,000 peer-reviewed journal papers in chemistry, physics, materials science, engineering, and computer science published from January 2023 through March 31, 2026, using OpenAlex, a large open index of scholarly works and citations. Our automated pipeline classified 1,135 references across 619 papers as fabricated, with 85.8% precision on masked expert review; fabricated is an operational label for a claimed title that could not be located in any of seven bibliographic and open-web sources. Affected-paper prevalence rose from 1 in 1,600 (6.3 per 10,000) in 2023 to 1 in 435 (23.0 per 10,000) in the first quarter of 2026, and full-period rates differed roughly sixfold across fields, from 25.6 per 10,000 papers in physics to 4.3 in chemistry. Most affected papers contained one or two fabricated references, but the 27 papers containing five or more accounted for more than a third of all fabricated references identified. Applying each field’s rate to the approximately 7 million OpenAlex papers indexed in these fields gives an estimated 8,500 papers carrying at least one fabricated reference. Routine automated reference verification at submission, together with retrospective screening of the published literature, can detect fabricated references before and after they enter the scientific record.

title: Resource-driven release from lag phase triggers the world’s fastest and largest coastal plant invasion
abstract:
What determines the duration of invasion lag phases remains one of the major unresolved questions in invasion ecology. Lag phases are often attributed to genetic adaptation, propagule limitation, or demographic stochasticity, yet the mechanisms by which environmental conditions regulate establishment success remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate the explosive expansion of
                     Spartina alterniflora 
                    along the coast of mainland China, the most rapid plant invasion recorded globally. Combining field experiments, demographic theory, and historical invasion records, we identify resource-regulated Allee effects as a mechanism governing the invasion lag phase. Experimentally, sediment accretion substantially increases clonal propagation and sexual reproduction, weakening demographic constraints associated with establishment and accelerating the transition from sparse founder patches to highly reproductive meadows. A theoretical model reveals that sediment-driven positive feedbacks weaken demographic constraints during establishment and shorten the duration of Allee effects. Historical invasion records spanning both sides of the Pacific Ocean support the predicted negative relationship between sedimentation rate and lag-phase duration. Invasion lag phases can arise solely from interactions between species traits and environmental resource availability. Contrary to the prevailing view that Allee effects are fixed properties of species, our results show that their duration is regulated by environmental resource availability. More broadly, environmental resources can govern ecological transitions by controlling transient dynamics during establishment, providing an explanation for why some introduced populations remain dormant for decades, whereas others rapidly become dominant ecosystem engineers.

title: Autonomous disproofs of the Erdős unit distance conjecture with GPT-5.5 Pro
abstract: OpenAI’s disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture marks a milestone in AI for mathematical research. However, the result relied on an internal model with undisclosed test-time compute, hindering independent reproduction and analysis by the community. Here we present a simple autonomous agent built on the publicly available GPT-5.5 Pro. The agent uses a problem-agnostic three-stage prompting pipeline: brainstorm, execute, and review. We ran eight independent trials with web search disabled. In each trial, the agent produced a correct or essentially correct disproof of the conjecture. The resulting proofs are diverse and do not merely reproduce earlier AI-generated proofs. Since GPT-5.5 Pro was released nearly a month before OpenAI published its disproof, our evaluation is free from data contamination. The system operates efficiently, using an average of 106.7 k reasoning tokens per trial. We release our code and all outputs, providing a publicly accessible AI agent to resolve this conjecture autonomously.

title: Fine and ultrafine Martian dust presents additional risks for future crewed missions to Mars
abstract:
Surface dust poses a fundamental challenge to extraterrestrial human exploration, a reality demonstrated by the operational hazards encountered during Apollo lunar missions. On Mars, this challenge is compounded by regional and global dust cycles that coat sensitive hardware. While previous Mars missions have constrained the bulk geochemistry of coarser particulates (≳3 µm), the properties of the fine (≲2.5 µm) and ultrafine (≲0.1 µm) fractions remain largely uncharacterized. This knowledge gap is critical as these respirable particles, defined by their ability to bypass upper respiratory defenses, possess the mobility to penetrate deep into the alveolar regions of biological systems, presenting a systemic toxicity risk to future crews. Here, we report on direct examination of these fine and ultrafine Martian dust fractions using X-ray fluorescence through the analysis and modeling of data acquired by the
                     Perseverance 
                    rover. We observe particulates measuring as small as 100 to 200 nm on spacesuit samples and calibration targets. Compositionally, this dust is a phosphorus-, iron-, and sulfur-enriched mafic silicate accumulating on materials analogous to the planned external layers of potential crew systems. Our results emphasize the importance of a thorough characterization of Martian dust properties in terrestrial laboratories to better prepare future crews and crew support systems destined for the surface of Mars.

title: FMRI-guided focal transcranial magnetic stimulation of anterior cingulate cortex reduces opioid seeking and restores connectivity
abstract: Relapse remains a major challenge in opioid addiction treatment. Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) has emerged as a potential therapeutic strategy for addiction, yet results had been mixed due to empirically selected stimulation targets and limited knowledge of neural circuit engagement. Here, we used a focal rat TMS platform to test whether high-density theta-burst stimulation (hdTBS) of the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), a corticostriatal node implicated in opioid relapse by prior causal and longitudinal functional MRI studies, decreases relapse-like oxycodone seeking and associated circuit dysfunction. Male rats self-administered oxycodone intravenously for 14 d and then underwent 13 d of electric barrier-induced abstinence, a procedure that suppresses drug taking while preserving drug availability and drug-associated context. During abstinence, the rats received seven daily sessions of sham stimulation or ACC-targeted hdTBS, with relapse tests and longitudinal functional MRI acquired during early and late abstinence to assess the behavioral and circuit-level effects of stimulation. Sham-treated rats showed a time-dependent increase (incubation) in oxycodone seeking and reduced ACC connectivity with dorsal and ventral striatum. In contrast, ACC-targeted hdTBS prevented incubation of oxycodone seeking and reversed abstinence-associated ACC-striatal connectivity reductions. Stimulation-sensitive functional circuits showed spatial correspondence with tracer-defined ACC projection patterns, suggesting that anatomical connectivity is critical to the circuit-level effects of focal stimulation. These findings support ACC-centered corticostriatal circuits as mechanistically informed targets for neuromodulation in opioid addiction and introduce a preclinical framework for linking stimulation, behavior, and longitudinal circuit remodeling.

title: Behavioral evidence for two-stage sleep in spiders
abstract:
Sleep is a fundamental behavioral state found across the animal kingdom, yet most of what we know about sleep is heavily vertebrate-biased. Studies are scarce or nonexistent in all but a few invertebrate lineages. A recent study of an REM sleep-like behavior in a jumping spider has reported unexpected parallels to sleep expression in vertebrates. So far, experimental evidence that these behavioral indicators truly represent sleep was lacking in spiders. Here, we present a comprehensive investigation into sleep behavior in the spider
                     Portia fimbriata 
                    (Salticidae). We demonstrate diurnal activity, a free-running circadian rhythm, robust sleep architecture, regularly occurring REM-like behaviors, elevated arousal thresholds during those REM-like states, as well as rebound effects following sleep disruption. We conclude that the behavior we observe in spiders is behavioral sleep, providing evidence for an REM-like sleep substate in a terrestrial invertebrate. These results contribute to fundamental questions about the evolution and function of sleep across animals.

title: Position-specific isotope signatures evolve during a reversible reaction
abstract:
Position-specific isotope distributions capture information about reaction dynamics, metabolism, and environmental processes, encoding the formation history of organic molecules. Kinetic and equilibrium isotope effects are fundamental drivers of isotope fractionation, yet how these effects are expressed in position-specific isotope distributions remains poorly constrained. Here, we use glucose mutarotation as a model reaction for tracking the evolution of position-specific isotope ratios in a system in disequilibrium. In aqueous solution, α- and β-glucose interconvert through a low-abundance open-chain intermediate, providing an ideal framework for probing isotope effects within a single molecular pool at natural
                     13 
                    C abundance. Using NMR spectroscopy, we simultaneously measure glucose anomer populations and position-specific
                     13 
                    C/
                     12 
                    C ratios, enabling direct, time-resolved observations of isotope fractionation at the anomeric (C1) carbon. Starting from α-glucose, initial β-glucose formation generates a large transient isotope disequilibrium driven by unequal forward and reverse kinetic isotope effects, producing a temporary divergence in
                     13 
                    C abundance of more than 30‰ between anomers. Continued interconversion redistributes the isotopes and yields an equilibrium difference of ~7‰ between α- and β-glucose at the C1 position. Together, these results demonstrate how kinetic and equilibrium isotope effects acting within a reversible reaction can generate substantial, time-dependent intramolecular isotope heterogeneity, with potential implications for how position-specific isotope signatures emerge and propagate through (biogeochemical) reaction networks.

title: Anchoring Anatolian tree-rings and Mesopotamian chronology with single-year radiocarbon patterns and ice-core evidence
abstract:
The historical chronology of Mesopotamia offers a key chronological bridge to connect the Near East and eastern Mediterranean during the second millennium BCE. It is unusually rich in written records, including king lists, administrative documents, royal inscriptions, and astronomical observations. The latter offer a number of alternate possible absolute anchor points, resulting in competing high, middle, low, and ultra-low temporal frameworks. Establishing which of these is correct has consequences far beyond Mesopotamia. Tree-ring sequences from preserved timbers at archaeological sites in Anatolia, linked directly to Mesopotamia via the Old Assyrian trade network, could provide the answer. However, attempts have been limited by the lack of calendar secured dendrochronological dating for these timbers. Here we develop transferable methodologies in single-year radiocarbon analysis, utilizing patterns of
                     14 
                    C preserved in single tree rings from Anatolian timbers to anchor their combined chronology 2072 BCE–744 BCE. This provides a calendrically-secured reference chronology for wood samples from Anatolian sites during this period as well as an annually resolved paleoclimatic record. Tree-ring dates are combined with archaeological and high-resolution ice-core evidence to evaluate the competing chronological frameworks for Mesopotamia between 2000 and 1500 BCE. Remaining dating uncertainties are constrained in strong support of the middle–low chronology.

title: A spatially deployable iron redox rheostat tunes root growth under nutritional stress
abstract:
Root growth must continuously adjust to fluctuating nutrient availability, yet the mechanisms that quantitatively integrate environmental signals into developmental responses remain poorly understood. Distinct nutrient stresses, including ammonium toxicity and phosphate deficiency, inhibit primary root growth through iron-dependent processes, suggesting that iron acts as a central regulatory node. Here, we show that plants use an antagonistic module composed of CYBDOM ferrireductases and LPR ferroxidases to regulate apoplastic iron homeostasis and control root growth in a graded manner. Genetic perturbation of this module demonstrates that root growth inhibition scales quantitatively with iron accumulation, supporting a proportional control mechanism rather than a binary response. Loss of CYBDOM function causes excessive iron accumulation, elevated reactive oxygen species, and impaired meristem activity, whereas increased CYBDOM activity buffers iron deposition and confers resistance to stress. Mechanistically, iron-induced oxidative stress promotes
                     HYP1 
                    expression, which in turn limits further iron accumulation. Transcriptomic analyses distinguish ammonium-specific responses from Fe-associated transcriptional changes enriched in redox buffering and cell-wall remodeling. Finally, we show that this regulatory module is redeployed in distinct tissues under phosphate deficiency, indicating that plants reuse a conserved iron-based mechanism to coordinate growth across environmental contexts. Together, our findings establish genetically controlled Fe accumulation as a key determinant of developmental plasticity under nutrient stress.

title: The scope and severity of bat fatalities at US wind energy facilities
abstract: Wind turbines are a major source of bat fatalities in the United States, yet the magnitude and species-specific patterns of these fatalities have remained poorly quantified because monitoring has been site-specific, unstandardized, and not designed for landscape-level synthesis. In the most comprehensive analysis to date, we synthesized 499 postconstruction monitoring reports and developed a multispecies Bayesian hierarchical framework with an adapted N-mixture model to pool information across sites and estimate total fatalities for ten bat species across the conterminous United States from 1981 to 2024. Our analysis predicts approximately 18.7 million bat fatalities over this period, with substantially higher species-specific totals than previously estimated. Our framework provides a landscape-level analysis that can predict fatalities for unmonitored locations and years, identify landscape-level drivers of fatalities, produce a multidecade hindcast of cumulative losses due to wind energy, and map where species-specific risk is highest. Although limitations and uncertainty remain, the magnitude of predicted fatalities may be comparable to total losses from white-nose syndrome, another major threat to North American bat populations. These threats affect largely different species, suggesting their impacts may compound, but updated population-level impact assessments could reveal potential cumulative effects. Our estimates of species-specific covariate relationships with rotor-swept area, ground clearance, land cover, and proximity to rivers, highlight opportunities to help reduce impacts through wind turbine design and siting. This work establishes a generalizable landscape-level framework for evaluating wildlife fatalities at wind energy facilities and highlights how coordinated monitoring, data sharing, and population-level impact assessments could further inform conservation efforts.

title: Human organ trafficking and missing persons in China
abstract: The persistent shortage of human organs for transplantation has long been a global challenge. The prospect of substantial profit creates strong incentives for illegal organ trafficking, including murder for organ harvesting, yet empirical evidence remains scarce. This study addresses this gap by exploiting a unique quasi-natural experiment created by China’s organ policy reform. From 1984 to 2014, executed prisoners were the primary source of transplant organs in China. In 2015, the Chinese government abolished the use of organs from executed prisoners, sharply exacerbating the organ shortage. Following this policy change, the number of missing persons rose notably nationwide. Employing difference-in-differences and triple-difference strategies, we show that, compared to cases unrelated to organ trafficking (e.g., voluntary disappearances), the number and incidence of involuntary missing persons plausibly related to organ trafficking increased significantly after 2015. The effects are especially pronounced among individuals with mental illness and in regions with higher transplant demand and greater transplant capacity. Although we do not directly observe organ trafficking, the spatial, temporal, and demographic patterns we document are consistent with the hypothesis that increased organ scarcity intensified incentives for illicit organ procurement. More broadly, the findings suggest that severe organ shortages may generate unintended and highly harmful consequences, even in a low-crime setting such as China. These results underscore the importance of accounting for behavioral responses and illicit-market incentives when designing policies that restrict the supply of scarce, high-value goods such as transplant organs.

title: Changes in American adolescents’ outdoor time over two decades
abstract: Spending time outdoors provides opportunities for physical activity, exposure to natural light, and social contact. Although young people’s time use has changed substantially in recent decades, little is known about long-term trends in adolescents’ outdoor engagement. This question is especially important because adolescence is a period of major life transitions and the development of lasting behavioral habits. This study examines 20-y trends in time spent outdoors among American adolescents using time-diary data from 14,235 individuals aged 15 to 19 in the 2003–2023 American Time Use Survey, a nationally representative survey of the US population. We describe trends in outdoor exposure and examine associations between outdoor time and leisure behaviors, including computer use for leisure, indoor physical activity, and time spent with friends. We find that outdoor engagement among boys has declined sharply, erasing a long-standing male advantage and causing boys’ participation levels to converge with girls’ at similarly low rates. Greater time spent in computer-based leisure was associated with less outdoor time, particularly among boys, whereas time spent with friends was positively associated with outdoor engagement for both sexes. Indoor physical activity did not change over the observation period and did not offset declines in outdoor time. These findings suggest that broader changes in leisure activities may be reshaping how young people engage with outdoor environments. Further research is needed to better understand the factors underlying these trends and their potential long-term implications.

title: circEPSTI1 regulates miR-942-5p–SERPINE1–AKT1 signaling axis to enhance dengue infection and is suppressed by Tiplaxtinin
abstract: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have recently been identified as crucial regulators of gene expression in various diseases. Their role in dengue remains unexplored. In this study, circEPSTI1 induction was observed in peripheral blood mononuclear cells and plasma of dengue patients. The induction of circEPSTI1 is interferon-dependent and enhances DENV infection by sponging the expression of miR-942-5p. The antiviral role of miR-942-5p is mediated by bidirectional inhibition through targeting conserved genomic sequences of the DENV genome of different subtypes across NS1, NS3, and NS5 and the host AKT1 signaling pathway. RNA-seq analysis of DENV-infected circEPSTI1 knockdown A549 cells identified SERPINE1 and AKT1 signaling pathways to be dysregulated significantly. circEPSTI1 relieves the inhibition of miR-942-5p over DENV genomic RNA and the host SERPINE1 to activate AKT1 signaling. The activation of AKT1 signaling facilitates cell survival and enhances DENV replication. The expression of SERPINE1 and circEPSTI1 was upregulated in Dengue patients, and pharmaceutical inhibition of SERPINE1 through Tiplaxtinin inhibits the DENV replication by reducing the expression of circEPSTI1. Overall, our result demonstrates the therapeutic potential of Tiplaxtinin by targeting the circEPSTI1–miR-942-5p–SERPINE1–AKT1 axis in dengue treatment.

title: Spatial reorganization during post-collapse population growth suggests conspecific attraction in baleen whale nursing grounds
Sources and sinks: Geoclimatic dynamics shaped the assembly of endemic fauna in the world’s Third Pole
abstract: The Qinghai–Tibet Plateau (QTP), a biodiversity hotspot shaped by tectonic and climatic forces, has seen significant progress in understanding its floristic origins. However, a comprehensive, multitaxon perspective on how its terrestrial fauna assembled remains lacking. Here we integrate time-calibrated phylogenies of over 20,000 species from five major groups (invertebrates, amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals), to reconstruct the evolutionary history of 527 terrestrial animal species endemic to the QTP. Our finding reveals that the QTP has functioned both as a center of in situ diversification and as a “biogeographic sink” that receives species from surrounding regions, however, with pronounced subregional differentiation: the Hengduan Mountains acted primarily as a diversification source, while the Himalaya and the Plateau Platform acted as sinks, accumulating lineages from adjacent regions. The Eocene–Oligocene climatic transition, rather than late Neogene uplift, initiated sustained faunal diversification and biotic exchange. Across subregions, distinct uplift histories and monsoon regimes drove asynchronous evolutionary trajectories, showing that even geographically adjacent regions can exhibit distinct accumulation patterns of lineages. Notably, integrating our faunal evidence with recent floristic assembly data reveals a consistent “plants first, animals later” pattern across the QTP and its subregions, suggesting that early-arriving plant lineages created ecological niches that facilitated subsequent faunal colonization and diversification. This framework advances our understanding of how mountain biotas assemble over time, with implications extending far beyond the QTP.

title: In vitro binding energies capture Klf4 occupancy across the human genome
abstract:
Transcription factors (TFs) regulate gene expression by binding to specific genomic loci determined by DNA sequence. Their sequence specificity is commonly summarized by a consensus binding motif. However, eukaryotic genomes contain billions of low-affinity DNA sequences to which TFs associate with a sequence-dependent binding energy. We currently lack insight into how the genomic sequence defines this spectrum of binding energies and the resulting pattern of TF localization. Here, we set out to obtain a quantitative understanding of sequence-dependent TF binding to both motif and nonmotif sequences. We achieve this by first pursuing accurate measurements of physical binding energies of human TF Krüppel-like factor 4 (Klf4) to a library of short DNA sequences in a fluorescence-anisotropy-based bulk competitive binding assay. Second, we show that the highly nonlinear sequence dependence of Klf4 binding energies can be captured by combining a linear model of binding energies with an Ising model of the coupled recognition of nucleotides by a TF. In this model, nucleotide–TF interfaces collectively switch between two states, weak binding and strong nucleotide-specific binding, and the states of neighboring interfaces are coupled with
                     
                       
                         
                           J 
                           ∼ 
                           2 
                           
                           
                             k 
                             B 
                           
                           T 
                         
                       
                     
                    . We find that this statistical mechanics model parameterized by our in vitro measurements captures Klf4 binding patterns on an individual long DNA molecule stretched in the optical tweezer, and is predictive for Klf4 occupancy across the entire human genome without additional fit parameters.

title: Spontaneous replication fork collapse regulates telomere length homeostasis in wild-type yeast
abstract: In most eukaryotes, the enzyme telomerase maintains the termini of linear chromosomes through the addition of repetitive telomeric sequences. It is widely assumed that the primary site of action for telomerase is the single-stranded G-rich overhang at the ends of linear chromosomes. However, increasing evidence indicates that a second telomerase substrate is generated in response to replication stress as the replisome traverses duplex telomeric DNA. We show here that this second substrate, created by spontaneous replication fork collapse in wild-type budding yeast, is elongated by telomerase at a much higher frequency than fully replicated chromosome termini. Furthermore, as much as ~200 nucleotides can be added in a single cell division to newly collapsed forks, indicating that replication fork collapse and the subsequent response by telomerase is a major determinant of telomere length homeostasis. This challenges a long-standing model which posits a length-sensing mechanism that assesses individual telomeres to determine whether yeast chromosome ends are in “telomerase-extendible” versus “telomerase-non-extendible” states. We propose that these two states are instead structurally and temporally distinct substrates for telomerase, generated by two different processes (fork collapse versus completion of DNA replication). We also show that fork collapse at telomeres is kept in check by a telomere-dedicated Cdc13/Stn1/Ten1 complex in collaboration with the canonical RPA complex, indicating that these two complexes stabilize single-stranded DNA exposed at the replication fork. Although failures during DNA replication are often genotoxic events, this represents an opposing example in which fork collapse has been co-opted to promote genome stability.

title: Solid-state laser refrigeration of nanoscale quantum sensors
abstract:
Photothermal heating remains a major challenge during the optical excitation of nanoscale quantum sensors [C. Bradac, S. F. Lim, H. C. Chang, I. Aharonovich,
                     Adv. Opt. Mater. 
                     8 
                    , 2000183 (2020)]. At low laser powers, heating of the sensor leads to the thermal drift of quantum electronic transition energies. At high laser powers, sensors degrade due to thermally induced phase transitions, including melting. Here, we report a general approach for mitigating the photothermal heating of nanoscale quantum sensors through solid-state laser refrigeration of the sensors’ underlying substrate. Experimentally, both nanodiamonds and gold nanocrystals are attached separately to a ceramic laser-cooling substrate through van der Waals interaction. A combination of Debye–Waller factor thermometry and optically detected magnetic resonance spectroscopy of nitrogen vacancy centers is used to demonstrate that solid-state laser refrigeration of the substrate can reduce the temperature of attached nanodiamond payloads by 25 ± 3 K below steady-state operating temperatures. Stokes/anti-Stokes Raman spectroscopy is used to demonstrate reduced photothermal heating of plasmonic gold nanocrystals by 8.8 ± 2.7 K during surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy sensing of rhodamine-6G molecules. These results suggest that solid-state laser cooling could open up experimental possibilities for rapid feedback-controlled cooling of a wide range of nanoscale quantum resources.

title: Global high rates of anaerobic methane oxidation at marine cold seeps recorded by isotope bonding in seep carbonates
abstract:
Microbial anaerobic oxidation of methane (AOM) regulates the flux of methane (CH

Accordingly, we estimate a mean AOM rate of
