title: Equity dimensions of future vulnerabilities to climate hazards: Long-term spatial population projections for New York City consistent with Shared Socioeconomic Pathways
abstract: Projections of future population are important for a myriad of reasons. Large cities, states, and countries routinely produce near- and mid-range population projections. In the context of climate change, the Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP) framework is used at global and national scales to project long-term population to inform future emissions scenarios and understand future climate-related exposures and impacts. Much less consideration has been given to long-term projections at smaller scales, even though climate impacts are place based and cities now host most of the world’s population. Cities and their metropolitan regions are complex, heterogeneous in terms of population, environmental, and built features. Thus, using global or national-scale approaches overlooks important aspects of urban futures. Cities are diverse, fluid population centers home to migrants, with employment opportunities yet substantial inequality. These quintessential city-centric features are ignored in global/national-scale population projection methods, including long-term ones consistent with the SSPs. Leveraging state-level SSP-based projections, here we extend that approach for New York City, currently home to 8.8 million persons. Combining multistate and multiregional demographic projection and spatial downscaling models, we project county-level population by racial/ethnic groups and age–sex to 2100 and downscale to 100 m. Such projections allow for an equity lens to inform assessments of future vulnerabilities to climate hazards. Four of the five SSPs project that the population of New York City will be smaller and much older at the end of the century, though these futures are dependent on demographic assumptions about fertility and especially migration.

title: Populations, exposures and outcomes: How social media data is poised to advance climate-demography research
abstract: As the natural environment continues to change, there is a shared sense among researchers, policymakers, and health practitioners that we need to better understand the impacts of those changes on health and health behaviors for individuals and populations. “Big” social media data, including large datasets from platforms like X (formerly Twitter), Reddit, Facebook, TikTok, and YouTube, provide access to previously hard-to-reach populations. These data are posed to revolutionize the data landscape in climate change research; however, there are limitations and ethical concerns with data from these platforms, such as ethical questions, biases, noise, and a distinct underrepresentation of marginalized groups. These issues could hamper the adoption of social media data in research on climate change and health. In this commentary, we propose leveraging and augmenting a “human-in-the-loop” approach that uses humans in data extraction, quality assurances, and model testing to ensure data quality and overcome known limitations of social media data. Using examples from health data, we propose new horizons in climate change health research made possible with qualitative research methods.

title: Propagating shocks and transitions across networked food systems: Insights from multiplayer microeconomic modeling
abstract: Accelerating global change is affecting coupled natural ecosystems and human activities in every part of the world. The local and regional expressions of these changes are a product of interacting and networked systems such that a shock, trend or development transition in one region, ecosystem, or sector can propagate impacts to other regions, ecosystems, and sectors. Informed adaptation and development strategies require an understanding of how signals propagate through these coupled systems and regions. Here, we synthesize findings from our work in Ethiopia and Mali, where we developed and applied a modeling system designed to capture cross-sector dynamics of networked food, water, and energy systems at subnational scale. We approach the problem using a multiplayer microeconomic model that accounts for diverse objectives through chains of food production, distribution, and consumption that connect resource regions to market regions. This paper draws lessons from three case studies in Ethiopia and one in Mali that are designed to examine impacts of a subnational climate shock (drought), a centralized national policy decision (export restrictions in response to food shortage), a distributed development strategy (solar-powered groundwater irrigation), and an external intervention (food aid). In each case, we consider how an initial signal propagates through the country via markets, infrastructure, and interactions between economic actors. An understanding of this propagation can inform strategies for food security in a changing climate.

title: Decoding climate anomalies—From scientifically sound to societally relevant
abstract: As climate impacts worsen, decision-makers, researchers, and public sector institutions increasingly need reliable, relevant, and appropriate information about emerging weather and climate anomalies. However, with the ever-expanding choice of datasets based on ground observations, satellite data, and models, it is critical to not only use the best dataset for a specific decision-making need but to avoid misinforming and even derailing decision-making due to dataset selection. The main objective of this perspective is to illustrate the importance of understanding datasets used to translate climate data into actionable knowledge, supporting the next generation of science- and data-driven climate risk management instruments, projects, and global initiatives. Through the lens of three use cases, we illustrate what data quality means for different applications, the implications of choosing, aggregating, and combining different climate datasets, and the potential consequences of dataset and baseline choice on decision-making. Choosing different datasets often leads to trade-offs that decision-makers need to be aware of, for instance, between the spatial resolution of a dataset and length of the data record. Here, we discuss the implications of selecting the appropriate time step, resolution, and dataset and provide examples of how these choices affect the identification of societally relevant anomalies.

title: Heterogeneous impacts of temperature extremes on climate attitudes and Green voting
abstract: In the past decade, the public in Europe has become more concerned about climate change and expresses stronger proenvironmental policy preferences. Based on data from the European Social Survey (2012–2022, 25 countries), we show that the increased exposure to temperature extremes has contributed to the observed changes in climate change attitudes and electoral support for environmentalist policy platforms. For each additional degree of excess temperature experienced during warm spells measured over the previous 12 mo, we find that the probabilities of being worried about climate change, of feeling responsible for climate change, and of voting for Green parties and Green coalitions increase by 4.0 [CI95: 2.5, 5.5], 2.5 [CI95: 1.1, 3.9], and 2.8 [CI95: 0.9, 3.7] percentage points respectively. We also document significant heterogeneity across individuals, based on gender and education, particularly between highly educated women and low-educated men. While the latter group consistently exhibits the lowest proenvironmental attitudes and voting, it is this group that shows the strongest increases when exposed to temperature extremes, converging toward the levels of their more educated counterparts. Further regional heterogeneity analyses reveal that the effects of warm temperature extremes are smaller in less prosperous or economically disadvantaged regions, as well as in regions with greenhouse gas emission levels above the median. The findings suggest a nuanced interplay between individual factors and contextual influences in shaping climate attitudes of European citizens and their motivations or reservations toward greater climate action.

title: Humid-heat shifts conceptions and increases pregnancy termination risks in Nigeria
abstract:
Climate change is increasing the occurrence of dangerous heat events globally with immediate health consequences, particularly in the Global South. In this paper, we spatially integrate Demographic and Healt 9 h surveys with a high-resolution, blended remotely sensed and station-derived dataset of humid-heat events spanning 1983–2016 to examine the effect of humid-heat exposure on fertility in Nigeria, one of the largest and most climate-vulnerable countries in the world. We use discrete-time models to examine the relationship between humid-heat exposure and conception probability and linear probability models to examine the relationship between humid-heat exposure and pregnancy termination (spontaneous and induced). We find that a 1
                     ° 
                    C increase in the current maximum wet bulb globe temperature decreases conceptions (0.2 conceptions per 1,000 woman-months, 95% CI: 0.03 to 0.4), but exposure to hotter temperatures 1 to 2 mo prior increases conception probability. Exposure to hot-humid temperatures during pregnancy increases probability of pregnancy termination (1.73 terminations per 100 pregnancies, 95% CI: 0.7 to 2.7). The net effect is an increase in births, but the timing may be shifted. Subgroup analyses reveal that effects of humid-heat on conception were larger for women residing in rural areas or in northern districts, or who are Muslim or have lower educational attainment, while the association between humid-heat and pregnancy termination was larger for women in southern areas, older women, and Christian women. Differences in how humid-heat affects populations may exacerbate existing inequalities. Overall, our analysis contributes to a better understanding of how humid-heat exposure affects fertility and reproductive health among women in the Global South.

title: Predicting birth weights in West Africa using subseasonal to seasonal climate and socioeconomic variables shows potential for an early warning system
abstract: Past research has shown a negative impact of climate extremes on child birth weight (BW), which is modulated by household socioeconomic and individual maternal conditions as well as the timing and degree of exposure. This study tests the potential of predicting BW using subseasonal to seasonal (S2S) climate predictors and socioeconomic indicators to support early warning systems for BW. Three sets of predictors were tested: a) a suite of biological and socioeconomic indicators from the Demographic and Health Survey (DHS), b) S2S climate predictors, and c) a combination of climate predictors and selected socioeconomic indicators. The most accurate models incorporated the full set of DHS variables [predictors set (a)], with within-country (models trained and tested on the same country) predictive errors ranging from 13.5 to 17% for Burkina Faso and 20 to 25% for Mali. Cross-country (models trained on one country and tested on others) errors varied from 14 to 21% in Burkina Faso to 20 to 26% in Senegal. Models using only climate predictors [predictors set (b)] showed comparable skill to those using the full set of DHS indicators, with a relative error difference of 1 to 5%. The predictive skill was highest for children born with the most in-utero exposure to the lean season (months between planting and harvest). The results of this study have important implications for the prospect of implementing child BW early warning systems in data-sparse regions, based solely on climate predictors or based on selected socioeconomic indicators with climate predictors, to support malnutrition surveillance, to improve antenatal/maternal nutrition, policy formulation, and mitigation decisions.

title: Exploring data science as a tool to advance linked socioecological systems in the context of climate change
Continuous mass photometry by single-molecule trapping
abstract:
Abstract 
                   The dynamic choreography of biomolecular interactions underpins the processes of life, but its direct observation remains challenging. Here we introduce continuous mass photometry, enabling hour-long, mass-resolved observation of individual biomolecules tethered to supported lipid bilayers, their complexes and interactions, with up to sub-kilodalton mass precision and millisecond temporal resolution. Our approach represents a quantitative time-resolved single-molecule measurement modality for studying complex biomolecular mechanisms in action.

title: Quantification method affects replicability of eQTL analysis, colocalization and TWAS
abstract: Nature Genetics, Published online: 26 October 2026;  doi:10.1038/s41588-026-02827-0  This study finds that upstream RNA-seq processing steps, specifically transcript annotations and quantification methods, can affect eQTL mapping, TWAS and colocalization with GWAS. It serves as a cautionary message to the community to carefully report transcript annotation and quantification methods in future work.

title: fastGxE is a powerful method for uncovering genotype–environment interactions in biobanks
abstract: Nature Genetics, Published online: 26 October 2026;  doi:10.1038/s41588-026-02806-5  fastGxE is a scalable and powerful method that accelerates genome-wide scans for genotype–environment interactions in biobank datasets. When applied to the UK Biobank, fastGxE identified previously uncharacterized genotype–environment interaction loci for physical traits and routinely assayed blood biomarkers, revealing context-dependent genetic effects.

title: Interferon-α directs hematopoietic stem cells toward competing fates
abstract: Nature Genetics, Published online: 26 October 2026;  doi:10.1038/s41588-026-02797-3  Chronic inflammation drives clonal hematopoietic expansions, yet IFNα depletes clones in myeloproliferative neoplasms. A new study tackles this paradox, revealing that IFNα induces competing trajectories whose balance ultimately determines clonal fate: depletion or persistence.

abstract: Nature Biotechnology, Published online: 26 October 2026;  doi:10.1038/s41587-026-03369-w  Giving AI a seat at the peer review table

title: Other effective area-based conservation measures may enhance global conservation networks
abstract: Nature Ecology & Evolution, Published online: 26 October 2026;  doi:10.1038/s41559-026-03222-y  A typology of the ways in which other effective area-based conservation measures can structurally contribute to protected-area networks identifies opportunities for optimization and consolidation of conservation areas.

title: A fully marine stem amphibian from the Late Triassic of China
abstract: Nature Ecology & Evolution, Published online: 26 October 2026;  doi:10.1038/s41559-026-03209-9  A new fossil species of a Late Triassic stem amphibian lacks the permeable skin of present-day amphibians, and its find location, taphonomic context and geochemistry suggest that it maintained a fully marine lifestyle.

title: Fern phloem evolution records a trend of decreasing conductivity through geological time
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Phloem, the sugar-transporting tissue in vascular plants, is one of the most important but least characterized tissues from an evolutionary perspective. Here we substantially extend the evidence for phloem evolution by carrying out a histological investigation of phloem conducting cells, termed sieve elements, in 26 extant fern species spanning 21 families and making over 18,000 measurements. We report high diversity in fern phloem and that sieve element radius preserves a strong phylogenetic signal. We also detect clear scaling relationships between sieve element radius and both leaf and vasculature characteristics in the leptosporangiate ferns. By integrating fossils into our analysis, we recognized a trend of decreasing sieve element radius and total conducting area through geological time. We conclude that this decrease likely had a major functional impact by reducing phloem conductivity in the highly diverse polypod ferns that diversified into angiosperm-dominated ecosystems.

SpikeFlow-4D maps rice panicle grain-filling kinetics by computed tomography
abstract: We developed SpikeFlow-4D, a non-destructive 4D X-ray CT phenotyping framework that integrates hierarchical segmentation and density-preserving analysis to quantify spatiotemporal grain-filling dynamics in intact rice panicles. Time series imaging revealed delayed density accumulation, shortened active filling duration, and reduced net density increment in inferior grains. Independent destructive measurements further supported the biological relevance of CT-derived attenuation traits, providing a quantitative framework for investigating spatial heterogeneity and developmental asynchrony during rice grain filling.

title: A seesaw between growth and cold defense gated by a membrane-chloroplast-nucleus relay
Single-cell multi-omics reveals distinct regulatory architectures coordinating carbon assimilation and cyclic electron flow in maize C4 photosynthesis
abstract: Efficient C4 photosynthesis requires coordinated carbon assimilation and electron transport. In maize, distinct regulatory architectures integrate these functions into a shared cell-specific programme, and bundle sheath-targeted ZmDOF30 expression upregulates NDH genes and enhances cyclic electron flow, photosynthesis and biomass accumulation. Dissection of promoter regulatory logic identifies a 49-bp DOF-responsive cis element that confers vascular bundle-associated expression from a heterologous promoter.

title: Avian germline-restricted chromosomes are reservoirs for active and expressed long-terminal-repeat retroviruses
abstract: Fang and Edwards show that songbird germline-restricted chromosomes (GRCs) are repeat rich and preserve abundant intact endogenous retroviruses that are actively transcribed in testis. In contrast, regular chromosomes largely eliminate these elements, revealing the GRC as a hidden retroviral reservoir with the potential to fuel genome innovation in birds.

title: Infants respond to alterations in their own voice months before they recognize themselves in the mirror
abstract: Belia et al. show that 5-month-old infants can detect and compensate for upward transpositions of the pitch of their voice, at an age where they show no evidence of recognizing their own face in a mirror. This reveals an earlier developing emergence of self-monitoring in the vocal domain.

title: Environment-specific virtual head direction representation in the human anteroventral thalamus during memory-guided spatial orientation
abstract: Lv et al. show that the human anteroventral thalamus carries environment-specific virtual head direction information during memory-guided spatial orientation, providing direct intracranial evidence that bridges animal head direction models and human navigation.

title: The antimicrobial peptide pileup promotes enterocyte shedding to maintain gut homeostasis in aging Drosophila
abstract: Lee et al. find that an antimicrobial peptide targets aging enterocytes. In Drosophila enterocytes destined for replacement, ROS induce pileup, which damages the cell and promotes its shedding. Loss of pileup leaves these cells in place, and gut homeostasis fails.

title: Effector-triggered immunity in oilseed crops is expanded despite the restricted specificity of the receptor ZAR1
abstract: Breit-McNally et al. uncover an extensive effector-triggered immunity landscape in the oilseed crops Brassica napus and Camelina sativa against Pseudomonas syringae. Compared with Arabidopsis thaliana, these oilseed crops showed expanded immunodiversity, while the recognition specificity of the conserved immune receptor ZAR1 has diverged.

title: In vivo genome-editing therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy: Preclinical studies and first-in-human trial
abstract: A single-dose AAV-CRISPR therapy restores dystrophin in humanized DMD mice and achieves durable editing with manageable safety in non-human primates. In a first-in-human DMD trial, the therapy yields molecular evidence of muscle editing but reveals a fatal dose-dependent immune complication, highlighting the urgent need to expand the safety margin of systemic AAV-CRISPR treatments.

title: Battery Electrode Engineering Enables Fast Charging LMFP Cells Without Carbon‐Coated Foil
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Lithium manganese iron phosphate (LiMn
                     x 
                    Fe
                     1‐x 
                    PO
                     4 
                    , LMFP) has emerged as a promising Li‐ion battery cathode material due to its high voltage, thermal stability, and cycle life, yet its intrinsically low electronic and ionic conductivity limits high‐rate performance and thus usefulness in fast‐charge applications such as electric vehicles. Here, we evaluate key electrode design aspects, investigating the interplay between calendering density and current collector priming (carbon‐coating) on the fast cycling performance of LMFP cathodes. For electrodes on pristine aluminium, calendering to high density induced particle embedment into the foil (quantified via segmentation of cross‐sectional microscope images), reducing interfacial resistance while enhancing both rate capability and long‐term cycling stability. In contrast, performance of electrodes on C‐coated aluminium exhibited minimal sensitivity to densification. Surprisingly, at sufficiently high calendering pressure (achieving density ≥ 2.5 g cm
                     −3 
                    ), the carbon coating provided no advantage to high‐rate performance, in stark contrast with conventional understanding, and cells manufactured with pristine Al achieved fast charging from 10% to 80% SOC in just over 15 min, a key milestone for this chemistry. These findings establish a mechanistic understanding of how density and interfacial properties govern transport and electrochemical behavior in LMFP cells, providing practical guidance for optimized electrode structures.

title:
An Integrated Framework Coupling Hierarchical Hyperspectral
                     i 
                    ‐trait Screening, Gene Identification, and Functional Validation for Genetic Dissection of Salt Tolerance in Cotton
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Cotton is an economically pivotal fiber crop worldwide, but its growth and yield are critically limited by soil salinity. Salt tolerance is a complex quantitative trait, and conventional destructive phenotyping methods have long hindered the efficiency and accuracy of gene discovery and genetic dissection. To overcome this phenotyping bottleneck and establish a streamlined workflow from phenotype to gene, we developed an integrated framework coupling dynamic hyperspectral phenomics, hierarchical trait selection, genome‐wide association study (GWAS), and functional validation, and applied it to dissect the genetic basis of salt tolerance using a natural population of 419 upland cotton accessions. We first confirmed abundant salt tolerance phenotypic diversity in the population via four core physiological traits and their phenotypic plasticity indices. Using time‐series hyperspectral imaging (HSI), we extracted large‐scale image‐derived traits (
                     i 
                    ‐traits) capturing dynamic physiological responses to salt stress. A three‐tiered screening strategy integrating t‐test, broad‐sense heritability (H²) estimation, and multi‐algorithm machine learning consensus was applied to identify core salt‐responsive
                     i 
                    ‐traits with biological relevance, genetic stability, and low redundancy. Using these core
                     i 
                    ‐traits as phenotypic inputs for GWAS, we successfully mapped GhST7 as a key candidate gene. Functional validation via CRISPR/Cas9‐mediated knockout and haplotype‐specific overexpression demonstrated that
                     GhST7 
                    acts as a key regulator of cotton salt stress responses, and natural variation in its promoter region confers differential salt tolerance by modulating gene expression levels. Collectively, this study not only identifies a functionally verified salt tolerance gene with breeding application value, but also establishes a coherent phenomics–genomics–functional validation framework, providing an efficient paradigm for high‐precision genetic dissection of complex stress‐tolerance traits in crops.

title: Amcinonide Exhibits Antitumor Effects in Radioresistant Colorectal Cancer Through the circRNF10/miR‐296‐5p/Snail Axis
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Radiotherapy, commonly used in the treatment of colorectal cancer (CRC), can induce local recurrence and malignant progression in cases of intrinsic and acquired radioresistance; therefore, effective treatment strategies are required. In this study, we screened an FDA‐approved drug library and identified amcinonide (AMC), a topical corticosteroid, as a potential agent that inhibits radiation‐induced epithelial‐mesenchymal transition (EMT), cell migratory ability, and invasiveness in radioresistant colorectal cancer cells. Mechanistically, ionizing radiation‐induced circRNF10 suppressed miR‐296‐5p, thereby increasing Snail expression and promoting EMT and aggressive phenotypes in radioresistant CRC cells. We verified in vitro, in vivo, and in CRC patient‐derived organoids (PDOs) models that AMC suppresses the malignant phenotype by restoring miR‐296‐5p expression and reducing Snail expression. These findings identify the circRNF10/miR‐296‐5p/Snail axis as a key factor in CRC radioresistance and suggest that it may serve as a therapeutic target. Together, these results suggest that AMC is a promising drug for overcoming CRC radioresistance and that components of this axis may serve as potential diagnostic biomarkers. Overall, these findings highlight the therapeutic potential of targeting the ncRNA‐mediated EMT circuit to overcome radioresistant CRC.

title: Tip60‐Mediated USP22 Lactylation Drives Glutamine Metabolic Reprogramming via SLC25A5 in TNBC
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Glutamine metabolism promotes breast cancer progression and metastasis, though the underlying mechanisms are not fully understood. In this study, we identified a significant positive correlation between glutamine metabolism and ubiquitin‐specific protease 22 (USP22)expression in breast cancer patients. USP22 drives glutamine reprogramming to promote lactate secretion, thereby supporting triple‐negative breast cancer (TNBC) growth and survival. This process involves the lactyltransferase Tat‐interactive protein, 60 kDa (Tip60), which catalyzes K134 lactylation of USP22. This post‐translational modification (PTM) stabilizes USP22 protein levels and facilitates its mitochondrial location. Moreover, USP22 stabilizes the solute carrier family 25 member 5 (SLC25A5) through its de‐ubiquitinase activity. Clinically, increased expression levels of both USP22 and SLC25A5 are significantly associated with a poor prognosis in patients with TNBC. Furthermore, USP22 regulates glutamine metabolism to promote α‐ketoglutarate (α‐KG) secretion, thereby activating M2 macrophages and suppressing the anti‐tumor immune response. Importantly, targeting USP22 synergized with CB‐839 in TNBC xenograft models. These findings underscore USP22 as a promising therapeutic target for TNBC.

title:
Interfacial and Hydration‐Associated Lithium Retention During FePO

abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Selective FePO
                     4 
                    precipitation is used to separate iron and phosphorus from lithium during hydrometallurgical recycling of spent LiFePO
                     4 
                    , yet measurable lithium can remain in the regenerated FePO
                     4 
                    precursor. Here, lithium partitioning was examined in a simulated Fe–P system, a commercial LiFePO
                     4 
                    ‐derived leachate, and a spent black‐mass‐derived leachate. Sequential washing resolved the lithium associated with the precipitates into fractions with different accessibility. Under representative conditions, approximately 70% of the retained lithium was washing‐removable, whereas approximately 30% remained after three washing cycles. Contact with lithium‐free FePO

Thermodynamic analysis indicated that the formation of the considered discrete lithium‐containing precipitates was unfavorable, while changes in hydration and local Fe–O–P environments correlated with the washing‐retained fraction. These results support a proposed precipitation‐associated model involving lithium retention in environments with different accessibility within hydrated amorphous FePO
                     4 
                    . The findings identify precipitation and washing as linked control stages for managing lithium carryover during FePO
                     4 
                    regeneration.

title: Highly Linear Perovskite Synapses for Neuromorphic Computing
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Neuromorphic computing offers a compelling route to data‐intensive applications with boosted computing power and energy efficiency. However, its accuracy for edge vision tasks is critically bottlenecked by the inherent non‐linearity and asymmetry of conductance updates in analog memristive synapses. Here, we report a highly linear memristive synapse based on vertically aligned alternating cations in the interlayer space phase halide perovskite. A synergistic regulation strategy involving additive engineering and solvent atmosphere annealing is introduced to fabricate GAMA
                     5 
                    Pb
                     5 
                    I
                     16 
                    halide perovskite films with vertical crystal orientation. The resulting films facilitate controllable ion migration, allowing the fabricated devices to achieve an ultra‐low energy consumption of 5.5 aJ alongside 100 discrete conductance states with non‐linearity as low as 0.027 and 0.064 and asymmetry of 0.037. These attributes enable the synapses to perform object detection tasks with an mAP50 of 57.6%, retaining 98.1% of the floating‐point baseline performance. This work provides a promising biomimetic solution for efficient visual perception in intelligent transportation, paving the way for high‐precision neuromorphic systems.

title: Hydrodynamic Selection of Polymorphic Assembly Pathways in Plant Protein Amyloid Fibrils
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Plant protein amyloid fibrils are universally assembled in liquid environments, yet their formation is often analyzed without explicitly considering the role of fluid motion. In practice, as a typical model system, soy protein amyloid fibrils (SAFs) are generated under dynamic hydrodynamic conditions involving shear and vortex transport. How such flow fields regulate fibril growth pathways and give rise to polymorphic assembly remains largely unexplored. Here, we elucidate the hydrodynamic selection of SAFs assembly pathways through nanoscale structural characterization combined with flow‐field analysis. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) identifies six distinct fibril morphologies, including short‐curved, javelin‐like, loop‐like, twisted ribbon, helical ribbon, and rod‐like structures. By integrating AFM observations with particle image velocimetry (PIV) results, we propose a drafting, kissing, and docking (DKD) dynamic as a plausible hydrodynamic model for understanding polymorphic fibril assembly. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations further reproduce key characteristics of the experimentally observed flow fields and provide hydrodynamic support for the proposed interpretation of fibrillation pathways. These results demonstrate that an in‐depth understanding of hydrodynamic selection behavior in polymorphic assembly pathways is important to pave the way for production of tailormade amyloid materials.

title: PIAS3 CircRNA‐Loaded Lipid Nanoparticles Restore ALOX15 SUMOylation to Suppress Cementoblast Ferroptosis and Attenuate Orthodontically Induced Root Resorption
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Excessive orthodontic compression induces cementoblast dysfunction and contributes to orthodontically induced root resorption (OIRR), yet the molecular mechanisms linking mechanical stress to cementoblast ferroptosis remain unclear. Compression‐induced PIAS3 loss attenuates SUMO3‐dependent ALOX15 SUMOylation and impairs ALOX15 ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation, thereby promoting lipid peroxidation and cementoblast ferroptosis. Based on these findings, PIAS3 circRNA‐loaded uridine‐derived lipid nanoparticles (PIAS3‐OLNPs) were developed, which efficiently restored PIAS3 expression and inhibited cementoblast ferroptosis and subsequent osteoclast differentiation. Moreover, the incorporation of PIAS3‐OLNPs into an injectable F127DA hydrogel prolonged local retention and sustained PIAS3 expression in the gingival sulcus, thereby inhibiting cementoblast ferroptosis and osteoclastogenesis and preserving root integrity in vivo. Collectively, this study establishes PIAS3‐mediated ALOX15 SUMOylation as a key mechanism that restrains cementoblast ferroptosis and demonstrates that restoring this pathway through local PIAS3 circRNA delivery offers a therapeutic strategy for OIRR and potentially other ferroptosis‐related disorders.

title: Photoelectrocatalytic Diazidation of Olefins via Synergistic Dual Iron Species
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    The 1,2‐diamine motif is prevalent in bioactive molecules, natural products, and synthetic chemistry. In this study, we report a simple and general approach for 1,2‐diazidation of alkenes by a photoelectrochemical dual iron‐catalysted ligand‐to‐metal charge transfer strategy process using TMSN
                     3 
                    as an azide source under mild reaction conditions. Dual iron species can regulate the generation rate of azide radicals, enhance catalytic efficiency, control reaction selectivity, and avoid overoxidation of substrates and products. This approach could accommodate various unactivated, activated, electron‐deficient, and internal alkenes, as well as complex drug‐like and natural‐product‐derived scaffolds. The synthetic potency is further demonstrated through a gram‐scale reaction and derivatizations into other vicinal diamine compound families. This protocol circumvents the use of dangerous or activated azide precursors, equivalent chemical oxidants or metals, and other unfriendly reaction conditions. Mechanistic experiments indicated that iron, ligand, electric current, cathodic half‐reactions, and light play an important role in regulating the generation of azide radicals.

title: Melatonin Mitigates Doxorubicin‐Induced Cardiotoxicity by Targeting the USP18/PKM2 Axis Without Compromising Antitumor Efficacy
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Doxorubicin (DOX) remains a widely used chemotherapeutic drug, yet its clinical value is constrained by pronounced cardiotoxicity. Although melatonin is known to protect the heart, how it counters DOX‐induced cardiotoxicity (DIC), and whether it interferes with chemotherapy, remains unclear. Here we set out to define how melatonin protects the heart during DOX treatment and to test whether this protection holds in tumor‐bearing animals. We used acute and chronic DIC mouse models together with a syngeneic melanoma‐bearing model, and combined transcriptomic profiling, pharmacological intervention, cardiomyocyte‐specific USP18 overexpression and knockout, co‐immunoprecipitation, mass spectrometry, ubiquitination assays, and PKM2 inhibitor treatment. Melatonin markedly improved cardiac function, an effect exerted mainly via the MT1/2 receptors. Mechanistically, DOX activated STAT1, which in turn drove myocardial USP18 upregulation. USP18 bound PKM2 and stabilized it through removing K33‐linked ubiquitin chains while favoring K27‐linked ubiquitination—thereby aggravating cardiac injury. Overexpressing USP18 specifically in cardiomyocytes worsened DIC and abolished the protection conferred by melatonin, whereas deleting USP18 or inhibiting PKM2 reproduced melatonin's benefits. Notably, in bearing melanoma or lymphoma, melatonin relieved DIC without weakening the antitumor activity of DOX. Together, these findings define a previously unrecognized cardioprotective pathway and provide preclinical support for melatonin as a safe adjunct therapy in cardio‐oncology.

title: Human Engineered Heart Tissues Reproduce Trigger‐ and Substrate‐Driven Mechanisms of Ventricular Tachycardia
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Human iPSC‑derived engineered heart tissues (EHTs) are used to model cardiac physiology and drug responses, yet whether they reproduce tissue‑scale ventricular arrhythmia mechanisms remains unclear. We combined modified milliPillar EHT fabrication with high‐resolution dual‐channel voltage/Ca
                     2+ 
                    optical mapping. Baseline electrophysiology showed action potential durations (APD) within the range reported for human ventricles and conduction velocities approximately half of human longitudinal values, with rate‑dependent restitution of APD and Ca
                     2+ 
                    transient duration, conduction slowing, and physiologic AP‐Ca
                     2+ 
                    latency. To interrogate a trigger arm of ventricular tachycardia (VT), we modeled acquired long‐QT syndrome (aLQTS; hERG blockade with hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia) in EHTs from two hiPSC lines. aLQTS EHTs developed VT‐like episodes with beat‑to‑beat instability. Early afterdepolarizations propagated heterogeneously, generating triggered activity, tissue acceleration, APD dispersion, wavebreak, and rotor formation. These were short and self‐terminating (median 0.4 s) and clustered at head/neck region curvatures. To test whether a fixed spatial substrate supports prolonged reentry, we developed a reproducible focal cryoinjury model. After injury, all tissues developed VT‐like episodes, and 70% anatomically anchored rotors at the border; three persisted beyond 10 s, a recording‐limited lower bound. Dual voltage/Ca
                     2+ 
                    mapping at this resolution establishes EHTs as a non‐animal platform for mechanistic study of both trigger‐ and substrate‐driven ventricular arrhythmias.

title: An Explainable Multimodal Deep‐Learning Model Using Histopathological Image and Clinical Information for Prognosis Prediction in Colorectal Cancer: A Multi‐Center Cohort Study
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Accurate prognostication is crucial for the individualized management of patients with colorectal cancer (CRC), while the accuracy and interpretability of current models still need to be improved. This study aims to develop and validate an explainable multimodal model for precise survival prediction. 3381 patients with resected CRC are enrolled from three medical centers, and a multimodal deep‐learning framework integrating clinical variables and histopathological images is developed. The multimodal model exhibits significantly more robust performance than unimodal models in prognosis prediction across all of the cohorts. By stratifying patients into low‐risk and high‐risk groups based on the model‐derived risk scores, high‐risk patients exhibit worse outcomes, and the stratification remains an independent prognostic factor in multivariable Cox regression. The model also identifies patients with markedly poorer survival among the stage II/III subgroup. Adjuvant chemotherapy demonstrates benefits in high‐risk patients with stage III CRC but not in the low‐risk group. Multi‐omic analyses disclose that low‐risk tumors are characterized by enhanced adaptive immune responses, whereas high‐risk tumors exhibit stronger angiogenesis and higher exhaustion scores of T cells, reflecting a hypoxic and immunosuppressive microenvironment. These results support the potential of the multimodal model to effectively predict survival outcomes in resected CRC with great explainability.

title: Flooding‐Driven Greenhouse Gas Emissions From Global Upland Croplands
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Greenhouse gas emissions from temporarily flooded upland croplands remain poorly characterized in the global greenhouse gas budget. We combined field measurements from 11 maize‐field sites temporarily flooded across the North China Plain with a global synthesis of 23 flooded upland cropland sites to quantify diffusive emissions. Flooded croplands release high fluxes of nitrous oxide, carbon dioxide, and methane, with emission factors exceeding relevant Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) defaults for rice paddies and newly flooded lands. Extrapolating site‐level fluxes from limited observations over the estimated global area of flooded upland cropland and mean flooding duration yields a mean of 63.3 teragrams (Tg) of carbon dioxide‐equivalent (CO
                     2 
                    ‐eq) emissions per year during the standing‐water flooding periods, comprising 7.2 (1.7–17.2), 34.6 (9.0–83.7), and 21.5 (6.2–45.6) Tg from nitrous oxide, carbon dioxide, and methane, respectively. Temporarily flooded upland croplands are therefore identified as a previously overlooked component of the global greenhouse gas budget, providing an empirical basis for incorporating flood‐driven emissions into future agricultural inventories.

title: From Artificial to Embodied and Physical Intelligence in Smart Manufacturing
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Manufacturing is evolving from automation‐centered production toward systems capable of sensing, adaptation, and autonomous response across digital, mechanical, and material domains. Although recent progress has been largely driven by artificial intelligence, current manufacturing intelligence often remains external to physical systems and suffers from limited robustness, interpretability, and transferability in complex industrial environments. Here, we present a unified perspective on smart manufacturing through the framework of artificial intelligence (AI), embodied intelligence (EI), and physical intelligence (PI). AI provides abstraction, prediction, and generative capability; EI enables closed‐loop perception, decision‐making, and physical interaction; and PI embeds adaptive intelligence directly into materials, structures, and physicochemical processes. We further discuss how generative intelligence is beginning to connect these domains through inverse design, adaptive fabrication, and physics‐constrained behavior realization. Recent advances in collaborative robotics, embodied digital twins, self‐optimizing production systems, and physically intelligent materials, including self‐actuating, self‐healing, multistable, and shape‐morphing systems, are reviewed. Finally, we propose an integrated AI–EI–PI framework spanning the full manufacturing lifecycle, highlighting a transition toward manufacturing systems in which intelligence is increasingly co‐designed across algorithms, embodied agents, and matter itself.

title: A Biomimetic PLK1 Nanodelivery System Promotes Migrasome‐Mediated Mitocytosis to Restore Efferocytosis and Functional Recovery After Spinal Cord Injury
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Excessive accumulation and insufficient clearance of apoptotic cells following spinal cord injury (SCI) are key factors contributing to persistent injury. Macrophage efferocytosis is essential for resolving injury but is compromised by mitochondrial dysfunction and lysosomal overload. Maintaining mitochondrial functional homeostasis is therefore crucial for preserving the acidic lysosomal environment, alleviating the cellular lysosomal burden, and sustaining efferocytosis. Common mitochondrial quality control (MQC) pathways such as mitophagy increase the lysosomal burden. Here, we investigated how polo‐like kinase 1 (PLK1) regulates macrophage efferocytosis and elucidated the underlying mechanism of migrasome‐mediated mitocytosis. We demonstrate that PLK1 regulates TSPAN4‐dependent migrasome formation, which drives the selective extrusion of damaged mitochondria, alleviates the lysosomal burden, and increases efferocytic capacity. To enable targeted PLK1 delivery, we engineered macrophage membrane‐coated, reactive oxygen species (ROS)‐responsive nanocomplexes encapsulating PLK1 plasmids (MM‐NPs@PLK1). This biomimetic nanoplatform preferentially accumulates in the injured spinal cord, promotes macrophage‐associated PLK1 delivery, enhances mitocytosis and efferocytosis, supports neural tissue repair, and significantly improves locomotor recovery in SCI mice. In summary, our study reveals a PLK1‐regulated MQC mechanism that sustains macrophage efferocytosis through migrasome‐mediated mitocytosis, providing a promising therapeutic strategy for SCI.

title: Maternal Hyperglycemia Disrupts Cerebral Cortex Development Through the Foxp1‐Dll1‐Notch Axis
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Maternal hyperglycemia is associated with adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes in offspring, but the mechanisms by which it affects fetal brain development remain incompletely understood. Using a mouse model of pregestational diabetes mellitus (PGDM), we found that maternal hyperglycemia was associated with reduced cortical thickness and altered cortical lamination. These abnormalities were accompanied by changes in neural stem cell differentiation and asymmetric division, as well as impaired neuronal migration and dendritic development. Transcriptomic analysis identified the transcription factor Foxp1 as markedly downregulated in the PGDM embryonic cortex. Restoring Foxp1 expression in vivo substantially alleviated the observed cortical abnormalities. Mechanistic experiments showed that Foxp1 represses transcription of the Notch ligand Delta‐like 1 (Dll1) and attenuates Notch signaling. Together, these findings implicate the Foxp1–Dll1–Notch axis as one pathway contributing to disrupted corticogenesis in the PGDM model and provide insight into how an adverse intrauterine metabolic environment affects embryonic brain development.

title: Prepolymerization Enables On‐Demand Viscosity Tuning for Xolography of Soft Hydrogels
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Xolography enables contactless volumetric additive manufacturing by suspending objects in a viscous resin. This avoids the build platforms and shear forces that distort soft materials in layer‐by‐layer printing. However, low‐viscosity resins such as hydrogels allow printed parts to sediment, and conventional thickeners can compromise the final material. Here, we report an in situ prepolymerization strategy that raises viscosity without altering the base resin composition. A room‐temperature redox reaction converts a fraction of the monomer into high‐molecular‐weight linear chains, tuning viscosity by more than four orders of magnitude (4.37 to >90000 mPa s) through reaction time alone. Across six formulations, longer prepolymerization suppresses sedimentation and lowers the critical light dose by up to 40%, enabling high‐fidelity printing of complex hydrogels within 4 min. The strategy extends to a solvent‐free organic resin, achieving 80 µm resolution. Sequential overprinting yields multi‐material objects with mechanically isolated rigid components embedded in a hydrogel matrix, a geometry difficult to produce by platform‐based printing. The resulting hydrogels retain 99.3% of their peak stress over 5000 compression cycles.

title: Polarity‐Controlled Coexistence of Electrochemical Metallization and Valence Change Mechanisms in a Unified Metal Halide Perovskite Memristor
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Metal halide perovskites (MHPs), owing to their mixed ionic‐electronic conductivity and defect‐tolerant lattice, have emerged as promising candidates for next‐generation memristors. Yet, the interplay of distinct resistive switching mechanisms remains poorly understood. Here, we provide direct experimental evidence that two distinct resistive switching mechanisms, electrochemical metallization (ECM), driven by the reactive metal electrode, and the valence change mechanism (VCM), mediated by intrinsic ion migration within the perovskite lattice, can coexist within the same perovskite memristor and can be selectively activated by simply reversing the electroforming voltage polarity, without altering the device structure or active layer composition. This controllable switching enables a systematic comparison of their intrinsic performance. ECM‐driven devices exhibit low operating voltages (+0.18/−0.3 V), high endurance (> 10
                     4 
                    cycles), and moderate retention (∼ 4 × 10
                     3 
                    s), whereas VCM switching achieves superior data retention (∼ 7 × 10
                     3 
                    s) and a higher resistance contrast (∼ 10
                     5 
                    ), albeit with higher operating voltages and reduced cycling stability. Replacing the active Ag electrode with inert contacts confirms the absence of ECM and isolates intrinsic ion migration as the origin of VCM switching. These findings establish a clear framework for distinguishing and engineering operating mechanisms in MHP‐based memristors, providing design guidelines for reliable, multifunctional memory and neuromorphic devices.

title: An Integrated Artificial Intelligence Framework for Nanomedicine Engineering
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   The translation of nanomedicines is frequently bottlenecked by trial‐and‐error optimization. Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) transforms this process into a closed‐loop, experimentally grounded discovery ecosystem. This Review provides a roadmap for this paradigm, demonstrating how AI, high‐throughput testing, and nanoscale design converge to generate clinically translatable nanotherapeutics. We emphasize the necessity of standardized multimodal data—spanning pharmacokinetic, biodistribution, and drug‐release profiles—anchored strictly to validated biological phenomena. Furthermore, we evaluate an algorithmic spectrum, ranging from classical machine learning to physics‐informed neural networks (PINNs) and reinforcement learning (RL), to align models with specific formulation objectives. To bridge computational design and empirical reality, we examine how high‐throughput technologies, such as robotic laboratories and in vivo DNA‐barcoding multiplexing, operationalize the “Design‐Make‐Test‐Analyze” (DMTA) cycle for dynamic model recalibration. Ultimately, this review demonstrates how integrating AI, physical constraints, and automated validation accelerates the rational design of next‐generation nanomedicines.

title: Functional MXene Inks for Printed Electronics: Chemistry, Rheology, and Devices
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   MXene‐based functional inks have emerged as a promising platform for printed electronics by combining high electrical conductivity, tunable surface chemistry, and solution processability. This review establishes a unified framework linking MXene synthesis, surface engineering, ink rheology, printing behavior, and device performance across diverse additive manufacturing technologies. Particular emphasis is placed on how chemical functionalization, composite design, and interfacial engineering influence colloidal stability, printability, and functionality. By elucidating structure–ink–process–property relationships, the review reveals how MXene chemistry and rheology govern printed microstructure and performance in sensors, energy‐storage devices, and electromagnetic interference shielding systems. Despite rapid progress, widespread implementation remains constrained by three interconnected challenges: ensuring long‐term chemical and colloidal stability, achieving printability without sacrificing electrical transport, and establishing scalable, reproducible manufacturing routes. Future advances will depend on oxidation‐resistant formulations, manufacturing‐aware rheological design, sustainable processing strategies, and standardized evaluation protocols. These developments provide a roadmap for translating MXene inks from laboratory‐scale demonstrations to reliable, high‐performance flexible and multifunctional electronic systems.

title: STING/Type I Interferon Pathway Activation Confers Multimodal Therapeutic Benefits in Osteomyelitis
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Osteomyelitis is an inflammatory bone disease caused by pathogenic microorganisms and characterized by severe pain, extensive bone destruction, and reduced antibiotic efficacy due to local abscess formation. This study investigates the therapeutic potential of activating the STING (stimulator of interferon genes) pathway in osteomyelitis. In murine femoral osteomyelitis models induced by
                     Staphylococcus aureus 
                    (
                     S. aureus 
                    ), STING agonists alleviate osteomyelitis‐associated pain, suppress infection‐induced bone destruction, and reduce local abscess formation. These effects depend on host STING/type I interferon (IFN‐I) signaling and involve three mechanisms: inhibition of nociceptor activation by pathogens, suppression of osteoclast differentiation and function without affecting osteoblast activity, and downregulation of interleukin‐1β (IL‐1β), leading to reduced neutrophil recruitment and abscess formation. By reducing abscess formation as a physical barrier, STING agonists enhance the antibacterial efficacy of conventional antibiotics such as vancomycin at the site of infection. In summary, these findings suggest that the synergistic mechanisms activated by STING represent a promising therapeutic target for alleviating pain and improving clinical outcomes in osteomyelitis.

title: CNTN2 Deficiency Disrupts Ascending Auditory Neuroglial Interactions and Redox Homeostasis in Neural Presbycusis
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Neural presbycusis disrupts auditory timing and speech perception, yet its molecular basis remains poorly understood. This study identifies
                     Cntn2 
                    as the Ranvier's nodal molecule significantly downregulated in aged auditory nerves.
                     Cntn2 
                    heterozygous knockout (
                     
                      Cntn2
                       +/− 
                     
                    ) mice showed elevated auditory brainstem response thresholds and prolonged wave latencies and interpeak intervals, whereas distortion product otoacoustic emission thresholds were largely preserved. Hair cell and ribbon synapses were preserved, with no obvious ultrastructural changes, suggesting that overt hair cell loss or synaptic structural loss is unlikely to be the main cause of the early phenotype. Instead, transmission electron microscopy revealed myelin outfoldings and aberrant node of Ranvier morphology in myelinated auditory nerve fibers, accompanied by increased Schwann cell density. Multiplex immunofluorescence and Western blot analysis showed disruption of nodal molecular organization along the ascending auditory pathway from cochlea to auditory cortex. Transcriptomic profiling and oxidative stress assays further linked CNTN2 deficiency to altered neuroglial interaction and redox imbalance. Early unilateral AAV‐mediated CNTN2 restoration partially improved threshold and latency abnormalities. These findings identify CNTN2‐dependent neuroglial integrity as an important contributor to auditory conduction of neural presbycusis and may provide a new direction for future therapeutic studies.

title: Integrating Ecology and Economics in Agent‐Based Models to Support Agricultural Policy
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Agriculture is a complex social‐ecological system with numerous interactions between policies, markets, farm management, landscapes, and ecosystems. Agent‐based models are a valuable method for studying these agricultural systems, as they are able to simulate the spatiotemporal dynamics and heterogeneous actors inherent to them. This potentially also makes such models helpful tools for scientific policy advice. Here, we conduct a literature review to evaluate how agent‐based models represent social‐ecological systems in agriculture. We analyze 56 published models using a set of 26 criteria to determine whether socio‐economic and ecological aspects of agriculture have been studied. We find that there is a particularly robust tradition of using agent‐based models for economic impact analyses of policy changes, and much effort has gone into studying decision‐making by land users. However, ecological models of biodiversity and ecosystem services are still often very abstract and ignore important land‐use processes, impeding their usefulness for providing policy advice. Research areas that are currently underdeveloped include simulating farm management and landscape dynamics in ecological models, risk management in economic models, and bidirectional human‐nature interactions in social‐ecological models. Agent‐based modeling of agriculture would also profit from using model coupling to represent more of the breadth of social‐ecological systems.

title: A single‐nucleus multiome profiling reveals the regulatory programs driving plant nematode–induced syncytium
authors:
Tarek Hewezi, 
Sobhan Bahrami Zadegan, 
Peitong Li, 
Cengizhan Öztürk, 
J. Hollis Rice, 
Hari B. Krishnan
abstract:
Summary 
                   
                     
                       
                         Plant‐parasitic cyst nematodes induce the formation of specialized feeding structures, known as syncytia, within host roots by orchestrating extensive transcriptional and epigenetic reprogramming. 
                       
                       
                         
                          Here, we generated parallel single‐nucleus RNA‐seq and ATAC‐seq libraries from fully developed
                           Heterodera schachtii 
                          –induced syncytia on Arabidopsis roots. We analyzed high‐quality transcriptome and chromatin profiles independently and in an integrated framework.
                         
                       
                       
                         
                          We identified multiple transcriptomic cell states, several of which were highly syncytium‐enriched and spanned vascular and cortical identities. Differential expression analysis identified hundreds of syncytium‐enriched genes, and pseudotime trajectory inference points to potential compartmentalization or functional heterogeneity of syncytium nuclei, consistent with the possibility of distinct transcriptional programs within or between mature syncytia. Joint clustering of snATAC‐seq with snRNA‐seq delineated syncytium‐unique chromatin accessibility landscapes, with several cell states exhibiting extensive open chromatin linked to upregulated genes. Motif enrichment across these accessible regions highlighted
                           cis 
                          ‐regulatory elements mainly for AP2, bZIP, bHLH, MYB, and TCP transcription factors and identified functionally validated members of these families as candidate regulators of syncytium identity.
                         
                       
                       
                         Our study establishes a multiome atlas of syncytial cells and uncovers the regulatory programs driving nematode feeding site maintenance, as well as transcriptionally distinct nuclear states that may reflect functional specialization within or between the syncytia.

title: Phosphatidylcholine acyl turnover facilitates thylakoid lipid remodeling and promotes plant survival under heat stress
authors:
Dongling Xie, 
Shasha Wang, 
Jilian Fan, 
Changcheng Xu
abstract:
Summary 
                   
                     
                       
                         
                          Heat stress destabilizes chloroplast membranes, requiring rapid lipid remodeling to maintain photosynthetic function. Although thylakoid lipid remodeling and triacylglycerol (TAG) accumulation are established heat responses, the role of phosphatidylcholine (PC) acyl turnover remains unclear. We investigated lysophosphatidylcholine acyltransferase 1 and 2 (LPCAT1/2), REDUCED OLEATE DESATURATION1 (ROD1), phospholipid:diacylglycerol acyltransferase 1 (PDAT1), and lipins in heat‐induced lipid remodeling and thermotolerance in
                           Arabidopsis thaliana 
                          .
                         
                       
                       
                         Using genetic, lipidomic, physiological, and photosynthetic analyses, we examined mutants defective in PC acyl editing, PC–diacylglycerol (DAG) interconversion, TAG synthesis, and phosphatidic acid dephosphorylation during heat stress. 
                       
                       
                         
                          Loss of LPCAT1/2 severely impaired basal and acquired thermotolerance, caused irreversible photosystem II damage, and disrupted thylakoid lipid remodeling.
                           rod1 
                          showed minor defects, whereas
                           rod1 lpcat1/2 
                          exhibited enhanced thermosensitivity. In mature vegetative plants,
                           pdat1‐2 
                          showed thermotolerance and photosystem II defects comparable to
                           lpcat1/2 
                          . Lipin‐mediated phosphatidic acid dephosphorylation provided the major DAG source for heat‐induced TAG synthesis. Defective PC acyl turnover also increased free fatty acids and lipid peroxidation.
                         
                       
                       
                         These findings establish LPCAT1/2‐mediated PC acyl turnover as a central regulator of heat‐induced membrane remodeling and thermotolerance and link lipin‐dependent DAG production and TAG synthesis with chloroplast membrane homeostasis.

title: Frenemies forever: when parasitic fungi become an insect's secret weapon
abstract:
Insect symbiotic yeast and fungi shape host–plant interactions.







Summary
Plant‐feeding insects pose a major threat to global food production, and finding sustainable pest control strategies is challenging. Insect‐associated symbiotic microorganisms fulfill important beneficial functions for their host insects, enabling them to adapt and thrive in a changing environment. Understanding how these interactions evolve and what they mean for insect–plant interactions is key to the development of novel targets and potential tools for pest control. Since yeast and fungal insect symbionts are understudied in comparison to bacterial symbionts, this Tansley Insight explores their role in insect–plant interactions.

title: Pathogen nutrient acquisition strategy mediates the strength of diversity–disease relationships in natural grasslands
authors:
Tianyun Li, 
Peng Zhang, 
Junsheng Ke, 
Kui Hu, 
Xiang Liu
abstract:
Summary 
                   
                     
                       
                         The relationship between biodiversity and disease risk is a cornerstone of disease ecology, yet predicting its direction and strength remains challenging. Pathogen nutrient acquisition strategies may be key to resolving this context dependency, but their roles in mediating diversity–disease relationships are poorly understood. 
                       
                       
                         Here, we combine a large‐scale survey spanning 2000 km in natural grasslands with advanced statistical modeling to demonstrate that pathogen nutrient acquisition strategy is a critical mediator. 
                       
                       
                         We show that diseases caused by biotrophic pathogens (e.g. rusts and powdery mildews), which depend on living host tissues, exhibit a significantly negative diversity–disease relationship, whereas diseases caused by necrotrophic pathogens (e.g. leaf spots and blights) show no significant relationship. Furthermore, the strength of this negative relationship for biotrophic pathogens is amplified in regions with higher disease severity. Bayesian structural equation modeling reveals that plant species richness directly reduces biotrophic disease severity, while for necrotrophic pathogens, precipitation is the primary driver of severity, with no direct effect of richness. 
                       
                       
                         Our findings provide a trait‐based framework linking climatic drivers, pathogen nutrient acquisition strategies, and the strength of diversity–disease relationships. These results enhance our ability to predict disease dynamics under biodiversity loss and inform biodiversity‐based disease management strategies.

title: A license to disperse: climatic niche lability and geographic expansion shape the diversification of Oleaceae
authors:
Hang Luo, 
Enze Li, 
Yushuang Wang, 
Kangjia Liu, 
Xuanwei Cheng, 
Shawn Laffan, 
Juan Viruel, 
Wenpan Dong
abstract:
Summary 
                   
                     
                       
                         Patterns of species diversity reflect interactions among ecological, biogeographic, and lineage‐specific evolutionary processes. Oleaceae provides a useful comparative system because its five tribes differ markedly in species richness, geographic extent, dispersal history, and genomic background. 
                       
                       
                         Using distribution data for 476 species and a time‐calibrated phylogeny of 283 Oleaceae species spanning all five tribes, we integrated ecological niche modelling, ancestral‐range and climatic‐niche reconstruction, diversification‐rate analyses, and phylogenetic comparative methods while accounting for uneven tribal sampling. 
                       
                       
                         Climatic niche position and breadth evolved heterogeneously across Oleaceae, while major range expansions beyond the reconstructed ancestral Asian region were concentrated in Jasmineae and Oleeae. Climatic niche evolution and speciation rates were not consistently coupled; rather, their relationships with dispersal and diversification were lineage‐ and climatic‐axis‐specific. Oleeae showed more coordinated associations among niche evolution, dispersal, and speciation, whereas Jasmineae exhibited a more restricted, axis‐specific pattern. The ancient whole‐genome duplication (WGD) in Oleeae may have contributed to its distinctive evolutionary trajectory. 
                       
                       
                         Overall, our results support a conditional ‘license to disperse’ framework in which climatic niche lability facilitates geographic expansion, thereby indirectly increasing opportunities for diversification.

title: High‐light adaptation via ferredoxin‐mediated tuning of the photosynthesis–photoprotection trade‐off
authors:
Julián Gabriel Bultri, 
Candela Brugnara, 
Celina Lobais, 
Michael Melzer, 
Nicolás Ernesto Blanco
abstract:
Proposed model of the alternative regulation of the photosynthesis in Fd1-OE  Nicotiana tabacum  plants.
 
 
 Summary 
 
Plants continuously adjust photosynthesis to balance growth and photoprotection under changing environmental conditions. Environmental fluctuations frequently impose a mismatch between energy production and CO 2  assimilation. How photochemical reactions are regulated to maintain performance under these conditions remains a central question in plant biology.
We previously developed transplastomic tobacco ( Fd1- OE plants) overexpressing ferredoxin displaying enhanced photoprotection and growth penalties with a variegated leaf phenotype under glasshouse conditions. Here, we investigate how these plants respond to different growth irradiances using physiological, ultrastructural, and photosynthetic analyses, including Pulse-Amplitude Modulation (PAM), gas exchange, and P700 absorbance measurements, and dynamic-light assays.
 Fd1 -OE plants progressively recovered growth, leaf phenotype, and photosynthetic performance as growth irradiance increased, reaching near wild-type performance at 1400 μmol m −2  s −1 . This enhanced adaptation to ‘high-light’ was associated with a larger fraction of open Photosystem II reaction centers and enhanced nonphotochemical quenching. Dynamic-light analyses further revealed faster plastoquinone (PQ) turnover, a more oxidized (PQ) pool and enhanced electron withdrawal downstream of Photosystem I.
Our results indicate that ferredoxin overexpression redefines the balance between photochemistry and photoprotection. This adjustment shifts adaptation toward higher irradiance and enhances photosynthetic performance under changing light environments. Electron partitioning downstream of Photosystem I emerges as a promising target to improve photosynthetic resilience.
 
 Resumen 
 
Las plantas regulan continuamente la fotosíntesis para equilibrar el crecimiento y la fotoprotección frente a condiciones ambientales cambiantes. Las fluctuaciones ambientales imponen con frecuencia un desajuste entre la producción de energía y la asimilación de CO 2 . La forma en que se regulan las reacciones fotoquímicas para mantener el rendimiento bajo estas condiciones continúa siendo una cuestión central en la biología vegetal.
Previamente desarrollamos plantas de tabaco transplastómicas ( Fd1 -OE) que sobreexpresan ferredoxina y presentan una fotoprotección mejorada, junto con penalizaciones en el crecimiento y un fenotipo foliar variegado bajo condiciones de invernadero. En este trabajo, investigamos cómo estas plantas responden a diferentes irradiancias de crecimiento mediante análisis fisiológicos, ultraestructurales y fotosintéticos, incluyendo mediciones con PAM, intercambio gaseoso y absorbancia de P700, así como ensayos bajo luz dinámica.
Las plantas  Fd1 -OE recuperaron progresivamente el crecimiento, el fenotipo foliar y el rendimiento fotosintético a medida que aumentó la irradiancia de crecimiento, alcanzando un rendimiento cercano al del tipo silvestre a 1400 μmol m −2  s −1 . Esta mayor adaptación a condiciones de ‘alta luz’ se asocia con una mayor fracción de centros de reacción del fotosistema II abiertos y un mayor NPQ. Los análisis bajo luz dinámica revelaron además una mayor velocidad de recambio de las plastoquinonas, un pool de plastoquinonas más oxidado y una mayor extracción de electrones cadena abajo del fotosistema I.
Nuestros resultados indican que la sobreexpresión de ferredoxina redefine el equilibrio entre la fotoquímica y la fotoprotección. Este ajuste desplaza la adaptación hacia irradiancias más altas y mejora el rendimiento fotosintético frente a entornos lumínicos cambiantes. La partición de electrones cadena abajo del fotosistema I emerge como un blanco prometedor para mejorar la resiliencia fotosintética.
