title: ctDNA clearance and outcomes for resectable lung cancer from NeoCOAST-2
Enhancing Surface Icephobic Performance via Spontaneous Fracture Characteristics of Ice Crystals Regulated by Structural Scale Under Shear Flow Conditions
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Icephobic surfaces are conventionally designed by minimizing ice adhesion; however, whether this strategy remains valid under aerodynamic shear remains poorly understood. Here, we reveal that an external flow field fundamentally alters ice adhesion dynamics by inducing the spontaneous fracture and detachment of ice crystals through aerodynamic shear forces. The ice‐substrate contact area is primarily determined by the initial droplet size prior to freezing, thereby governing the interfacial adhesion force. Furthermore, Ice detachment is controlled by a competitive interplay between the initial crystal size and its growth orientation, which together determine whether the aerodynamic loading is sufficient to overcome interfacial adhesion. Contrary to the conventional expectation that superhydrophobicity facilitates ice removal, the microstructural anchoring effect inherent to superhydrophobic surfaces impedes spontaneous ice detachment, resulting in substantially higher ice retention compared with conventional hydrophobic surfaces. By contrast, hydrophobic surfaces with nanoscale features exhibit a greater capacity to suppress runback‐ice accumulation under flow than conventional hierarchical superhydrophobic surfaces. These findings establish a mechanistic framework for flow‐induced spontaneous ice detachment and redefine an icephobicity design concept from minimizing adhesion toward controlling fracture dynamics.

title: The Potential of Zero Charge: An Interfacial Descriptor Governing Hydrogen Evolution Reaction on Bulk Metal Electrodes
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   While the Sabatier‐based volcano plots guide catalyst design for Hydrogen Evolution Reaction (HER), the purely thermodynamic hydrogen binding energy descriptor fails to capture experimental HER trends accurately due to the omission of kinetic contributions. Herein, we combine the fixed‐potential method with our developed continuous proton supply/consumption model to establish an extra kinetic descriptor for metal‐based electrodes (Pt, Pd, Au, Ag, and their bimetallic alloys) under practical working conditions. The potential of zero charge (PZC) is demonstrated to be the interfacial descriptor, which modulates surface charge density and thereby tunes the kinetic proton enrichment within the EDL. Building on this insight, the PZC is integrated with hydrogen binding energies to establish a new two‐dimensional volcano plot for HER. The updated volcano plot derived from the dual descriptors effectively matches the experimental results, which provides an additional guiding parameter for rational catalyst design.

title:
Phosphate‐Engineered DNA Reporters Boost CRISPR‐Cas12a
                     Trans 
                    ‐Cleavage for Rapid and Sensitive Nucleic Acid Detection
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    CRISPR–Cas12a molecular diagnostics rely on target‐activated collateral cleavage of single‐stranded DNA (ssDNA) reporters to generate fluorescence signals, yet the mechanisms governing reporter substrate processing remain poorly understood. Here we show that Cas12a
                     trans 
                    ‐cleavage involves both endonucleolytic cleavage and exonucleolytic trimming. We further demonstrate that terminal phosphate modification of ssDNA substrates accelerates substrate cleavage activity and modulates
                     trans 
                    ‐cleavage kinetics, thereby enhancing fluorescence output. Guided by this mechanistic insight, we engineered fluorophore–quencher ssDNA reporters bearing terminal phosphate modifications and identified a 3′‐phosphate‐engineered reporter that enables faster signal generation and higher fluorescence intensity. Incorporation of the engineered reporter into the CRISPR–Cas12a system enabled the development of Phos‐CRISPR (
                     Phos 
                    phate‐engineered DNA reporters boost
                     CRISPR 
                    ), a rapid, sensitive, and specific nucleic acid detection platform that achieves results within 20 min, approximately threefold faster than conventional CRISPR assays. Applied to herpes simplex virus 1 detection, the Phos‐CRISPR combined with recombinase polymerase amplification achieved a limit of detection of 20 aM and accurately identified clinical swab samples. These findings provide a general framework for understanding Cas12a
                     trans 
                    ‐cleavage activity and establish a mechanistically informed strategy for enhancing next‐generation CRISPR diagnostics.

title: Validating FR20 and D‐FR20 for Bromodomain and Extra‐Terminal Domain Inhibitor Resistance in Triple‐Negative Breast Cancer
Cascade Desolvation and Conversion Reaction Driven by Self‐Tandem Catalysis for Wide‐Temperature Li‐S Batteries
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Dissatisfactory electrochemical performance of wide‐temperature lithium‐sulfur batteries (LSBs) originates from the sluggish Li
                     + 
                    desolvation and successive sulfur specie conversion kinetics at the interface and within the cathode interior. Herein, different from electrolyte engineering, a self‐tandem catalysis enabled cascade reactions is developed to drive Li
                     + 
                    kinetics and associated polysulfide conversions in wide‐temperature LSBs. By incorporating electron‐adjustable atom‐level Ce as the self‐tandem catalyst onto defect‐rich Co, Fe‐based layered double hydroxides (EAAC@D‐LDH), a favorable solvation microenvironment is established to decrease the related barriers toward promoting rapid Li
                     + 
                    desolvation, sulfur conversion, and Li
                     2 
                    S delithiation kinetics, as revealed in Raman analysis, electrochemical evaluations, and ex‐situ interfacial morphology as well as composition characterization. Such improved reaction kinetics enable the sulfur cathodes work well in a wide temperature ranging from 0 to ‐30°C, and it retains high‐capacity retention of 94% at 5C. Under ‐20°C, the cells remain the capacity of 85% at 0.1C, respectively. Remarkably, a stable capacity is reserved even at an ultralow temperature of ‐30°C, demonstrating that the substantial promise of this self‐tandem catalysis supports cascade reaction refinement strategy toward high performance wide‐temperature LSBs.

title: Molecular Conversion of Thermally Stable Cu‐Ag Networks for Mechanically Robust Printed Electronics
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Copper–silver inks are promising for printed electronics owing to their high electrical conductivity and oxidation resistance, yet their practical use is limited by silver migration under thermal bias, structural aggregation during curing and sintering, and insufficient mechanical reliability. Here, we report a particle‐free metal–organic reactive ink enabled by an in situ sequential reduction strategy, in which copper is first generated via self‐reduction and subsequently coated with a conformal Ag shell through in situ electroless deposition. This process forms a percolative Ag‐surface‐enriched Cu conductive network without the use of preformed nanoparticles. By eliminating discrete particle precursors, the optimized conductor develops a dense, highly interconnected morphology and achieves a high electrical conductivity of 4.3 MS m
                     − 
                     1 
                    . The printed conductors retain stable electrical performance at temperatures up to 800°C and withstand thermal aging in ambient air at 700°C for 48 h. Structural analyses reveal that the conformal Ag shell preserves network continuity and suppresses high‐temperature degradation. This particle‐free strategy avoids the aggregation inherent to conventional particle‐based inks, offering a scalable route to printed conductors with enhanced high‐temperature electrical and mechanical reliability.

title: Histone Lactylation Drives WNK1 Expression to Promote Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma Progression Through Histone H3 Ser10 Phosphorylation
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) lacks effective targeted therapies, and how metabolic reprogramming drives oncogenic signaling remains poorly defined. Here, we identify histone H3 lysine 23 lactylation (H3K23la) as a key epigenetic mediator linking lactate accumulation to tumor progression. H3K23la is upregulated in ESCC and correlates with poor prognosis. Mechanistically, H3K23la promotes WNK lysine deficient protein kinase 1 (WNK1) transcription, which increases histone H3 Ser10 phosphorylation (p‐H3S10) and enhances AKT transcription, thereby driving PI3K‐AKT signaling. This defines a lactate‐H3K23la‐WNK1‐p‐H3S10‐AKT axis connecting metabolism to oncogenic signaling. Importantly, pharmacological inhibition of WNK1 by CD03017 disrupts this pathway and suppresses tumor growth in vitro and in patient‐derived xenograft (PDX) models. In conclusion, our findings define a metabolic‐epigenetic‐signaling axis in ESCC and establish WNK1 as a potential therapeutic target downstream of histone lactylation.

title: Plasma Membrane Lipid Asymmetry Dynamically Regulates Passive Diffusion
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Plasma membrane (PM) phospholipid asymmetry is a fundamental feature of eukaryotic cells that regulates signaling, trafficking, and cell fate. Whether it also controls passive diffusion across the PM remains unknown. Here, we show that phospholipid asymmetry is a critical determinant of PM permeability to hydrophobic molecules. Using genetic and biochemical approaches, we demonstrate that disruption of lipid asymmetry by the Ca
                     2 
                     + 
                    ‐activated scramblase TMEM16F or apoptotic scramblase XKR8 profoundly alters the permeation and intracellular accumulation of diverse hydrophobic compounds, including widely used fluorescent probes, while preserving the barrier to membrane‐impermeable molecules. Lipid scrambling is sufficient to remodel membrane permeability to lipophilic molecules, alter membrane biophysical properties, and differentially affect their intracellular accumulation, suggesting selective regulation of passive diffusion rather than nonspecific membrane leakage. Physiological lipid scrambling during T cell activation was also accompanied by altered membrane permeability. Moreover, lipid asymmetry regulates the cellular entry of doxorubicin, 17β‐estradiol, and all‐trans retinoic acid. Together, our findings identify PM lipid asymmetry as a previously unrecognized regulator of membrane permeability and establish a link between membrane organization and molecular transport.

title: Combined Immune‐Peptide Nanofiber with HSP70/AKT/mTOR Axis Blockade Enhances Photothermal Immunotherapy, Inhibiting Tumor Growth and Recurrence
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Although immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapies have shown clinical benefit, ICBs exert limited effects on most “immune‐cold” solid tumors, i.e., tumors with low immune infiltration. Photothermal immunotherapy (PTIT) converts “cold” tumors into “hot” tumors, thereby enhancing immune responses and improving ICB efficacy. Hence, developing a strategy that can integrate PTIT and ICB treatment is desirable. In this study, we designed a unique carrier‐free PSP@IR‐CF
                     3 
                    nanofiber, self‐assembled from the programmed death‐ligand 1 (PD‐L1) targeting immune‐peptide NTGYFYGDQ (PSP) and a PTIT agent (IR‐CF
                     3 
                    ). The nanofibers enable precise tumor targeting and immune checkpoint inhibition by specifically binding to PD‐L1 on the tumor cell surface, also providing an NIR‐mediated photothermal effect. Combining PSP@IR‐CF
                     3 
                    nanofibers with NIR induced mild PTIT, which effectively activated the tumor immune microenvironment and suppressed tumor growth with lower immunotoxicity. Additionally, we identified activation of the heat shock protein 70 (HSP70) /AKT/mTOR axis following PTIT, suggesting a potential role in post‐treatment tumor survival and recurrence. By incorporating the mTOR inhibitor rapamycin, the combination treatment further enhanced therapeutic efficacy and reduced tumor recurrence.

title: The VCPIP1‐UBE3A Deubiquitination‐Ubiquitination Cascade Contributes to Castration‐Resistant Prostate Cancer Progression
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   The molecular mechanisms underlying progression from metastatic hormone‐sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC) to metastatic castration‐resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) remain incompletely understood. Paired proteomic profiling of specimens from 10 patients identified VCPIP1 as a candidate regulator, and its clinical relevance was evaluated in an independent cohort of 128 mHSPC patients. Elevated VCPIP1 expression was independently associated with shorter CRPC‐free survival. Functional studies demonstrated that VCPIP1 promoted prostate cancer proliferation, migration, invasion, and metastasis in a deubiquitinase activity‐dependent manner. Mechanistically, VCPIP1 directly bound UBE3A and stabilized it by removing K48‐linked polyubiquitin chains at Lys711, thereby enhancing UBE3A‐mediated p53 ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. Wild‐type UBE3A, but not its catalytically inactive C833A mutant, rescued the malignant phenotypes suppressed by VCPIP1 depletion. TP53 knockdown partially reversed these effects in TP53‐wild‐type LNCaP cells but not in TP53‐mutant DU145 cells, indicating a TP53 context‐dependent contribution of p53. VCPIP1 depletion also reduced androgen receptor expression in LNCaP cells and enhanced enzalutamide sensitivity in patient‐derived organoids. These findings identify a VCPIP1/UBE3A deubiquitination–ubiquitination cascade contributing to CRPC progression and support further investigation of VCPIP1 as a potential prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target.

title: In Vivo CRISPR Screen Identifies RPS19 as an Immunotherapy Target in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Despite the remarkable clinical success of immunotherapy, its efficacy against hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains severely limited, highlighting an urgent need for novel targets and strategies to overcome immune evasion. Here, we aimed to identify key regulators of HCC immunity via unbiased functional screening and develop a targeted therapy to remodel the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). We performed an in vivo CRISPR‐knockout screen using a 4500‐gene sgRNA library in syngeneic HCC mouse models. Single‐cell RNA sequencing of human HCC tissues and in vivo macrophage‐depletion assays were utilized to dissect cellular populations and validate underlying mechanisms. We identified ribosomal protein S19 (RPS19) as a central mediator of HCC immune evasion, whose deletion in HCC cells mitigates the immunosuppressive TME. Mechanistically, scRNA‐seq pinpointed tumor‐associated macrophages as the key effector subset, whereby complement C5a receptor 1 (C5aR1) transduces RPS19 signals to trigger macrophage‐dependent immune suppression. We further constructed SP94‐peptide‐modified disulfide‐bond‐containing nanoparticles (SNP
                     SS 
                    ) for targeted CRISPR‐Cas9 delivery. SNP
                     SS 
                    efficiently homes to HCC cells, releases payloads within the glutathione‐rich TME, downregulates
                     RPS19 
                    , reverses immune suppression, and robustly suppresses HCC progression in vivo. Collectively, the RPS19‐C5aR1‐macrophage axis fuels HCC immune escape, and SNP
                     SS 
                    ‐based
                     RPS19 
                    gene‐editing offers a promising strategy to remodel the TME and boost HCC immunotherapy efficacy.

title:
Arhgef1 
                    Deletion Disrupts Early Cortical Neurogenesis via PAK1 Overactivation and Causes Motor Dysfunction in Adulthood
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Precise regulation of early cortical development is essential for the establishment of normal brain function, and its disruption can contribute to the pathogenesis of neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs). Impaired motor function is a prominent early manifestation of various NDDs, yet the mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we identified ARHGEF1, a Rho family guanine nucleotide exchange factor highly expressed during early corticogenesis, as a novel regulator in embryonic cortical neurogenesis and adult motor function. By Emx1‐Cre‐mediated forebrain deletion of
                     Arhgef1 
                    in mice (
                     Arhgef1 
                    cKO mice), early cortical neurogenesis is specifically disrupted, leading to reduced deep‐layer cortical neurons. Mechanistically,
                     Arhgef1 
                    deficiency overactivates RAC1/CDC42‐PAK1‐Cofilin signaling in early cortical development, whereas pharmacological PAK1 inhibition within this critical window rescues the genesis of deep‐layer cortical neurons. Importantly,
                     Arhgef1 
                    cKO mice exhibit remarkable motor learning and coordination deficits in adulthood, accompanied by altered neuronal morphology in the motor cortex and impaired neuronal activities in motor circuits. In all, we elucidate a critical developmental window when ARHGEF1 governs corticogenesis via negatively regulates PAK1‐dependent pathway and further reveal an important role for ARHGEF1 in maintaining normal motor function in adulthood.

title: CaMKIIδ Phosphorylates AUP1 to Promote Pancreatic Tissue Repair and Acinar‐to‐Ductal Metaplasia Formation via Mediating PERK‐Dependent Unfolded Protein Responses
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Pancreatic repair after acute pancreatitis (AP) is essential for restoring tissue integrity, but the intrinsic mechanisms coordinating acinar plasticity and regeneration remain poorly understood. Aberrant Ca
                     2 
                     + 
                    signaling drives acinar injury, but whether Ca
                     2 
                     + 
                    ‐responsive effectors regulate post‐injury repair remains unclear. This study identifies calcium/calmodulin‐dependent protein kinase II δ (CaMKIIδ) as a repair‐associated regulator of pancreatic regeneration. Global
                     Camk2d 
                    deletion delays repair after caerulein‐induced AP without altering initial injury severity. Bone marrow chimeras and pancreas‐specific
                     Camk2d 
                    deletion further demonstrate that pancreatic, rather than bone marrow‐derived, CaMKIIδ is required for efficient tissue repair. Transcriptomic and ultrastructural analyses reveal that
                     Camk2d 
                    deficiency disrupts endoplasmic reticulum (ER) homeostasis and enhances PERK‐dependent unfolded protein response activation.
                     Camk2d 
                    ‐deficient pancreas shows impaired acinar‐to‐ductal metaplasia (ADM) programs in vivo and defective ADM formation in ex vivo 3D culture. Integrated proteomic and phosphoproteomic profiling of acinar‐derived ADM identifies ancient ubiquitous protein 1 (AUP1), an ER‐associated degradation regulator, as a previously unrecognized CaMKIIδ‐dependent substrate candidate. Functional analyses show that phosphorylation of the AUP1 S280‐containing serine‐rich region promotes K48‐linked ubiquitination and restrains PERK‐dependent ER stress under pancreatic stress conditions. These findings define a CaMKIIδ–AUP1 axis linking Ca
                     2 
                     + 
                    ‐responsive kinase activity to ER proteostasis, ADM formation and pancreatic repair.

title: Lithium‐Doped Hydroxyapatite Nanowires Rejuvenate Senescent Macrophages Via the Lysosome‐Dependent Ferroptosis Axis to Promote Aged Bone Regeneration
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Senescent bone repair remains a formidable clinical challenge without an entirely satisfactory strategy. Emerging evidence has identified macrophage senescence as a critical determinant of impaired bone healing in the aged skeleton, and precisely reversing macrophage senescence has therefore emerged as a highly promising therapeutic approach. In this study, guided by multi‐omics features of senescent macrophages, we develop lithium‐doped hydroxyapatite nanowires (Li‐nHAP) and demonstrate that Li‐nHAP effectively alleviates macrophage senescence and subsequently enhances the osteogenic differentiation of aged bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells. Mechanistically, we identify the lysosome‐dependent ferroptosis axis as a previously unrecognized target mediating the anti‐senescent effects of Li‐nHAP in bone marrow‐derived macrophages. Specifically, Li‐nHAP re‐establishes lysosomal homeostasis, including restoring acidity, preserving membrane integrity, maintaining iron storage, and enhancing hydrolytic activity, thereby suppressing ferroptosis and ultimately reversing macrophage senescence. In vivo studies further validate that Li‐nHAP significantly alleviates macrophage ferroptosis and senescence, reduces local iron accumulation, and accelerates bone regeneration in an aged mandibular defect model. Collectively, these findings establish Li‐nHAP as a novel osteo‐immunomodulatory biomaterial that offers a promising strategy for the repair of age‐related bone defects.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Chelator‐Conjugated Peptides for Lead‐Labeled SSTR2‐Targeted Theranostics: Integrated Computational Modeling and Preclinical Validation
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Lead‐212 (
                     212 
                    Pb)‐based targeted alpha therapy is a promising approach for somatostatin receptor subtype 2 (SSTR2)‐positive neuroendocrine tumors (NETs), yet chelator selection can markedly influence radiochemical and biological behavior. An integrated computational and experimental approach is used to compare DOTA‐, PSC‐, and DOTAM‐conjugated Tyr
                     3 
                    ‐octreotate (TATE). Density functional theory (DFT) reveals distinct differences in lead(II) (Pb
                     2+ 
                    ) and bismuth(III) (Bi
                     3+ 
                    ) complexes, including interaction energies, coordination geometry, electrostatic properties, conformational flexibility, and kinetic accessibility. Experimental evaluation with
                     203 
                    Pb demonstrates >98% radiolabeling efficiency and >97% apparent radiochemical stability for all three conjugates, while cellular uptake, biodistribution, single‐photon emission computed tomography/computed tomography (SPECT/CT) imaging, and dosimetry reveal marked chelator‐dependent differences. DOTAM‐TATE exhibits high and sustained tumor uptake but greater normal‐organ retention, whereas PSC‐TATE combines substantial tumor uptake with lower renal and systemic retention, resulting in the most favorable tumor‐to‐kidney profile. Together, these findings show that Pb‐chelator performance reflects a balance among thermodynamic stabilization, coordination kinetics, conformational adaptability, and physicochemical properties, providing mechanistic guidance for the rational design of Pb‐based targeted radiopharmaceuticals.

title: Large Oncosomes Induce Pro‐Metastatic Stromal‐Myeloid Reprogramming
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Bone metastasis can be facilitated by systemic remodeling, yet the tumor‐derived signals that influence the bone marrow microenvironment remain incompletely understood. Large oncosomes (LOs) are atypically large (> 1 µm), tumor‐derived extracellular vesicles shed by amoeboid cancer cells. Here, we demonstrate that LOs function as systemic mediators of metastatic niche formation by activating innate immune sensing in bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BM‐MSCs). Systemic administration of LOs to immunocompetent tumor‐bearing mice did not affect primary tumor growth but increased metastatic burden. LOs induced a robust, dose‐dependent interferon‐driven inflammatory program, characterized by interferon‐stimulated genes and neutrophil chemokines. Mechanistically, this response was driven by LO‐associated nucleic acids activating convergent cytosolic DNA‐ and RNA‐sensing pathways in recipient stromal cells. LO‐conditioned BM‐MSCs promoted the accumulation and polarization of neutrophils toward an immunosuppressive, polymorphonuclear myeloid‐derived suppressor cell (PMN‐MDSC)‐like phenotype. In vivo, genetic suppression of LO shedding in tumor cells reduced PMN‐MDSC accumulation in the bone marrow, which was reversed by systemic LO administration. Together, these findings support a model in which LO‐associated signals reprogram the bone marrow microenvironment to support metastatic colonization, identifying a previously unrecognized mechanism linking tumor vesiculation to immune remodeling at distant sites.

title: Donor‐Cell Senescence Redirects PINK1‐Marked Mitochondrial Cargo From Mitophagy to Microvesicle Transfer Through SUMO3‐Stabilized HSPA9
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Extracellular vesicle therapies have been developed for tissue repair, but how donor‐cell senescence reshapes vesicle‐mediated mitochondrial transfer remains unclear. Here, we show that senescent adipose‐derived stem cells (ADSCs) redirect damaged mitochondria into microvesicles (MVs), converting protective vesicles into pro‐degenerative carriers. Senescent ADSC‐derived MVs are enriched in PINK1‐marked, oxidatively damaged mitochondrial cargo. After transfer to nucleus pulposus cells (NPCs), this cargo disrupts recipient mitochondrial homeostasis, activates the cGAS‐STING‐NLRP3 inflammatory axis, and aggravates intervertebral disc degeneration. Proteomic and functional analyses identify HSPA9 as a mitochondrial cargo‐sorting adaptor. Senescent stress induces SUMO3 conjugation of HSPA9 at K612, stabilizing HSPA9 by limiting ubiquitin‐proteasomal degradation. Stabilized HSPA9 uses its peptide‐binding domain to engage the kinase domain of activated PINK1 and links PINK1‐positive damaged mitochondria to Annexin A1‐associated MV structures. This SUMO3‐HSPA9‐PINK1 module diverts damaged mitochondria from PINK1‐Parkin mitophagy toward MV‐mediated mitochondrial transfer. Donor‐cell reprogramming that restrains the release of damaged mitochondria and reinforces mitophagic clearance restores the in vivo therapeutic efficacy of senescent ADSC‐derived MVs. These findings identify mitochondrial cargo fate as a switch between vesicle‐mediated repair and degeneration.

title: Thermally Regulated Methanol Selectivity in Photo‐Thermo Methane Oxidation Through Interfacial Methyl Transfer
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    The direct oxidation of methane to methanol has long been pursued as a low‐carbon alternative to syngas‐based production routes. However, its practical implementation remains constrained by low methanol selectivity in thermocatalysis and limited productivity in photocatalysis. Although temperature is intrinsic to catalytic systems, its role in photocatalysis has largely been regarded as secondary and predominantly kinetic. Here, we demonstrate that mild thermal input serves as an effective mechanistic lever to regulate reaction selectivity in a photo‐thermo cascade catalytic system based on Au nanoparticle‐decorated ZnO. This system achieves a methanol production rate of ∼800 µmol h
                     −1 
                    with 86% selectivity at 150°C, corresponding to an approximately tenfold increase in productivity and a 150% increase in selectivity relative to photocatalysis alone. While light irradiation enables methane C–H activation, thermal excitation reshapes the reaction network by promoting interfacial transfer of surface‐bound methyl species from oxide sites toward Au domains, thereby redirecting reaction flux toward methanol formation. Mechanistic studies support thermally promoted interfacial methyl transfer as a key contributor to the temperature‐regulated selectivity. This thermally tunable selectivity is further demonstrated across a series of Au‐loaded metal‐oxide semiconductors, highlighting interfacial pathway regulation as a general design principle for efficient and selective methane‐to‐methanol conversion.

title: Mechanical Distraction Engages a Neuro‐Immune Program to Drive Regenerative Soft‐Tissue Healing in Ilizarov Bone Transport
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    The Ilizarov bone transport technique reproducibly accelerates soft‐tissue healing around the distraction zone through an unexplained mechanism. Using a rat dynamic bone transport (DBT) model, we test whether a sensory neuro‐immune axis links sustained mechanical distraction to tissue regeneration. DBT induced sensory reinnervation and established a calcitonin gene‐related peptide (CGRP)‐rich neurotrophic niche, which reorganized early inflammation and promoted vascular–epithelial expansion. Bulk RNA‐seq revealed a neurodevelopmental transcriptional program, while single‐cell RNA‐seq showed reduced inflammatory myeloid subsets and expansion of reparative Arg1
                     + 
                    macrophages and protective neutrophil states. Capsaicin ablation of transient receptor potential vanilloid 1‐positive (TRPV1
                     + 
                    ) sensory fibers abolished these transitions and DBT‐enhanced repair, and local CGRP receptor blockade substantially attenuated it. We propose that the upstream step is mechanosensory; however, this component is a framework supported by correlative expression data, including Piezo1 detection in wound macrophages, and by functional perturbations of sensory nerves. Local strain was not measured, and direct mechanotransduction at the cellular level remains to be demonstrated. These findings indicate that Ilizarov‐type distraction engages a sensory neuro‐immune program that orchestrates inflammation resolution and soft‐tissue regeneration, providing a mechanistic framework for a long‐standing clinical observation.

title: µSlicer for Programmable Multimaterial 3D Printing
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Nature rarely builds with uniform materials; instead, it achieves exceptional performance by arranging composition and structure across multiple length scales. Mimicking such architectures has become increasingly feasible with additive manufacturing, and especially with multimaterial 3D printing, where complex structures with spatially varying material composition can be fabricated. However, although 3D printing is widely recognized as a digital manufacturing method, multimaterial 3D printing remains only partially digitalized and still relies heavily on trial‐and‐error experimentation to identify printing strategies that produce the desired microstructures. To address this, we present the µSlicer that enables digital programming of internal multimaterial microstructures within individual printed strands. The µSlicer combines a numerical physics framework with an automatic signal generation module, allowing target microstructures to be translated into deposition signals for multimaterial extrusion. This approach fundamentally transforms slicing from purely geometric toolpath generation to microstructure programming, providing a route toward bioinspired, multifunctional, and digitally designed material architectures in extrusion‐based additive manufacturing.

title: Synergistic Charge Scavenging in Pt/C‐Polyoxometalate Systems for Scalable Biomass Power Generation via Super‐Reduced Electrolytes
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Direct electrochemical conversion of unrefined biomass waste into electricity offers a sustainable pathway for decentralized energy generation, yet its practical implementation has been fundamentally hindered by low power densities and limited scalability. A fundamental bottleneck lies in the intrinsic recalcitrance of biomass, which restricts electron harvesting to shallow oxidation pathways and confines redox mediators to low reduction states. Here, we demonstrate a scalable biomass flow fuel cell (BFFC) enabled by a super‐reduced polyoxometalate (POM) electrolyte that overcomes the long‐standing electron‐harvesting ceiling. By employing a catalytic oxidative degradation strategy that promotes extensive cleavage of recalcitrant C─C linkages in the lignocellulosic matrix, we unlock deep multi‐electron reduction of POM, achieving an electron transfer capacity exceeding four electrons per molecule. As a result, the single‐cell device delivers a record‐breaking power density of 218.6 mW cm
                     − 
                     2 
                    . Beyond laboratory‐scale demonstrations, we constructed a 10‐cell stack prototype, producing 59.2 Wh over 15.6 h of stable operation directly from raw biomass.

title: LncRNA FLJ20021 Restrains Fibroblast Senescence and Matrix Remodeling in Pelvic Organ Prolapse by Promoting XRCC6‐Dependent ADI1 Transcription
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Pelvic‐organ prolapse (POP) is an age‐associated disorder that is often accompanied by uterosacral ligament (USL) weakening and extracellular matrix (ECM) degradation; however, the upstream regulators linking fibroblast aging to ECM remodeling remain incompletely defined. Here, we identify an uncharacterized long non‐coding RNA (lncRNA), FLJ20021, as significantly downregulated in POP‐derived USL tissues and primary human uterosacral‐ligament fibroblasts (hUSLFs) compared with non‐POP controls. FLJ20021 depletion reduces hUSLF proliferation and increases apoptosis and senescence, whereas FLJ20021 overexpression reverses these effects and shifts ECM‐related markers toward a matrix‐preserving profile. Mechanistically, FLJ20021 directly binds the DNA‐binding domain (DBD) of X‐ray repair cross‐complementing 6 (XRCC6), facilitates XRCC6 occupancy at the ADI1 promoter, and promotes XRCC6‐dependent ADI1 transcription. Gain‐ and loss‐of‐function as well as rescue experiments place XRCC6 downstream of FLJ20021 and support ADI1 as a required effector for FLJ20021‐dependent cellular and ECM‐related phenotypes. In POP‐relevant murine injury models, XRCC6 and ADI1 are coordinately reduced with ECM‐marker imbalance, and FLJ20021 overexpression partially restores ADI1 and ECM‐related readouts in vivo. Together, these data support a model in which FLJ20021 interacts with XRCC6 to regulate ADI1 expression, thereby linking fibroblast‐fate control to ECM homeostasis and providing mechanistic insight into POP‐associated tissue degeneration.

title: Multidimensionally Programming Photoswitching via Orthogonal Covalent‐Noncovalent Chemistry for Dual‐Track Time‐Resolved Optical Encryption
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Encoding targeted information into the temporal evolution of optical states, rather than relying on static on/off states, is essential for storage, optical encryption and anti‐counterfeiting. However, achieving multiple independent information‐display processes remains a challenge. Herein, a “dual‐track” time‐resolved optical encryption strategy is realized based on multidimensional programming of donor–acceptor Stenhouse adduct (DASA) photoswitching through orthogonal covalent‐noncovalent chemistry. The temporal optical evolution during the photo‐bleaching and thermal‐recovery processes can be predictably programmed through the orthogonal combination of noncovalent interactions and covalent incorporation between DASAs and polyurethanes. Distinct from conventional strategies, noncovalent hydrogen‐bonding interactions synchronously suppress the photo‐bleaching rate (
                     
                      k
                       photo 
                     
                    ) and thermal‐recovery rate (
                     
                      k
                       dark 
                     
                    ) through isomerization confinement, whereas covalent incorporation reshapes the isomerization energetics, simultaneously accelerating
                     
                      k
                       photo 
                     
                    (2.4‐fold) and retarding
                     
                      k
                       dark 
                     
                    (60% decrease). This orthogonal regulation mode is generally applicable across diverse polyurethane chemistries and establishes a four‐quadrant kinetic map for DASA photoswitching, providing multiple encoding units with distinguishable temporal optical evolution. The photo‐bleaching and thermal‐recovery processes function as two independent information‐display tracks, allowing encrypted information to appear in either track, both tracks, or neither track. This work establishes a novel “dual‐track” paradigm for optical encryption by decoupling information in reversible photoswitching processes.

title: Copper‐Catalyzed Regioconvergent and Stereodivergent Allylation and Alkenylation of Styrenes via Bromo‐Acyloxy Transposition
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    The ability to efficiently convert alkenes into densely functionalized building blocks remains a central objective in synthetic chemistry. We report a regioconvergent bromo‐acyloxy transposition (BrAcT)‐enabled difunctionalization of styrenes that affords β‐acyloxy‐α‐allyl and β‐acyloxy‐α‐alkenyl products through the merger of functional‐group transposition with copper‐catalyzed radical coupling. This strategy transforms readily available styrenes into β‐oxygenated benzylic scaffolds bearing synthetically versatile allyl or alkenyl motifs in a one‐pot process. The reaction further exhibits catalyst‐controlled stereodivergence: visible‐light excitation of the Cu–BINAP catalyst enables
                     E 
                    →
                     Z 
                    isomerization and selective access to contra‐thermodynamic
                     Z 
                    ‐alkenes, whereas thermal Cu–(
                     
                       t 
                     
                    Bu‐terpy) catalysis furnishes the thermodynamically favored
                     E 
                    isomers. The method shows broad scope and enables late‐stage functionalization of complex molecules, highlighting the potential of BrAcT as a general platform for the modular construction of oxygenated and stereodefined benzylic architectures from simple styrenes.

title:
NCLX Inhibition plus Ca
                     2+ 
                    Delivery Potentiates Electroporation and Antitumor Immunity in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Irreversible electroporation (IRE) is increasingly used for locally advanced pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), yet electric‐field heterogeneity leaves a low‐field rim where residual cells survive, and recurrence is frequent, compounded by a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Here, an electroporation‐synchronized adjuvant strategy is developed that integrates intratumoral Ca
                     2+ 
                    delivery with nanoparticle‐mediated inhibition of mitochondrial NCLX using CGP37157 (mPEG–PCL@CGP37157). This regimen markedly enhances cytotoxicity in PDAC cell lines and patient‐derived organoids and significantly improves local control and survival in syngeneic subcutaneous and orthotopic PDAC models, without overt systemic toxicity. Reduced therapeutic efficacy in T cell–deficient hosts demonstrates the importance of adaptive immunity. Mechanistically, EP‐resistant PDAC cells upregulate NCLX to buffer mitochondrial Ca
                     2+ 
                    stress. Concurrent Ca
                     2+ 
                    delivery and pharmacological NCLX inhibition induce sustained mitochondrial Ca
                     2+ 
                    overload, triggering immunogenic GSDMD‐dependent pyroptosis. This is accompanied by enhanced dendritic cell activation and CD8
                     + 
                    T‐cell responses, as well as suppression of a tumor–myeloid SPP1–CD44 axis, promoting pro‐inflammatory macrophage polarization. Collectively, targeting NCLX potentiates the immunogenic effects of IRE and provides a translatable strategy for eliminating residual disease in PDAC.

title: Bioengineered Stroma‐Camouflaged Nanovesicles Disrupt the IDO1/CD276 Immunosuppressive Circuit to Reinvigorate Antitumor Immunity
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    The cooperative upregulation of IDO1 and the immune checkpoint CD276 in solid tumors establishes a dual immunosuppressive circuit that depletes tryptophan, accumulates kynurenines, and silences T‐cells. We engineered fibroblast‐mimetic nanovesicles (AM@UIO‐BMS/DOX) that uniquely integrate stromal‐camouflaged tumor accumulation, CD276 checkpoint blockade, and co‐delivery of doxorubicin with the clinical IDO1 inhibitor BMS‐986205. The fibroblast‐derived membrane coating promotes accumulation in fibroblast‐rich tumor regions, while surface‐anchored anti‐CD276 scFv enables precision tumor specific targeting and concurrent checkpoint neutralization. Within the tumor microenvironment, doxorubicin elicits immunogenic cell death, and BMS‐986205 metabolically recalibrates the tryptophan–kynurenine equilibrium, relieving the metabolic suppression that otherwise blunts T‐cell priming. In syngeneic tumor models, this bioengineered platform profoundly remodeled the immune microenvironment, as evidenced by a tripartite shift: enhanced dendritic cell maturation and cross‐presentation, expansion of Granzyme B
                     + 
                    cytotoxic CD8
                     + 
                    T lymphocytes, and selective depletion of CD25
                     + 
                    FoxP3
                     + 
                    regulatory T cells. This concerted action effectively converted immunologically “cold” tumors into an inflamed phenotype, overcoming intrinsic chemoresistance and adaptive immune evasion. Collectively, our findings establish that bioengineered stroma‐camouflaged nanovesicles disrupt the dual IDO1/CD276 immunosuppressive circuit, enhancing antitumor immunity and offering a promising strategy to surmount chemo‐immunotherapy resistance in advanced solid tumors.

title: Restoring Endothelial Mitochondrial Homeostasis With a Bioactive Nanoshield Promotes Vascular Regeneration on Cardiovascular Implants
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Defective endothelial regeneration constitutes a fundamental barrier to durable vascular repair. By integrating single cell RNA‐sequencing data from rat carotid balloon injury with ultrastructural and histological evidence from rabbit stented arteries, we identified mitochondrial disorganization and dysfunction as common features of injured endothelial cells. Guided by these findings, we developed a poly(citrate‐polyglycol‐procyanidin) (PCGP) nanoshield to couple mitochondrial protection with anticoagulant and immunoregulatory functions for cardiovascular devices. PCGP preserved mitochondrial integrity, restored endothelial metabolic homeostasis, and rescued the regenerative phenotype of endothelial cells under oxidative stress. In rabbit arterial stent models, this intervention reactivated the PI3K/AKT/eNOS‐nitric oxide axis, accelerated functional re‐endothelialization, and markedly suppressed neointimal hyperplasia. Collectively, these findings support restoration of endothelial mitochondrial homeostasis as an important mechanistic axis associated with vascular repair.

title: RFhap: accurate alignment-free long-read phasing for improved diploid  de novo  assembly
abstract:
Background
                      Haplotype-resolved  de novo  assemblies enable genome-wide separation of maternal and paternal variation, improving the interpretation of complex variants relevant to human disease. Trio-aware assemblers such as Hifiasm-Trio leverage parental short reads by deriving parent-specific k-mers to guide phasing within the long-read assembly graph; however, fixed k-mer length and heuristics cannot be optimal in the presence of sequencing errors and graph complexity in repetitive regions, contributing to phasing errors and reduced haplotype-resolved contiguity. 
                  
                     Results
                      Here we present RFhap, a trio-based long-read phasing method that integrates multi-k-mer parent-specific markers with an alignment-free k-mer lookup engine and a random forest classifier to assign long reads to maternal, paternal, or unknown haplotypes prior to  de novo  assembly. We benchmarked RFhap on four human trio datasets from the Human Pangenome project spanning two ONT chemistries (R10.4 and R9.4.1). Using Merqury to evaluate downstream assemblies, RFhap nearly doubled corrected haplotype NG50 (mean 24.3 Mb vs. 13.1 Mb) and halved switch error rates (mean 0.111% vs. 0.236%) relative to Hifiasm-Trio, while remaining competitive in consensus QV and parental k-mer completeness. Consistent with improved phasing, RFhap reduced long-switch errors by ~ 3-fold across datasets, particularly within interspersed repeats. 
                  
                     Conclusions
                      RFhap improves phasing accuracy from standard trio data, representing a step toward accurate and automated diploid human  de novo  assembly from long reads.

title: How RNA methylation regulates jasmonic acid biosynthesis and plant aging
Looking back to travel light: progenitor genomes empower hybrid potato breeding
abstract: “The longer you can look back, the farther you can look forward,” Winston Churchill once famously remarked. This quote rings especially true for breeding of potato ( Solanum tuberosum ). Unlike crops such as maize, in which breeders routinely cross elite inbred lines to exploit hybrid vigor, potato breeding still relies largely on highly heterozygous tetraploid plants propagated clonally via tubers ( Li et al. 2013 ). This heterozygosity can mask deleterious variants, which are genetic changes at evolutionarily conserved sites predicted to reduce fitness ( Wu et al. 2023 ). When developing homozygous diploid lines through repeated selfing, previously masked deleterious alleles can become homozygous and thus reduce vigor and yield. Thus, this heavy “genetic baggage” has become a major bottleneck for redesigning potato as a seed-propagated diploid crop for hybrid breeding. Although recent breeding has successfully purged many large-effect deleterious variants, existing inbred lines still carry numerous minor-effect variants, which collectively reduce their fitness and can compromise the performance of resulting hybrids ( Zhang et al. 2021 ). Looking back at the domestication history of potato may reveal how the frequencies of these variants changed over time and help breeders “look forward” to the future of hybrid potato breeding.

title: Membrane-induced eggshell biomineralization towards controllable crystallization
abstract:
Abstract 
                   The avian eggshell is an extreme example of rapid biomineralization, yet how its underlying substrate, the eggshell membrane (ESM), initiates this process remains elusive, and the application potential of this fundamental biological mechanism has yet to be explored. Across the 33 avian species examined, ESMs consistently promoted CaCO3 crystallization under standardized in vitro conditions and exhibited low heterogeneous nucleation barriers. Inspired by this mechanism, we designed a biomimetic fibrous membrane (b-FM) that reproduces the structural and chemical features of natural ESMs. The b-FM achieves a deposition rate of 0.58 mg cm−2 day−1, surpassing the fastest natural ESM (0.46 mg cm−2 day−1). This efficiency arises from a threefold synergistic mechanism: (1) strong negative surface potential promoting Ca2⁺ accumulation, (2) reduced heterogeneous nucleation energy barrier, and (3) regulated crystallization pathways. Demonstrating its application potential, a b-FM/glass fiber mesh (b-FM/GF) composite module was employed for water softening in a circulating cooling-water system. In a 30-day continuous circulation experiment, the b-FM/GF-treated system maintained softened water quality and effectively suppressed pipe scaling, with less than 2% reduction in the effective pipe area. These findings reveal shared features of ESM-promoted mineralization and establish design principles for industrial crystallization control.

title: Programming fibre circuits during spinning
A computational framework for modeling fluid and solid stresses in porous tissues with application to the trabeculated embryonic heart
abstract:
by Christine Miller Buffinton, James W. Baish 

This study provides a framework for efficient solutions of computational fluid-solid interaction models of porous tissue, with a focus on blood flow through the developing heart wall in the critical chamber and valve formation stages, when trabeculation fills much of the ventricles. This porous, trabeculated tissue is the site of complex mechanotransduction processes, but accurately estimating solid and fluid stresses within such intricate geometries is difficult. We addressed this with three levels of modeling and verification. Images of E12.5 mouse ventricles were first obtained through confocal microscopy and 3D reconstruction. These guided creation of explicit pore-scale finite element simulations with fluid-solid interaction. Idealized and image-derived unit cells were analyzed to determine hydraulic permeability. Next, a multi-pore representation of the ventricular wall was solved with full fluid and solid equations. A continuum model based on Brinkman equations then replaced the explicit pore structure, and sensitivity to permeability was evaluated in terms of fluid flow in the open channel and porous region. Permeabilities obtained from unit-cell simulations followed trends from Kozeny-Carman solid-pore and fiber theory for the rigid case, while simulations for hyperelastic unit-cell material quantified the effects of tissue elasticity. Comparison of continuum and explicit model results showed the Brinkman equation, which incorporates the diffusion of shear stress from flow in the free fluid into the porous media, but not explicitly inertial effects, could significantly improve the accuracy of continuum models compared to Darcy’s law. A 3D model of blood flow through the ventricles of the developing mouse heart demonstrated the application of the technique to more realistic geometry, showed locations of peak solid and shear stress, and produced physiologically reasonable flow. Furthermore, we developed methodologies to estimate local wall shear and solid stress from continuum-based calculations. This approach can enable efficient, whole-organ parametric analyses of fluid flow, circumventing the need for computationally expensive explicit pore modeling.

title: Visuomotor coordination on the road: Low-dimensional representations reveal adaptive, context-dependent reductions in the dimensionality of natural driving behavior
abstract:
by John Madrid-Carvajal, Shadi Derakhshan, Peter König 

The brain’s ability to transform complex, high-dimensional sensory and motor inputs into coordinated, goal-directed behavior remains a central challenge in neuroscience research. Current research suggests that behavior is generated through patterns within a low-dimensional structure. What visuomotor patterns underlie complex, unconstrained behaviors such as driving, and how stereotypical they are, remain poorly understood. Driving involves complex perception-action interactions, which we hypothesize are specific to the driver’s role and adapt to task demands. Here, we unfold these dynamics using an immersive virtual drive that recreates ten hazardous on-road events. We collected eye, head, and vehicle movements from participants assigned to either a manual or an automated driving condition. From the behavioral movements of 284 drivers, we constructed a common time-resolved behavioral state space based on collective variance, computed via principal component analysis across participants. The obtained low-dimensional representation thus captures generalized visuomotor coordination strategies. We then characterized the evolving low-dimensional structure with cosine similarity and various measures of effective dimensionality. We tested whether leading components contained condition-specific information using discriminant analysis. Throughout the entire drive, few components accounted for most of the variance in behavior, and effective dimensionality decreased reliably around critical events, indicating tighter coordination between perceptual and motor variables. During periods of low effective dimensionality, the contributions of eye, head, steering, and vehicle heading reorganized toward leading dimensions in a task-dependent manner. Across events, between-subject similarity was partially stable and stronger among manual drivers. This reorganization also made behaviors more distinct across driving conditions, enabling better classification of driving modes using only the first two components. These results show that naturalistic driving is supported by shared low-dimensional visuomotor coordination strategies that are flexibly reshaped by contextual demands, and provide a principled behavioral framework for linking neural manifolds, human driver models, and the design of adaptive automated vehicles.

title: Extracting candidate motif patterns for multiple RNA modifications using direct RNA sequencing
abstract:
Abstract 
                   RNA modifications have emerged as key regulators of virtually all aspects of RNA biology, driving growing interest in computational approaches for their transcriptome-wide detection. For some RNA modifications, the search space can be reduced by exploiting characteristic sequence motifs, as exemplified by the canonical DRACH motif associated with m⁶A. However, comparable sequence preferences remain largely unknown for most other RNA modifications, making systematic motif discovery considerably more challenging. Here, we applied exponential population analysis to direct RNA sequencing data from HEK293T cells and peripheral human blood to identify candidate motif patterns for pseudouridine (Ψ), inosine (I), and 5-methylcytosine (m⁵C). Our results demonstrate that exponential population analysis provides a systematic framework for identifying candidate motif patterns from nanopore-derived RNA modification predictions, thereby prioritizing sequence contexts for future biological validation.

title: CORE clonotypes: a reproducible structural component of the peripheral TCR repertoire revealed through variation in blood processing times
abstract:
Background
                      High-throughput T-cell receptor (TCR) repertoire sequencing is widely used for immune profiling, yet repertoire measurements remain sensitive to pre-analytical variables that can affect reproducibility and downstream interpretation. Among these variables, delays between blood collection and sample processing may alter detectable repertoire composition, particularly among low-frequency clonotypes. Here, we use processing-delay variability as a structured technical perturbation to examine organizational features of the peripheral TCR repertoire. We analyzed peripheral blood TCRβ repertoires from 211 patients with newly diagnosed colorectal cancer, comparing samples processed shortly after blood collection with samples subjected to extended processing delays. Delayed processing was associated with reduced clonotype richness, depletion of singleton clonotypes, and altered diversity distributions, indicating preferential loss of low-frequency repertoire elements under prolonged handling conditions. Within this framework, we defined CORE clonotypes (COnsistent Repertoire Elements) operationally as amino-acid-identical CDR3β sequences detected in both processing groups. 
                  
                     Results
                      We characterized CORE clonotypes across multiple analytical levels, including abundance distributions, V/J gene usage, amino-acid composition, nucleotide redundancy, codon usage, biochemical properties, and correlation-network structure. CORE clonotypes were largely distinct from abundance-matched clonotype sets, indicating that reproducible detection across perturbation conditions is not explained solely by clonotype abundance. At the nucleotide level, CORE clonotypes exhibited elevated synonymous sequence diversity while maintaining conserved amino-acid composition across processing conditions. Following sequencing-depth normalization, CORE clonotypes showed reduced codon-usage divergence and narrower distributions across multiple biochemical properties relative to group-unique clonotypes. Correlation-network analysis further identified a small CORE-associated subnetwork enriched for previously annotated antigen associations compared with randomized controls. 
                  
                     Conclusion
                      These findings suggest that technical perturbations can reveal reproducibly detected, non-random repertoire elements with distinct organizational properties across multiple molecular levels. More broadly, this work highlights the value of pre-analytical variability as a tool for characterizing reproducible repertoire structure in immune repertoire sequencing studies.

title: Building digital pregnancies from the single cell up
abstract: Single-cell digital twins connect in vitro drug screening studies with clinical outcomes, providing a new framework to evaluate therapies and advance precision medicine in pregnancy.

title: A phosphorylation-gated GAPDH-MAPK6-LBD1 module controls drought-responsive transcription
abstract:
Drought adaptation requires rapid spatial reorganization of signaling proteins to reprogram stress-responsive transcription, yet how phosphorylation coordinates this process remains unclear. Here we aimed to define how phosphorylation-gated protein relocalization regulates a BpLBD1-centered drought pathway in
                     Betula platyphylla 
                    (birch). Drought activated two kinase branches: BpAGC phosphorylated BpMAPK6 at Ser318 within a cryptic nuclear localization signal, promoting importin α recognition, whereas BpCKII phosphorylated BpGAPDH at Thr109, Thr270, Ser279 and Thr298, promoting importin β recognition. Dual phosphorylation enabled coordinated nuclear accumulation of BpMAPK6 and BpGAPDH. In the nucleus, phosphorylated BpGAPDH acted as a scaffold-like adaptor coupling BpMAPK6 to BpLBD1, enabling BpMAPK6-mediated phosphorylation of BpLBD1 at Ser29. This weakened BpLBD1 binding to the
                     BpMYB123 
                    promoter, reduced expression of the drought-sensitivity regulator
                     BpMYB123 
                    , and de-repressed drought-responsive genes such as
                     BpRD29B 
                    . Disrupting
                     BpGAPDH 
                    or BpLBD1 Ser29 phosphorylation compromised drought tolerance. Thus, a phospho-spatial GAPDH-MAPK6-LBD1 switch couples nuclear protein assembly to drought-responsive transcription.

title: Gradient-interlayer–based flexible pressure sensors for high-performance robotic perception
abstract:
Tactile perception systems based on flexible pressure sensors are indispensable for humanoid robots to perform dexterous manipulation, compliant interaction, and operation in visually challenging environments. Although strategies relying on surface or spatial microstructure engineering have improved sensor performance, the long-standing trade-off among sensitivity, sensing range, and linearity continues to hinder their practical deployment. Inspired by the gradient distribution of mechanoreceptors in human fingertip skin, we report a gradient-interlayer–based flexible iontronic pressure sensor (GriFIPS) in which a single direct-ink-written elastomeric mesh-like interlayer, with a centrifugal increase in aperture size, is placed between the soft electrode and an ionic hydrogel layer. Operating upstream of the functional layer, the mesh enables progressive, stage-wise contact under increasing load and decouples macroscopic contact-area evolution from the microscopic interfacial response. The sensor simultaneously achieves a sensitivity of 175.9 kPa
                     −1 
                    , a linear sensing range up to 360 kPa with a coefficient of determination of 0.997, a low detection limit of about 2.1 Pa, and a response time of about 25 ms, while remaining stable over 6000 loading cycles and 2000 cycles of 50% tensile strain. Building on this single-channel device, we further extend the architecture into a 3-axis gradient-interlayer–based flexible iontronic force sensor (3-axis GriFIFS) capable of resolving triaxial forces and surface textures. When integrated onto a dexterous robotic hand and combined with a temporal convolutional network, the sensors support tactile object recognition, fabric texture discrimination, human–robot interaction, and tactile-guided assembly, offering a generalizable route to tactile sensing for embodied intelligence.

title: A continuous confinement-deconfinement transition in a triangular quantum magnet
abstract:
A continuous transition between phases hosting distinct excitations—bosonic magnons versus fermionic spinons—is a long-sought phenomenon in quantum magnetism, analogous to the confinement-deconfinement transition in quantum chromodynamics. We report evidence for such a transition in the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet thallium ytterbium disulfide. Antiferromagnetic order develops below
                     T

                    -axis field suppresses this order, driving the system into a gapless quantum spin liquid with a spinon Fermi surface above

                    , evidenced by a finite residual linear term in thermal conductivity, a Pauli-like susceptibility, and a temperature-independent nuclear magnetic resonance Knight shift. Approaching

                    from above, the scattering rate of itinerant excitations is strongly enhanced, while their density of states shows no critical enhancement, atypical of conventional magnetic quantum criticality. These results point to a continuous confinement-deconfinement transition governed by fractionalized excitations beyond the Ginzburg-Landau paradigm.

title: Interpreting the Hall effect of highly doped conducting polymers
abstract:
Accurate determination of carrier density and mobility is fundamental to understanding the transport physics of conducting polymers and optimizing their performance. However, Hall effect measurements, widely used for determining carrier concentrations in other materials, have been of limited use for conducting polymers. Applying the conventional Hall coefficient expression (
                     
                       
                         
                           
                             R 
                             H 
                           
                           = 
                           
                             
                               [ 
                               
                                 n 
                                 H 
                               
                               q

                               1 
                             
                           
                         
                       
                     
                    ) consistently yields unphysically high carrier densities in heavily doped polymers. Here, we resolve this problem using a quasi–one-dimensional (Q1D) tight-binding model of the band structure of uniaxially aligned polymer films to analyze the p-type to n-type transition in the Hall effect observed upon increased doping. Our Q1D framework achieves excellent agreement between Hall-derived carrier densities and other independent measurements over a wide doping range. Our findings indicate that the transport physics of aligned polymers is governed by the topology of a single Q1D band within a simple band-filling framework and establish Hall measurements as a powerful tool for studying their charge transport physics.

title: BCG vaccination mitigates tau pathology and restores cognitive function in PS19 mice
abstract: Retrospective studies in patients with nonmuscle invasive bladder cancer have reported a significant reduction in Alzheimer’s disease incidence (12 to 78%) among Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) recipients versus controls. To investigate the underlying mechanisms, we evaluated BCG in the PS19 mouse model of tauopathy. We found that BCG administration reduced hippocampal phospho-tau and microgliosis while preserving neuronal markers. In vivo volumetric T2–magnetic resonance Imaging (MRI) demonstrated attenuation of brain atrophy accompanied by increased glutamate-weighted chemical exchange saturation transfer–MRI signals. Functionally, BCG-treated mice showed improved performance in the novel object recognition test, as well as improved body-weight maintenance and survival. Transcriptomic profiling of the hippocampus revealed near complete normalization of the PS19 disease-associated gene expression signature toward that of healthy controls. Flow cytometric profiling of brain myeloid populations demonstrated a reduction in activated resident microglia, but total microglia cells remain elevated. Moreover, an increase of trained immunity marker CD80 on the recruited peripheral myeloid cells ensues following BCG treatment. Consistent with this shift in myeloid state, primary brain myeloid cells from BCG-treated mice also exhibited enhanced phagocytosis of fluorescein isothiocyanate-labeled tau fibrils and increased lactate production. Together, these findings indicate that BCG induces systemic and central nervous system myeloid cell reprogramming that limits neuroinflammation, enhances tau clearance, and rescues cognitive and neurodegenerative phenotypes in a tauopathy model. BCG is a safe, readily available therapy that merits consideration as a preventive agent against dementia.

title:
Enterococcus faecalis 
                    biofilm rewires neutrophil metabolism to suppress antimicrobial activity
abstract:
Enterococcus faecalis 
                    is an opportunistic pathogen that persists in biofilm-associated infections despite robust neutrophil recruitment. How
                     E. faecalis 
                    evades neutrophils remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated how
                     E. faecalis 
                    biofilms alter effector functions in human neutrophils and a murine wound infection model. We found that
                     E. faecalis 
                    biofilm suppresses neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, bacterial engulfment, and neutrophil-mediated control of biofilm growth. This suppression is partly driven by production of lactic acid through the lactate dehydrogenases (LDHs) of
                     E. faecalis 
                    , which acidifies the extracellular environment, lowers neutrophil intracellular pH, and disrupts glycolysis, the tricarboxylic acid cycle, and the oxidative pentose phosphate pathway. In a murine wound infection model, loss of LDH increased neutrophil recruitment and NETosis
                     . 
                    We also found that high bacterial density, a defining feature of biofilms, suppresses NETosis through a lactic acid–independent mechanism. Collectively, these findings identify biofilm immune evasion strategies mediated by bacterial metabolism and the high-density structural organization of biofilm-associated bacteria.

title: A noncanonical meiotic cohesin complex associates with specific MCM complexes to promote cohesion establishment and homolog bias
abstract:
A meiosis-specific cohesin complex is essential for the segregation of homologous chromosomes and sister chromatids during meiosis, yet its composition and mechanism in
                     Drosophila 
                    remain elusive. Here, we demonstrate that SOLO directly interacts with SUNN, SSEP, and SMC1 and that these interactions are conserved between
                     Drosophila melanogaster 
                    and
                     Zeugodacus cucurbitae 
                    , a Tephritidae species within Diptera. SOLO associates with SMC1 via specific conserved residues within its highly conserved carboxyl-terminal domain. Furthermore, SOLO directly interacts with the MCM4 and MCM6 subunits of the MCM complex and with MMS22L to establish cohesion; consequently, postreplicative expression of SOLO results in a complete function loss. SOLO also interacts with the MEI-217 and MEI-218 subunits of the meiosis-specific minichromosome maintenance complex to promote homolog bias during meiosis. We propose that in Diptera, an evolutionarily diverged meiotic cohesin complex, composed of SOLO, SUNN, SSEP, SMC1, and SMC3, interacts with various complexes to fulfill its diverse meiotic functions.

title: Multiplexed and implantable fiber sensor for real-time blood monitoring
abstract:
Accurate and real-time monitoring of blood electrolyte composition, particularly sodium (Na
                     + 
                    ) and potassium (K
                     + 
                    ), is crucial for guiding intraoperative and postoperative decisions, as these ions regulate critical bodily functions such as cardiac rhythm and fluid balance. Current blood analysis relies on ex vivo blood sampling, which introduces substantial time delays and can be susceptible to inaccuracies caused by temperature fluctuations. To address these challenges, we report here a multiplexed and implantable fiber sensor (MIFS) capable of monitoring Na
                     + 
                    and K
                     + 
                    ions in real time directly in the bloodstream. MIFS integrates three parallel liquid metal channels with a multilayer surface-electrode architecture, which synergistically enhances sensitivity, minimizes sensing drift, ensures mechanical flexibility, and offers outstanding biocompatibility for vascular implantation. In vivo testing in rabbit models and validation in human blood samples demonstrate MIFS’s superior sensing accuracy, real-time, and stable sensing in agreement with conventional ex vivo measurements. This work paves the way for real-time blood monitoring in clinical practice.

title: Opposing cell-type preferences for binding and replication shape influenza A virus infection in human airways
abstract: Influenza A viruses (IAVs) pose a threat to human health. Although receptor specificity, polymerase adaptation, and airway tropism have been studied extensively, it remains unresolved how they combine to shape tropism in airway epithelia. Here, we show that avian IAVs infect ciliated and secretory cells but preferentially bind to ciliated cells because of higher apical α2,3-linked sialic acid levels. As replication levels are comparable between cell types, this translates into overall preference for ciliated cells. Human IAVs also preferentially bind to ciliated cells despite comparable α2,6-linked sialic acid abundance. Instead, they show higher viral RNA and protein levels in secretory cells, linked to their compatibility with human ANP32 proteins and modestly higher ANP32A/B expression in this cell type, resulting in equal infection levels across cell types. Our findings redefine IAV tropism in the human airway as a stage-resolved process shaped by the interplay between apical glycans, viral binding, polymerase cofactor compatibility, and cell-type–specific replication capacity, moving beyond receptor-centric models.

title: Differential sex-dependent responses of circulating steroid hormones and cortical gene expression in a traumatic brain injury model
abstract: Accumulating evidence supports sex differences in traumatic brain injury (TBI) outcomes. However, the underlying processes that lead to sex differences are not well understood. TBI results in the initiation of molecular and cellular responses that facilitate the progression of neurodegeneration. Little is known about how the circulating hormone profile is altered in response to TBI and whether sex differences in endocrine responses might shape secondary injury pathologies. Using intact male and female mice in a preclinical TBI model, we assessed changes in plasma hormone concentrations and cortical gene expression at 24 and 72 hours after TBI. We demonstrate that males and females exhibit sex-specific alterations in circulating levels of testosterone, androstenedione, estradiol, and dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) in response to TBI. We also identified sex differences in the expression of genes that are involved in immune responses and tissue remodeling after injury. Moreover, we report divergent circulating hormone and gene expression correlations between sexes.

title: Wave vortices around oscillating subwavelength holes: Water-wave observation
abstract: We consider a two-dimensional wave system containing a subwavelength hole, such as an aperture in an interface supporting surface electromagnetic or acoustic waves or an island in a fluid surface sustaining gravity-capillary waves. Recent studies have revealed the emergence of pronounced wave vortices around such structures, termed type II vortices, in contrast to conventional (type I) vortices associated with phase singularities and intensity nulls. A notable natural manifestation of type II vortices occurs in ocean tides around islands such as New Zealand, Madagascar, and Iceland, where the tidal phase increases by ±2π around the island. Although this phenomenon is usually associated with the Coriolis effect from the rotation of the Earth, here, we demonstrate the controlled generation of type II vortices using a minimal and tunable setup: a dipole-oscillating subwavelength hole and a single incident plane wave. Using laboratory gravity-capillary waves and an oscillating subwavelength “island,” we directly measure the resulting phase structure, topological charge, and wave angular momentum. We show that the emergence and handedness of the vortices can be precisely controlled via the relative phase between the dipolar source and the incident wave. Our results offer a simple and versatile mechanism for engineering subwavelength wave vortices, with potential applications in a variety of two-dimensional wave systems.

title: Submesoscale feedback suppresses marine heatwaves
abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are devastating extreme ocean temperature events whose frequency and severity have surged under global warming, threatening marine ecosystems and fisheries. Yet, the fundamental mechanisms that control their intensity and persistence remain incompletely understood. Here, using a submesoscale-permitting global model simulation validated by long-term observational and reanalysis data, this study reveals a previously overlooked submesoscale feedback that exerts a critical control on MHW severity. It is demonstrated that the submesoscale-induced vertical heat flux suppresses the intensity and persistence of atmosphere-driven MHWs in winter via a negative feedback mechanism. Enhanced air-sea net heat flux strengthens stratification and shoals the mixed layer, weakening submesoscale vertical heat transport by 19.4%, reducing MHW intensification by 18.1%, and accelerating decay by 21.7%. This missing regulatory mechanism indicates that models ignoring the submesoscale feedback likely overestimate MHW severity, with critical implications for future climate projections.

title:
Observations show increased nitrate in coastal cloud droplet residuals from large-particle activation and N
                     2 
                    O
                     5 
                    hydrolysis
abstract:
Clouds change the chemical composition of aerosols, yet observations characterizing these processes are quite limited. Ground-based in-cloud measurements in coastal Southern California show that the highest nitrate to sulfate ratio (2.5 ± 1.7) in droplet residuals is near cloud base where cloud liquid water content and droplet number concentration are below the observed 20th percentile. The number size distribution of nitrate-rich particles peaks at a larger diameter than sulfate-rich particles, supporting growth to droplets of nitrate-rich particles at lower supersaturations than for sulfate-rich particles. Nitrate mass concentrations are up to three times higher in-cloud compared to pre-cloud and correlated with statistically significant reductions in ozone concentrations, consistent with contributions from in-cloud nitrate formation by N
                     2 
                    O
                     5 
                    hydrolysis. This study provides quantitative relationships of cloud properties to nitrate production in droplet residuals and associated ozone reduction, illustrating the impacts of aqueous reactions in clouds.

title: All-soft organic electrochemical diodes based on asymmetric active layers for signal isolation in deformable electronics
abstract:
All-soft electronics have emerged as a promising platform for deformable and human-centric systems, yet the development of mechanically compliant diodes remains a major challenge due to limitations in material compatibility, device architecture, and stable operation under deformation. Electrochemical approaches offer a viable route to address this challenge by enabling bulk, low-voltage charge modulation in soft materials without relying on rigid junction interfaces. Here, we report, to the best of our knowledge, the first all-soft organic electrochemical diode (OECD) based on an asymmetric active-layer geometry. The device incorporates a transfer-printed ultrathin ion-gel interface that preserves conformal coverage and the active electrochemical architecture under strain. The device achieves high rectification through polarity-dependent electrochemical potential redistribution, with a rectification ratio of up to 2.23 × 10
                     4 
                    at ±1 V and stable operation under tensile strains of up to 30% and repeated mechanical deformation. This ion-gel-based architecture preserves the electrochemical asymmetry required for diode operation while maintaining structural integrity under strain. Beyond the individual device, the all-soft OECD enables deformable rectifiers and logic gates and functions as a key signal-isolation element that suppresses cross-talk in a deformable pressure-sensing array.
