title: Lineage-specific and gestational age–dependent DNA methylation programming orchestrates human placental development
abstract:
The human placenta is essential for pregnancy, yet the dynamic regulation of its DNA methylome during development remains poorly understood. To address this, we generated a single base–resolution DNA methylation atlas of human placental trophoblasts across gestation. We identified a lineage-specific methylation program established immediately after implantation, followed by gestational age–dependent methylation accumulation. This program acted as a developmental barrier that coordinated placental maturation and immune homeostasis. By integrating histone modifications and functional perturbations, we revealed a temporal dynamic between H3K27me3 and DNA methylation that silenced proinflammatory loci and a switch from H3K9me3 to DNA methylation at repeat elements to maintain genome stability. Aberrant methylation in preterm placentas underscored the physiological importance of methylation regulation. Using human trophoblast stem cells, we demonstrated that
                     DNMT1 
                    was critically required for maintaining trophoblast methylome integrity and self-renewal, while the DNMT3 family were equally essential for trophoblast survival. Overall, we established a placenta-specific epigenetic framework for human trophoblast development.

title: Polycomb factor PHF19 affects AML initiation, patient prognosis, and survival
abstract:
Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is marked by unchecked expansion of undifferentiated myeloid cells. Although oncogenic fusions such as MLL-AF9 can initiate disease, the early steps of leukemogenesis and the role of cell-intrinsic regulators remain unclear. We previously showed that the Polycomb-associated factor Phf19 is required for hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) maintenance and state control in mice and that its loss (Phf19
                     KO 
                    ) impairs HSC function. To define Phf19’s role in transformation, we expressed MLL-AF9 in Phf19
                     KO 
                    hematopoietic cells and performed integrated multiomic analyses. Phf19 deletion promoted acquisition of stemlike features and reduced responsiveness to differentiation-inducing AML therapies. Molecular and functional consequences of Phf19 loss paralleled those observed in the datasets of patients with AML. From these data, we derived a prognostic signature—PHFScore—which reveals previously unrecognized AML survival-correlating genes that robustly stratify patients across distinct cellular origins and leukemogenic stages, underscoring Phf19’s key role in AML biology and prognosis.

title: Towards intense single-digit attosecond pulses with a 100-mJ-class mid-infrared sub-cycle laser
abstract: The duration of isolated attosecond pulses created via high-order harmonic generation is determined by the number of optical cycles in the driving laser. Achieving shorter attosecond soft x-ray pulses requires minimizing the number of cycles while maintaining a high pulse energy. Here, we demonstrate a carrier-envelope-phase-stable, 100-mJ-class sub-cycle mid-infrared laser that produces a supercontinuum coherent soft-x-ray with unprecedented bandwidth. The system delivers 50-mJ, 6.7-fs (0.88-cycle) pulses at a center wavelength of 2.26 μm—over two orders of magnitude more energetic than any previous sub-cycle laser. We applied the system to high-order harmonic generation and compared the results to simulations based on the three-dimensional time-dependent Schrödinger equation to identify unique features of sub-cycle lasers. This work represents a decisive step toward high-energy half-cycle lasers and high-energy single-digit attosecond soft x-ray pulses that can be used to probe matter and light-matter interactions at previously inaccessible temporal resolutions.

title: Death receptors regulate entry to therapy-induced senescence and orchestrate addiction to IAPs
abstract:
Cytotoxic chemotherapy typically results in the elimination of a fraction of the tumor with surviving cells entering a state of persistence or premature replicative senescence that can lead to recurrence. Here, we show that therapy-induced senescence is associated with robust up-regulation of Fas and/or TRAIL-R2/DR5 death receptors in vitro and in vivo. The latter receptors restricted entry to senescence and exerted selective pressure on senescent cells through promoting assembly of proapoptotic receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)/Fas-associated death domain protein (FADD)/Caspase-8 “FADDosome” complexes, restrained by cFLIP
                     L 
                    . Accordingly, deletion of
                     CASP-8 
                    robustly enhanced entry to senescence and prolonged the life span of senescent cells. cIAP-2, which inhibits death receptor–driven cell death, was also up-regulated in senescent cells, and deletion of IAPs suppressed entry to senescence. Consistent with this, small-molecule IAP antagonists exhibited potent senolytic activity through enhancing death receptor–initiated Caspase-8 activation. Thus, death receptor–driven assembly of RIPK1/FADD/Caspase-8 complexes in senescent cells orchestrates addiction to IAPs that can be exploited by IAP antagonists.

title: Learning by moving: Physical motion accelerates category learning
abstract: Categorization is crucial for survival, helping animals forage, navigate, and avoid predators—all tasks involving movement. Yet, dominant theories of category learning treat it as a purely cognitive or perceptual process. Here, we challenge this view by demonstrating that physical movement can enhance category learning—but selectively. Using immersive virtual reality, we found that performing large actions, such as swinging a lightsaber, substantially improved learning of categories requiring integration of multiple cues (e.g., distinguishing aggressive from noncancerous lesions), while having minimal impact on categories involving independent evaluation of features (e.g., sorting by color and shape). This selective enhancement reveals a previously unrecognized motor contribution to categorization and may explain why prior studies missed it, opening avenues for optimizing training in critical categorization tasks.

title: Single-cell–level digital twins for preterm birth prevention strategies
abstract:
Digital twin models can accelerate therapeutic development by enabling low-risk testing of candidate interventions. In preterm labor (PTL), a major pregnancy complication where clinical trials face ethical and financial barriers, digital twins are especially valuable for evaluating new therapies targeting immune dysfunctions driving PTL. Yet, current models lack single-cell resolution, limiting detection of cell type–specific mechanisms, off-target effects, and the design of personalized interventions. We present Simulated Immunome Modeling of Clinical Outcomes (SIMCO), a single-cell–level digital twin framework that models immunomodulatory treatment effects on the timing of labor using immunome-wide, single-cell simulations. SIMCO’s digital twins are trained and validated on a newly generated mass cytometry atlas of the pregnant immunome exposed to nine candidate drugs preselected for PTL prevention. Applying SIMCO to an independent cohort of pregnant individuals, we simulate treatment effects on gestational length, screening for candidate drugs that delay labor timing and providing system-level mechanistic insight for each drug candidate. Tetrahydrofolate and the combination of aspirin and lansoprazole emerged as top candidates for PTL prevention, delaying labor onset primarily through enhanced mTOR signaling in innate immune cells and attenuated JAK/STAT signaling in naïve CD4
                     + 
                    T cells.

title: In situ processing of fibrous hydrogels by photochemistry for adaptive cellular microenvironments
abstract: Omnipresent in biology, fibrous networks like collagen possess unique properties: dynamic network via crosslinking and degradation. This intrinsic adaptivity plays a critical role in regulating cell behavior via cell-matrix interactions. Built from biological building blocks, however, these networks are challenging to manipulate or even control. Here, we introduce dynamic network regulation via photochemical control in a synthetic and fibrous highly biomimetic hydrogel. As a proof-of-concept, we demonstrate that the dynamic control over the mechanical properties of this adaptive in vitro model can be used to modulate cell spreading and mechanotransduction in three-dimensional (3D) mesenchymal stromal cell cultures. Our approach not only opens the door to on-demand mechanically adaptive gels with unprecedented control, but simultaneously offers easy processibility and cell extraction of the used synthetic gel.

title: How high-pressure ices on large ocean worlds can support habitability: The compatibility of amino acids into ice VI and VII
abstract:
Water oceans in large icy moons and exoplanets are isolated from the rocky interior by thick layers of high-pressure ice, which hinder the direct release of nutrients and organics derived from water-rock interaction to the ocean. Possible uptake of these bio-essential compounds into high-pressure ice phases could regulate their availability in the ocean, but this process is poorly constrained. Here, we measured partition coefficients of glycine and alanine into ices VI and VII under elevated temperature-pressure conditions using a diamond-anvil cell. We observed moderate compatibility of glycine and alanine with partition coefficients:
                     K 
                     
                       p 
                      ,glycine
                     
                     = 0.14 and 0.40 in ices VI and VII, respectively;
                     K 
                     
                       p 
                      ,alanine
                     
                     = 0.21 and 0.35 in ices VI and VII, respectively. First-principles calculations suggested that amino acids could be incorporated into high-pressure ice’s lattice via cogrowth. Compatibility of amino acids into high-pressure ices would favor their transport in large extraterrestrial oceans, opening an avenue to habitability.

title: Coordinated mosquito biting dynamics at the human skin interface
abstract:
The bite of a female mosquito is the critical point of pathogen transmission, yet the fine-scale biting dynamics on human skin remain unknown. Here, we combine high-speed videography, deep-learning–based tracking, and electrophysiology to analyze biting dynamics of the malaria vector
                     Anopheles coluzzii 
                    in real time at the human skin interface. We uncover a previously uncharacterized synchronization of mouthpart and leg movements during probing and identify five distinct below skin sub-behaviors: piercing, vessel searching, blood ingestion, retraction, and withdrawal. We show that disruption of the
                     orco 
                    and
                     IR76b 
                    chemosensory genes can alter some components of normal biting but these effects are subtle, suggesting possible plasticity in direct-contact chemosensation and mosquito bite execution. Comparative analyses show genus-specific biting strategies between
                     An. coluzzii 
                    and
                     Aedes aegypti 
                    linked to distinct ways they find blood vessels. Our findings indicate that female mosquitoes exhibit a complex synchronization of body parts at the bite site via motor and chemosensory processes.

title:
CASTOR1 
                    functional inactivation drives
                     KRAS 
                    -mutant NSCLC and therapy resistance by a noncanonical mechanism of tumor suppression
abstract:
CASTOR1, a cytosolic arginine sensor and regulator of mTORC1 signaling, is identified here as a tumor suppressor in
                     KRAS 
                    -driven non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). In a
                     
                      KRAS
                       G12D 
                     
                    mouse model,
                     CASTOR1 
                    deletion enhances tumor initiation and progression, accompanied by increased proliferation. Although CASTOR1 is rarely mutated or deleted in human cancers, its expression progressively declines during tumor progression and is associated with increased AKT activation and CASTOR1 phosphorylation, consistent with functional inactivation. Loss of CASTOR1 results in constitutive mTORC1 hyperactivation, impaired arginine-dependent regulation of mTORC1 signaling, elevated p-4EBP1 and p-S6 levels, increased AKT and ERK activation, genomic instability, and resistance to KRAS
                     G12D 
                    inhibitors. Tumors and tumor-derived organoids deficient in CASTOR1 are resistant to KRAS inhibition, but this resistance can be overcome by cotargeting mTORC1 or dual PI3K/mTOR inhibition. These findings identify CASTOR1 as a critical link between nutrient sensing and oncogenic signaling and reveal its functional inactivation as an important mechanism contributing to
                     KRAS 
                    -driven NSCLC progression and therapeutic resistance. The results further support rational combination therapies to overcome KRAS inhibitor resistance in CASTOR1-low NSCLC.

title: Primary tumor–derived lactate primes prostate cancer cells for a dormant fate
abstract: The metastatic outcome depends on the state of disseminated cancer cells (DCCs) leading to overt metastasis or undergoing dormancy. Before distant organ colonization, primary tumor microenvironment may shape the decision between proliferation and dormancy. Here, we identify lactic acid (LA), a highly abundant environmental metabolite at the primary site in prostate cancer (PCa), as a key inducer of dormant state. LA-uploading PCa cells undergo a proliferation delay, associated with stemness, therapy tolerance, and invasiveness through the nuclear receptor subfamily 2 group F member 1 (COUP-TF1/NR2F1) activation. These traits rely on LA-driven accumulation of lipid droplets (LDs), which serve as reservoirs of lipid-derived acetyl moieties essential for histone acetylation. Notably, the epigenetic reader BRD4 is essential for COUP-TF1 expression and for establishing and maintaining dormancy. In metastatic sites, where LA levels are low, dormant features are lost, allowing DCCs to support metastatic growth. Last, targeting LA-mediated LD formation or BRD4 activation prevents dormancy entry, reducing PCa cell adaptability and increasing vulnerability to antiproliferative therapies.

title: An innovative colon inflammation-targeting platform for ulcerative colitis treatment
abstract: The therapeutic options for patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) have recently expanded substantially. Tofacitinib, an oral small-molecule inhibitor of Janus kinase (JAK), recently FDA approved for ulcerative colitis, represented a paradigm shift in a field previously dominated by biologics. Tofacitinib, however, carries a black box warning for major adverse cardiovascular events, an elevated risk of malignancies, risk of blood clots, and pulmonary embolism. In addition, tofacitinib is avoided in pregnancy and used with caution in women of child bearing age due to potential risks to the developing fetus. Notably, these potential complications are all due to the systemic distribution of tofacitinib. To address these issues, we developed Lipo-tm-HA, a liposomal platform incorporating mannitol (m) and hyaluronic acid (HA) for targeting tofacitinib (t) to the inflamed colon. We characterized Lipo-tm-HA and have shown that it (i) remains stable in gastric conditions due to HA coating, (ii) adheres to transferrin in inflamed mucosa due to its negative charge, and (iii) enhances macrophage uptake through mannose receptor–mediated endocytosis. Due to targeting, we show that a single oral administration of Lipo-tm-HA at a dose of 10 milligrams per kilogram is superior in efficacy compared with daily treatment with free tofacitinib in a dextran sodium sulfate–induced colitis model. Collectively, our innovative formulation will enable colonic inflammation targeting, reduce systemic exposure, and allow administration of decreased doses.

title: NRF2 coordinates cystine import and glutathione use to sustain ferroptosis resistance and formaldehyde tolerance in cancer
abstract: Cancer cells must balance detoxification of reactive metabolic by-products while preserving redox homeostasis, but how this trade-off is managed remains unclear. The Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 (KEAP1)–nuclear factor–erythroid 2–related factor 2 (NRF2) pathway, a key regulator of antioxidant defenses, is frequently hyperactivated in cancer. Formaldehyde, a genotoxic one-carbon by-product, is typically detoxified via glutathione (GSH), which is also essential for suppressing ferroptotic cell death. Here, we show that NRF2 promotes formaldehyde tolerance through up-regulation of the cystine transporter SLC7A11, enabling a protective mechanism that is largely independent of GSH, which remains necessary for ferroptosis resistance. In NRF2-active cells, formaldehyde reacts with cysteine to form a thiazolidine conjugate, and the combination of formaldehyde stress and SLC7A11 inhibition activates the integrated stress response, suppresses global protein synthesis, and markedly compromises cell viability. Together, these findings reveal that NRF2 coordinates ferroptosis resistance and formaldehyde tolerance, exposing a cancer vulnerability through combined inhibition of cystine uptake and GSH synthesis.

title:
An in situ forming immunomodulatory hydrogel reinvigorates exhausted CD8
                     + 
                    T cells via preserving their mitochondrial fitness
abstract:
CD8
                     + 
                    T cell exhaustion driven by mitochondrial dysfunction remains a major barrier to effective cancer immunotherapy. Here, we report an in situ forming
                     d 
                    -α-tocopheryl polyethylene glycol succinate (TPGS)–based hydrogel [multifunctional thermosensitive composite gel (MTC Gel)] that reinvigorates exhausted CD8
                     + 
                    T cells by preserving mitochondrial fitness through a two-pronged strategy. After intratumoral injection, MTC Gel rapidly undergoes gelation at physiological temperature and dissociates to generate a high local concentration of TPGS, which targets cancer cell mitochondria to trigger prodeath mitophagy. This process induces robust immunogenic cell death (ICD) and blocks tunneling nanotube–mediated mitochondrial hijacking. Meanwhile, NLG919-loaded hybrid nanoparticles released from MTC Gel synergistically restore mitochondrial biogenesis in CD8
                     + 
                    T cells suppressed by indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1. Across multiple murine tumor models, MTC Gel reprograms T cell immunity by reducing CD8
                     + 
                    T cells exhaustion while enhancing effector and cytotoxic functions, thereby eliciting potent tumoricidal activity. These findings highlight this rationally designed hydrogel system as a clinically translatable platform for next-generation ICD-based cancer immunotherapies.

title: Ocean carbon sequestration during glacial climates due to combined Antarctic sea ice expansion and ocean circulation change
abstract: Glacial-interglacial transitions punctuate Earth’s Quaternary climate, accompanied by substantial atmospheric carbon dioxide and ocean carbon storage changes. The cause of atmospheric carbon drawdown during glaciations is uncertain, involving many mechanisms whose interactions are poorly understood. Here, we show that the combined expansion of Antarctic sea ice and associated changes in the meridional overturning efficiently sequester carbon in the ocean abyss, leading to a decline in atmospheric carbon dioxide. In contrast, changes in sea ice and circulation individually result in ocean carbon dioxide outgassing. When sea ice expansion and circulation changes act together, they enhance biological carbon storage by reducing ocean-atmosphere fluxes in the Southern Ocean, without invoking external drivers of the biological pump. This reduction inhibits the outgassing of upwelled remineralized carbon and promotes its resubduction into the abyss. Together, these results reveal a reinforcing feedback linking atmospheric cooling, Antarctic sea ice expansion, and ocean circulation changes to enhanced biological carbon storage and atmospheric carbon dioxide drawdown.

title: Biophysically constrained learning from healthy neural priors improves motor decoding in pathological cortical networks
abstract:
High-performance brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) rely on stable neural representations, yet brain functional impairments inherently disrupt canonical encoding, creating a fundamental decoding paradox. Conventional data-driven approaches struggle to bridge this gap because of pathological data scarcity and heterogeneity. Here, we propose to leverage healthy neural priors and introduce Pathology-Aware Consensus Training (PACT), a paradigm embedding biophysical constraints into healthy neural recordings to guide neural decoding. In a gesture classification task using high-density electrocorticography from patients with gliomas infiltrating the motor cortex, PACT improved the accuracy by more than 10%, effectively restoring the distorted semantic geometry of motor commands and realigning them with healthy canonical representations (correlation increase:
                     r 
                     = 0.66 to
                     r 
                     = 0.94). Mechanistically, PACT induced an emergent “inverse weighting” strategy: The model autonomously suppresses high-power pathological noise while reanchoring spatial attention to functional compensatory regions. This study provides a proof of concept for improving decoding in compromised networks by harnessing healthy neural dynamics, laying the theoretical foundation for future BCI deployments in clinical populations.

title:
The
                     MdVQ22 
                    ‐
                     MdWRKY33d 
                    complex regulates
                     
                       MdPER55 
                     
                    and
                     
                       MdDREB1D 
                     
                    expression to modulate apple salt tolerance by reactive oxygen species scavenging
abstract:
SUMMARY 
                   
                    Apple is a globally significant fruit tree with considerable economic value. However, it is severely affected by soil salinization, which leads to a reduction in both yield and quality. Since salt tolerance in grafted apple trees largely depends on the rootstock, this study compared transcriptomic responses between salt‐tolerant (R5‐5) and salt‐sensitive (M9T337) rootstocks under salt stress. A key salt‐responsive gene,
                     MdWRKY33d 
                    , was identified. Overexpressing
                     MdWRKY33d 
                    in apple improved salt tolerance, while silencing it had the opposite effect. Additionally, under salt stress, compared with the control, chlorophyll fluorescence values, superoxide dismutase (SOD), peroxidase (POD), and catalase (CAT) levels were elevated in
                     MdWRKY33d 
                    transgenic apple and poplar materials. Functional analyses demonstrated that
                     MdWRKY33d 
                    directly activates the expression of
                     Peroxidase55 
                    (
                     MdPER55 
                    ) and
                     Dehydration‐Responsive Element‐Binding protein1D 
                    (
                     MdDREB1D 
                    ), thereby enhancing reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging and salt tolerance in transgenic plants. Yeast two‐hybrid screening identified MdVQ22 as an interacting partner of MdWRKY33d, which was confirmed by pull‐down, bimolecular fluorescence complementation (BiFC), and luciferase complementation imaging (LCI) assays.
                     MdVQ22 
                    negatively regulated apple salt tolerance by suppressing MdWRKY33d‐mediated transcriptional activation of
                     MdPER55 
                    and
                     MdDREB1D 
                    . Collectively, this study explores a putative regulatory module MdVQ22‐MdWRKY33d‐
                     MdPER55 
                    /
                     MdDREB1D 
                    to coordinate the responses to apple salt stress and provides potential targets for engineering salt‐tolerant varieties.

title:
Reconstructing tissue culture to improve
                     Agrobacterium 
                    ‐mediated transformation of maize
abstract:
SUMMARY 
                   
                    The ability to insert, delete, or modify genetic information is crucial for mechanistic studies and biotechnological applications. However, efficient genetic transformation remains a major bottleneck for research in maize and many other crops. Here, we report an optimized
                     Agrobacterium 
                    ‐mediated transformation platform based on systematic reconstruction of tissue culture handling in the maize inbred line A188. Refinement of callus induction, selection, and regeneration substantially improved recovery of transgenic plantlets. To distinguish independent T‐DNA insertion events, we developed TAFLP (T‐DNA amplified fragment length polymorphism), a simple and inexpensive assay that amplifies T‐DNA flanking sequences and can be performed using standard laboratory equipment. Our enhanced transformation pipeline was also applicable to the inbred line B104 as well as to hygromycin and G418 selection systems, demonstrating broad utility of our method. We validated the platform for CRISPR/Cas9 mutagenesis and reporter‐line generation. Using this approach, we isolated new loss‐of‐function alleles of the maize‐specific
                     MAC1 
                    (
                     MULTIPE ARCHESPORIAL CELLS 1 
                    ) and F‐box protein encoding
                     ACOZ1 
                    (
                     ABNORMAL CHROMOSOME ORGANIZATION IN ZYGOTENE 1 
                    ), a homolog of the Arabidopsis
                     RMF1/2 
                    (
                     REDUCED MALE FERTILITY 1/2 
                    ) and rice
                     ZYGO1 
                    (
                     ZYGOTENE 1 
                    ). The concomitant generation of reporter lines for ACOZ1 and the nuclear lamin‐like proteins NCH1 (NMCP/CROWN HOMOLOG1) and NCH2, as well as SUN1 (SUN DOMAIN PROTEIN 1) revealed that the function of this F‐box protein class in releasing the somatic constraints of chromosome organization for meiotic recombination is highly conserved in flowering plants.

title:
MdMPK6a/b‐mediated phosphorylation of MdANN2 restricts cytosolic Ca
                     2+ 
                    influx and attenuates cold tolerance in apple
abstract:
SUMMARY 
                   
                    Annexins (ANNs) are Ca
                     2+ 
                    ‐dependent phospholipid‐binding proteins that play important roles in plant responses to environmental stress. However, the apple
                     ANN 
                    gene family and the regulatory mechanisms by which ANNs participate in cold‐stress responses remain poorly understood. In this study, 15 MdANN family members were identified in the apple genome and divided into three subfamilies. Among them,
                     MdANN2 
                    expression was strongly induced by low temperature. Functional analyses showed that
                     MdANN2 
                    overexpression markedly enhanced cold tolerance in apple, whereas virus‐induced gene silencing (VIGS) of
                     MdANN2 
                    compromised cold tolerance. Subcellular localization assays revealed that MdANN2 localized to the plasma membrane, cytoplasm, and nucleus. Non‐invasive micro‐test technology (NMT) further showed that MdANN2 is associated with Ca
                     2+ 
                    ‐permeable channel activity: cold stimulation significantly enhanced cytosolic Ca
                     2+ 
                    influx in
                     MdANN2 
                    ‐overexpressing plants, whereas exogenous application of the Ca
                     2+ 
                    channel blocker LaCl
                     3 
                    or the Ca
                     2+ 
                    chelator EGTA substantially inhibited this influx. The kinases MdMPK6a and MdMPK6b physically interacted with and phosphorylated MdANN2 both
                     in vitro 
                    and
                     in vivo 
                    . Silencing
                     MdMPK6a/b 
                    significantly increased apple cold tolerance, whereas overexpression of
                     MdMPK6a/b 
                    reduced apple cold tolerance. Moreover, transient overexpression of
                     MdMPK6a/b 
                    in the
                     MdANN2 
                    ‐overexpression background attenuated MdANN2‐mediated cold tolerance and Ca
                     2+ 
                    influx. In addition, co‐localization assays showed that MdMPK6a/b decreased the accumulation of MdANN2 at the plasma membrane. Together, these findings demonstrate that MdANN2 positively regulates apple cold tolerance by promoting cold‐induced Ca
                     2+ 
                    influx, a process inhibited by MdMPK6a/b‐mediated phosphorylation. This study identifies a novel MdMPK6a/b‐MdANN2 module that governs Ca
                     2+ 
                    signaling in apple under cold stress, thereby providing promising molecular targets for improving cold tolerance in apple and other crop species.

title:
SDG26 
                    integrates
                     ABA 
                    ‐dependent and
                     ABA 
                    ‐independent pathways to regulate cold stress responses in Arabidopsis via chromatin modification
abstract:
SUMMARY 
                   
                    Plants constantly face adverse environmental conditions, with temperature drops posing major threats to growth and productivity. To adapt, plants have evolved complex mechanisms of transcriptional reprogramming. While various cold‐responsive pathways have been described, the contribution of chromatin‐level regulation, particularly histone modifications, remains poorly understood. Here, we identify the histone methyltransferase SET DOMAIN GROUP 26 (SDG26) as a positive regulator of cold stress responses in
                     Arabidopsis thaliana 
                    . We show that
                     SDG26 
                    is transcriptionally induced and posttranscriptionally stabilized by cold, and that its loss of function compromises several abscisic acid (ABA)‐related phenotypes. At the molecular level, SDG26 promotes the expression of cold‐responsive genes, including members of the CBF‐COR regulon, through direct chromatin binding and deposition of histone H3 lysine 36 trimethylation (H3K36me3). Additionally, SDG26 modulates ABA biosynthesis, catabolism, and transport, thereby promoting ABA accumulation, stomatal closure, and drought tolerance. Collectively, our results reveal that SDG26 integrates ABA‐dependent and ABA‐independent pathways to fine‐tune Arabidopsis responses to abiotic stresses. We further establish SDG26 as a chromatin modifier contributing to stress‐responsive H3K36me3 enrichment at specific loci. Together, our findings position SDG26 as a chromatin‐based hub that coordinates cold acclimation and water conservation to enhance plant resilience.

title: Non‐peroxisomal allantoin biosynthesis reveals unexpected flexibility in plant purine catabolism
abstract:
SUMMARY 
                   
                    Allantoin, a central intermediate of purine catabolism, plays key roles in nitrogen remobilization and is also implicated in stress protection in plants. As in other eukaryotes, allantoin biosynthesis in land plants has long been considered restricted to peroxisomes, where this process is catalyzed by ALLANTOIN SYNTHASE (ALNS). However, angiosperms produce not only the canonical peroxisomal isoform but also a shorter splice variant lacking a type 2 peroxisomal targeting signal (PTS2), raising the question of whether allantoin biosynthesis can occur outside peroxisomes. Through comparative sequence analyses across Archaeplastida, we show that PTS2‐lacking ALNS exhibits a patchy distribution within Viridiplantae, including species without identifiable PTS2‐containing ALNS homologs, suggesting the evolutionary significance of non‐peroxisomal allantoin biosynthesis. Fluorescent protein fusion analysis showed that PTS2‐lacking ALNS proteins from the angiosperm
                     Arabidopsis thaliana 
                    , the monilophyte
                     Dryopteris erythrosora 
                    , and the bryophyte
                     Marchantia polymorpha 
                    localize outside peroxisomes, consistent with cytosolic localization. Furthermore, recombinant proteins from all three species catalyzed stereospecific (
                     S 
                    )‐allantoin formation.
                     Arabidopsis alns 
                    knockout mutants accumulated racemic allantoin, indicating that ALNS ensures the stereospecific formation of (
                     S 
                    )‐allantoin while preventing the generation of poorly metabolizable (
                     R 
                    )‐allantoin, which likely arises through spontaneous decomposition of the unstable ALNS substrate 5‐hydroxyisourate. Importantly, expression of either ALNS isoform restored normal allantoin metabolism and largely rescued the growth and physiological defects of the
                     alns 
                    mutants. These findings demonstrate the functional equivalence of cytosolic and peroxisomal ALNS in
                     Arabidopsis 
                    and reveal previously unrecognized flexibility in the subcellular organization of purine catabolism in plants.

title:
Leaf‐to‐root
                     ROS 
                    signaling recruits rhizosphere
                     Bacillus 
                    : a synbiotic mechanism for rice adaptability under foliar Cd stress
authors:
Jiahui Liu, 
Xin Yang, 
Yan Gao, 
Wei Chen, 
Yuting Chen, 
Eduardo Moreno‐Jiménez, 
Paul N. Williams, 
Mingzhe Yan, 
Siyu Ren, 
Xiaoyang Zhao, 
Qiuyue Bi, 
Changquan Wang, 
Bing Li, 
Tingqiang Li, 
Qi Tao, 
Zhongmin Dai
abstract:
Summary 
                   
                     
                       
                         
                          In paddy fields near mining sites or transport corridors, elevated foliar cadmium (Cd) exposure is an emerging threat to rice (
                           Oryza sativa 
                          ) production. While rice recruits beneficial rhizosphere microbes against environmental stress, how this recruitment is coordinated under foliar Cd stress remains elusive.
                         
                       
                       
                         We assessed physiological responses to foliar Cd exposure in 26 rice cultivars and characterized rhizosphere bacterial communities and root exudates in six representative cultivars. 
                       
                       
                         
                          Foliar Cd reduced leaf biomass by 6–29% and induced pronounced oxidative stress. In parallel, this foliar stress reshaped the rhizosphere microbiota, with consistent enrichment of
                           Bacillus 
                          . This microbial shift was accompanied by increased root exudation of L‐valine and L‐leucine, which was associated with reactive oxygen species (ROS) signaling and increased root membrane permeability. Crucially, these amino acids promoted chemotaxis and root colonization by the representative
                           Bacillus 
                          strains SRS50 and SRS107, selected from 11 candidates among 241 rhizosphere isolates, whereas colonization was reduced in ROS‐deficient mutants. Functionally, application of a ‘synbiotic’ (amino acid‐
                           Bacillus 
                          combination) reduced grain Cd concentrations by 40.5–43.3%, associated with
                           Bacillus 
                          ‐induced leaf lignification.
                         
                       
                       
                         These findings highlight a plant–microbe feedback loop that contributes to rice adaptation to foliar Cd stress.

title: Ten rules for identifying horizontal gene transfers in deep plant phylogenies
authors:
Siri Fjellheim, 
Lara Pereira, 
Simen Rød Sandve
abstract:
Deep‐level clustering in the GH32 gene family is unsupported and is not robust to the alignment substitution matrix or the rooting method.







Summary
Horizontal gene transfer (HGT) is one of the most intriguing aspects of genome evolution, challenging classical views of vertical inheritance. Growing genome availability across the tree of life offers opportunities to discover HGT, yet recent reanalyses suggest many reported cases may not withstand scrutiny. Detecting ancient transfers is especially difficult, as phylogenetic signal erodes over time and analytical choices strongly shape conclusions. Here we propose 10 practical rules for evaluating HGT in deep plant phylogenies, organised around three themes: genomic foundation, rigorous analytical framework, and biological interpretation. A reliable genomic foundation requires excluding contamination, verifying genomic integration, and avoiding biased taxon sampling. Rigorous phylogenetics is essential, as deep phylogenies are sensitive to alignment parameters, substitution model, rooting strategy, and branch support. We illustrate this with three glycosyl hydrolase families: for GH9 and GH32, analytical choices can eliminate apparent HGT signals entirely, while GH18 shows why complex, multi‐domain families resist confident inference. Finally, HGT signatures demand cautious, biologically plausible interpretation. Recurrent gene duplication, loss, and domain shuffling commonly produce HGT‐like patterns and should always be considered as alternatives. Our rules offer a pragmatic checklist helping authors and reviewers distinguish robust HGT from artefacts, fostering more reliable evidence on HGT in plants.

title:
Embryonal degreening and seed longevity require plastid
                     LEA 
                    proteins
authors:
Dennis Brandt, 
Ana Carolina Vilchez, 
Jürgen Eirich, 
Paulina Heinkow, 
Lea Hembach, 
Ke Zheng, 
Pedro Barreto, 
Jan‐Ole Niemeier, 
Lando Lebok, 
Ivo Feussner, 
Felix Buchert, 
Alexey Amunts, 
Kristina Kühn, 
David Macherel, 
Till Ischebeck, 
Michael Melzer, 
Iris Finkemeier, 
Markus Schwarzländer
abstract:
Working model of how plastidial LEA proteins aid the remodelling of photosynthetic structures during degreening of Arabidopsis seed embryos. LEA42 and LEA48 support thylakoid proteostasis and membrane remodelling in embryonal cells during late seed maturation by maintaining a local physicochemical environment compatible with protein turnover and membrane re-organisation. ATP synthase F1 subunits, ClpP4 and HSP90-5, as pinpointed as potential LEA interactors by proteomic approaches, are highlighted as candidate molecular entry points.
 
 
 Summary 
 
Seeds enable plant embryos to endure extended periods and environmental extremes. Orthodox seeds acquire desiccation tolerance during maturation, before metabolic quiescence. Coordinated thylakoid disassembly and Chl degradation lead to embryo degreening, a hallmark of orthodox seed maturation. While degreening is hormonally controlled, our understanding of the molecular players involved and its physiological significance remains incomplete.
By serendipity, we observed a stay-green seed phenotype in an  Arabidopsis thaliana  mutant lacking two LATE EMBRYOGENESIS ABUNDANT (LEA) proteins, LEA42 and LEA48, which we identified as the most abundant LEA proteins in seed mitochondria and plastids.
Using  lea48xlea42  as a model for impaired LEA function in seed mitochondria and plastids, proteomic, transcriptomic and transmission electron microscopy analyses indicate incomplete thylakoid degradation. Freshly harvested  lea48xlea42  seeds were unaffected in germination but were impaired in germination after high-temperature/high-humidity ageing. Genetic complementation with specifically targeted LEA expression in either mitochondria or chloroplasts revealed that seed longevity support is associated with plastidial, but not mitochondrial, LEA. Light exposure of mature seeds (‘light storage’) reduced longevity, providing a physiological framework for embryo degreening.
Our data identify a role for LEA proteins in remodelling seed plastids before maturation drying and highlight LEA-dependent embryo degreening as a decisive contributor to seed longevity.
 
 Zusammenfassung 
 
Samen ermöglichen Pflanzenembryonen, lange Zeiträume und extreme Umweltbedingungen zu überdauern. Orthodoxe Samen erlangen während der Reifung und vor dem Eintritt in einen metabolischen Ruhezustand Trocknungstoleranz. Der koordinierte Abbau von Thylakoiden und Chlorophyll führt zur Entgrünung des Embryos, einem charakteristischen Merkmal der Reifung orthodoxer Samen. Obwohl die Entgrünung hormonell reguliert wird, ist unser Verständnis der daran beteiligten molekularen Komponenten und ihrer physiologischen Bedeutung bislang unvollständig.
Durch Zufall beobachteten wir unvollständig entgrünte Samen in einer  Arabidiopsis thaliana  Mutante, der zwei LATE EMBRYOGENESIS ABUNDANT (LEA) Proteine, LEA42 und LEA48, fehlten. Diese identifizierten wir als die am häufigsten vorkommenden LEA-Proteine in den Mitochondrien und Plastiden von Samen.
Wir verwendeten  lea48xlea42  als Modell für eine beeinträchtigte LEA-Funktion in Mitochondrien und Plastiden von Samen. Proteomische und transkriptomische Analysen sowie elektronenmikroskopische Daten deuteten auf einen unvollständigen Abbau der Thylakoide hin. Frisch geerntete  lea48xlea42 -Samen zeigten keine Beeinträchtigung der Keimung. Nach Alterung der Samen bei hoher Temperatur und Luftfeuchtigkeit war die Keimfähigkeit jedoch verringert. Die genetische Komplementation durch gezielte LEA-Expression entweder in Mitochondrien oder Chloroplasten zeigte, dass der Beitrag zur Samenlanglebigkeit mit plastidären, nicht jedoch mit mitochondrialen LEA-Proteinen verbunden ist. Die Lichtexposition reifer Samen (‘Lichtlagerung’) verringerte ihre Langlebigkeit und liefert damit einen physiologischen Erklärungsrahmen für die Entgrünung des Embryos.
Unsere Daten zeigen eine Rolle von LEA-Proteinen bei der Umstrukturierung von Samenplastiden vor der Austrocknung während der Reifung. Außerdem unterstreichen sie die Bedeutung der LEA-abhängigen Entgrünung des Embryos als entscheidenden Faktor für die Samenlanglebigkeit.
 
 Résumé 
 
Les graines permettent aux embryons de se conserver pendant de longues périodes et de résister à des conditions environnementales extrêmes. Les graines orthodoxes acquièrent une tolérance à la dessiccation au cours de leur maturation, avant d’entrer en quiescence métabolique. La dégradation coordonnée des thylakoïdes et de la chlorophylle entraîne le déverdissage des embryons, une caractéristique de la maturation des graines orthodoxes. Bien que le déverdissage soit contrôlé par des hormones, notre compréhension des composants moléculaires impliqués et de la signification physiologique de ce processus reste incomplète.
Nous avons observé que les graines de mutants d’ Arabidopsis thaliana  dépourvus de deux protéines LATE EMBRYOGENESIS ABUNDANT (LEA), LEA42 et LEA48, ne déverdissaient pas complètement (phénotype « stay-green »). Nous avons identifié LEA42 et LEA 48 comme les protéines LEA les plus abondantes dans les mitochondries et les plastes des graines.
Nous avons utilisé  lea48xlea42  comme modèle d’une fonction altérée des protéines LEA dans les mitochondries et les plastes des graines. Des analyses protéomiques et transcriptomiques ainsi que la microscopie électronique en transmission indiquent une dégradation incomplète des thylakoïdes. Les graines  lea48xlea42  fraîchement récoltées ne présentaient aucune altération de la germination. Néanmoins, le vieillissement des graines à des températures et humidités élevées réduisait leur capacité de germination. La complémentation génétique de  lea48xlea42  par une expression ciblée des protéines LEA dans les mitochondries ou dans les plastes a montré que la longévité des graines est liée aux protéines LEA plastidiales, mais pas aux protéines LEA mitochondriales. L’exposition des graines matures à la lumière (« stockage à la lumière ») a réduit leur longévité, fournissant ainsi un cadre physiologique pour expliquer le déverdissage des embryons.
Nos analyses montrent un rôle des protéines LEA dans le remodelage des plastes avant la dessiccation au cours de la maturation. De plus, nos résultats soulignent l’importance des protéines LEA dans le déverdissage des embryons, un facteur déterminant de la longévité des graines.

title: Field generation of triparental sugar beet plants through polyspermy‐induced three‐parent breeding
authors:
Saurabh Joshi, 
Christian A. Beer, 
Yanbo Mao, 
Thomas Nakel, 
Thomas Baum, 
Dawit G. Tekleyohans, 
Constantin Bubenheim, 
Joakim Palovaara, 
Olaf Czarnecki, 
Dieter Hackenberg, 
Rita Groß‐Hardt
abstract: Polyspermy, the fertilization of an egg by two sperm cells, can generate viable triparental offspring in the model plant  Arabidopsis thaliana . To explore the potential for three-parent breeding in a crop species, male-sterile sugar beet plants were grown alongside genetically distinct pollen donors carrying dominant, traceable selection markers. Progeny carrying genetic signatures from two fathers were identified and subjected to further genetic analysis. The combined detection of paternal markers from two pollen donors and an additional chromosome set confirms the triparental origin of these plants, demonstrating the potential for three-parent breeding in sugar beet under field conditions.

title: Developmental transcriptomic analysis of primary mouse cortical neurons reveals sex-specific expression of neuropeptides
abstract: Primary neuronal cultures derived from mouse tissue serve as an essential model for investigating neuronal development and function. Despite this, comprehensive developmental and sex-specific transcriptomic profiles in primary neurons have not been defined. Here, we perform multiplexed RNA sequencing of neurons derived from male and female cortices across time. We validate this approach by assessing established neuronal maturation genes and identify highly stable genes to serve as controls across development. Next, using linear modeling and temporal regression, we define developmentally regulated transcripts, longitudinal expression dynamics, and gene signatures associated with transition states throughout development. Unexpectedly, this also reveals sex-specific effects on autosomal genes that emerge only after neuronal maturation even in the absence of in vivo cues. Most notably, neuropeptide genes Cortistatin and Neurokinin A are more highly expressed in female neurons. Furthermore, exposure to these neuropeptides elicits distinct transcriptional responses in male- versus female-derived cultures. These findings provide a valuable resource and reveal sex-specific autosomal transcriptional signatures that emerge in neurons maintained ex vivo.

title: A new noninvasive prenatal paternity test based on double nucleotide polymorphisms abates sequencing uncertainties and improves sensitivity
abstract:
Noninvasive prenatal paternity testing (NIPAT) based on fetal cell-free DNA (fetal cfDNA) has gained increasing relevance in forensic genetics. However, its applicability and reliability are often limited by the low fetal DNA fraction and by high-throughput sequencing errors that can be misinterpreted as inherited paternal variants. Here, we present NEWPAT, a novel NIPAT approach based on Double Nucleotide Polymorphisms (DNPs), i.e. biallelic variants composed of two adjacent nucleotides arising from a single mutational event. These markers offer a key advantage compared to single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs): the likelihood of both positions being affected by independent sequencing errors is extremely low, thus improving the specificity of fetal DNA detection. We develop a targeted amplicon-based panel including 979 markers (845 autosomal and 80 X Chromosome DNPs, plus 54 Y SNPs), and test at depths ranging from 1,000× to 10,000× on 42 individuals, including genomic DNA from 4 families, 2 artificial maternal-child mixtures simulating cfDNA and actual cfDNA from 12 pregnant women plus the putative biological fathers. We observe a DNP sequencing error rate of 8.9×10
                     -5 
                    , i.e. ~12 times lower than the observed single base error rate. By exploiting the full range of sequencing depths at loci supporting the fetal genotype, we obtain Combined Paternity Index curves that consistently lead to the correct paternity attribution or exclusion in all true or false mother-father pairs. Notably, NEWPAT proves effective even at fetal cfDNA levels as low as 0.2%, when existing SNP-based protocols lead to inconclusive results, offering a highly sensitive and accurate NIPAT strategy.

title: A cotton MAPK cascade protects the cell wall against Verticillium wilt

BnaA8.RAP2.1 negatively regulates cuticular wax accumulation and drought tolerance in
                     Brassica napus
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Cuticular wax is an important component of the plant surface barrier that contributes to water retention and drought adaptation. However, the transcriptional mechanisms that negatively regulate wax accumulation remain poorly understood. Here, we identify BnaA8.RAP2.1, an AP2/ERF transcriptional repressor, as a negative regulator of cuticular wax accumulation and drought tolerance in Brassica napus. Loss- and gain-of-function analyses revealed reciprocal effects of BnaA8.RAP2.1 on wax deposition, cuticle permeability, water loss, and drought tolerance. BnaA8.RAP2.1-overexpressing plants exhibited reduced wax accumulation, increased cuticle permeability and water loss, and greater drought sensitivity, whereas knockout plants showed the opposite phenotypes. Stomatal aperture measurements further revealed genotype-dependent responses under drought, suggesting that altered stomatal responses may also contributes to BnaA8.RAP2.1-mediated drought phenotypes. Mechanistically, BnaA8.RAP2.1 directly bound to and repressed the promoters of BnCER1-2 and BnGCN5, as demonstrated by ChIP–qPCR, EMSA, and dual-luciferase assays. Genetic rescue analysis showed that BnCER1-2 overexpression partially restored wax accumulation, water retention, and drought tolerance in RAP2.1-overexpression plants, supporting BnCER1-2 as a functional downstream target. Moreover, constitutive expression of BnaA8.RAP2.1 in Arabidopsis rap2.1 mutant backgrounds produced wax- and drought-related phenotypes consistent with the negative regulatory activity of BnaA8.RAP2.1 in a heterologous system. Together, our findings establish BnaA8.RAP2.1 as a transcriptional repressor of cuticular wax accumulation and reveal that its effects on drought tolerance involve both cuticle-associated water retention and stomatal responses, providing a potential target for improving drought resilience in rapeseed.

title: Plastid tRNA-derived small RNAs associate with AGO1 and accumulate upon sulfur deprivation in Chlamydomonas
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Transfer RNA-derived small RNAs (tDRs) represent a diverse class of noncoding RNAs with emerging regulatory roles across all domains of life. In the green alga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii, next-generation sequencing revealed abundant, specific tDRs, with a predominance of those derived from plastid-encoded tRNAs. Most of these tDRs map to the 5’ ends of mature tRNAs and are 29-33 nucleotides in length, suggesting that they arise from cleavage at the anticodon loop or stem. We confirmed the plastid origin of some tDRs by engineering the chloroplast genome to replace the plastid-encoded tRNAAsn(GTT) gene with a nuclear counterpart. As reported in land plants, DICER-LIKE endonucleases play a limited role in tDR biogenesis in Chlamydomonas. However, a distinct subset of abundant tDRs, originating from both nucleus- and chloroplast-encoded tRNAs, associates with ARGONAUTE1 (AGO1). Using Gaussia luciferase reporter assays, we demonstrated that AGO1-associated tDRs can mediate RNAi-like gene silencing, and that tDRs originating from plastid-encoded tRNAs can function outside the chloroplast. Additionally, the tDR population in Chlamydomonas undergoes dynamic changes in response to nutrient availability. While nitrogen starvation causes a general decrease in both mature tRNA and tDR levels, sulfur deprivation specifically induces the accumulation of certain tDRs. Furthermore, strains in which the plastid tRNAAsn(GTT) gene was replaced by a nuclear counterpart exhibited phenotypic defects under sulfur-deprived conditions, suggesting a potential regulatory role for plastid-derived tDRs in nutrient stress responses. Collectively, these findings expand our understanding of tDR functions, particularly those of chloroplast origin, in photosynthetic eukaryotes.

title: MITE insertions generate enhancers for iron transporter CwIRT1 activation in citrus
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Iron (Fe) deficiency constrains citrus productivity in alkaline soils. Although the high-affinity Fe transporter IRT1 is essential for Fe acquisition, its transcriptional regulation in citrus remains unclear. Here, we reveal that differential tolerance to Fe deficiency between Fe-sensitive Poncirus trifoliata (P. trifoliata) and Fe-tolerant Citrus wilsonii Tanaka (C. wilsonii) is linked to rapid induction of CwIRT1. We further identify two unique miniature inverted-repeat transposable elements (MITE1 and MITE2) in the promoter region of CwIRT1, which act as Fe-deficiency-responsive enhancers. These two MITEs respectively generate binding sites for the transcription factors CwERF12 and CwARF12, both of which are upregulated under low-Fe conditions. CRISPR/Cas9-mediated dual knockout of CwERF12 and CwARF12, but not single mutations, suppresses CwIRT1 expression and reduces root Fe uptake. We propose that MITEs carrying TF-binding motifs can serve as enhancers recruiting stress-responsive transcription factors to activate CwIRT1, highlighting transposable element-mediated cis-regulatory as a driver of nutrient stress adaptation in perennial crops.

title:
A novel
                     Phytophthora 
                    -specific putative lipid-binding protein triggers plant immunity
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Plants recognize conserved pathogen-derived molecules to activate pattern-triggered immunity (PTI), yet many secreted proteins from oomycete pathogens remain functionally uncharacterized. Here, we identified PcCF16, a previously uncharacterized secreted protein from Phytophthora capsici, through activity-guided fractionation of the pathogen secretome. PcCF16 induced cell death and PTI-associated gene expression in Nicotiana benthamiana, and purified recombinant PcCF16 triggered reactive oxygen species production across multiple plant species. PcCF16-induced cell death was independent of the co-receptors BAK1 and SOBIR1, while defense gene activation remained SOBIR1-independent but was partially dependent on BAK1. Recombinant PcCF16 pretreatment enhanced resistance to P. capsici, while P. capsici lines constitutively expressing PcCF16 exhibited reduced virulence. Structure-function analysis identified residues 202-291 as the shortest fragment tested that was sufficient for cell death induction, whereas N-glycosylation enhanced PcCF16 accumulation and activity but was not strictly required. Structural analyses revealed similarity between PcCF16 and members of the tubular lipid-binding protein (TULIP) superfamily and predicted internal hydrophobic cavities. Consistent with these features, PcCF16 preferentially associated with phosphatidic acid in vitro. Despite substantial sequence divergence, PcCF16 homologs retained similar predicted protein folds but differed in cell death-inducing activity, with surrounding protein context influencing the activity of the conserved C-terminal region. PcCF16 was preferentially expressed during the necrotrophic phase of infection, suggesting a biological function distinct from that of typical early-stage immune elicitors. Together, these findings identify PcCF16 as a Phytophthora-specific secreted immune elicitor with potential lipid-associated functions and reveal an unusual link between late-stage pathogen biology and plant immune activation.

title: Phytohormonal networks and thermomemory in plant heat stress tolerance: From mechanistic integration to precision engineering
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Rising global temperatures pose a major threat to crop productivity, requiring mechanistically informed, scalable strategies to enhance heat stress (HS) tolerance. Phytohormones are central regulators of plant HS responses; however, tolerance instead emerges from dynamic, context-dependent network behavior. This review provides a mechanism-oriented synthesis of how major phytohormones coordinate HS adaptation. Specifically, we (i) reframe phytohormone action through core regulatory modules, including redox control, carbon-energy allocation, reproductive stability, and growth–defense trade-offs; (ii) resolve phytohormonal crosstalk into functional interaction networks that determine stress outcomes; (iii) define the molecular basis of heat priming and thermomemory; and (iv) evaluate translational strategies, including genetic engineering, precision breeding, and advanced delivery systems, together with their limitations under field conditions. We propose a unifying conceptual model in which HS tolerance is an emergent property of hierarchical phytohormonal networks operating across fast signaling, transcriptional memory, and metabolic buffering layers. This framework shifts the focus from single-pathway manipulation toward precision “hormonomics” and network-level engineering, providing a systems-level platform for developing climate-proof crops in a future, hotter climate.

title:
LhMYB93–LhEAT1 module modulated by LhBRG3 regulates tapetum degradation and pollen fertility in lily (
                     Lilium Asiatica. 
                    hybrida)
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Male sterility is crucial for solving pollen contamination and promoting inter-varietal hybridization. As the innermost layer of the anther, the tapetum directly contacts microspores, and tapetal abnormalities typically lead directly to male sterility. However, the regulatory mechanisms of tapetal degradation and its transport of substances to microspores remain poorly understood. This study identified LhMYB93 as a key positive regulator of tapetum degradation and microspore development in lilies. Specifically, transcriptomic analysis combined with transcriptomic and functional analyses revealed that LhMYB93 is expressed at lower levels in male-sterile lilies, and LhMYB93 can partially restore pollen fertility in male-sterile lilies. Additionally, LhMYB93 interacts with LhEAT1 to effectively activate the transcription of LhABCG26, a gene essential for tapetum degradation and microspore development. Additionally, in vitro and in vivo ubiquitination experiments have demonstrated that the LhEAT1–LhMYB93 module is ubiquitinated by the E3 ubiquitin ligase LhBRG3 during the late stages of anther development (S9–10) and subsequently degraded by the 26S proteasome. This process ensures the normal development and timely degradation of the tapetum, promoting the normal development of pollen. These findings provide novel insights into the regulatory mechanisms governing microspore development following tapetum degradation during lily anther development, expanding the regulatory framework of programmed cell death (PCD) and nutrient transport in tapetum during pollen development in monocotyledons.

title: VvMYBC2-L1 cooperates with histone deacetylase VvHDA15 to repress anthocyanin biosynthesis in grape under high temperature
abstract:
Abstract 
                   High temperature restricts anthocyanin accumulation in grape berries, but how transcriptional repressors coordinate with chromatin regulation remains unclear. We identified the MYB repressor VvMYBC2-L1 as a heat-responsive regulator through transcriptome analysis and functional assays. VvMYBC2-L1 overexpression reduced berry and callus pigmentation, anthocyanin accumulation, and expression of phenylpropanoid and anthocyanin biosynthetic genes. VvMYBC2-L1 associated with selected VvPAL and VvUFGT promoter regions, interacted with the basic helix-loop-helix protein VvMYC1, weakened the VvMYBA1–VvMYC1 interaction, and reduced their activation of both promoters. VvMYBC2-L1 also directly interacted with VvHDA15, a nuclear class II histone deacetylase with enzymatic activity in vitro. VvHDA15 overexpression repressed anthocyanin accumulation and reduced histone H3 lysine 9 acetylation at selected VvPAL and VvUFGT promoter regions. Conversely, VvHDA15 silencing partially restored berry coloration and anthocyanin accumulation under high temperature. Co-expression of VvMYBC2-L1 and VvHDA15 strengthened repression of anthocyanin accumulation and target-gene expression and further reduced histone acetylation at selected promoter regions relative to VvHDA15 overexpression alone. These findings identify functional cooperation between a heat-responsive MYB repressor and histone deacetylation that limits anthocyanin biosynthesis in grape berries.

title: SWEET uniporters – a 2026 update
abstract:
Abstract 
                   SWEETs are a family of ancient sugar transporters found in Archaea, Eubacteria, oomycetes, fungi, plants and metazoa. In plants, SWEETs play central roles in carbon allocation from source to sink tissues, as well as reproductive development, response to changes in environmental conditions, and biotic interactions. Recent studies have provided deeper mechanistic insights into SWEET-mediated transport, including substrate specificity, transport selectivity, structural dynamics, and the physiological diversification of family members across species. Emerging evidence highlights roles of SWEETs in symbiotic interactions and microbiome-associated carbon exchange. Given the growing number of recent reviews on SWEET physiology, this update focuses on current challenges and emerging perspectives on SWEET-mediated transport processes, cell-type specificity, functional diversification, the interpretation of overexpression phenotypes, and functions in symbiotic interactions. We also discuss how these insights may be leveraged to optimize carbon partitioning, improve resilience, and enhance crop productivity and biofuel production.

title: Spatiotemporal Transcriptomics of Litchi Fruitlet Abscission Reveals a Compartmentalized Regulatory Network and Identifies LcERF61 as a Key Regulator
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Organ abscission is a developmental process crucial for both plant life cycles and agricultural productivity, but its spatial restriction to the tiny abscission zone (AZ) has made investigating the underlying molecular mechanisms challenging. Here, we applied spatiotemporal transcriptomics to dissect fruitlet abscission in litchi (Litchi chinensis Sonn.). This approach reveals an unexpected spatial compartmentalization of the gene regulatory landscape within the AZ. Upon attenuation of IAA polar transport, local ET, ABA, and GA pathways within the AZ core may converge to form an abscission initiation center. These signals are subsequently interpreted by spatially defined transcription factors, which translate them into domain-specific outputs and coordinate the spatiotemporal programs of cell wall remodeling. Accordingly, we show that the onset of cell degradation within the AZ begins in the central region and then extends to the outer boundary. Crucially, we functionally established LcERF61, which is strongly induced in the AZ following abscission, as a key positive regulator of fruitlet abscission. Moreover, DNA affinity purification sequencing (DAP-seq) indicated that LcERF61 directly binds to and activates the promoters of LcIDL1 (INFLORESCENCE DEFICIENT IN ABSCISSION-like) and LcIDL3, which encode small signaling peptides essential for abscission. Our findings reveal a spatially compartmentalized regulatory framework for organ abscission and establish the LcERF61-LcIDL1/3 module as a key signaling hub, providing a conceptual advance in understanding how plants execute precise organ abscission.

title: Unveiling the role of crystallinity of RuO2 catalysts for regulating the acidic oxygen evolution reaction
abstract:
Abstract 
                   The intrinsic role of crystallinity in regulating the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) on RuO2 remains elusive due to the synthetic challenge of decoupling structural order from compositional variations. Here, we develop an oxygen-partial-pressure-controlled pyrolysis strategy to achieve graded crystallinity in pure RuO2 nanocatalysts, establishing a pristine model to elucidate this structure-function relationship. We reveal that amorphous RuO2 features disordered dangling oxygen that readily undergoes protonation, triggering a rapid but degradative lattice oxygen-mediated mechanism (LOM) with an ultralow overpotential of 154 mV at 10 mA cm−2. Conversely, increasing crystallinity stabilizes the RuO6 framework, suppressing protonation and shifting the pathway toward the stable adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM). Crucially, highly crystalline RuO2 demands excessive cell voltages (1.72 V at 1.0 A cm−2) in proton exchange membrane electrolyzers, paradoxically accelerating oxidative etching. This work uncovers a crystallinity-driven LOM-to-AEM transition, identifying intermediate crystallinity as a practical strategy for balancing activity and stability.

title: Two pathways driving Phanerozoic temperature change: low-latitude radiative forcing and outgassing-weathering-vegetation carbon feedbacks
abstract: Two potentially interacting pathways may have shaped Phanerozoic temperature change: radiative effects linked to low-latitude land area and carbon-cycle feedbacks involving volcanic outgassing, silicate weathering, and terrestrial organic-carbon burial. Together, these processes provide a framework for understanding long-term climate evolution over the past 540 million years.

title: The Evolution of Brain-Computer Interfaces Towards Collaborative Intelligence
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) are evolving from unidirectional control toward deeper integration of biological and machine intelligence. This transition is constrained by two complementary bottlenecks: Intent Mismatch, or Brain-to-Machine Underreach, in which user intentions cannot be sufficiently decoded, represented, or executed by the machine; and State Mismatch, or Machine-to-Brain Overload, in which system demands exceed the user’s current cognitive, affective, or neural resources. This review uses these two mismatches as an organizing framework for examining the evolution of BCIs toward brain-machine collaborative intelligence, while distinguishing non-invasive and invasive modalities according to their signal characteristics and translational constraints. We review neural decoding, generative artificial intelligence, and shared control as approaches for reducing Intent Mismatch, and passive BCIs, adaptive interaction, neurofeedback, and neuromodulation as approaches for reducing State Mismatch. By integrating these solution paths, this review outlines a pathway toward adaptive, bidirectional, and human-centered BCI systems.

title: Electrons and phonons running hot and cold in boron arsenide
Metastable synchronization and inertial-beating sensing in nonlinear oscillators
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Synchronization is widely used to enhance the sensitivity and noise resilience of mechanical sensors, while nonlinear operation is often assumed to substantially broaden the usable synchronization bandwidth. Here, we show that this apparent bandwidth enhancement is fundamentally metastable. In nonlinear self-oscillating systems, large portions of the nominal synchronization region are dynamically inaccessible under direct signal injection, despite being theoretically stable. We demonstrate that this breakdown originates from phase inertia, which endows phase evolution with an effective second-order response and creates inertial barriers to phase capture. As a result, nonlinear synchronization splits into a narrow dynamically accessible locking region and a much larger metastable regime in which stable phase locking exists in principle but cannot be reached in practice. Rather than suppressing this inertial unlocking behavior, we exploit it as a sensing mechanism. Near the inaccessible locking boundary, phase inertia sustains slow beating dynamics that continuously encode frequency detuning while intrinsically averaging fast phase fluctuations. The resulting inertial-beating transduction produces a continuous, history-independent sensing response and enables faster synchronization dynamics beyond the conventional locking regime. More broadly, our results reveal that synchronization bandwidth is fundamentally governed by dynamical accessibility rather than static stability, establishing phase inertia as a general organizing principle for nonlinear synchronization dynamics across driven oscillatory systems.

title: A Full-Duplex Metasurface for Simultaneous and Independent Control of Radiation and Reflection
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Metasurfaces have transformed electromagnetic interfaces from fixed, material-defined boundaries into engineered platforms for tailoring wave propagation, spanning both passive designs and actively programmable implementations. For future information systems, a central challenge is to make the same physical aperture operate simultaneously as a radiating antenna and a reconfigurable reflector. Radiation–reflection-integrated (R2I) metasurfaces combine these functions, but their responses remain coupled: configuring the surface for radiation constrains its behavior in reflection. They therefore cannot generally provide independent operation at the same time, frequency, and polarization. Here, we show an intelligent full-duplex R2I metasurface that overcomes this constraint. The surface integrates controllable meta-atoms with a substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW). Because the SIW-guided and free-space excitations occupy largely separated regions of the spatial spectrum, the radiated and reflected fields can be manipulated simultaneously and independently on the same aperture. We experimentally demonstrate this capability in integrated sensing and communication and in integrated detection and stealth, both realized using a single artificial-intelligence-assisted metasurface under identical operating conditions. These results establish a route towards full-duplex, single-aperture information systems.

title: Susumu Tonegawa (1939–2026): A molecular biologist who transformed immunology and neuroscience
abstract: Susumu Tonegawa transformed two fields of biology. His discovery of the genetic mechanism generating antibody diversity established the foundations of modern immunology and earned him the 1987 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. Remarkably, he then began a second scientific career in neuroscience, pioneering genetic approaches to dissect the molecular and circuit mechanisms of learning and memory and, ultimately, the neuronal ensembles that store specific memories. He was also an ambitious institution builder whose leadership shaped neuroscience at Massachusetts Institute of Technology and RIKEN. As former trainees from his immunology and neuroscience labs, we remember a scientist of extraordinary curiosity, intensity, and intellectual courage, who was never afraid to leave familiar territory in pursuit of a fundamental question.

title: Reply to Burger et al.: Powerless paradigms and the myth of equal fitness
Energy and fitness: Power is not all-powerful in evolution

A functional two-pore-domain K
                     + 
                    channel from a large DNA virus
authors: Oliver RauhSebastian MachOliver ClarkeJonas ToewsJames L. Van EttenMike AlthausAnna MoroniGerhard Thielahttps://ror.org/04m2anh63Institute for Functional Gene Analytics, Department of Natural Sciences, Bonn-Rhein-Sieg University of Applied Sciences, Rheinbach 53359, Germanybhttps://ror.org/05n911h24Department of Biology, Membrane Biophysics, Technische Universität Darmstadt, Darmstadt 64287, Germanychttps://ror.org/01esghr10Department of Anesthesiology, Columbia University Irving Medical Center, New York, NY 10032dhttps://ror.org/00hj8s172Department of Biology, Irving Institute for Clinical and Translational Research, Columbia University, New York, NY 10032eDepartment of Plant Pathology and Nebraska Center for Virology, University of Nebraska Lincoln, Lincoln, NE 68583-0900fhttps://ror.org/00wjc7c48Department of Biosciences, University of Milan, Milan 20133, Italy
abstract:
The evolutionary history of proteins helps to understand their structure/function correlates and suggests on how functional complexity evolved from primitive precursors. In the superfamily of K
                     + 
                    channels, functional features of complex eukaryotic inward rectifier (Kir) channels and voltage-dependent (Kv) channels could be understood in terms of an increase in structural complexity of their prokaryotic precursors. K2P channels, which are made from tandem repeats of two pore domains, are not found in prokaryotes and their evolutionary origin is still unknown. In searching for primitive K2P channel precursors, we screened the genomes of nucleocytoplasmic large DNA viruses (NCLDVs) for genes coding for K2P channels. This was motivated by two reasons: NCLDVs are already known for coding primitive Kir type channels, and they play important roles in the evolution of eukaryotes. Here, we report that the NCLDV
                     Pyramimonas orientalis 
                    virus codes for K2P-like K
                     + 
                    channels. With only 178 amino acids and no cytosolic domains, this Kpov protein is much smaller than any eukaryotic K2P channel, but still functional as K
                     + 
                    selective channel in lipid bilayers. Phylogenetic analysis suggests that Kpov is not the product of molecular piracy from the host but may result from fusion of primitive viral K
                     + 
                    channel pore domains.

title: Action features dominate cortical representation during natural vision
authors: Heejung JungHunar JainXiaochun HanMa FeilongJane HanDeepanshi ShokeenCara Van UdenIsabella HansonAndrew C. ConnollyTor D. WagerJames V. HaxbySamuel A. Nastaseahttps://ror.org/049s0rh22Department of Psychological and Brain Sciences, Dartmouth College, Hanover, NH 03755bIndependent Researcher, Sunnyvale, CA 94085chttps://ror.org/03taz7m60Department of Psychology, Center for Computational Language Sciences, University of Southern California, Los Angeles, CA 90089
abstract: Cortical resources are allocated into systems specialized for processing ecologically relevant features of the world. These features are typically studied in isolation using controlled experimental stimuli, making it difficult to assess the relative importance of different kinds of features that tend to overlap during natural vision. In the current study, we evaluated the relative contributions of action, agent, and scene features in predicting cortical activity while participants viewed a 1-h nature documentary. We tested four sets of model features: semantic vectors capturing the observed action, agent, and scene features derived from an annotation of the stimulus, as well as low-level visual motion-energy features. We used banded ridge regression to fit vertex-wise encoding models from the combination of all four sets of features. While each set of features predicted neural activity in the expected areas, the action features predicted more widespread activity. A variance partitioning analysis revealed that the action features captured the most unique variance in neural activity across a much larger extent of cortex than the agent or scene features. Our findings suggest that cortical activity during dynamic, natural vision is dominated by features for understanding the actions of others.

title:
Deconfined criticality between an antiferromagnetic insulator and a nodal
                     d 
                    -wave superconductor: A quantum Monte Carlo study
authors: Chuang ChenSubir SachdevZi Yang Mengahttps://ror.org/02zhqgq86Department of Physics and Hong Kong Institute of Quantum Science and Technology, The University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong, Special Administrative Region, Chinabhttps://ror.org/02zhqgq86Department of Physics and State Key Laboratory of Optical Quantum Materials, The University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong, Special Administrative Region, Chinachttps://ror.org/03vek6s52Department of Physics, Harvard University, Cambridge, MA 02138dhttps://ror.org/00sekdz59Center for Computational Quantum Physics, Flatiron Institute, New York, NY 10010
abstract:
We present a quantum Monte Carlo study of the transition between the insulating Néel state and the nodal
                     d 
                    -wave superconductor on the square lattice at half-filling. We access a regime of frustrated magnetic order without a sign problem using a parton representation of the electron in terms of fermionic spinons and bosonic chargons. Both partons move in a background
                     π 
                    -flux (so the electron experiences no net flux) and are coupled to a quantum fluctuating SU(2) lattice gauge field. In contrast to earlier studies directly on the electronic degrees of freedom, we find evidence for a second-order deconfined quantum phase transition at which both the Néel and
                     d 
                    -wave superconductivity orders vanish continuously. We compute correlators of the spinon-chargon composite with the same quantum numbers as the electron: we find a gapless Dirac dispersion inside the
                     d 
                    -wave superconductor, turning into a gapped dispersion in the antiferromagnet.
