title: Reduction of aflatoxin contamination in maize kernels mediated by host-induced gene silencing
authors: Ali AhmedKeri CavanaughPatricia BaldrichIoannis StergiopoulosRichard Michelmoreahttps://ror.org/05rrcem69Genome Center, University of California, Davis, CA 95616bhttps://ror.org/05rrcem69Department of Plant Pathology, University of California, Davis, CA 95616chttps://ror.org/05rrcem69Department of Plant Sciences, University of California, Davis, CA 95616
abstract:
Aflatoxins produced by some species of
                     Aspergillus 
                    pose a significant threat to global food safety, because they contaminate a variety of crops including maize. In this study, we used host-induced gene silencing (HIGS) to reduce aflatoxin accumulation in maize upon infection with
                     Aspergillus flavus 
                    and
                     Aspergillus parasiticus 
                    . Two RNAi constructs were designed and introduced into maize, one targeting two essential fungal genes involved in ergosterol biosynthesis (
                     CYP51A 
                    and
                     CYP51B 
                    ) and the other targeting three aflatoxin biosynthesis genes (
                     AflC 
                    ,
                     AflD 
                    , and
                     AflR 
                    ). The presence of RNAi transgenes was confirmed in 17 and 14 independent lines possessing the
                     CYP51A/CYP51B 
                    RNAi construct and the
                     AflC/AflD/AflR 
                    RNAi construct, respectively. Most transgenic lines had single-locus integrations and one or two copies of the transgene. Transgene expression varied considerably among the lines. Small RNA sequencing confirmed the production of siRNAs from the HIGS trigger sequences. Levels of
                     CYP51A 
                    ,
                     AflC 
                    ,
                     AflD, 
                    and
                     AflR 
                    transcripts in
                     Aspergillus 
                    spp. were successfully decreased upon infection of transgenic maize. However, significant reduction in the level of
                     CYP51B 
                    transcripts was not achieved and the
                     CYP51A/CYP51B 
                    RNAi transgene had no discernible effect on fungal growth in infected maize. In contrast, we observed significant reductions in aflatoxin accumulation in four
                     AflC/AflD/AflR 
                    RNAi transgenic lines infected with
                     A. flavus 
                    and in two transgenic lines infected with
                     A. parasiticus 
                    . Notably, one
                     AflC/AflD/AflR 
                    transgenic line exhibited minimal aflatoxin contamination upon kernel infection with
                     A. parasiticus 
                    . These results demonstrate the potential of HIGS to reduce aflatoxin production in mature corn kernels.

title: Virus transmission required for maintenance and host adaptation mirrors neurophysiological differences in rabies-derived peptides
authors: Alice RemalEmily S. AchesonPatrick A. LeightonErin E. ReesJohn RhodesBrittany C. V. O’BrienMaegan M. WeltzinKarsten Huefferahttps://ror.org/0161xgx34Département de pathologie et microbiologie, Faculté de médecine vétérinaire, Université de Montréal, Québec J2S 2M2, CanadabGroupe de recherche en épidémiologie des zoonoses et santé publique, University of Montréal, Québec J2S 2M2, Canadachttps://ror.org/023xf2a37Modelling Hub Division, Applied Public Health Sciences Directorate, Science and Policy Integration Branch, Public Health Agency of Canada, Québec J2S 2M2, Canadadhttps://ror.org/01j7nq853Department of Mathematics and Statistics, University of Alaska Fairbanks, Fairbanks, AK 99775ehttps://ror.org/01j7nq853Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry, University of Alaska Fairbanks, Fairbanks, AK 99775fhttps://ror.org/01j7nq853Institute of Arctic Biology, University of Alaska Fairbanks, Fairbanks, AK 99775ghttps://ror.org/01j7nq853Department of Veterinary Medicine, College of Natural Science and Mathematics, University of Alaska Fairbanks, Fairbanks, AK 99775
abstract: Pathogen adaptations to new hosts are central to the disease ecology of cross-species transmission and host switching of viruses. The rabies virus is a model for adaptations to different hosts as it induces behavioral changes that facilitate transmission, while being maintained in distinct species-specific cycles of infection. Here, we demonstrate that the rabies virus requires distinct transmission dynamics in two hosts with different ecologies to establish maintenance, using agent-based modeling, analyses of virus glycoprotein-mediated manipulation of neuroreceptor function, and phylogenetic analysis. Epidemiological models suggest that rabies virus variants adapted to arctic foxes, which sustain rabies virus at very low host densities, require a higher probability of transmission than viruses adapted to raccoons. Using in vitro electrophysiology, we demonstrate that the rabies glycoprotein-derived peptides from arctic fox rabies variants are more potent antagonists of alpha7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors. These findings suggest a possible functional basis for the behavioral modifications that drive enzootic rabies transmission in the context of host ecology. In addition, a large proportion of residues that may drive rabies virus adaptation to raccoons and arctic foxes are found within this neurotoxin-like region. Furthermore, a residue in the neurotoxin-like region of the mature rabies virus glycoprotein (residue 183) has been associated with pathogenicity, host switching, and disease ecology in previous studies. We propose the hypothesis that rabies virus transmission dynamics adapt to the ecology and physiology of novel hosts through the selection of glycoproteins that elicit specific degrees of behavioral modification and transmission probability.

title: Superlubricity by glycerosome boundary layers
authors: Yihui DongWei CaoRoman KamyshinskyNir KampfPanpan ZhaoYaelle SchiltUri RavivJacob Kleinahttps://ror.org/0316ej306Department of Molecular Chemistry and Materials Science, Weizmann Institute of Science, Rehovot 76100, Israelbhttps://ror.org/03sd35x91School of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering, Nanjing Tech University, Nanjing 211816, Chinachttps://ror.org/03sd35x91State Key Laboratory of Materials-Oriented Chemical Engineering, College of Chemical Engineering, Nanjing Tech University, Nanjing 211816, Chinadhttps://ror.org/0316ej306Department of Chemical Research Support, Weizmann Institute of Science, Rehovot 76100, Israelehttps://ror.org/03qxff017Institute of Chemistry, The Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Jerusalem 9190401, Israel
abstract:
The search for high-performance lubricants is of broad relevance to biomedical applications, including artificial joints, regenerative scaffolds, and osteoarthritis therapies. Here we introduce glycerosomes—phosphatidylcholine (PC)-based vesicles containing glycerol—as a promising boundary lubricant. Using a surface force balance, we show that glycerosomes achieve a friction coefficient as low as 10
                     − 
                     5 
                    under a high compression pressure of 15.6 MPa, representing a 20-fold reduction compared to conventional PC liposomes. This level of lubrication surpasses any previously reported boundary lubricant system at such pressures in aqueous media. Mechanistically, glycerosomes exhibit substantially lower adhesion energy than PC liposomes, and theoretical simulations reveal enhanced vesicle stability and flexibility. Our findings establish glycerosomes as a superior hydration lubrication platform, with promising implications for both biomedical implants and industrial applications requiring robust lubricity.

title:

authors: Xinyun ChenMengyan LiZhichao LiuLongjiang DiQingren MengTingting FengJun ZhangQian ZhuXiaopeng LuYuxin ShuJinbo HuangMonika GullerovaYuan TianWei-Guo Zhuahttps://ror.org/01vy4gh70International Cancer Center, Guangdong Key Laboratory of Genome Instability and Human Disease Prevention, Marshall Laboratory of Biomedical Engineering, Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, Shenzhen University Medical School, Shenzhen 518055, Chinabhttps://ror.org/03hz5th67Faculty of Pharmaceutical Sciences, Shenzhen University of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Shenzhen 518055, Chinachttps://ror.org/052gg0110Sir William Dunn School of Pathology, University of Oxford, Oxford OX1 3RE, United Kingdomdhttps://ror.org/037ejjy86Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, School of Basic Medical Sciences, Wannan Medical College, Wuhu 241002, Anhui, China
abstract: DNA double strand breaks (DSBs) are repaired through distinct pathways, with homologous recombination (HR) favored when DNA ends undergo extensive resection. Although cytoplasmic N7-methylguanosine (m7G)-modified RNA increases after UV-induced single-strand breaks, its role in DSB repair (including HR) remains unclear. Here, we show that m7G-modified RNA accumulates at DSB sites, where it recruits the m7G reader protein Quaking (QKI)5, to selectively promote HR. Mechanistically, QKI5 directly interacts with MRE11 and enhances its DNA binding affinity, thereby facilitating DNA end resection. Depletion of QKI5 impairs recruitment of the MRE11–RAD50–NBS1 complex to DSBs and reduces HR repair efficiency. Moreover, elevated QKI5 expression is associated with resistance to radiotherapy in both mouse models and clinical cohorts. Together, these findings identify the m7G RNA–QKI5–MRE11 axis as a regulator of HR pathway choice and suggest QKI5 as a promising therapeutic target in cancer treatment.

title: Mechanistic insight into conflicting valence fluctuation of Cu(I) photocorrosion pathways: The role of charge behaviors
authors: Yi-Cheng WangChenyu XuPeng-Fei SuiRenfei FengYi LiuHanxiao ZhangHongbo ZengXiaolei WangJing-Li Luoahttps://ror.org/0160cpw27Department of Chemical and Materials Engineering, University of Alberta, Edmonton, AB T6G 1H9, Canadabhttps://ror.org/00a2xv884State Key Laboratory of Clean Energy Utilization, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou 310027, Zhejiang, People’s Republic of ChinacCanadian Light Source Inc., Saskatoon, SK S7N 0X4, Canadadhttps://ror.org/01vy4gh70College of Materials Science and Engineering, Shenzhen University, Shenzhen 518060, Guangdong, People’s Republic of China
abstract:
Photocorrosion remains a major challenge that hinders the development of photoelectrochemical (PEC) solar fuel production. Although Cu
                     2 
                    O is a promising photocathode material due to its suitable band structure and visible light absorption, both oxidative and reductive photocorrosion pathways have been reported, with no consensus established in the research community in the PEC system. In this work, we fabricate three Cu
                     2 
                    O photocathodes with distinct charge transport properties to investigate the correlation between charge accumulation and photocorrosion behavior. Both oxidative and reductive photocorrosion were observed depending on the type and location of charge accumulation. Notably, we propose a refined oxidative photocorrosion mechanism in which photogenerated holes induce surface Cu
                     2 
                    O dissolution to Cu
                     2+ 
                    , followed by coordination with adsorbed *OH to form Cu(OH)
                     2 
                    /CuO under illumination, which is contrary to the widely assumed direct oxidation from Cu
                     2 
                    O to CuO. This work not only provides a unified understanding of the dual photocorrosion pathways in Cu
                     2 
                    O, but also offers a generalizable framework for understanding photo-induced degradation in metal oxide photocathodes and for guiding the design of more robust PEC systems through charge transport engineering.

abstract: Huntingtin-associated protein 40 (HAP40) forms a stable protein complex with huntingtin (HTT). Its cellular function and how HAP40 loss influences mutant HTT (mHTT) abundance and pathobiology are currently unclear. Here, using diverse cellular models and omics methods, we demonstrate that HAP40 is an obligate interaction partner of HTT and through its binding controls HTT interactions and the abundance of HTT-associated proteins, indicating that it functions as a HTT interaction regulatory unit. Also, loss of HAP40 in mHTT-expressing striatal cells impairs autophagic protein degradation and triggers transcriptional activation of the CLEAR network, demonstrating that it functions as a proteostasis regulator that acts on quality control pathways. Finally, mHTT-expressing cells lacking HAP40 showed increased secretion of a ~205 kDa mHTT fragment through an endoplasmic reticulum (ER)/Golgi-associated route, indicating that striatal cells reduce intracellular mHTT-induced proteotoxicity through activation of secretory pathways. Together, these results establish HAP40 as a critical proteostasis regulator that through controlling HTT interactions maintains cellular homeostasis.

title: Molecular drivers of cotranslational protein assembly in bacteria
authors: Jaro L. SchmittJosef J. AuburgerFlorian WruckJiří KoubekSander J. TansBernd BukauGünter KrameraCenter for Molecular Biology of Heidelberg University, German Cancer Research Center - Center for Molecular Biology of Heidelberg University Alliance, Heidelberg 69120, GermanybAutonomous Matter Department, AMOLF institute, Amsterdam 1098 XG, The Netherlandschttps://ror.org/02e2c7k09Bionanoscience Department of Delft University of Technology and Kavli Institute of Nanoscience Delft, Delft 2629 HZ, The Netherlands
abstract:
Protein complexes are pivotal to all major cellular processes. Translation-coupled complex assembly is ubiquitous in eukaryotes, but its molecular basis and prevalence in bacteria remain poorly understood. Here, we combine ribosome profiling and single-molecule optical tweezers to establish principles governing cotranslational assembly of four structurally diverse complexes in
                     Escherichia coli 
                    . We reveal how heterotetramers form cotranslationally via hierarchical assembly pathways, with initial heterodimer formation priming the assembly of higher-order oligomers through a topology-dependent organization of homomeric and heteromeric interfaces. Co-post assembly, defined as interaction between nascent and fully synthesized subunits, initiates when dimerization domains are completely exposed at the ribosome. The assembly order is predominantly unidirectional and matches the operon gene order, with upstream-encoded subunits being synthesized first, and then engaging downstream nascent partner subunits. The co-post assembly efficiency depends both on the native operon structure and the ribosome-associated chaperone trigger factor, which binds emerging oligomerization domains and whose dissociation marks the onset of partner subunit engagement. The handover from chaperone engagement to cotranslational assembly is mediated by nascent chain folding. Finally, we show that co-post assembly provides a fitness advantage. Together, these findings reveal how genome organization and chaperone-assisted folding coordinate cotranslational assembly to promote efficient complex biogenesis and cellular fitness in bacteria.

authors: Yingying TanAshley G. LewisIris C. abstract: A few studies have shown that brain catecholamines are implicated in language comprehension. However, the specific cognitive processes they modulate remain underexplored. We hypothesized that catecholamines enhance the unification of syntactic roles and word meanings into coherent multiword structures. This study combined electroencephalography and psychopharmacology to examine the effects of a catecholaminergic stimulant (methylphenidate) on processing sentences containing local syntactic ambiguities. Methylphenidate amplified the P600 event-related potential effect, which has been linked to the recruitment of cognitive resources for processing sentences with increased syntactic load. The drug’s impact on semantic processing was subtler, showing a suggestive attenuation of the N400 effect to ambiguous sentences. Furthermore, the increase in the P600 effect under methylphenidate was most pronounced in participants with lower working memory capacity. This study provides evidence for linking catecholamine activity to syntactic unification in healthy individuals. Elevated catecholamine levels appear to increase the cognitive effort invested in syntactic unification, and to support the dynamic prioritization of syntactic information when contextual demands require it.

title: The survival paradox of close-in planets orbiting red-clump giants
authors: Wen-Xu LinSheng-Bang QianQi-Bin SunLi-Ying ZhuWen-Ping LiaoTing LiFu-Xing LiXiang-Dong ShiTao WangEr-Gang ZhaoHui-Ting ZhangPing LiaDepartment of Astronomy, School of Physics and Astronomy, Yunnan University, Kunming 650091, People’s Republic of Chinabhttps://ror.org/034t30j35Yunnan Observatories, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Kunming 650011, People’s Republic of Chinachttps://ror.org/05qbk4x57University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing 101408, People’s Republic of ChinadYunnan Training Center for Ethnic Leadership, Yunnan Minzu University, Kunming 650504, People’s Republic of China
abstract: Close-in planets orbiting core-helium-burning red-clump giants directly challenge tidal-engulfment theory, which predicts that planets within about 1 au of Sun-like stars should be engulfed during red-giant-branch (RGB) expansion. The existence of such survivors would imply missing physical processes in the late stages of stellar and planetary evolution. Yet only one such “forbidden” planet had been identified to date. Here we report three systems—24 Boo b, HD 12648 b, and TYC 4282-605-1 b—whose host stars are confirmed red-clump giants through asteroseismology, showing that each has already undergone dramatic expansion and contraction following helium ignition. Their planets now reside at orbital separations smaller than the maximum stellar radii attained during the RGB phase, implying that they should not have survived. Among them, 24 Boo b orbits at only 0.183 au with a 30-d period, making it the closest planet known around a red-clump giant. These findings demonstrate that this paradox is not an isolated anomaly but signals the emergence of a class of evolved planetary systems. Their survival defies current models of stellar–planetary coevolution and points to unexplored physics shaping planetary architectures around post-RGB stars.

title: c-FLIP loss links arrest of gene expression to TNFα-dependent antiviral guard immunity
authors: Matthew SonnettSanne BoersmaMadeline E. WardLaura C. Van EyndhovenEdoardo CentofantiMax BrambachChanghong ZhouDavid M. KnipeArjun RajAlon Oyler-YanivJennifer Oyler-YanivaThe Department of Systems Biology, Harvard Medical School, Boston, MA 02115bhttps://ror.org/00b30xv10The Department of Bioengineering, School of Engineering and Applied Sciences, University of Pennsylvania, Philadelphia, PA 19104cDepartment of Microbiology, Blavatnik Institute, Harvard Medical School, Boston, MA 02115dhttps://ror.org/00b30xv10The Department of Genetics, Perelman School of Medicine, University of Pennsylvania, Philadelphia, PA 19104
abstract: Cells sense infection through dedicated receptors, yet these surveillance pathways are often subverted by pathogen-encoded virulence factors. Guard immunity provides complementary defense by rapidly killing infected cells in response to infection induced stress. However, the symptoms of infection frequently resemble noninfectious stress, raising the question of how they are distinguished. Using quantitative transcriptomics, proteomics, and global translation measurements during viral infections in vitro and in vivo, we show that infection globally suppresses host gene expression and prevents direct antiviral responses. However, the resulting proteostatic stress does not activate guard immunity unless tumor necrosis factor-α (TNFα) is present. We identify the anti-apoptotic protein c-FLIP as a guard for gene expression integrity: its loss sensitizes cells to TNFα, triggering cell death and limiting viral spread. Modeling demonstrates that TNFα and c-FLIP loss function as a biological AND-gate, providing specificity and speed. These findings show how cells integrate internal stress signals with external inflammatory cues to improve the fidelity of death decisions, and how this circuitry may misfire during noninfectious inflammation.

title: CauTrigger: deciphering biological system state transitions by hierarchical causal decomposition
Tracing causal cascades underlying biological state changes
OpenDVP: an experimental and computational framework for community-empowered deep visual proteomics
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Deep visual proteomics (DVP) is an emerging approach for cell-type-specific and spatially resolved proteomics. However, its broad adoption has been constrained by the lack of an open-source end-to-end workflow within a community-driven ecosystem. Here we introduce openDVP, an experimental and computational framework for accessible and scalable DVP. OpenDVP combines open-source image analysis tools (MCMICRO, QuPath and napari) with scverse formats (AnnData and SpatialData) for multiomics integration. It provides two workflows: a fast-track pipeline requiring no image analysis expertise, and an artificial intelligence-powered pipeline incorporating state-of-the-art methods for image preprocessing, segmentation and spatial analysis. We apply openDVP across three archival tissue studies (human placenta, early stage lung cancer and locally relapsed breast cancer), integrating spatial single-cell phenotypes with exploratory proteomic measurements. Finally, we introduce deep proteomic profiling of cellular neighborhoods as a scalable approach for spatial discovery proteomics.

title: Genome-wide detection of genotype–environment interactions at biobank scale with fastGxE
Near-complete assembly of wild emmer wheat unveils centromere reorganization during polyploid evolution
High false sign rates in transcriptome-wide association studies
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS) are widely used to identify genes involved in complex traits and to infer the direction of gene effects on traits. However, despite their popularity, it remains unclear how accurately TWAS recover the true direction of a gene’s effect on a trait. Here we estimate the false sign rate of TWAS for plasma proteins, leveraging the expectation that increased gene expression should generally increase protein expression. We then extend this framework to complex traits, where loss-of-function burden tests provide the expected direction of effect. In both analyses, we observe high discordance with expectations, with TWAS showing a false sign rate of 23% for plasma proteins and 33% for complex traits. We propose that much of the sign discordance arises when expression quantitative trait loci in non-trait-relevant tissues tag haplotypes associated with traits in genome-wide association studies via distinct, tightly linked regulatory variants, yielding spurious TWAS associations with the correct genes but with unreliable direction of effect. These findings show that TWAS-based direction-of-effect estimates should be interpreted with caution and raise concerns about the reliability of TWAS more broadly.

title: Co-regulation confounds direction of genetic effects in transcriptome-wide association studies
abstract: Nature Genetics, Published online: 22 October 2026;  doi:10.1038/s41588-026-02793-7  Co-regulation of gene expression profiles across cell types arising from linkage disequilibrium makes it challenging to distinguish causal variants from nearby tagging variants. A study now quantifies the effect of this confounding factor on the direction of the gene–disease association in transcriptome-wide association studies.

title: Human Argonaute 2 is a programmable targeting domain for RNA editing
abstract: Nature Biotechnology, Published online: 22 October 2026;  doi:10.1038/s41587-026-03358-z  ALTER is a programmable RNA base editor built entirely from human proteins. By using human AGO2 instead of bacterial CRISPR–Cas proteins, ALTER mitigates a key risk factor for harmful immune responses in therapeutic applications while also proving generally more effective than dCas13-based editors.

title: Recordanelles capture transient gene expression in single human cells
abstract: Nature Biotechnology, Published online: 22 October 2026;  doi:10.1038/s41587-026-03350-7  RNA sequencing can capture high-resolution snapshots of a cell’s transcriptome, but transient changes in individual cells cannot be captured over long periods at a transcriptome-wide scale. Now, a synthetic organelle termed the ‘recordanelle’ can record cellular RNAs in cells for several days and be read with single-cell sensitivity.

title: Author Correction: Light-induced LLPS of the CRY2/SPA1/FIO1 complex regulating mRNA methylation and chlorophyll homeostasis in Arabidopsis
Synthetic activation of gibberellin signalling reveals spatial coordination of root growth
Reconstructing spore evolution recalibrates the timescale of land plant diversification
abstract:
Abstract 
                   The origin and evolution of land plants precipitated fundamental changes to the Earth system and enabled the diversification of life on land. Their early evolution is documented by a rich fossil record of sporopollenin-walled spores that is difficult to interpret because the evolution of plant spore characteristics is unresolved. We employ a suite of ancestral state estimation methods to elucidate the pattern of spore character evolution among land plants. We find that the ancestral embryophyte underwent monoplastidic meiosis and produced unenveloped spores with a three-layered sporoderm. We infer that trilete spores (that developed in tetrahedral tetrads), traditionally considered a feature of vascular plants, were produced by the crown-embryophyte. We recalibrate the molecular timescale of early land plant evolution on the basis of a reinterpretation of the fossil record in this light. We find that crown-embryophytes originated in the Late Ordovician (457–450 Ma) and that both crown-tracheophytes (432–428 Ma) and crown-bryophytes (445–429 Ma) diverged in the early Silurian.

title: Daily briefing: The tell-tale features of a Denisovan
Can a 'lullaby' save coral reefs from extinction?
Can maths survive AI? Fields medallist Terence Tao calls for a ‘Maths 2.0’ world
A first for CRISPR: powerful prime editing alters DNA directly in the human body
A planthopper-secreted miRNA facilitates viral infection by disrupting plant growth–defense balance in rice
abstract: Short summary: White-backed planthoppers deliver miR-133 into rice, where it cleaves OsGLK31 mRNA and weakens auxin-dependent growth and jasmonate-mediated antiviral defense. OsJAZ10 further restricts OsGLK31-dependent activation of the jasmonate-biosynthetic gene OsLOX11. Together, these effects promote southern rice black-streaked dwarf virus (SRBSDV) infection, linking an insect-derived miRNA to viral disease.

title: Engineering BBM cis-regulatory elements releases epigenetic repression to enable highly efficient parthenogenesis and haploid induction
abstract: Short summary: H3K27me3 methylation on BBM results in silencing of the BBM. Mutation of four putative polycomb response elements in BBM coding region decreased H3K27me3 methylation on BBM and increased its expression, leading to 88.7% egg cell division without fertilization, and produced 9.0% haploid and 60.4% doubled haploid plants after fertilization. This study elucidates a fine mechanism that inhibits parthenogenesis.

title: Females shape hunting of vertebrates in wild bonobos
abstract: Hohmann et al. find that arboreal primates and terrestrial ungulates contribute almost equally to prey captured by bonobos. While both sexes caught primates at similar rates, females dominated ungulate capture, which supports the hypothesis that hunting activity varies with dominance and challenging models suggesting that male-biased hunting represents the ancestral state.

title: A language-model approach to species distribution reveals alternative stable states
abstract: Coulon et al. introduce a language-model approach that improves predictions of reef fish communities through sequential generation. Independent model realizations under identical environmental conditions yield statistically coherent alternative configurations. Directional influence networks quantify how species asymmetrically affect others’ occurrence and biomass, supporting investigation of multistability and community assembly.

title: Plant synergid embryonic potential is unlocked following egg cell collapse
abstract: Xiong et al. show that synergid cells, long recognized as fertilization partners closely coordinated with the egg cell, can acquire embryogenic competence upon egg cell collapse, most likely without adopting egg cell identity. This ECcollapsed system enables maternal haploid production in Arabidopsis and haploid generation in tomato.

title: Dorsal forerunner cells couple epiboly movements to zebrafish notochord extension
abstract: Here, Small and Williams show that dorsal forerunner cells couple epiboly movements to the posterior end of the notochord, promoting its extension during zebrafish gastrulation.

title: Top-down inferior colliculus signals engage unipolar brush cell circuits in the dorsal cochlear nucleus of the mouse auditory system
abstract: Candler et al. identify inferior colliculus neurons that project to the dorsal cochlear nucleus and target unipolar brush cells (UBCs), which amplify these descending signals directly to fusiform and cartwheel cells. In vivo, UBCs suppress auditory responses, revealing a circuit that could guide adaptive filtering.

title: Selective control of course correction over long timescales in the Drosophila central complex
abstract: Crown et al. describe a behavioral correlate between optomotor steering maneuvers and the navigational circuitry of the fly brain. Several populations of columnar neurons contribute different aspects of these maneuvers, and their influence is most evident when the fly moves over timescales of several seconds.

title: Microbial inositol phosphates orchestrate host diurnal metabolism and energy homeostasis via HDAC3
abstract: Zhang et al. show that gut microbial inositol phosphate metabolism transduces feeding cues into intestinal diurnal rhythms through histone deacetylase 3. This pathway activates PGC-1α and enhances nutrient absorption during feeding, promoting juvenile growth during undernutrition but exacerbating obesity during overnutrition.

title: Metazoan lagging-strand DNA synthesis is distributive
abstract: Single-molecule imaging reveals that metazoan lagging-strand DNA synthesis is distributive, and it relies on the repeated recruitment of Pol α and Pol δ rather than their stable replisome association, thereby uncoupling leading- and lagging-strand synthesis.

title: MCT6 is an intestinal Lac-Phe exporter required for metformin-associated weight loss
abstract: The orphan transporter MCT6 is the route by which the meal- and exercise-associated metabolite Lac-Phe exits intestinal cells and enters the blood. Mice lacking gut MCT6 cannot maintain normal circulating Lac-Phe levels and exhibit resistance to metformin-associated weight loss, establishing metabolite export as a regulatory node for systemic action.

title: Lifestyle-induced regulatory T cell fragility primes adverse events after immune checkpoint blockade
abstract: Dietary and microbial alterations increase susceptibility to irAEs by promoting IFN-γ-driven Treg fragility and cytotoxic tissue-resident T cell responses. Treg-specific disruption of IFN-γ signaling restores tissue homeostasis and reduces irAEs without compromising antitumor immunity, highlighting Treg stability as a potential therapeutic strategy for limiting checkpoint blockade toxicity.

title:
Biomimetic Nanoplatform for Fibrosis Remodeling and Anti‐PD‐1 Potentiation via Cu
                     + 
                    /Ca
                     2+ 
                    Ion Dysregulation and TGF‐β Inhibition in PDAC
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains refractory to immunotherapy, largely due to the dense fibrotic stroma that promotes immune evasion and restricts drug penetration. Here, we report a multifunctional biomimetic nanoplatform (RPm@CC‐LY) that simultaneously remodels the fibrotic tumor microenvironment and potentiates antitumor immunity. RPm@CC‐LY achieves efficient tumor accumulation and effectively attenuates fibrosis through sustained release of Transforming growth factor‐β (TGF‐β) inhibitor LY2157299 (LY). Concurrently, intracellular acid‐triggered degradation induces Cu
                     + 
                    ‐mediated Fenton‐like reactions and Ca
                     2+ 
                    overload, leading to oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and tumor cell apoptosis. In parallel, RPm@CC‐LY reprograms tumor‐associated macrophages (TAMs) toward an M1 phenotype and enhances dendritic cell maturation, thereby promoting robust CD8
                     + 
                    T cell infiltration. Notably, when combined with anti–PD‐1 (αPD1) therapy, RPm@CC‐LY induces a systemic immune response in mice. This work establishes a synergistic nanotherapeutic strategy that integrates fibrosis remodeling with ion interference therapy to overcome the immunotherapeutic barriers posed by fibrosis in PDAC.

title: Enriched Soil Organic Carbon Underpins Long‐Term Stable Crop Productivity Across China's Croplands
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Maintaining stable agricultural production amid intensifying climate extremes is critical for global food security. While soil organic carbon (SOC) is a widely recognized pillar of agricultural sustainability, the extent to which SOC accrual can enhance crop stability remains poorly quantified. Here, comprehensive large‐scale datasets across China's maize and wheat croplands were leveraged to quantify nonlinear relationships using diverse nonparametric models. Critical SOC baselines (10.5–13.1 g kg
                     −1 
                    for maize; 8.4–9.9 g kg
                     −1 
                    for wheat) were identified as necessary for soils to effectively buffer crops against climatic fluctuations. Causal analysis revealed that approximately 20% of China's croplands were below these thresholds but exhibited significant marginal stabilizing effects from SOC enhancement. Specifically, in these high‐gains regions, a 1 g kg
                     −1 
                    increase in SOC improved crop stability by 6.2% to 11.1%, far exceeding the national average gains of 1.1% to 2.0%. Spatially, these pronounced gains were concentrated in municipalities characterized by high yields and extensive planting areas, highlighting that targeted SOC accrual in China's main breadbaskets was essential to secure food supply stability. By segmenting functional SOC ranges and spatially mapping marginal causal benefits, this study provides policymakers with quantitative evidence for targeted soil carbon management to enhance agricultural resilience.

title: Spatiotemporally Precise Rheumatoid Arthritis Therapy via a Triple‐Locked Cascaded Nanoplatform With Dual‐Channel Self‐Reporting
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Achieving precise spatiotemporal control over combination therapies in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) remains heavily compromised by conventional nanoplatforms, which typically suffer from premature off‐target leakage, coupled drug release, and inadequate in vivo tracking capabilities. Herein, a programmable orthogonally branched triple‐locked nanotheranostic platform (MB@YW NPs) is engineered to seamlessly synchronize spatial localization, chemically orthogonal multidrug liberation, and real‐time multichannel self‐reporting. The system comprises a pH‐responsive polymeric matrix co‐encapsulating a HOCl‐activatable methotrexate prodrug (MB‐MTX) and an ONOO
                     − 
                    /light‐responsive sulfasalazine prodrug (YW‐SSZ). Precluding systemic leakage, synovial acidity dictates initial spatial targeting by triggering tissue‐specific disassembly and subsequent macrophage internalization. Subsequently, non‐interfering pathophysiological triggers exclusively liberate distinct therapeutics through independent pathways: intracellular HOCl purely unlocks methotrexate with concomitant near‐infrared “turn‐on” fluorescence, whereas an isolated ONOO
                     − 
                    /light sequence locally activates sulfasalazine accompanied by a blue “on‐to‐off” readout. This lack of cross‐talk successfully discriminates multiplexed activation states. In vivo, this triple‐locked platform efficiently alleviates oxidative stress and remodels the inflammatory microenvironment, leading to markedly suppressed joint destruction in collagen‐induced arthritis models. Furthermore, transcriptomic analysis reveals these synergistic macroscopic benefits are driven by targeted modulation of the cAMP/NF‐κB signaling axis. Collectively, this work establishes a transformative and generalizable framework for independently coordinated, next‐generation precision multi‐prodrug nanomedicine.

title: Photo‐Induced Stepwise Liquid Crystal Phase Transition Enabled by Hydrazone Photoswitch
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Advanced liquid crystal (LC) materials with photo‐induced phase transition behaviors hold significant scientific and technological importance because of its potentials in next‐generation optoelectronic devices and information encryption. Azobenzene‐based LC has been widely studied in this field for several decades. However, the relatively poor thermal stability of the
                     cis 
                    isomer of azobenzene severely limits its applications in state‐locking and high‐temperature scenarios. Herein, a photoisomerizable and bistable hydrazone molecule was judiciously designed and synthesized. The hydrazone photoswitch undergoes linear‐to‐bent configurational changes via light‐driven isomerization, achieving isothermal and reversible control of LCs from ordered to disordered states. The perturbation effects of hydrazone isomerization on LC phase were analyzed by measuring the dichroism ratio (
                     
                       R 
                     
                    ) and order parameter (
                     
                       
                        S
                         Φ 
                       
                     
                    ). Thanks to the bistability of hydrazone molecules, the phase transition temperatures of the LCs can be precisely and stepwise controlled by regulating light intensity and exposure time. Utilizing the unique light‐induced phase transition of hydrazone‐doped cholesteric liquid crystals (CLCs), thermoresponsive colorful optical devices with reversibly writable and erasable patterns by light were demonstrated, highlighting their significant potential for applications in smart optical materials.

title: An AI‐Driven Framework for Directed Self‐Assembly Toward Design‐Technology Co‐Optimization
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Directed self‐assembly (DSA) provides a promising route for sub‐10‐nm patterning, but its integration into design‐technology co‐optimization (DTCO) remains limited by the difficulty of translating self‐assembly process constraints into manufacturable layout solutions. Here, an artificial‐intelligence‐driven closed‐loop simulation framework for DSA is presented to convert experimentally constrained DSA process knowledge into a process‐constrained design‐space map for DSA‐aware layout decomposition. The framework integrates a three‐dimensional Ohta‐Kawasaki model with Bayesian optimization and convolutional neural network screening, enabling automated model calibration using experimental racetrack‐template data without manual tuning. It efficiently identifies optimal model parameters, achieving a mean simulation‐experiment error below 1.5 nm while maintaining morphological consistency. In addition, four multimodal large language models are further evaluated for DSA morphology screening and are shown to adapt to new image modalities and defect criteria without additional task‐specific fine‐tuning, relying solely on text‐based rules and few‐shot examples. The calibrated model enables target‐constrained inverse design of experimentally validated template windows, translating DSA constraints into a manufacturable solution‐space map for layout decomposition. Its extension to peanut‐shaped templates without additional parameter calibration further supports DSA‐aware layout decomposition and DTCO. Overall, this work establishes an intelligent closed‐loop workflow linking experiment, simulation, and design, providing a practical route toward DTCO.

title: Photochemical Regiodivergent Functionalization of Quinolines with Aryl Ketones
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    We report a catalytic system‐controlled strategy for the selective C2‐ and C4‐ functionalization of quinolines with aryl ketones through a kinetically regulated downstream hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) process. Regiodivergent functionalization is modulated by aryl thiol HAT photocatalysts and formate salt reductants. Fine‐tuning the structure of the aryl thiol and the loading of formate enables the regioselectivity:
                     o 
                    ‐(isopropoxycarbonyl) thiophenol in the presence of excess formate promotes C4‐dearomatization to furnish bridged 1,3‐oxazepanes, whereas
                     m 
                    ‐(methoxycarbonyl) thiophenol with reduced formate loadings favors a C2‐Minisci‐type pathway, delivering quinolin‐2‐yl tertiary alcohols. Mechanistic and DFT studies reveal that although C2‐coupling is intrinsically slightly favored over C4‐coupling, the hydrogen‐atom abstraction capability of the thiyl radical plays a crucial role in controlling the fate of a key intermediate, thereby dictating regioselectivity. This work expands the synthetic toolbox for the construction of diverse quinoline architectures and establishes a new strategy for controlling regioselectivity in reversible radical‐mediated photocatalytic transformations.

title: Engineering a Bioelectronic Hybrid Heart with Integrated Sensing and Electrical Modulation
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of mortality worldwide, motivating the development of advanced therapeutic strategies, including engineered cardiac substitutes. Here, we report a bioelectronic hybrid heart that integrates engineered cardiac tissue with embedded electrophysiological sensing and stimulation capabilities. A decellularized cardiac scaffold was cellularized by injection of induced pluripotent stem cell‐derived cardiomyocytes and assembled with a cell‐laden, three‐dimensional‐printed extracellular matrix coating containing a custom‐designed electronic mesh. After 14 days of culture, the embedded electrodes recorded spontaneous cardiac activity, while localized electrical stimulation affected the tissue, enabling pacing at controlled frequencies. Calcium imaging demonstrated spatial activation across the engineered tissue during pacing. This platform establishes a foundation for integrating real‐time monitoring and electronic functional regulation into engineered cardiac constructs and represents an initial step toward bioelectronic organ engineering.

title: Dramatic Enhancement and Integration of Properties in Pork Belly‐Inspired All‐Biomass Composite Films via Facile, Sustainable, and Controllable Design
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Although all‐biomass composite films that integrate electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding, thermal management, and mechanical properties are promising alternatives to conventional flexible electronic materials owing to the renewability, degradability, and sustainability, the substantial performance shortcomings severely limit the practical availability of these materials. In this study, an effective layer‐by‐layer assembly strategy inspired by the hierarchical structure of pork belly was proposed to fabricate alternating multilayer (AM) biomimetic composite films composed of cellulose nanofibers (CNFs), graphitized carbon nanosheets (GCNs), and gelatin. Efficient stress transfer, phonon transport, and electromagnetic attenuation were achieved through the construction of a robust hierarchical multilayer architecture enabled by the synergistic interactions among GCNs, CNFs, and gelatin. The results showed that the AM‐7 composite film exhibited a tensile strength of 121.20 MPa, which was increased by 266% and 199% compared with CF and CG composite films, respectively. An enhanced in‐plane thermal conductivity of 6.34 W·m
                     − 
                     1 
                    ·K
                     − 
                     1 
                    was achieved, and the EMI shielding effectiveness attained 56.35 dB. This work provides a sustainable strategy for the high‐value utilization of agricultural waste while offering new insights into the rational design of high‐performance multifunctional biomass‐based composites.

title: Snapshot Spatiotemporal‐Spectral Imaging Enabled by Joint Photonic Encoding
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) enables simultaneous acquisition of spectral and spatial information and has been widely adopted across science and engineering. However, existing HSI systems are primarily designed for x‐y‐λ datacube acquisition, with the temporal dimension insufficiently incorporated and limiting their ability to capture rapid variations in spatial structures or spectral signatures. Here we report Spectra4D (x, y, λ, t), a snapshot spatiotemporal‐spectral imaging architecture that enables high‐dimensional and high‐resolution observation of dynamic scenes beyond the native camera frame‐rate limit. Enabled by joint photonic encoding approach, Spectra4D synergizes high‐speed temporal modulation with on‐sensor spectral multiplexing to jointly encode spatiotemporal and spectral information into a single compressed exposure, which is computationally reconstructed using a dual‐mask guided reconstruction network. Experiments demonstrate that Spectra4D reconstructs 28 visible spectral channels under 4× temporal compression, achieving spectral fidelity above 96.5% and pixel‐level localization accuracy across continuous multi‐frame sequences. We further validate the capability of Spectra4D in dynamic spatio‐spectral scenarios, including dual‐color fluorescent microsphere tracking and frame‐resolved elemental monitoring in flame combustion. In summary, Spectra4D presents a practical and scalable route toward temporally resolved spatio‐spectral imaging of dynamic processes with rapidly varying spectral features.

title: Probe‐Free, Primer‐Programmed Amplicon Encoding Enables Nanopore‐Based Multiplex Detection With Deep Learning Decoding
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Single‐reaction multiplex nucleic acid testing (NATs) must both co‐amplify multiple targets and distinguish the resulting amplicons within the product mixture. Most conventional assays achieve this distinction using target‐specific reporters or other external encoding elements. Here, we introduce a primer‐programmed multiplexing strategy in which primer design generates target‐associated amplicons with predefined lengths that are read electrically with nanopores. In a proof‐of‐concept implementation, one‐pot recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) generated four amplicons with predefined product lengths from Monkeypox (Mpox), Cowpox, Vaccinia, and human RNase P. The resulting amplicons were analyzed with glass nanopores, and individual translocation events were classified by a deep neural network (DNN) based on a six‐dimensional feature set derived from nanopore recordings. Event‐level decoding achieved >95% accuracy, >94.7% sensitivity, and >98.3% specificity, and aggregation of classified events yielded sample‐level calls with >93.3% sensitivity and >93.9% specificity in blinded samples, with qualitative calls matching polymerase chain reaction (PCR) results across the 9 PCR‐benchmarked samples. These results demonstrate a probe‐free multiplexing architecture in which target identity is programmed through primer‐defined amplicon design and decoded from the resulting multidimensional nanopore response using a DNN, eliminating the need for target‐specific reporter chemistry and opening new opportunities for all‐electrical multiplex nucleic acid testing based on unmodified amplification products.

title: Long‐Term Expandable Periosteal Organoids Reconstruct a Functional Regenerative Niche That Support Hematopoietic Stem Cell Maintenance and Bone Repair
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   The periosteum plays a central role in skeletal regeneration by serving as a reservoir of skeletal stem cells and a dynamic regenerative niche. However, in vitro models that faithfully preserve its cellular complexity, long‐term stability, and functional capacity remain limited, restricting mechanistic studies and translational applications. Here, we establish a long‐term expandable periosteal organoid system that can be stably propagated for over 20 passages while preserving cellular heterogeneity, multilineage differentiation potential, and genomic integrity. Single‐cell transcriptomic analysis reveals sustained maintenance of core periosteal lineages and regenerative signaling programs over extended culture. Functionally, these organoids reconstruct a niche‐like microenvironment that supports hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) maintenance, preserves stem cell fitness, and attenuates aging‐associated functional decline under prolonged ex vivo conditions. Upon transplantation, periosteal organoids robustly engraft and actively participate in tissue repair, promoting vascularized bone formation and reconstruction of marrow‐like structures across multiple defect models. Mechanistically, we identify ZFP575 as a 3D niche‐dependent regulator required for maintaining in vivo osteogenic competence. Together, our findings establish periosteal organoids as a physiologically relevant and functionally competent regenerative platform, providing a versatile system for modeling skeletal repair and stem cell‐niche interactions.

title: Special Issue Editorial: Advanced Science for Tissue‐Interfaced Organic Bioelectronics
Water‐Coupled Interfacial Modulation Enhances Photovoltaic and Pyroelectric Responses in Transparent Self‐Powered ZnO/NiO Photodetectors
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Transparent self‐powered photodetectors are attractive for smart windows, environmental monitoring, and underwater optoelectronics, yet using the surrounding medium remains largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate a water‐assisted interfacial modulation strategy in a transparent FTO/ZnO/NiO/AgNW/ZnO photodetector, where direct water contact enhances performance. Water introduces two interfacial effects. First, refractive‐index matching at the ZnO/water interface suppresses Fresnel reflection, raising average visible transmittance from 61.0% to 77.02%. Second, an electric double layer (EDL) electrostatically modulates the ZnO surface, promoting charge separation and carrier transport. Under 365 nm illumination, the open‐circuit voltage (
                     
                      V
                       oc 
                     
                    ) increases from 0.223 to 0.265 V, the short‐circuit current density from 0.751 to 0.797 mA cm
                     −2 
                    , and the power conversion efficiency from 1.63% to 2.53%. Impedance and Mott–Schottky analyses confirm reduced series resistance, enhanced interfacial capacitance, and a positive flat‐band shift. The water‐induced interfacial field strengthens transient polarization, yielding a responsivity of 93.1 mA W
                     −1 
                    , a specific detectivity of 1.52 × 10
                     11 
                    Jones, an effective pyroelectric coefficient rising from 6.8 to 8.5 mC m
                     −2 
                    K
                     −1 
                    , and fast rise/fall times of 0.953/2.82 ms. These findings establish liquid‐interface engineering as an effective and reversible strategy for simultaneously enhancing transparency and photodetection, opening new opportunities for water‐compatible transparent electronics, intelligent glazing, and submerged optical sensing.

title: Phosphonium Ionic Liquids for Electrochemical Energy Storage: Structure–Property–Interphase Relationships and Design Rule
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Phosphonium ionic liquids are emerging electrolyte platforms for safer and more durable electrochemical energy‐storage systems because they combine low volatility, reduced flammability, thermal robustness, broad electrochemical stability windows, and highly tunable cation–anion chemistry. Their performance emerges from coupled cation–anion structure, salt concentration, electrolyte formulation, solvation environment, and electrode chemistry. This Review develops a structure–property–interphase framework for phosphonium‐based electrolytes in lithium, sodium, zinc, magnesium, and aluminum batteries, as well as supercapacitors and quasi‐solid‐state systems. For phosphonium‐based electrolytes, we analyze how alkyl chain length, branching, ether functionalization, and anion identity govern viscosity, conductivity, ion coordination, metal plating/stripping, corrosion, gas evolution, and solid–electrolyte and cathode–electrolyte interphase formation. The analysis shows that smaller, asymmetric, branched, or ether‐functionalized cations generally promote faster ion transport, whereas long‐chain hydrophobic cations are better suited for thermally robust, low‐volatility, gel, or deep‐eutectic‐type formulations. Finally, we propose practical design rules emphasizing low‐viscosity cation design, fluorine‐reduced anion chemistry, standardized benchmarking, full‐cell validation, and surface‐sensitive/operando interphase characterization.

title: Polyphosphate Copper Nanospheres Drive Mitochondrial Metabolic Reprogramming via Calcium Phase Separation for Self‐Sensitizing Cuproptosis
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Precise spatiotemporal control of intracellular Ca
                     2+ 
                    signaling remains a major bottleneck in reversing tumor glycolytic dominance and reactivating mitochondrial therapies. To overcome this limitation, we developed a polyphosphate (polyP)‐engineered nanoplatform that exploits liquid‐liquid phase separation (LLPS) to drive calcium‐mediated metabolic reprogramming. We discovered that FITC‐polyP coacervates with Ca
                     2+ 
                    to form biomolecular condensates that function as localized Ca
                     2+ 
                    signaling microdomains. By selectively activating key mitochondrial enzymes, these microdomains shift tumor cells toward a mitochondria‐dependent metabolic phenotype. Crucially, disturbing condensate formation via Ca
                     2+ 
                    chelation or enzymatic degradation prevents this transition, confirming polyP/Ca
                     2+ 
                    condensates as the indispensable master regulator of mitochondrial metabolic activation. Sustained mitochondrial reactivation creates a primed cellular state that sensitizes tumor cells to cuproptosis. This work establishes a resourceful self‐sensitizing nanoplatform that utilizes polyP‐induced phase separation to precisely reprogram tumor metabolism and activate cuproptosis, highlighting polyP‐induced LLPS as a novel strategy for targeted cancer therapy.

title:
Quantized Analog Inference Hardware Enabled by MoS

                     1‐x

                     2 
                    FeFET Synapses
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Analog in‐memory computing can accelerate edge‐AI inference by executing vector–matrix multiplication directly in memory crossbars, but practical analog deployment is constrained by finite weight resolution and stochastic programming. Here we demonstrate program‐pulse‐engineered MoS
                     2– 
                    Hf
                     1‐x 
                    Zr
                     x 
                    O
                     2 
                    (HZO) ferroelectric field‐effect transistor (FeFET) synapses and a hardware‐consistent quantized machine‐learning workflow for noise‐robust analog inference. The device integrates an atomically thin monolayer MoS
                     2 
                    channel, representing ultimate body‐thickness scaling in advanced logic roadmaps, with a CMOS‐compatible HZO ferroelectric gate stack. Operating in a near‐coercive regime, trains of identical potentiation/depression pulses yield gradual and reversible multi‐level conductance updates with ∼100 states, enabling array‐realistic programming without per‐device program‐and‐verify. Systematic pulse engineering provides knobs to tune update granularity and dynamic range, and enables offset control of the usable conductance window via asymmetric depression conditions. Crucially, we quantify cycle‐to‐cycle write variability using state‐dependent Δ
                     G 
                    statistics and incorporate the measured quantization levels and noise directly into training and evaluation. Using MNIST as a benchmark, noise‐aware quantization‐aware training outperforms post‐training quantization across quantization levels and noise scaling, sustaining up to ∼97% test accuracy under low precision and elevated noise. These results connect measured programming physics to robust quantized analog inference and establish practical device–algorithm co‐design principles for scalable FeFET‐based synaptic hardware.

title: Quenching Photo‐Induced Free Radicals Endows Superomniphobic Atmospheric Water Harvesting Hydrogels With UV Resistance for Durable Bifacial Photovoltaic Cooling
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Bifacial photovoltaic (PV) modules constitute 75% of global PV manufacturing output and are playing an increasingly vital role in the clean energy transition. However, their operational efficiency is severely compromised by heat accumulation and dust soiling. Moreover, the rear‐side optical transparency required for bifacial light harvesting renders conventional thermal management techniques infeasible. This work reports a zero‐energy‐demand and liquid water‐free cooling strategy for bifacial PV panels: Functionalized fullerene C
                     60 
                    is homogeneously incorporated into the atmospheric water harvesting (AWH) hydrogel and terminates light‐induced radical chain reactions, enhancing the hydrogel's UV stability by over 385%. Meanwhile, the modified hydrogel surface imparts superomniphobicity with oil and water contact angles exceeding 160°, resists dust adhesion, and maintains 92.5–96.0% transmittance in the PV response spectrum. The hydrogel cooling layer has a calculated unit cost as low as $9.0 m
                     −2 
                    and delivers a daytime cooling power of 550–650 W m
                     −2 
                    when the PV panels are in operation, reducing the panel temperature by up to 14.3°C and boosting both the maximum power output and conversion efficiency by 9.03%. This strategy holds a global annual carbon mitigation potential of 537.56 million metric tons of CO
                     2 
                    , offering a sustainable route for photovoltaic thermal management.

title: NSUN3‐Associated m5C Modification of tRF5‐GlyTCC Suppresses Colorectal Cancer Progression via RPL23‐Linked Nucleolar Stress and p53‐Associated Autophagy and Enhances 5‐FU Sensitivity
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   tRNA‐derived small RNAs (tsRNAs) regulate gene expression and cellular stress responses in cancer, but their roles in colorectal cancer (CRC) progression and chemotherapy response remain incompletely understood. Dysregulated tsRNAs in CRC were identified by RNA sequencing. The functions of tRF5‐GlyTCC were evaluated using in vitro assays and an in vivo xenograft model. Its targets and molecular effects were investigated by bioinformatic analyses, luciferase reporter assays, western blotting, and immunofluorescence. m5C modification was assessed by MeRIP‐qPCR. tRF5‐GlyTCC was downregulated in CRC tissues and associated with advanced disease and poor prognosis. Restoration of tRF5‐GlyTCC suppressed CRC cell growth and migration in vitro and tumor growth in vivo. tRF5‐GlyTCC interacted with the RPL23 3′UTR and was associated with altered ribosomal homeostasis, nucleolar stress, p53 signaling, and autophagy. Restoration of tRF5‐GlyTCC enhanced 5‐FU sensitivity, while its agomir increased the antitumor effect of 5‐FU in vivo. NSUN3‐mediated m5C modification contributed to tRF5‐GlyTCC stability. NSUN3‐mediated m5C modification contributes to tRF5‐GlyTCC stability, which is associated with ribosomal homeostasis, nucleolar stress responses, and p53 signaling. This network contributes to tumor suppression and chemotherapy response in CRC.

title: An Oral Antiviral Combination Against Severe COVID‐19 Enabled by the Synergistic Mechanisms of Action of Auranofin and Remdesivir
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Auranofin, an FDA‐approved oral anti‐rheumatic drug, was previously shown by our group to restrict Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus‐2 (SARS‐CoV‐2) replication and pathology in preclinical models. Here, we systematically characterized its mechanism of action (MOA) through biochemical drug‐protein interactions, cell‐based mechanistic assays, and preclinical efficacy studies. Auranofin directly binds and inhibits SARS‐CoV‐2 MPro while simultaneously targeting multiple stages of the viral life cycle, disrupting endosomal trafficking, suppressing Spike S1/S2 proteolytic processing, impairing syncytia formation, and attenuating NF‐κB‐driven proinflammatory signaling. In cell culture, Auranofin demonstrated robust synergy with Remdesivir but competed with the MPro inhibitor Nirmatrelvir, informing rational combination design. In mice infected with the SARS‐CoV‐2 Delta variant, the oral combination of Auranofin and the Remdesivir prodrug GS‐621763 outperformed monotherapy, markedly reducing viral replication, inflammatory cytokine responses, and lung pathology, and improving clinical outcomes. These findings establish a multi‐target antiviral MOA of Auranofin and provide a mechanistic rationale for an all‐oral antiviral combination regimen against COVID‐19.

title: ZMIZ2–DUX4–LGR5 Signaling Axis Maintains Stemness Properties and Facilitates Docetaxel Resistance in Triple‐Negative Breast Cancer
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Triple‐negative breast cancer (TNBC) is a highly aggressive malignancy with limited targeted treatment options and frequent chemoresistant. Through integrated RNA‐seq analysis of docetaxel‐resistant cell lines and three publicly available docetaxel‐resistant TNBC datasets, we identified zinc finger MIZ‐type containing 2 (
                     ZMIZ2 
                    ) as a critical mediator of chemoresistance in TNBC. ZMIZ2 is markedly upregulated in TNBC tissues and chemoresistant specimens and inversely correlates with clinical chemotherapy response. Functional studies have reveal that ZMIZ2 promotes cancer stemness‐associated properties, malignant progression and docetaxel resistance. Mechanistically, ZMIZ2 directly binds to the transcription factor DUX4 via its MIZ domain and cooperatively activates LGR5 transcription by interacting with BRG1 and BAF57, core components of the SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complex. This ZMIZ2–DUX4–LGR5 axis sustains tumor cell stemness‐associated properties and promotes tumorigenesis, thereby driving therapeutic resistance. We also identify liquiritin as a ZMIZ2 inhibitor that synergises with docetaxel to effectively enhance tumor regression. Collectively, our findings establish ZMIZ2 as a promising therapeutic target and provide a potential strategy to overcome docetaxel resistance in TNBC.

title: Precision Nanomedicine for Traumatic Neural Injury: Functional Paradigms and Translational Frameworks
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Traumatic neural injuries, including traumatic brain injury (TBI), spinal cord injury (SCI), and peripheral nerve injury (PNI), impose a substantial global burden. These injuries converge on oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, regulated cell death, demyelination, and extracellular matrix remodeling, while diverging in timing, cellular effectors, and regenerative capacity. Current management still fails to arrest secondary injury or restore functional neural circuitry. Nanomedicine integrates targeted delivery, microenvironmental regulation, and regenerative support, yet existing strategies and reviews remain compartmentalized by injury type or material class. Such fragmentation constrains the integration of shared mechanisms with injury‐specific requirements. To address this gap, we develop a cross‐injury framework for nanoparticle‐based intervention. Separate reanalysis of three single‐cell datasets suggests recurrent myeloid involvement and injury‐specific within‐dataset patterns. We compare lipid‐based, polymeric, inorganic, carbon‐based, biomimetic, and hybrid platforms in relation to physicochemical properties and biological fate. Six paradigms are organized by pathological need: scaffold construction and microenvironment remodeling, topographical guidance, biomimetic targeting, endogenous stimulus‐responsive release, external physical‐field activation, and intracellular reprogramming. We trace evolution from passive encapsulation to multi‐omics‐guided and artificial intelligence (AI)‐assisted precision design and examine barriers to manufacturing, biodistribution, safety, protein‐corona control, and regulatory evaluation. This framework connects injury mechanisms, functional needs, and material selection to guide translation.

title: Catalytic Luminescent Polymer Micromotors With Shape‐Programmed Motion
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Photoactive polymers hold promise for powering micromotors by converting light into energy. However, traditional energy polymers cannot catalyze on one side of Janus structures in chemically driven micromotors because they only store and convert energy, not perform efficient photocatalysis. In this work, we introduce an indium tin oxide (ITO) conductive interlayer that functions as a dedicated charge‐transfer pathway. This layer efficiently extracts photogenerated holes and spatially separates electron–hole pairs from the PFN‐Br/Pt catalytic layer, thereby creating stable interfacial electric fields and ionic gradients. The combination of self‐electrophoresis and self‐diffusiophoresis enhances propulsion efficiency and long‐term stability compared to traditional single‐catalyst micromotors. The PFN‐Br polymer layer also serves as a fluorescent marker, enabling stable propulsion and real‐time tracking of micromotor movements. Additionally, we show that ultrasonic‐assisted self‐assembly can effectively shape and program these micromotors. This method enables the transition from random movement to more directed trajectories by forming single, dimeric, or trimeric assemblies, which is vital for future investigations of collective dynamics and swarm intelligence. Meanwhile, we have begun initial efforts to utilize its luminescent properties for optical signal encoding, creating opportunities for micro‐ and nano‐scale platforms capable of UV‐controlled optical signaling paired with light‐driven movement.

title: Accelerated Discovery of Earth‐Abundant Oxygen Evolution Catalysts Through Surface‐Informed Active Learning
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    The development of efficient electrocatalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) remains a challenge in alkaline water electrolysis. Discovering optimal compositions for complex multi‐element electrocatalysts is time‐intensive and resource‐consuming due to the vast compositional space. Here, we propose a hybrid computational strategy that integrates active learning (AL)‐assisted screening with density functional theory (DFT) calculations to accelerate the development of multielement alloy electrocatalysts. Our approach employs 15 cycles of active learning, with 20 NiCoFe (NCF) surface configurations evaluated per cycle, totaling 300 DFT calculations. To minimize computational cost, we utilized scaling relationships and calculated only *O and *OH adsorption energies, while the AL featurization incorporated surface configuration information. This methodology filtered the compositional space of Ni
                     x 
                    Co
                     y 
                    Fe
                     100‐x‐y 
                    alloys and identified the optimal composition of Ni
                     55 
                    Co
                     10 
                    Fe
                     35 
                    . Experimental validation demonstrated that the optimized NCF exhibits accelerated OER kinetics and practical activity, as evidenced by a low Tafel slope of 43.07 mV dec
                     −1 
                    while maintaining 98.68% of its initial performance over 24 h at 10 mA cm
                     −2 
                    . This study demonstrates the effectiveness of the hybrid AL‐DFT strategy for resource‐efficient composition screening within the NiCoFe ternary alloy system and highlights its potential for application to other multicomponent catalyst systems following appropriate system‐specific model development and validation.

title: Scaffold RNA Reengineering for a Leakage‐Suppressed CRISPR/Cas12a Cascade System Toward Precise Nucleic Acid Diagnostics
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Amplification‐free CRISPR detection has attracted significant attention for its capacity to circumvent the intricacies of nucleic acid amplification. Yet, the persistent challenge of high background signals remains a critical bottleneck, motivating intensive efforts toward background suppression strategies. Here, we present a 3’‐end DNA extension of scaffold RNA (3’D‐SR) conformational switch to drive the cascade‐activatable and leakage‐suppressed Cas12a system, a mechanism we denote as CALCas. By engineering the crRNA of Cas12a system and introducing steric hindrance as an activation barrier, we reshape crRNA into a “threshold‐controlled” smart molecular switch, enabling Cas12a to shift from “inhibition” to “precise activation”. Unlike other Cas cascade reaction generally suffer from internal self‐activation that leads to uncontrolled background increase, this newly developed framework, leveraging a DNA‐mediated allosteric regulation mechanism and a leakage‐suppressed design based on inherent steric hindrance, effectively solves the dilemma between signal enlargement and minor background variation. Through rational design, this cascaded CRISPR system achieves femtomolar sensitivity (over 10,000‐fold higher than single Cas12a system), enables rapid HPV16/18 detection, and reduces assay time to under 30 min. This engineered crRNA approach unlocks a new pathway to reprogram Cas12a's enzymatic activities with a stabilized benchmark signal that can be critical in precise quantitative nucleic acid detection.

title: Magnetic Thermal Ablation Combined with Temporally Coordinated CpG Immunotherapy Promotes cDC1‐Dependent Immune Priming in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) imposes a major global health burden, with current ablation techniques limited by invasiveness and post‐treatment recurrence. Here, size‐controllable, polylactic acid/iron oxide magnetic microspheres containing 30% Fe
                     3 
                    O
                     4 
                    (P@Fe30 MSs) were fabricated via shirasu porous glass membrane emulsification for transarterial magnetic thermal ablation (MTA). The optimized microspheres exhibit superior magnetothermal performance under an alternating magnetic field, effectively killing tumor cells and triggering immunogenic cell death (ICD). Mechanistically, MTA‐induced tumor disruption cooperates with the TLR9 agonist CpG ODN to accelerate dendritic cell maturation and promote a tumor–TDLN immune‐priming cascade, featuring CD103
                     + 
                    cDC1 enrichment and CCR7‐associated cDC1 migration dynamics, functional CD8
                     + 
                    T‐cell activation, and systemic memory‐associated immune remodeling. Crucially, direct evaluation of CpG timelines reveals that early post‐MTA CpG administration significantly outperforms delayed delivery, validating a transient post‐ablation immune‐priming window. Furthermore, experiments in Batf3
                     − 
                    /
                     − 
                    mice confirm that this systemic antitumor immunity strictly depends on a cDC1‐ mediated priming pathway. Finally, preclinical validation in an orthotopic rabbit VX2 liver tumor model demonstrates excellent transarterial feasibility, localized metabolic tumor suppression via
                     18 
                    F‐FDG PET imaging, and a favorable safety profile. This work establishes a remotely activated transarterial ablation platform that coordinates with temporal innate immunotherapy to drive systemic cDC1‐dependent antitumor responses.

title: ERα–PADI4–CXCL8 Axis Drives MDSC‐Mediated Immune Evasion in Anaplastic Thyroid Carcinoma
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma (ATC) is a highly lethal malignancy with a median survival of merely 4–6 months and no effective systemic therapies. Although ATC predominantly arises in elderly postmenopausal women with negligible circulating 17β‐estradiol (E2), we observed that estrogen receptor alpha (ERα) is constitutively phosphorylated at serine 118 (S118) in ATC tissues, independently of its canonical ligand. Here, we identify peptidyl arginine deiminase 4 (PADI4) as a direct transcriptional target of ligand‐independently activated ERα, driven by EGF/MAPK signaling. PADI4 is overexpressed in ATC along a dedifferentiation gradient, and its high expression defines an immune‐excluded tumor microenvironment characterized by dense CD33
                     + 
                    myeloid‐derived suppressor cell (MDSC) infiltration and CD8
                     + 
                    T cell exclusion, portending poor prognosis. Mechanistically, PADI4 citrullinates histone H3 at the CXCL8 promoter, opening chromatin and driving CXCL8 secretion, which recruits MDSCs through CXCR2. Pharmacological inhibition of PADI4 with GSK484 triggers compensatory CXCL1 upregulation, sustaining residual MDSC chemotaxis through CXCR1/2. Combined blockade of PADI4 (GSK484) and CXCR1/2 (SX‐682) synergistically suppresses tumor growth, eliminates pulmonary metastasis, and achieves 80% long‐term survival in an orthotopic ATC model, without appreciable systemic toxicity. These findings establish the ERα–PADI4–CXCL8–MDSC signaling axis as a central driver of immune evasion in ATC and provide a preclinical rationale for dual‐targeted epigenetic‐immunotherapy.

title: Proton transport drives allosteric conformational changes in the MmpL3 transporter
abstract:
Tuberculosis (TB), caused by
                     Mycobacterium tuberculosis 
                    (
                     Mtb 
                    ), remains a global health crisis, further complicated by increasing drug resistance. The mycobacterial membrane protein MmpL3, which is essential for transporting cell wall precursors such as trehalose monomycolate (TMM), is a promising therapeutic target. However, the mechanistic link between proton-driven dynamics and substrate transport in MmpL3 is not fully understood. In this study, we use molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how protonation of conserved Asp-Tyr dyads (Asp256-Tyr646 and Asp645-Tyr257) in
                     Mycobacterium smegmatis 
                    (
                     Msmg 
                    ) MmpL3 regulates conformational changes and TMM binding. Protonation at Asp256 induces an open dyad conformation, increases local water accessibility, and is associated with a tendency toward more open configurations of the periplasmic binding pocket. In contrast, protonation at Asp645 stabilizes a closed dyad conformation, reduces water accessibility, and narrows the transmembrane binding pocket. These findings support a proposed sequential protonation model in which protonation-dependent conformational changes are allosterically coupled to substrate translocation.

title: The successor representation in high-risk drinking and alcohol-related contexts
abstract:
by Milena P. M. Musial, Sam Hall-McMaster, Kanji Shimomura, Ayaka Kato, Erik L. Bode, Clarissa C. Grundmann, Claudia Ebrahimi, Kenji Morita, Samuel J. Gershman, Tanja Endrass, Florian Schlagenhauf 

The successor representation (SR) is a reinforcement learning strategy which has been suggested to underlie nuanced forms of habitual behavior, rendering it a candidate mechanism for mental health conditions thought to involve habitual control, such as addiction. However, paradigms used to assess habits in humans cannot detect SR use. Together with the fact that they are usually conducted in disorder-irrelevant contexts, this may explain why the evidence for a hypothesized shift from goal-directed to habitual behavior in addiction is inconsistent. Here, we tested whether individuals with high-risk ( n  = 260) compared to low-risk drinking behavior ( n  = 260) rely more on SR or a rigid goal-based dimension-reduced SR variant (redSR), particularly in alcohol-related contexts. An online multi-stage decision-making task performed in either a virtual bar or apartment context allowed us to dissociate (red)SR from model-based and model-free learning strategies by testing how well participants adapted their choices to different types of distal changes in the environment. Findings suggest that a particular type of SR, namely a (reduced) random-policy SR-like strategy, contributes to human behavior, but that high-risk drinkers do not differ from low-risk drinkers in their use of this strategy.
