In vivo Gene Writing with engineered retrotransposons
abstract: Computational reconstruction, screening, and engineering of non-LTR retrotransposons uncovers elements, termed Gene Writers, that enable stable transgene integration in human cells using all-RNA delivery. After extensive characterization and optimization, Gene Writers is deployed to generate functional CAR-T cells in vivo in a humanized mouse model.

title: A bioavailable GPX4 inhibitor for ferroptosis induction in vivo and tumor suppression
abstract: Selective pharmacological induction of ferroptosis in vivo has remained difficult. By developing the bioavailable GPX4 inhibitor KY0418, this work links systemic ferroptosis induction to tissue metabolic remodeling and demonstrates context-dependent suppression of tumor progression, including metastatic spread.

title: Contrasting demographic impacts of Roman colonization and early medieval migrations in the Iberian Peninsula
abstract: Roman and post-Roman Iberia was transformed by extensive mobility across the Mediterranean, with large-scale inputs from Eastern Mediterranean and North African populations reshaping its genetic landscape. During the migration period, Central-Northern European ancestry arrived largely through elite-associated groups that intermarried with local populations but did not replace the highly diverse population that had formed under Roman rule.

title: Proteomic atlas of T cell exhaustion defines proteostatic collapse
abstract: A multi-omic atlas of human T cell exhaustion reveals that dysfunctional T cells undergo broad remodeling of protein turnover and ubiquitin regulation that is not captured by transcriptomic analysis. The E3 ubiquitin ligase RNF166 regulates T cell persistence and anti-tumor function, highlighting proteostasis as a targetable axis for improving immunotherapy.

title: Multitask Deep Learning Model for Predicting Lymph Node Metastasis and Disease‐Free Survival From Cytology Images in Bladder Cancer: A Multicenter Study With Pan‐Cytology Validation
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Accurate prediction of lymph node metastasis (LNM) and survival outcomes is crucial for personalized treatment in bladder cancer, yet remains clinically challenging. This study aimed to develop a Cytology‐based multitask predictive Network (CytoNet) to simultaneously predict LNM and disease‐free survival (DFS) in bladder cancer, and to evaluate its generalizability in cervical and thyroid cancers. This study included a multicenter cohort of 5273 patients, with bladder cancer (n = 1134), cervical cancer (n = 598), and thyroid cancer (n = 3541). CytoNet was constructed through a three‐stage pipeline comprising self‐supervised pretraining, supervised fine‐tuning, and multitask prediction. In bladder cancer, CytoNet achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.831‐0.881 for LNM prediction and a C index of 0.680‐0.710 for DFS prediction across all cohorts, outperforming single‐task models and standard radiological assessments. In cervical cancer, CytoNet demonstrated robust performance for both LNM prediction (AUC 0.847‐0.862) and DFS prediction (C index 0.690‐0.709), while in thyroid cancer, it achieved an AUC of 0.819‐0.855 for LNM prediction. In conclusion, CytoNet represents a reliable tool for predicting LNM and prognosis from cytopathology images across multiple cancer types, showing potential as a valuable adjunct to current clinical decision‐making. Further prospective validation is warranted to assess its clinical utility.

title: PROBE: a multi-organism benchmark for evaluating general-purpose large language models on Gene Ontology protein function annotation
abstract:
Background
                      One of the most important unresolved issues in computational biology is systematic protein function annotation. Despite decades of curation by the Gene Ontology Consortium and UniProt Swiss-Prot, most sequenced proteins lack experimentally validated functional annotations. The emergence of Large Language Models (LLMs) trained on scientific literature raises the question of whether they can map natural-language descriptions of experimentally characterized protein function to the correct Gene Ontology (GO) terms without task-specific training. Answering this question requires a benchmark with gold-standard experimental annotations and multi-organism coverage, which existing benchmarks lack. 
                  
                     Results
                      We introduce PROBE ( PR otein functi O n  B enchmark  E valuation): 1,000 UniProt Swiss-Prot proteins from five organisms, experimental-evidence-only annotations. We evaluate 10 open-source LLMs across five prompt formats, zero-shot and inference-only, yielding 150,000 predictions. The best model (Mistral Large 123B) achieves macro-F1 of 9.3%, yet a most-frequent-5 heuristic outperforms four of the ten LLMs. 41.3% of predicted GO terms were unmatched to the benchmark’s annotations; a temporal-holdout check against current UniProt records found only 1.25% newly supported, suggesting most are genuine errors rather than incomplete ground truth. Performance varied by organism— Saccharomyces cerevisiae  unexpectedly scored highest (F1 = 8.6%), but with only five organisms this does not track evolutionary distance, and neither literature density nor annotation-pool size reaches significance, so the finding remains exploratory. Candidate-selection prompting (P5) reduces the unmatched-prediction rate by 33.5 percentage points relative to P1 while achieving the highest F1 (8.2%). GO semantic similarity analysis shows LLM predictions exceed a random baseline by 2.1–2.6× across all namespaces, indicating biologically meaningful semantic alignment despite exact-match failures. A preliminary 50-protein comparison of four closed-source models against the best open-source model found F1 of 0.081–0.127 versus 0.099 (0.028-point gap), suggesting but not establishing that current limitations extend beyond open-source models. 
                  
                     Conclusions
                      PROBE shows that general-purpose LLMs can map some natural-language descriptions of protein function to GO terms, but performance is often insufficient and unreliable for autonomous annotation. Unmatched predictions are common, and organism-level performance differences remain an open question rather than explained by training data or evolutionary relationships. The benchmark, evaluation pipeline, and all 150,000 experimental response records are publicly available to ensure reproducibility.

title: Red to green: catching gene silencing as it takes hold

Genomic insights into trichome and inflorescence evolution of the palaeopolyploid tree genus
                     
                       Greyia
abstract:
SUMMARY 
                   
                    The southern African endemic tree
                     Greyia 
                    Hook. & Harv. (Francoaceae, Geraniales) comprises three species distinguished by striking variation in trichome morphology and inflorescence architecture, yet the genomic and regulatory basis of these traits has remained largely unexplored. Here, we present chromosome‐scale genome assemblies for all recognised
                     Greyia 
                    species, namely
                     Greyia radlkoferi 
                    ,
                     Greyia sutherlandii 
                    , and
                     Greyia flanaganii 
                    , providing the first high‐quality genomic resources for Geraniales. Phylogenomic analyses placed Geraniales as sister to Crossosomatales, with divergence at ~103 million years ago (Mya), and indicated that
                     Greyia 
                    diversified recently during the Quaternary (~1.39 Mya). Comparative genomics revealed a
                     Greyia 
                    ‐specific palaeo‐hexaploidisation event dated to ~87 Mya, followed by fractionation but with extensive retention of ancestral gene sets in either triplicated or duplicated states across syntenic regions. Transcriptomic analyses revealed regulatory divergence in the conserved MYB–bHLH–WD40 (MBW) network likely associated with variation in trichome morphology, including undetectable
                     GL1 
                    expression and altered
                     GL3/EGL3 
                    expression in
                     G. sutherlandii 
                    . In addition, analyses of flower and inflorescence traits identified expansion of MADS‐box transcription factor families and species‐specific
                     cis 
                    ‐regulatory divergence in
                     LFY 
                    and
                     FT 
                    . Notably, predicted AGL6 binding sites are retained in the
                     LFY 
                    and
                     FT 
                    promoters of
                     G. radlkoferi 
                    and
                     G. sutherlandii 
                    but absent in
                     G. flanaganii 
                    , consistent with differences in inflorescence density among species. Together, these results demonstrate how polyploidy and regulatory divergence of conserved developmental pathways have shaped morphological diversification in
                     Greyia 
                    .

title: A Heat‐Inducible Rubisco Activase Safeguards Photosynthesis via Multilevel Regulation and Dual Function
authors:
Yuqing Cao, 
Xiaomian Zhang, 
Fangqian Qu, 
Mengxuan Liu, 
Zheng Li, 
Bing Liu, 
Xianbin Gu, 
Qianyi Hu, 
Hong Zhou, 
Liangsheng Zhang, 
Yiping Xia, 
Xiuyun Wang
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Rubisco activase (RCA) is critical for maintaining photosynthetic efficiency under heat stress, yet its regulatory mechanisms and functional diversification remain poorly understood. Here, we characterize a novel heat‐inducible RCA family member (RCA1), which plays a pivotal role in mediating multidimensional thermotolerance in a tropical azalea. Both heterologous and homologous overexpression of
                     RCA1 
                    significantly mitigated heat‐induced cellular damage and better maintained photosynthetic capacity, confirming its essential function in thermal resilience. Heat‐induced
                     RCA1 
                    expression is transcriptionally activated by a synergistic HSFA1‐HSFA2 complex and post‐transcriptionally fine‐tuned by extensive alternative splicing, forming a multilevel regulatory network under heat stress. Beyond its canonical Rubisco‐activating enzymatic activity, RCA1 exhibits an additional thermoprotective function that suppresses the thermal aggregation of several chloroplast proteins, such as Lhca2, PetC and PsaK. RCA1 also interacts with the constitutive RCA2, likely through heteromeric RCA complex assembly, which helps retain RCA2 in a soluble pool under heat stress. Evolutionary analyses reveal functional divergence within the RCA family, with convergent evolution of heat‐inducible
                     RCA 
                    clades in Panicoideae grasses. Collectively, our findings uncover a novel dual‐functional heat‐inducible RCA, which provides a promising target for photosynthetic bioengineering to enhance crop thermotolerance and ensure agricultural sustainability under global warming.

title: Tropical leaf phenology as a thermoregulation trait: how changes in crown structure modulate thermal dynamics for two dominant Hawaiian trees
authors:
Shannon L. J. Bayliss, 
Eben N. Broadbent, 
Angélica M. Almeyda Zambrano, 
Stephanie Pau
abstract:
Summary 
                   
                     
                       
                         Canopy and leaf temperatures often diverge from air temperature, influencing photosynthesis, water loss, and heat stress. While leaf traits are known to affect heat exchange, how changes in crown structure interact with environmental drivers to regulate canopy thermal dynamics is poorly understood, particularly in tropical forests. 
                       
                       
                         
                          In a Hawaiian wet tropical montane forest, we used repeated UAV‐based (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle) thermal and LiDAR (light detection and ranging) measurements of sunlit leaves within and across 397 tree crowns of
                           Acacia koa 
                          and
                           Metrosideros polymorpha 
                          to investigate (1) seasonal and species‐specific variation in crown traits; (2) how crown traits and environmental drivers interact to determine canopy–air temperature differences (Tdiff), within‐crown thermal variability (Tcan
                           SD 
                          ), and maximum leaf temperatures (Tcan
                           MAX 
                          ); and (3) whether crowns with greater seasonal structural change exhibit enhanced thermoregulation.
                         
                       
                       
                         
                          All crown traits showed species‐specific seasonal dynamics, with trait–trait and trait–environment interactions shaping thermal metrics differently across species. In
                           M. polymorpha 
                          , crowns with greater seasonal structural change exhibited lower relative Tdiff, whereas
                           A. koa 
                          did not show this buffering effect.
                         
                       
                       
                         These results indicate that canopy thermoregulation emerges from interacting crown traits dynamically reshaped across phenological and seasonal cycles. Seasonal crown dynamics provide partial thermal buffering in some species, highlighting species‐specific pathways of thermal acclimation or vulnerability under climate change.

title:
Comparative genomics of dark septate endophytes: shedding light on the enigmatic lifestyle and biology of
                     DSEs
authors:
Sándor Csíkos, 
Zsolt Merényi, 
Dániel G. Knapp, 
Anna Lipzen, 
Kurt LaButti, 
Jasmyn Pangilinan, 
Robert Riley, 
Sajeet Haridas, 
Asaf Salamov, 
Kerrie Barry, 
Alan Kuo, 
Elodie Drula, 
Igor V. Grigoriev, 
Bernard Henrissat, 
Francis Martin, 
László G. Nagy, 
Gábor M. Kovács
abstract:
Summary 
                   
                     
                       
                         Dark septate endophytes (DSE) are widespread root‐colonising fungi with poorly understood lifestyle and ecological functions. We investigated their genomic traits, sexual reproduction signatures, carbohydrate‐active enzyme (CAZyme) and secondary metabolites profiles, and tested whether genomic features distinguish DSEs and other endophytes from fungi with other lifestyles. We also reconstructed ancestral states to clarify the evolutionary origins of DSEs. 
                       
                       
                         We analysed 107 Ascomycota genomes representing diverse lifestyles, including nine newly sequenced DSE genomes. The dataset allowed us to test whether secreted enzyme profiles differ between fungi colonising roots vs shoots and those associated with grass vs nongrass hosts. 
                       
                       
                         DSEs evolved through multiple independent trajectories and diverse lifestyles and show remarkable metabolic diversity. They possess extensive degradative capacities and some of the largest biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) richness among fungi. Despite sharing BGC richness with other endophytes, DSEs form a distinct subgroup with fewer cellulose‐ and more hemicellulose‐targeting enzymes. Genomes also revealed genomic signatures associated with fungi colonising grass vs nongrass hosts and root‐ vs shoot‐associated niches. 
                       
                       
                         Our comparative genomics approach highlights how genome‐level data can deepen our understanding of endophytic lifestyle and the biology of the enigmatic DSE fungi.

title:
A single amino‐acid switch reprograms
                     ROP6 
                    signaling to drive functional evolution in plants
authors:
Liuqin Zhang, 
Yahong An, 
Ting Lan, 
Jinyu Cui, 
Xinyue Du, 
Liman Mu, 
Lina Liu, 
Mingxuan Xu, 
QingQing Li, 
Liping Cheng, 
Jianyan Zeng, 
Lei Hou, 
Yan Pei, 
Mi Zhang
abstract:
Summary 
                   
                     
                       
                         Rho‐related GTPases of plants (ROPs) are evolutionarily conserved molecular switches that typically maintain PIN‐formed proteins at the plasma membrane (PM), yet their functional divergence remains poorly understood. 
                       
                       
                         Here, we reveal that a single amino‐acid substitution at residue 194 acts as a core determinant, driving the evolutionary split between Brassicaceae and Malvaceae ROP6 orthologs: glycine enforces PM stabilization, whereas alanine licenses endocytic function. 
                       
                       
                         In cotton, the Malvaceae‐predominant alanine mutated GhROP6 displays an auxin‐independent manner. The distinct activity is attributed to the recruitment of three GhRIC effectors that directly bind the actin cytoskeleton and promote F‐actin assembly and bundling. The resulting actin reorganization facilitates GhPIN3a internalization and proteolysis, consequently enhancing cotton fiber elongation. 
                       
                       
                         Our findings demonstrate that a single amino‐acid change can reprogram ROP signaling and uncover a molecular switch underlying the functional evolution of ROP6 in regulating plant development.

title: The MBW complex regulates floral volatiles in petunia: transcriptional repressor EOBV is a MYB component of the complex
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Anthocyanin biosynthesis in Petunia is regulated by the bHLH AN1 and the WDR protein AN11, which together with interchangeable MYBs form the MYB–bHLH–WDR (MBW) complex. As they share the same biosynthetic pathway, anthocyanins are interlinked with phenylalanine-derived volatiles. However, involvement of the MBW complex in regulating these floral volatiles has not been demonstrated. TRV-based suppression of either AN1 or AN11 led to an increase in volatile emission, indicating that they are involved in negative regulation of this trait. Yeast two-hybrid and in-planta pairwise and three-way protein-interaction assays revealed that EMISSION OF BENZENOIDS V (EOBV) is a component of the MBW complex. Headspace and internal pool analyses of flowers from eobv-knockout lines, generated using a viral-based CRISPR/Cas9 system, revealed that EOBV fine-tunes volatile production: phenylpropenes and vanillin levels increased while those of benzenoids and phenylpropanoid-related compounds decreased. Accordingly, transcript levels of C4H2, directing carbon flux to phenylpropenes and vanillin production, and ADT3 were significantly elevated in eobv-knockout flowers, along with decreases in PAAS and BSMT. Moreover, in-planta promoter activity assays in petunia flowers further demonstrated that C4H2 is negatively transcriptionally regulated by EOBV. In addition to its involvement in volatile production, EOBV is heat-responsive and affects flower development under high-temperature conditions by mitigating the reduction in flower size. EOBV’s participation in the MBW complex that regulates volatiles and anthocyanins reveals an intriguing molecular link between these showy traits and flower development.

title:
CHH demethylation of the
                     BcMAM1 
                    promoter contributes to cold tolerance in autotetraploid wucai (
                     Brassica campestris 
                    L.)
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Polyploidization has long been recognized as a driving force in plant adaptation to adverse environments. Chilling injury poses a major challenge to global crop production, and the regulatory hierarchies that govern cold adaptation in polyploid crops are unexplored. Here, we show that tetraploid wucai (Brassica campestris L.) displays greater cold tolerance than its diploid counterpart. Under prolonged cold stress, tetraploid plants displayed enhanced glucosinolate-associated transcriptional and metabolic responses, which may contribute to their improved stress adaptation. At the epigenetic level, diploid and tetraploid wucai showed distinct DNA methylation responses to short-term cold, with diploid plants tending toward greater CHH hypermethylation in promoter regions. This ploidy-specific increase in methylation correlates with transcriptional repression of multiple stress-responsive loci in diploids. Notably, expression of the glucosinolate biosynthesis gene METHYLTHIOALKYLMALATE SYNTHASE1 (BcMAM1) diverged between ploidies after cold treatment, inversely correlating with opposing CHH methylation (H = A, C, or T) trends in its promoter. Pharmacological demethylation using 5-azacytidine upregulated BcMAM1 and improved cold tolerance. Through a combination of functional assays and promoter-binding analyses, we identify the upstream transcription factor C-REPEAT BINDING FACTOR4 (BcCBF4), which binds to differentially methylated regions within the BcMAM1 promoter in a methylation-sensitive manner, supporting an association between the epigenetic state and transcriptional output. Together, our findings support a mechanistic model for the distinct cold response observed in the autotetraploid wucai line, involving coordinated changes in transcriptional activation and DNA methylation dynamics. The epigenetic and transcriptional targets identified in this study may inform breeding strategies for cold-resilient crops.

title: ct-validation: an open framework for benchmarking target-indication evidence against clinical trial outcomes
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Summary 
                     Human genetic evidence provides a strong foundation for selecting drug targets. However, consistent benchmarking of target-indication evidence against clinical trial outcomes has been hindered by proprietary data and customized pipelines. To address this, we present the Python package ct-validation, which evaluates whether target-indication pairs supported by specific evidence sources are enriched for clinical progression. This package computes relative success (RS) and odds ratios with confidence intervals across clinical phase transitions. It also supports ontology-based semantic disease matching and offers interfaces in Python, on the command line, and via the Model Context Protocol. By remapping the benchmark from Minikel et al. (2024) to the Experimental Factor Ontology, we reproduced their per-transition enrichment, with a maximum difference of only 1.4% across any transition. In a systematic 3 × 3 benchmark that independently varies the genetic evidence and clinical trial sources, we found that a single curated open clinical trial source reproduces the signal of the proprietary comparator (RS = 2.92 versus 2.65; 2.34 versus 2.55 without oncology). However, aggregating open clinical trial registries compresses this signal (RS = 1.52); this loss is primarily driven by the breadth of the indication data rather than the genetic evidence. 
                   
                   
                     Availability and implementation 
                     ct-validation is implemented in Python (version 3.11 or higher), distributed via pip, and freely available at https://github.com/gero-science/ct-validation, with support for Python, command-line, and Model Context Protocol interfaces. Archived code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22901497. Benchmark data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22901451

title: pxGPT: a schema-constrained multimodal large language model framework for plant phenotyping
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Summary 
                     Deep learning can scale image-based plant phenotyping but typically targets predefined traits, whereas manual phenotypic description is more flexible but difficult to scale. We present Phenotype eXplorer Generative Plant Traits (pxGPT), a Python framework that converts multi-view plant images into structured phenotype records. The workflow combines free-text description, dataset-specific schema generation with human review, and schema-constrained information extraction. We evaluated the extraction stage on three Brassica datasets using 78 973 annotations from 10 annotators who had no access to pxGPT predictions. For 38–45 qualitative traits per dataset, pxGPT-human agreement ranged from 0.572 to 0.712, compared with 0.620 to 0.739 agreement among human annotators. All 32 736 required trait fields were present; 93 values were empty, and no qualitative descriptor violations were recorded. For selected morphological structures, pooled false-positive rates were 0.5%–8.0%, while sensitivity varied across structure types in one mature-plant dataset (37.5%–100%). The curated schemas were applied unchanged with two commercial models and one locally hosted open-weight model, with differences in mean accuracy of 0.03 or less. In the evaluated Brassica datasets, these results support schema-guided extraction of visible plant traits without separate model training for each trait. Human-guided schema development offers a path to extend pxGPT to other crops and imaging conditions, with accuracy requiring validation in each new setting. 
                   
                   
                     Availability and implementation 
                     The software is available at https://github.com/YaoChengLab/pxgpt and an archival version of the source code is available on Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22931745). Curated schemas used in this study, annotation guides, phenotype records, and human annotations are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907554.

title: Integration of polygenic risk with single cell methylation data using met-scDRS
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Motivation 
                     Although large scale genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified many risk variants for psychiatric traits their functional implication remain largely unknown. One potential mechanism for their risk is through cellular context-dependent epigenetics such as methylation. Previous methodologies have focused on integrating GWAS with single cell transcriptomics, which allowed identification of within-cell-type heterogeneity in disease risk association. We extended this framework to provide a method called met-scDRS that integrates GWAS with single cell epigenomics and investigates how psychiatric disease risk can manifest through methylomics at single cell resolution. 
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     We propose an approach that integrates single cell methylomes with disease associated genes identified from GWAS at single-cell resolution. We found our method to be well calibrated and powered in different scenarios. We then analysed a publicly available single cell methylome dataset of the human brain for 75 different traits and generated disease relevance scores for each cell for each trait. We find high brain specificity with major cell type enrichments congruent with known findings. We identify within-cell-type heterogeneity for psychiatric disease risk along the brain spatial axis as well as subpopulations that are differentially associated with diseases. Finally, we showed that genes with high correlation between methylation levels and disease relevance scores to be highly enriched in specific functional pathways such as synaptic formation and transmission. 
                   
                   
                     Availability 
                     met-scDRS is freely available in GitHub as a python package under MIT license: https://github.com/bogdanlab/met-scDRS. Source code is also available from Zenodo with DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21841506. All dataset used in this work are publicly available.

title: MR-MAS: an end-to-end multi-agent system for autonomous Mendelian randomization analysis
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Motivation 
                     Understanding disease-related causal mechanisms is essential for biomedical research, yet the practical use of Mendelian Randomization (MR) remains constrained by fragmented analytical workflows and a strong dependence on specialized expertise. These challenges limit the efficient, standardized, and reproducible execution of end-to-end MR analyses. 
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     We propose MR-MAS, an end-to-end automated MR analysis system built on a multi-agent architecture. MR-MAS leverages the reasoning and coordination capabilities of large language models (LLMs) and integrates external tools to unify data acquisition, causal effect estimation, results interpretation, and manuscript preparation into a single workflow, thereby reducing manual effort. MR-MAS further incorporates a structured Mendelian Randomization Knowledge Base (MRKB) to support MR method implementation and targeted repair of MR analysis code. Across diverse test scenarios, MR-MAS demonstrated stable workflow execution, reproduced several literature-supported causal signals, and maintained consistent causal estimates across repeated runs and different model backends. Additional evaluations showed robust trait retrieval and improved code-repair performance with MRKB guidance. These results suggest that MR-MAS may provide practical support for scalable, standardized, and reproducible MR analyses in biomedical research. 
                   
                   
                     Availability and Implementation 
                     The source code, MRKB, and benchmark data are freely available at https://github.com/Zaiwen/MR-MAS, with the version used in this study archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20342636.

title: A tunable immune-evasion function of Zika virus NS5 governs viral fitness and pathogenesis
authors: Yu ZhangYaqing ZhangChengyu LiuWenlin RenYu ZhaoChenhao LiYongqi GuoLeyi BaiPeigang WangJing AnJun LiuQiang Dingahttps://ror.org/03cve4549Center for Infection Biology, School of Basic Medical Sciences, Tsinghua University, Beijing 100084, Chinabhttps://ror.org/034t30j35State Key Laboratory of Virology and Biosafety, Wuhan Institute of Virology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Wuhan, Hubei 430062, Chinachttps://ror.org/05qbk4x57University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing 100049, Chinadhttps://ror.org/03ybmxt82Strategic Pandemic Preparedness Action and Research Center (SPARC), Guangzhou National Laboratory, Guangzhou 510005, Chinaehttps://ror.org/00rd5t069School of Laboratory Medicine and Life Sciences, Wenzhou Medical University, Wenzhou, Zhejiang 325035, Chinafhttps://ror.org/041pakw92The High School Affiliated to Renmin University of China, Beijing 100080, Chinaghttps://ror.org/013xs5b60Department of Microbiology, School of Basic Medical Sciences, Capital Medical University, Beijing 100069, Chinahhttps://ror.org/00z0j0d77State Key Laboratory of Respiratory Disease, National Clinical Research Centre for Respiratory Disease, National Centre for Respiratory Medicine, Guangzhou Institute of Respiratory Health, The First Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University, Guangzhou Medical University, Guangzhou 510182, China
abstract:
Type I interferon (IFN) signaling is a central antiviral defense, with STAT2 driving the expression of IFN-stimulated genes (ISGs) to restrict viral infection. Zika virus (ZIKV) and dengue virus evade this pathway through nonstructural protein 5 (NS5)-mediated ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of STAT2, yet the contribution of this immune-evasion strategy to viral fitness and pathogenesis remains incompletely defined. Here, using a multistep mutational scanning strategy that jointly assessed STAT2 degradation and viral RNA replication, we identified a single NS5 residue, L162, as uniquely permissive to substitution that abolishes STAT2 degradation without compromising intrinsic replication functions. Substitution of L162 with alanine or glycine (L162A or L162G) selectively disrupted NS5 recruitment of the ZSWIM8-CUL3 E3 ubiquitin ligase, thereby preserving STAT2 stability and restoring IFN signaling. Recombinant ZIKV carrying these mutations exhibited reduced replication and enhanced ISG induction in human cells, defects fully rescued by STAT2 knockout. In A129 mice (type I IFN receptor deficient), mutant and WT viruses replicated comparably, but in human STAT2 knock-in mice, ZIKV-NS5
                     L162G 
                    exhibited markedly reduced viral loads and disease. In pregnant human STAT2 knock-in mice, the mutant also reduced placental and fetal viral burdens and adverse pregnancy outcomes. Notably, infection with ZIKV-NS5
                     L162G 
                    elicited robust neutralizing antibody and T cell responses that conferred protection against WT challenge. Together, these findings establish NS5-mediated STAT2 degradation as a central determinant of ZIKV immune-evasion, viral fitness, and pathogenesis and highlight disruption of NS5–STAT2 antagonism as a promising strategy for antiviral intervention and rational attenuation.

title: Molecular basis for discrimination of cGAMP linkage isomers by a c-di-GMP-II riboswitch variant
authors: Xiaochen XuWang ChengHuiqin YouZejia HuXinyue BaoHongcheng LiJinzhu ZhangDinshaw J. PatelAiming RenaDepartment of Cardiology of The Second Affiliated Hospital and Life Sciences Institute and School of Medicine, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou 310058, ChinabStructural Biology Program, Memorial Sloan-Kettering Center, New York, NY 10065
abstract: Riboswitches are noncoding RNA regulatory motifs predominantly found in bacteria. Signaling molecules such as c-di-GMP, c-di-AMP, and 3′,3′-cGAMP have been reported to be recognized by riboswitches. In contrast, 2′,3′-cGAMP functions as a second messenger in mammalian cells, yet its interaction with RNA molecules remains unclear. Here, we report the crystal structures of a c-di-GMP-II riboswitch variant, c-di-GMP-II-Bh, bound to 2′,3′-cGAMP and 3′,3′-cGAMP. Both complexes adopt a similar overall RNA scaffold with an identical binding pocket composition. However, the ligand bases adopt inverted orientations in the binding pocket, resulting in distinct interaction patterns with residues A64 and G68 and differences in base-pair stacking against the phosphodiester backbone. Structural comparison together with ligand-binding assays of structure-guided mutants using isothermal titration calorimetry reveals the molecular principles by which an RNA riboswitch discriminates among cyclic dinucleotide linkage isomers, highlighting the remarkable sensitivity of RNA binding pockets to subtle ligand structural variations and provides a mechanistic framework for understanding ligand specificity in RNA–small molecule recognition.

title:
Programmable chemoenzymatic synthesis of a keratan sulfate
                     N 
                    -glycan library for glycocode decoding
authors: Kaixuan WangWenjing MaWei ZhangTianhui HaoMengjia ZhangWentao LiWei ZhaoZhuojia XuTiehai Liahttps://ror.org/034t30j35State Key Laboratory of Chemical Biology, Carbohydrate-Based Drug Research Center, Shanghai Institute of Materia Medica, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Shanghai 201203, Chinabhttps://ror.org/02kjtx631Qingdao Central Hospital, National Health Commission Key Laboratory of Cardiopulmonary Rehabilitation and Functional Recovery, School of Medicine, University of Health and Rehabilitation Sciences, Qingdao 266113, Chinachttps://ror.org/017zhmm22School of Pharmacy, Xi’an Jiaotong University, Xi’an 710061, Chinadhttps://ror.org/05qbk4x57University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing 100049, Chinaehttps://ror.org/023b72294College of Veterinary Medicine, Huazhong Agricultural University, Wuhan 430070, China
abstract:
Keratan sulfate (KS) is a unique and widely distributed glycosaminoglycans family implicated in diverse biological processes. KS features branched glycan architectures with diverse sialylation and sulfation patterns, encoding a vastly expanded chemical and biological space. The limited accessibility of well-defined structures has hindered precise investigations into the KS biological functions. Here we report a programmable chemoenzymatic platform for assembling a 106-membered library of KS
                     N 
                    -glycans and their nonsulfated counterparts, featuring length-variable oligo-
                     N 
                    -acetyllactosamine (LacNAc) extensions and encompassing diverse sulfation and sialylation patterns. The synthetic strategy integrates length-controlled iterative glycosylation to assemble versatile precursors, orthogonal deprotection for site-specific sulfation, and modular enzyme-driven diversification. Glycan microarray analysis of this comprehensive library reveals that glycan–protein recognition is governed by the interplay of sulfation and sialylation patterns, oligo-LacNAc chain length, and terminal epitope presentation, providing insight into the functional versatility of KS glycans.

title: Structure of bovine viral diarrhea virus E2 glycoprotein in complex with CD46 reveals the molecular basis of virus–receptor recognition
authors: Yanping DuanSheng LinFei WangYu YouZimin ChenLiyan GuoWenjie GongLianjing LiangShiyuan TangHai-fang YuYarong HeBin HeZhi WanYu CaoFanli YangGuangwen Luahttps://ror.org/011ashp19Department of Emergency Medicine, State Key Laboratory of Biotherapy, West China Hospital, Sichuan University, Chengdu 610041, Sichuan, Chinabhttps://ror.org/011ashp19Department of Hematology, West China Hospital, Sichuan University, Chengdu 610041, Sichuan, ChinacDepartment of Veterinary Public Health, State Key Laboratory for Diagnosis and Treatment of Severe Zoonotic Infectious Diseases, Key Laboratory for Zoonosis Research of the Ministry of Education, College of Veterinary Medicine, Jilin University, Changchun 130062, Jilin, Chinadhttps://ror.org/011ashp19Laboratory of Emergency Medicine, Disaster Medicine Center, West China Hospital, Sichuan University, Chengdu 610041, Sichuan, Chinaehttps://ror.org/034z67559Center for Design and Biomanufacturing of Anti-infective Agents, Institute for Advanced Study, Chengdu University, Chengdu 610106, Sichuan, China
abstract: Bovine viral diarrhea virus (BVDV) is a major contagious pathogen of ruminants and imposes substantial economic burdens on the global livestock industry. The viral envelope glycoprotein E2 mediates host cell attachment by recognizing the CD46 receptor; however, the molecular basis of this interaction remains unclear. Here, we report the crystal structure of BVDV-1 E2 in complex with bovine CD46 at 3.1-Å resolution. The structure reveals that the SCR1-2 domains of CD46 engage the DII-DIV domains of E2 in a roughly antiparallel orientation. Atomic interactions at the E2/CD46 interface are dominated by van der Waals contacts, accompanied by only a limited number of hydrogen bonds, which explains the observed low-affinity binding between the two molecules. Structural analysis and mutagenesis studies identify key receptor features that govern host susceptibility to the virus and propose an interesting bipartite model: The D′/D interloop within SCR1 of CD46 likely serves as the “molecular determinant,” and key interface residues within SCR2 function as the “affinity regulator.” We further engineered CD46 decoy proteins exhibiting over 1,800-fold higher apparent binding to E2 than the wild-type receptor and demonstrated their potent virus-neutralizing activity. Collectively, these findings elucidate the molecular basis of CD46 recognition by BVDV, provide a structural framework for understanding the viral host range, and establish a receptor-based strategy for potential antiviral intervention.

title: Heterogeneous amyloid β dimerization revealed by single-molecule FRET and MD simulation
authors: Fanjie MengGeorge A. PantelopulosJae-Yeol KimRobert B. BestHoi Sung Chungahttps://ror.org/00adh9b73Laboratory of Chemical Physics, National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases, National Institutes of Health, Bethesda, MD 20892-0520
abstract: The correlation between specific amyloid fibril polymorphs and diseases suggests that characterization of heterogeneity in the aggregation process is key to understanding disease mechanisms. In this work, we use single-molecule Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) spectroscopy and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation to quantitatively characterize dimerization of amyloid β (Aβ), the first step of the aggregation process. We find that dimerization is extremely rare, with a high dissociation constant of >16 mM, yet there are multiple dimer states with distinct FRET efficiencies and stabilities, many of which survive for milliseconds to seconds. The dimer population increases with the increasing ionic strength and decreasing pH, indicating the importance of nonspecific electrostatic interactions in dimer formation. MD simulations with enhanced sampling demonstrate the formation of diverse bound states having a range of FRET efficiencies and flexible N termini, compatible with the experimental observations. There are conformational clusters represented by the formation of three mixed parallel/antiparallel β strands forming Greek key-like motifs and the formation of antiparallel β strands, which may be representative of dimers with longer and shorter lifetimes, respectively, observed in the FRET experiment. This structural and kinetic heterogeneity, resulting from transient interactions, reflects the rugged energy landscape of amyloid formation and may be related to the great diversity of fibrils ultimately formed in the aggregation process.

title: Mechanism of HIV-1 capsid rupture and uncoating by reverse transcription
authors: Kuntal GhoshManish GuptaGregory A. Vothahttps://ror.org/024mw5h28Department of Chemistry, Chicago Center for Theoretical Chemistry, James Franck Institute, and Institute for Biophysical Dynamics, The University of Chicago, Chicago, IL 60637
abstract: One of the key events in the HIV-1 life cycle is reverse transcription (RT), during which single-stranded viral RNA (ssRNA) is converted into double-stranded DNA (dsDNA). This process occurs inside the mature HIV-1 capsid and, once it reaches a critical threshold, drives capsid rupture. This uncoating is essential for infection because it releases viral genetic material into the host cell nucleus. Despite its importance, many mechanistic details of this process remain to be fully understood. To address this gap, we develop a multiscale computational method for simulating RT inside the capsid, termed Coarse-Grained Kinetic Monte Carlo (CG-KMC). CG-KMC stochastically adds deoxynucleotide triphosphates (dNTPs) to the coarse-grained RNA model, enabling stepwise growth of DNA inside the HIV-1 capsid. We implement this method within an integrative coarse-grained framework that combines a “bottom-up” capsid model with a “top-down” representation of the viral RNA/DNA genome. Our simulations phenomenologically capture and predict diverse capsid rupture pathways during RT. The resulting ruptured structures closely match previously identified cryo-ET images. We further perform an extensive analysis of the rupture process, examining its mechanistic and kinetic aspects as well as the role of capsid–DNA interactions. Our findings illuminate how different capsid–DNA conditions give rise to distinct rupture pathways, which differ from ruptures due to simple outward pressure expansion models from within the capsid.

title: Multiple sources contribute to predictive tactile attenuation in the mouse whisker system
authors: Kalpana GuptaShubhodeep ChakrabartiCornelius Schwarzahttps://ror.org/03a1kwz48Systems Neurophysiology, Werner Reichardt Center for Integrative Neuroscience, Eberhard Karls University Tübingen, Tübingen 72076, Germanybhttps://ror.org/04zzwzx41Systems Neurophysiology, Hertie Institute for Clinical Brain Research, Eberhard Karls University Tübingen, Tübingen 72076, Germanychttps://ror.org/03a1kwz48Graduate Training Center for Neuroscience, Eberhard Karls University Tübingen, Tübingen 72076, Germany
abstract: The brain predicts action outcomes using interacting neuronal systems that integrate sensory feedback, movement, and rewards. In the mouse whisker system, we investigated whether two presumed predictive mechanisms jointly attenuate ascending tactile signals during movement. To this end, we employed an open-loop whisker-reach task that monitored facial nucleus motor activity and presented experimental tactile consequences while measuring tactile attenuation in the barrel cortex. Experimentally manipulating sensory consequences revealed two distinct systems. Sensory gating, a previously documented but functionally unclear mechanism of tactile attenuation, appeared graded but persisted during and after movement. In contrast, a second system was found to be temporally precise, generate suppression when stimuli are omitted, and capable of being learned within hundreds of trials. We label it state estimation as its characteristics—active suppression of expected tactile input—aligns well with the classical reafference principle, previously overlooked in the whisker system.

title: Meta-analysis of 990 EBV genomes identifies EBER2 SNP7048 and its interaction with HLA-A*11:01 driving nasopharyngeal carcinoma risk
authors: Ching-Yuan WangFei YaoXinyi ZhangLing WangYee Yen SiaEnya Hui Wen OngEugenia Li Ling YeoAndrea Nicole RioChor Hiang SiowHan Lee GohZhi Kang ChinRachel Jia Xuan NgYing Yu TanJavier Cher An CheeWei Keat TeoWeiwei ZhaiYanhong ChenMiao XuKwok Seng LohWan-Teck LimMelvin Lee Kiang ChuaJoshua K. abstract: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a major health burden in East and Southeast Asia (SEA). While EBV infection is a primary driver, the specific viral strains responsible for NPC development and their interaction with host genetics across geographically diverse endemic regions remain poorly understood. We performed a whole-genome sequencing of 388 EBV isolates and matched host whole-exome sequencing in a Singaporean cohort. To define the global significance of these findings, we conducted a meta-GWAS and phylogenetic analysis across three independent cohorts (Singapore, Hong Kong, and Guangdong and Guangxi provinces of China), totaling 990 EBV genomes. Our study identifies high-risk EBV strains—carrying a core variant in the EBER2 locus (SNP7048)—as the key viral determinator of NPC risk, accounting for approximately 68% of the attributable risk in SEA. Meta-analysis reveals these strains are consistently associated with NPC across all populations, resolving previous regional genetic discordances. We demonstrate a potent synergistic interaction between these EBV risk strains and the host HLA-A*11:01 protective allele; individuals lacking this protection while carrying a high-risk strain exhibit a 30.9-fold increase in NPC risk. Phylogenetic analysis further reveals that these high-risk lineages populated SEA through clonal expansion from Southern China, following historical migration routes. These findings establish that NPC development is driven by the distribution of specific high-risk EBV lineages and their synergistic interaction with host immune susceptibility. This provides a definitive genetic framework for precision population screening and early diagnosis of NPC in the endemic regions.

title: Causality in liquid water as a hallmark of emergent glassy dynamics
authors: Léon HuetVittorio Del TattoDebarshi BanerjeeAlessandro LaioAli A. Hassanaliahttps://ror.org/009gyvm78Condensed Matter and Statistical Physics, The Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics, Trieste 34151, Italybhttps://ror.org/004fze387Scuola Internazionale Superiore di Studi Avanzati, Trieste 34136, Italy
abstract: In molecular liquids such as water, time-delayed influences between microscopic or mesoscopic variables are typically probed using time-correlation functions, which are symmetric under detailed balance and therefore blind to dynamical asymmetries. Here, we characterize water’s dynamics using a causal inference metric that captures asymmetric couplings between collective variables. Analyzing equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations at ambient conditions and in the high-density liquid (HDL) regime of supercooled water, we uncover pronounced asymmetries in the couplings between orientational and translational degrees of freedom across multiple time and length scales. At room temperature, rotational modes exert a modest directional influence on translational dynamics. In contrast, in the supercooled HDL regime, translational motions emerge as the primary drivers of the dynamics, suggesting facilitation-like relaxation mechanisms characteristic of glassy systems. These results reveal a qualitative reorganization of dynamical couplings across thermodynamic conditions, implying that molecular liquids at thermal equilibrium can exhibit an emergent directionality in their fluctuation couplings. As a consequence, our analysis reveals that external perturbations acting on specific degrees of freedom can induce a stronger arrow of time in the causal relations between translational and orientational modes.

title: Widespread plasma jets in the Martian magnetosheath revealed by dual-spacecraft observations
abstract: Plasma jets in planetary magnetosheaths are transient, high dynamic pressure structures capable of strongly perturbing downstream magnetospheres and modulating solar wind energy transfer. Although recently identified at Mars, their formation mechanisms and global occurrence remain poorly constrained. Using dual-spacecraft observations from Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN and Tianwen-1, we show that magnetosheath jets occur throughout the Martian magnetosheath, in striking contrast to Earth where jet occurrence is strongly controlled by interplanetary magnetic field orientation and largely confined to quasi-parallel shock regions. We propose that this widespread distribution is linked to Mars’ extended hydrogen corona, which generates pickup ions that drive proton-cyclotron waves upstream of the bow shock. Because this mechanism is generic to any body with an extended corona (or exosphere) embedded in a stellar wind, this finding bears on solar–wind interactions at comets and other small bodies, and on the space environments of unmagnetized terrestrial exoplanets. These results indicate that magnetosheath jet formation can be governed not only by external solar wind forcing but also by intrinsic planetary properties, pointing to a previously unrecognized pathway for solar wind–planet coupling at unmagnetized worlds.

title: Diminishing cooling returns of urban greening amid a warming climate
authors: Song LengHongbin HeAlfredo HueteEkena Rangel PinagéWenjie ZhangHonghao DingLiding ChenRanhao Sunahttps://ror.org/034t30j35State Key Laboratory of Regional and Urban Ecology, Research Center for Eco-Environmental Sciences, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing 100085, Chinabhttps://ror.org/05qbk4x57University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing 100049, Chinachttps://ror.org/03f0f6041School of Life Sciences, Faculty of Science, University of Technology Sydney, ultimo, NSW 2007, Australiadhttps://ror.org/01xnsst08Forest and Climate Change Program, Wildlife Conservation Society, Bronx, NY 10460ehttps://ror.org/02y0rxk19School of Geographical Sciences, Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology, Nanjing 210044, China
abstract: Urban greening is widely prioritized as a nature-based solution to mitigating intensifying heat extremes in the context of climate change, yet its long-term global efficacy remains inadequately quantified. Here we present a two-decade assessment of vegetation dynamics and associated cooling effects across 3,806 urban clusters worldwide, integrating multisource satellite observations with ground measurements from 4,855 meteorological stations. We identify a pronounced climate equity gap: While cities in the Global North have largely expanded green infrastructure, they exhibit cooling saturation with diminishing biophysical returns. Conversely, most cities in the Global South show vegetation stagnation or loss, compounding rapid warming trends. This asymmetry exposes a critical climate justice challenge, indicating that current greening efforts are insufficient to offset a warming trend. Our findings underscore the necessity for context-specific, integrated climate adaptation frameworks that address both the quantity and quality of urban vegetation to achieve equitable thermal resilience in an increasingly warm world.

title: Magnetically guided programmable thermomechanical protection enabled by biomimetic asymmetric design
authors: Zimu LiJianfeng HuangSheng WangJianpeng WuShuai LiuZhihao HuGuilin MeiXinglong Gongahttps://ror.org/04c4dkn09Chinese Academy of Sciences Key Laboratory of Mechanical Behavior and Design of Materials, Department of Modern Mechanics, University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei 230027, Anhui, People’s Republic of Chinabhttps://ror.org/04c4dkn09State Key Laboratory of Fire Science, University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei 230026, Anhui, People’s Republic of China
abstract: Precision instruments operating in harsh environments require protective materials that can dissipate impact energy while resisting heat. However, actively tunable thermomechanical protection under coupled multiphysics conditions remains challenging. Inspired by shellfish and echinoderms, here we show that an asymmetrically engineered shear-stiffening gel (SSG) yields a Janus magnetorheological elastomer whose two faces mimic the brick-and-mortar architecture of shellfish and the impact-hardening behavior of echinoderms, respectively. Unlike single-modification anti-creep strategies of SSG that degrade shear-stiffening or severely increase initial modulus, our design achieves a 40-fold mechanical tunability, with the storage modulus ranging from 11.29 to 450.28 kPa, arising from the synergistic enhancement of strain-rate-dependent stiffening and magnetic interactions. The integration of magnetic and optical functions enables semiactive noncontact 2D-to-3D protection, achieving an 85% reduction in impact force and a 40 °C temperature difference via bidirectional photothermal regulation, demonstrating competitive thermomechanical protection performance. Furthermore, this strategy establishes a magnetically guided programmable pathway for thermomechanical protection and provides a generalizable blueprint for multifunctional intelligent materials, advancing protective technologies for outdoor equipment operating in extreme environments involving coupled physical fields.

title: Bridging spatial scales in respiratory viral infection
authors: Ulrik HvidBjarke Frost NielsenKim SneppenaPandemiX - Center for Interdisciplinary Study of Pandemic Signatures, Copenhagen 2300, Denmarkbhttps://ror.org/035b05819Biocomplexity, Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen, Copenhagen 2100, Denmark
abstract: Respiratory viruses spread within the host through a combination of local expansion and occasional long-range dissemination that seeds new infection foci. We present LEAP (Lotka-Euler Airway Pathogen model), an analytically tractable within-host model that captures this two-scale process. The model takes the form of an age-dependent branching process and yields a closed-form expression for the exponential growth rate during early infection. Using empirical data to parameterize the model, we find that productive dissemination requires only a small number of successful long-range seeding events per infected cell, with distinct values for SARS-CoV-2 and influenza A virus. LEAP further predicts that, in these well-adapted viruses, interferon-mediated restriction only weakly affects exponential growth, while remaining decisive for poorly adapted pathogens. More broadly, the model provides a flexible framework for experimentally testable predictions of early infection dynamics.

title: PSF3 recruits Polθ to stalled replication forks to promote DNA repair
authors: Umeshkumar VekariyaBenjamin Lee PratherRoland L. DunbrackRongsheng E. WangTomasz Skorskiahttps://ror.org/00kx1jb78Fels Cancer Institute for Personalized Medicine, Lewis Katz School of Medicine, Temple University, Philadelphia, PA 19140bhttps://ror.org/00kx1jb78Department of Chemistry, College of Science and Technology, Temple University, Philadelphia, PA 19122chttps://ror.org/0567t7073Cancer Signaling and Microenvironment Program, Fox Chase Cancer Center, Philadelphia, PA 19111dhttps://ror.org/00kx1jb78Department of Cancer and Cellular Biology, Lewis Katz School of Medicine, Temple University, Philadelphia, PA 19140ehttps://ror.org/0567t7073Nuclear Dynamics and Cancer Program, Fox Chase Cancer Center, Philadelphia, PA 19111
abstract: DNA polymerase theta (Polθ) plays a pivotal role in the maintenance of stalled replication forks. However, little is known about how Polθ is recruited to the stalled forks. Here we show that PSF3, a member of GINS replicative complex, recruits Polθ to the stalled replication forks. Polθ, which is recruited by interacting with the C-terminal portion of PSF3, restarts the forks, exerts DNA double-strand break end-joining to repair the breaks resulting from collapsed forks in BRCA1/2-deficient and proficient tumor cells, and also fills single-stranded gaps on the replication fork lagging strand in BRCA1/2-deficient tumor cells. Thus, PSF3–Polθ interaction promotes the proliferation of homologous recombination-deficient and proficient tumor cells. Overall, this study highlights an important mechanism of Polθ recruitment to the stalled replication forks to maintain Polθ-dependent fork protection in tumor cells.

title: The susceptibility to weight gain in male C57BL/6 mice fed high-fat diet is due to a small set of genes predominantly not expressed in the brain
authors: Yingga WuAgata M. RudolfLu WangZhengjie ZhangChaoqun NiuFan XiaMin LiAnyongqi WangDavina DerousSharon E. MitchellHaoran ZhangYalin HeJohn R. abstract: Obesity results from a gene by environment interaction. Understanding the impacts of environmental factors like diet on body weight/fatness has been greatly facilitated by rodent models. We previously identified the responses of males of five mouse strains fed 30 different diets. Two of these strains showed much greater weight gain and two were resistant. Sixty-six marker SNPs in 57 genes were identified, which have a genetic motif across the four strains reflecting their protection or susceptibility to high-fat diet (HFD). We used two of these strains: C57BL/6 and BALB/c, in a classic approach of cross-breeding the strains, to generate a F1 generation, and then cross-breeding their offspring to generate an F2 population. The F2 males were fed HFD and phenotyped for body weight, fat mass, and energy intake and genotyped for the 66 SNPs. Body mass gain on HFD was influenced by 17 SNPs in 11 genes explaining 87% of the individual variation in weight gain. We then measured gene expression of these 11 genes in 16 tissues of male and female C57BL/6 and Balb/c mice when fed high- or low-fat diets, and in 6 tissues of mice exposed to different levels of calorie restriction, to map their expression profiles. The genes were widely expressed in a diversity of tissues including several not normally suspected to be important for fat storage regulation (e.g., testis, lungs, and spleen) with only four expressed predominantly in the hypothalamus. Body fat regulation is probably more complex than current models focused on the brain–adipose axis suppose.

title: Disentangling the evolving effects of climate change and technology diffusion on building electricity demand
authors: Mai ShiZiqi WeiFlavio LehnerMichael T. Craigahttps://ror.org/00jmfr291School for Environment and Sustainability, University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, MI 48109bhttps://ror.org/042nb2s44Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, MA 02139chttps://ror.org/05bnh6r87Department of Earth and Atmospheric Sciences, Cornell University, Ithaca, NY 14853dhttps://ror.org/00jmfr291Department of Industrial and Operations Engineering, University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, MI 48109
abstract: Climate change and technology diffusion will jointly drive future growth in building electricity demand. How this nonadditive response evolves over time with the pace of climate change and technology diffusion has not previously been examined, despite its importance for maintaining reliable power systems. We estimate electricity demand from residential and commercial buildings under climate change and/or technology diffusion across 183 counties in the United States through 2060. Our framework drives 209,352 machine learning models of building electricity demand with 100 spatiotemporally downscaled climate realizations across four climate models and three emissions scenarios, and 18 technology diffusion pathways of air source heat pumps and insulation. We find that the combined response of peak demand to climate change and technology diffusion diverges substantially from the sum of their individual responses, with distinct patterns across hot and cold grid regions. In cold regions, climate change and technology diffusion drive roughly up to 10 times larger peak demand growth than climate change alone by 2060. Conversely, in hot regions, technology diffusion counteracts climate-change-driven peak demand growth. Across regions, climate-change-induced warming reduces or eliminates a shift toward winter peaking driven by technology diffusion. Via uncertainty partitioning, we find climate-related uncertainty dominates near-term peak demand uncertainty, while technology-diffusion-related uncertainty increases to 10 to 80% of uncertainty by 2060. Internal variability accounts for a much larger share of climate-related uncertainty in peak demand than in temperature itself. Our results demonstrate that capturing nonadditive responses between climate change and technology diffusion is important for planning reliable power systems.

title:
Conformational flexibility of the nitrogenase-like reductase CfbC/D involved in coenzyme F
                     430

authors: Lin ZhangFlorian SchuhmacherAlena KusslerOliver EinsleGunhild Layerahttps://ror.org/0245cg223Institut für Biochemie, Fakultät für Chemie und Pharmazie, Albert-Ludwigs-Universität Freiburg, Freiburg 79104, Germanybhttps://ror.org/03hz5th67Faculty of Synthetic Biology and Institute of Emerging Agricultural Technology, Shenzhen University of Advanced Technology, Shenzhen 518107, Chinachttps://ror.org/0245cg223Institut für Pharmazeutische Wissenschaften, Fakultät für Chemie und Pharmazie, Albert-Ludwigs-Universität Freiburg, Freiburg 79104, Germanydhttps://ror.org/0245cg223Centre for Integrative Biological Signalling Studies, University of Freiburg, Freiburg 79104, Germany
abstract:
The nitrogenase-like reductase CfbC/D catalyzes the six-electron reduction of the tetrapyrrole macrocycle of Ni
                     2+ 
                    -sirohydrochlorin
                     a,c 
                    -diamide during the biosynthesis of coenzyme F
                     430 
                    , an essential cofactor for biological methane formation and consumption. The individual dimeric protein components, CfbC
                     2 
                    and CfbD
                     2 
                    , form a complex to allow for electron transfer from the [4Fe:4S] cluster in CfbC
                     2

                     2

                     2
