title: Screw dislocation–mediated galaxy-mimicking superspiral assembly with amplified bio-piezoelectricity
authors: Jiahao ZhangHaoran WuShixuan XuHaoye JiangKang MaSyed A. M. TofailDeqing MeiJunbai LiKai TaoaState Key Laboratory of Fluid Power and Mechatronic Systems, School of Mechanical Engineering, and Institute of Fundamental and Transdisciplinary Research, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou 310058, Chinabhttps://ror.org/00a2xv884Future Science Research Institute, Zhejiang University-Hangzhou Global Scientific and Technological Innovation Centre, Hangzhou 311200, Chinachttps://ror.org/03893we55School of Mechanical Engineering, Zhejiang Sci-Tech University, Hangzhou 310018, Chinadhttps://ror.org/00a2xv884Key Laboratory of Advanced Manufacturing Technology of Zhejiang Province, School of Mechanical Engineering, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou 310058, ChinaeZhejiang-Israel Joint Laboratory on Self-Assembling Functional Materials, Hangzhou 311200, ChinafZhejiang-Ireland Joint Laboratory on Bio-Organic Dielectrics and Devices, Hangzhou 310058, Chinaghttps://ror.org/00a0n9e72Department of Physics and Bernal Institute, University of Limerick, Castletroy, Limerick V94T9PX, IrelandhBeijing National Laboratory for Molecular Sciences, Chinese Academy of Sciences Key Lab of Colloid, Interface and Chemical Thermodynamics, Institute of Chemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing 100190, Chinaihttps://ror.org/04f49ff35CAS Key Laboratory for Biomedical Effects of Nanomaterials and Nanosafety, National Center for Nanoscience and Technology, Beijing 100190, China
abstract: From the galaxies to the petals, spiral architectures are ubiquitous to confer hierarchical organizations, supporting asymmetric galactic evolutions and biological activities. Herein, inspired from nature, we report the superspiral architectures self-assembled by a minimalist amino acid. These superspirals, with spirality and geometry programmably tuned by enantiomeric excess and organization parameters, are determined to arise from the screw dislocation induced hierarchical crystallization. Notably, the spiral organization can integrate and amplify electrical polarization, yielding 17-fold enhancement in piezoelectric response contrast to random aggregates. This allows engineering of piezoelectric bioelectronics, resulting in high gain direction-selective motion sensing. Our work establishes an alternative paradigm for developing bioinspired hierarchical architectures of oriented and amplified properties, offering a self-assembling route to explore programmably modulated functional architectures for bioelectronic engineering.

title:
Methanogenic archaea
                     Methanobrevibacter smithii 
                    and
                     Methanosphaera stadtmanae 
                    promote mucosal homeostasis and protect from colitis
authors: Emily E. ByrdBenjamin W. HarrisHongpan ZhangW. Elise WarrenSree H. KolliAudrey M. PuteloMitchell T. McGintyMichael D. SolgaMelanie R. RutkowskiMelissa M. Kendallahttps://ror.org/0153tk833Department of Microbiology, Immunology, and Cancer Biology, University of Virginia School of Medicine, Charlottesville, VA 22908bhttps://ror.org/0153tk833University of Virginia School of Medicine, Charlottesville, VA 22908chttps://ror.org/0153tk833Department of Genomic Sciences, University of Virginia School of Medicine, Charlottesville, VA 22908dhttps://ror.org/0153tk833Flow Cytometry Core Facility, University of Virginia School of Medicine, Charlottesville, VA 22908
abstract:
The intestinal microbiota is a critical determinant of mucosal homeostasis, yet the functional contributions of Archaea—which constitute up to 10% of the anaerobic community—remain largely undefined. Here, we provide evidence that the human methanogens
                     Methanobrevibacter smithii 
                    (MSm) and
                     Methanosphaera stadtmanae 
                    (MSt) promote colonic health. Transcriptomic analysis of germ-free mice reveals that MSm and MSt induce distinct colonic programs important for epithelial integrity. Using gnotobiotic and antibiotic-treated specific-pathogen-free mouse models, we show that MSm and MSt reinforce the epithelial barrier, characterized by increased goblet cell expansion, mucus thickening, and enhanced epithelial regeneration. Furthermore, methanogens expand Foxp3
                     + 
                    regulatory T cell (T
                     reg 
                    ) populations without inducing pro-inflammatory T
                     H 
                    17 responses. Notably, MSm and MSt protect against dextran sodium sulfate-induced colitis. While MSt-mediated protection requires adaptive immunity, MSm retains partial efficacy in lymphocyte-deficient mice, revealing nonredundant protective mechanisms. These findings indicate that methanogenic archaea promote mucosal integrity during host association and suggest that methanogens may hold therapeutic potential for inflammatory bowel disease, though translation to human disease remains to be established.

title: Evolution of the arbuscular mycorrhizal regulatory network through differential GRAS gene retention and protein interaction in land plants
authors: Wen-Shen WuPeng ZhaoZhen ZengXiao-Tong LiPing WuQian DingXing-Yu FengYan-Mei ZhangShuai-Ya HuJia-Yu XueQiang WangYang LiuJian-Qun ChenZhu-Qing Shaoahttps://ror.org/01rxvg760State Key Laboratory of Pharmaceutical Biotechnology, School of Life Sciences, Nanjing University, Nanjing 210023, Chinabhttps://ror.org/00nqzn326Jiangsu Provincial Key Laboratory for Plant Taxonomy, Resource Conservation and Utilization, Institute of Botany, Jiangsu Province and Chinese Academy of Sciences, Nanjing 210014, Chinachttps://ror.org/05td3s095College of Horticulture, Bioinformatics Center, Academy for Advanced Interdisciplinary Studies, Nanjing Agricultural University, Nanjing 210095, Jiangsu, China
abstract: Plants rely on an ancient genetic “toolkit” to establish arbuscular mycorrhizal symbiosis (AMS) with fungal partners. However, the symbiotic outcomes vary among AMS hosts, indicating divergence in downstream transcriptional reprogramming after the perception of symbiotic signals. To uncover the cross-species variation of the AMS regulatory network, we traced the evolutionary trajectory of the GRAS gene family, which encodes the major group of transcription factors in AMS regulation. Phylogenetic analysis of the GRAS family across land plants placed known symbiotic GRAS members within 12 anciently diverged lineages, with multiple lineages showing pronounced gene loss in nonmycorrhizal plants. This pattern pointed to three additional GRAS lineages as candidates for AMS regulation. Given that tomato harbors single-copy, AMS-induced genes in these lineages, we selected it for functional validation. CRISPR-Cas9 mutagenesis, combined with detailed phenotyping of fungal colonization and arbuscule morphology, and transcriptome profiling of mutant roots, confirmed that all three tomato genes are individually required for AMS development, designated Symbiosis-Required GRAS (SRG) 1 to 3. Large-scale phylogenomic analysis and protein interaction assays (by yeast two-hybrid and bimolecular fluorescence complementation) further showed that both the repertoire and interaction networks of symbiotic GRAS members vary among AMS hosts. In summary, together with 12 previously characterized lineages, the three SRGs identified in this study bring the total number of GRAS lineages with known symbiotic members across land plants to fifteen. Furthermore, our findings demonstrate that the symbiotic GRAS network has been dynamically reshaped by gene loss and rewiring of protein interactions during land plant evolution.

title: First-principles channel model and capacity-achieving transmission scheme in thermal noise backscatter links
authors: Geneva EcolaJida ZhangJoseph M. KahnZerina Kapetanovicahttps://ror.org/00f54p054Department of Electrical Engineering, Stanford University, Stanford, CA 94305
abstract: Thermal noise communication systems transmit information by modulating thermal radiation, eliminating the need for a dedicated signal power source and making them attractive solutions for low-power sensor networks. Their efficiency enables long-lived, unobtrusive operation, which is valuable in the Internet of Things, electromagnetic interference-sensitive environments, and radio frequency identification tag systems. However, a limited understanding of the wireless channel model and efficient transmission schemes has hindered their practical deployment. Here, we present a wireless channel model that elucidates how systems operating at ambient temperature can modulate thermal noise to convey information. Our results reveal a thermal noise backscatter mechanism that enables significantly higher data rates than previously achieved. We designed and built a thermal noise communication system leveraging this mechanism to achieve data rates in the kilobits-per-second range—over two orders of magnitude higher than prior demonstrations. We also derive the system capacity and show that using polar codes, we are able to achieve this expected capacity. Our channel model and transmission scheme pave the way for strategies in thermal noise sensing and communication, advancing practical low-power networking for next-generation wireless applications.

title: Mediator-associated proteins and the small RNA–guided Polycomb repressive complex enhance cryptic transcription for transposon exclusion
authors: Zhihao ZhaiHaoyu HeTomoko NotoMingmei LiucongJialuo LiJulie SaksoukYike LiuXue WangYujie LiuKazufumi MochizukiMiao Tianahttps://ror.org/04rdtx186Key Laboratory of Evolution & Marine Biodiversity (Ministry of Education), and Institute of Evolution & Marine Biodiversity, Ocean University of China, Qingdao 266003, Chinabhttps://ror.org/051escj72Institute of Human Genetics, Genetics, Cell Biology and Development Department, CNRS, University of Montpellier, Montpellier 34090, France
abstract:
Suppression of transposable elements (TEs) is critical for maintaining genome integrity. The evolutionary arms race between TEs and their eukaryotic host organisms has driven the development of small RNA–dependent mechanisms that specifically suppress TEs while leaving non-TE regions unperturbed. In the binucleated ciliate
                     Tetrahymena 
                    , small RNAs (sRNAs) are generated from both TE and non-TE regions of the germline genome, whereas noncoding RNAs (ncRNAs) from the TE-free somatic genome target and eliminate non-TE sRNAs, thereby selectively preserving TE-specific sRNAs for guiding TE recognition. Since sRNAs are produced from both strands, the counteracting ncRNAs must also occur bidirectionally. However, the mechanism by which the somatic genome generates ncRNAs from both strands remains unresolved. Here, we show that these ncRNAs arise from widespread cryptic transcription initiated outside canonical promoters and dependent on the developmentally specific Mediator complex–associated proteins Dima1 and Emit2. We further demonstrate that sRNA-guided recruitment of the
                     Tetrahymena 
                    Polycomb repressive complex 2 and Dima1 occupancy are mutually reinforcing, promoting local accumulation of RNA polymerase II, which may facilitate cryptic transcription from these loci in a histone methyltransferase-independent manner. Disruption of Dima1 abolishes cryptic transcription, leads to aberrant accumulation of non-TE sRNAs, and results in erroneous genome elimination and cell death. These findings reveal a regulatory circuit involving sRNAs, Polycomb, and the Mediator-associated protein Dima1 that promotes cryptic transcription, thereby ensuring accurate TE exclusion and genome integrity.

title: Connexins are essential for the contribution of latent progenitors to healing after spinal cord injury
authors: María Victoria FalcoGabriela FabbianiDaniel PrietoMateo VidalMilagros BenítezMaría Inés RehermannMaría Constanza SilveraRenata SimeoneFederico F. TrigoRaúl E. Russoahttps://ror.org/05b50ej63Departamento de Neurofisiología Celular y Molecular, División Neurociencias, Instituto de Investigaciones Biológicas Clemente Estable, Montevideo CP11600, Uruguaybhttps://ror.org/05b50ej63Departamento de Señalización Neuronal y Glial, División Neurociencias, Instituto de Investigaciones Biológicas Clemente Estable, Montevideo CP11600, Uruguay
abstract:
Gap junctions are important regulators of the biology of neural stem cells. Both in vertebrates with regenerative abilities and neonatal rodents, ependymal cells communicate via connexin (Cx) 43 and Cx26. Gap junction coupling and Cx26 are down-regulated as the ependyma becomes quiescent in adulthood, but injury overrules this developmental down-regulation suggesting a role for Cx signaling in the reactivation of ependymal cells. However, direct evidence of the involvement of these Cxs in the reactivation of the ependymal stem cell niche is lacking. Here, we aim to explore the role of Cx26 and Cx43 in the response of ependymal cells to injury by means of specific genetic deletion. We find that Cx26 is critical for the proliferative response of ependymal cells to injury. The reduced response of ependymal cells by Cx26 deletion increased the extension of the lesion because of impaired healing resulting from a weak contribution of the ependymal stem cell niche. On the other hand, Cx43—via gap junction coupling and hemichannels—plays a key role in the communication of Ca
                     2+ 
                    signals between ependymal cells induced by activation of P2X7 receptors. Our data show that Cxs are relevant targets to manipulate the ependymal stem cell niche to achieve better healing after spinal cord injury.

title:
Lhx9 
                    specifically modulates phalanx number, whereas
                     Lhx2 
                    constrains digit length in tetrapods
authors: Yining TangShibin BaiShanshan LiYing MaoWanyi DangHuiling XueSongyang ShangZiqiu JiaXiaoping LiYanlei LiuXiaona XuDavid M. IrwinJunpeng ZhangShuyi ZhangZhe Wangahttps://ror.org/01n7x9n08College of Animal Science and Veterinary Medicine, Shenyang Agricultural University, Shenyang 110866, Chinabhttps://ror.org/02bzkv281School of Basic Medical Science, Chengde Medical University, Chengde 067000, Hebei, Chinachttps://ror.org/03dbr7087Department of Laboratory Medicine and Pathobiology, University of Toronto, Toronto, ON M5S 1A8, Canada
abstract:
Most nonmammalian tetrapods exhibit more than three phalanges in their posterior digits (III–V), whereas mammals are restricted to no more than three. So far, the molecular mechanism underlying this evolutionary reduction and the functions of
                     Lhx2 
                    and
                     Lhx9 
                    in digit development remain unclear. Here we show divergent evolution of
                     Lhx2 
                    and
                     Lhx9 
                    expression patterns in embryonic limbs across tetrapods. We further demonstrate that although ectopic overexpression of each gene in chick embryos delayed limb skeletal development, only
                     Lhx9 
                    reduced the phalanx number in the posterior digits. Transcriptomic analysis showed that
                     Lhx2 
                    regulates pathways for chondrocyte and osteoblast differentiation, and
                     Lhx9 
                    preferentially influences skeletal segmentation via the bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) pathway. The unique function and differential expression of
                     Lhx9 
                    in the limb buds between mammals and nonmammalian tetrapods suggest it may have acquired a role in suppressing phalanx number, driving the evolutionary reduction of phalanx number in mammals.

title: CX3CL1 (fractalkine)–CX3CR1 interface drives CD8⁺ T cell–induced neurodegeneration in human brain organoids
authors: Woo Sub YangMin Sun ShinMu Seog ChoeFerdi Ridvan KiralJumee KimHong-Jai ParkMario FelixLais OsmaniIn-Hyun ParkInsoo KangaDepartment of Genetics, Interdepartmental Neuroscience Program, Yale Stem Cell Center, Yale Child Study Center, Wu Tsai Institute, Yale School of Medicine, New Haven, CT 06520bDepartment of Internal Medicine, Section of Rheumatology, Allergy & Immunology, Yale School of Medicine, New Haven, CT 06520chttps://ror.org/00vvvt117College of Pharmacy, Sookmyung Women’s University, Seoul 04310, Republic of KoreadDepartment of Pathology, Yale School of Medicine, New Haven, CT 06520
abstract:
Immune–neuron interactions play a critical role in neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer’s disease (AD), but how CD8⁺ T cells contribute to brain pathology remains poorly understood. Amyloid-β (Aβ), a hallmark of AD, is known to trigger neuronal stress and inflammation. Here, we established a human cortical organoid (hCO) model to investigate CD8⁺ T cell responses to Aβ-induced neurodegenerative stress. Aβ exposure increased neuronal expression of CX3CL1 (fractalkine), which engages its receptor CX3CR1 on CD8⁺ T cells. Transwell migration assays showed enhanced recruitment of CX3CR1⁺ CD8⁺ T cells toward Aβ-treated hCOs. In parallel, Aβ upregulated IL-15 expression, a cytokine that supports CD8⁺ T cell activation. The infiltration of CD8⁺ T cells led to neuronal injury, marked by MAP2 loss and cleaved Caspase-3 activation, accompanied by an increase in gene signatures for cell death and inflammation. Exposure to the conditioned medium of activated CX3CR1
                     high 
                    CD8⁺ T cell recapitulated this damage, and the neutralization of CD8
                     + 
                    T cell cytokines and cytotoxic molecules rescued the phenotype. These findings identify the CX3CL1–CX3CR1 axis and CD8⁺ T cell effector programs as drivers of neurotoxicity and establish brain organoids as a platform to study immune-driven neurodegeneration.

title:
Gut microbiota vesicle reprogramming by
                     Ganoderma lucidum 
                    polysaccharide alleviates mycoplasmal pneumonia via the gut–lung axis
authors: Zimu ZhangHanfei GongZhenzhen ZhangPing YingChao ZhangWenjun XuLingyi Kongahttps://ror.org/01as92r37Joint International Research Laboratory of Target Discovery and New Drug Innovation, Ministry of Education, State Key Laboratory of Natural Medicines, and Jiangsu Key Laboratory of Bioactive Natural Product Research, China Pharmaceutical University, Nanjing 211198, Chinabhttps://ror.org/001f9e125Institute of Veterinary Medicine, Jiangsu Academy of Agricultural Sciences, Nanjing 210014, ChinacGuo’Tai (Taizhou) Center of Technology Innovation for Veterinary Biologicals, Taizhou 225300, Chinadhttps://ror.org/0418kp584Modern Industrial College of Traditional Chinese Medicine and Health, Lishui University, Lishui 323000, China
abstract:
Respiratory infections remain a major global health challenge, further compounded by antibiotic resistance. Among these, mycoplasmal pneumonia represents a particularly prevalent and refractory form. Here, using targeted enzymatic fragmentation combined with multidimensional NMR analysis, we resolved the structure of a homogeneous
                     Ganoderma lucidum 
                    polysaccharide, GLFP2, and identified β-(1→6)-linked galactosyl motifs as key structural features. Despite minimal systemic absorption, oral GLFP2 alleviated mycoplasmal pneumonia in mice. Instead, GLFP2 reshaped the gut microbiota and functionally reprogrammed gut microbiota-derived extracellular vesicles (GMEVs), whose transplantation alone was sufficient to confer pulmonary protection. Orally administered GMEVs remained bioactive, showed systemic exposure, associated with the lung, and were preferentially taken up by alveolar macrophages. These vesicles activated AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) signaling, suppressed the S100A8/A9 inflammatory axis, and limited neutrophil-driven immunopathology. Collectively, these findings identify microbiota-derived vesicles as effectors of gut–lung communication and use a defined polysaccharide to uncover a remote protective mechanism against pneumonia.

title: Ecological, physiological, and evolutionary drivers of stoichiometry in insects
authors: Léo LaborieuxRichard J. KnechtWilliam F. FaganNathan J. SandersAnshuman Swainahttps://ror.org/00jmfr291Department of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology, University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, MI 48109bhttps://ror.org/00jmfr291Museum of Paleontology, University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, MI 48109chttps://ror.org/047s2c258Department of Biology, University of Maryland, College Park, MD 20742
abstract: The elemental composition of organisms links physiology to biogeochemical cycles, yet the relative contributions of evolutionary divergence, ecology, and allometry to stoichiometric variation remain incompletely resolved. Here, we integrate a global insect stoichiometric database spanning 223 species with a comprehensive phylogenetic backbone to evaluate the relative importance of hypothesized ecophysiological drivers of carbon (C), nitrogen (N), and phosphorus (P) stoichiometry within a multivariate framework. We found a strong phylogenetic signal in stoichiometric ratios and in P and N content, with evolutionary divergence (phylogenetic structure) accounting for approximately half of the explained variation in P-based ratios, exceeding the contribution of any individual ecological predictor. Phylogenetically corrected models recover trophic enrichment across successive trophic levels, consistent with previously documented patterns, and positive scaling between body mass and both C:P and N:P, in line with the general predictions of the Growth Rate Hypothesis. Temperature was the strongest ecological predictor of insect stoichiometry, with positive effects on C:P and N:P ratios and a negative effect on C:N, highlighting the thermal underpinnings of previously observed geographic patterns. Finally, our models recover higher P and lower C in terrestrial insects relative to their aquatic counterparts, contrary to classic expectations that invoke differences in structural constraints and autotrophic composition across habitats. Together, our work shows that variation in insect stoichiometry emerges from the interacting influences of evolutionary divergence and ecological and physiological variation, which can be disentangled through appropriately scaled, phylogenetically informed analyses.

title: PLD1-driven oncogenic secretion creates a therapeutic vulnerability in chromosome 3q–amplified NSCLC
authors: Xiaochao TanShike WangSieun LeeGuan-Yu XiaoDerrick L. CardinDakai ZhangYuting XuChao WuBiyao ZhouWilliam K. RussellGuangwei DuaSection of Hematology and Medical Oncology, Department of Medicine, Tulane University School of Medicine, New Orleans, LA 70112bhttps://ror.org/03gds6c39Department of Integrative Biology and Pharmacology, University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston McGovern Medical School, Houston, TX 77030chttps://ror.org/02k3smh20Department of Toxicology and Cancer Biology, The University of Kentucky, Lexington, KY 40536dhttps://ror.org/04twxam07Department of Thoracic/Head and Neck Medical Oncology, The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center, Houston, TX 77030ehttps://ror.org/016tfm930Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, The University of Texas Medical Branch, Galveston, TX 77555
abstract: Chromosome 3q (3q) amplification is a frequent event in non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and other cancer types, yet therapeutic strategies targeting oncogenic drivers within this amplicon have been unsuccessful. Our study revealed that the 3q amplicon encodes multiple Golgi-related proteins, including Phospholipase D1 (PLD1), which catalyzes the production of a potential oncogenic lipid, phosphatidic acid. We found that PLD1 is highly expressed in 3q-amplified NSCLC (3q-NSCLC) and its enzymatic activity is further boosted by coamplified PLD1 activator, ARF-like GTPase 14. High PLD1 activity is essential for 3q-NSCLC growth and metastasis. Mechanistically, PLD1 drives secretion of oncogenic factors via the carriers from the trans Golgi network to the cell surface pathway to support tumor growth. Transferrin receptor 1 (TFRC), which encodes a membrane protein, is coamplified with PLD1 and overexpressed in 3q-NSCLC. A TFRC antibody–drug conjugate (ADC) carrying a PLD1 inhibitor exhibited potential antitumor activity in mouse models. These findings establish PLD1 as a promoter of 3q-NSCLC and provide proof of concept for the development of PLD1-targeted therapies, including ADC-based approaches, for this challenging cancer subtype.

title: Transient ATM inhibition enhances knock-in efficiency in hematopoietic stem cells by attenuating the DNA damage response
authors: Munkh-Erdene NatsagdorjHiromasa HaraKohei IidaYuji KashiwakuraNemekhbayar BaatartsogtEnkhzaya GanzorigDaniele CanaruttoSandra PinhoLuigi NaldiniTsukasa OhmoriYutaka HanazonoFumio Nakaharaahttps://ror.org/010hz0g26Division of Regenerative Medicine, Center for Molecular Medicine, Jichi Medical University, Shimotsuke 329-0498, Tochigi, Japanbhttps://ror.org/010hz0g26Laboratory of Regenerative and Cellular Medicine, Center for Development of Advanced Medical Technology, Jichi Medical University, Shimotsuke 329-0498, Tochigi, Japanchttps://ror.org/010hz0g26Division of Animal Resource Development, Center for Development of Advanced Medical Technology, Jichi Medical University, Shimotsuke 329-0498, Tochigi, Japandhttps://ror.org/010hz0g26Center for Experimental Medicine, Jichi Medical University, Shimotsuke 329-0498, Tochigi, Japanehttps://ror.org/010hz0g26Department of Biochemistry, School of Medicine, Jichi Medical University, Shimotsuke 329-0498, Tochigi, Japanfhttps://ror.org/006x48140San Raffaele Telethon Institute for Gene Therapy, Istituto di Ricovero e Cura a Carattere Scientifico San Raffaele Scientific Institute, Milan 20132, Italyghttps://ror.org/01gmqr298Faculty of Medicine and Surgery, Faculty of Medicine and Surgery, Vita-Salute San Raffaele University, Milan 20132, Italyhhttps://ror.org/02mpq6x41Department of Pharmacology and Regenerative Medicine, University of Illinois at Chicago, Chicago, IL 60612ihttps://ror.org/010hz0g26Translational Research Laboratory, Center for Development of Advanced Medical Technology, Jichi Medical University, Shimotsuke 329-0498, Tochigi, Japan
abstract: Precise genome editing in hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) holds great potential for treating inherited blood disorders; however, low knock-in (KI) efficiency and loss of functional HSCs after genome editing remain major obstacles. Here, we demonstrate that transient inhibition of Ataxia-Telangiectasia Mutated (ATM) kinase markedly enhanced KI efficiency in mouse HSCs genome-edited with Cas9/ribonucleoprotein (RNP) and AAV donor DNA. Phosphoproteomic and capillary western blot analyses revealed that ATM inhibition suppressed aberrant Cas9-AAV-induced ATM activation and the subsequent DNA damage response, reduced p53-dependent apoptosis, and enhanced survival of KI HSCs. In serial transplantation assays, ATM inhibition preserved long-term engrafting KI HSCs, increasing their frequency from ~0.3 to 40% in secondary recipients, an over 100-fold improvement. Furthermore, in an X-linked severe combined immunodeficient mouse model, ATM inhibition increased KI efficiency and restored T- and B cell differentiation. Comprehensive safety analyses, including long-read nanopore sequencing, amplicon deep sequencing, whole genome sequencing and clonal tracking, did not detect increased genomic alterations, chromosomal abnormalities, or clonal expansion following transient ATM inhibition. Taken together, these findings establish transient ATM inhibition as an effective strategy to enhance KI-mediated genome editing while maintaining the long-term repopulating capacity of HSCs.

title: In This Issue
Multiancestry conditional and joint analysis applied to GWAS summary statistics
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Conditional and joint (COJO) analysis of genome-wide association study (GWAS) data is a standard post-GWAS analysis for identifying statistically independent associations. Although GWAS meta-analyses are increasingly conducted across multiple ancestry groups, the optimal strategy for multiancestry COJO analysis remains unclear. Here we introduce Manc-COJO, a method for multiancestry COJO analysis. Simulations and real-data analyses show that Manc-COJO improves detection of independent association signals while reducing false positives compared with single-ancestry COJO implemented in genome-wide complex trait analysis (GCTA) and its ad-hoc multiancestry adaptations. We also introduce Manc-COJO:FIX, a follow-up algorithm to identify ancestry-specific independent associations. The C++ implementation of Manc-COJO is over 120-fold faster than GCTA-COJO and supports linkage disequilibrium references derived from either individual-level genotype data or pre-computed matrices, facilitating analyses when data sharing is limited.

title: Imputation of fluid intelligence to increase power for gene discovery
A systems perspective on monoallelic inborn errors of immunity
The landscape of gene loss and missense variation across the mammalian tree informs on gene essentiality
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Patterns of gene and sequence preservation across species provide insight into gene essentiality under natural selection. Here we developed two interspecies constraint metrics across 462 mammalian species: Gene Identity Score of Mammalian Orthologs (GISMO), which quantifies gene loss weighted by evolutionary distance to humans, and GISMO-mis, which measures missense constraint using the ratio of missense to synonymous variation across mammals. Both metrics are strongly correlated with human loss of function, missense and dosage constraint derived from large-scale sequencing studies, yet are largely independent of coding sequence length. GISMO and GISMO-mis identify essential genes missed by existing human-only metrics, particularly short genes. Genes in the most constrained deciles are enriched for rare variant associations in disorders linked to reduced fecundity, including schizophrenia, autism and neurodevelopmental disorders, and show strong enrichment for common variant heritability. These deciles also exhibit reduced copy number variation, consistent with dosage sensitivity. In addition, GISMO improves prioritization of recessive disease genes and captures signatures of homozygous selection across the mammalian tree. Taken together, GISMO and GISMO-mis leverage deep mammalian evolution to provide complementary, length-robust measures of gene essentiality that strengthen disease–gene prioritization and illuminate the selective forces shaping human biology.

title: MAKR6 integrates TMK and CAMEL/CANAR signalling for auxin canalization in Arabidopsis
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                    Adaptive plant development is orchestrated, among other means, by directional, intercellular transport of the phytohormone auxin. Self-organizing phenomena such as flexible vasculature formation depend on auxin canalization, which manifests as the gradual formation of auxin-transporting channels through feedback between auxin signalling and transport. Here we identify MAKR6 as a component of this feedback.
                     MAKR6 
                    transcripts accumulate in vascular cells and are tightly regulated by auxin via the Aux/IAA–ARF–WRKY23 transcriptional cascade. MAKR6 is required for auxin canalization-dependent processes, including leaf venation, vascular regeneration and de novo channel formation from local auxin sources. Mechanistically, MAKR6 interacts with the PIN1 auxin transporter and modulates its trafficking and polarization. MAKR6 also associates with and integrates TMK1/4 and CAMEL–CANAR, two key receptor-like kinase complexes involved in canalization. Together, our study establishes MAKR6 as a multifaceted regulator that couples transcriptional auxin signalling to PIN1 repolarization and coordinates multiple RLK-mediated pathways into a concerted process. This provides mechanistic insight into auxin canalization and exemplifies a framework for exploring similar regulatory nodes in other developmental contexts.

abstract: Summary: Wall-associated kinases (WAKs) and WAK-like kinases (WAKLs) are cell surface receptors that, among other functions, contribute to pathogen resistance. This review synthesizes genetic and signaling evidence to establish a model of WAK and WAKL function in plant disease resistance, including ligand perception and activation of defense networks. Additionally, we discuss strategies for engineering WAKs and WAKLs to improve durable disease resistance in crops.

title: Trait-Informed Machine Learning Improves Precise Genomic Selection and Hybrid Design in Wheat
abstract: Short Summary: We developed GLRS, a trait-informed marker selection framework that reduces 570,441 SNPs to a few hundred per trait, lowering genotyping requirements while improving genomic prediction accuracy in wheat. GLRS was validated in 1,163 breeding lines and 292 F1 combinations, which supports accurate selection of elite pure lines and superior hybrid combinations, and significantly improves breeding efficiency in wheat.

title: The RNA binding protein RGGA acts as a sugar-responsive cofactor of the 5'-3' exoribonuclease XRN4 to function in selective mRNA degradation and post-transcriptional regulation of plant growth
abstract: Short Summary: RGGA, an RGG-repeat RNA-binding protein, interacts with the 5'-3' exoribonuclease XRN4 to promote selective degradation of mRNAs involved in sugar transport/metabolism, chlorophyll biosynthesis, and root development. In rgga mutants, these transcripts have longer half-lives and higher steady-state levels; disrupting RGGA–XRN4 prevents their decay and robustly upregulates these mRNAs, enhancing growth under exogenous sucrose. This study reveals RGGA as a sugar-responsive cofactor that directs XRN4-mediated mRNA turnover to modulate carbon allocation and plant growth.

title: Wheat TaHGH1/HSFA2D integrates temperature and gravity signals to control starch granule biogenesis and auxin asymmetry for shaping shoot architecture plasticity
abstract: Short summary: TaHGH1/HSFA2D, a wheat HSFA2 transcription factor, integrates temperature and gravity signals to control shoot architecture plasticity. Gravity- and heat-induced transcription and cold-induced alternative splicing of TaHGH1 modulate its functional protein levels, while TaHGH1 promotes starch granule biogenesis and directly activates TaLAX3 and TaARF19 to establish asymmetric auxin distribution and differential cell elongation. These findings reveal a molecular module that links starch biogenesis and auxin asymmetry to adaptive shoot architecture in winter wheat.

abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Multifunctional neuromorphic hardware has emerged as a promising paradigm to transcend the physical separation of sensing, memory, and computing inherent in traditional von Neumann architectures. The central challenge lies in developing integrated devices with high functional density for in‐situ fusion of sensing, memory, and computing. Here, we propose a multifunctional vertical bulk‐heterojunction transistor (MVBT) based on amorphous GaO
                     x 
                    dielectric layer, integrating four functions within a single device: deep‐ultraviolet (DUV) photodetection, threshold neuronal firing, broadband optoelectronic synaptic function, and reconfigurable logic gates. In the two‐terminal (gate‐source) mode, the ultraviolet‐selective photoresponse and electrochemical reactions of amorphous gallium oxide (a‐GaO
                     x 
                    ) enable deep‐ultraviolet photodetection and neuronal firing, respectively. In the three‐terminal mode, the organic bulk‐heterojunction active layer supports broadband optoelectronic synaptic function from ultraviolet to near‐infrared wavelengths. Asymmetric interfacial carrier‐injection barriers further enable bias‐reconfigurable AND/OR logic functions. In addition, a pixelated MVBT array demonstrates dual‐mode image sensing and visual preprocessing. Building upon these multifunctional capabilities, an MVBT‐based convolutional spiking neural network (CSNN) hybrid simulation architecture achieves a fingerprint recognition accuracy of 97.4%. This work provides a new strategy for constructing high‐functional‐density neuromorphic hardware integrating sensing, memory, computing, and decision‐making.

title: Astrocytic Ketogenesis Protects Central Nervous System Injury via CPT1A Stabilization and Epigenetic Regulation
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Following central nervous system (CNS) injury, reactive astrocytes proliferate and encapsulate the lesion to facilitate repair. However, the specific metabolic characteristics remain unknown. Here, through integrated single‐cell and spatial transcriptomics, we uncovered a subset of astrocytes that undergo enhanced lipid and ketone metabolic reprogramming following spinal cord injury (SCI). The ketone body β‐hydroxybutyrate (β‐OHB) inhibited autophagic degradation of carnitine‐palmitoyltransferase‐1A (CPT1A) via P300‐mediated lysine β‐hydroxybutyrylation (Kbhb). Astrocyte‐specific deletion of
                     Cpt1a 
                    led to impaired wound healing, reduced axonal sparing and worsened locomotor recovery after SCI, effects rescued by exogenous β‐OHB. Mechanistically, ketogenesis promotes wound repair and lipid metabolic reprogramming, forming a positive feedback loop via H3K9bhb‐dependent epigenetic remodeling in astrocytes after SCI. Furthermore, ketogenic diet (KD) promoted tissue repair across multiple CNS injury models. Clinically, elevated β‐OHB levels were associated with better tissue preservation and functional recovery in SCI patients. Collectively, our findings underscore the critical role of astrocytic lipid metabolic and epigenetic reprogramming after CNS injury and identify KD as a promising therapeutic strategy.

title: Synergistic Effects of Separator Architecture and Electrolyte Chemistry on the Electrochemical Stability of Lithium Ion Batteries With Li–Mn Rich Cathodes and µ‐Si Anodes
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    High‐voltage, high‐capacity lithium ion batteries (LIBs) combining cobalt‐free lithium manganese‐rich (LMR) cathodes with pure silicon (µ‐Si) anodes offer a promising route toward more sustainable and cost‐effective energy storage. In this study, the capacity fading behavior of LMR||µ‐Si cells is correlated with the poor wettability of the conventional polyolefin Celgard 2500 separator, which leads to non‐uniform electrolyte distribution and localized Li metal deposition on the µ‐Si surface. Consequently, cells with Celgard separators exhibit rapid degradation, with capacity roll‐over occurring after less than 75 cycles. In contrast, replacing Celgard 2500 with an electrospun polyacrylonitrile (PAN) membrane enhances cycling stability, retaining 80% of the initial capacity after approximately 230 cycles, due to improved electrolyte wetting and mechanical contact with µ‐Si anode. Further optimization of the electrolyte composition, using
                     N, N 
                    ‐dimethylsulfamoyl fluoride (DMFSA) as co‐solvent with fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC), extends LMR||µ‐Si cell lifetime to more than 400 cycles, regardless of the separator type. These findings highlight the synergistic influence of separator selection and electrolyte formulation in stabilizing interphases at both electrodes. A holistic materials design approach is therefore essential for advancing the performance and durability of next‐generation LMR||µ‐Si‐based LIBs cells.

title: Interfacial Polarization Dynamics of Nitrile Dipoles in Organic Synaptic Transistors for Acoustic Reservoir Computing
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Polar polymer interlayers have emerged as core functional layers in organic synaptic transistors (OSTs), enabling diverse neuromorphic behaviors through interfacial dipolar polarization and relaxation. However, the interfacial dipolar mechanisms governing memory window (ΔV) formation and modulation remain insufficiently understood. Here, polyacrylonitrile (PAN) is selected as a representative polar polymer interlayer to exploit nitrile (CN) dipolar relaxation for temporal acoustic reservoir computing (RC). It is found that the ΔV varies nonmonotonically with PAN concentration, suggesting a dipolar competition mechanism between interfacial polarization strength and dipole relaxation capability. Accordingly, dipolar relaxation underpins multiscale synaptic responses and fading memory for temporal RC. The device further exhibits stable and symmetric weight updates, with a low asymmetry ratio (AR) of 5.06% and cycle‐to‐cycle variations (CCVs) below 1%. Notably, the PAN‐OST operates with an ultralow event energy of 50 aJ while maintaining a high signal‐to‐noise ratio (SNR) of 50.47 dB. The PAN reservoir achieves 97.17% accuracy in spoken digit recognition and a maximum accuracy of 94.8% in the more challenging speech emotion recognition. Overall, this work establishes an interfacial polarization‐driven pathway for energy‐efficient neuromorphic computing and next‐generation intelligent hardware.

title: Hypothalamic POMC Neurons Gate the Fear‐Feeding Trade‐Off
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   To survive, animals must constantly balance the need to obtain food with the need to avoid danger. Feeding is essential, yet perceived danger shifts priority toward safety and transiently suppresses food intake, even when organisms are hungry. Hypothalamic pro‐opiomelanocortin (POMC) neurons align metabolic outputs with energy demands and control feeding. However, the role of POMC neurons in determining the trade‐off between feeding and threat responses remains unclear. Here, fasted mice are exposed to a fear‐conditioning paradigm to examine how POMC neurons influence the choice between feeding and defensive behaviors. Behavioral analyses combined with chemogenetic, neuroanatomical, and molecular approaches show that activation of POMC neurons suppresses feeding during a learned threat and it is associated with corticotropin releasing hormone (CRH) neuron–dependent activation of the hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal (HPA) axis. These effects require cannabinoid type 1 receptor (CB1R) signaling in POMC neurons, uncovering a POMC–CB1R pathway that tunes behavioral flexibility under a perceived threat. Collectively, the data identify POMC neurons as key integrators of metabolic and stress signals that bias decision making between feeding and threat‐avoidance behaviors.

title: Mechanism of Direct Acoustic Construction and Gradient Properties Tuning
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Despite the effectiveness of microstructured elastomers for force sensing, current fabrication methods struggle to precisely control the gradient properties of complex microstructures due to limited energy‐field flexibility, resulting in uniform performance that hinders high‐sensitivity sensing. Here, directed acoustic construction (DAC) technology is employed to fabricate fingerprint‐inspired elastomeric microstructures with intra‐layer gradient properties, and the underlying mechanisms of acoustic curing, particle reinforcement, and property tuning are revealed. The acoustic‐induced curing of polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) arises from synergistic physical, chemical, and mechanical effects. The incorporation of diamond particles into the PDMS matrix reinforces all three acoustic effects, thereby promoting polymerization and curing, which in turn broadens the tunable range of properties via acoustic waves. DAC enables omnidirectional patterning of microstructures and wide‐range gradient modulation, with feature sizes of approximately 200 µm. The resulting microstructure exhibits distinct inner–outer mechanical responses, producing a linear contact area–pressure relationship that enhances sensitivity and linearity. Compared with those of the uniform microstructures, the force sensing sensitivity is improved by 52.06%. When integrated onto a robotic fingertip as a functional sensing layer, it can distinguish fine textures and detect multidirectional forces. DAC enables site‐specific quantitative modulation and rapid fabrication (within 10 min), expanding its applications in micro/nanofabrication and flexible sensing.

title: MagGami: An Electromagnetic Origami Actuator With High Stiffness‐Switching Density for Lightweight Joint‐Space Wearable Haptics
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Kinesthetic feedback gloves play a central role in immersive virtual and augmented reality (VR/AR) by enabling the perception of object shape, stiffness, and spatial constraints. However, key challenges remain: 1) achieving a large stiffness contrast between free‐space and constrained‐space states, 2) enabling independent actuation on finger joints, and 3) maintaining lightweight, low‐power wearable operation. Here, we introduce MagGami, a miniaturized origami‐based variable‐stiffness actuator weighing 1.2 g for distributed joint‐space integration. By combining origami geometric interlocking with an electromagnetic bistable mechanism, it can be triggered by transient current pulses at the flattened 0° configuration of the origami mechanism. MagGami switches from a freely compliant state to a self‐locked high‐resistance state with a mean locking response time of 102.8 ms, while requiring no coil power to hold the locked state. The mean device‐level locked‐to‐free effective rotational‐stiffness ratio is 795.46, corresponding to a module‐level stiffness‐switching density of 6.63 × 10
                     5 
                    kg
                     − 
                     1 
                    , and the specified switching cycle consumes 444 mJ. MagGami uses distributed joint‐space actuation to deliver lightweight, independently addressable binary constraint cues at individual finger joints, thereby enhancing the perception of virtual spatial constraints and high‐resistance contact in VR/AR interactions. This work demonstrates a compact and energy‐efficient strategy for next‐generation wearable haptic interfaces.

title: Hybrid Semi‐Transparent Perovskite‐Photovoltaics and Concentrated Solar‐Thermal Harvesting Collectors
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Photovoltaics and solar thermal collectors each face limitations in efficiently harnessing solar energy. This study presents a hybrid semi‐transparent perovskite‐photovoltaic and concentrating solar thermal (SPV‐CST) collector designed to maximize solar energy utilization through spectral splitting. The perovskite solar cell captures both diffuse and direct solar irradiance, converting shorter‐wavelength sunlight into electricity while transmitting the near‐infrared spectrum. The SPV‐CST collector achieves effective thermal decoupling between the photovoltaic and thermal components. Specifically, the lens concentrates the transmitted light onto a solar‐thermal collector, producing heat at temperatures ranging from 88.0°C to 154.9°C. Meanwhile, the operating temperature of the perovskite solar cell is limited to 38.5°C to reduce thermal stability issues and preserve its electrical efficiency at 13.8%. Using state‐of‐the‐art semi‐transparent perovskite cells from the literature, the SPV‐CST collector is projected to improve its electrical efficiency from 13.8% to 21.3%, with only a slight reduction in thermal efficiency from 20.7% to 19.2% at 100°C output temperature. This work provides insights into the design, modeling, and operational optimization of hybrid solar collectors, paving the way for sustainable solar energy applications across diverse conditions and climates.

title: Black Silicon for Solar Fuels
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Photoelectrochemical (PEC) solar energy conversion offers a promising route for transforming sunlight into chemical fuels and value‐added products through light‐driven redox reactions at semiconductor–electrolyte interfaces. Among semiconductor photoabsorbers, black silicon (b‐Si) is particularly attractive because its micro‐/nanostructured surface enables ultralow reflectance, broadband light absorption, a large electrode–electrolyte interfacial area, and versatile integration of catalysts and protective layers. These characteristics allow b‐Si to combine effective photon management with interfacial reaction engineering, making it relevant to a broad range of PEC processes. This review first introduces the fundamental characteristics of b‐Si and summarizes representative fabrication methods, with emphasis on the relationships among processing, morphology, and physicochemical properties. It then examines how these properties affect PEC water splitting, nitrate reduction, nitrogen reduction, and carbon dioxide reduction. Particular attention is given to the roles of surface morphology, junction design, passivation, catalyst integration, charge separation and transport, and the local reaction environment in governing activity, selectivity, and stability. Finally, the major limitations of b‐Si‐based PEC systems—including charge‐carrier recombination, photocorrosion, parasitic reactions, and mass‐transport constraints—are critically assessed. On this basis, future research directions are proposed for developing reaction‐adaptive b‐Si photoelectrodes capable of efficient, selective, durable, and practically relevant solar‐fuel and chemical production.

title: The Characteristics of Tumor Microenvironment by the Single Cell Profile in Endometrial Cancer of no Specific Molecular Profile (NSMP) Subtype
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Endometrial cancer (EC) of no specific molecular profile (NSMP) subtype lacks specific molecular features, and the relationship of tumor microenvironment (TME) and relapse in NSMP EC remains incompletely understood. This study integrates single‐nucleus RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and multiplex immunohistochemistry to elucidate the TME and mechanisms of relapse in NSMP EC. The results showed reduced immune infiltration and increased immune‐suppressive cells, including SPP1+ macrophages and regulatory T cells (Tregs) in NSMP EC. More epithelial cell clusters with high stemness scores are observed in primary NSMP EC tumors collected before recurrence. In NSMP EC, tip endothelial cells and MMP11+ LEF1+ cancer‐associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are linked with angiogenesis and epithelial‐mesenchymal transition, and CD4+ T cells remain in a stress‐response state and are functionally impaired. Interestingly, a subset of tumor‐associated macrophages (TAMs) characterized by SPP1 expression is discovered, which may remodel the tumor microenvironment by potentially promoting CD4+ T cells stress and maintaining epithelial cells stemness through SPP1‐CD44, thereby potentially contributing to the proliferation and migration of tumor cells, which has verified by in vitro experiments. This study advances the mechanistic understanding of recurrence‐related TME and provides a foundation for the development of personalized treatments for NSMP EC patients.

title: Pseudo‐Haptic Feedback: Multi‐Modal Approaches to Stiffness Perception and User Experience
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Pseudo‐haptics is a technique that creates the illusion of haptic sensations in virtual environments by leveraging visual feedback and the interplay between visual and haptic perception. Pseudo‐haptic feedback can enhance virtual reality interactions by providing perceptual cues that substitute for or complement physical haptic feedback. This work extends a 3D deformation rendering approach to generate visual deformation cues for stiffness perception in virtual reality and evaluates their impact on user experience through a user study measuring presence and workload. Results from a user study () indicate that deformation cues support stiffness perception at levels comparable to physical haptic feedback in both objective and subjective measures. Combining pseudo‐haptic and force feedback further enhances stiffness perception accuracy and presence without increasing workload. These findings demonstrate that well‐designed pseudo‐haptic feedback mechanisms can effectively complement or substitute for force feedback in virtual reality interactions.

title: VCP‐Regulated LMF2 Stabilizes the Cholesterol Biosynthesis Enzyme HMGCS1 to Drive Cancer Progression and Confer Capecitabine Resistance in Triple‐Negative Breast Cancer
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Triple‐negative breast cancer (TNBC) is the most therapeutically challenging breast cancer subtype owing to its aggressive nature and lack of effective targeted therapies. Here, we identify lipase maturation factor 2 (LMF2), a previously uncharacterized gene in human cancer, as a novel oncogenic driver that promotes tumor growth, metastasis, and resistance to capecitabine in TNBC both in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, LMF2 localizes predominantly to the endoplasmic reticulum membrane and is targeted for autophagic degradation mediated by the autophagy receptor NBR1. Valosin‐containing protein (VCP) counteracts this process to stabilize LMF2 by impeding the LMF2‐NBR1 interaction, and pharmacological inhibition of VCP effectively suppressed LMF2‐driven TNBC progression and capecitabine resistance. LMF2, in turn, disrupts the interaction between the autophagy receptor NDP52 and HMGCS1, the rate‐limiting enzyme in cholesterol biosynthesis, thereby shielding HMGCS1 from autophagic degradation and enhancing cholesterol production. Importantly, re‐expression of HMGCS1 or exogenous cholesterol supplementation partially rescued the malignant and chemoresistant phenotypes impaired by LMF2 depletion. Clinically, the VCP‐LMF2‐HMGCS1 axis is significantly co‐upregulated in TNBC patient specimens. Collectively, these findings unveil a previously unrecognized VCP‐LMF2‐HMGCS1 regulatory axis that drives TNBC progression and chemoresistance, and identify LMF2 as a promising therapeutic target for this recalcitrant disease.

title: Skyrmion Bubbles by Design in a Centrosymmetric Kagome Magnet
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Topologically protected nanoscale spin textures, such as magnetic skyrmions, have attracted significant interest for spintronics applications. While skyrmions in noncentrosymmetric materials are known to be stabilized by the Dzyaloshinskii‐Moriya interaction (DMI), their deliberate design in centrosymmetric materials remains a challenge. This difficulty largely stems from the complexity of controlling magnetocrystalline anisotropy–a critical factor in the absence of DMI. Here, we demonstrate the chemical tuning of magnetocrystalline anisotropy in the centrosymmetric Kagome magnet . The resulting compound exhibits a spin reorientation transition accompanied by an emergent skyrmion bubble lattice, confirmed by cryogenic Lorentz transmission electron microscopy and cryogenic Lorentz differential phase contrast scanning transmission electron microscopy. Our findings overcome a key materials design challenge and open possibilities for deliberate design of skyrmionic textures in centrosymmetric systems.

title:
Chiral‐Nematic Lattice Instability in Charge Density Wave of 1
                     T 
                    ‐TiSe
                     2
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Chiral charge‐density waves (CDWs) are a rare form of electronic order with handedness, enabling novel couplings among light, lattice, and topology in quantum materials. Yet the microscopic origin of chirality has remained elusive, even in the prototypical chiral CDW system 1
                     T 
                    ‐TiSe
                     2 
                    . Using ab initio calculations, we investigate the structural stability and electronic structure of competing CDW models in 1
                     T 
                    ‐TiSe
                     2 
                    . We show that a chiral monoclinic () structure is stabilized by the cooperative condensation of multiple phonon modes and reproduces the chiral topography and energy gap observed experimentally. We further find an exceptionally soft potential landscape around this energy‐minimized structure, along the direction that removes the remaining rotational symmetry, allowing the lattice to fluctuate through fully asymmetric configurations while its average structure remains chiral. This dynamical chiral CDW naturally reconciles the chiral domains seen by time‐averaged topographic probes with the complete loss of symmetry detected by bulk spectroscopy, and clarifies how chiral CDWs emerge from the interplay of lattice instability and fluctuation.

title: Intrinsic i‐Wave Altermagnetism in 2D Graphene Superlattices
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Altermagnets feature unconventional magnetism due to their momentum‐dependent spin splitting purely driven by magnetic order, for which a variety of transition‐metal‐based ‐wave altermagnets have been proposed. However, carbon‐based altermagnets remain largely unexplored, even though magnetism of graphene nanostructures has been widely demonstrated. Here, through a comprehensive symmetry analysis, we establish a symmetry‐guided design principle for realizing higher‐order ‐wave altermagnetism in graphene antidot superlattices and demonstrate its emergence in both monolayer and bilayer graphene, particularly in the Bernal‐stacked bilayer. By combining atomistic tight binding models and first principles methods, we show the appearance of an interaction‐induced ‐wave altermagnetic splitting, originating from the intrinsic magnetic instability of 2D graphene antidot superlattices. Our work establishes a strategy to engineer ‐wave altermagnetism in a graphene platform, extending the materials landscape beyond conventional ‐wave altermagnets and putting forward a carbon‐based platform for higher‐order altermagnetic spintronics.

title: Coordination Chemistry of Single‐Atom Catalysts in Expediating Kinetics for Advanced Lithium‐Sulfur Batteries
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   The shuttling effect and sluggish conversion kinetics of lithium polysulfides (LiPSs) hinder the further advancement of lithium‐sulfur (Li‐S) batteries, exhibiting high barriers. Among catalysts, single‐atom catalysts (SACs) can accelerate LiPSs redox kinetics by leveraging M‐S coordination, interfacial charge transfer, and anchoring effect of coordinating heteroatoms. Numerous researches have reported improved catalytic activity via screening central metal and coordinating atoms as well as optimizing coordination configurations. However, systematic summary concerning the principles in screening and design of asymmetric coordination structures, the evolution mechanisms of orbital hybridization and spatial geometry, and the corresponding structure‐activity relationships governing LiPSs conversion kinetics remain unknown. In this review, we systematically summarize the modifications brought by asymmetric coordination chemistry and dual‐atom coordination structures in terms of geometric configuration engineering, molecular orbital hybridization, and interfacial charge rearrangement, together with the underlying mechanisms for boosting LiPSs conversion kinetics. Centered on theoretical calculations supplemented by experimental validations, we elaborate the critical significance of asymmetric coordination chemistry of SACs in elevating the catalytic efficiency. Finally, the future developments of SACs in Li─S batteries are outlooked and prospected.

title: Elastic Graphene‐Shell Architectures Enable Stress Regulation in High‐Capacity Lithium‐Ion Battery Electrodes
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Silicon‐based anodes are limited by large volume changes, stress accumulation, and sluggish kinetics during cycling. Porous electrode designs can alleviate these problems, but conventional approaches often rely on multistep processing or sacrificial pore formers. Here, hollow graphene‐shell (GS) spheres are introduced as slurry‐compatible pore‐engineering additives. In a 5–60–5 MPa pressure cycle, the SiO
                     x 
                    /GS electrode shows greater thickness recovery than pristine SiO
                     x 
                    , with thickness‐recovery indices of 4.18 and 1.24 percentage points, respectively. Individual GS particles show a largely recoverable response within the small‐displacement range probed by atomic force microscopy (AFM), with an apparent modulus of approximately 114 MPa. Upon full lithiation, the through‐plane thickness of the SiO
                     x 
                    /GS electrode increases by 15%, compared with 94% for pristine SiO
                     x 
                    . The SiO
                     x 
                    /GS electrode also retains approximately 702 mAh g
                     −1 
                    after 400 cycles at 1.6 A g
                     −1 
                    . GS improves the performance of the tested SiO
                     x 
                    /graphite, Si@C, and LiNi
                     0.8 
                    Co
                     0.1 
                    Mn
                     0.1 
                    O
                     2 
                    (NCM811) formulations as well. These results demonstrate a simple, slurry‐compatible strategy for accommodating electrode deformation while maintaining electrochemical performance.

title: MZF1 Inhibits TGFβ‐1/SMAD Signaling by Transcriptionally Activating SnoN to Augment Tumorigenic Potential in Colon Cancer
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Colon cancer progression is associated with transcriptional and signaling abnormalities. MZF1, linked to leukemogenesis, has an unclear role in colon cancer. This study examined its function in colon tumorigenesis and signaling‐targeted therapies. Multi‐omics (RNA‐seq, CUT&Tag) identified MZF1 targets, validated in vitro/in vivo using xenografts and epithelial‐specific MZF1 knockout mice. Virtual screening found MZF1 inhibitors. MZF1 activated SnoN transcription, suppressing TGF‐β/SMAD signaling. Overexpression enhanced proliferation and colony formation; knockdown reversed these. In vivo, MZF1‐overexpressing xenografts grew faster with more Ki67+ cells, while MZF1
                     −/− 
                    mice had reduced tumor burden. Organoids from MZF1
                     −/− 
                    mice grew poorly. 10Panx Acetate, an MZF1 inhibitor, disrupted MZF1‐SnoN interaction, inhibiting cell and xenograft growth. Our results indicate MZF1 as a key colon cancer regulator via SnoN‐mediated TGF‐β pathway suppression and suggest 10Panx Acetate for precision therapy. MZF1/SnoN co‐expression may predict aggressive disease.

title: Taxonomic, predicted functional, and network-based characterization of the breast cancer-associated gut microbiome

Contrasting
                     
                      CH
                       4 
                     
                    flux responses to distinct drought regimes and nitrogen enrichment in a temperate steppe
authors:
Lan Du, 
Jiatao Zhang, 
Yan Shen, 
Yonghong Luo, 
Jinbao Zhang, 
Ru Tian, 
Zhuwen Xu
abstract:
Summary 
                   
                     
                       
                         
                          Drought and nitrogen (N) deposition alter greenhouse gas fluxes, but how distinct drought scenarios interact with N enrichment to regulate the methane (CH
                           4 
                          ) sink remains poorly understood. We conducted a 4‐yr field experiment in a temperate steppe to examine CH
                           4 
                          fluxes under three drought regimes – early‐season intense drought (ID), mid‐season chronic drought (CD), and mid‐season reduced rainfall frequency (RF) – and N addition.
                         
                       
                       
                         
                          CH
                           4 
                          uptake and its driving mechanisms were assessed through field measurements and structural equation modeling, focusing on the interplay between soil physicochemical properties, microbial abundance, and plant‐mediated emissions.
                         
                       
                       
                         
                          All drought treatments reduced the CH
                           4 
                          sink with divergent temporal dynamics; reduced RF caused the most persistent reduction, while N addition alleviated the inhibitory effects of CD. These shifts were driven by distinct mechanisms: ID acted via lowering previous‐year belowground net primary productivity and increasing dissolved organic N, CD functioned through increased
                           Artemisia frigida 
                          cover and reduced arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal abundance, and RF suppressed uptake via the morphological expansion of
                           A. frigida 
                          .
                         
                       
                       
                         
                          We conclude that CH
                           4 
                          sink stability is highly sensitive to drought regime, and that the morphological expansion of specific plants such as
                           A. frigida 
                          may partially offset the soil CH
                           4 
                          sink.

title:
Evolutionary shifts to gynomonoecy correlate with changes in capitulum architecture in South African
                     
                       Helichrysum 
                     
                    (Asteraceae)
authors:
Zaynab Shaik, 
Nicola G. Bergh, 
Carme Blanco‐Gavaldà, 
G. Anthony Verboom
abstract:
Summary 
                   
                     
                       
                         
                          Gynomonoecy has evolved repeatedly in Asteraceae, suggesting selective advantages for species whose capitula combine pistillate and bisexual flowers. Theories invoking conspicuous peripheral flowers and achene heteromorphism do not account for gynomonoecy in the southern African‐centred genus
                           Helichrysum 
                          , which lacks both these features. We investigated whether gynomonoecy is associated with changes in capitulum architecture in South African
                           Helichrysum 
                          , focusing on flower packing density and achene size.
                         
                       
                       
                         
                          We compared flower packing density and achene size between hermaphroditic and gynomonoecious
                           Helichrysum 
                          species using phylogenetic generalised least squares and reconstructed ancestral sexual systems using a well‐sampled, time‐calibrated phylogeny.
                         
                       
                       
                         Gynomonoecious species produced nearly twice as many flowers per unit receptacle area as hermaphroditic species and had subtly but significantly smaller achenes. Ancestral‐state reconstruction strongly supported hermaphroditism as ancestral, with gynomonoecy originating independently 18 times. 
                       
                       
                         Our results provide the first phylogenetically informed evidence within a single Asteraceae genus that shifts to gynomonoecy correlate with shifts in capitulum architecture. The association between gynomonoecy, denser flower packing, and reduced achene size is consistent with the hypothesis that accentuated resource gradients within capitula and priority access to resources by first‐maturing peripheral flowers may have favoured the evolution of gynomonoecy.

title: CPK10 phosphorylates zinc‐sensing transcription factors bZIP19/23 to establish time‐delayed negative feedback in plant zinc homeostasis
authors:
Yuan Deng, 
Chenyue Yang, 
Yaru Wu, 
Yongke Zhou, 
Ying Chen, 
Cun Wang, 
Zhenqian Zhang, 
Chuanfeng Ju
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Zinc (Zn) homeostasis is essential for plant growth; yet, how zinc‐deficiency‐triggered calcium (Ca) signals are decoded into homeostatic adjustments remains elusive. Here, we identify the calcium‐dependent protein kinase 10 (CPK10) as a key decoder of zinc‐deficiency‐triggered Ca
                     2+ 
                    signals. Under zinc‐deficient conditions, both the protein level and the kinase activity of CPK10 increase. Subsequently, CPK10 interacts with and phosphorylates the zinc‐sensing transcription factors bZIP19 and bZIP23, thereby repressing their DNA‐binding and transcriptional activities. Zrt/Irt‐like protein (ZIP) family members are the primary transporters responsible for zinc uptake from the soil, and CPK10‐mediated phosphorylation of bZIP19 and bZIP23 reduces the expression of
                     ZIP1 
                    ,
                     ZIP4 
                    , and defensin‐like (DEFL) genes such as
                     DEFL208 
                    . CPK10 activation is time‐delayed, peaking at 72 h after zinc‐deficiency treatment, providing a braking mechanism that prevents prolonged high‐rate ion flux driven by sustained high‐level expression of zinc transporters. The CPK10‐targeted phosphorylation site Ser241 of bZIP19 is conserved in dicots but absent in monocots, suggesting evolutionary divergence in this zinc homeostasis‐regulatory module. Our work reveals a Ca
                     2+ 
                    –CPK10–bZIP19/23 module that mediates spatiotemporal control of zinc homeostasis, highlighting a key regulatory layer in plant nutrient signaling.
