abstract:
The crystalline structure, the atomic numbers of the constituent elementsand the size of MOF crystals each influence their photoluminescence and scintillation properties in distinct ways. Together, these factors provide valuable guidelines for designing systems with optimized performance and tunable timing characteristics, arising from the synergistic interplay of their components.








ABSTRACT
Metal‐organic framework (MOF) scintillators are promising emitters for fast timing techniques due to their high scintillation efficiency and rapid response time. These materials are composed of high‐atomic‐number metal‐oxide cores connected by scintillating organic dyes. A quite‐overlooked drawback of MOF scintillation properties is the possible presence of intrinsic structural defects and dark states that can introduce energetic disorder and also trap the energy released by the ionizing radiation. Here, we systematically investigate the luminescence properties of three different MOF architectures wherein the scintillating ligand is 9,10‐diphenylanthracene and the linking nodes consist of Zr, In and Hf‐oxo‐hydroxy clusters. The various crystalline structures, the atomic numbers of the constituent elements, and the size of MOF crystals affect their photoluminescence and scintillation properties in distinct ways, providing guidelines to develop systems with optimized performance and tailorable timing capabilities, resulting from the synergy among the properties of the components.

title: From topology to biological meaning: why plant family classification matters beyond systematics
abstract:
Conceptual framework for family‐level classification.







Summary
Plant family names are routinely used to structure comparative analyses, trait databases, floras, conservation assessments, and teaching. Yet, these names are not neutral labels: changing family boundaries changes the units across which biological patterns are compared, summarized, and interpreted. Modern phylogenetic inference resolves evolutionary relationships with increasing confidence, but it does not by itself determine which monophyletic groups should be recognized as families. We argue that this choice should be guided not only by monophyly, but also by diagnosability, biological interpretability, stability, and practical utility. Recent debates around large‐scale consensus classifications show why these criteria must be explicit. Recognizing classification as shared scientific infrastructure means that family delimitation matters not only to systematists, but to all plant scientists who rely on taxonomic units to formulate questions and communicate results.

title: Recent plant photosynthate as a driver of ecological and evolutionary processes
abstract:
Timeline of key eco-evolutionary outcomes arising from belowground allocation of recent plant photosynthate from shoots.
 
 
 Summary 
 Plants rapidly allocate carbon from photosynthesis belowground via root exudates and root-associated microorganisms. Here we synthesise recent evidence of our understanding of the consequences of this ‘fast’ pathway of recent photosynthate flux for major ecological and evolutionary processes. This rapid input of plant-derived carbon to soils shapes food webs and drives processes including soil CO 2  efflux, nutrient cycling, plant community dynamics, stability of symbioses and evolution of contrasting modes of nutrition, such as parasitism and mycoheterotrophy. We also highlight how seasonality and anthropogenic and natural perturbations likely determine the magnitude and dynamics of this fast pathway across major vegetation types, but these factors remain understudied. Further gaps in understanding include demonstrating causal links between photosynthate flow and key biogeochemical cycling processes and the capture of photosynthate by co-occurring root-associated microorganisms.

title: Pyrolyzed Photoresist as a Continuous‐Tone Mask for Grayscale Lithography
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Grayscale lithography enables single‐step fabrication of continuous 3D surface relief for complex optics, MEMS, and scalable replication templates. However, its broad adoption is hindered by the cost, complexity, and resolution constraints associated with fabricating high‐quality grayscale masks. Here, we address this challenge by developing a method to produce continuous‐tone photolithography masks/reticles through the pyrolysis of 2.5D photoresist structures fabricated using standard multiphoton lithography systems. During pyrolysis, the pattern densifies from micrometers in thickness in the resist state to nanometers in thickness in the carbon state. While the pyrolyzed patterns undergo significant vertical shrinkage, adhesion to the substrate is maintained, preserving overall lateral pattern fidelity despite a systematic in‐plane expansion. The amorphous carbon is chemically inert and mechanically robust, enabling repeated exposure and mask cleaning steps, converting the single‐use polymer pattern written via direct‐write technology into an optical mask capable of repeated exposures.

title: Persistent Photoluminescence Superlinearity Beyond Static Recombination Physics in Metal Halide Perovskites
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Persistent intermediate power‐law exponent (β) values in metal halide perovskites commonly occur across excitation regimes in which assignment to a single carrier‐population recombination limit becomes ambiguous. Their strong dependence on excitation conditions further indicates that excitation‐dependent photoluminescence cannot always be interpreted uniquely through a static Shockley‐Read‐Hall (SRH)‐bimolecular‐Auger recombination picture. Here, power‐dependent and time‐resolved photoluminescence measurements on methylammonium lead iodide (MAPbI
                     3 
                    , MA = CH
                     3 
                    ​NH
                     3 
                    ) thin films reveal correlated evolution of excitation scaling, delayed emission, and illumination‐history response under conditions that systematically modify vibrational dissipation and carrier‐relaxation pathways. These behaviors are described using a dual‐channel framework in which transient vibrational energy retention contributes to delayed radiative response. The results support an interpretation of PL superlinearity as an emergent, condition‐dependent response associated with coupled carrier‐lattice relaxation dynamics, rather than a simple transition between fixed recombination‐order limits. More broadly, these results show that β and photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) should not be treated as fixed intrinsic material constants, but as excitation‐conditioned observables shaped by the evolving relaxation environment, highlighting limitations in interpreting PL scaling laws as direct indicators of recombination pathways in soft semiconductors.

title:
Multiscale Regulation of Ru‐Based Catalysts for Upgrading Biomass‐Derived Levulinic Acid and Levulinates to
                     γ 
                    ‐Valerolactone: Mechanisms, Advances, and Challenges
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                     γ 
                    ‐Valerolactone (GVL) serves as a bridge connecting biomass‐derived levulinic acid (LA) and its esters to value‐added chemicals. Ru‐based catalysts exhibit high efficiency for LA/levulinates‐to‐GVL conversion, owing to their strong C═O activation ability, excellent GVL selectivity, and compatibility to diverse hydrogen sources such as H
                     2 
                    , formic acid (FA), and alcohols. Based on an analysis of the mechanisms, thermodynamics, and kinetics of this process, the review summarizes recent advances in the multiscale regulation of Ru‐based catalysts, covering electronic structure and Lewis/Brønsted acid sites, support structure, Ru particle size and dispersion, reaction conditions and solvent microenvironments, and resistance to deactivation. By integrating the two primary reaction pathways, rate‐determining steps (RDS), and reaction orders with respect to H
                     2 
                    , the adoption of these strategies is proposed to follow a streamlined workflow by 1) defining reaction system, 2) eliminating heat and mass transfer limitations, 3) identifying primary limiting factor of catalytic performances, and 4) selecting and validating optimization strategy. Additionally, a brief comparison with non‐noble metal (Ni‐, Cu‐, Co‐, and Zr‐based) catalysts further reveals the conditions that justify the higher cost of Ru. These frameworks identify key metrics for catalyst design, which are anticipated to advance the efficient conversion and utilization of biomass.

title:
Hepatocyte CBX2 Safeguards Hepatic Lipid Homeostasis by Elevating Ca
                     2+ 
                    ‐CaMKK2‐AMPK Signaling to Counter MASLD
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Metabolic dysfunction‐associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects approximately one‐third of adults and lacks effective pharmacological therapies. Here, we identify Chromobox 2 (CBX2), a Polycomb‐associated chromatin regulator, as a previously unrecognized regulator of hepatic lipid homeostasis. CBX2 expression is markedly reduced in hepatocytes from patients with MASLD, multiple mouse models (
                     db/db 
                    ,
                     ob/ob 
                    , HFD, and HFHC), and steatotic hepatocytes
                     in 
                     vitro 
                    . Hepatocyte‐specific CBX2 overexpression ameliorates hepatic steatosis, improves glucose metabolism, and suppresses inflammation, whereas CBX2 deficiency exacerbates these metabolic disturbances. Mechanistically, CBX2 enhances H3K4me3 enrichment at the
                     Orai1 
                    promoter, promoting
                     Orai1 
                    transcription and increasing intracellular Ca
                     2+ 
                    levels. Elevated Ca
                     2+ 
                    activates the CaMKK2‐AMPK signaling pathway, leading to ACC phosphorylation, inhibition of
                     de novo 
                    lipogenesis (FAS, ACC, and SCD‐1), enhancement of fatty acid oxidation (PPARα and CPT‐1a), and suppression of NF‐κB/JNK‐mediated inflammation. Genetic and pharmacological interventions further establish the necessity of this Ca
                     2+ 
                    ‐CaMKK2‐AMPK axis for CBX2‐mediated metabolic protection. Collectively, our findings reveal a CBX2‐driven metabolic regulatory circuit and highlight CBX2 and its downstream signaling pathway as potential therapeutic targets for MASLD.

title: Poloxamer‐Enabled Thermoresponsive Biobased Controlled‐Release Fertilizer for On‐Demand Nutrient Delivery
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Synchronizing nutrient release of fertilizers with crop uptake remains a central challenge in precision agriculture. Here, we present a novel temperature‐responsive biobased controlled‐release fertilizer (TRBFs) incorporating Poloxamer 407 (F127) as a thermal switch within a castor oil‐derived polyurethane coating. The optimized TRBF10 (3 wt.% coating rate, 10 wt.% F127 in coating) exhibits a sharp, reversible phase transition at ∼20°C, matching the phenological requirements of overwintering crops. As quantified by digital refractometry, the 30‐day cumulative nitrogen release is suppressed to 9.22% at 10°C (crop dormancy) and increases 8.7‐fold to 80.32% at 30°C (active growth). This scalable technology overcomes intrinsic limitations of conventional diffusion‐controlled coated fertilizers and offers potential for on‐demand nutrient delivery with reduced environmental loss. Our work establishes sustainable strategies for climate‐adaptive precision agriculture and offers new insights and design paradigms for intelligent controlled‐release materials.

title: Deciphering Electrochemical Generation, Transport, and Reactivity of Hydrogen Species in the Electrochemical Palladium Membrane Reactor
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Electrochemical palladium membrane reactor (ePMR) enables hydrogenation chemistry by mechanically separating, but (electro)chemically coupling reduction and chemical hydrogenation by transporting hydrogen species through a dense Pd membrane, yet the identity and transport mechanism of the reactive hydrogen species remain underdefined. Here, we disentangled the roles of hydrogen species, including hydrogen atoms and molecules for both electrochemical and chemical compartments using 1hexyne electrochemical hydrogenation reaction as a model reaction. Tafel analysis with H/D electrolytes, isotopic effects, and quantification of products show that the apparent kinetics were strongly affected by the electron transfer kinetics and hydrogen permeation through the Pd membrane. Furthermore, mathematical description of hydrogen atom transport through the Pd membrane provided qualitative model framework. Electrochemically deposited Pd, Rh, and PdRh layers with controlled thickness and morphology tuned the reaction pathway of hydrogen atom vs. H
                     2 
                    ‐mediation at the chemical compartment, enabling systematic variation of 1‐hexyne conversion and
                     n 
                    ‐hexane selectivity. A dominant role of in situ generation and re‐dissociation of H*/H
                     2 
                    was observed in the hydrogenation process, supported by control experiments including gas‐purging experiments. Collectively, these insights establish design principles of surface engineering for ePMR, strategically coupling atomic and molecular hydrogen pathways for efficient and selective organic hydrogenation.

title: Therapeutic Peptide‐Programmed Liquid‐Crystalline Topology Switching for pH‐Gated Postoperative Cancer Immunotherapy
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Stimuli‐responsive depots for postoperative cancer therapy often treat therapeutic payloads as passive cargo, resulting in premature leakage and limited on‐demand activation. Herein, we report a therapeutic peptide‐programmed liquid‐crystalline depot in which the Vpr‐derived antitumor peptide (VDAP) functions simultaneously as an immunotherapeutic effector and a supramolecular topology regulator. At physiological pH, cationic α‐helical VDAP was electrostatically anchored by oleic acid‐containing lipid domains, reinforcing a compact inverse hexagonal (
                     H 
                     II 
                    ) topology associated with reduced peptide diffusion. In the acidic postoperative tumor microenvironment, protonation of oleic acid could disrupt anionic anchoring, whereas histidine protonation within VDAP amplified intrachannel electrostatic repulsion. This cooperative peptide–lipid charge reprogramming could drive graded liquid‐crystalline topology remodeling from a diffusion‐restrictive
                     H 
                     II 
                    organization to a more interconnected bicontinuous cubic
                     Im 
                    3̄
                     m 
                    network, consistent with increased pH‐responsive peptide release. In an orthotopic incomplete‐resection breast tumor model, the depot induced immunogenic tumor destruction, enhanced damage‐associated molecular pattern release, promoted dendritic cell maturation and CD8
                     + 
                    T cell infiltration, and reshaped the immunosuppressive surgical bed. These results demonstrate that electrostatic‐topology‐gated VDAP‐enabled supramolecular topology switching provides effective adaptive local cancer immunotherapy, effectively suppressing postoperative tumor recurrence and attenuating pulmonary metastasis.

title: To Be or Not to Be Eutectic: Anomalous Glass Forming Ability Governed by Melt Structural Complexity
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    For decades, the search for metallic glass formers has followed a simple rule: go for the eutectics. However, this conventional wisdom has been challenged by a lingering mystery—certain congruent melting alloys exhibit higher glass‐forming ability (GFA) than their eutectic neighbors. Here, we unravel this anomaly by probing the structure of high‐temperature melt—the direct precursor to a glass. Using Ti‐Cu as a model system, we conduct a comparative study on a eutectic Ti
                     27 
                    Cu
                     73 
                    and its congruent melting counterpart Ti
                     50 
                    Cu
                     50 
                    . By combining aerodynamic levitation, in situ synchrotron x‑ray diffraction, and an energy minimization‐enhanced reverse Monte Carlo method, we resolve the atomic structures of these alloys in both the melt and glassy states. We reveal that the congruent melt is structurally more complex than the eutectic, exhibiting higher cluster diversity and stronger inter‑cluster correlations owing to the entropy‐enthalpy competition. This structural complexity is then inherited and amplified during the glass transition via cluster transformations, serving as dual kinetic and energetic barriers to crystallization that lead to the anomalously higher GFA. Our work establishes melt structural complexity as a new framework for understanding the glass transition at the atomic cluster level, with important implications for designing superior glasses from high‐entropy intermetallic alloys.

title:
Harnessing Methylselenol (CH
                     3 
                    SeH): A Highly Effective Platform for Stimuli‐Responsive Delivery With Therapeutic Potential
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Methylselenol (CH
                     3 
                    SeH) is not only a key selenium (Se) metabolite but also a potent therapeutic molecule. Chemical tools for stimulus‐responsive delivery of CH
                     3 
                    SeH should be crucial for exploring Se‐related biomedicine. Nevertheless, the classical 1,6‐self‐immolation is inefficient in releasing the poorly leaving selenol, and donation platforms for triggerable release of the CH
                     3 
                    SeH remain lacking. Herein, we report the first general responsive platform (Triggered Donation for MethylSelenol, termed TD‐MSe) via fast intramolecular amino‐activated methylselenocarbamates (
                     t 
                     1/2 
                    = 5 s at pH 7.4), enabling the efficient cyclization release of CH
                     3 
                    SeH without electrophilic byproducts. We leverage the caged TD‐MSe motifs to successfully create triggered donors that are stable before activation but can liberate CH
                     3 
                    SeH under different stimulus conditions in vitro and in live cells. Additionally, we demonstrate that the tumor‐associated oxidoreductase (hNQO1)‐triggered CH
                     3 
                    SeH donor was activated in hNQO1‐positive HT‐29 cells but not in hNQO1‐negative cells. Moreover, we can use the CH
                     3 
                    SeH prodrug to selectively kill metastatic cells of hNQO1‐overexpressing cancer types, providing a promising therapeutic strategy for difficult‐to‐treat diseases. We anticipate that the new‐release chemistry will be widely applied for developing advanced tools toward smart selenol delivery and therapy.

title: Lewis Acid‐Catalyzed Strain‐Enabled (3+3) Annulation of Bicyclo[1.1.0]Butanes With Indolylalcohols: Synthesis of Indole‐Fused Aza‐Bicyclo[3.1.1]Heptanes
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Strain release has long inspired the discovery of unique reactivity, enabling diverse synthetically valuable transformations. Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs), due to their high ring strain, have emerged as versatile building blocks for constructing complex bicyclic architectures. Herein, we report a Lewis acid‐catalyzed formal (3 + 3) annulation of BCBs with indolyl alcohols, providing rapid access to indole‐fused aza‐bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes. The reaction proceeds under mild conditions, tolerates a broad range of functional groups, and delivers rigid, sp
                     3 
                    ‐rich scaffolds efficiently. Mechanistic studies, including control experiments and computational analysis, indicate a stepwise pathway in which Lewis acid activation of indolyl alcohols generates reactive intermediates, while strain‐release of BCBs drives C–C bond formation, followed by C–N bond formation via ring expansion to furnish the fused Aza‐bicyclic products.

title: H‐Bonding‐Induced Repulsion Between Small Groups Toward a Highly Puckered Benzene
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Benzene ring puckering generally arises from the strong repulsion between bulky substituents, while in this study, we present that benzene ring puckering can be achieved by repulsion between small substituents (nitro and methyl groups) facilitated by hydrogen‐bonding attraction, as exemplified in 1,3,5‐trinitro‐2,4,6‐trimethylaminobenzene. The role of intramolecular hydrogen bonding and steric repulsion is further investigated through comparison with four structurally related compounds differing in hydrogen‐bond donor availability and substituent size.

title: Acinar‐Derived Organoids Reveal Stage‐Specific Control of Acinar Plasticity
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Adult pancreatic acinar cells undergo ordered metaplastic conversion during injury and tumor initiation. Whether individual cells retain redifferentiation capacity after metaplastic expansion, and what signals each transition requires, remains unknown. Here, using organoids derived from single acinar cells, we show that expanded acinar‐lineage organoids can reacquire acinar features under stage‐specific culture conditions. We defined conditions that preserve acinar identity ex vivo and showed that epidermal growth factor (EGF)/EGF receptor (EGFR) signaling initiates conversion from this maintained state. The expansion trajectory recapitulates injury‐ and oncogene‐associated acinar‐to‐ductal metaplasia (ADM) programs in vivo. After expansion, the conditions that preserved acinar identity could not restore it; a staged regimen containing transient insulin‐like growth factor 1 receptor (IGF1R) inhibition and dexamethasone promoted redifferentiation. The Kras
                     G12D 
                    ;Trp53
                     R172H 
                    ;Pdx1‐Cre (
                     KPC 
                    ) genotype reduced EGFR dependence during initiation but destabilized post‐expansion redifferentiation;
                     Kras 
                    ‐pathway inhibition increased endpoint acinar‐marker expression. These findings demonstrate that acinar plasticity is organized by stage‐specific signals, and that the
                     KPC 
                    genotype disrupts this control at specific transition points.

title: AKAP1 Protects Retinal Ganglion Cells and Preserves Vision by Improving Mitochondrial and Synaptic Health in Glaucomatous Neurodegeneration
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Glaucoma, a leading cause of irreversible blindness, is characterized by progressive loss of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and lacks effective neuroprotective therapies. Despite evidence implicating mitochondrial dysfunction in glaucoma, the mechanisms linking elevated intraocular pressure, synaptic dysfunction, mitochondrial failure, and RGC death remain incompletely understood. Here we identify the mitochondrial scaffold protein A‐kinase anchoring protein 1 (AKAP1) as a critical regulator of RGC resilience in glaucoma. AKAP1 expression is reduced in glaucomatous retinas and correlates with disrupted mitochondrial dynamics, oxidative stress, synaptic impairment, and visual decline. AAV2‐mediated restoration of AKAP1 preserves RGC survival and visual function in two independent experimental glaucoma models. These data suggest that retinal AKAP1 promotes mitochondrial fusion, cristae integrity, and bioenergetic capacity in the inner retina and in stressed cultured RGCs, and is accompanied by increased mitochondrial content in presynaptic terminals of the inner plexiform layer. Retinal AKAP1 is further associated with higher PKA abundance, normalized CaMKII and synapsin phosphorylation, preserved synaptophysin, and lower complement C1q and glial activation markers; these associations do not, by themselves, establish causality. These findings identify AKAP1 as a candidate regulator of mitochondrial and synaptic homeostasis and highlight AAV2‐AKAP1 gene therapy as a promising neuroprotective strategy for vision preservation in glaucoma.

title: Symptom‐Driven Prediction of Chronic Multimorbidity with a Macro–Micro Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   The growing prevalence and complexity of multimorbidity pose significant challenges to healthcare systems worldwide. Here, we developed a heterogeneous graph neural network framework for multilabel multimorbidity prediction. The framework jointly encodes symptom and diagnostic information within a heterogeneous graph and incorporates biomedical knowledge subgraphs on both the disease and symptom sides. By integrating macro‐level clinical representations of symptoms and diseases with micro‐level molecular knowledge, the model generates multilabel probabilities across candidate disease categories. We evaluated the framework in two complementary tasks: Patient‐Level Symptom–Disease Association (Task 1) and Visit‐Level Multimorbidity Completion (Task 2). In Task 1, symptoms recorded across all eligible visits within each patient's observation window were aggregated into a patient‐level symptom set to predict the disease categories recorded for that patient within the same observation window. In Task 2, symptoms and a subset of recorded positive diagnoses from the same visit were used to predict the remaining disease categories recorded for that visit. Together, these two tasks provide a unified framework for patient‐level symptom–disease association and visit‐level multimorbidity completion. The framework characterized symptom–disease–biomedical knowledge associations and non‐random patterns of disease co‐occurrence, while supporting both patient‐level symptom–disease association and visit‐level multimorbidity completion.

title: Magnetoelectric Multiferroics for the Next‐Generation Ultralow‐Power Electronics
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Magnetoelectric multiferroics enable voltage control of magnetic states for low‐energy, non‐volatile memory and logic. Their practical value, however, depends on the complete device pathway, not coupling strength alone. This Review evaluates materials, switching mechanisms, and devices against these requirements, distinguishing measured performance from projected targets. We compare three magnetoelectric random‐access memory (MeRAM) routes with ferroelectric RAM and spin‐transfer torque magnetic RAM, and assess magnetoelectric spin–orbit (MESO) logic alongside complementary metal‐oxide‐semiconductor (CMOS) technology and current‐driven spintronics. MeRAM combines electric‐field writing, magnetic storage, and nondestructive readout, with prospects for low write energy and closer memory–logic integration. However, no integrated device has yet combined these benefits with competitive speed, retention, endurance, read margin, and density. For magnetoelectric logic, projected low‐voltage, non‐volatile operation has yet to be matched by experimental demonstrations of the full conversion path, gain and fan‐out. Results from BiFeO
                     3 
                    , room‐temperature hexaferrites and other platforms identify deterministic switching, interface quality and thin‐film integration as central to closing the gap between projections and experiments. Magnetoelectric devices are therefore more likely to complement CMOS than replace it, particularly in logic‐in‐memory, compute‐near‐memory and normally‐off systems, where non‐volatility and reduced data movement could support next‐generation ultralow‐power electronics.

title: Intelligent Field‐Adaptive Electrohydrodynamic Printing for Curved Conformal Electronics
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Curved conformal electronics are increasingly important for wearable devices, biosensing, and advanced communication systems, requiring high‐resolution and high‐precision manufacturing on complex surfaces. Electrohydrodynamic printing is a promising method for fabricating conformal electronics, but its application on curved insulating substrates is hindered by local electric‐field disturbances arising from residual charge accumulation and spatial variations, leading to poor dimensional control. To address this challenge, an intelligent field‐adaptive electrohydrodynamic printing framework is established, in which alternating‐electric‐field modulation reduces the effects of residual charge, the equivalent electrical gap quantitatively characterizes spatially varying electric‐field conditions, and machine learning‐based parameter regulation compensates for local electric‐field variations. Based on this framework, a machine‐learning and alternating‐electric‐field synergistic modulated electrohydrodynamic printing approach is developed to achieve stable printing and precise line‐width control on curved substrates. The approach rapidly optimizes parameters for target line widths, achieving average relative errors around 10% or lower at the initial printing position, and further reduces average relative line‐width errors by up to 7.24 percentage points through adaptive regulation during curved‐substrate printing. Diverse high‐precision patterns are printed, and the conformal frequency‐selective surface and antenna with excellent electromagnetic performance are fabricated, demonstrating the potential of this framework for advancing curved conformal electronics manufacturing.

title: Spatiotemporal Computational Meta‐Imager for Broadband Dual‐Layer Optical Convolution
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Optical neural networks face a tradeoff between device footprint and computational expressivity: deep systems are bulky, whereas single‐layer hardware lacks intrinsic depth and native negative‐weight support. We experimentally demonstrate a single‐layer metalens imager with “spatiotemporal intrinsic depth” for equivalent broadband dual‐layer convolution. A polarization‐multiplexed metasurface provides fixed Bessel‐vortex channels (
                     l 
                    = 0 to 3) as the immutable first convolution layer, where the (
                     l 
                    = 0) channel implements a hardware‐native residual connection. A metasurface‐generated 3 × 3 optical vortex matrix forms the second functional layer; time‐sequential liquid‐crystal amplitude modulation delivers tunable positive/negative weights. This temporal encoding solves the optical sign problem and converts fabrication imperfections into compensable biases via in‐situ training. Experiments verify rotational robustness for fashion‐item classification, raise full‐color CIFAR‐10 accuracy from 57.5 % to 86.6 %, and reach 99.3 % on the SIPaKMeD medical dataset, offloading 99.7 % of convolutional multiply‐accumulate operations to optics. By removing volumetric diffractive layers, this work enables low‐latency hybrid optoelectronic edge intelligent vision.

title: HECTD1 Directs HIF‐1α to Facilitate Intestinal Inflammation and Carcinogenesis via Promoting Th17 Differentiation and Glycolysis
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Targeting glucose metabolism in Th17 cells may be beneficial for treating inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and colitis‐associated cancer (CAC), however, the molecular mechanisms orchestrating Th17 cell metabolism remain unclear. Here, we revealed that HECTD1 regulates IGF2BP3‐dependent HIF‐1α translation to promote Th17 cell glycolysis and differentiation and that HECTD1 expression correlates with IBD and CAC pathogenesis. T‐cell‐specific deletion of HECTD1 mitigated the severity of colitis and CAC in murine models. RNA‐seq revealed enrichment of Th17 differentiation, glycolysis/gluconeogenesis, and HIF‐1 signaling pathways among differentially expressed genes between HECTD1‐sufficient and HECTD1‐deficient CD4
                     + 
                    T cells. Consistently, loss of HECTD1 suppressed Th17 cell differentiation both in vitro and in vivo, and suppressed glycolytic metabolism and HIF‐1α activity, revealing the mechanism underlying its protective effects against IBD and CAC. Mechanistically, HECTD1 potentiates m
                     6 
                    A‐based HIF‐1α translation by mediating IGF2BP3 K63‐linked ubiquitination to promote the binding of IGF2BP3 with the translation initiation machinery of
                     Hif1a 
                    mRNA. Reciprocally, HIF‐1α acts as a key transcription factor that promotes
                     Hectd1 
                    gene expression, establishing a distinct positive feedback loop. Our findings highlight a self‐reinforcing feedback mechanism in which HECTD1 and HIF‐1α engage in mutual regulation to dictate Th17 cell fate and metabolic reprogramming, providing novel potential IBD and CAC treatments targeting HECTD1.

title: Data‐Driven and Physics‐Informed Modeling Perspectives for Soft Manipulators: From SINDy to Hybrid Intelligence
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Soft manipulators offer a route to safer, more adaptive and physically intelligent robots, but their compliant bodies remain difficult to model, predict and control. Large deformation, distributed actuation, hysteresis, material variability and contact‐rich interaction challenge both classical mechanics‐based models and purely data‐driven approaches. Here, we examine emerging modeling perspectives for soft manipulators through a conceptual progression from sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics to hybrid intelligence. We discuss how sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics (SINDy), Koopman learning, neural ordinary differential equations, physics‐informed neural networks, and hybrid physics machine learning models contribute complementary capabilities, including interpretable reduced‐order dynamics, control‐ready prediction, continuous‐time latent modeling, physics‐constrained field reconstruction, and residual correction. We present that no single modeling approach is sufficient for the next generation of soft robotic systems. Instead, progress requires integrated modeling ecosystems that combine mechanical structure, data‐driven discovery and task‐aware adaptation. Such hybrid‐intelligence frameworks can transform models from passive descriptions of deformation into active components of sensing, control, design and decision‐making, enabling soft manipulators that are more interpretable, robust and deployable in real‐world environments.

title: Astrocyte‐Associated ABCA1/APOE Responses Accompany Hippocampal Lipid Remodeling and Ectopic Neuronal Accumulation During Epileptogenesis
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) is characterized by progressive hippocampal remodeling, including reactive astrogliosis and aberrant neuronal positioning. Although lipid disturbances are implicated in epileptogenesis, how astrocyte‐associated lipid responses relate to hippocampal remodeling remains poorly understood. Here, human TLE and kainic acid (KA)‐treated mouse transcriptomic datasets identified ATP‐binding cassette transporter A1 (ABCA1)/Abca1 as a nominal astrocyte‐associated candidate, while KA‐ and pilocarpine‐induced status epilepticus (SE) elicited astrocyte‐associated ABCA1/apolipoprotein E (APOE) responses. Ectopic granule cells and immature neurons accumulated in the hilus and were spatially associated with ABCA1‐positive cells, including astrocytic profiles; perilipin 2 (PLIN2)‐positive puncta were nearby. Pretreatment with the retinoid X receptor (RXR) agonist bexarotene increased hippocampal ABCA1 expression, delayed severe KA‐induced behavioral seizure onset, and was associated with fewer chronic spontaneous seizures and reduced ectopic neuronal accumulation. Post‐SE bexarotene administration was associated with lower seizure frequency, ectopic neuronal accumulation, and astrocytic marker‐positive cell densities. Multi‐omic profiling identified bexarotene‐associated metabolic and lipidomic changes; transmission electron microscopy (TEM) showed a smaller mean hilar neuronal lipid‐droplet area per image, and protein analyses identified early changes in p38 and extracellular signal‐regulated kinase 1/2 (Erk1/2) phosphorylation. Together, these findings warrant further investigation of astrocyte‐associated lipid pathways as potential therapeutic targets in epilepsy‐associated hippocampal remodeling.

title: A Chiral Virus‐Like Nanoplatform That Broadly Mediates Antibiotic Delivery to the Brain for Bacterial Meningitis Therapy

CeO
                     2 
                    ‐Based Electrocatalysts for the Oxygen Evolution Reaction: Design, Dynamic Mechanisms, and Electrolyte Adaptability
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    CeO
                     2 
                    ‐based electrocatalysts are promising for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) owing to their distinctive Ce
                     3+ 
                    /Ce
                     4+ 
                    redox flexibility, large oxygen‐storage capacity, and lattice adaptability. More importantly, CeO
                     2 
                    can dynamically regulate catalyst surface reconstruction and electronic structure while significantly enhancing catalytic activity and long‐term stability. In this review, we first focus on CeO
                     2 
                    ‐based electrocatalysts for OER from structural characteristics, design principles and strategies, structure–property relationships, interfacial structure, as well as critical evaluation of design strategies and selection principles. The mechanistic roles of CeO
                     2 
                    in OER are highlighted, including redox chemistry and oxygen‐vacancy (O
                     v 
                    ) dynamics, electronic‐structure modulation and charge transfer, interfacial coupling and surface reconstruction, as well as operando evidence and the controversy over lattice‐oxygen participation. The performance of CeO
                     
                       2 
                     
                    ‐based OER electrocatalysts in different electrolytes, including alkaline, acidic, and seawater media, is also summarized to demonstrate their applicability under diverse operating conditions. Finally, from the perspectives of electronic‐structure evolution, redox‐state transitions, lattice evolution, and catalytic pathways, this review summarizes the underlying mechanisms by which CeO
                     2 
                    regulates the dynamic catalytic behavior of OER and provides an outlook on future design strategies for developing highly efficient and durable CeO
                     2 
                    ‐based electrocatalysts.

title: Activation‐Induced Turbostratic Ordering in pDCPD‐Derived Hard Carbon Enables Stable Carbonate‐Based Sodium‐Ion Storage
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Sodium–ion batteries are widely considered a promising alternative to lithium‐ion batteries, due to the abundance and low cost of their raw materials. However, the development of high‐performance and cost‐effective electrode materials remains a significant challenge, particularly when competing with lithium iron phosphate systems. Herein, we present a hard carbon material derived from readily available poly(dicyclopentadiene) for use as a negative electrode in SIBs. This study investigates the influence of carbonization temperature and subsequent  activation on the hard carbon structure and electrochemical performance. The impact of activation proved to be dependent upon the first stage carbonization temperature, creating greater local ordering for samples carbonized at higher temperatures. The removal of defects and increase in interlayer distance resulted in a turbostratic structure that enhanced rate performance and capacity retention when compared with non‐activated samples. The optimized hard carbon exhibits a reversible capacity of 352 mAh  at 0.1 C and a capacity retention of 88.1% after 500 cycles with a carbonate based electrolyte. This work introduces a cost‐effective approach for producing hard carbon materials with distinctive nanostructure and provides valuable insights into achieving long cycle life in sodium–ion batteries.

title: Tubocapsenolide A Overcomes Oxaliplatin Resistance in Colorectal Cancer by Targeting PLK1 to Impair CEP55–ESCRT‐Associated Vesicular Damage Clearance
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Oxaliplatin (L‐OHP) is a first‐line chemotherapeutic agent for advanced colorectal cancer (CRC) and postoperative adjuvant therapy. However, acquired L‐OHP resistance remains a clinical obstacle. Here, we identify Tubocapsenolide A (TA), a natural withanolide isolated from
                     Tubocapsicum anomalum 
                    , as a promising antitumor agent that suppresses CRC growth and sensitizes L‐OHP‐resistant CRC to L‐OHP. Using a PROTAC‐based target deconvolution strategy, we identify PLK1 as a direct molecular target of TA. PLK1 is elevated in L‐OHP‐resistant CRC and is associated with reduced patient sensitivity to L‐OHP. Mechanistically, elevated PLK1 promotes CEP55 Ser436 phosphorylation and facilitates ESCRT recruitment to nuclear and mitochondrial budding sites. This process facilitates the clearance of L‐OHP‐induced damaged components through nuclear budding and TOM20
                     − 
                    /PDH
                     + 
                    mitochondrial‐derived vesicles, thereby contributing to organelle homeostasis and cell survival. By inhibiting PLK1, TA interferes with this vesicle‐associated damage clearance process, leading to intracellular accumulation of damaged components. This damage accumulation is accompanied by nucleolar stress and mitochondrial dysfunction, ultimately contributing to cell death. Collectively, our findings identify a previously unappreciated role of the PLK1–CEP55–ESCRT axis in vesicle‐associated damage clearance during L‐OHP resistance and support this axis as a potential therapeutic target. TA represents a promising lead compound for overcoming L‐OHP resistance in CRC.

title: Thioredoxin‐2 Alleviates Osteoporosis by Restraining FOXO3a Nuclear Translocation
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Osteoporosis is a prevalent age‐ and disease‐associated skeletal disorder characterized by bone loss, remodeling imbalance, and vascular niche deterioration, yet how endothelial redox dysfunction drives this process remains unclear. Here, we identify mitochondrial thioredoxin‐2 (TRX2) as an endothelial safeguard against osteoporotic bone loss. TRX2 was markedly reduced in aging bone vascular endothelial cells, and endothelial Trx2 deficiency accelerated skeletal degeneration by suppressing osteogenic activity and enhancing osteoclastogenesis. Mechanistically, TRX2 directly bound FOXO3a through a redox‐sensitive Cys90–Cys31 disulfide interaction, retaining FOXO3a at the mitochondrial outer membrane and limiting its nuclear translocation. TRX2 loss or oxidative stress disrupted this complex, enabling FOXO3a‐dependent transcriptional activation of tumor necrosis factor–related apoptosis‐inducing ligand (TRAIL) and generating a pro‐osteoclastogenic vascular niche. TRAIL neutralization or endothelial TRX2 restoration attenuated ovariectomy‐induced osteoporosis by preserving angiogenic–osteogenic coupling. These findings establish the endothelial TRX2–FOXO3a–TRAIL axis as a vascular redox checkpoint and potential therapeutic target for osteoporosis.

title: Physics‐Guided Multi‐Channel Restoration for Efficient and Accurate Atomic Force Microscopy Imaging
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Scientific imaging instruments often acquire multiple physically complementary signals within a single measurement. In atomic force microscopy (AFM), high‐throughput imaging requires higher scan speeds, however, image quality is fundamentally limited by multiple distortions. These artifacts are further amplified for sharp nano/microstructures, making accurate image restoration inherently challenging. Most deep learning‐based approaches rely on a single primary channel and improve performance by increasing model complexity or training data. Here, we introduce a physics‐guided multi‐channel input approach for AFM that utilizes co‐acquired auxiliary signals to improve image restoration efficiency and accuracy. We construct a four co‐acquired channel input, each containing complementary physical information. By integrating these channels into a lightweight convolutional neural network, the proposed approach significantly improves restoration quality with minimal additional parameters. At a scan rate of 7.0 Hz, the four‐channel DnCNN achieved higher reconstruction accuracy than a single‐channel Restormer with approximately 47 times as many parameters, while providing approximately 24 times faster inference. Across the evaluated EFM and PFM conditions, four‐channel inputs reduced the training‐patch requirement by approximately two to three times at matched PSNR.

title: Habitat‐Specific Design Strategies for Untethered Soft Robots
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Untethered soft robots are governed by habitat‐specific constraints because operation without physical tethers requires their compliant structures, actuation mechanisms, and energy‐delivery pathways to remain compatible with the environment. Adopting a habitat‐centric framework, this review compares untethered soft robots across terrestrial, aquatic, aerial, and in vivo environments. On terrestrial substrates, design strategies are shaped by locomotion‐specific demands, including contact modulation in crawling, energy storage and release in jumping, switchable adhesion in climbing, and granular fluidization in burrowing. In aquatic habitats, the dominant constraint shifts with depth, from capillary support at the air‐water interface, to hydrodynamic drag in shallow water, and to hydrostatic pressure in the deep sea. In aerial environments, strict mass and power limits favor actively flapping insect‐scale robots, buoyancy‐assisted vehicles, and passively dispersed aeroelastic structures. In vivo, miniaturization and biocompatibility confine the viable design space to magnetic, acoustic, and biohybrid actuation. A multi‐environment comparison shows that no single actuation modality is universally optimal. Each habitat filters actuation strategies by the compatibility between energy transmission and the local medium. Material longevity, onboard energy autonomy, multi‐environment transition, extraterrestrial operation, and perception and feedback control are identified as cross‐cutting challenges whose resolution is required to translate laboratory demonstrations into real‐world deployment.

title: AI‐EXAFS: Physics‐Informed Prediction of EXAFS from Atomic Structure
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Understanding atomic structure across chemical systems relies heavily on extended X‐ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) because of its sensitivity to local atomic environments. However, quantitative interpretation remains inherently iterative, requiring structural parameters or models to be fitted against experimental spectra using explicit multiple‐scattering calculations. Machine‐learning approaches have accelerated EXAFS analysis, yet direct prediction of full spectra from atomistic structure across diverse chemical environments remains challenging. Here, we introduce AI‐EXAFS, a physics‐informed graph neural network that predicts spectra directly from three‐dimensional atomic coordinates. Combining an absorber‐centered graph representation with distance‐modulated message passing and an EXAFS‐specific training objective enables direct learning of structure–spectrum relationships without predefined structural descriptors or manual parameter selection. Trained and evaluated across a dataset of 85,991 transition‐metal complexes with FEFF‐generated spectra, AI‐EXAFS achieves average held‐out test‐set
                     R 
                    ‐factors of 0.043 in ‐space and 0.019 in ‐space, demonstrating accurate structure‐to‐spectrum prediction across a broad range of local chemical environments. AI‐EXAFS establishes a scalable structure‐to‐spectrum framework for EXAFS, enabling direct inference across large sets of candidate structures and providing a foundation for data‐driven prediction across increasingly complex and experimentally relevant environments.

title: Foundation Model‐Enabled Pathology‐Informed MRI Model for Preoperative Prediction of Vessels Encapsulating Tumor Clusters in Resectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Multicenter Retrospective Study
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Vessels encapsulating tumor clusters (VETC) are an aggressive vascular phenotype of hepatocellular carcinoma that is usually determined after surgery. A foundation model‐enabled framework for pathology‐informed VETC prediction on pretreatment magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), termed PIVOT, uses paired preoperative multiparametric MRI, postoperative hematoxylin and eosin whole‐slide images, and CD34 immunohistochemistry during model development, while inference requires only preoperative MRI. PIVOT‐MRI uses morphologic and vascular embedding alignment, and PIVOT‐Clinical combines the PIVOT‐MRI score with tumor size and alpha‐fetoprotein. The multicenter retrospective study includes 2052 patients in a training cohort, an internal test cohort, and four external validation cohorts. PIVOT‐MRI achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.887 in the internal test cohort and 0.839‐0.861 across external cohorts. PIVOT‐Clinical increases the internal‐test area under the curve to 0.904 and PIVOT‐Clinical‐defined groups are associated with different two‐year recurrence risks. Removing both histopathologic alignment branches results in the largest ablation‐related performance decrease. Exploratory radiotranscriptomic analyses showed that higher PIVOT‐MRI scores were associated with angiogenesis‐related, endothelial, and proliferative transcriptional programs. PIVOT enables noninvasive preoperative assessment of pathology‐defined vascular aggressiveness in resectable hepatocellular carcinoma while preserving an MRI‐only clinical inference pathway.

title:
Oral Astilbin Nanogels Modulate Senescence‐Associated CD4
                     + 
                    T Cells and Promote T
                     reg 
                    Induction in Aged Mice with Colitis
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) in older individuals is characterized by immune senescence and deteriorating intestinal homeostasis, both of which limit the efficacy of current therapies. Here, we develop fluorinated β‐glucan/pectin nanogels (F
                     2 
                    ‐Ast@NGs) for oral delivery of astilbin, a natural flavonoid with anti‐inflammatory and immunoregulatory activities. This multifunctional platform integrates gastrointestinal protection, colon‐targeted release, and local immune modulation. The β‐glucan shell preserves nanogel stability during upper gastrointestinal transit while enabling β‐glucanase‐responsive disassembly in the colon. Fluorocarbon segments enhance mucus penetration, and the pectin matrix prolongs colonic retention, promoting drug accumulation at inflamed sites. In aged mice with dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)‐induced colitis, F
                     2 
                    ‐Ast@NGs alleviate disease severity, attenuate senescence‐associated features of colonic CD4
                     + 
                    T cells, and enhance Foxp3
                     + 
                    regulatory T cell (T
                     reg 
                    ) responses. Concurrently, the β‐glucan/pectin nanogel matrix contributes to increased short‐chain fatty acid production and favorable alterations in gut microbial composition. Notably, the therapeutic efficacy of F
                     2 
                    ‐Ast@NGs is markedly attenuated in Foxp3
                     + 
                    T
                     reg 
                    ‐depleted mice, supporting an important role for T
                     reg 
                    ‐mediated immunoregulation. Collectively, F
                     2 
                    ‐Ast@NGs enable precise colonic delivery while coordinately remodeling the intestinal immune and microbial microenvironment, providing a promising oral nanotherapeutic strategy for colitis in aged hosts.

title: PBRM1 Deficiency in Microglia Leads to Excessive Neurogenesis and Autism‐Like Behaviors via the CCL5‐CCR1/5‐β‐catenin Signaling Axis
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    The prevalence of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental disorder with limited effective therapeutic drugs, has been rising worldwide. Missense mutations in Polybromo 1 (
                     Pbrm1 
                    ), a core component of the SWI/SNF (switch/sucrose non‐fermentable) chromatin remodeling complex, have been identified as a risk factor for ASD; however, whether PBRM1 loss of function contributes to the pathogenesis remains elusive. Here we provide direct evidence that microglial PBRM1 deficiency leads to altered microglial clusters, excessive neurogenesis, and ASD‐like behaviors in mice. Integrated molecular analyses reveal that PBRM1 directly binds to the
                     Ccl5 
                    promoter and represses the expression of CCL5. Elevated CCL5 promotes the proliferation and neuronal differentiation of neural stem/progenitor cells (NSPCs) via the CCR1/5‐β‐catenin signaling pathway. Importantly, pharmacological blockade of CCR1/5 ameliorates behavioral deficits in
                     Pbrm1 
                    cKO mice. Together, these findings identify a previously unrecognized microglia–NSPC communication mechanism linking PBRM1 dysfunction to aberrant neurodevelopment and suggest the CCL5–CCR1/5 axis as a potential therapeutic target for ASD.

title: qcGEM: A Graph‐Based Molecular Representation With Quantum Chemistry Awareness
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   The advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has reshaped drug discovery. AI‐based models typically rely on molecular representations for prediction. However, the absence of physically grounded information in mainstream molecular representations not only limits the model performance in practical applications but also hinders mechanistic understanding and exploitation by humans. To overcome this issue, we introduce qcGEM, a quantum‐chemistry‐aware graph‐based embedding of molecules that incorporates physical priors into molecular representation learning. Through a specially designed model architecture to adequately process quantum chemistry information, qcGEM provides a compact, physics‐informed molecular representation that supports a diverse range of downstream applications. Particularly, qcGEM demonstrates state‐of‐the‐art performance across a broad range of molecule‐related benchmarks, as evidenced by comprehensive evaluations on 83 tasks including molecular property prediction, activity cliff detection, protein–ligand interaction modeling, and opioid drug regression, and simultaneously offers strong interpretability at multiple representation levels. We additionally propose a simplified variant, qcGEM‐Hybrid, with substantially accelerated embedding generation and robust performance. Overall, our method provides an advanced molecular representation that will benefit molecule‐related modeling and prediction, supporting further progress in AI‐aided drug discovery.

title: Molecular Signatures of HIV‐Induced Neuroinflammation and Neurodegeneration in Human Cerebral Organoids: Identification of Therapeutic Targets for NeuroHIV
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   HIV‐associated neurological complications remain a major concern in people living with HIV (PWH), even under effective viral suppression with combination antiretroviral therapy (cART), underscoring unresolved mechanisms driving HIV‐related neurodegeneration. To address this gap, we used HIV‐1‐infected human cerebral organoids (hCOs) containing microglia as a physiologically relevant three‐dimensional model of the central nervous system (CNS) and validated key findings in the brain region of simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV)‐infected, cART‐treated rhesus macaque model. Integrated single‐nucleus RNA sequencing with ATAC‐seq (multi‐omics), identifies cell‐type‐specific alterations in dual innate immune‐driven inflammatory signaling pathways across neural and glial populations in hCOs. Microglia were preferentially infected and activated, initiating IL‐17A–mediated cascades involving IFN‐γ/STAT1, CEBPB, and NF‐κB signaling. These pathways converged with cGAS‐STING and Notch–NEURL1 signaling, both associated with neuroinflammation and synaptic dysfunction. cART suppressed viral replication, reduced IL‐17A‐mediated neuroinflammation, improved mitochondrial function, and restored synaptic gene expression. Collectively, these findings identify dysregulation of IL‐17A, STAT1, CEBPB, and cGAS‐STING signaling as key molecular drivers of HIV‐associated neuroinflammation. They also establish a potential mechanistic link between IL‐17A signaling and microglial remodeling, providing a translational framework for the development of CNS‐targeted therapies in PWH.

title: A Micropeptide Component of the OGDH Complex Modulates ATP Production in the TCA Cycle
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Since its elucidation, the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle has been regarded as a fully defined enzymatic pathway. Here, we report the discovery of a previously unrecognized micropeptide component of this central metabolic system. Through analyzing ribosome profiling data from the mouse sORFs.org database, we discovered APPM (ATP production–promoting micropeptide), a 29–amino acid peptide encoded by a non‐canonical small open reading frame within the mouse Ctsb gene. APPM localizes to the mitochondrial matrix and inner membrane, where it directly binds to the E1 subunit (OGDH) of the α‐ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complex (OGDHc). This interaction modulates OGDHc enzymatic activity, thereby regulating NADH and ATP production. We identified tyrosine‐13 as the critical residue mediating the APPM‐OGDH interaction and functional activation. Exogenous APPM administration increased ATP levels in vivo and, in a mouse model of heart failure, restored cardiac function, outperforming the reference drug trimetazidine. Collectively, our findings identify APPM as the first micropeptide regulator of the OGDH complex, expanding the known repertoire of the TCA cycle and presenting a potential therapeutic strategy for diseases characterized by bioenergetic insufficiency.

title: Amira: detection of single and multi-copy antimicrobial resistance genes directly from long reads using gene-space de Bruijn graphs
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Accurate detection of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes is essential for AMR surveillance and genotypic prediction. Current approaches typically either depend on a correct genome assembly or use k-mers directly from the reads. However AMR genes are often multicopy and are enriched at repeat loci where genome assemblers tend to fail, and k-mer methods struggle to distinguish different copies. We present Amira, which detects AMR genes directly from long reads by building gene-space de Bruijn graphs, allowing precise association of reads with distinct AMR gene copies, enabling accurate assembly. Across simulations, curated samples, and public datasets, Amira improves copy-number recall and nucleotide accuracy compared with existing methods.

title: A hybrid beam search framework with deep representation learning for the multiple longest common subsequence problem
ParaDISM: precise mapping of short reads to genes with highly homologous regions
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Background 
                     Genes with highly similar genomic copies (paralogs, tandem duplications and pseudogenes) pose a major challenge for Short-Read High Throughput Sequencing (srHTS). High sequence similarity makes it difficult to unambiguously identify the sequences of origin of short reads. This results in misalignment artifacts which can propagate through bioinformatic pipelines and increase error rates in subsequent steps such as single nucleotide variant calling. 
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     
                      We present
                       ParaDISM 
                      , a pipeline that refines standard alignments to improve read placement and reduce misalignment-driven false variant calls in highly homologous sequences. The pipeline uses a multiple sequence alignment of reference sequences to identify disambiguating positions and assign a read/read pair to a sequence only when supported by unambiguous sequence-specific evidence.
                       ParaDISM 
                      focuses on specificity and precision (positive predictive value) rather than sensitivity by adopting a conservative strategy of read placement and reporting reads with insufficient evidence for the gene of origin as unassigned. An optional iterative refinement procedure calls variants from confidently assigned reads, updates the reference sequences to gain sample-specific evidence for read placement, and re-processes remaining non-assigned reads to mitigate the loss of sensitivity caused by the stringent criteria for read placement. We evaluated the performance of ParaDISM both in terms of read alignment and the resulting short variant calls using extensive computational simulation experiments and the Genome in a Bottle HG002 benchmark. We applied ParaDISM to reanalyze two case studies: five public tumour exomes at the GNAQ/GNAQP1 locus, and 18 short-read sequencing datasets of patients diagnosed with Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (15 exomes and 3 panel sequencing datasets). Compared to Bowtie2, BWA-MEM2 and minimap2, ParaDISM reduced the number of misalignment artifacts, thus increasing specificity and precision of subsequent single nucleotide variant calls.
                     
                   
                   
                     Conclusions 
                     ParaDISM refines BAM files to improve the precision of read placement and downstream analyses in highly homologous sequences. The pipeline can be used as a precision-focused add-on to standard bioinformatic pipelines before the variant calling step to provide a stronger level of evidence for variants called in regions of high homology. This approach is useful for applications where false positive variant calls have more severe consequences than false negative ones, such as identifying causal mutations for genetic disorders. In applications where experimental wet-lab confirmation of shortlisted variants is necessary, ParaDISM can be used to prioritise variants with strong support to reduce cost and effort spent on attempting to confirm false positive calls. ParaDISM can be used alongside the results of standard mappers to cross-check results and identify unreliable read placement and variants potentially caused by misalignment artifacts. The pipeline is open source and available under the MIT license at github.com/BioGeMT/ParaDISM.

title: Metacontextify: automated environmental annotation of marine metagenomic samples
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Background 
                     Environmental metadata is essential for using metagenomic and microbiome data to gain relevant biological insights like relations between the environment and microbial communities, genome content and protein-level adaptations. Unfortunately, obtaining standardized environmental context for those samples remains difficult. One possible solution is to use Earth observation data to retrieve the missing metadata. However, using such data requires spatiotemporal coordinate matching and handling large environmental datasets in specialized file formats, creating a barrier for its applicability. 
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     
                      Metacontextify addresses this gap by automatically retrieving environmental properties (e.g., temperature, salinity, pH, nutrients) for marine metagenomic samples using Copernicus Marine Service data. The tool connects ENA and MGnify identifiers or sampling coordinates and dates to historical environmental observations, enabling large-scale ecological, genomic, and functional analyses. The tool is used to study the difference in environmental context between cold-shock proteins, involved in adaptation to temperature decreases, and antifreeze proteins, which prevent ice formation in the cell. We show that cold-shock proteins are present across the full range of marine temperatures observed in the dataset, while antifreeze proteins are predominantly found below 5 
                       ∘ 
                      C (83% of matched proteins). However, we observe a negative association between temperature and the number of cold-shock proteins per sample (Spearman correlation of -0.439,
                       p 
                      -value 1.2 × 10
                       −70 
                      ). After a genome-level analysis, we find a negative correlation between genome length and temperature (
                       ρ 
                       = − 0.28,
                       p 
                       = 4.2 × 10
                       −65 
                      ) and a positive correlation between genome length and the count of cold-shock proteins in a genome (
                       ρ 
                       = 0.41,
                       p 
                       = 1.5 × 10
                       −144 
                      ).
                     
                   
                   
                     Conclusion 
                     Metacontextify enables researchers to integrate environmental context into large-scale metagenomic analyses, even when original datasets lack environmental metadata. This is shown for a collection of marine samples where the number of samples with temperature annotations increased 1.45-fold. For the use case, we identified distinct temperature-associated distributions of cold-shock and antifreeze proteins and demonstrated how environmental contextualization can reveal biologically meaningful patterns in large metagenomic datasets. Metacontextify is implemented in Python and is freely available under an MIT license. It can be installed via pip, conda or a container image and is accessible as a Python library and command-line tool with source code available on GitHub.

Beyond sanctions: where the costs of nursery pollination are borne

title: Drought‐induced plant dominance shift amplifies functional niche differentiation in steppe communities
authors:
Wang Ma, 
Xiaosa Liang, 
Wentao Luo, 
Bingchuan Zhang, 
Jiaxin Hu, 
Jia Guo, 
Nazim Hassan, 
Qiang Yu, 
Xingguo Han, 
Zhengwen Wang, 
Yann Hautier
abstract:
Summary 
                   
                     
                       
                         Trait‐based studies on community assembly under environmental change often overlook intraspecific trait variation (ITV), despite its considerable role in modulating community dynamics, which may largely mislead the inference of community assembly. 
                       
                       
                         Under simulated extreme droughts in a temperate steppe, we integrated ITV and interspecific trait variation for four key traits, plant height (Height), specific leaf area (SLA), leaf dry matter content (LDMC), and leaf thickness (LT), to examine how drought alters functional niche structure and underlying processes. 
                       
                       
                         Drought shifted communities toward conservative resource‐use strategies, reduced community variation in LT, and interspecific trait overlap in terms of SLA, LDMC, LT, and the multivariate trait space, whereas community‐level ITV remained stable across all traits. These changes were driven primarily by diversity loss and increases in the dominance of fewer species, with negligible effects of intraspecific trait plasticity or species turnover. Communities with fewer but more dominant species exhibited smaller trait overlap. 
                       
                       
                         Our findings advance our understanding of the paradigm of trait convergence under environmental filtering. Drought‐induced diversity loss amplifies functional niche differentiation, underscoring the critical role of species reorganization through dominance shifts, with little evidence for intraspecific trait plasticity in mediating community assembly under climate extremes.

title:
Cell‐type‐specific PIN‐FORMED 3‐mediated polar auxin transport regulates cambial activity and tension wood formation in
                     
                       Populus tomentosa
authors:
Dongmei Xiang, 
Lingmin Ran, 
Yuanjin Li, 
Liqing Zong, 
Baoxia Li, 
Qingqing Chu, 
Mi Zhang, 
Xiaokang Fu, 
Lianghanxiao Sun, 
Shutang Tan, 
Markus Geisler, 
Bangjun Wang, 
Xiaoyan Gu, 
Keming Luo, 
Changzheng Xu
abstract:
Summary 
                   
                     
                       
                         
                          Auxin is a central regulator of tree secondary growth and forms maxima in the vascular cambium, yet how these maxima are established remains elusive. Here, we functionally characterized two redundant PIN‐FORMED 3 (
                           PIN3 
                          ) paralogs from
                           Populus tomentosa 
                          to define their roles in secondary growth and gravity‐induced tension wood (TW) formation.
                         
                       
                       
                         We employed fluorescent reporter lines, clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats‐generated knockout mutants, phloem‐specific RNA interference transgenic plants and isotopic auxin transport assays to dissect PIN3 functions during secondary growth of poplar stems. 
                       
                       
                         
                          Loss of function of
                           PIN3 
                          paralogs severely compromises cambial proliferation, secondary xylem differentiation and TW development. PIN3 proteins display cell‐type‐specific polar localization with basal polarity in phloem cells and outer lateral polarity in endodermal cells. Phloem‐expressed PIN3 facilitates basipetal auxin transport and is required for cambial auxin response. Upon gravistimulation, endodermal PIN3 repolarizes along the gravity vector, correlating with TW formation.
                         
                       
                       
                         Our findings identify a cell‐type‐specific, PIN3‐mediated auxin transport mechanism that contributes to auxin‐driven secondary growth of tree stems.

title:
Arabidopsis cyclin‐dependent kinases and
                     MAP65 
                    phosphorylation link microtubule dynamics with salt stress adaptation
authors:
Xiaoxiao Qu, 
Junjie Zou, 
Chunxia Zhang, 
Junling Yue, 
Kezhen Yang, 
Jie Le
abstract:
Summary 
                   
                     
                       
                         Plants possess sophisticated regulatory mechanisms to balance growth and stress responses. Cyclin‐dependent kinases (CDKs) are established regulators of cell division and endoreduplication, yet their roles in abiotic stress responses remain poorly understood. 
                       
                       
                         
                          Here, using reverse genetics, biochemical, and cell biological approaches, we show that Arabidopsis (
                           Arabidopsis thaliana 
                          ) CDKB1s contribute to salt stress adaptation through a mechanism involving the phosphorylation of MAP65‐1 and MAP65‐2, two microtubule‐associated proteins essential for cytoskeleton dynamics under salt stress.
                         
                       
                       
                         
                          Loss of CDKB1 function enhances salt tolerance, accompanied by attenuated plasma membrane depolarization and reactive oxygen species accumulation.
                           In vitro 
                          phosphorylation assays demonstrate that CDKB1;1 directly phosphorylates MAP65‐1 at Ser‐503. Genetic analyses indicate that phospho‐dead MAP65 variants confer enhanced salt tolerance, whereas phosphomimetic variants compromise tolerance even in the
                           cdkb1;1 1;2 
                          background, supporting a critical role for MAP65 phosphorylation status at these sites in salt stress adaptation. We further found that CDKA;1 can similarly interact with and phosphorylate MAP65‐1, suggesting a potential parallel role for CDKA;1 in this process.
                         
                       
                       
                         Collectively, our findings identify a regulatory module involving CDKs, MAP65, and microtubules that links cell cycle kinases and cytoskeleton dynamics with plant salt stress adaptation.

title:
MicroRNA 
                    160 controls the auxin response factor–class
                     III 
                    peroxidase module and couples salicylic acid and redox signaling networks in the potato hypersensitive response to potato virus Y
authors:
Maja Križnik, 
Tjaša Lukan, 
Maja Zagorščak, 
Anna Coll Rius, 
Karmen Pogačar, 
Nastja Marondini, 
Katja Stare, 
Valentina Levak, 
Jitka Široká, 
Ondřej Novák, 
Aleš Kladnik, 
Kristina Gruden
abstract:
Summary 
                   
                     
                       
                         Hypersensitive response (HR) is an effector‐triggered immune response leading to pathogen restriction and local cell death. Small RNAs (sRNAs), mediating RNA silencing, have a well‐established role in antiviral immunity; however, their role in HR has not been addressed to date. 
                       
                       
                         
                          We applied a spatially resolved sRNA‐omics approach to uncover changes at the sRNA level and the dynamics of sRNA–gene regulatory networks in potato (
                           Solanum tuberosum 
                          L.) HR to potato virus Y (PVY).
                         
                       
                       
                         
                          We show that miR160 is repressed in cells adjacent to HR lesions in the resistant cultivar, but not in PVY‐sensitive, salicylic acid (SA)‐depleted plants. Beyond its canonical regulation of
                           StARF10 
                          and
                           StARF17 
                          , miR160 controls a broader regulatory network spanning auxin signaling, cell‐wall remodeling, redox homeostasis, and tuberization. Elevated miR160 levels promote susceptibility‐associated traits, reduce thermotolerance, and suppress genes strongly activated in HR.
                         
                       
                       
                         
                          Mechanistically, we identify a novel miR160–
                           StARF10/StARF17 
                          –
                           StPRX28 
                          module that links miR160 repression to the induction of a Class III apoplastic peroxidase in HR, with SA acting upstream. Together, these findings establish miR160 as an important regulatory node that connects SA–auxin–redox signaling pathways and tunes development, defense, and heat resilience, and highlight miR160 as a promising target for fine‐tuning tolerance to multiple stresses with minimal yield loss.

title:
Engineering
                     uORFs 
                    in wheat improves abiotic stress tolerance without growth penalties
authors:
Xiaomin Si, 
Yonghui Yan, 
Shenglong Bai, 
Guanghui Guo, 
Panpan Xiao, 
Mengxiao Hu, 
Kai Xia, 
Yongqi Ren, 
Jintao Jiang, 
Rong Fan, 
Xiang Ji, 
Yue Wang, 
Hao Li, 
Tingting Dang, 
Qinmin Gao, 
Luyu Liu, 
Changbin Xiong, 
Kangpeng Liu, 
Yun Zhou, 
Chun‐Peng Song
abstract:
Summary 
                   
                     
                       
                         Developing climate‐resilient crops is critical for ensuring global food security, yet agricultural productivity is frequently constrained by the trade‐off between stress tolerance and growth. This challenge is particularly acute in allohexaploid wheat, a staple crop susceptible to abiotic stresses, underscoring the demand for precise gene regulation. 
                       
                       
                         
                          Here, we established a simple, efficient, and transgene‐free method for regulating gene expression in allohexaploid wheat by disrupting or creating
                           de novo 
                          upstream open reading frames (uORFs) via genome editing.
                         
                       
                       
                         
                          Using ribosome profiling, we identified 1199 actively translated uORFs across the wheat genome and developed a dual‐luciferase screening pipeline to pinpoint potent translational repressors of positive regulators of abiotic stress. CRISPR/Cas9‐mediated disruption of the uORFs in
                           TaCIPK14 
                          and
                           TaGGP1 
                          elevated downstream protein accumulation, thereby enhancing drought, cold, and salt tolerance of plants. Furthermore, base editing was employed to generate
                           de novo 
                          uORFs in
                           TaMADS26, 
                          effectively downregulating gene expression and improving drought resilience. Notably, both the transgene‐free
                           uorf 
                           
                             TaGGP1‐ACG 
                           
                          and uORF
                           TaMADS26
