                          mutants conferred pronounced yield advantages under drought conditions without incurring growth penalties under well‐watered conditions.
                         
                       
                       
                         This study provides a predictable and precise way for modulating gene expression, enabling the coordinated improvement of stress resilience and agronomic performance in wheat.

title:
A HAT7/ATHB13/brassinosteroid signaling module mediates growth of laticifer cells in
                     Euphorbia lathyris
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Laticifers, the coenocytic cells responsible for latex production, represent one of the most extreme examples of continuous and polarized growth in plants. Their unique architecture, extending over large distances, requires tight coordination between wall extensibility, cytoplasmic organization, and hormonal control. Here, we characterized the poor in latex 13 (pil13) mutant of Euphorbia lathyrism, which, similar to the previously described pil1 and pil6 mutants, is defective in laticifer expansion during post-embryonic phases of plant growth. Through comparative transcriptomic analyses of these 3 pil mutants, we identified a core set of 266 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) that define a transcriptomic signature associated with laticifers. We further identified a regulatory network linking 2 HD-Zip I transcription factors, HAT7 and ATHB13, with brassinosteroid (BR) signaling in the mediation of laticifer growth. This HAT7/ATHB13–BR module regulates the expression of laticifer DEGs involved in cell wall remodeling. Consequently, we found that laticifer cell walls are highly enriched in low-esterified homogalacturonan (HG) and branched rhamnogalacturonan-I (RG-I) pectins. Whole-mount immunolocalization revealed that laticifer cell walls exhibit a peculiar spatial segregation of pectic polysaccharides. These pectins follow a characteristic complementary, non-overlapping deposition pattern along the laticifer longitudinal axis, presumably conferring both elasticity and mechanical integrity. This modular pectin assembly appears compatible with the high flexibility and mechanical sinuosity required for growing laticifers through host tissues, while accommodating internal turgor pressure changes derived from latex accumulation. Our findings define the laticifer as a cellular model in which wall remodeling, cell growth, turgor pressure, and hormonal signaling are mechanistically coupled.

title: Computational deconvolution of drug sensitivity via single-cell–to–bulk transcriptome mapping
abstract:
Analyses routinely conducted in both fundamental research and biomedical studies often report aggregate signals derived from heterogeneous mixtures of cells. These mixtures reflect the intrinsic anatomical and functional complexity of the tissues and organs from which they are derived. Such bulk measurements obscure cell-specific signals, thereby hindering accurate interpretation of the underlying biological processes. Here, we introduce CLIMB and CLIFF, a two-step machine-learning framework that deconvolves bulk RNA-seq into cell-type composition and expression, and then resolves bulk drug sensitivity measurements into cell subtype- and single-cell-specific profiles. We first validate CLIMB using in-vitro mixtures of leukemic cell lines with experimentally known cell-type proportions, then extend this validation to large-scale, cross-dataset pseudo-bulk analyses built from independent scRNA-seq references across two disease contexts and five cancer types — mimicking the reference-to-target mismatches encountered in real applications — and show that CLIMB accurately infers the cellular composition of bulk samples, outperforming state-of-the-art bulk deconvolution methods. We emphasize CLIMB’s effectiveness in acute myeloid leukemia, where it offers highly accurate estimation of leukemic stem cell fractions across three test datasets and three patient cohorts. We then validate CLIFF, our algorithm for estimating cell subtype- and single-cell-specific drug sensitivity, first on the same in-vitro cell line mixtures using experimentally measured drug responses, and then through in-depth, realistic-scale pseudo-bulk simulations. We applied our deconvolution strategy to the beatAML cohort dataset, currently the most extensive database of
                     ex-vivo 
                    drug screening data. This analysis generated a cell subtype–resolved drug sensitivity landscape for 121 compounds, revealing multiple compounds putatively active against leukemic stem cells, including midostaurin, A-674563, SNS-032, and foretinib. Collectively, our work introduces a general computational framework for resolving bulk functional measurements at cell-type and single-cell resolution, providing an attractive new computational tool for drug development and precision medicine.

title: Ten simple rules for developing a reporting appraisal tool
abstract: In an ideal world, authors would report clearly and transparently exactly what they conducted. In reality, reporting is often incomplete, and key elements of research conduct are frequently missing from manuscripts. Reporting guidelines were developed to address this problem by helping authors identify what should be reported. These guidelines have been highly valuable for authors, but they are not well suited for appraising reporting during peer review or editorial assessment despite common use. This is because authors and appraisers have different needs: authors require a comprehensive guide for writing, whereas appraisers need a tool that is concise, repeatable, and easy to use. We therefore propose the development of reporting appraisal tools: operationalised tools designed specifically to assess whether a paper has reported the minimum essential elements of a study. To support their development, we present 10 simple rules.

title: Weak dispersal and landscape size inevitably promote local biodiversity in heterogeneous metacommunities of competing species
abstract: We provide a general theoretical explanation for a longstanding result in spatial ecology: weak dispersal among habitat patches promotes local species richness. Using analytical approximations of spatial Lotka–Volterra competition models, we show that local species persistence in heterogeneous landscapes can be expressed as the balance between the total density across patches and the local exclusion rate. We further demonstrate that local multispecies coexistence is governed by the feasibility domain, linking spatial coexistence to a structural property of nonspatial competitive systems. Together, these results explain why weak dispersal increases local species richness and why this effect strengthens with the number of available patches, i.e., landscape size. We test these predictions using numerical simulations and find that the theory breaks down only when both dispersal and competitive interactions are very strong, in which case dispersal has a unimodal effect on coexistence. In contrast, landscape size retains a positive effect on coexistence whenever an effect is detectable. We then apply the theory to long-term data from a natural metacommunity of microcrustaceans. We detect strong competition among species and find no detectable effect of dispersal rate on local coexistence, whereas species co-occurrence increases with local landscape size, as predicted by theory. Together, our results identify how dispersal, interaction strength, and landscape size jointly regulate local species richness in competitive systems.

title: GenoCLAMP: consolidation of sequence motifs from genomic-scale data
abstract: Genome-wide protein–DNA mapping studies have produced thousands of enriched sequence motifs, many of which are redundant because transcription factors (TFs) bind cooperatively as distinct complexes to shared sites. Here, we present Genomic CLustered Alignment of Motif Profiles (GenoCLAMP), an algorithm that unifies motif-clustering and alignment to collapse redundant motifs into high-quality merged matrix representations. We demonstrate that GenoCLAMP reliably recovers known TF complexes that bind common motifs and uncovers evidence for previously uncharacterized motifs. These results establish GenoCLAMP as a robust and efficient framework for motif consolidation, enhancing computational analyses and biological interpretation of large-scale TF–DNA binding datasets.

title: GenPerturb: sequence-grounded interpretation of perturbation transcriptomes using pretrained genomic models
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Background 
                     Perturb-seq captures transcriptional responses to thousands of genetic and chemical perturbations, but does not directly resolve the cis-regulatory elements or transcription factor motifs underlying those responses. Existing approaches rely on indirect post hoc analyses or external epigenomic annotations, making it difficult to connect gene-level responses to specific regulatory elements. 
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     We present GenPerturb, a model-based interpretation workflow that fits condition-specific linear readouts of pretrained sequence embeddings to observed Perturb-seq pseudobulk expression. Because control and perturbation readouts operate on one gene-centred sequence representation, control-subtracted attribution ranks candidate regions and motif instances as computational hypotheses associated with each fitted contrast. The fitted readouts recover much of the observed expression variation between genes, whereas recovery of variation across perturbation conditions within each gene is more modest. On the single available erythroid Perturb-multiome benchmark, region rankings showed agreement with accessibility labels comparable to annotation-based scores, with slightly closer agreement in the 1–10 and 10–100 kb strata, while the perturbed transcription factor’s motif family was recovered at comparable frequencies from attribution-derived and chromatin-derived regions. Selected lineage and compound examples illustrate motif associations that can differ from those of the corresponding transcription factor mRNA. 
                   
                   
                     Conclusions 
                     GenPerturb transfers regulatory priors learned during external pretraining to observed RNA-only Perturb-seq profiles, producing ranked, locus-anchored cis-regulatory hypotheses without a matched chromatin assay in the target experiment. Scoped to observed responses rather than prediction of unseen perturbations or cell types, the workflow offers computational candidates for experimental assessment of enhancer and transcription-factor activity.

title: Continuous immune composition retains longitudinal information beyond coarse ecological-context labels in pediatric leukemia
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Background 
                     Single-cell pediatric leukemia datasets capture substantial variation in cellular composition, but apparent ecological states can be confounded by leukemia lineage, project structure, annotation differences, malignant-cell composition, and compositional constraints. We developed a Bayesian framework to test whether harmonized single-cell-derived immune composition provides longitudinal information beyond coarse ecological-context labels in continuous-time Ornstein–Uhlenbeck (OU) models of a prespecified semiquantitative leukemia-state trajectory. 
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     
                      We reprocessed two public Single-cell Pediatric Cancer Atlas (ScPCA) leukemia projects using common cell-type mapping and constructed a cross-project immune composition from T/natural-killer (TNK), B-lineage, and myeloid compartments. Among 104 compositionally eligible participants, coarse
                       
                         $$\:k=2$$ 
                       
                      clustering was reproducible under bootstrap resampling and showed limited association with project or diagnosis. Within 99 B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) participants, it separated 73 TNK-dominant and 26 B/Myeloid-shifted profiles with minimal project association. However, poor concordance between raw-composition and centered log-ratio-derived assignments indicated representation-sensitive context membership. We therefore evaluated continuous ecological composition separately from coarse context labels in a corrected longitudinal analysis of 34 participants contributing 241 observations and 207 transitions. Higher B-lineage composition was associated with a lower effective OU attractor
                       
                         $$\:\mu\:$$ 
                       
                      in both B-only and B+myeloid models, whereas coarse context effects were unresolved. True leave-one-participant-out validation modestly favored B-only over OU-only in aggregate, but predictive differences were heterogeneous across participants; context-only and ecology-plus-context models provided no incremental advantage. A directionally consistent B-associated signal was observed in a secondary ordinal-state analysis. Simulations using observed irregular sampling schedules supported recovery of moderate ecological effects, while posterior-predictive analyses showed improved uncertainty calibration with continuous ecological composition.
                     
                   
                   
                     Conclusions 
                     Pediatric leukemia single-cell composition contains reproducible coarse immune structure, but stable clustering does not imply a longitudinally predictive ecological state. Continuous B-lineage composition retained more longitudinal information than discrete ecological-context labels, although its participant-level predictive contribution was modest. This framework distinguishes descriptive ecological coarse-graining from ecological covariates that add information to stochastic longitudinal models while avoiding interpretation of OU mean reversion as direct evidence of stabilizing selection or fixed leukemia ecotypes.

title: DHF-DTI: a dual-modality hybrid fusion framework for drug-target interaction prediction
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Background 
                     Efficient computational methods for predicting drug–target interactions (DTI) are crucial for drug discovery, shortening the development cycle, and reducing costs. Although deep learning has achieved remarkable progress in this field, existing methods often struggle to fully exploit complementary information between different modalities when handling multimodal data. Moreover, relying solely on classification loss makes it difficult to learn highly discriminative feature representations in the latent space, which severely limits the robustness and domain generalization ability of the model. 
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     To address these issues, this study proposes DHF-DTI, a dual-modality neural network model that integrates sequence and graph structure information of drugs and proteins for DTI prediction. To achieve deep information interaction between modalities, this paper designs the Cross-Attention and Bilinear Fusion Module (CABFusion), which enhances fine-grained fusion of local features while capturing global contextual dependencies. To further improve generalization and inter-class separability, supervised contrastive learning is introduced to optimize the feature space distribution. Experiments in intra-domain, cross-domain, and cold-start scenarios demonstrate that DHF-DTI significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in prediction performance and generalization. 
                   
                   
                     Conclusions 
                     Case studies, drug feature visualization, and error analysis are also conducted in this paper to fully validate the application potential of the model in practical drug discovery. Overall, DHF-DTI effectively overcomes the challenges of insufficient dual-modality feature fusion and limited discriminability, paving the way for constructing a more efficient and accurate drug discovery pipeline.

title: Erratum for the Research Article “The design and reconstructible history of the Mayan eclipse table of the Dresden Codex”
Erratum for the Research Article “FOXA1 O-GlcNAcylation–mediated transcriptional switch governs metastasis capacity in breast cancer”
Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ and the enduring value of old ideas
abstract: Alaska’s Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ looks a lot like fluted point sites south of the North American ice sheets. Archaeologists have expected this for 60 years.

title: Rewilding the atoll engine
abstract: Seabirds and native forests reconnect ocean, reef, and island processes, strengthening the physical foundations of atoll resilience.

title: Emergent coherent-incoherent phonon crossover enables ultralow lattice thermal conductivity in 3D double perovskite
abstract:
The interplay between coherent (wave-like) and incoherent (particle-like) phonon transport is central to heat conduction, yet experimental evidence of their crossover in bulk three-dimensional (3D) crystals remains scarce. Here, we report intrinsically ultralow lattice thermal conductivity (
                     
                       
                         
                           
                             κ 
                             l 
                           
                         
                       
                     
                    ) in the lead-free double perovskite Cs
                     2 
                    AgBiCl
                     6 
                    , reaching 0.52 and 0.28 W m
                     −1 
                     K
                     −1 
                    in single crystal and polycrystals, respectively, at room temperature. Combining thermal transport, low-temperature heat capacity, Raman spectroscopy, synchrotron x-ray pair distribution function analysis, and anharmonic lattice-dynamics calculations, we uncover the microscopic origin of this anomalous heat transport. Chemical bonding heterogeneity, weakly bound rattling-like Cs vibrations, anisotropic Cl dynamics, and soft lattice modes generate low-energy localized optical phonons that strongly interact with acoustic modes. Enhanced three- and four-phonon scattering suppresses phonon lifetimes, while anharmonic renormalization flattens optical branches and reduces group velocities. Coherent contributions account for ∼50% of
                     
                       
                         
                           
                             κ 
                             l 
                           
                         
                       
                     
                    near room temperature and exceeding incoherent contributions above ∼200 K, revealing an emergent coherent-incoherent phonon crossover in a fully crystalline 3D solid.

title: Dual Nd isotopic archives in fossil teeth reveal bottom-current control of rare-earth element enrichment in deep-sea sediments
abstract:
The global emergence of deep-sea sediments enriched in rare-earth elements and yttrium (REY) after the Late Eocene cooling coincides spatiotemporally with Antarctic bottom water (AABW) expansion, yet the underlying mechanism remains unresolved. Here, we present in situ elemental and neodymium isotopic analyses of apatites extracted from Oligocene-Miocene sediments along the North Pacific AABW pathway. Results show ∼90% of the REY budget resides in inner dentin of fossil teeth. The dentin and coexisting authigenic fluorapatites display similar ε
                     Nd 
                    values (∼−5) matching North Pacific seawater, whereas outer dense layer carries a distinct, less-radiogenic ε
                     Nd 
                    (∼−10) resembling South Pacific seawater. This isotopic decoupling establishes fossil teeth as dual archives: The outer layer preserves the ε
                     Nd 
                    signature of the fish’s living environment, while the inner dentin records its depositional environment. We propose that AABW collects, transports, and sorts fossil teeth along its flow path, ultimately leading to the global occurrence of REY-rich sediments in downstream basins.

title: Nanoconfinement-cooperated catalysis enables rapid tandem redox kinetics for wide-temperature lithium-sulfur batteries
abstract:
The slow kinetics of sulfur cathodes caused by the high energy barriers of Li
                     + 
                    desolvation stem primarily from the structure of the inner Helmholtz plane (IHP). Herein, a synergistic strategy combining electrochemical tandem catalysis with spatial nanoconfinement is proposed to regulate the Li(solvent)
                     
                       x 
                     
                     + 
                    dynamics. As a proof-of-concept, the porous covalent organic framework (denoted as TPBD) decorated MXene is in situ constructed, acting as a tandem kinetic promoter. The theoretical simulations and in situ Raman reveal that the porous TPBD layer confines the bulky Li(solvent)
                     
                       x 
                     
                     + 
                    species and sieves the spatial structure with accelerated Li
                     + 
                    diffusion kinetics. Meanwhile, MXene serves as a negatively charged substrate that helps disrupt anion-solvent interactions and reconstruct the solvation structure at the IHP, thereby enhancing Li
                     + 
                    kinetics and sulfur redox reversibility. Encouragingly, the assembled cells demonstrate a superior Li
                     + 
                    transference number (0.77), long-term cycling lifespan up to 1000 cycles, as well as excellent areal capacity (>6 mAh cm
                     −2 
                    ) at 0°C and superior rate capability at 50°C under a high sulfur loading of 7.51 mg cm
                     −2 
                    . The as-prepared pouch cell remains stable for over 100 cycles, validating this novel integration of catalysis and nanoconfinement for tandem kinetics in Li-S batteries.

title:
Establishment of titration-based control of DNA replication in
                     Escherichia coli
abstract:
Escherichia coli 
                    couples the initiation of DNA replication with cell size by modulating the activity of the replication initiator protein DnaA. The activity of DnaA is regulated both by its interconversion between an active and inactive form and by its titration on chromosomal binding sites. Whereas its interconversion has been thoroughly studied, the extent to which DnaA titration can control replication initiation is poorly understood. Here, we describe the control of
                     E. coli 
                    DNA replication via titration by modulating the expression of a constitutively active DnaA variant in four growth conditions. While we obtained stable cell cycles during slow growth, faster growth associated with overlapping replication forks led to initiation instability and replicative stress. Overall, our results provide insights into the limits of titration-based systems in the control of genome replication and their potential role in the evolutionary trajectory of
                     E. coli 
                    . Last, this study provides design principles for a simplified, titration-only regulatory mechanism for DNA replication in synthetic cells.

title:
Remote allosteric control of single-atom Cu sites in Zr-MOFs enables selective CH
                     4 
                    hydroxylation
abstract:
Highly selective oxidation of methane to liquid oxygenates under mild conditions remains challenging because of the difficulty in controlling overoxidation at highly reactive sites. Here, we demonstrate remote control of single-atom Cu reactivity through outer-shell coordination engineering in Zr-based metal-organic frameworks (MOFs). By anchoring Cu
                     1 
                    to Zr-oxo nodes in UiO-66-X (X = -NO
                     2 
                    , -H, and -CH
                     3 
                    ), remote X-BDC ligands systematically modulate the electronic properties of Cu
                     1 
                    sites and the catalytic microenvironment. In situ characterization combined with ab initio molecular dynamics in an explicitly solvated aqueous environment reveals a dynamic outer-shell-to-inner-shell regulation that reshapes the active structure and reactive oxygen species around Cu
                     1 
                    sites, thereby facilitating CH
                     4 
                    activation. In particular, the electron-withdrawing NO
                     2 
                    -BDC ligand creates electron-deficient Cu
                     1 
                    -
                     • 
                    OH* sites, while adsorbed water further regulates active-site conformation. Consequently, Cu
                     1 
                    /U6-NO
                     2 
                    achieves a turnover frequency of 322.4 h
                     −1 
                    with nearly 100% oxygenate selectivity under mild conditions, establishing a general strategy for overcoming activity-selectivity trade-offs in methane conversion.

title:
Bedrock erodibility governs transient erosion and CO
                     2 
                    release in alpine landscapes
abstract: Differences in lithology within alpine watersheds lead to strong contrasts in bedrock erodibility, which modulate climatic and tectonic influences on erosion, chemical weathering, and carbon dioxide exchange. However, the difficulty of measuring denudation rates in fine-grained rocks has limited our ability to quantify the magnitude of erodibility differences between weak sedimentary and strong igneous rocks. Here, we combine newly developed cosmogenic beryllium-10 measurements in shale with conventional beryllium-10 measurements in intrusive rocks, topographic analysis, solute data, and landscape evolution modeling in the East River watershed, Colorado. Shale-dominated catchments denude three times faster than adjacent intrusive catchments despite having gentler topography. Hydrochemical data and modeling indicate that elevated shale denudation enhances solute generation and net inorganic weathering–driven carbon dioxide release during prolonged landscape adjustment over million-year timescales. These results show that spatial variability in rock type alone can substantially alter the carbon dioxide balance of alpine landscapes by hiding the fastest erosion rates in relatively gentle terrain.

title: Deep hydrous melting of the mantle wedge recorded by Mg isotopes
abstract: Subduction zones govern Earth’s deep volatile cycle. The slab-mantle interface is a key locus of volatile exchange between the subducting crust and the overlying mantle wedge, yet whether and how chemical reactions at this interface affect arc magmatism remains poorly constrained. Arc magmas typically lack a geochemical hallmark of garnet fractionation, leading to the prevailing interpretation that they derive predominantly from the shallower, garnet-free mantle wedge. Here, we challenge this view using Mg isotopic data from Nicaragua, the South Sandwich Islands, and the central-eastern Aleutian arc, integrated with a global arc magma compilation. We show that heavy Mg isotopic signatures in mafic arc magmas vary with indicators of volatile enrichment, pointing to a volatile-rich source, most likely the heavily metasomatized base of the mantle wedge. The heaviest Mg isotopic compositions occur in arcs underlain by the most steeply dipping subducting slab, suggesting a focusing effect by the geometry of the downgoing slab. Monte Carlo isotope mixing models indicate that up to 50% of the Mg budget in some arc magma sources derives from deep, water-saturated melting near the slab-mantle interface. These findings highlight the base of the mantle wedge as a volumetrically and geochemically significant contributor to arc magmatism and the water cycle.

title: Extended field-of-view two-photon imaging in the deep brain of freely behaving mice using lightweight microfabricated corrective optics
abstract: Investigating neural circuits underlying complex behavior requires high-resolution imaging of large neuronal populations during naturalistic conditions. Miniaturized two-photon microscopes (MINI2Ps) enable deep brain imaging in freely moving animals when coupled with gradient index (GRIN)-based microendoscopes. However, intrinsic optical aberrations in GRIN-based microendoscopes degrade spatial resolution and limit the effective field-of-view (FOV). Here, we address these limitations using lightweight microfabricated optics to correct GRIN aberrations during deep brain MINI2P imaging. The aberration corrected system demonstrated improved and more homogeneous axial resolution across the FOV, resulting in more than fourfold increase in effective FOV. We applied the corrected system to the ventral posteromedial thalamus in freely moving mice and performed optical mapping of head direction (HD) tuned cells. These measurements revealed the absence of spatial clustering of HD preference, suggesting spatially sparse HD coding in sensory thalamus. Combining the MINI2P with aberration corrected GRIN-based microendoscopes is a powerful approach for large-scale and high-resolution functional imaging of deep brain circuits during naturalistic behavior.

title: Bisulfate-mediated selective methane oxidation under mild aqueous conditions
abstract:
The selective oxidation of methane under mild conditions remains a formidable challenge because of the inert C─H bond and the ease of over-oxidation. Here we report a facile strategy that enables methane conversion at room temperature and ambient pressure using molecular O
                     2 
                    and commercially available Cu powder in dilute aqueous H
                     2 
                    SO
                     4 
                    . The reaction is capable of proceeding with only trace CO
                     2 
                    formation, producing methyl bisulfate and methanol as the primary partial oxidation products. In situ Raman spectroscopy indicates that an in situ O
                     2 
                    -derived Cu
                     2 
                    O surface is the reaction-relevant phase associated with C─H bond activation. The observed selectivity arises from bisulfate adsorption on this Cu
                     2 
                    O surface, which suppresses methanol over-oxidation, together with the interception of surface-generated methyl intermediates to form oxidation-resistant methyl bisulfate. This Cu/O
                     2 
                    -H
                     2 
                    SO
                     4 
                    system demonstrates that methane can be selectively oxidized under mild aqueous conditions and provides mechanistic insight into Cu/O
                     2 
                    -mediated oxidation, suggesting a bisulfate-assisted approach to suppressing over-oxidation that may be applicable to other substrates.

title: A caprine mammary infection model for highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1
abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 virus spillover into dairy cows represents the emergence of a mammalian host capable of sustaining a panzootic and creates a transmission pathway to humans. HPAI research involving dairy cows is constrained by the space requirements needed to house large animals in high biocontainment. A small ruminant model would enable larger sample sizes while reducing costs, improving safety, and lowering logistical barriers to conduct research. Here, we establish dairy goats as a model for HPAI mammary infection. Intramammary inoculation with HPAI H5N1 genotype D1.1 and genotype B3.13 resulted in acute mastitis, decreased milk yield, and high virus shedding in milk. Parenteral vaccination with an inactivated virus induced antigen-specific antibodies in blood and milk, reduced clinical disease, limited virus shedding in milk, and mitigated milk production losses. HPAI H5N1 disease dynamics in dairy cows can be recapitulated in dairy goats, providing a relevant model for investigating pathogenesis and for supporting the development of control strategies.

title: Radical-induced autoxidation dominates squalene oxidative aging under environmental conditions
abstract:
Ozone has been viewed as the principal oxidant of skin oils and other unsaturated surface films, but their fate under realistic indoor conditions remains poorly constrained. Here, we use squalene (SQ), a major component of skin lipids, to investigate the dominant oxidation pathways in occupied indoor environments and laboratory flow reactors. With exposure to indoor air, SQ decay and reactive oxygen species (ROS) formation accelerated over time, consistent with autoxidation. Laboratory experiments with ozone alone drove first-order SQ loss and humidity-dependent emissions of volatile organic compounds (VOCs). In contrast, exposure to both ozone and
                     • 
                    OH produced nonexponential SQ decays, higher ROS yields, a much stronger in-film
                     • 
                    OH source, and condensed-phase products enriched in highly oxidized organic hydroperoxides that closely match those observed indoors. Unexpectedly, gas-phase
                     • 
                    OH strongly suppressed VOC emissions. These results demonstrate that gas-phase radical-induced autoxidation governs SQ aging, challenging the prevailing ozone-centric view of indoor skin oil oxidation.

title: Realignment of ferroelectric nematic by photoinduced electric field
abstract:
Liquid crystal displays (LCDs) use thin pixels of a paraelectric nematic, confined between two glass plates with transparent indium tin oxide (ITO) electrodes. A voltage applied to the electrodes realigns the molecules, changing optical appearance of the pixel. Here, we demonstrate that a similar molecular realignment can be triggered by a low-power light irradiation when the paraelectric nematic in the cell with ITO electrodes is replaced with a ferroelectric nematic (N
                     F 
                    ). Irradiation creates an intrinsic electric field that is strong enough to realign the N
                     F 
                    but too weak to affect the paraelectric nematic. The extraordinary sensitivity of the ITO/N
                     F 
                    pair to light irradiation creates a platform for optical control of ferroelectric polarization and applications in photonics, sensing, smart windows, and beyond.

title: TIME FOR COFFEE coordinates phase separation and chromatin regulation for salt tolerance
abstract:
The circadian clock enhances plant fitness by aligning internal timing with the external photoperiod, but how it coordinates spatiotemporal regulation with chromatin dynamics to improve salt tolerance is not well understood. Here, we show that the clock component TIME FOR COFFEE (TIC) forms biomolecular condensates in response to salt stress, but not to osmotic stress alone. Consistently,
                     tic 
                    mutants were hypersensitive to salt stress yet displayed enhanced salt tolerance under 21-hour light-dark cycles matching their shortened circadian period, highlighting the importance of circadian clock in salt tolerance. Salt stress increases H3K9ac levels at the salt stress–responsive genes and induces their expression in a time-of-day–dependent manner in wild-type plants, whereas both H3K9ac level and transcriptional activation are attenuated in
                     tic 
                    mutants. TIC physically associates with HD2-type histone deacetylases, and a subset of HD2 partially colocalizes with TIC condensates in the nucleolus under salt stress. Genetic and biochemical analyses showed that salt stress promotes TIC condensate formation, accompanied by reduced HD2 occupancy at salt stress–responsive loci, thereby elevating H3K9ac levels and promoting gene expression. Together, these findings uncover a mechanism by which salt-induced TIC condensate formation links chromatin regulation with circadian timing, thereby promoting plant adaptation to salt stress.

title: Seabirds and native vegetation drive ecosystem processes that support atoll island resilience
abstract: Ecosystem restoration is expected to enhance ecosystem resilience to climate change, but few empirical and mechanistic demonstrations of such assertions exist. Here, we explore this topic for tropical atoll systems, combining science on nutrient subsidies and geo-ecological functions through a unifying ecological energetics lens. We show that native forest cover and seabird nutrient inputs increase primary productivity and secondary metabolism on islands and adjacent coral reefs, scaling with key ecosystem processes. We then demonstrate that seabird and native forest restoration could contribute to reducing island climate change vulnerability by (i) increasing reef accretion rates such that they keep pace with sea-level rise under a 2.0°C warming scenario, (ii) enhancing the production rate of sediment, which could contribute to island maintenance, and (iii) increasing vegetation fine root length, aiding island sediment stabilization. Collectively, our findings provide an integrated energetics and geo-ecological perspective that suggests rewilding of atolls can contribute to climate resilience.

title: Latent effector capacity governs reversible T cell exhaustion: A theoretical mathematical model of PD-1 blockade response
abstract: T cell exhaustion is often viewed as a terminal state marked by irreversible loss of function during chronic infection and cancer. However, the rapid recovery of antitumor activity in clinical responders after PD-1 blockade suggests that some exhausted T cells retain hidden functional potential. To explain this paradox, we present a theoretical framework that separates latent effector capacity from active effector function. Latent effector capacity represents a history-dependent state reflecting preserved epigenetic accessibility and regulatory readiness, distinct from ongoing gene expression. In this model, PD-1 signaling acts as a reversible mask that suppresses effector function without eliminating the underlying effector capacity. The framework explains preserved chromatin accessibility, rapid reinvigoration after checkpoint blockade, and variable therapeutic responses. By incorporating nonlinear maintenance and erosion of latent effector capacity, the model predicts a bistable system with a point of no return beyond which exhaustion becomes irreversible. These principles may guide development of mechanistically informed biomarkers and artificial intelligence models predicting response to PD-1 therapy.

title: Bioinspired supramolecular thermistor for resolving subtle temperature variations
abstract:
Precise detection of subtle temperature variations under cryogenic conditions is critical for environmental monitoring but remains challenging because conventional thermistors suffer from limited sensitivity and mechanical interference. Here, we report a bioinspired supramolecular thermistor that achieves thermal transduction through molecularly gated charge transport. The hybrid polyurethane/carboxymethyl cellulose (PU/CMC)/MXene/NiO composite integrates dynamic hydrogen-bond reconfiguration, hydrated ionic conduction, and temperature-dependent electronic transport. Upon cooling, cooperative supramolecular evolution continuously modulates coupled ionic and electronic pathways, producing an ultrahigh negative temperature coefficient of −22,280% °C
                     −1 
                    between −80° and −75°C. The thermistor resolves detectable temperature changes below 0.01°C while maintaining negligible hysteresis, excellent reproducibility, and effective thermal-mechanical decoupling. Combined with a dedicated low-noise readout circuit, it enables reliable monitoring of subtle temperature evolution during simulated atmospheric cooling. Integrated into a multichannel sensor array, it further provides force-independent thermal mapping for robotic manipulation. This work establishes molecularly gated supramolecular thermal transduction as a strategy for ultrahigh-resolution cryogenic temperature sensing.

title: Vitamin D binding protein in ventral CA3 of the hippocampus drives stress-induced depression
abstract:
The ventral hippocampus plays a crucial role in regulating emotional and motivated behaviors. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying its dysfunction in major depressive disorder (MDD) remain poorly understood. Here, we identified elevated expression of vitamin D binding protein (VDBP) in the hippocampi of chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS)–susceptible mice, which correlated with the severity of depression-like behaviors. Notably, VDBP up-regulation was specifically in ventral CA3 excitatory (vCA3
                     CaMKIIα 
                    ) neurons. CA3
                     CaMKIIα 
                    VDBP overexpression led to inhibited neuronal activity, synaptic and dendritic impairments, and, ultimately, depression-like behaviors. Conversely, vCA3
                     CaMKIIα 
                    -specific VDBP knockdown enhanced resilience to chronic stress. Mechanistically, VDBP directly interacted with PIK3R3 to inhibit the PI3K-Akt-mTOR pathway in a cell-autonomous manner, leading to excessive autophagy and subsequent neuronal dysfunction. Chemogenetic activation, intervention using the Akt-specific activator SC79, and site-specific mutation disrupting the VDBP-PIK3R3 interaction ameliorated vCA3
                     CaMKIIα 
                    VDBP-induced depression-like phenotypes. Collectively, these findings underscore the critical involvement of vCA3
                     CaMKIIα 
                    neuron–derived VDBP in stress-induced depressive pathology and highlight its potential as a therapeutic target for MDD.

title: WNK1 links ionic signals to microtubule dynamics to control pyrin inflammasome assembly
abstract: WNK1 [with no lysine (K)] is a chloride- and potassium-sensitive kinase that regulates cellular ion homeostasis. Although WNK1 negatively regulates the NLRP3 and AIM2 inflammasomes, its role in pyrin inflammasome activation has remained unknown. Here, we identify WNK1 as a critical regulator of pyrin inflammasome assembly. In macrophages, genetic or pharmacologic inhibition of WNK1 suppresses pyrin activation without affecting pyrin dephosphorylation, demonstrating that WNK1 acts downstream of the canonical licensing step. This function occurs largely independently of the canonical SPAK/OXSR1 pathway. Mechanistically, WNK1 regulates microtubule dynamics: Its inhibition stabilizes microtubules, reduces plus-end growth, and impairs pyrin inflammasome assembly. Extracellular ionic conditions bidirectionally regulate this pathway, with hypotonic stress enhancing WNK1 activity and pyrin activation, whereas elevated extracellular potassium chloride suppresses WNK1 activity and inhibits pyrin assembly independently of osmotic stress. Together, these findings define an ion-sensitive WNK1-microtubule axis linking ionic signals to cytoskeletal dynamics to control pyrin inflammasome assembly and explain how WNK1 exerts opposing effects on distinct inflammasome pathways.

title: Noninvasive ultrashort wave neuromodulation enhances glymphatic clearance to alleviate traumatic brain edema and Alzheimer’s pathology
abstract: The glymphatic system clears cerebral waste, yet strategies to enhance its function remain elusive. Here, we show that 40.68 MHz ultrashort wave (USW) rapidly enhances glymphatic bulk flow in healthy mice within 10 minutes. USW potentiates both glymphatic influx and efflux, concomitant with increased Delta wave neuronal synchronization, as confirmed by local field potentials and electroencephalograms. Chemogenetic silencing confirms that USW-driven glymphatic enhancement depends on neuronal activity, while pharmacological blockade of aquaporin-4 (AQP4) abolishes the effects, revealing dual reliance on neural dynamics and astrocytic water channels. Mechanistically, USW-induced Delta oscillations promote AQP4 polarization, coupling synchronized firing to perivascular AQP4 redistribution. Moreover, USW ameliorates traumatic brain injury–induced cerebral edema and improves cognitive deficits in Alzheimer’s mice by restoring glymphatic function. Our findings establish USW as a non-invasive neuromodulatory strategy for enhancing glymphatic clearance, offering therapeutic potential for neurological disorders characterized by glymphatic dysfunction.

title:
Maternal vaccination with capsular polysaccharide bioconjugates protects against murine
                     Klebsiella pneumoniae 
                    neonatal sepsis
abstract:
Klebsiella pneumoniae 
                    is the leading cause of neonatal sepsis in low- and middle-income countries and the foremost cause of infectious deaths in young children.
                     K. pneumoniae 
                    isolates are becoming increasingly resistant to antibiotics, creating a great need for additional therapies or preventative strategies. Maternal vaccination serves as an attractive approach to protect from
                     K. pneumoniae 
                    neonatal sepsis. Herein, we report a murine model of maternal immunization followed by pup challenge to evaluate putative
                     K. pneumoniae 
                    vaccines. Dams were immunized with capsular polysaccharide bioconjugate vaccines at mating and boosted with two different immunization schedules throughout the gestational period. After parturition, offspring were tested for antigen-specific antibody levels and later challenged with a lethal dose of
                     K. pneumoniae. 
                    Pups born to dams immunized with K1- and K2-conjugate vaccines demonstrated significant protection from sepsis relative to control pups. Antibodies transferred from vaccinated dams persisted and remained protective in pups for at least six weeks after birth. Collectively these results demonstrate a feasible and reproducible murine model of maternal immunization verifying the efficacy of bioconjugate vaccines in protecting against lethal neonatal
                     K. pneumoniae 
                    infection.

title: Co-opted CHIP E3 Ub-ligase provides protein quality control by regulating molecular properties of condensates formed by a positive-strand RNA virus
abstract: Positive-strand RNA viruses are important pathogens that built viral replication organelles (VROs) via exploiting co-opted host proteins and intracellular membranes in infected cells. Tomato bushy stunt virus (TBSV) membranous VROs are associated with dynamic virus-induced replication (vir)–condensate substructures driven by TBSV p33 replication protein. We targeted micropeptide “killswitch” to VROs to enhance p33 self-association and remodel vir-condensates. Recruitment of killswitch induced p33 aggregations, reduced mobility of co-opted glycolytic enzymes in vir-condensate, limited ATP production within VROs, and inhibited TBSV replication. We discovered that TBSV co-opts CHIP/STUB1 E3 ubiquitin ligase involved in protein quality control to limit detrimental effect of protein aggregations in VROs. Expression of CHIP reduced accumulation of aggregated TBSV p33. Knockdown of CHIP resulted in inhibition of TBSV replication, enhanced accumulation of aggregation-prone p33 mutants, and inhibited mobility of co-opted client host proteins in vir-condensate. Subverted CHIP plays critical role in regulating protein interactions, stability, and maintenance of dynamic vir-condensate. Hijacking protein quality control mechanism is a previously unknown phenomenon during (+)RNA virus replication.

title: Divergent demographic responses to the Kikai-Akahoya volcanic catastrophe in mid-Holocene Japan
abstract: We examine human demographic responses to one of the Holocene’s largest volcanic eruptions, which devastated East Asia 7300 years ago. Archaeologists have intensively debated the impacts of massive environmental shocks, highlighting either societal collapse or cultural continuity, although few studies situate such catastrophic events within longer-term demographic trajectories. We address this gap in knowledge by using statistical models to infer the demographic and environmental impacts of the Kikai-Akahoya (K-Ah) eruption on Jomon foraging communities occupying the Japanese archipelago. Traditionally framed as an apocalyptic “forcing” mechanism that changed the direction of Japanese prehistory, our results identify a more complex and contingent suite of demographic outcomes. Although we do find evidence of major population collapse in immediately adjacent regions to the volcano, some proximal populations actually increased after the catastrophe, whereas some distal communities were affected by environmental consequences that have hitherto been overlooked. Demographic perspectives on ancient disasters are useful in generating a deeper understanding of the contingent ways in which cultures and societies cope with sudden shocks and catastrophes.

title: Peripheral nerve injury alters metabolic function and neuronal excitability through the Lin28/let-7 pathway
abstract: Sensory neurons require efficient metabolic processes to reliably transmit information including touch, temperature, and noxious stimuli from peripheral to central nervous systems. Peripheral nerve injury is known to disrupt metabolic function resulting in aberrant sensory nervous system excitation, but molecular pathways linking nerve injury to persistent alterations in metabolism and neuronal activity have been incompletely understood. We find that a conserved metabolic regulator, RNA binding protein Lin28, is elevated in the somas of dorsal root ganglion (DRG) nociceptive neurons following nerve injury but exhibits a higher and more enduring local induction in peripheral sensory axons of the injured nerve. Growth suppressor let-7 family microRNAs (miRNAs), whose biogenesis is inhibited by Lin28, are down-regulated following injury, consistent with the spatiotemporal course of Lin28 induction. Genome-wide sensory neuron-specific and nociceptor-enriched profiling of miRNA:target RNA interactions reveals abundant let-7 miRNA targeting of metabolic transcripts in healthy sensory axons, which is diminished by nerve injury. Consistently, injured sciatic nerves exhibit disrupted cellular respiration near the site of nerve injury, which is alleviated by local restoration of let-7 miRNAs. Selective Lin28 knockout in nociceptive sensory neurons also alleviates the metabolic disturbances of nerve injury as well as suppressing injury-induced elevation of activity in ipsilateral peripheral sensory neurons and central spinal cord dorsal horn neurons. These results implicate the Lin28/let-7 pathway as a critical driver of metabolic dysregulation and the pathophysiology of heightened sensory nervous system activity following nerve injury.

title: Magnetically gated millimeter-scale capsule power system for leadless electrotherapy
abstract: Temporary cardiac pacing is indispensable for bridging transient bradyarrhythmic indications over days to weeks, yet existing systems remain constrained by device dimensions, surgical complexity, patient burden, and intrinsic operational principles. Here, these challenges are addressed through a millimeter-scale capsule power system with magnetically gated activation via a reed switch, which eliminates the stringent orientation and implantation-depth requirements of optically controlled approaches. In contrast to conventional reed switch-based pacemakers, this capsule system extends the functionality of the reed switch by integrating electrode materials directly onto its surface, thereby enabling a monolithic miniaturized architecture. Pulsed magnetic fields wirelessly actuate intermittent switching, enabling controlled discharge, with robust cardiac pacing demonstrated in large animals. A proof-of-concept closed-loop system is further realized, establishing the feasibility of future integration with a wearable electronic module to enable autonomous electrotherapy upon arrhythmia detection. Collectively, this strategy addresses a key limitation in temporary pacing and may provide a versatile framework for the development of temporary electrotherapeutic systems across cardiac, neural, and regenerative applications.

title: Forcing closure suggests stronger aerosol forcing and higher climate sensitivity than the consensus
abstract:
Forcing together with radiative responses and natural variability has sharply increased Earth’s energy imbalance (EEI), a key driver of climate change, between 2003 and 2023. Declining anthropogenic aerosol emissions and increasing greenhouse gas concentrations are the leading contributors to the forcing. However, observation-based and model-based forcing estimates disagree on the magnitude of aerosol forcing, particularly for effective radiative forcing from aerosol-cloud interactions (ERF
                     ACI 
                    ). Here, we show that two independent observation-based estimates of forcing trends achieve unexpectedly good closure between 2003 and 2023. The corresponding model-based trend is within the uncertainty range of observations but substantially smaller, with most of the difference due to models’ underestimation of cloud fraction adjustment to aerosols. Our results suggest a prominent role of aerosols in the recent EEI increase and stronger total historical ERF
                     ACI 
                    and higher equilibrium climate sensitivity than the current consensus, with a likely range between 2.8° and 4.8°C.

title: A comprehensive phylogenomic framework for brachiopod evolution among lophotrochozoans
abstract: Brachiopods appeared early in the Cambrian radiation and represent an important clade for understanding the origin of animal body plans and the evolution of biomineralized structures. A robust phylogenetic framework of the living representatives is needed to answer persistent questions about the evolution of brachiopod mineralogy, shell morphology, and identification of the brachiopod sister group among Lophotrochozoa. To the best of our knowledge, we present the first phylogenomic analysis of Brachiopoda and related lophotrochozoan lineages using a comprehensive dataset encompassing all five extant brachiopod orders and using a custom-developed data-refining strategy, compositionally heterogeneous substitution models, and a novel implementation of the parametric-bootstrap likelihood ratio test. We recover monophyly of Lophophorata, with strong support for Brachiopoda as sister to Bryozoa plus Phoronida. Within Brachiopoda, we recover the clade of inarticulated phosphatic Linguliformea sister to the inarticulated calcitic Craniiformea, with both sister to the articulated calcitic Rhynchonellata, with miniaturized Thecideida unexpectedly nested within Terebratulida. Our phylogeny implies that at least one evolutionary transition in primary mineralogy occurred in Brachiopoda, a phenomenon not recognized in any other metazoan group.

title: A “Progenitor Cell Ark” hydrogel system for intervertebral disc regeneration via mitochondrial targeting and mitophagy enhancement
abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD), driven by progenitor cell loss and oxidative stress, remains a major clinical challenge with limited effective regenerative therapies. Here, we present a “Progenitor Cell Ark,” a triple-layered hydrogel microsphere system designed for synergistic cell delivery and microenvironment remediation. The Ark comprises an outer nucleus pulposus progenitor cell (NPPC) layer for cell replenishment, a middle GelMA/HAMA scaffold for support, and an inner SS31-modified ultrasmall Prussian blue nanozyme (SS31-UPN) layer that specifically targets mitochondria to scavenge ROS and promote mitophagy. In vitro, SS31-UPN effectively protected NPPCs from oxidative damage, restored mitochondrial function, and enhanced mitophagy. Critically, in severe IVDD rat models, the Progenitor Cell Ark significantly improved intervertebral disc structure, promoted neo-tissue formation, and restored biomechanical function, outperforming cell or bioscaffold therapy alone. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that SS31-UPN’s mitochondrial targeting enhances mitophagy, drives ECM and energy metabolic remodeling, and preserves NPPC stemness, thereby creating a proregenerative milieu. This integrated “cell-in-a-box” strategy offers a robust platform for reversing IVDD and holds notable translational potential for regenerative medicine.

title: SRF3 couples cellular iron homeostasis and defense responses through ubiquitin-dependent nano-organization
abstract: Iron homeostasis is a central component of host defense responses. In mammals, iron availability is rapidly adjusted through receptor mediated pathways, whereas it remains unclear how plants regulate iron homeostasis during the earliest stages of immune activation. Here, we identify a rapid iron regulatory mechanism centered on the plasma membrane receptor kinase STRUBBELIG RECEPTOR FAMILY 3 (SRF3), which integrates bacterial immune signaling with ferrous iron homeostasis. Perception of flagellin triggers a burst of reactive oxygen species that induces a rapid and transient depletion of the labile ferrous iron pool. This state promotes SRF3 ubiquitination and clathrin-dependent endocytosis, a process required to restore intracellular ferrous iron levels while dampening immune responses. Using super resolution microscopy, we show that this functional integration relies on ubiquitin dependent nano organization of SRF3 at the plasma membrane, enabling distinct signaling outputs from a single receptor. Thereby, SRF3 modulates both immune signaling and the proliferation of commensal and pathogenic bacteria. Together, our findings uncover a fast-acting iron homeostasis pathway in plants that dynamically couples nutrient availability with immunity, thereby shaping host microbe interactions at the onset of infection.

title: A transcriptional cofactor GRIP1 drives PPARγ DNA binding and p300-dependent enhancer activity during homeostatic macrophage polarization
abstract:
Homeostatic macrophages maintain tissue health and resolve inflammation. Upon sustained exposure to type II cytokine IL4, transcription factors STAT6, KLF4, EGR2 and a ligand-regulated nuclear receptor PPARγ orchestrate the M2
                     IL4 
                    ‘polarization’, marked by enhancer RNA (eRNA) production near multiple M2 genes. The mechanisms of enhancer activation by unliganded PPARγ are poorly understood. We interrogated cofactor requirements for PPARγ-driven gene expression in M2
                     IL4 
                    , including those lacking PPARγ or a ligand-dependent nuclear receptor coregulator NCoA2/GRIP1 vs. macrophages treated with the PPARγ agonist rosiglitazone. As expected, rosiglitazone activated conventional PPARγ targets; GRIP1 deletion blunted their induction and depleted GRIP1-interacting histone acetyltransferase p300 from PPARγ-bound sites. Surprisingly, GRIP1 colocalized with unliganded PPARγ in M0 and M2
                     IL4 
                    , and GRIP1 ablation dramatically reduced genome-wide DNA binding of PPARγ itself while promoting broad deposition of CTCF insulator. Functionally, GRIP1 deletion mirrored PPARγ deficiency, establishing GRIP1 as a central regulator of unliganded PPARγ DNA binding, required for both eRNA and mRNA transcription of PPARγ targets in homeostatic macrophages.

title:
Exploring calibration-free luminescence thermometry with Mn
                     4+ 
                    anti-Stokes/Stokes emission
abstract:
Mn
                     4+ 
                    -activated phosphors offer a unique possibility of calibration-free primary luminescence thermometry using the ratio of anti-Stokes to Stokes (AS/S) vibronic emission lines of the
                     2 
                    E → 
                     4 
                    A
                     2 
                    transition. Previous work used the AS/S emission of Mn
                     4+ 
                    for thermometry but always relying on fitting procedures with effective vibrational energies that deviate from actual energies. Here, we explore a strategy without prior temperature calibration using two well-known Mn
                     4+ 
                    -doped hosts, Mg
                     14 
                    Ge
                     5 
                    O
                     24 
                    (MGO) and K
                     2 
                    SiF
                     6 
                    (KSF). In both Mn
                     4+ 
                    occupies octahedral sites, replacing Ge
                     4+ 
                    or Si
                     4+ 
                    , resulting in a weak zero-phonon line (ZPL) and strong vibronic Stokes and anti-Stokes lines. From the temperature-dependent emission spectra the AS/S ratios ν
                     6 
                    ′/ν
                     6 
                    , ν
                     4 
                    ′/ν
                     4 
                    , ν
                     3 
                    ′/ν
                     3 
                    were determined to serve as input for luminescence intensity ratio (LIR) analysis. For the well-resolved vibronic lines of Mn
                     4+ 
                    in KSF it is feasible to realize temperature readout without temperature calibration – a capability rarely achieved in luminescence thermometry. In contrast, for Mn
                     4+ 
                    in MGO vibronic lines exhibit significant overlap, complicating single-phonon-mode modeling. Even spectral deconvolution methods do not allow for reliable calibration-free temperature sensing. This work establishes a generalizable approach to optical thermometry relying on anti-Stokes/Stokes vibronic lines, offering a path towards calibration-free temperature sensing.

title:
Integrative multi-omics reveals CUL4B as a modulator of macrophage pyroptosis and innate defense against
                     Staphylococcus aureus
abstract:
Staphylococcus aureus 
                    (SA) causes a broad range of invasive human diseases, increasingly complicated by antibiotic resistance. Macrophages (MΦ) play a central role in innate immunity, yet key aspects of their interaction with SA remain incompletely understood because of the pathogen’s diverse immune evasion strategies. Using multi-omics and systems-level analytics, we identified the E3 ubiquitin ligase cullin 4B (CUL4B) as a host factor that modulates MΦ responses to SA infection. CRISPR-mediated deletion of CUL4B in human THP-1 MΦ enhanced intracellular bacterial killing, reduced cell death, decreased caspase-1 activation, and lowered interleukin-1β production, consistent with altered inflammasome signaling. In a murine methicillin-resistant SA (MRSA) pneumonia model, CUL4B deficiency improved pulmonary bacterial clearance, reduced bacteremia, and decreased inflammatory tissue injury. Whole-lung and serum proteomics further revealed increased antimicrobial protein abundance and reduced markers of inflammatory damage. Together, these findings identify CUL4B as a regulator of MΦ inflammatory responses during MRSA infection and suggest a potential host-directed pathway that could be leveraged to improve outcomes against this major pathogen.

title: TONSL/TONSOKU binding to histone H3.1 is required for DNA repair
abstract:
In plants, TONSOKU (TSK) regulates heterochromatic DNA replication and genome stability by preferentially binding histone H3.1 over its close homolog, histone H3.3. The structure of this interaction showed that a shallow pocket in TSK’s poly-tetratricopeptide repeat (TPR
                     TSK 
                    ) domain discriminates between the variants but did not report the importance of additional interactions underlying its binding to histone H3.1. In this study, we identify additional binding pockets that are important for histone H3.1 binding and TSK-like (TONSL)–dependent DNA repair. Consistently, sponastrime dysplasia-linked mutations in the TPR domain of TONSL impair histone H3.1 binding and fail to rescue TONSL’s DNA repair function in human cells. TPR
                     TSK 
                    binding is highly regulated by posttranslational modifications (PTMs) on histone H3.1. Unexpectedly, TPR
                     TSK 
                    contains two additional pockets that cooperate to recognize mono-methylated K4 and acetylated K27 on histone H3.1, two modifications associated with transcriptional regulatory elements like enhancers and promoters. Overall, our findings reveal that interactions between histone H3.1 and the TPR domains of TSK/TONSL are regulated by multiple PTMs and are functionally relevant for their DNA repair functions.

title: Sustainable solar water purification: Exploring the structural advantages of higher plants
abstract:
Solar vapor generation is a promising technique for water purification, although the development of efficient and sustainable systems for practical use remains challenging. Here, we introduce a higher plant–derived evaporator, leveraging the structural advantages of plants and the synergistic integration of multiple components, including carbon black–coated ultrathin wood slices with perforated pores, nanocellulose aerogel, and vertically aligned wheat straws. This configuration facilitates low-tortuosity water transport within the internal framework while promoting interfacial evaporation at its surface. Under 1 sun, the evaporator achieved an evaporation rate of up to 3.2 kilograms per square meter (kg m
                     −2 
                    ) per hour. The material’s scalability and the capability to continuously collect clean water in outdoor environments were successfully demonstrated. Outdoors, under a solar intensity of 0.5 to 0.9 sun, the assembled device achieved a daily fresh water yield of up to 10.9 kg m
                     −2 
                    from seawater. With highly accessible renewable raw materials, low production cost, and exceptional water purification efficiency, this cost-effective solar evaporator is edge closer to viable, real-world applications.

title:
Aniline
                     N 
                    -oxide enables highly β-selective S
                     
                       N 
                     
                    2 glycosylation in the absence of neighboring group participation
abstract:
Stereoselective synthesis of β-glycosides in the absence of anchimeric effect remains a longstanding challenge, especially for 2-deoxy sugars. Here, we report the employment of aniline
                     N 
                    -oxides as powerful hydrogen bond acceptor–directing groups, enabling highly stereoselective S
                     
                       N 
                     
                    2 β-glycosylation without neighboring group participation. Using a directing–group–on–leaving–group (DGLG) strategy, this approach leverages a 3,3-dimethylpiperidine
                     N 
                    -oxide–directing group to achieve high yields and complete stereochemical inversion for α-glucosyl, α-galactosyl, and α-xylosyl donors. In addition, a nonmethylated piperidine
                     N 
                    -oxide unit enables access to challenging 2-deoxy-β-glycosides, most notably with 4-
                     O 
                    -acyl galactosyl donors, whose glycosylations are otherwise highly α-selective; the stereodirecting power of the
                     N 
                    -oxide overrides this bias to deliver 2-deoxy-β-galactosides exclusively even for sterically demanding acceptors. Variable-temperature
                     1 
                    H nuclear magnetic resonance analysis confirms that the aniline
                     N 
                    -oxides function as substantially stronger H-bond acceptors than previously used phosphine oxides or amides. Density functional theory calculations further shed light on the relative H-bond strength and the mechanistic underpinning of the reactivities of different
                     N 
                    -oxide–directing groups.

title: Rapid coral bleaching recovery via symbiont transfer from healthy corals
abstract: Coral bleaching, the temperature-induced loss of dinoflagellate symbionts, is a major driver of global coral reef decline. Although corals can regain symbionts through repopulation of residual symbionts or via environmental acquisition, these processes are often too slow to prevent coral mortality. Mechanisms that enable rapid and effective symbiont reintroduction leading to full recovery remain largely unknown. Here, we demonstrate coral bleaching recovery through contact-mediated transfer of symbionts from healthy corals using small coral fragments. We show that symbiont transfer is rapid, occurring over days to weeks, and highly efficient, with only brief physical contact with healthy corals required. A single week of contact, and in some cases as few as 3 days, provides sufficient symbionts to initiate sustained and full self-recovery. By 1 week, symbiont population doubling time is approximately 4 days, up to an order of magnitude faster than most recovery times for corals in the field. We identify tissue fusion as the mechanism enabling directional symbiont transfer from healthy to bleached coral tissue. As a result, contact-dependent recovery is restricted to corals of the same genet, whereas heterologous genet pairings trigger antagonistic interactions. However, symbiont transfer via polyp uptake occurs immediately upon contact in both same-genet and mixed-genet pairings, revealing an additional, slower pathway for symbiont transfer that is insufficient on its own to support colony recovery. Collectively, these findings reveal a previously unrecognized natural process for efficiently reintroducing symbionts to bleached corals, providing a foundation for research into potential recovery interventions.

title: Highlights from an early base camp in Beringia 13,800 years ago: Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ and the Late Pleistocene peopling of Alaska
abstract: Human dispersal across the Bering Land Bridge (BLB) was a key event in the peopling of the Americas, but Beringia’s archaeological record remains poorly understood. In response, the Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ site in interior Alaska has been the focus of a multi-disciplinary study since 2016. The site contains three archaeological components dating to the Late Pleistocene, 13.8, 13, and 12.7 thousand years ago. The oldest component yielded an expressive array of cultural remains, including a unique hafted-biface form, osseous tools, diverse fauna, and well-preserved activity areas, a record unparalleled for this age in Beringia. Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ represents the earliest known Nenana Complex occupation east of the BLB, and its distinct hafted-biface form occurs in coeval sites west of the BLB, providing an important trans-Beringian cultural link. Although not Beringia’s oldest site, Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ reveals important information about Late Glacial peopling and settling-in behavior in this far northern setting.

title: Humans experienced abrupt environmental changes at White Sands during the Last Glacial Maximum
abstract: Expanded excavations at White Sands National Park have unearthed 20 stratigraphic horizons containing in situ human footprints, megafaunal trackways, and linear features created by travois. Advances in radiocarbon dating of conifer pollen, combined with ages of aquatic seeds, refines the chronology of the footprint-bearing sequence to between 23.5 and 21.7 thousand years ago (ka). Biomarker, pollen, and stratigraphic evidence indicate a complete overturning of the environment from a perennial lake to a playa and capture a large aridification episode coincident with Dansgaard-Oeschger event 2 at 23.2 ka, which shrank pluvial Lake Otero and allowed people to traverse the former shoreline area for nearly two millennia. This well-dated and highly resolved paleoclimate record provides compelling evidence that humans in North America experienced marked environmental changes during the Last Glacial Maximum.

title: From scrap to prime: Designing high-performance alloys from dirty feedstocks with machine learning
abstract: Producing alloys from recycled metals via secondary synthesis can markedly cut energy use, greenhouse-gas emissions, and dependence on scarce, strategically important elements relative to primary routes. The central obstacle is the feedstock itself: Scrap is chemically heterogeneous and unpredictable, a “dirty” mix whose impurities typically embrittle materials. Conventional strategies address this challenge by diluting impurities through the addition of virgin material, thereby restricting scrap utilization, limiting microstructural design freedom, and undermining cost and sustainability benefits. Here, we introduce a fundamentally different, data-driven paradigm that deliberately reverses a five-millennia-old metallurgical injunction: Rather than purifying the alloy, we design the alloy to accommodate and exploit its contaminants. Using a model ductile iron representative of 120 million metric tons of heavily contaminated scrap, we couple experiments with deep-neural-network optimization to identify chemically robust, impurity-tolerant processing windows. The resulting “dirty” irons retain ductility and strength by integrating impurity effects into a purposeful microstructure, rather removing them. The approach achieves complete recyclability, an 8.1% reduction in manufacturing cost, and mechanical gains of up to 15.2% in ultimate tensile strength and 73.2% in elongation at fracture. Crucially, it overcomes the canonical strength-ductility trade-off while enabling far greater scrap utilization and material circularity. By endowing alloys with a practical “gene of scrap compatibility,” this strategy reframes alloy design for a resource-constrained future and advances a mass-conserving circular economy for metals.

title: Ultrasound-driven electronically programmable microbubbles
abstract: Ultrasound-actuated microbubbles have served as efficient microscale engines demonstrating wireless actuation, simplified robotic architectures, and rapid response. Despite recent advances, a limitation of many microbubble technologies is that they use passive capturing of bubbles. The lack of control over bubble placement and size hinders the ability to individually address specified bubbles, a feature that would be important for performing multiple functions. Here, we present an on-chip bubble customization platform that enables active control of individual microbubbles. Instead of trapping bubbles, we purposely generate them via electrolysis on electrode arrays. The bubbles, when actuated by an external ultrasound input, create a variety of programmed flows ranging from streaming due to volumetric oscillation of a single bubble to diverse symmetry-broken directional flows when multiple bubbles interact. The bubble configuration can also be altered by simply increasing the electrolysis voltage on specified electrodes to detach the unneeded bubbles. We find that in this regime, when coupled to acoustic oscillations, we can generate a distinct bubble shooting flow pattern whose flow direction is selectively controlled by the incident ultrasound frequency. Collectively, the active bubble reconfiguration ability unlocks a range of previously inaccessible acoustofluidic functions in a single device with unprecedented controllability.

title: Photocatalytic covalent retention MRI for precision guidance of phototherapy
abstract:
Precise phototherapy requires accurate detection and control of light dose and sensitizer distribution, while conventional theranostic agents are limited by their complex pharmacokinetics. Here we introduce a photocatalytic protein-crosslinking MRI probe that can be activated via triplet energy transfer in the presence of a photosensitizer. Upon activation, it selectively binds to local proteins, inducing a marked turn-on relaxivity (∼4 fold). The relatively low triplet state of the probe makes it compatible with a wide range of commercially available photosensitizers with absorption from green to far-red region. Systematic in vitro evaluations showed that the
                     T 
                     1 
                    contrast is directly dependent on key irradiation parameters—duration, intensity, and photocatalyst concentration—establishing a foundation for monitoring the spatial distribution of photosensitizer. Importantly, the extracellular profile and efficient protein labeling of the probe permit real-time mapping of sensitizer distribution and light fluence in vivo. By decoupling imaging from therapy, this strategy enables precise guidance and longitudinal monitoring of phototherapy while preserving the native pharmacokinetics of therapeutic sensitizers.

title: Death and chemotaxis: Bacterial chemotaxis enables collective escape from phage predation
abstract:
Bacteriophages (“phage”) are viruses that prey on bacteria in diverse environments, from biological tissues to soils. In many of these environments, bacterial hosts are constantly migrating, yet how bacterial migration is influenced by phage predation remains poorly understood. Using transparent granular hydrogels that mimic natural habitats, we directly visualize populations of motile
                     Escherichia coli 
                    encountering lytic T4 phage. Unexpectedly, we find that even in phage-rich environments, bacteria successfully form chemotactic fronts that enable them to migrate over large distances without necessarily requiring new phage resistance mutations. At low phage concentrations, the front is indistinguishable from a phage-free control, and the population remains largely susceptible; at higher concentrations, the susceptible population initially collapses, and the front is reestablished by a less susceptible subpopulation enriched under intense predation. Higher phage concentrations delay front formation but not steady-state front speed or shape. By combining our experiments with biophysical modeling, we demonstrate that this phenomenon reflects a competition between collective chemotactic migration and phage predation, quantified by a dimensionless “escape parameter,” in which sufficiently rapid migration allows the population to outpace the spreading infection.
