Seed weight was a key axis of variation in beech (lighter seeds germinated more frequently and developed faster), but its effects in fir were confounded with geographic differentiation. 
                       
                       
                         Post‐establishment survival was dominated by site‐level environmental filtering and site‐by‐provenance interactions, with limited consistent provenance effects. This reveals a life‐stage shift from fine‐scale provenance‐by‐environment effects during germination and early development to broader environmental control of survival – an important consideration for regeneration‐based management and assisted migration.

title:
Phosphorylation and epigenetic remodeling mediate
                     BpEBP1 
                    ‐dependent drought resistance in birch
authors:
Shilin Sun, 
Pengyu Wang, 
Xue Yang, 
Jingxin Wang, 
Jingwen Wang, 
Xiaofu Li, 
Siyuan Niu, 
Xue Han, 
Di Wu, 
Chao Wang, 
Yucheng Wang
abstract:
Summary 
                   
                     
                       
                         
                          BpEBP1, an ethylene‐responsive factor VII transcription factor, coordinates stress resilience in birch (
                           Betula platyphylla 
                          ), but its molecular mechanisms underlying drought response remain unclear.
                         
                       
                       
                         Using transgenic birch lines (overexpression and knockout), chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP)‐seq, biochemical assays, and protein interaction studies, we dissected the multilayered regulatory network of BpEBP1. 
                       
                       
                         
                          BpEBP1 enhances drought tolerance in birch by directly activating key lignin and anthocyanin biosynthesis genes (
                           BpMYC2 
                          ,
                           BpCOMT 
                          , and
                           BpPOD5 
                          ), thereby promoting lignin deposition and anthocyanin accumulation, which reinforce cell wall rigidity and boost reactive oxygen species scavenging capacity. Beyond the canonical GCC‐box
                           cis 
                          ‐element, BpEBP1 binds to novel Noyes and ZNF449 motifs and uses these
                           cis 
                          ‐elements to drive expression of the previously described target genes. Mechanistically, BpEBP1 recruits the histone demethylase BpJMJ25 to remove repressive H3K9me2 marks, thereby increasing chromatin accessibility to facilitate transcriptional activation. Meanwhile, drought‐induced phosphorylation at Thr148 by BpEDR1 specifically increases the DNA‐binding affinity of BpEBP1, without affecting its transactivation activity or interaction with BpJMJ25.
                         
                       
                       
                         BpEBP1 functions as a central regulatory hub that unites transcriptional activation of anthocyanin and lignin‐related genes, BpJMJ25‐mediated H3K9me2 epigenetic remodeling, and BpEDR1‐dependent Thr148 phosphorylation. These two regulatory layers act independently yet synergistically, collectively activating drought‐adaptive metabolic pathways and conferring robust drought resistance in birch.

title:
Mapping the epigenetic regulatory network of cotton single‐cell fiber elongation mediated by
                     H3K4me3
authors:
Mengli Yu, 
Le Liu, 
Yuling Guo, 
Yameng Xu, 
Yujun Li, 
Xiaonan Li, 
Yu Wang, 
Liqiang Fan, 
Zuoren Yang
abstract:
Summary 
                   
                     
                       
                         Histone modifications are central to plant development, yet how they coordinate cellular morphogenesis remains poorly understood. Cotton fibers, as single‐celled trichomes derived from seed epidermal cells, provide an ideal model to address this question. 
                       
                       
                         Multi‐omics approaches were used, including cleavage under targets and tagmentation for genome‐wide H3K4me3 profiling and transcriptome sequencing. These were integrated with molecular and genetic validation experiments such as virus‐induced gene silencing, overexpression, CRISPR/Cas9, yeast one/two‐hybrid, electrophoretic mobility shift assay, co‐immunoprecipitation, and split‐luciferase complementation assays. 
                       
                       
                         
                          We identify GhMYBL as a core transcriptional repressor that negatively regulates fiber elongation.
                           GhMYBL 
                          is subject to dual control: H3K4me3 governs its transcription, whereas GhHBI1 posttranslationally attenuates its DNA‐binding activity. GhMYBL directly represses the positive regulators
                           GhXTH22 
                          and
                           GhALP1 
                          , limiting elongation; GhHBI1 relieves this repression, enabling their normal expression and synergistic promotion of fiber elongation.
                         
                       
                       
                         Our results demonstrate that differential H3K4me3 modification orchestrates GhMYBL‐mediated transcriptional repression, which is fine‐tuned by GhHBI1 interaction to coordinate fiber cell elongation. This study provides mechanistic insights into the epigenetic control of cell elongation and highlights promising targets for cotton fiber improvement.

title: Dormancy type, seed traits, and species identity shape seed‐associated fungal community composition in tropical pioneer trees
authors:
Lindsay A. McCulloch, 
A. Elizabeth Arnold, 
James W. Dalling, 
Adam S. Davis, 
Carolina Sarmiento, 
Paul‐Camilo Zalamea
abstract:
Dormancy type, as well as chemical and physical seed traits, explain variation in seed fungal community composition. 
 
 
 Summary 
 
Seed germination is regulated in many plants by seed dormancy, while postdispersal survival is often determined by soilborne fungi that infect seeds. In tropical forests, seeds in each of three dormancy types (physical, physiologically dormant, or quiescent) often share similar physical and chemical traits. We hypothesized that variation in seed traits aligned with seed dormancy should shape seed-associated fungal communities, linking dormancy to seed survival.
Seeds of 18 pioneer tree species were buried in each of five common garden plots in a lowland tropical forest in Panama for up to 36 months. Seeds were screened for viability and fungal infection at intervals throughout the experiment.
Plant species with different dormancy types harbored distinct fungal communities. Dormancy type explained 6.5% of variation in fungal community composition after accounting for the far stronger signature of plant species identity (34%). Within dormancy types, differences in seed traits among species explained 49–56% of the variation in fungal communities, suggesting that seed traits drive niche partitioning beyond what is imposed by dormancy type alone.
This study shows that variation in seed traits within a dormancy type filters seed-associated fungal communities, which likely shapes the demography of tropical forest trees by influencing seed survival and germination.
 
 Resumen 
 
En muchas plantas, la germinación de las semillas está regulada por la dormancia, mientras que la supervivencia posterior a la dispersión con frecuencia está determinada por hongos del suelo que infectan las semillas. En bosques tropicales, semillas de cada uno de los tres tipos de dormancia (física, fisiológica o quiescente) suelen compartir características físicas y químicas. En este estudio planteamos la hipótesis que la variación en los rasgos de las semillas asociada con el tipo de dormancia debería determinar la composición de las comunidades de hongos asociados a ellas, vinculando así la dormancia con la supervivencia de las semillas.
Se enterraron semillas de 18 especies de árboles pioneros en cinco parcelas experimentales en un bosque tropical de tierras bajas en Panamá durante un período de hasta 36 meses. A lo largo del experimento, se evaluó la viabilidad de las semillas y la presencia de infección por hongos en intervalos de tiempo regulares.
Especies de plantas con diferentes tipos de dormancia tienen comunidades de hongos diferentes. El tipo de dormancia explicó el 6.5% de la variación en la composición de las comunidades de hongos, después de controlar por la identidad de la especie de árbol (34%). Dentro de cada tipo de dormancia, las diferencias entre especies en los rasgos de las semillas explicaron entre el 49% y el 56% de la variación en las comunidades de hongos, sugieriendo que los rasgos de las semillas guían la diferenciación de nicho más allá de lo determinado únicamente por el tipo de dormancia.
Este estudio demuestra que la variación en los rasgos de las semillas dentro de un mismo tipo de dormancia filtra las comunidades de hongos asociados a las semillas, lo que probablemente tiene un efecto en la demografía de los árboles de bosques tropicales al afectar la supervivencia y germinación de las semillas.

title: Engineering root development with high precision
abstract:
Conceptual framework for precise engineering of root development.







Summary
Root development is controlled by dynamic interactions between gene regulation, hormonal signalling, developmental history and environmental inputs, creating multiple layers of control that can be harnessed for engineering. Recent advances in single‐cell technologies, spatial transcriptomics and synthetic biology are beginning to resolve root development at the cellular level and enable increasingly precise manipulation of developmental programmes. Here, we discuss how lineage tracing, genetic recording of developmental history, cell‐type‐specific engineering and programmable genetic circuits can be integrated to understand and control root architecture. We highlight emerging strategies for engineering adaptive and context‐dependent developmental behaviours, including history‐dependent and reversible response programmes and rewired root‐environment interactions. Together, these approaches establish a foundation for programmable and adaptive root system engineering in plants.

title: Liver X receptors participate in the fasting response by assisting CEBPB binding to enhancers and promoting the fasting transcriptional program
abstract: Upon fasting, a group of transcription factors (TFs) activates an extensive transcriptional program in the liver to alter hepatocyte metabolism and cope with fasting. This is achieved by TF-mediated activation of enhancers, which become more accessible, leading to gene induction. Liver X receptors alpha (NR1H3) and beta (NR1H2), collectively termed here LXRs, are important TFs known to participate in transcriptional programs in the fed state, but their role in fasting is unclear. Here, we examined the effect of LXR deletion on the transcriptional and chromatin programs activated in the fasted and fed states. We profiled the liver transcriptome and genome-wide chromatin accessibility in single-knockout mice lacking either LXR isoform and in double-knockout mice lacking both isoforms. We find that double-knockout of LXRs impairs fasting-induced genes and enhancers. Analysis of genome-wide NR1H3 binding by ChIP-seq, together with chromatin accessibility profiling by ATAC-seq, shows that NR1H3 directly binds enhancers and increases their accessibility. We find that LXRs assist the binding of CCAAT/enhancer-binding protein beta (CEBPB) to enhancers during fasting. CEBPB is a key TF regulating the fasting response, and its genome-wide binding is perturbed in the absence of LXRs. Cooperation between LXRs and CEBPB promotes fasting-dependent gene induction. These findings reveal a previously unknown role for LXRs in the fasting response, whereby LXRs bind and increase enhancer accessibility, assist CEBPB binding, and promote gene induction. This study demonstrates the complex cooperation of TFs in regulating gene expression to maintain homeostasis during fasting and places LXRs as novel regulators of the fasting response.

title: Pangenome and transcriptomics reveal the genomic basis associated with interspecific variation of sexually dimorphic nuptial spines in moustache toads
abstract:
Sexual dimorphism is a widespread phenotypic innovation that plays a crucial role in species diversification, yet its genetic origins and evolutionary trajectories remain poorly understood in vertebrates.
                     Leptobrachium 
                    provides a tractable system in which male moustache toads develop maxillary nuptial spines used in male–male combat, whereas closely related pseudo-moustache toads lack this trait. To investigate the evolutionary genomics of these sexually dimorphic nuptial spines, we construct a pangenome from chromosome-level assemblies of six
                     Leptobrachium 
                    species and integrate
                     trans 
                    -species transcriptomic analyses. We find that keratin gene expansion predated the origin of nuptial spines, potentially providing genetic material for keratinized skin innovation. Recently duplicated hair keratin genes acquired putative Hoxc13 binding sites, and promoter reporter assays confirm that Hoxc13 can activate these genes in both moustache toads and pseudo-moustache toads. Differential
                     hoxc13 
                    expression may therefore be more important for affecting whether duplicated hair keratin genes are recruited to develop nuptial spines. Transcriptomic comparisons further reveal maxillary skin–specific expression of genes involved in keratinocyte proliferation and differentiation, as well as melanogenesis during the formation of nuptial spines. In
                     Leptobrachium tengchongense 
                    , which has undergone secondary loss of nuptial spines,
                     igfbp2 
                    , a conserved gene highly expressed in keratinized skin appendages across amphibians, shows positive selection and represents a candidate associated with this evolutionary transition. Our study provides amphibian pangenome resources and highlights how gene duplication coupled with regulatory recruitment may shape the evolution of novel sexually dimorphic traits in vertebrates.

title: Conditional diffusion for single-cell Hi-C data imputation and enhancement with scHiC-Diff
abstract: Single-cell high-throughput chromosome conformation capture (scHi-C) enables the analysis of cell-to-cell variability in three-dimensional (3D) genome organization, but its utility is severely limited by pervasive technical dropouts, leading to extremely sparse contact maps. Accurately identifying dropout events and imputing the corresponding missing chromatin contacts remains a challenging problem, as technical dropouts are confounded with genuine absences of chromatin interactions. Existing imputation and enhancement methods often rely on smoothing strategies or restrictive parametric likelihood assumptions, which may obscure fine-scale chromatin structures and cell-specific features. Here, we present scHiC-Diff, a conditional diffusion-based framework for scHi-C data imputation and enhancement. scHiC-Diff employs a forward process that progressively perturbs contact maps and a reverse denoising process that reconstructs chromatin interactions from noisy observations. To better capture long-range dependencies in complex 3D genome structures, scHi-C contact matrices are treated as masked images and modeled using a Diffusion Transformer (DiT). Across two complementary simulated datasets and three real scHi-C datasets, scHiC-Diff improves the recovery of chromatin interaction patterns and enhances downstream analyses compared with existing methods. Application to a developmental scHi-C dataset further demonstrates improved reconstruction of chromatin organization and enhanced chromatin loop detection.

title: Glucocorticoid regulation of the human noncoding genome
abstract: Glucocorticoids (GCs) are widely used anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive agents known to induce substantial changes in gene expression, yet their effects on noncoding RNAs such as long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) or microRNAs (miRNAs) remain poorly characterized. Here, we present the first comprehensive and systematic analysis of GC regulation of the noncoding genome across nine human primary cell types from both hematopoietic and nonhematopoietic lineages. In vitro GC treatment was applied to each cell type, with transcriptomic profiling (total RNA-seq and small RNA-seq) at 2 and 6 h posttreatment. We identify more than 2000 GC-responsive noncoding transcripts, including 654 annotated lncRNAs, 1376 novel lncRNAs, and 39 miRNAs. The noncoding RNA response to GCs is highly cell type dependent: 80% of GC-responsive lncRNAs and 97% of miRNAs are unique to a single cell type. Hematopoietic cells exhibit a greater magnitude of lncRNA induction compared with nonhematopoietic cells. Notably, GC treatment uncovers dozens of facultative, stimulus-dependent lncRNAs. GC-responsive transcripts span diverse lncRNA classes, with enrichment of host lncRNAs. In contrast, only a limited number of miRNAs are GC responsive. GC regulation of transcript abundance for miRNAs and their host lncRNAs appears to be independent. Our results, which are accessible through an interactive web application, establish a framework for studying how noncoding transcription contributes to physiological and clinical heterogeneity in GC responses. The newly identified GC-responsive noncoding transcripts could represent biomarkers of GC exposure, determinants of GC sensitivity or resistance, or candidate regulators of tissue-specific GC effects.

title: Glycogen phosphorylase and phosphoenolpyruvate synthase are key metabolic nodes for high-light acclimation in cyanobacteria
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Balancing energy supply from photosynthetic light reactions with downstream metabolic demand is critical for preventing photosystem damage. Although energy-dissipation mechanisms involving remodeling of photosystems are well known, the role of downstream metabolic routes in energy dissipation remains understudied. Here, we show that two metabolic nodes, glycogen phosphorylase (glgP) and phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP) synthase (pps), participate in photoprotection under high light in Synechococcus elongatus PCC 7942. Glycogen phosphorylase is important for photosystem I protection under high or changing light conditions. Under high light, the ΔglgP mutant exhibits severe chlorosis and reduced cyclic electron flow (CEF), approximated from the P700+ re-reduction rate, without major changes in carbon metabolism. Comparative proteomics further suggests redox exchange from NADPH to NADH, consistent with a role of GlgP in maintaining P700 acceptor side oxidized via enhanced CEF. Meanwhile, PEP synthase acts as a key node regulating tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle flux and potentially NADPH production. Under high light, the Δpps mutant rewires its metabolism to enhance CEF, likely a compensatory mechanism that offsets excess NADPH from elevated TCA flux. Long-term maintenance of Δpps resulted in a spontaneous secondary deletion in adhE, encoding succinate semialdehyde dehydrogenase of the TCA bypass. This suppressor mutation, combined with the loss of PEP synthase, partially mitigates high-light stress at the cost of reduced amino acid synthesis. These findings reveal important roles for downstream carbon metabolism in high-light acclimation and provide new insights into photoprotective mechanisms in phototrophs.

title: OsGSK2-OsBSK3 feedback loop controls rice BR signaling
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Brassinosteroids (BRs) are essential plant hormones that regulate growth and development, including leaf angle regulation and grain size determination. Maintaining appropriate BR signaling requires precise coordination between pathway activation and attenuation. BR signaling is initiated by OsBRI1 activation, which triggers a phosphorylation cascade that ultimately inhibits OsGSK2 kinase activity, releasing OsBZR1 from repression and activating downstream responses. However, whether additional regulatory mechanisms fine-tune BR signaling remains unclear. Here, we identify OsBSK3 as a direct substrate of OsGSK2 and uncover a phosphorylation-dependent feedback mechanism within the BR signaling pathway. OsGSK2-mediated phosphorylation enhances the interactions of OsBSK3 with OsBRI1, OsGSK2, and OsPPKL1 while attenuating the regulatory activity of OsBSK3. Genetic analyses revealed that overexpression of wild-type OsBSK3 or the phosphorylation-deficient variant OsBSK3SA enhances BR responses and fully rescues the leaf angle and grain size defects of the osbsk3 mutant, whereas the phosphomimetic variant OsBSK3SD fails to restore these phenotypes. Together, our findings establish a phosphorylation-dependent OsGSK2-OsBSK3 negative feedback mechanism that fine-tunes BR signaling homeostasis in rice.

title: Lysine biosynthesis integrates carbon availability and energy homeostasis under fluctuating CO2
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Lysine metabolism connects amino acid biosynthesis with mitochondrial respiration through coordinated synthesis and degradation pathways that interface with the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle and the mitochondrial electron transport chain (mETC). The critical role of this pathway is underscored by the embryonic lethality of the Arabidopsis L,L-diaminopimelate aminotransferase mutant (dapat), which is defective in a key step of lysine biosynthesis. Hypomorphic dapat mutant plants exhibit profound metabolic reprogramming and a constitutive energy-limited phenotype under non-stress conditions, suggesting that lysine biosynthesis contributes to basal metabolic homeostasis. We therefore hypothesized that impaired lysine biosynthesis restricts metabolic flexibility, but that changes in CO2 availability may partially compensate through carbon and nitrogen remodeling. To test this, we performed comprehensive metabolite profiling of wild-type and dapat mutant plants under low-, ambient-, and elevated-CO2 conditions. Elevated CO2 (eCO2) induced broad reorganization of carbon and nitrogen metabolism in both genotypes, reducing photorespiratory and stress-associated amino acids and modulating key metabolic ratios, including glycine/serine and malate/aspartate, in a genotype- and time-dependent manner. Proteomics revealed DAPAT photosynthetic compensation under ambient CO2, with RuBisCO over-accumulation and suppressed TOR activity, as indicated by decreased RPS6 phosphorylation, which eCO2 restored in parallel with phenotypic rescue. These adjustments were associated with partial attenuation of the DAPAT metabolic imbalance. Our findings reveal functional connections among lysine biosynthesis, photorespiration, and CO2-responsive metabolic flexibility, demonstrating that lysine metabolism serves as a regulatory node linking amino acid homeostasis to carbon availability and respiratory adjustment. This provides mechanistic insight into how plants maintain energy balance under fluctuating CO2 environments.

title:
Transcription factor ANAC087 coordinates symplastic Cd exclusion and apoplastic Cd sequestration to enhance cadmium resistance in
                     Arabidopsis thaliana
abstract: Abstract Cadmium (Cd) exclusion and sequestration are vital mechanisms for plant survival under heavy metal stress, yet the upstream regulatory networks governing these coordinated processes remain poorly understood. In this study, we identified the NAC transcription factor ANAC087 as a key positive regulator of Cd resistance in  Arabidopsis thaliana . Loss-of-function  anac087  mutants exhibited hypersensitivity to Cd stress and significantly higher Cd accumulation in both roots and shoots compared to the wild type Col-0. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that ANAC087 coordinates 2 complementary pathways involving symplastic Cd influx control and apoplastic sequestration. First, ANAC087 contributes to ABA homeostasis and directly binds to the promoter of  ABSCISIC ACID-INSENSITIVE5  ( ABI5 ) to activate its expression, which subsequently antagonizes the MYB49 -bHLH38/101  regulatory module to suppress  IRT1 , thereby limiting Cd uptake. Exogenous ABA application partially alleviated the Cd-sensitive phenotype of  anac087 . Second, ANAC087 directly transactivates  ANAC017  to promote  XTH31 -mediated xyloglucan accumulation, substantially enhancing the Cd binding capacity of the root cell wall. Genetic analyses confirmed that ectopic expression of  ABI5  or  ANAC017  partially rescued the Cd sensitive and high-Cd accumulation phenotypes of  anac087 , whereas  XTH31  overexpression complemented the  anac017 anac087  double mutant. Furthermore, Cd stress increases both ANAC087 transcript abundance and protein stability. Collectively, our findings support a regulatory framework in which ANAC087 coordinates processes that limit symplastic Cd accumulation and promote apoplastic Cd sequestration.

title: A cellular view of seed development and germination
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Seeds are fundamental to global food security, yet their encapsulated structure, dense storage compounds, and spatial heterogeneity have created a “hidden box” problem, often restricting research to bulk and tissue approaches that mask cell type–specific regulatory programs. Advances in single-cell and spatial transcriptomics now enable systematic dissection of seed biology at cellular resolution. This review provides a cellular view spanning the developmental continuum from fertilization to seedling establishment by synthesizing single-cell and spatial transcriptomic studies in Arabidopsis thaliana and major crops (Oryza sativa—rice, Zea mays—maize, Hordeum vulgare—barley, Glycine max—soybean, Triticum aestivum—wheat). These technologies reveal previously undetected cellular complexity and heterogeneity: distinct transcriptional subpopulations within morphologically uniform tissues, specialized endosperm microdomains mediating nutrient transfer and metabolic polarity, cell type–specific genomic imprinting patterns, and spatially segregated hormone signaling hubs controlling dormancy and germination. Integration of transcriptional profiling with chromatin accessibility and transcription factor binding data has enabled construction of cell type–specific gene regulatory networks for seeds, advancing from correlation to causal inference and identifying master regulators of developmental transitions. These approaches illuminate how early embryonic patterning establishes transcriptional identities, how metabolic zonation coordinates storage compound accumulation and mobilization, how chromatin states maintain dormancy and license germination competence, and how spatiotemporal coordination integrates hormone signaling with energy metabolism across tissues. Single-cell and spatial approaches are establishing seeds not as opaque structures but as assemblies of coordinated cellular programs amenable to systematic analysis and targeted manipulation for crop improvement.

title: Iron electronic delocalization enables catalytic selective trisilyla-tion: beyond steric hindrance
abstract:
Abstract 
                   The efficient synthesis of sterically congested tetrasubstituted alkenes, particularly the synthetically valuable 1,1,2-trisilylalkenes, remains a longstanding challenge due to significant steric hindrance encountered during the bond formation. Here, we report an iron-catalyzed trisilylation of ynamides that leverages iron electronic delocalization to modulate the character of double bonds toward that of single bonds, effectively mitigating steric constraints during the reaction. This strategy enables a regioselective and controllable synthesis of 1,1,2-trisilylated alkenes, trans-1,2-disilylated alkenes, and monosilylated alkynes under mild conditions with high efficiency. Notably, the method allows for late-stage functionalization of biologically relevant molecules, offering a valuable platform for the structural diversification of alkynes. In addition, the resulting multisilylated intermediates undergo diverse downstream transformations, granting access to a broad array of otherwise elusive tetrasubstituted silylalkenes. Experimental and computational studies reveal that monosilylalkynes serve as key intermediates, with β-N elimination, double migratory insertion, and reductive elimination steps likely involved in the catalytic cycle. This work provides fundamental insights into the construction of sterically hindered chemical bonds via base metal catalysis and underscores the potential of iron to unlock unconventional reactivity through electronic delocalization effects.

title: High mobility narrowband-emissive organic semiconductors
abstract: This work proposes a synergistic control strategy of molecular packing and transition dipole moment orientation for achieving high mobility narrowband-emissive organic semiconductors.

title: Using gene topologies to partition sex chromosomes into regions with distinct histories
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Sex chromosomes often evolve through successive recombination arrests, forming evolutionary strata. Accurately describing these strata, their boundaries and history is crucial for studying sex chromosome evolution, but this can be very challenging, particularly in young sex chromosomes where X–Y or Z–W divergence is low or in highly rearranged sex chromosomes where strata are divided into pieces. Standard approaches to distinguish recently evolved strata involve combining signals from dS, Fst and gene-by-gene phylogenies, all of which can be noisy. Here, we propose a new method that uses the proportion of allele topologies observed on sex-linked genes between at least a pair of sister species, obtained from reconstructed X and Y sequences aligned to the same reference, along with an outgroup to infer ancestral alleles, with flexibility in the reconstruction pipeline. We implement a change-point analysis to objectively identify transitions in these proportions. Our method both delimitates strata and infers whether their evolutionary history is shared or convergent between species. We illustrate and test this method on Silene and Artemia species. Our new method is reliable and robust, globally confirming previous findings known for some of these species. The method is also sensitive, refining those previous findings and identifying regions that were not previously reported. We finally illustrate how this approach can inform scenarios that retrace the history of sex chromosomes in these species. Overall, this approach presents a tool that can be widely used and that complement existing methods to study sex chromosomes.

title: DNAharvester: a nextflow pipeline for analysing highly degraded DNA from ancient and historical specimens
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Motivation 
                     Ancient DNA (aDNA) research has advanced rapidly with the development of high-throughput sequencing, enabling genome-wide analyses of large collections of prehistoric specimens. However, analysing palaeontological and archaeological material with highly degraded DNA constitutes a major bioinformatic challenge. DNA from such samples is characterized by short fragment lengths, low endogenous content, post-mortem damage, and cross-species contamination, which can increase spurious mapping and reference bias, affecting downstream population genetic inferences. 
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     We present DNAharvester, a modular and reproducible pipeline designed specifically for processing highly degraded DNA from ancient and historical specimens. DNAharvester integrates metagenomic filtering, competitive mapping, adaptive aligner selection (incorporating BWA-aln, BWA-mem, and Bowtie2), and systematic evaluation of reference bias and spurious mapping. By incorporating flexible mapping and filtering strategies, the pipeline can be adapted to varying sample preservation, focusing on maximizing authentic data recovery. DNAharvester features subworkflows for iterative assembly of mitogenomes, identification of genomic repeats and CpG sites, taxonomic classification, microbial/pathogen screening, genetic sex determination, and variant calling. To accommodate varying sequencing depths, the pipeline supports diploid variant calling, genotype likelihood estimation, and pseudo-haploid random allele calling. We validated the pipeline using simulated and empirical datasets, demonstrating its ability to systematically mitigate complex background contamination while preserving authentic genomic signals. By streamlining complex bioinformatic tasks through simple configuration files, DNAharvester establishes a standardized approach for analysing aDNA datasets and makes genomic analyses of ancient remains accessible to the broader research community. 
                   
                   
                     Availability and Implementation 
                     Implemented in Nextflow, DNAharvester provides a highly scalable, containerized framework that enhances reproducibility, portability, and robustness in aDNA analyses. DNAharvester is open source under the GNU General Public License v3.0 and freely available at https://github.com/NBISweden/DNAharvester.

title: Deepweed: automated individual segmentation and tracking for duckweed lineage analysis
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Motivation 
                     Aquatic duckweeds, including Wolffia australiana, are the smallest and fastest growing flowering plants on the planet, with numerous emerging biotechnological applications. Duckweed populations grow through rapid clonal budding, but existing phenotypic characterization and image analysis tools typically operate only at the population level, tracking neither individual plants nor their lineage structure. Deepweed addresses this gap, combining automated individual segmentation, temporal tracking, and clonal lineage reconstruction from time-lapse imaging of duckweed. 
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     Deepweed processes time-lapse duckweed imaging datasets using deep-learning–based instance segmentation and multi-object tracking to assign persistent identities to individual fronds and infer mother–daughter relationships. The workflow outputs lineage graphs, individual-level morphological metrics, and population-level growth summaries, supported by lineage-annotated time-lapse visualizations. Applied to dense Wolffia populations, in both freely growing or controlled microfluidic environments, our framework can track hundreds of Wolffia plants simultaneously, resolves overlapping individuals, and reconstructs multi-generation lineage structure, enabling analyses that are inaccessible with population-level phenotyping methods. 
                   
                   
                     Availability 
                     Deepweed is implemented in Python using PyTorch, scikit-image, OpenCV, and btrack. Source code, trained models, example datasets, and documentation are freely available at https://github.com/SamOliveiraLab/Deepweed. The Deepweed code is archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18844282 and the datasets are archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18843917.

title: Seq2Pocket: augmenting protein language models for spatially consistent binding site prediction
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Motivation 
                     Protein–ligand binding site prediction (LBS) is important for many areas of structural biology and molecular modeling, where, as in other tasks, protein language models (pLMs) have shown great promise. In their application to LBS, the pLM classifies each amino acid as binding or not, but translating these predictions into three-dimensional binding pockets remains challenging; in particular, residue-centric predictions tend to produce spatially fragmented pockets. 
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     We present Seq2Pocket, a methodology for pocket-level LBS prediction that combines pLM finetuning, data enhancement, and structure-aware post-processing. First, we introduce sc-PDBenhanced, an extended training dataset that augments an existing sc-PDB dataset with additional small-molecule and ion-binding sites, improving coverage of non-obvious and small pockets. Second, we employ an embedding-supported smoothing classifier to refine residue-level predictions. Third, we define the Pocket Fragmentation Index and use it to select a clustering approach that preserves a consistent mapping between predictions and ground-truth pockets. We evaluate Seq2Pocket on two tasks: general binding site prediction using the LIGYSIS benchmark and cryptic binding site prediction using CryptoBench benchmark. Across both benchmarks, Seq2Pocket achieves state-of-the-art DCCtop-N and DCCtop-(N + 2) performance. In particular, for general binding site prediction on the LIGYSIS benchmark, it improves distance-center-to-center recall by up to 13%, outperforming existing predictors. This improvement originates from training data quality rather than model architecture, as demonstrated by an ablation study. We believe that these findings contribute to more reliable evaluation practices in ligand binding site prediction, highlight the importance of training data curation, and provide pocket-level prediction tools that are better suited for downstream applications such as drug discovery. 
                   
                   
                     Availability 
                     The Seq2Pocket web interface is available at https://seq2pocket.projekty.ms.mff.cuni.cz, running the ESM-2 650M variant. The sc-PDBenhanced is published using Zenodo platform at https://zenodo.org/records/18271517. The models are published at HuggingFace: https://huggingface.co/skrhakv/seq2pocket.

title: Motion-corrected Noise2Noise denoising for structural analysis of cells and tissues with (cryo-)FIB/SEM
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Motivation 
                     (Cryo-)FIB/SEM enables 3D ultrastructural analysis of cells and tissues at nanoscale resolution. However, its characteristically low signal-to-noise ratio severely hinders interpretation of the volume data. Noise2Noise (N2N) has emerged as a state-of-the-art denoising paradigm with outstanding performance in 3D electron microscopy—particularly cryo-ET—but its direct application to (cryo-)FIB/SEM remains unfeasible due to the inherent acquisition workflows. 
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     A method to enable N2N denoising in (cryo-)FIB/SEM is introduced. The input volume is split into even and odd slices, followed by the application of motion correction methods to estimate and compensate for the structural differences between the two subvolumes. The resulting motion-corrected subvolumes are then used to train the N2N model, which is ultimately applied to denoise the original volume. Representative (cryo-)FIB/SEM volumes have been used to validate the method and to demonstrate the critical importance of the motion correction stage for volumes with a slice thickness >10 nm. 
                   
                   
                     Availability and implementation 
                     Code is available at https://github.com/microscopy-processing/N2N-REO and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22303478.

title: Thermal imbalance drives avian performance and responses to climate warming
abstract: Thermal performance curves are widely used to predict ectothermic responses to climate warming but are less effective for predicting endotherm performance across environmental conditions because thermoregulation often decouples body temperature from ambient temperature. We develop theory and provide empirical evidence for performance curves in endotherms structured by net sensible heat flux (Q), an integrative index of thermoregulatory imbalance. Using biophysical simulations in tree swallows, we show that performance varies predictably with Q (which we term “QPCs”), thereby explaining variation in nestling provisioning performance, reproductive fitness, and geographic limits, while also forecasting responses to climate change. We also demonstrate that thermal imbalance helps shape breeding ranges of birds across North America. Our findings introduce Q as a broadly relevant ecophysiological dimension that constrains performance in endotherms and provides a framework for predicting endotherm responses to climate warming.

title:
Membrane contact activation of Piezo2 drives lysosome–mitochondrion Ca
                     2+ 
                    transfer and signaling in
                     Trypanosoma cruzi
abstract:
Calcium ion (Ca
                     2+ 
                    ) transfer from other organelles is central to mitochondrial metabolism and cell survival, yet how mechanical forces regulate interorganelle communication remains unclear. Here we report a lysosome-to-mitochondrion pathway in
                     Trypanosoma cruzi 
                    , the etiologic agent of Chagas disease, mediated by the mechano/osmosensitive channel TcPiezo2. Using ultrastructural, biochemical, and live-cell superresolution imaging, we define lysosome–mitochondrion contact sites (LMCs) that enable direct Ca
                     2+ 
                    transfer. TcPiezo2 triggers Ca
                     2+ 
                    release, which generates perilysosomal nanodomains that drives mitochondrial Ca
                     2+ 
                    uptake via the voltage-dependent anion channel and the mitochondrial Ca
                     2+ 
                    uniporter complex. Disruption of TcPiezo2-dependent Ca
                     2+ 
                    transfer impairs mitochondrial metabolism, perturbs redox homeostasis, induces autophagy, and eventually leads to parasite death. These findings establish LMCs as a signaling platform that directly regulates interorganelle Ca
                     2+ 
                    transfer and mitochondrial bioenergetics.

title: Nitrogen deposition does not alter the temperate forest soil carbon pool: A 14-y experiment on varied nitrogen fertilization
abstract:
Soil carbon (C) pools in nitrogen-limited temperate forests are critical to the global C cycle, but there are no long-term experiments examining soil C, with various nitrogen (N) forms. Here, a 14-y experiment (100 kg N ha
                     −1 
                    y
                     −1 
                    ), with added N simulating atmospheric deposition proportions (~70% inorganic, ~30% organic) did not affect soil C pools, whereas organic N (ON) and inorganic N (IN) individually significantly increased values by 2.7-fold and 1.8-fold, respectively. Although no treatment significantly affected soil pH, treatment effects on pH were negatively associated with soil C pools. In addition, treatments containing ON forms increased mineral-associated organic C fractions, indicating enhanced C stability vs. IN. These findings enhance our understanding of N deposition-soil C pool interactions.

title: Controlled functionalization of cellulose nanocrystals directs polymer-specific protein coronas and immune cell interactions
abstract: Polymer coatings are widely used to suppress nonspecific protein adsorption and modulate nanoparticle–cell interactions. However, the biological outcomes of polymer-functionalized nanoparticles remain difficult to predict in complex biological environments because protein corona formation rapidly alters nanoparticle identity. This challenge is particularly pronounced when hydrophobic moieties are incorporated for imaging or therapeutic applications, as they can promote nonspecific interactions at the nano–bio interface. Herein, we establish a modular grafting-to platform based on cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) that enables systematic comparison of polyethylene glycol (PEG)-based, zwitterionic, and acrylamide-based polymers with controlled grafting density and chain conformation on a common porphyrin-modified surface. We demonstrate that dense polymer brushes reduce nonspecific protein adsorption in single-protein assays. By contrast, all CNC surfaces form dynamic coronas upon exposure to serum proteins, while specific polymer coatings selectively enrich or suppress distinct protein populations. We further demonstrate that polymer-dependent immune cell interactions are substantially reduced following protein corona formation, although differences among polymer chemistries persist. Zwitterionic coatings broadly suppress immune cell interactions, whereas PEG-based coatings preferentially promote interactions with antigen-presenting cells. These findings establish design principles for polymer-functionalized nanoparticles with specific immune cell interaction profiles.

title:
A “knob-in-hole” gate in the antibody C
                     H 
                    1 domain underlies subclass-independent IgA hinge cleavage by the commensal metallopeptidase IgAse
abstract:
Human immunoglobulin (Ig) A (IgA) protects ≈400 m
                     2 
                    of mucosae from microbes. Bacterial IgA-peptidases subvert this defense by cleaving the F
                     ab 
                    –F
                     c 
                    hinge of subclass IgA1 while sparing the hinge-divergent, colon-dominant IgA2 subclass. The exception is IgAse, a ≈140-kDa, seven-domain, membrane-bound metallopeptidase from the colonic commensal
                     Thomasclavelia ramosa 
                    that targets both subclasses but no other protein. We previously narrowed the minimal functional assembly down to the IgAse catalytic and wrapping domains (CD and WD) plus the IgA1/2 F
                     ab 
                    ′, i.e., the hinge and a F
                     ab 
                    of light and heavy chains (LC, HC), each with a variable and a constant Ig domain (V
                     L 
                    + C
                     L 
                    , V
                     H 
                    + C
                     H 
                    1). The transient interaction culminates in cleavage of a proline–valine bond within the first two hinge residues, downstream of a conserved C-terminal C
                     H 
                    1 disulfide (SS2). Here, single-particle cryoelectron microscopy of a disulfide-stabilized minimal IgAse:IgA2 F
                     ab 
                    ′ complex yielded high-quality density strongly supporting two states along the cleavage reaction coordinate, a “recognition complex” and a subsequent “precatalytic complex,” in which F
                     ab 
                    ′ binds frontally to the IgAse CD via a C
                     H 
                    1 β-sheet and overhang loop LβEβF. This loop binds like a knob to a preformed hole in the active-site cleft. Binding rearranges the knob and rotates SS2 ≈ 180°, enabling access of the hinge into the cleft of the otherwise unaffected precatalytic complex. Together, this work defines a unique, C
                     H 
                    1-mediated hinge-delivering “gate” mechanism, validated by a crystal structure of unbound IgA2 F
                     ab 
                    , point mutations disrupting the C
                     H 
                    1:CD interface, and molecular dynamics calculations, which provide the structural framework for subclass-independent IgA cleavage.

title:
Dynamic partitioning shapes the in vivo organization of the
                     Escherichia coli 
                    RNA degradosome
abstract:
The bacterial RNA degradosome is a central mediator of RNA turnover, yet how its components are organized and regulated in living cells remains unclear. Using live-cell single-molecule imaging, we quantified the spatial distribution and dynamics of the four major
                     Escherichia coli 
                    degradosome components: RNase E, RhlB, PNPase, and enolase. These proteins occupied distinct membrane-associated and cytoplasmic pools whose relative abundance varied among proteins and changed with physiological state. In particular, PNPase underwent pronounced redistribution between membrane-associated and cytoplasmic states in response to altered RNA availability and growth conditions, whereas RNase E and RhlB remained largely membrane associated. To determine the functional consequences of this organization, we examined the degradation of
                     lacZ 
                    reporter transcripts with different translation initiation strengths. PNPase and RhlB preferentially promoted degradation of weakly translated transcripts, whereas strongly translated transcripts were largely insensitive to their loss. Together, these results reveal that the bacterial RNA degradosome is not a static, uniformly assembled molecular machine. Instead, RNA decay is organized through dynamic intracellular partitioning of degradosome components, linking physiological state and translation status to transcript degradation.

title: A conserved Hox9–10 code underlies the early establishment of hind appendage progenitors in zebrafish and the Iberian ribbed newt
abstract:
The acquisition of paired appendages was a key innovation in vertebrate evolution. Although
                     HoxA/D 
                    paralog groups (PGs) 9–13 play central roles in patterning paired fins and limbs, the evolutionary origin of this paired appendage-patterning system remains unknown. Here, we show that
                     HoxA/D 
                    PG9–10 genes are essential for the early establishment of pelvic fin progenitors in zebrafish, and that
                     Hox9–10 
                    function is similarly required for hindlimb progenitor formation in the Iberian ribbed newt. In zebrafish, combined disruption of five
                     HoxA/D 
                    PG9–10 genes abolishes the detectable pelvic fin progenitor population, resulting in complete loss of pelvic fins. A
                     Tg(hoxa10b:EGFP) 
                    reporter labeled cells in the presumptive pelvic fin field before pelvic fin bud formation. Importantly, simultaneous CRISPR-mediated disruption of all seven
                     Hox9–10 
                    paralogs in the Iberian ribbed newt similarly impaired the establishment of hindlimb progenitors, suggesting that an early requirement for
                     Hox9–10 
                    function in hind appendage development predates the divergence of ray-finned and lobe-finned vertebrates. Together, these findings identify an evolutionarily conserved role for posterior
                     Hox9–10 
                    genes in the initial establishment of hind appendage progenitors. Because overlapping posterior Hox paralog groups are subsequently deployed during paired appendage patterning, this early
                     Hox9–10 
                    requirement provides a developmental link between the posterior axial Hox code and the paired appendage-patterning system. Our results are therefore consistent with the hypothesis that recruitment of a posterior Hox code into hind appendage progenitor formation contributed to the evolutionary assembly of the vertebrate paired appendage-patterning system.

title:
S 
                    -adenosyl-L-homocysteine triggers an adaptive response that extends lifespan through the
                     YBT1 
                    ABC transporter
abstract:
S 
                    -adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM) is a fundamental methyl donor; however, the physiological role of its byproduct and competitive inhibitor,
                     S 
                    -adenosyl-L-homocysteine (SAH), remains unclear. Here, we show that transient reactive oxygen species (ROS) production triggered by SAH during the early logarithmic phase mimics partial SAH hydrolase inhibition, extending the yeast chronological lifespan (CLS) through a hormetic mechanism. This study reveals that the dual nature of ROS in aging is determined by the specific degree of SAH hydrolase activity. We identified the adenosine 5’-triphosphate-binding cassette (ABC) transporter Ybt1 as a key downstream effector of SAH. Ybt1 localizes to the vacuolar membrane and facilitates the sequestration of SAM from the cytosol into the vacuole. Notably,
                     YBT1 
                    overexpression extends CLS, mimicking SAH effects through an integrated pathway involving target of rapamycin complex 1 downregulation, autophagy, and adenosine 5’-monophosphate-activated protein kinase activation. Our findings establish that SAH acts as a metabolic signal coupling nutrient and energy availability to longevity via Ybt1, defining an adaptive/hormetic response for lifespan regulation in yeast.

title: Nuclear BbAtg8 interacts with BbMac1 as a transcriptional modulator to sustain nuclear copper homeostasis during conidial germination
abstract:
Pathogenic fungi endure host impose copper starvation by tightly coordinating trace metal homeostasis. However, how pathogens synchronize endogenous metal recycling with exogenous copper uptake to promote infection remains enigmatic. Using the entomopathogenic fungus
                     Beauveria bassiana 
                    , we uncovered a synergistic regulatory network that prioritizes nuclear copper enrichment during conidial germination. Under copper deprivation, the fungus deploys a highly coordinated dual-track survival strategy. In the cytoplasm, the core autophagy protein BbAtg8 drives autophagic flux, specifically triggering mitophagy to degrade mitochondria, thereby promoting the turnover and mobilization of endogenous copper stores. Concurrently, a nonlipidated pool of BbAtg8 translocates to the nucleus to coordinate exogenous uptake. Within the nucleus, BbAtg8 directly interacts with the copper-fist transcription factor BbMac1 via a functional Atg8-interacting motif (AIM). This physical interaction serves as a potent transcriptional modulator, significantly enhancing BbMac1’s DNA-binding affinity. Consequently, the Atg8-Mac1 complex hyper-activates the expression of three functionally redundant copper transporters (BbCtr1, BbCtr2, and BbCtr4) to aggressively absorb extracellular copper. Strikingly, severe copper deprivation triggers a dynamic spatial enrichment of these classical copper transporters at the nuclear envelope, which correlates with the sustained maintenance of nuclear copper homeostasis required for essential genomic functions and full fungal virulence. Together, these findings reveal how pathogens synchronize mitophagy-mediated endogenous turnover with Mac1-driven exogenous uptake, fundamentally expanding the role of autophagy proteins BbAtg8 into direct transcriptional coordinators of metal homeostasis. This dual-track regulatory model not only deepens our understanding of fungal adaptation to nutritional immunity but also provides potential targets for disrupting copper homeostasis to control fungal pathogens.
