title: A muscle-enriched mitochondrial protein regulates postnatal heart growth through mitonuclear ubiquinone–PPAR signaling
abstract:
Increased mitochondrial biogenesis and aerobic respiration in postnatal mammalian organs are essential for adaptation to extrauterine life, yet the functions of many tissue-enriched, developmentally regulated mitochondrial proteins remain poorly defined. By integrating mitochondrial proteome annotations with mouse and human transcriptomic datasets, we identified Coenzyme Q10a (Coq10a), a striated muscle-enriched mitochondrial protein, as a regulator of postnatal cardiac growth. Coq10a, the mammalian homolog of the yeast ubiquinone-binding protein Coq10p, is highly induced in the heart after birth through thyroid hormone-, Nkx2.5-, and Tbx5-dependent regulation. To define its physiological function, we generated three independent
                     Coq10a 
                    -deficient mouse models. Both global and cardiomyocyte-specific loss of
                     Coq10a 
                    promoted postnatal cardiac hypertrophy without impairing basal cardiac function or mitochondrial respiration. Instead,
                     Coq10a 
                    deficiency altered intracellular ubiquinone partitioning, resulting in increased ubiquinone accumulation in a microsomal membrane fraction. Transcriptomic analyses revealed enrichment of PPAR-associated metabolic gene sets and induction of established PPAR-responsive genes in
                     Coq10a 
                    -deficient hearts. Pharmacological inhibition of PPARα and PPARγ, but not PPARδ, attenuated the hypertrophic phenotype. Molecular dynamics simulations, docking analyses, and mutagenesis identified PPARα residues that contribute to differential responsiveness to ubiquinone. Although
                     Coq10a 
                    -deficient hearts maintained near-normal function under basal conditions, they exhibited increased susceptibility to pressure-overload stress. Together, these findings establish Coq10a as a regulator of intracellular ubiquinone partitioning and support a model linking altered mitochondrial lipid distribution and PPAR-associated signaling to postnatal cardiac growth. More broadly, they demonstrate how tissue-enriched mitochondrial proteins can mediate organ-specific physiological functions beyond energy production.

title: Omega-3 fatty acids reprogram tumor-associated macrophage cytokine signaling and suppress pancreatic cancer growth
abstract:
Dietary polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) shape inflammatory signaling within the pancreatic tumor microenvironment (TME), but the cellular mechanisms underlying their effects on tumor progression remain unclear. Using orthotopic models of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), we show that omega-3 (n-3) and omega-6 (n-6) PUFAs are differentially incorporated into tumor lipid pools, generating spatially heterogeneous lipid microenvironments. While an n-6–enriched diet accelerated PDAC growth, an n-3–enriched diet suppressed tumor growth in a T cell-independent manner. Examining inflammatory effects in PDAC tumors, the n-3 PUFA–enriched diet reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines, including IL-6 family members, and single-cell and spatial analyses identified tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) as the primary diet-responsive population. Indeed, selective conversion of n-6 to n-3 fatty acids within myeloid cells using an inducible
                     fat-1 
                    transgene, which encodes an n-3 desaturase that converts n-6 to n-3 PUFAs in vivo, was sufficient to suppress tumor growth, whereas fibroblast-restricted conversion had no effect. This finding is the first to formally establish that cellular origin of PUFA metabolism within the TME is a key determinant of tumor progression and identifies TAMs as critical mediators of n-3–dependent tumor suppression. Furthermore, the n-3 PUFA–enriched diet reduced Arg1
                     + 
                    immunosuppressive TAMs and promoted C1q
                     + 
                    and MHC-II
                     + 
                    antigen-presenting TAM populations enriched for antigen processing machinery and T cell–recruiting chemokines, alongside reduced IL-6 family cytokine production. Together, these findings establish macrophages as key mediators of n-3–driven tumor control and define a mechanism by which dietary lipids remodel cytokine signaling in the PDAC microenvironment.

title: Physical origins of speed control in swimming fishes
abstract: The linear relationship between tail-beat frequency and swimming speed in fish, first described by Bainbridge in 1958, has since been confirmed in species as disparate as eels and tuna. Dimensional scaling has explained why linearity should emerge at high Reynolds numbers, but the frequency–speed relationship itself has remained empirical, with no physical framework describing its behavior across swimming regimes, and no account of what sets the two quantities that define it: the distance covered per tail beat and the frequency below which forward motion supposedly ceases. Here, we derive a relationship from a balance of fin thrust, generated by a leading-edge vortex, and drag due to the boundary layer on the body. This framework yields an explicit expression for speed in terms of midline kinematics and body morphology. This formulation shows that the maximum stride length is set by the undulatory wavelength and the tail-beat phase offset, rather than by the conventional scaling metric of body length, and that no minimum frequency is required for forward motion. The model reproduces kinematic measurements from freely swimming glass catfish, published simulations, and Bainbridge’s original data. Without recalibration, it predicts the results of independent simulations spanning wide variations in wavelength, phase offset, and morphology to within ten percent. Linear scaling is thus one asymptotic limit of a more general propulsive relationship linking morphology and body-wave kinematics to swimming speed in fishes and bioinspired vehicles, where the body waveform, rather than the actuation frequency, emerges as the variable that sets performance.

title: Poly(phenolic) deposition is a prerequisite to poly(aliphatic) deposition for functional potato suberin
abstract:
Suberin deposition in specialized cells is a critical aspect of plant protection, providing both water retention and pathogen protection functions. Tissue specific suberization during plant development is mirrored by its wound induction in cells that do not normally suberize and provides a robust experimental system to investigate the process. Suberized cells are characterized by a cell wall–associated lignin-like poly(phenolic) domain, and an ester-linked poly(aliphatic) domain, with the latter often laid down in distinct lamellar bands between the cell wall and plasma membrane. Previous work provides evidence that poly(phenolic) deposition precedes, and is necessary for, poly(aliphatic) deposition. To test this further, we generated RNAi knockdown lines of three wound-induced peroxidase genes,
                     PRX19, PRX55, 
                    and
                     PRX105 
                    , in potato (
                     Solanum tuberosum 
                    ), the tubers of which produce an abundance of suberin upon wounding. Peroxidases catalyze the oxidative free radical coupling of phenolic monomers to form the suberin poly(phenolic) domain. The wound-induced suberin of PRX19-RNAi tubers had severely reduced poly(phenolics), reduced poly(aliphatics), and no apparent lamella. Functionally, wound-induced PRX19-RNAi tubers were more permeable to water loss and susceptible to bacterial soft rot. Overall, our data support the hypothesis that poly(phenolic) domain assembly is a strict requirement for subsequent deposition of aliphatic lamella within wound-induced suberin.

title: Modulation of avian iridescence via melanogenesis
abstract: The iridescent colors of birds originate in nanoscale feather structures that interact with light. Although the physical principles governing avian iridescence are well established, the molecular mechanisms assembling these nanostructures into photonic materials remain unknown. Here, we integrated genomic, cellular, and optical approaches to investigate the molecular basis of iridescent color formation in birds. We leveraged mutations that arose in the domesticated Indian peafowl and natural color variation in wild birds. In peafowl, we identified eight genes underlying gains, losses, and shifts of iridescence, whereas in two wild species, we used single-cell transcriptomics to profile asymmetric feathers in which iridescent and noniridescent barbules develop on opposite sides of the same feather. We found that all peafowl mutations mapped to melanogenesis genes, showing that variation in this pathway can modify diverse geometric features of feather photonic nanostructures. Mutations altering melanin composition collapsed multilayered photonic systems and yielded noniridescent tissues, whereas changes in melanosome abundance, elongation, or deposition timing generated multilayer architectures with variable periodicity and color. We further show in peafowl that transitions from noniridescent to iridescent plumage were associated with single-nucleotide mutations in a melanogenesis gene, suggesting that, in species already capable of forming multilayered nanostructures, iridescence can be gained by relatively small genetic changes. Single-cell transcriptomes from wild species also supported extensive melanocyte-centered regulatory rewiring associated with iridescence, including changes in melanosome maturation, trafficking, and intercellular signaling. Together, these results show that the nanoscale order underlying iridescence is developmentally plastic and highly responsive to the melanogenic environment.

title: A promoter G-quadruplex recruits Hrb27C to regulate NEMO and immune defense against Lyme disease pathogens in the deer tick
abstract:
Genomic DNA can adopt noncanonical secondary structures, such as G-quadruplexes (G4s), which serve as critical regulatory elements beyond the traditional double helix. Whether promoter G4s also participate in controlling innate immune signaling and host–pathogen interactions, however, remains unknown in arthropods. In this study, we identify a G4 structure within the promoter of the
                     NEMO 
                    (NF-κB essential modulator) gene in the deer tick
                     Ixodes scapularis 
                    . Using a combination of circular dichroism, isothermal difference spectra, and fluorescence-based assays, we demonstrate that this sequence forms a stable, parallel G4 topology in vitro and in vivo. Functional characterization via luciferase reporter assays reveals that this G4 scaffold is essential for proper
                     NEMO 
                    transcriptional output. Importantly, disruption of the G4 structure significantly reduces
                     NEMO 
                    expression and increases the burden of the Lyme disease spirochete
                     Borrelia burgdorferi 
                    . Genome-wide expression profiling further reveals that perturbation of the
                     NEMO 
                    G4 produces transcriptional changes that overlap with those observed following
                     NEMO 
                    silencing. These shared transcriptional responses are enriched for immune-associated genes and ribonucleoprotein-related pathways. We further identify the heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein Hrb27C as a structural binding protein that specifically recognizes the
                     NEMO 
                    G4 through its RNA recognition motif domains and facilitates
                     NEMO 
                    expression. Collectively, our findings establish promoter G4 architecture as an important regulatory layer in tick immunity, linking DNA topology to pathogen proliferation and providing a structural framework for understanding host–pathogen dynamics in disease vectors.

title: AI can persuade people to take political actions
abstract:
There is substantial concern about the ability of advanced AI to influence people’s behavior. A rapidly growing body of research has found that AI can produce large persuasive effects on people’s attitudes, but whether AI can persuade people to take consequential real-world actions has remained unclear. In two large preregistered experiments (
                     
                       
                         
                           N 
                           = 
                           17 
                           , 
                           950 
                         
                       
                     
                    responses from 14,779 people), we used conversational AI models to persuade participants on a range of attitudinal and behavioral outcomes, including signing real petitions and donating money to charity. We found sizable AI persuasion effects on these behavioral outcomes (e.g.
                     
                       
                         + 
                       
                     
                    19.7 percentage points on petition signing). However, we observed no evidence of a correlation between AI persuasion effects on attitudes and effects on behavior. Moreover, we replicated prior findings that information provision drove effects on attitudes, but found no such evidence for our behavioral outcomes. In a test of eight behavioral persuasion strategies, the strategy focused on information provision produced the smallest behavioral effect, though differences among the eight were small. Taken together, these results suggest that previous findings relying on attitudinal outcomes may generalize poorly to behavior, and therefore risk substantially mischaracterizing the real-world behavioral impact of AI persuasion.

title: Efficient and accurate steering of large language models through attention-guided feature learning
abstract: Activation steering, or direct manipulation of internal activations to guide large language model (LLM) responses toward specific semantic concepts, is emerging as a promising avenue for both understanding how semantic concepts are stored within LLMs and advancing LLM capabilities. Yet, existing steering methods are remarkably brittle, with seemingly nonsteerable concepts becoming completely steerable based on subtle algorithmic choices in how concept-related features are extracted. In this work, we introduce an attention-guided framework for activation steering that overcomes three core challenges associated with steering: 1) automatic selection of relevant token embeddings for extracting concept-related features; 2) accounting for heterogeneity of concept-related features across LLM activations; and 3) identification of layers most relevant for steering. Across a steering benchmark of 512 semantic concepts, our framework substantially improved steering over previous state-of-the-art (nearly doubling the number of successfully steered concepts) across model architectures and sizes (up to 70 billion parameter models). Furthermore, we use our framework to shed light on the distribution of concept-specific features across LLM layers. Overall, our framework opens further avenues for developing efficient, highly scalable fine-tuning algorithms for industry-scale LLMs.

title:
Loss of tRNA uridine thiolation affects mRNA translation, protein production, and metabolite accumulation in
                     Arabidopsis
abstract:
It is well established in yeast and animal system that the level of uridine thiolation at position 34 of tRNA anticodon loops can impact the decoding potential of the corresponding codons. Using
                     Arabidopsis thaliana 
                    , we confirm that the ability of the plant ribosome to decode AAA, GAA, and CAA codons is impaired when this thiol group is lost, leading to a reduction in protein production, especially for genes enriched in these codons. Interestingly, we observed that loss of tRNA thiolation results in variations in the levels of numerous proteins involved in sulfur-compound metabolism and amino acid biosynthesis. These variations, in turn, affect the accumulation of several sulfur-containing metabolites and amino acids, suggesting that the level of tRNA thiolation has a direct and profound impact on plant metabolism. We also demonstrate that U
                     34 
                    thiolation is essential for adjusting plant growth in response to sulfur limitation and that its absence directly affects the plant’s interaction with bacteria, including both pathogens and beneficial organisms. Our results support the hypothesis that the level of tRNA thiolation can be used in plant to link nutritional status to translation.

title: The basins of attraction of soft-sphere packings are not fractal
abstract: The energy landscape picture is a central tool to study many-body systems. In particular, the energy landscapes of glass-forming liquids, jammed packings, constraint satisfaction problems, or neural networks contain a plethora of minima corresponding to competing states. Due to their complexity, these landscapes resist analytical treatment and must be studied numerically. We focus on jammed soft spheres, a paradigmatic model of glasses and granulars, to expose the limitations of standard numerical methods in resolving the true structure of energy landscapes. We show that the C-language Variable-coefficients ordinary differential equation solver is the one with the best time-for-error trade-off for this problem, outperforming commonly used steepest-descent solvers by several orders of magnitude. Using this numerical approach, we provide unequivocal evidence that optimizers widely used in computational studies destroy all semblance of the true landscape geometry, even in moderately low dimensions. Employing a range of geometric indicators, both low- and high-dimensional, we show that earlier claims on the fractality of basins of attraction of minima originated from the use of inadequate mapping strategies. In reality, the basins of attraction of soft-sphere packings are smooth structures with well-defined length scales, a result that likely extends to a much broader family of problems.

title: Reconstructing actin dynamics of the leading edge from observational data
abstract: Mesenchymal cell migration starts with the protrusion of the cell’s leading edge, enabled by the branching growth of the actin network. Two crucial molecular players in protrusion are actin filaments and the Arp2/3 complex, the branching agent. Traditionally, protrusion models are intuited from several perturbative experiments. Recent multiplex microscopy imaging data promise to change this paradigm by providing measurements of naturally fluctuating densities of key proteins at the leading edge of unperturbed cells. We report an attempt to reconstruct the mechanistic protrusion model from such data. We analyze fluctuations of densities of actin filaments and Arp2/3 complex and cell edge velocity using phase space and regression analysis to reconstruct linearized dynamics of the coupled actin-Arp2/3-velocity system. We then build a nonlinear model of these dynamics based on previous knowledge of this system and parsimony. The resulting models recover the rates of reactions and mechanical and transport processes in the lamellipodium from a single nonperturbative experiment. The models posit that the dominant nonlinear term in the lamellipodial dynamics corresponds to the retrograde flow of the actin network in the cell frame. The models suggest that the protrusion is dominated by a damped oscillatory cycle resulting from a combination of positive feedback from the Arp2/3 complex to protrusion velocity and negative feedback from actin density to the velocity.

title:
A transposon inserted into
                     HELD1 
                    repressed maize husk leaf blade extension during maize domestication
abstract:
Husk leaves are the closest photosynthetic organs to the ear, which contribute directly to grain filling and have potential for yield improvement in maize. Teosinte has a long husk extended leaf blade, whereas maize exhibits a reduced or even no husk leaf blade. However, the genetic basis of this transition in the husk leaf during domestication remains unknown. In this study, we identified a major quantitative trait locus (QTL),
                     Husk Extended Leaf Blade 1 
                    (
                     HELD1 
                    ), corresponding to the
                     tassels replace upper ears1 
                    (
                     tru1 
                    ) gene. A 133-base pair (bp) Harbinger transposon inserted into the
                     tru1 
                    intron introduces two TEOSINTE BRANCHED 1 (TB1) binding motifs, thereby recruiting TB1 to directly enhance
                     tru1 
                    transcription. Further analyses revealed that TRU1 interacts with the transcription factor ALOG1, which in turn enhances the expression of
                     liguleless2 
                    (
                     lg2 
                    ), a key regulator of ligule development. Together with
                     brassinosteroid-deficient dwarf1 
                    (
                     brd1 
                    ) and
                     GA2ox1 
                    , these genes set up a regulatory network that defines the ligular-auricular position, controls the leaf blade-to-husk (sheath) ratio in husk and stem leaves, and regulates husk leaf blade length. Population genetic analyses indicate that
                     HELD1 
                    experienced significant human selection, resulting in the transposon insertion becoming the dominant allele in domesticated maize. Additionally, the teosinte
                     HELD1 
                    allele with extended husk leaf blades significantly enhances yield in maize. Our results demonstrate
                     HELD1 
                    is an important regulator of husk and stem leaf architectures, contributing to the ligular-auricular position to adjust the ratio of leaf blade to husk or sheath.

title: Quiescence to proliferation transition regulates asynchronous mitochondrial DNA replication dynamics
abstract: Each human cell contains hundreds to thousands of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) copies, only a small fraction of which replicates independently of the cell cycle. An asynchronous replication of the leading and lagging strands has been proposed to represent a major replication mode in mitochondria, complicating the investigation of mechanisms that regulate mtDNA replication. Using single-DNA-molecule analysis that distinguishes the origins and timing of replication of each strand, we show that the mitochondrial DNA replication machinery responds to the transition from quiescence to proliferation by dynamically dissociating strand-specific replication rates and modulating the physiological requirements for factors involved in replication and transcription. During this response, the requirement for mitochondrial RNA polymerase (POLRMT) in replication initiation increases, whereas that for primase-polymerase (PrimPol), which is thought to function in DNA repriming at DNA lesions, eventually decreases. Thus, precise quantification of mtDNA replication rates at the single-strand level reveals the temporally dynamic nature of the mtDNA replication machinery during the transition from quiescence to proliferation.

title: Insights from coproduced scenarios toward urban sustainability transformations
abstract: Urban sustainability transformations call for fundamental shifts in how cities are organized, developed, and governed. Yet we need a better understanding of the diversity of visions and pathways that can enable transformative change. We address this gap through an analysis of 60 coproduced positive scenario visions and pathways developed using the Sustainable Future Scenario process, across nine US and Latin American cities participating in the Urban Resilience to Extremes Sustainability Research Network. We engaged diverse urban stakeholders—including government, nonprofit, and private decision-makers, community leaders, residents, and academic collaborators—in more than 20 coproduction workshops to explore alternative urban futures of sustainability and resilience. We examined how the coproduced scenarios represent five domains of transformative change (nature–human relationships, economic transformation, governance, social and environmental justice, and infrastructure futures) and four theories of transformative change (structural/institutional, agency/power, goals of the system, and worldviews/values). Most pathways combined multiple theories of change operating across multiple domains, revealing urban transformations as entangled rather than singular interventions. Some strategies were common across cities—car-free regions, decentralized infrastructure, community-based governance, expanded fundamental rights—yet were pursued with different transformative aims, demonstrating how a strategy’s transformative intent depends on the theories of change behind it. These findings position coproduced scenarios as more than a normative or planning tool and offer an analytical approach for surfacing the possibility space of urban transformation.

title: Altered sperm DNA methylation provides an epigenetic route from overweight and older men to intergenerational disease transmission
abstract: The occurrence of childhood neurodevelopmental disorders has been steadily increasing for decades, yet we have little understanding of modes of inheritance implicated in these diseases. Epidemiology studies have revealed an association between an elevated paternal Body Mass Index (BMI) and age as factors implicated in increased risk for neurodevelopmental disorders in children. Epigenetic regulation of gene expression by DNA methylation at cytosines is susceptible to environmental, diet, and lifestyle changes. Yet, whether a man’s BMI and age influence the sperm methylome and potentially impact offspring development remains unresolved. Using MethylC capture sequencing, we identified over 38,000 differentially methylated CpGs in the sperm of men with an elevated BMI, with overlap occurring in regions associated with advanced paternal age. These were enriched for neural gene and disease ontologies. Differentially methylated regions localized to transposable elements that can act as active enhancers during human zygotic genome activation, and at gene promoters for early lineage specification. These results suggest that sperm methylome alterations that are linked to an elevated BMI may influence key embryonic transcriptional processes, notably those associated with trophectoderm and placental development.

title: Systemic collapse emergence from climate-induced perturbations in transportation networks
abstract: The interaction between human infrastructures and external events results in loss of functionality or even complete system disruption through a snowball effect of cascading failures. Their complex interplay challenges their prevention, affecting the human population that rely on their functionality. Understanding how these networks respond to external perturbations is crucial for predicting and mitigating the impacts of disruptive events. In particular, meteorological events, while not preventable, can have significant impacts on human infrastructure. Here, we propose a model coupling the dynamics of transportation systems to the dynamics of external events considered as fields, to capture at the same time the critical behavior of the former and the level of influence of the latter. The impact of rainfalls on real-world railway networks provides a compelling case study, showcasing local endemic and system-wide disruptions above a critical value of the rainfall strength. Remarkably, localized perturbations on the wider network reveals the local weaknesses of the global infrastructure, and we assess them in terms of system perturbability and corresponding societal risk. Our framework opens the door to the quantitative analysis of criticalities in essential human infrastructure imputable to vulnerabilities that are set to intensify due to climate change.

title: A neural operator framework for data-driven discovery of stability and receptivity in physical systems
abstract: Understanding how complex systems respond to perturbations, such as whether they will remain stable or what their most sensitive patterns are, is a fundamental challenge across science and engineering. Traditional stability and receptivity (resolvent) analyses are powerful but rely on known equations and linearization, limiting their use in nonlinear or poorly modeled systems. Here, we introduce a data-driven framework that automatically identifies stability properties of both equilibrium points and periodic orbits, as well as optimal forcing responses from observation data alone, without requiring governing equations. By training a neural network as a dynamics emulator and using automatic differentiation to extract its Jacobian, we can perform stability and receptivity analyses directly from data. We demonstrate the method on systems of increasing complexity, from canonical models to high-dimensional fluid flows and a real-world climate dataset, employing model reduction where needed and successfully identifying dominant instability modes and optimal input–output structures, even in strongly nonlinear regimes. By leveraging a neural network emulator, we readily obtain a nonlinear representation of system dynamics while additionally retrieving intricate dynamical patterns that were previously difficult to resolve. This equation-free methodology establishes a broadly applicable tool for analyzing complex, high-dimensional datasets, with potential relevance to grand challenges in fields such as climate science, neuroscience, and fluid engineering.

title: PCS-UQ: Uncertainty quantification via the Predictability–Computability–Stability framework
abstract: As machine learning (ML) enters high-stakes domains, trustworthy uncertainty quantification (UQ) is essential for safety. In this paper we introduce PCS-UQ, a framework based on the predictability, computability, and stability (PCS) principles for veridical data science. Starting with a candidate set of models or algorithms, PCS-UQ integrates a rigorous prediction-check to screen out unsuitable models in the set and utilizes bootstrap samples in order to capture both inter-sample variability and algorithmic instability for the prediction-checked algorithms. We then introduce a multiplicative calibration scheme to enhance local adaptivity, which can be viewed as a score function in conformal prediction. Moreover, we produce a compilation of 17 real-world regression datasets with manually constructed subgroups. On this benchmark, PCS-UQ maintains the target coverage while outperforming or matching conformal methods equipped with oracle-selected algorithms in interval width. PCS-UQ achieves consistent subgroup coverage, outperforming these oracle-selected conformal methods. Notably, PCS-UQ stands out in achieving both competitive interval widths and consistent subgroup coverage. Across six classification datasets, PCS-UQ reduces prediction set sizes by 20%. To scale the framework for deep learning, we propose computationally efficient variants that bypass expensive retraining. On three computer vision benchmarks, these variants reduce prediction set sizes by 20% over conformal baselines. Finally, we provide a theoretical proof that a modified PCS-UQ algorithm preserves valid coverage under exchangeability as a form of split conformal inference.

abstract: Ocean ecosystems have played a crucial role in people’s lives around the world for millennia. However, questions persist about when, why, and how people first began removing biomass from offshore habitats and established fisheries in distant, oceanic environments. We explore the antiquity and evolution of tuna (Thunnini) and billfish (Istiophoridae/Xiphiidae) fisheries, two groups of fishes that occur around the world, are economically significant, and are ecologically important open ocean apex predators. The earliest archaeological evidence of fishing for tuna occurs ~44,000 years ago and billfish at ~10,000 years ago, with early fisheries for some tuna species appearing around the world by 3,000 to 1,000 years ago. Most early fisheries are in areas where tunas and billfishes could be accessed relatively close to shore (e.g., submarine canyons) and/or where these fishes may come inshore seasonally or during warm ocean events. Early tuna and billfish fisheries were often linked to ceremony/ritual, alongside advances in maritime technologies. With few exceptions, sustained and intensive commercial exploitation of pelagic predators in offshore and oceanic habitats is a late development in the human past, occurring primarily during the last 200 y. Our findings document a long-term continuum of human interactions with global marine ecosystems spanning thousands of years, including significant differences between the timing and pathways by which people became dominant ecological drivers in nearshore compared to offshore/oceanic ecosystems.

title: Recent developments of fluorescent proteins and biosensors driven by cross-disciplinary insights
AmpliconSuite: an end-to-end workflow for analyzing focal amplifications in cancer genomes
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Here we present AmpliconSuite, a toolkit for focal amplification analysis from cancer whole-genome sequencing that identifies extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA), breakage–fusion–bridges and other amplification modes. Its ecContext module categorizes ecDNA structures to understand formation mechanisms. Validation across 175 metaphase fluorescence in situ hybridization-probed genes in 72 models demonstrated accurate predictions. Analysis of 6,506 patient pan-cancer samples revealed ecDNA-mediated oncogene co-amplification preferences. To democratize data sharing, we created AmpliconRepository, a community-contributable platform, enabling investigation of results across >15,000 publicly hosted samples.

abstract: Nature Reviews Genetics, Published online: 16 October 2026;  doi:10.1038/s41576-026-01028-z  In this Comment, the authors outline how the lack of a consistent evolutionary framework for defining and naming cell types complicates comparisons across species and obscures questions of homology. As a solution, they propose that cell-type nomenclature be grounded in evolutionary theory by identifying conserved regulatory cores and explicitly incorporating phylogenetic origins into cell-type names.

The class VIII myosin ATM2 stabilizes actin–plasma membrane contacts in tobacco pollen tubes by locally promoting PtdIns(4,5)P2 formation
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                    The intersection of actin filaments with the plasma membrane (PM) in plant cells involves lipid–protein interactions by the
                     Arabidopsis 
                    class VIII myosin ATM2 that are currently not understood. Using pollen tube cells as a model, we describe how ATM2 enables actin–PM contacts by modulating membrane lipid nano-organization. ATM2 bound anionic PM lipids, including phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PtdIns(4,5)P
                     2 
                    ), with no apparent preference for any particular lipid species. Overexpression of ATM2 unexpectedly stabilized actin dynamics and altered pollen tube morphology. Actin dynamics remained unaltered upon overexpression of a lipid-binding-defective ATM2 variant. ATM2 effects on actin dynamics required PtdIns(4,5)P
                     2 
                    , as artificial PtdIns(4,5)P
                     2 
                    depletion in pollen tubes abolished the effects of full-length ATM2 on actin dynamics despite its retained PM association. ATM2 colocalized and interacted with the PI4P 5-kinase PIP5K2, which resides at actin–PM contacts and forms PtdIns(4,5)P
                     2 
                    nanodomains facilitating rho-of-plants-dependent actin stabilization. Upon ATM2 overexpression, a fluorescent PtdIns(4,5)P
                     2 
                    biosensor decorated an extended PM region in vivo, indicating a promoting effect of ATM2 on PtdIns(4,5)P
                     2 
                    abundance. The catalytic activity of purified recombinant PIP5K2 protein was enhanced upon coincubation with a purified carboxy-terminal ATM2 fragment in vitro, suggesting that ATM2 contributes to the intrinsic regulation of PtdIns(4,5)P
                     2 
                    formation. Actin dynamics are thus stabilized at the actin–PM interface by ATM2 locally promoting the formation of PtdIns(4,5)P
                     2 
                    nanodomains, thereby self-reinforcing ATM2 recruitment while also facilitating rho of plants activation to stabilize membrane-proximal actin filaments.

title: Assembly-graph-assisted haplotype-resolved scaffolding of polyploid genomes
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                    Assembling polyploid genomes at the chromosome level remains a major challenge due to the difficulty of accurately distinguishing homologous chromosomes, leaving a vast number of polyploid species without high-quality genome sequences. Current chromatin conformation capture (3C)-based haplotype-resolved scaffolding methods often produce highly incomplete and mis-phased assemblies of complex polyploids, as short sequences lacking sufficient interaction support and collapsed regions with misleading signals are difficult to resolve. Here we present GPhase, a haplotype-resolved scaffolding algorithm that integrates 3C (for example, Hi-C, Pore-C and Omni-C) data with assembly graphs to enhance accuracy, completeness and contiguity. By leveraging graph connectivity derived from long-read overlaps, GPhase effectively overcomes key limitations of 3C. When applied to 15 complex polyploid genomes, GPhase reduced the sequence missing rate (BUSCO-based) by up to tens-fold, decreased the sequence error rate (
                     k 
                    -mer-based) by up to an order of magnitude and improved the contiguity (N50) of gap-free sequences by several-fold compared with existing tools.

abstract: Lewis et al. show that the shell coiling direction and body asymmetry of Japanese Euhadra snails are determined by variation in a myosin I gene. This natural variation in the left-right asymmetry or “chirality” of snails is ancient and not associated with any pathology.

title: Akkermansia muciniphila attenuates macrophage efferocytosis to enhance anti-PD-1 efficacy in microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer
abstract: Jiang et al. show that Akkermansia muciniphila reshapes the tumor immune environment to overcome PD-1 resistance in microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer (MSS CRC). Mechanistic studies and a phase 1 trial support gut microbiome modulation as a promising strategy to improve immunotherapy in this common treatment-resistant disease.

title: Thickness‐Gradient Liquid Metal Connectors for Seamless Electrophysiological Sensors
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   High‐fidelity electrophysiological monitoring requires wearable bioelectronic devices with mechanical properties closely matched to human skin. However, current approaches focus primarily on electrode design and performance, while overlooking mechanical compliance and interfacial continuity with complex and dynamic human skin. Mechanical mismatches across electrodes, connectors, and interconnects often lead to interfacial noise, motion artifacts, and electrical instability. In order to overcome these critical issues, we introduce a thickness‐gradient liquid metal (LM)/SEBS connector that enables seamless interfacial integration with skin, electrode, and interconnector interfaces through gradual mechanical compliance matching and manually activated metal network formation. The activated LM forms continuous and robust conductive networks, maintaining electrical stability under large tensile strain (∼1100%) and for repeatable deformation cycles. Skin‐mimetic conformal integration suggested here suppresses interfacial void formation and stress concentration and thereby preserves stable electrical pathways under dynamic skin deformation. As a result, the proposed system delivers markedly improved signal amplitude and signal‐to‐noise ratio, along with substantially lower noise, relative to conventional connector platforms. By systematically aligning mechanical compliance across sensor components, this mechanically adaptive design preserves seamless electrical pathways and minimizes motion‐induced artifacts under dynamic conditions, providing a robust platform for reliable electrophysiological monitoring in long‐lasting wearable bioelectronics.

title: An Anti‐Amyloidogenic Approach to Specifically Block Memory Consolidation in Mice for Therapeutic Intervention
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Post‐traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a mental health disorder triggered by exposure to a traumatic event, which manifests with anguish, intrusive memories, and negative mood changes. So far, there is no efficient treatment for PTSD other than symptomatic palliative care. However, the cytoplasmic polyadenylation element binding protein‐3 (CPEB3) has been recently associated with a potential risk gene for PTSD. Considering that the CPEB3 protein is a functional amyloid whose importance for long‐term memory consolidation in mammals is well established, we propose the active (amyloid) state of CPEB3 as a promising potential therapeutic target to investigate the blockade of the consolidation of traumatic memories using the anti‐amyloidogenic polyglutamine binding peptide 1 (QBP1). Here we report a genetic preclinical development evaluation in mice of this concept, providing a framework for future pharmacological treatment for PTSD based on the action of the QBP1 peptide. We first characterized the human CPEB3 (hCPEB3) protein in vitro, showing how its amyloid aggregation is inhibited by the active core of QBP1 (QBP1‐M8) without affecting other self‐assembly processes such as phase separation. Then, we generated and characterized a novel transgenic mouse that constitutively expresses QBP1 in tandem (TgQBP1). TgQBP1 mice exhibit impaired consolidation of simple learning after 24 h, affecting both hippocampus‐dependent and aversive memories. While recall of the fear context is reduced—resulting in a lack of extinction—QBP1 does not affect short‐term memory. Moreover, under a PTSD‐like protocol, TgQBP1 mice showed significant extinction of the traumatic memory and reduced anhedonia compared to WT mice, which showed the expected PTSD‐like symptoms of persistent aversive memory and anhedonia. Finally, the analysis of CPEB3 amyloid presence in extracted hippocampal samples showed a correlative decrease in murine CPEB3 oligomerization in the TgQBP1 mice. Taken together, these results strongly suggest that the amyloidogenic blockade of CPEB3 by the QBP1 peptide is a potential avenue for exploring future therapeutic approaches for the prevention and treatment of PTSD, pending validation through post‐developmental or pharmacological approaches.

title: From prompts to genomes: A constraint-first framework for AI-driven sequence design across life and viruses
Ten simple rules to build genomics capacity for routine laboratory practice in the Global South
abstract: Developing sustainable genomics capacity in the Global South requires more than technology transfer; it depends on human-centered approaches based on the workflows and existing expertise of laboratory personnel, institutional collaboration, and long-term integration into health systems. Drawing on lessons learned from regional capacity-building initiatives, this article proposes ten simple rules for implementing and sustaining genomics capacity within public health and clinical laboratory settings. These rules emphasize local context, strategic planning, continuous learning, and equitable collaboration. Together, they provide a roadmap for laboratories aiming to transform genomic technologies from research tools for diagnosis, surveillance and decision-making, into routine instruments for public health in low- and middle-income countries.
authors: Arabela Leal e Silva de Melo

title: Leveraging spatial structure to design spatially-targeted malaria interventions at the community-scale
abstract: Progress in malaria control has stagnated since the early 21st century in many countries, requiring new approaches such as the use of spatially-targeted interventions. However, evidence on the effectiveness of spatially-targeted interventions is mixed, depending on both the setting and intervention. In addition, the potential role of community health programs in implementing spatial targeting is underexplored, with models focusing on coarser spatial scales than those needed to guide programmatic activities. We developed a two-age-class, spatially-explicit model of malaria at the community-scale for a district in southeastern Madagascar, accounting for environmental heterogeneity and spatial structure, to explore spatially-targeted community health interventions. The model was fit to field-based case notifications and malaria prevalence data and then used to simulate three interventions: indoor residual spraying (IRS), supplemental coverage of long-lasting insecticide-treated nets (LLIN), and active case detection (ACD). We compared five scenarios, one with no spatial targeting and others targeting communities (i) nearest to clinics, (ii) furthest from clinics, (iii) with highest incidence, and (iv) that are spatially central. The non-targeted intervention was generally the most effective, but the least resource efficient. The second most effective intervention was based on spatial centrality, which reached a larger population while using fewer transportation resources than the non-targeted intervention. No combination of interventions was able to eliminate malaria in the district, although detecting symptomatic cases through ACD could avert 100% of severe malaria cases at high detection rates. These results highlight the potential for targeted malaria interventions, especially in low-income settings, that take into account spatial structure in the human population and transport networks to reduce malaria burdens using fewer resources than conventional district-wide interventions. [A French language abstract is available as Text A in S1 Appendix].

title: Computation-through-Dynamics Toolkit: Simulated datasets and quality metrics for dynamical models of neural activity
abstract: A primary goal of systems neuroscience is to discover how ensembles of neurons transform inputs into goal-directed behavior, a process known as neural computation. A powerful framework for understanding neural computation uses neural dynamics – the rules that govern how neural activity evolves over time – to explain how goal-directed input-output transformations occur. As dynamical rules are not directly observable, we need computational models that can infer neural dynamics from recorded neural activity. We typically validate such models using synthetic datasets with known ground-truth dynamics, but unfortunately existing synthetic datasets don’t reflect fundamental features of neural computation and may therefore be poor proxies for neural systems. Further, the field lacks validated metrics for quantifying the accuracy of the dynamics inferred by models. The Computation-through-Dynamics Toolkit (CtDToolkit) addresses these critical gaps by providing: 1) synthetic datasets that reflect computational properties of biological neural circuits, 2) interpretable metrics for quantifying model performance, and 3) a standardized pipeline for training and evaluating models with or without known external inputs. In this manuscript, we demonstrate how CtDToolkit can help guide the development, tuning, and troubleshooting of neural dynamics models. In summary, CtDToolkit provides a necessary framework for model developers to better understand and characterize neural computation through the lens of dynamics.

title: TraSPIN: inferring transporter specificity through language model-guided graph learning
abstract: Membrane transporters mediate cellular chemical exchange, yet their substrate specificities remain poorly characterized, with experimental studies constrained by the instability of membrane proteins. Existing computational tools often target narrow substrate classes or fail to generalize to distant homologs. We present TraSPIN, a geometric deep learning framework that jointly models transporter proteins and small-molecule substrates. TraSPIN outperforms existing methods, generalizes to unseen substrates and sequence-dissimilar transporters, and reveals structural determinants and sequence motifs of transporter–substrate recognition. Cross-species inference and de-orphanization of uncharacterized solute carrier proteins further demonstrate its utility for investigating transporter specificity and accelerating functional annotation.

title: ROMET-RNA benchmarks and selects RNA 3D structures using multiple predictors and alignment strategies
abstract:
Background
                      Accurate prediction of RNA tertiary structure is essential for understanding RNA function, yet systematic, controlled benchmarking and integration of RNA three-dimensional structure prediction methods, particularly with respect to multiple sequence alignment strategies used by deep learning models, remain limited. 
                  
                     Results
                      Here, we present ROMET-RNA, an automated benchmarking framework and meta-selection toolkit that benchmarks eleven state-of-the-art RNA structure predictors within a standardized workflow and evaluates three complementary MSA pipelines, rMSA, RNAcmap3 MARS, and Infernal RNAcentral. Model selection is performed using a consensus scoring strategy combining TM-scoreRNA based structural similarity with the deep learning derived statistical potential lociPARSE. Benchmarking across four non-redundant test sets comprising 205 RNAs, including CASP15, RNA Puzzles, and recent PDB structures, demonstrates that ROMET-RNA consistently selects more accurate models than individual methods would on its own and we confirm that this is not an artefact of training-test overlap. Further analysis reveals that coevolutionary information substantially improves accuracy, that optimal MSA strategies are method specific, and that MSA depth exhibits a nonlinear relationship with performance. 
                  
                     Conclusions
                      ROMET-RNA provides an open-source standardized framework that enhances RNA 3D structure model selection, supporting advances in RNA structural biology and genomics.

title: Dynamic landscapes of gene regulatory networks during early mammalian neurogenesis for understanding brain evolution and disorder risk
abstract:
Background
                      Neurogenesis is governed by dynamic transcriptional programs that vary across developmental time, brain region, and cell type, thereby forming regionally specialized neuronal circuits. However, the gene regulatory networks (GRNs) that coordinate these processes across species and brain regions are still not fully characterized. 
                  
                     Results
                      To address this, we construct a comprehensive GRN resource encompassing 24 neurogenic lineages from human, macaque, and mouse, enabling systematic cross-species and cross-regional comparisons. Integrated analyses characterize temporal regulatory dynamics and introduce a dynamic score to identify lineage-specific regulatory subnetworks, revealing hundreds of dynamic regulons and co-regulatory modules. We identify both known and novel candidate regulators that underlie neuronal differentiation and regional identity across the human brain and uncovered evolutionary divergence in neurogenic GRNs that distinguishes neurogenesis in humans from other species. Experimental characterization of the candidate neurogenic regulator ILF2 provides evidence for its role in neurogenesis. Furthermore, mapping disease-associated genes onto this resource reveals gene regulatory dynamics linked to 30 neurological disorders and traits, including autism spectrum disorder, schizophrenia, intellectual disability, and microcephaly. 
                  
                     Conclusions
                      Our study provides a comprehensive cross-species and cross-regional atlas of neurogenic gene regulatory networks and their temporal dynamics. This resource facilitates the discovery of key regulators of early neuronal development, offers insights into the evolution of human brain regulatory programs, and enables the investigation of disease-associated regulatory mechanisms. The resource is freely accessible through an interactive online platform.

title: Human DCM-time machine unravels cell state changes during primitive gut tube differentiation
Non-invasive genomic sampling uncovers novel connectivities and origins of confiscated gorillas
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Background 
                     Gorillas are a group of African great apes with two species and four subspecies that are currently critically endangered or endangered. Previous studies analyzing the genetics of wild gorillas from non-invasive samples such as faeces or hair have analysed short mitochondrial or nuclear markers, which may not reflect the wider nuclear genome. Recent technical advances in target capture hybridisation, enrich the endogenous DNA content of non-invasive samples, allowing contiguous genomic regions to be sequenced. 
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     Here, we generate georeferenced genetic dataset from faecal and hair samples of 280 wild gorillas, sampled from three of the four gorilla subspecies, across large parts of their present-day distributions. With this expanded representation of gorilla genetic diversity in the wild, we detect three population clusters in western lowland gorillas, with the Sangha River and its affluents acting as significant barriers to gene flow. We reconstruct patterns of past population connectivity between western lowland gorillas in the north-eastern distribution range and Cross River gorillas, which may have been facilitated by a migration corridor also used by the Central and Nigeria-Cameroon chimpanzee subspecies. Finally, we predict the geographic origins of wild-born gorillas, achieving a mean prediction error of 65 km, with a population-level resolution for mountain gorillas and some populations of western lowland gorillas. 
                   
                   
                     Conclusion 
                     Our work characterises fine-scale population structure in western lowland gorillas, which will be informative for future conservation strategies. This proof-of-concept in predicting geographic locations of wild gorillas, will be useful for future applications to geolocalise trafficked or rescued gorillas.

title: Commensal  Lachnospiraceae bacterium  mitigates colitis-induced mucin fucosylation deficits through ILC3/IL-22 axis
abstract:
Background
                      Flagellins from commensal bacteria are potent modulators of intestinal immunity, yet their strain-specific functions, particularly in promoting homeostasis in ulcerative colitis (UC), remain poorly defined. We investigate whether flagellin from the commensal  Lachnospiraceae bacterium 3–1-57 FAA CT1  ( L. 3–1-57  Fla) plays a role in UC pathogenesis and mucin fucosylation deficits. 
                  
                     Results
                      Clinically, compared with healthy controls and patients with UC in remission, patients with active UC exhibit reduced abundance of  L. 3–1-57 , which inversely correlates with disease severity. In mouse colitis models, we show that live  L. 3–1-57  or  L. 3–1-57  Fla attenuates intestinal inflammation and mucus barrier dysfunction, whereas  E. coli  flagellin exacerbates disease. Mechanistically,  L. 3–1-57  Fla directly binds TLR5 with high affinity and activates dendritic cells to produce IL-23. This cascade expands IL-22 +  group 3 innate lymphoid cells, drives fucosyltransferase 2-mediated MUC2 fucosylation, and restores mucus integrity. Crucially, genetic ablation of  Tlr5 , inhibition of α-1,2-fucosylation, or IL-22 neutralization abolishes these benefits, confirming that the TLR5–IL-23–IL-22 immune axis and fucosylation are indispensable for protection. 
                  
                     Conclusions
                      Our study establishes  L. 3–1-57  flagellin as a key mediator of intestinal homeostasis via a TLR5–IL-23–IL-22-dependent mucin fucosylation pathway. These findings nominate  L. 3–1-57  as a candidate next-generation probiotic, its flagellin as a potential postbiotic therapy for UC, and its fecal depletion as a potential noninvasive auxiliary diagnostic biomarker.

title: Benchmarking long-read aligner-caller pipelines for structural variant detection across ten angiosperm species with PacBio high-fidelity sequencing
abstract:
Background
                      Structural variants (SVs) play a central role in genome evolution and phenotypic diversity, yet the large genome size, high repeat content, and structural complexity hinder SV detection in plants. Despite extensive benchmarking on human data, the performance and cross-species generalizability of HiFi long-read SV detection pipelines for plants have been overlooked. 
                  
                     Results
                      Here, we use multiple assembly-based variant calling strategies to construct SV truth sets at base-level resolution for ten representative angiosperm species, followed by systematic benchmarking of 91 HiFi-based SV calling pipelines. Cross-species evaluation reveals pronounced heterogeneity in performance across pipelines and species with deletion detection generally outperforming insertion detection. Using a stability score to quantify the across-species generalizability, we identify NGMLR/Sniffles2 and NGMLR/DeBreak as optimal cross-species pipelines for deletion detection, while Minimap2/Sniffles1, Minimap2/cuteSV2, and pbmm2/cuteSV1 exhibit robust insertion detection. We also find that detection accuracy declines sharply for large SVs and variants located within repetitive regions, particularly simple repeats. Moreover, SV calling precision shares a nonlinear relationship with sequencing depth for each individual haplotype, with  F  1  scores peaking at ~ 15 × coverage. 
                  
                     Conclusions
                      This study establishes a benchmarking framework for plant SV detection and provides high-confidence SV truth set resources that can, together, guide the selection of robust, scalable SV calling pipelines for plant genomics.

title: Germline structural variation involving gynecologic and breast cancers reveals polygenic signatures of tumor mutational load
abstract:
Background
                      Germline structural variants (SVs), genomic variants involving larger segments of the human genome, are understudied in the context of cancer. The impact of germline variants on the regulation of specific genes is highly dependent on tissue and cellular context, necessitating focused, multi-omics studies by cancer tissue of origin. 
                  
                     Results
                      Here, we combine patient germline SV data with tumor multi-omics profiling across 2006 breast and gynecologic cancers, including breast, cervical, ovarian, uterine endometrial, and uterine carcinosarcoma tumors, to determine the extent to which germline SV patterns influence the tumor molecular landscape. Rare germline SV events predicted to disrupt specific cancer-relevant genes cumulatively affect approximately 29% of patients. We find thousands of genes exhibit significant associations between nearby germline SV breakpoints and altered tumor gene expression or DNA methylation. These associations are either specific to tumor type or shared across multiple tumor types and involve numerous cancer-relevant genes. We also identify widespread associations of germline SV patterns with tumor somatic mutational load, including copy number alteration and somatic structural variation, with similar patterns observed in additional cancer cohorts beyond gynecologic and breast cancers. Notably, we find a germline deletion SV spanning  UGT2B17  (involving 36% of patients), is associated with reduced  UGT2B17  expression and lower tumor mutational load. 
                  
                     Conclusions
                      Germline SV-associated dysregulation in known cancer susceptibility genes or established cancer related genes considerably expands the spectrum of patients with evidence of a germline contribution to cancer development or progression. The patient’s genetic background may influence tumor characteristics, including somatic mutational load.

title: The contribution of short tandem repeats to splicing variation in the human prefrontal cortex
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Background 
                     Splicing disruption has been implicated in a range of heritable phenotypes, including numerous psychiatric and neurological disorders. Recent studies have focused largely on single nucleotide polymorphisms or short indels. Despite growing evidence that genetic variation at short tandem repeats (STRs) influences splicing, large-scale studies of STR-mediated splicing in the brain have been limited by low sample sizes of available RNA-seq data or exclusion of certain classes of STRs. 
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     
                      Here, we leverage deep RNA-seq and SNP array data from 336 human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) samples collected by the Human Brain Collection Core. We identify 51,343 unique STRs for which copy number is significantly associated with one or multiple alternative splicing events of nearby genes (spliceSTRs). We prioritize and characterize candidate causal spliceSTRs using three orthogonal fine-mapping strategies, identifying 1,313 high-confidence fine-mapped spliceSTRs, and further find strong associations between copy number of certain repeat units and binding of specific RNA-binding proteins (RBPs). Co-localization analyses using summary statistics from genome-wide association studies for 6 brain-related disorders identified multiple signals that may be driven by fine-mapped spliceSTRs, including a previously identified (
                       GT 
                      )
                       n 
                       repeat that is a spliceSTR for
                       PLEKHA1 
                      associated with Alzheimer’s disease as well as a newly identified (
                       AGG 
                      )
                       n 
                      spliceSTR in
                       SEPTIN3 
                      co-localized with schizophrenia.
                     
                   
                   
                     Conclusions 
                     Our findings highlight the role of STRs in regulating alternative splicing in the human brain, suggesting a general relationship between STR polymorphism and RBP-mediated splicing events, and identify specific spliceSTRs detected by co-localization analysis as candidate causal variants for brain-related disorders.

title: Extensive admixture and introgression shape genetic diversity and evolutionary adaptation in indigenous East Asian cattle
abstract:
Background
                      The complex introgression history of indigenous East Asian cattle is at the root of their remarkable diversity. Characterization of this diversity is a crucial step in understanding the genomic basis of adaptation to East Asian agricultural systems. However, the evolutionary history of indigenous East Asian cattle has remained poorly documented. 
                  
                     Results
                      Here, we present the largest short-read whole-genome sequencing dataset to date, including 802 indigenous Chinese cattle of 55 breeds/populations from diverse geographic regions, to address the population structure, genetic origins, and biological adaptations of this underrepresented population. We identify seven distinct genetic populations within Chinese cattle that were influenced by inter- and intraspecific introgression. We review introgression from Asian bovine species and reveal its geographical distribution characteristics in Chinese cattle. We identify a major taurine × indicine cattle admixture event during the Tang and Song dynasties (894–1210  AD ), which facilitated rapid local adaptation with a predominant effect on the immune system. Moreover, we present a comprehensive catalog of loci that underwent divergent selection across East Asian agroecological zones, including genes associated with cold tolerance, heat tolerance and meat production. 
                  
                     Conclusions
                      Our findings indicate that admixture between taurine and indicine cattle, together with introgression from other Asian bovine species, contributed to the adaptive evolution of indigenous East Asian cattle.

title: A new phased assembly of the Antarctic spiny plunderfish provides novel insights into the evolution of the notothenioid radiation
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Background 
                     Notothenioids are a well characterised species flock endemic to the Antarctic and an important model group for studying genome adaptation to extreme cold. A new reference assembly and clade-wide comparative genomic analysis allow for investigation of cryonotothenioid evolution and the appearance of novel functionalities linked to cold adaptation. 
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     
                      A new phased assembly of a model notothenioid,
                       Harpagifer antarcticus 
                      , demonstrated low levels of haplotypic variability across the genome. Nevertheless, numerous insertions from multiple LINE-L2 clades were found, suggesting ongoing transposition with potential contribution to speciation. Contrary to expectations the
                       afgp 
                      locus was highly similar between haplotypes, except for large length allelic variants of afgp genes. Analysis suggests a model for the
                       afgp 
                      locus expansion in
                       H. antarcticus 
                      through segmental tandem duplications involving two pairs of
                       afgp 
                      genes at time. Syntenic reconstruction of genomes from across the clade demonstrates conserved macrosyntenic relationships and group specific chromosomal fusions of notothenioids. Quantification of genome gain and transposition rates during cryonotothenioid diversification showed a first ancestral slow genome expansion concurrent with historic temperature drops. This was followed by lineage-specific massive peaks of genomic gain and transposition activity. Finally, we identified a set of genes that underwent ancestral diversifying selection and acquired novel conserved non-coding elements during the cryonotothenioid emergence. These were related to antioxidants and proteostasis, which may have facilitated the notothenioid Antarctic radiation.
                     
                   
                   
                     Conclusions 
                     Diversifying selection and genomic gain linked to transposon activity are primary contributors to lineage-specific evolutionary dynamics through the clade which facilitated adaptation to life in the cold.

title: To reverse nature loss, change what drives it
abstract: This week, at the 17th Meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP17), delegates from 195 countries and the European Union are gathering in Yerevan, Armenia, for a global review of progress under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, an international set of goals and targets adopted in 2022 to tackle the biodiversity crisis. The urgent question before them is clear: What must change now to halt and reverse nature’s decline and put it on a path to recovery by 2030? COP-17 comes as international cooperation is under increasing strain. Extreme weather is intensifying, ecosystem deterioration is creating new security risks, and geopolitical tensions are rising. Yet nature’s decline does not pause for geopolitical instability—it deepens it. That makes effective multilateralism, with North and South as equal partners, more important, not less.
