title: In situ structure of the human ciliary transition zone links linker defects to primary ciliary dyskinesia
abstract:
The ciliary transition zone (TZ) regulates ciliary proteome composition, yet its molecular architecture, protein content, and contribution to motile ciliopathies remain poorly defined. We applied in situ cryo–electron tomography and subtomogram averaging to human multiciliated epithelial cells. This approach resolved TZ-specific doublet microtubules at subnanometer resolution and identified nine constituent proteins. We found that epithelial cell transforming 2 like (ECT2L) and double zinc ribbon and ankyrin repeat-containing protein 1 (DZANK1) form the major linker complexes between adjacent TZ doublet microtubules. Biallelic loss-of-function variants in either gene cause primary ciliary dyskinesia.
                     ECT2L 
                    and
                     DZANK1 
                    deficiency disrupted TZ architecture, caused microtubular abnormalities and abnormal bulbous ciliary tips, and impaired mucociliary clearance. These findings establish a direct genetic link between TZ defects and human motile ciliopathy and illustrate how in situ structural biology can uncover mechanisms of human disease.

title: Modular van der Waals MOSFETs through layer-by-layer chalcogen substitutions
abstract:
In two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), the local electrostatic field of the chalcogen
                     p 
                    -orbitals dictates the crystal field splitting of the transition metal
                     d 
                    -orbitals, stabilizing diverse electronic states from semiconducting and semimetallic to exotic topological phases. On-demand substitution of the lattice chalcogens is therefore an efficient route to tuning TMDC electronic phases. Here, we custom-molded van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures by layer-by-layer vapor-phase chalcogen substitution starting from
                     p 
                    -type WSe
                     2 
                    multilayers into which we locally inscribed insulating WO
                     
                       x 
                     
                    ,
                     n 
                    -type WS
                     2 
                    , and semimetallic WTe
                     2 
                    . This spatially precise conversion seamlessly integrated distinct electronic phases, both vertically and laterally, into modular vdW semiconductor heterostructures that are otherwise inaccessible. As a demonstration, we integrated WO
                     
                       x 
                     
                    /WSe
                     2 
                    local gate stacks to build ultrascaled metal oxide–semiconductor field effect transistors (MOSFETs), achieving an unprecedented subthreshold swing at subnanometer equivalent oxide thickness.

title: Stereoselective polysubstituted bicyclo[1.1.0]butane synthesis by rhodium-catalyzed kinetic resolution
abstract:
Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) are a distinctive class of strained small-ring carbocycles of growing importance in synthetic and medicinal chemistry. However, the enantioselective synthesis of polysubstituted BCBs remains a largely unsolved challenge. In this study, we report a general chemical platform for the stereoselective assembly of chiral or meso 1,2,3,4-tetrasubstituted BCBs from internal alkynes and carbenes through stepwise [2+1+1’] or one-pot [2+1+1] cycloaddition reactions, respectively. Successful execution of these transformations exploits the combination of triftosylhydrazones (carbene precursors) and chiral dirhodium catalysts. The sterically hindered catalyst Rh
                     2 
                    (
                     R 
                    -3,5-
                     di 
                    PheTPCP)
                     4 
                    features a confined chiral microenvironment that enables exquisite discrimination between cyclopropene enantiomers, affording highly enantioenriched polysubstituted BCBs through kinetic resolution upon reaction with chiral rhodium carbenes. This chemistry operates under mild reaction conditions, uses readily available starting materials, and exhibits broad substrate scope.

title: Deterministic generation and distribution of genuine multipartite entanglement in macroscopic acoustic resonators
abstract: Generating complex multimode entanglement is a central goal of quantum information science. However, scalable creation of genuine multipartite entanglement is challenging as it requires excellent control and efficient state verification. We report the generation and transfer of genuine multimode entanglement across two multimode acoustic resonators. We prepare genuine multipartite entangled states involving two, four, and six modes across the resonators with respective fidelities of 0.912 ± 0.003, 0.790 ± 0.003, and 0.570 ± 0.001. We further demonstrate the transfer of two- and four-mode genuine entangled states between the resonators with fidelities of 0.785 ± 0.006 and 0.601 ± 0.006. This hardware-efficient and scalable architecture enables deterministic control and generation of complex multimode mechanical states. Our results push the boundary of quantum control in macroscopic mechanical systems, establishing a pathway toward large-scale mechanical quantum networks.

title: Electrically driven chiral emission from plasmonic tunnel junctions
abstract: Chirality plays a crucial role in a broad range of processes, including light-matter interactions in physics, chemistry, and biology, while quantum tunneling provides a promising mechanism for light generation at the nanoscale. By integrating tunnel junctions with chiral plasmonic nanohelicoids, we achieved electrically induced nanoscale generation of chiral light at the single-particle level. The tunneling-driven resonant excitation of chiral dipolar modes of the nanohelicoids results in emission of a vortex light beam possessing both spin angular momentum with handedness selectivity of more than 0.8 and orbital angular momentum equal in magnitude and opposite in sign. Our electrically driven approach offers a means for engineering photon spin generation at the nanoscale, highlighting its potential for next-generation optical components in display applications, as well as quantum information processing and photochemistry.

title: Atomic functional site scaffolding in biopolymers with RFdiffusion3
abstract: The catalytic and other sophisticated functions of biomolecules arise from the placement of many atoms in three-dimensional space. Here, we describe a generative artificial intelligence method for biopolymers, RFdiffusion3 (RFD3), which employs free atom diffusion to satisfy complex sets of atomic constraints more rapidly and accurately than previous methods across several challenges from enzyme design to RNA structure design. We demonstrate experimentally the power of the RFD3 pipeline for enzyme design by designing de novo phosphotriesterases with a complex active site architecture incorporating a carbamylated lysine coordinating two metal ions and zinc proteases specific for the transthyretin protein involved in amyloid diseases; in both cases we obtain active catalysts in zero shot 96 construct design campaigns.

title: Engineering ordered two-dimensional defect phases to strengthen structural alloys
abstract: Defects in crystals are usually considered to be consequences of deformation, but they can also be engineered as strengthening features. Planar defects can strengthen structural alloys but usually form only during deformation or service, limiting control over their density, stability, and chemistry. We show that predeformation followed by aging can convert such defects into a designed architecture of ordered defect phases. In a single-crystal cobalt-nickel–based superalloy and a polycrystalline cobalt-chromium-tungsten alloy, this treatment creates dense networks of coherent, atomically thin, ordered defect–confined phases. These increase room-temperature strength by more than 200 megapascals and reduce the superalloy’s minimum creep rate by more than threefold. Electron microscopy and simulations show that local chemical ordering amplifies strengthening and that the ordered defect phases remain shearable while impeding slip transmission.

title: Magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor
abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires a universal gate set, but the necessary non-Clifford gates represent a significant resource cost for most quantum error correction architectures. Magic state cultivation offers an efficient alternative to resource-intensive distillation protocols; however, testing the proposal’s assumptions represents a challenging departure from quantum memory experiments. We present an experimental study of magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor. We implement cultivation, including code-switching into a surface code, and develop a fault-tolerant measurement protocol to bound the magic state fidelity. Cultivation reduces the error by a factor of 40, with a state fidelity of at least 0.9999(1) (retaining 8% of attempts). Our results experimentally establish magic state cultivation as a viable solution to one of quantum computing’s most important challenges.

title: Airflows redefine the cost of aerial transport in the wild
abstract: Fuel economy matters to both animals and machines, as the cost of transport can determine where, when, and how far locomotion is possible. However, established estimates of these values for animal flight come from laboratories and treat the atmosphere as constant, even though free-flying animals routinely extract energy from atmospheric flows. Using high-resolution movement data, we estimate the cost of transport for 50 bird and bat species flying in the wild. Our results revise the classic ranking of locomotion costs, suggesting that flying can be cheaper than swimming though almost as costly as running, depending on interactions between physical environment, morphology, and behavior. Linking transport costs to atmospheric conditions provides a mechanistic basis for predicting how changing windscapes will reshape the energetics, movements, and distributions of flying animals.

title: Empirical constraints on ice cliff calving
abstract: When calving cliffs at the margins of Earth’s ice sheets exceed a critical height, runaway retreat may be initiated in a process called the marine ice cliff instability. However, sufficiently tall ice cliffs have rarely been observed. To address this gap, we measured the characteristics of 15,330 ice cliffs across Earth’s ice sheet margins using laser altimetry. We show that cliff height is highly correlated with mélange thickness, water depth, and crevassing. We found that tall cliffs calve more rapidly than parameterizations assume, but dynamic thinning and retreat into regions with low ice thickness gradients prevent runaway retreat. These observations suggest that model projections may underestimate subannual rates of cliff calving, but that the potential for instability will depend sensitively on additional quantities, not cliff height alone.

title: Glycan recognition by a plant damage-sensing immune receptor
abstract: Pathogens target and degrade the extracellular matrix surrounding plant cells. A central question is how cell wall–derived damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) are recognized and integrated to trigger immune responses. We address this question by determining the structure of the extracellular multidomain of the impaired in glycan perception 1 (IGP1) receptor in both apo form and bound to the cellulose-derived DAMP cellotriose. Structural analyses reveal that constitutive interactions of leucine-rich repeat (LRR)–malectin domains preconfigure IGP1 for ligand recognition and that the receptor features a highly specific sugar-binding pocket in the LRR domain capable of distinguishing fine variations in glycan structures. By directly sensing cello-oligomers, IGP1 operates as a cell wall surveillance receptor that links pathogen-induced wall degradation to immune alerting, equipping plants to mount rapid and robust defense responses.

title: Dendritic computation for abstract rule-based flexible decision-making
abstract: Intelligent behavior involves flexible integration of sensory input and abstract rule knowledge. Dendritic computation has been shown to contribute to top-down modulation of sensory processing; however, whether and how it is involved in flexible cognitive processing remains to be elucidated. Combining a rule-based flexible decision-making task with in vivo two-photon imaging and optogenetics in mice, we found that within single layer 5 extratelencephalic neurons in the auditory cortex, apical dendrites preferentially encoded the inferred abstract rule and somata preferentially represented sensory stimuli, whereas choice signals were present in both compartments. Optogenetic dendritic inhibition impaired rule-dependent somatic choice coding, supporting a task-relevant integration across the dendritic and somatic compartments. These results indicate that dendritic computation in cortical neurons mediates flexible behavior.

title: Regulation of target gene expression by chromatin-associated protein-coding transcripts in plants
abstract:
Protein-coding transcripts are regarded as intermediates that mediate DNA-to-protein information flow, leaving their noncoding regulatory potential largely underappreciated. Genome-wide profiling of RNA–chromatin interactions in
                     Arabidopsis 
                    has uncovered widespread associations between protein-coding transcripts and distinct genomic loci, implying that they possess regulatory functions. Here, we found that
                     BT2 
                    and
                     GSL8 
                    transcripts modulate target gene transcription independently of their protein products through distinct mechanisms. The
                     BT2 
                    transcript represses transcription of its targets
                     CEP2 
                    and
                     MRF4 
                    by forming RNA–DNA triplexes, thereby restricting root growth and promoting flowering, whereas
                     GSL8 
                    acts through a triplex-independent pathway. Our findings unveil intrinsic regulatory activities of protein-coding transcripts, challenging the canonical definition of mRNA function and blurring the functional distinction between coding and noncoding RNAs in the context of genome evolution.

title: Structural basis for size-selective perception of chitin in plants
abstract:
Plants detect microbes through pattern recognition receptors that perceive conserved microbial surface motifs known as microbe-associated molecular patterns (MAMPs). Lysin motif (LysM) receptors recognize and mediate downstream responses to chitinous MAMPs. In this study, we elucidated the mechanism for the specific recognition of long-chain chitin oligomers and identified a hallmark bridge domain characteristic of the CHITIN PERCEPTION (CHIP) receptor class. Structural analysis of receptor-ligand complexes, biochemistry, and in planta functional studies of inhibitory nanobodies revealed the mechanism of size-selective, high-affinity chitin perception in
                     Lotus japonicus 
                    and
                     Medicago truncatula 
                    . Additionally, we identified the CHITIN ELICITOR RECEPTOR KINASE (CERK) class as low-affinity, yet essential, co-receptors and propose a mechanistic model for a ligand-induced core signaling heterocomplex. Our findings establish the structural and mechanistic basis of differential chitin perception and receptor complex assembly in chitin-elicited plant immune signaling.

title: A pair of chitosan receptors confer broad-spectrum fungal resistance
abstract:
Chitosan, a major fungal cell wall component, activates plant immunity, yet the underlying perception mechanism remains unknown. In this study, we identified OsFID1, an apoplast-localized DUF26 domain protein, as a chitosan-binding receptor essential for chitosan-triggered immunity. OsFID1 forms a receptor complex with OsFID2, a plasma membrane–localized DUF26 receptor-like kinase, to mediate chitosan sensing and immune activation, requiring OsFID2 phosphorylation for function. The OsFID1-OsFID2 complex confers broad-spectrum resistance to fungal pathogens. OsFID1 homologs are conserved in land plants, which show chitosan-binding activity in both monocots and dicots. Ectopic expression of
                     OsFID1 
                    in wheat and maize enhanced fungal resistance without growth penalty. These findings uncover a conserved receptor complex for direct chitosan sensing, advancing our understanding of plant-fungus interactions and providing a potential strategy for engineering durable fungal resistance crops.

title: Frequency encoding regulates cell type composition in the small intestine
abstract: Intestinal homeostasis requires tight regulation of stem cell maintenance and differentiation to absorptive and secretory cell types, two major intestinal lineages. Key signaling pathways have been identified, but how they balance cell type composition remains unclear. We uncovered oscillatory expression of the Notch-target protein Hes1 (hairy and enhancer of split 1) that controls cell fate specification in a frequency-dependent manner. An endogenous fluorescent Hes1 reporter revealed distinct, cell type–specific oscillation frequencies forming a gradient along the crypt-villus axis, which was modulated by cell cycle phase as well as Wnt (wingless-related integration site)–signaling and Notch-signaling activity. We developed a microfluidic system to modulate Notch-signaling oscillations in organoids and found the oscillation frequency to regulate the balance of cell type composition. This study provides evidence that information for cell fate specification is encoded in the frequency of an oscillatory signal.

title:
Gate-tunable chiral spin mode in WSe
                     2 
                    /WS
                     2 
                    moiré superlattices
abstract:
The interplay between many-body and spin-orbit coupling (SOC) effects can lead to previously unobserved phenomena in solids. Chiral spin modes (CSMs) are collective spin excitations that arise from such interplay and connect states with opposite chirality. Here, we report a gate-tunable CSM that occurs between conduction SOC-split minibands in near-0°-twisted WSe
                     2 
                    /WS
                     2 
                    bilayers. This mode manifests as a sharp resonance with giant Raman efficiency in the pseudovector-symmetry channel of the Raman spectra. By varying the filling, the CSM transitions from a chiral spin exciton to an excitonic polaron. The spin-flip nature is directly confirmed by the Zeeman effect, and the filling dependence indicates a charge-transfer insulator at unity filling. Our results demonstrate that transition metal–dichalcogenide moiré superlattices are a fertile platform for exploring exotic low-lying collective excitations.

title:
PbSnRK1 
                    ‐Mediated Phosphorylation of
                     PbTCP13 
                    Regulates Glucose‐Responsive Lignin Biosynthesis via
                     PbMYB11 
                    During Pear Stone Cell Formation
authors:
Jianan He, 
Xuxu Wang, 
Abdul Basit, 
Wen Li, 
Jiahui Chao, 
Wenyu Zhao, 
Mingxu Niu, 
Xin Yan, 
Yuanhui Yu, 
Kaijie Qi, 
Zhihua Xie, 
Shaoling Zhang, 
Katsuhiro Shiratake, 
Khanizadeh Shahrokh, 
Shutian Tao
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Stone cell lignification is a key determinant of pear fruit texture and commercial quality, and this process has been reported to be tightly coupled to cellular glucose availability. However, how glucose dose‐dependently targets transcription factor phosphorylation during lignin biosynthesis remains largely unknown. Using yeast two‐hybrid library screening and phosphorylation assays, we found that PbSnRK1, a glucose‐responsive kinase, interacts with and directly phosphorylates PbTCP13, thereby participating in the regulation of stone cell lignification. PbSnRK1 serves as an energy‐status sensor linking glucose signalling to biphasic regulation of lignin metabolism in pear. Under low‐glucose conditions, activated PbSnRK1 phosphorylates the transcription factor PbTCP13 at Ser265, targeting it for 26S proteasome‐mediated degradation and thereby derepressing PbMYB11‐
                     PbCCR1 
                    cascade associated with lignin biosynthesis. Under high‐glucose conditions, suppressed PbSnRK1 kinase activity results in PbTCP13 protein accumulation, which restricts excessive lignification by both repressing
                     PbCCR1 
                    transcription and physically interacting with PbMYB11 to inhibit its transactivation capacity. This PbSnRK1‐PbTCP13‐PbMYB11 cascade, balanced by glucose concentration, acts as a molecular switch that activates stone cell formation and lignification at low‐glucose levels during early fruit development, while restricting excessive lignification at high‐glucose levels during later stages, providing new mechanistic insights into energy‐coupled secondary wall metabolism in fleshy fruits.

title:
A St‐derived genome contributes to the formation of the wheat
                     BB 
                    genome
abstract:
Summary 
                   
                     
                       
                         Although substantial efforts have been made to identify the progenitor of the wheat BB genome, the precise donor remains elusive. 
                       
                       
                         
                          In this study, we first investigated the origin of the BB genome using a BB‐specific
                           atp6 
                          gene harboring unique 5′‐end sequences, which is present in multiple copies and partially pseudogenized in the BB genome. BLAST searches revealed that multi‐copied
                           atp6 
                          (pseudo)genes occur exclusively in polyploid St‐genome species.
                         
                       
                       
                         
                          An ultrametric phylogeny constructed from genome‐wide single‐copy genes resolved the divergence of
                           Aegilops speltoides 
                          (SS genome) and the St genome
                           c 
                          . 4 million years ago, coinciding with the estimated origin of the BB genome. Furthermore, genome‐wide single‐nucleotide polymorphism (SNP)‐based allele matching showed that the St genome best explains BB alleles after SS, with an SS : St SNP ratio of 3 : 1, suggesting that the St genome likely contributed to the BB formation via two independent hybridization events with the SS ancestor. Finally, we identified 52 BB‐specific genes to facilitate the search for the true BB donor or the transitional hybrid.
                         
                       
                       
                         This study provides compelling evidence for the St genome's critical contribution to the BB genome and advances our understanding of how the complex hexaploid genome of bread wheat was formed and reshaped over evolutionary time.

title: Preparing, pairing and recovering: how angiosperms coordinate double fertilization
abstract:
Summary 
                   Double fertilization is a defining reproductive characteristic of angiosperms. During this process, two sperm cells fuse separately with the egg cell and the central cell to generate the embryo and endosperm, the two core components of the seed. Recent studies have revealed that male and female gametes are maintained in tightly regulated prefusion states and that their subsequent interaction proceeds through a series of precisely controlled steps. In angiosperms, gamete interaction also raises distinctive biological questions because it involves two fertilization events. Elucidating the molecular basis of male–female gamete interaction will not only deepen our understanding of double fertilization but also provide a conceptual foundation for improving crop‐breeding strategies.

title: Alexandre Antonelli
A suppressor screen uncovers flu as a weak mutant and chloroplastic 1O2 triggers EX1‐independent stress responses in Arabidopsis
authors:
Fan Zhang, 
Min Hu, 
Huan Zhao, 
Fengguang Wang, 
Mingxuan Li, 
Yu Zhang, 
Jiale Shi, 
Shiguo Chen, 
Jingrui Li, 
Liangsheng Wang
abstract:
The logical basis and proposed model for  1 O 2  generation and dosage-dependent signaling. 
 See also the Commentary on this article by  Grimm,  252 : 1354–1356.  
 
 Summary 
 

Singlet oxygen ( 1 O 2 ) is the main reactive oxygen species produced in chloroplasts, particularly under environmental stress conditions. Studies using the Arabidopsis conditional  flu  ( flu1-1 ) mutant have shown that chloroplastic  1 O 2  acts as a signal, activating retrograde signaling that eventually leads to photoinhibition or cell death.

Through a forward genetic screen for suppressors using ethyl methanesulfonate (EMS)-mutagenized Arabidopsis  flu1-1/ex1  mutants, we isolated two suppressor mutants ( mut1  and  mut2 ) that restored  1 O 2 -induced stress responses. Using combined methods of map-based cloning and high-throughput sequencing, we mapped the causal mutations in both  mut1  and  mut2  to the  FLUORESCENT  ( FLU ) gene again.

We verified that the widely used  flu1-1  is not the long-recognized null mutant, but rather a weak allele, encoding a variant that binds weakly to GluTR1 and leads to partial shutdown of tetrapyrrole biosynthesis in the dark. We further found that the  FLU -knockout mutants produce more  1 O 2 , activating transcriptional changes, enzymatic lipid peroxidation, and programmed cell death (PCD) even in the absence of EX1. Overexpression of SAFE1 suppressed  1 O 2 -induced PCD in  mut2  in a dosage-dependent manner.

Collectively, our findings redefine the nature of the widely used  flu1-1  mutant and reveal that excessive  1 O 2  can overwhelm the inhibitory effect of endogenous SAFE1 and induce stress responses independently of EX1.
 
 概括 
 

单线态氧( 1 O 2 )是叶绿体中产生的主要活性氧(ROS)，在环境胁迫条件下大量产生。对拟南芥突变体 flu ( flu1-1 )的研究表明，叶绿体 1 O 2 可作为信号分子，激活逆行信号转导，导致光抑制或细胞死亡。

通过对EMS诱变的拟南芥 flu1-1/ex1 突变体进行抑制子筛选，我们分离到了两个突变体( mut1 和 mut2 )，它们恢复了 1 O 2 诱导的胁迫响应。结合图位克隆与高通量测序方法，我们将 mut1 和 mut2 中导致抑制子表型的突变位点均定位到 FLU 基因上。

长期以来， flu1-1 一直被认为是一个FLU蛋白缺失的无效突变体。我们的这项研究表明 flu1-1 是一个弱等位突变体，编码一种与GluTR结合较弱的FLU A262V 蛋白，部分抑制黑暗中四吡咯生物合成。FLU功能敲除突变体会产生更多的 1 O 2 ，即使在缺乏EX1的情况下也能激活转录变化、酶促脂质过氧化反应和程序性细胞死亡(PCD)。在 mut2 中，SAFE1的过表达以剂量依赖的方式抑制了 1 O 2 诱导的程序性细胞死亡。

综上所述，本研究结果重新定义了广泛使用的 flu1-1 突变体的分子本质，并揭示过量的 1 O 2 能够突破内源SAFE1的抑制作用，以不依赖EX1的方式诱导胁迫响应。

authors:

abstract:
Genomic dissection of 2,377 soybean accessions identified 261 trait-associated loci with distinct beneficial alleles in Chinese and American germplasms, enabled development of the Soybean Targeted Improvement Navigation System framework for targeted allele introgression, and provided genomic resources for knowledge-driven soybean design breeding.
  
 ABSTRACT 
 Soybean ( Glycine max  [L.] Merr.) was domesticated in China over five millennia ago; yet, its global expansion has resulted in two distinct, independently evolved breeding pools in China and the Americas. While regional breeding has optimized specific traits, a comprehensive roadmap for the reciprocal exchange of these “breeding-specific” beneficial alleles is lacking. Here, we performed a large-scale genomic dissection of 2,377 soybean accessions, integrating 8.4 million high-quality SNPs with multi-environment phenotyping across 11 locations. Through genome-wide association studies (GWAS), we identified 261 significant loci (223 novel) governing six key agronomic traits, revealing that Chinese and American germplasms have accumulated distinct sets of beneficial alleles of seed size/protein in China and oil/yield in the Americas. To harness this untapped potential, we developed the Soybean Targeted Improvement Navigation System (STINS), a framework integrating population genomics, GWAS, and genomic selection (GS). We demonstrate the potential of targeted beneficial allele introgression between populations via gene modification for rapid trait improvement. Proof-of-concept functional evaluation through CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout of  GmST05  in an American cultivar and overexpression of a resistant  GmSNAP18  haplotype in a Chinese cultivar provided experimental support for STINS-predicted targets for protein content and SCN resistance improvement. Our study provides a navigable genomic resource for “knowledge-driven design breeding”, offering a blueprint for the global exchange of elite alleles to ensure future food security.

title:
The BIK1–WRKY9 module activates jasmonate signaling to confer apple resistance to
                     Alternaria

abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Apple
                     Alternaria 
                    blotch, caused by
                     Alternaria alternata 
                    f. sp.
                     mali 
                    (
                     A. alternata 
                    ), is a devastating fungal disease threatening global apple production. However, the early signaling pathway underlying apple resistance to
                     A. alternata 
                    remains unclear. In this study, through transcriptomic analysis, we identified that
                     MdWRKY9 
                    is a key positive regulator of apple resistance to
                     A. alternata 
                    , whose expression is induced in the resistant “Hanfu” while being reduced in the susceptible “Gala” following
                     A. alternata 
                    infection. Stable overexpression of
                     MdWRKY9 
                    enhanced apple resistance to
                     A. alternata 
                    , whereas RNA interference (RNAi)‐mediated knockdown of
                     MdWRKY9 
                    increased susceptibility. We further demonstrated that MdWRKY9 directly represses the expression of
                     MdJAZ8 
                    , a key repressor of jasmonate (JA) signaling. Accordingly, stable overexpression of
                     MdJAZ8 
                    in apple calli reduced resistance to
                     A. alternata 
                    and suppressed JA signaling. Consistently, transient overexpression of
                     MdJAZ8 
                    in apple leaves decreased resistance to
                     A. alternata 
                    , whereas transient silencing of
                     MdJAZ8 
                    via RNAi enhanced disease resistance. Furthermore, we identified that the receptor‐like cytoplasmic kinase MdBIK1 (
                     BOTRYTIS 
                    ‐INDUCED KINASE1, a core component of the PTI pathway) interacts with and phosphorylates MdWRKY9 at Thr‐2. The phosphorylation of MdWRKY9 enhances resistance to
                     A. alternata 
                    by further suppressing
                     MdJAZ8 
                    and activating JA signaling. Together, our findings define a complete PTI‐associated signaling module in which the MdBIK1–MdWRKY9 complex enhances JA‐mediated immunity against
                     A. alternata 
                    by directly repressing
                     MdJAZ8 
                    . This study refines the regulatory mechanism by which the BIK1 family kinases modulate JA signaling, providing new insights into the plant immune signaling network.

title:
A TALE of

abstract: Brassica oleracea  is an important vegetable crop cultivated globally. Selection for different traits in  B. oleracea  has resulted in impressive morphotypic diversity, and these morphotypes account for numerous household vegetables such as broccoli, Brussels sprouts, cabbage, cauliflower, kale, and kohlrabi. However, these vegetables are the hosts of several pathogens that cause yield-limiting disease. Among them, black rot, caused by the bacterial pathogen  Xanthomonas campestris  pv.  campestris  ( Xcc ), is one of the most devastating, resulting in up to 60% yield loss in susceptible cultivars ( Greer et al 2023 ).

title: From stress perception to metabolite disposition: dynamic regulation of stilbene biosynthesis in plants
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Stilbenes are inducible plant specialized metabolites, best exemplified by resveratrol, a phytoalexin that links environmental perception, defense responses, and phenylpropanoid resource allocation. Stilbene accumulation may be controlled at 3 mechanistically distinct levels: signaling cascades that connect environmental and hormonal cues to kinase-dependent activation; combinatorial transcriptional control, which governs the response amplitude and specificity of stilbene synthase (STS) genes; and branch selection together with product disposition, which shapes the final metabolic output. Within this framework, MYB and WRKY proteins serve as major transcriptional nodes as activators or repressors, yet their regulatory effects depend on combinatorial interactions, phosphorylation events, competitive promoter occupancy, and metabolic context. We explicitly distinguish strongly supported mechanisms, defined by genetic perturbation, direct target validation, and metabolite quantification from emerging models built primarily on transient expression assays or co-expression correlations. This distinction avoids equating regulators supported by disparate levels of experimental evidence, identifies the most robust principles governing pathway control, and highlights experiments required to turn descriptive associations into causal mechanistic models. We further highlight conceptual insights extending beyond stilbene metabolism to inducible specialized metabolism in general, and outline research priorities for comparative genetics, cell-resolved analysis, and predictive pathway engineering.

title: The energy sensor SnRK1 promotes starvation-induced autophagosome formation by modulating ATG13a phosphorylation in Arabidopsis
abstract:
Abstract 
                   In eukaryotes, autophagy is an evolutionarily conserved cellular degradation and recycling process that is tightly associated with cellular nutrient status. The energy sensor SNF1-RELATED KINASE 1 (SnRK1) is thought to sense nutrient starvation and induce autophagy, but how it regulates autophagosome formation in plant cells remains largely unknown. Here, we show that the SnRK1 α-catalytic subunit KIN10 regulates autophagosome formation in Arabidopsis (Arabidopsis thaliana) by interacting with and phosphorylating AUTOPHAGY-RELATED PROTEIN 13a (ATG13a), a key component of the ATG1a–ATG13a protein kinase complex involved in autophagy initiation. KIN10 directly phosphorylates ATG13a in vitro and in vivo, inhibiting its ubiquitination and increasing its abundance. Moreover, we identified ten serine residues in ATG13a that are important for KIN10-mediated phosphorylation. Transgenic plants accumulating a nonphosphorylatable ATG13a variant with mutations of these ten residues were less tolerant of starvation than ATG13a-overexpressing plants and displayed accelerated leaf senescence and lower autophagic flux. The KIN10-mediated phosphorylation of ATG13a did not affect ATG1a–ATG13a complex formation; instead, it facilitated ATG1a phosphorylation, thereby promoting autophagosome formation. Therefore, our findings suggest that the KIN10–ATG13a module modulates SnRK1-mediated autophagosome formation, likely representing a key step in integrating energy sensing and autophagy initiation in plant cells.

title: Net Global Enhancement of Surface Chlorophyll by Oceanic Fine-scale Eddies
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Fine-scale oceanic eddies (FEs), with horizontal scale smaller than the Rossby deformation radius, cover the variability at submesoscale and small-mesoscale wavelengths. They serve as critical drivers for vertical transport that helps close the nutrient budget and sustain observed levels of primary production. However, the fine-scale eddies have never been directly observed on a global scale prior to the launch of the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) satellite mission. Consequently, their global contribution to surface chlorophyll variability has remained unknown. By combining SWOT observations with multi-platform datasets, we show that FEs are ubiquitous throughout the global ocean and are roughly an order of magnitude more abundant than large mesoscale eddies observed by traditional altimetry missions. In contrast to mesoscale eddies, fine-scale cyclones are systematically stronger than anticyclones by approximately 10% on average. Globally composited results reveal that the magnitude of positive surface chlorophyll anomalies driven by cyclonic fine-scale eddies exceeds the magnitude of negative chlorophyll anomalies of anticyclones by more than twofold, producing a consistent net positive effect on surface chlorophyll concentrations across the global oceans, which is driven by the combined effect of horizontal and vertical motions of fine-scale eddies. Our results provide the first observational benchmark for characterizing FEs and their biogeochemical influence, offering critical constraints for future coupled physical-biogeochemical models and helping to reduce longstanding uncertainties.

title: MetaEarth3D: Spatially Scalable Generative Modeling for World-scale 3D Scenes
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Recent generative AI models have achieved remarkable breakthroughs in language and visual understanding. However, although these models can generate realistic visual content, their spatial scale remains confined to bounded environments, preventing them from capturing how geographic environments evolve across thousands of kilometers or from modeling the spatial structure of the large-scale physical world. This limitation poses a critical challenge for ultra-wide-area spatial intelligence in Earth observation and simulation, revealing a deeper gap in generative AI: progress has relied primarily on scaling model parameters and training data, while overlooking spatial scale as a core dimension of intelligence. Here, motivated by this missing dimension, we investigate spatial scale as a new scaling axis in foundation models and present MetaEarth3D, the first generative foundation model capable of spatially consistent generation at world scale. Taking optical Earth observation simulation as a testbed, MetaEarth3D enables the generation of multi-level, unbounded, and diverse 3D scenes spanning large-scale terrains, medium-scale cities, and fine-grained street blocks. Built upon 10.2 million globally distributed real-world training images, MetaEarth3D demonstrates both strong visual realism and geospatial statistical realism. Beyond generation, MetaEarth3D serves as a generative data engine for diverse virtual environments in ultra-wide spatial intelligence. We argue that this study may help empower next-generation spatial intelligence for Earth observation.

title: Geomagnetic instability as a potential deep-Earth forcing factor in the Permian environmental and biotic crisis
abstract:
Abstract 
                   The Permian witnessed profound geomagnetic, environmental, and biotic upheavals, yet high-resolution paleomagnetic constraints across critical transitions remain sparse. Here, we present a 3.75-million-year magnetostratigraphic record from the Fengshan section (South China) spanning the Guadalupian-Lopingian transition (262.5-258.75 Ma). It yields extreme geomagnetic instability, characterized by 29 magnetozones and an unprecedented reversal frequency of 11 reversals/Myr – one of the highest records in Earth’s history. These features are temporally correlated with the end-Guadalupian extinction (∼261 Ma), suggesting a potential deep-Earth force contributing to surface ecosystem collapse, though the causation remains unproven. This implies that, together with other global forcing factor, geomagnetic instability might have influenced late Permian climatic and biotic upheavals.

title: Towards Next-Generation Artificial Intelligence Models for Integrated Diagnostics Embedding Eye-Brain Connections
abstract:
Abstract 
                   The brain and eye share profound and homologous relationships in terms of development, anatomy, and microcirculatory structures, yet current analyses typically examine them in isolation, limiting cross-organ insights and the development of integrated artificial intelligence (AI) models. Such a fragmented paradigm also constrains clinical understanding despite growing evidence of shared, anatomically connected, and predictive relationships between ocular and cerebral phenotypes in both brain and eye diseases. In this context, this review introduces an Eye-Brain Connection Pyramid, a multiscale organizational framework for examining eye-brain relationships at three complementary biological levels: genetic and genomic susceptibility, molecular and protein processes, and neurovascular and tissue phenotypes. The pyramid does not represent a serial causal pathway. Across these levels, the framework distinguishes shared vulnerability and parallel pathology, direct brain-to-eye effects, retinal correlates and predictors of cerebral or systemic disease, and putative eye-to-brain causal contributions, which remain insufficiently established in humans. This framework may inform future clinical research and the development of AI models integrating multimodal cross-organ data, whose incremental diagnostic value over existing single-organ and clinical approaches requires prospective validation. Furthermore, this review presents a comprehensive AI research roadmap, spanning longitudinal prognostic models, explainable algorithms for clinical adoption, validation of incremental clinical value, fundus-based brain health screening setups, and multi-site collaboration. By outlining these priorities, the proposed Eye-Brain Connection Pyramid provides an organizational framework for investigating integrated eye-brain diagnostics and for evaluating the potential clinical value of cross-organ AI in risk stratification, longitudinal monitoring, and healthcare delivery.

title: Programming multiconfiguration into bistable robots via traversable energy landscapes
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Soft robots using bistable structures often face limitations due to a fixed energy landscape, which restricts their configurational adaptability and functional diversity. To address this challenge, we introduce an energy-landscape-traversing (ELTra) bistable structure that enables on-demand reconstruction of the energy landscape, continuous stabilization of intermediate states, and precise modulation of energy release, capabilities that are challenging to achieve with conventional systems. Based on the established theoretical model of the ELTra bistable structure, we developed an ELTraBot prototype that features four distinct configurations, including two intermediate-stable configurations absent in traditional bistable structures. We further demonstrated the ELTraBot’s remarkable versatility, allowing it to perform nine distinct functions by leveraging its reconfigurable states. This design reduces the need for complex dedicated hardware and significantly simplifies design. Our work establishes a new design method for multifunctional, reconfigurable robots by advancing beyond binary bistability into the realm of continuously programmable materials.

title: On-chip wavelength-programmed deep-ultraviolet laser array
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Monolithic laser arrays represent a foundational technology for chip-scale photonics, offering precise control and multiplexing of light to advance fields such as integrated optics and quantum information processing. While such arrays have been successfully realized in the visible and infrared regimes over the past decades, developing on-chip deep ultraviolet (DUV) laser arrays has remained a significant challenge. Here, we overcome this barrier by demonstrating a DUV laser array with deterministic, emitter-by-emitter wavelength programmability, achieved through a ridge-width-engineering approach. By tailoring the lateral dimensions of ridge waveguides, we deliberately modulate optical field confinement, which in turn adjusts the effective modal refractive index and shifts the cavity resonance wavelength for each individual laser emitter. Combined with smooth, vertical cavity facets, this strategy enables room-temperature optically-pumped DUV lasing across a programmable range from 252 to 259 nm on a single integrated chip. This work demonstrates an optically-pumped wavelength-programmed DUV laser array on a single chip, providing a useful proof-of-concept toward future integrated DUV photonic systems and compact multi-wavelength ultraviolet light sources.

title: Efficient broad-temperature Ettingshausen cooling unlocked in Bismuth
abstract:
Abstract 
                   The discovery of the first thermoelectric effect in bismuth (Bi) by Thomas Seebeck in 1821 ushered in an era of research that, for over a century, has been dominated by narrow-gap semiconductors, typified by Bi2Te3 and Bi1-xSbx for room temperature and low temperatures, respectively. Unlike Peltier coolers, which rely on pairs of n- and p-type semiconductors for longitudinal current and heat flows, Ettingshausen ones leverage both electrons and holes in a single material to enable heat flow transverse to the current. However, high transverse thermoelectric performance has long been confined to narrow temperature windows of only tens of kelvin. Here, we propose a strategy that tailors the intrinsic band transport landscape to optimize semimetal transverse thermoelectrics over broad temperature ranges. Guided by this strategy, historical Bi is revealed as a broadly optimized transverse thermoelectric material, showing an average power factor exceeding 350 μW cm−1 K−2 and an average figure of merit of 1.25 over 200–300 K, outperforming typical longitudinal semiconductors. The resultant Ettingshausen cooler achieves a temperature drop of up to 84 K from 300 K and a specific cooling power density five times that of Peltier coolers under 8 T. This work might enlighten Ettingshausen cooling an alternative and competitive route for advancing thermoelectricity.

title: PanRes: a database of latent and acquired antimicrobial resistance allowing 3D-based protein homology search
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Motivation 
                     Antimicrobial resistance databases are central to genomic surveillance, but resistance determinants remain distributed across resources with different scopes, structures, and annotations. 
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     We developed PanRes, a curated resistance database of 11 717 genes integrating acquired and latent determinants of antibiotic, biocide, and metal resistance within a unified ontology. We predicted representative protein structures and clustered them by structural similarity, grouping proteins into 505 high-confidence structurally conserved clusters coherent despite sequence divergence. Their structure-guided alignments were used to build Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) for remote homology search. In seven wastewater metagenomes from five European cities, PanRes 3D-based HMMs expanded detection beyond what was possible with BLAST, with 35.3% of retained hits identified only by the HMMs and generally showing greater divergence from known proteins. For beta-lactamases, several proteins retained beta-lactamase-like folds and catalytic geometry despite weak sequence similarity. 
                   
                   
                     Availability and implementation 
                     PanRes is available through an interactive web platform (https://panres.rambio.dk/), a structure-informed resource for exploring the whole resistome. The database, HMM profiles, and ontology are available at Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.22876216).

title:
ScopeNovo: a
                     de novo 
                    peptide sequencing method using spectrum–spectrum similarity to refine the prediction accuracy
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Motivation 
                     De novo peptide sequencing from tandem mass spectra is essential for characterizing unknown proteins, identifying novel post-translational modifications, and analysing samples without reference databases. While recent deep learning models have improved the predicted peptide accuracy, they typically select the predicted peptide sequence based solely on sequence-level decoding scores. Very often, high scores are assigned to peptides without the direct support from the observed mass spectrum. 
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     We present “ScopeNovo”, a de novo peptide sequencing method that improves predicted peptide accuracy by using spectrum-spectrum similarity between the input spectrum and the “representative” spectrum corresponding to the predicted peptide sequence. ScopeNovo generates multiple candidate peptides using an existing peptide de novo sequencing learning model and reranks candidates based on spectrum–spectrum similarity. To test our method, we use π-PrimeNovo as the base learning model. Experimental results on the standard nine-species benchmark datasets V1 and V2 show that ScopeNovo can substantially improve the prediction accuracy. We designed two settings, where Setting 1 is for well-annotated species, and Setting 2 is for species that are not well annotated. For Setting 1, ScopeNovo improves the average peptide accuracies of π-PrimeNovo over the nine species by 6.1% and 4.0% on V1 and V2, respectively. For Setting 2, ScopeNovo can still improve the peptide accuracy of π-PrimeNovo over the nine species by 3.4% and 1.9% on the V1 and V2 benchmark datasets, respectively. Compared to the best-known method, RankNovo, the peptide accuracies over the nine species on V1 and V2 of our method for Setting 1 are 0.711 and 0.737, where the peptide accuracies for RankNovo are 0.687 and 0.682. Even for Setting 2, the peptide accuracies of our method are comparable to those of RankNovo. 
                   
                   
                     Availability and implementation 
                     ScopeNovo is implemented in Python under an MIT license. The source code is freely available at https://github.com/SoSongzhi/ScopeNovo.git. The test data are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23181841.

title: Ryder: epigenome normalization using a two-tier model and internal reference regions
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Motivation 
                     Sequencing-based epigenomic profiling methods are powerful but suffer from technical variability that complicates cross-sample comparisons and can obscure true biological signals. While existing normalization methods using spike-in controls or computational approaches have been proposed, they often rely on assumptions that may not hold across diverse experimental conditions or require additional data types. 
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     We present Ryder, a flexible and robust Python package for the normalization of epigenomic signal tracks. Ryder leverages stable internal reference regions, such as invariant CTCF binding sites, to correct for technical artifacts genome-wide. Our results show that it effectively adjusts both background noise and signal intensity, ensuring accurate signal alignment across samples while preserving genuine biological differences. We demonstrate that Ryder performs robustly across diverse assays including DNase-seq, CUT&RUN, ATAC-seq, MNase-seq, and ChIP-seq, with or without spike-in controls. By reducing technical noise, Ryder improves the detection of genuine biological changes, such as quantitative reduction of chromatin accessibility at key enhancer elements by depletion of BRG1, a key subunit of the chromatin remodeling BAF complexes. 
                   
                   
                     Availability and implementation 
                     The Ryder source code, documentation and test data are freely available at: https://github.com/YaqiangCao/ryder. The software version used in this study is archived at Zenodo: https://zenodo.org/records/21267457.

title: Retraction for Bonetti et al., Decoding the elite soccer player’s psychological profile
Structure-based targeting of Atg8 uncovers its essential role in autophagy-mediated detoxification
abstract:
Autophagy degrades and recycles intracellular material, allowing cells to maintain homeostasis and adapt to environmental stress. In the rice blast fungus
                     Magnaporthe oryzae 
                    , the core autophagy protein MoAtg8 is required for autophagosome formation and host infection. Here, we determined the crystal structure of MoAtg8 and used it for structure-guided virtual screening of a focused compound library enriched for natural products and autophagy-related molecules. This screen identified nordihydroguaiaretic acid (NDGA), a naturally occurring lignan, as a MoAtg8-binding compound. NDGA suppressed conidial germination and appressorium formation, disrupted membrane integrity, and reduced pathogenicity in
                     M. oryzae 
                    , with no detectable phytotoxicity to rice under the conditions tested. Mechanistically, the 5-lipoxygenase Mo5Lox, a target of NDGA, bound NDGA with lower affinity than MoAtg8. MoAtg8 associated with NDGA through Gln81 and promoted its autophagy-dependent delivery to vacuoles, thereby reducing compound availability to toxicity-associated targets. Disruption of autophagy or mutation of Gln81 in MoAtg8 increased fungal sensitivity to NDGA. These findings identify an autophagy-mediated detoxification route for an exogenous antifungal compound and reveal how MoAtg8-dependent trafficking modulates NDGA efficacy in a plant-pathogenic fungus.

title:
The impact of modulator therapy on the
                     Pseudomonas aeruginosa 
                    cystic fibrosis lung transcriptome
abstract:
Chronic lung infection with
                     Pseudomonas aeruginosa 
                    is a major complication of cystic fibrosis (CF), contributing to lung function decline and increased morbidity and mortality. Laboratory models are used to study CF infections, but their relevance depends on how accurately they reproduce microbial physiology during human infection. We previously developed a framework that uses bacterial gene expression in human infections to quantify model accuracy. Here, we applied this framework to determine how a major therapeutic intervention impacts
                     P. aeruginosa 
                    physiology in the lungs of people with CF (pwCF) and to develop and evaluate refined preclinical models. We focused on elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ETI), a highly effective CFTR modulator therapy that has improved outcomes for pwCF. However, evidence indicates that
                     P. aeruginosa 
                    lung infections persist despite ETI therapy. Analysis of
                     P. aeruginosa 
                    transcriptomes from human sputum collected before and after ETI initiation revealed minimal changes in gene expression, indicating that the CF airway continues to support a similar bacterial transcriptional state despite therapy. We then evaluated how strain selection, zinc limitation, and polymicrobial coculture influence the ability of laboratory models to recapitulate
                     P. aeruginosa 
                    gene expression in human CF sputum. Growth of CF clinical isolates in zinc-limited synthetic CF sputum medium produced the most accurate model, whereas population-based cultures and coculture with
                     Staphylococcus aureus 
                    had limited effects. These findings show that ETI therapy has little impact on the conserved
                     P. aeruginosa 
                    transcriptional state in human CF sputum and that refined sputum-like models remain useful for studying persistent infection in the postmodulator era.

title:
Superconductivity in the high-pressure tetragonal phase of UTe
                     2
abstract:
Electrical transport and magnetic measurements have been made on UTe
                     2 
                    under pressure
                     P 
                    up to ~16 GPa to determine the superconducting transition temperature
                     T 
                     c

                    phase diagram in the high-pressure tetragonal phase. Superconductivity emerges near ~5 GPa, coincident with the orthorhombic—tetragonal phase transition; in the tetragonal phase,
                     T 
                     c

                     2

                     H 
                     c2 
                    (0) ≈ 1.2 T at 5.3 GPa, smaller than the Pauli paramagnetic limit, and is orbitally limited with a coherence length ξ

                    ≈ 16.5 nm. This small value of
                     H 
                     c2 
                    (0) favors more conventional superconductivity; in contrast, the large values of
                     H 
                     c2 
                    (
                     T 
                    ) for orthorhombic UTe

This dichotomy is consistent with the proposal that U-dimers, present (absent) in the orthorhombic (tetragonal) phase, may play a role in spin-triplet superconductivity of orthorhombic UTe
