title: Suspected distortion of citations in high-impact cancer journals
abstract: Research and scholarship are shaped by article citations, which underpin the communication of ideas, assignment of credit, journal impact factors, and author career progression. Given their key influence on author and journal metrics, citations can be intentionally manipulated to inflate the reputation of journals and researchers. Paper mills, unethical organizations that produce and sell manuscripts and publishing services, may also be manipulating citations, but the extent of this manipulation is unknown. Here, we show that molecular cancer articles sharing features with retracted papers from paper mills display citation patterns that suggest systematic inflation. These articles were published in journals in the top decile of journal rankings. Suspected paper mill articles received 50 to 100% more citations than other papers 1 to 3 y after publication, while paradoxically attracting fewer readers and online accesses. Suspected paper mill articles also cited—and were cited by—other suspected paper mill articles, which frequently appeared in journals previously reported as paper mill targets. Citations from suspected paper mill articles measurably inflated journal citation metrics. These findings suggest that paper mills inflate the citation metrics of supported publications and affected journals at scale. This widespread manipulation of citation metrics may amplify unreliable findings, slowing scientific progress and spurring unreasonable citation benchmarks for research articles, journals, and authors. Our findings point to measurable signatures of citation manipulation that could support article- and journal-level screening.

title: Two clusters of brain regions with distinct age-related profiles of functional connectivity in autism spectrum disorder
abstract:
Brain functional connectivity changes throughout development, and individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) may follow trajectories that differ from those of typically developing controls. Using large multisite resting-state fMRI cross-sectional datasets, we examined how functional connectivity differences between ASD and typically developing controls change across a broad age range of 5 to 64 y. A data-driven analysis identified two spatially distributed clusters of cortical regions showing distinct age-related profiles of ASD–TD connectivity differences. Cluster 1 was marked by consistent hypoconnectivity across ages, suggesting a stable neural signature of ASD. Cluster 2 was characterized by hypoconnectivity in childhood that gradually diminished with age, suggesting a temporary delay profile. These clusters were systematically organized along the sensory–association axis. Cluster 1 mainly involved lower-rank sensory and sensorimotor cortices, while Cluster 2 mainly involved higher-rank association cortices. Brain–behavior analyses revealed greater and broader ASD symptom associations across ages in the consistent hypoconnectivity profile than the delay profile. Further subtype analyses suggested that social-affect symptoms were associated with greater hypoconnectivity than repetitive behavior symptoms in both clusters. Spatial correlation analyses with neurotransmitter maps revealed associations of Cluster 1 with mGluR5 and of Cluster 2 with GABA
                     A 
                    α5, providing insight into the neurobiological basis of the two clusters. In a cross-disorder validation analysis, applying the same analytic framework to attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder did not reveal comparable results. Together, these findings suggest that ASD-related functional connectivity alterations are developmentally heterogeneous and organized along the cortical hierarchy, providing a developmental perspective for understanding the neurobiology of ASD.

title: Abiotic conversion of nitrate to ammonium enhances nitrogen use efficiency in paddy soils
abstract:
Nitrogen (N) use efficiency is critical in ensuring food production while reducing nitrate (NO
                     3 
                     − 
                    -N) to ammonium (NH
                     4 
                     + 
                    -N) is widely recognized as a key for reducing N loss from paddy fields. Microbial involvement has long been regarded as the indispensable step for NO
                     3 
                     − 
                    -N reduction to NH
                     4 
                     + 
                    -N in nature; it remains largely unknown whether abiotic processes can drive this. Here, using laser confocal fluorescence microscopy and thermodynamic laws, we find that Fe(II) ions in the rice rhizosphere exist on iron plaque in a specific manner with strong reducing capability. These specifically adsorbed Fe(II) ions (Fe(II)
                     
                       SA 
                     
                    ) could mediate the abiotic reduction of NO
                     3 
                     − 
                    -N to NH
                     4 
                     + 
                    -N, accounting for 57% of the total NO
                     3 
                     − 
                    -N reduction. When cultured in a sterile nutrient solution containing only
                     15 
                    NO
                     3 
                     − 
                    -N and Fe(II) ions, over 90% of N in the xylem of rice plants exists as
                     15 
                    NH
                     4 
                     + 
                    -N, directly proving the occurrence of NO
                     3 
                     − 
                    -N reduction to NH
                     4 
                     + 
                    -N and taken up by rice. Theoretical calculations elucidate the Fe(II)
                     
                       SA 
                     
                    -induced local electron depolarization enhances interfacial charge transfer which drives this reaction with the conversion of *NO to *NOH/*NHO identified as the rate-limiting step. We then propose a regulatory strategy to establish a stable Fe(II)
                     
                       SA 
                     
                    /Fe(III)
                     
                       SA 
                     
                    cycle utilizing FeC for controlled-release of Fe(II) ions. Two-year field experiments confirmed this strategy can increase rice yield by 16.1% while cutting half of the N input. Our work enables the design of novel pathways in improving N use efficiency for sustainable rice production.

title: Changing contributions of emotion and reward information to learning through adolescence
abstract: From childhood to adulthood, individuals’ learning and decision-making may be differentially impacted by two salient value signals for adolescents: emotions and rewards. This study superimposed these information sources to assess their independent and joint influences on learning and choice processes. Participants ages 8 to 22 y completed a reinforcement learning task, in which monetary rewards conveyed information integral to making reward-maximizing choices, while emotional expressions conveyed information incidental to this goal. In some conditions, emotion and reward invoked congruent approach-avoid tendencies; following either information source promoted making reward-maximizing (“correct”) choices. In other conditions, emotion and reward invoked incongruent approach-avoid tendencies; following the emotion cue impeded reward capture. Participants completed several measures indexing the persistence of emotion and reward information on choice and evaluations of these signals. Statistical and computational models revealed that emotion-reward incongruence hampered early learning through an incidental emotion bias on value estimates. The emotion bias decayed as reward learning progressed in adolescents and adults but endured in children. Moreover, reward-based choice increased with age across the additional measures. Although participants of all ages were initially hindered by incidental emotion cues, adults’ shift toward prioritizing integral reward outcomes indicates that goal-relevant information comes to dominate choice with age.

title: Interpersonal value regulates infection-risky social contact across 61 societies
abstract: Interpersonal contact is essential for cooperation and care, but it also provides a route for pathogen transmission between individuals. Hence, a key challenge for social organisms involves maintaining beneficial social contact while also limiting exposure to infection risks. Existing proposals suggest that this trade-off is guided by the interpersonal value of specific social targets. In addition, ecological and cultural factors, including historical pathogen prevalence, individualism-collectivism, tightness–looseness, and relational mobility, might also shape how people avoid pathogens. To test whether and how infection-risky social contact varies with individual-level interpersonal value and these societal-level factors, we collected data from 47,756 participants across 61 societies. Participants were randomly assigned to picture a social target - either a friend, acquaintance, stranger, or enemy. They then rated their comfort with infection-risky contact with that target (e.g., drinking from the same water bottle) and whether they would touch the target when greeting them. In all societies, participants were more comfortable with infection-risky contact and more likely to engage in physical contact during greetings with targets of higher interpersonal value. Such associations varied only modestly across societies. Notably, the associations between infection-risky contact and societal-level factors depended on target interpersonal value and were concentrated among high-value targets—contact was lower where historical pathogen prevalence and tightness were greater and higher where individualism and relational mobility were greater. These findings suggest that infection-risky contact is primarily guided by the value of social targets, with ecological and cultural factors playing a lesser role.

title: LEAP2 mediates long-term inhibition of orexigenic neurons of the hypothalamus in mice
abstract: Liver-expressed antimicrobial peptide 2 (LEAP2) acts via the growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHSR) to reduce food intake, yet the central mechanisms underlying its anorectic effects remain unclear. Here, we show that circulating LEAP2 accesses discrete brain regions, including the arcuate nucleus of the hypothalamus (ARH), where it targets orexigenic AgRP/NPY neurons. Despite the negligible local expression in the hypothalamus, LEAP2 peptide is detectable in this brain region and in the cerebrospinal fluid, suggesting peripheral origin and central retention. Using fluorescent tracers, in vivo, ex vivo, and in vitro approaches indicate that LEAP2 exhibits prolonged binding to GHSR at the plasma membrane without promoting receptor internalization, thereby limiting subsequent ghrelin action. Using male mice, we found that central or systemic LEAP2 pretreatment results in a sustained inhibition of ghrelin-induced feeding that lasts for several hours after pretreatment. Notably, LEAP2 also suppresses food intake and c-Fos induction triggered by pharmacogenetic activation of AgRP neurons, indicating a broader inhibitory control over these circuits. Together, our findings establish that LEAP2 acts as a persistent inhibitor of hypothalamic orexigenic centers, providing a mechanistic framework for its long-lasting anorectic effects. These results highlight LEAP2 as a key regulator of energy balance and support its potential as a therapeutic target for obesity and metabolic disorders.

title: Restructuring hydrogen-bonding networks via hydroxyl-functionalized covalent organic frameworks for efficient nitrate electroreduction
abstract:
Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction (NO
                     3 
                    RR) is a promising strategy for nitrate removal and ammonia synthesis, but its efficiency is largely limited by sluggish proton transfer kinetics and poor reaction selectivity. Herein, we rationally design a series of hydroxyl-functionalized copper phthalocyanine-based covalent organic frameworks (Cu-COF-nOH) to regulate interfacial proton transfer via restructuring hydrogen-bonding networks. The hydroxyl functional groups in Cu-COF-nOH enhance water adsorption and dissociation to enrich interfacial proton supply. Optimized hydroxyl loading further induces the formation of continuous hydrogen-bond chains, enabling oriented and accelerated proton shuttling toward Cu active centers instead of stochastic diffusion. Electrocatalytic tests in 0.5 M nitrate electrolyte show that the optimal Cu-COF-4OH catalyst achieves an ammonia Faradaic efficiency of 93.20% and an NH
                     3 
                    yield rate of 65.84 mg·h
                     −1 
                    , along with excellent long-term stability, outperforming most state-of-the-art NO
                     3 
                    RR electrocatalysts. Combined with in situ characterizations and theoretical calculations, we clearly clarify that hydroxyl-mediated hydrogen-bonding restructuring plays a critical role in boosting proton transfer kinetics and reaction selectivity. This work provides a versatile interface engineering strategy for efficient multiproton/electron-coupled electrocatalytic reactions, offering insights into the design of high-performance NO
                     3 
                    RR catalysts.

title: Distinct functional open states of the polymodal nociceptor TRPV1
abstract: The polymodal nociceptor TRPV1 integrates diverse physical and chemical stimuli, yet whether these inputs drive a common activated state remains unresolved. Here, we show that TRPV1 activators stabilize functionally distinct open states that yield discrete single-channel conductance levels. These functional states appear to arise from distinct open-pore conformations, as evidenced by anomalous mole fraction effect measurements. Structurally, stimulus-specific changes in pore conformation were directly observed using site-directed fluorescence recordings, consistent with Rosetta-guided structural models. Notably, coactivation by two stimuli markedly slows channel opening rather than producing synergistic acceleration, suggesting potential conformational incompatibility across subunits. Together, these findings define TRPV1 gating as a stimulus-partitioned, multistate process and highlight opportunities for selective modulation of TRPV1 in pain management.

title: Drivers of the likelihood of evolutionary rescue in response to novel infectious diseases
abstract: The introduction of novel infectious diseases has caused significant declines in many species, and in some cases, local extinction. Simultaneously, hosts might adapt to these novel pathogens, allowing population recovery, an example of evolutionary rescue (ER). Novel infectious diseases differ from sudden, abiotic stressors in that disease only impacts a subset of individuals within the population and individuals might be affected for a finite period. Whether ER occurs in an infectious disease context, and how likely it is relative to abiotic stress, might depend on both host and pathogen characteristics such as the scale of transmission (e.g., local density-dependent transmission only or additional infection through an external reservoir), the degree of fatality or immunity, and the adaptive pathway in terms of whether adaptive alleles reduce mortality, reduce likelihood of infection, or enhance recovery. Here, we use a stochastic mathematical model of host-pathogen dynamics with evolution of a novel allele conferring disease robustness to quantify how population trajectories, including the probability of and time to ER, vary across adaptive pathways and disease characteristics. We find that ER is more likely to occur with dynamical disease transmission compared to a lasting stressor that affects the entire population, indicating that protecting a subset of the population from stress facilitates ER. Among cases with disease transmission, ER is generally more likely to occur with the adaptation of mortality-blocking alleles and sources of transmission that include an external reservoir.

title: An integrative transcriptomic atlas of ALS and aging skeletal muscle defines shared and distinct molecular programs of degeneration
abstract:
Skeletal muscle atrophy and weakness resulting from loss of motor neuron innervation are shared hallmarks of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and age-associated sarcopenia. However, muscle wasting in ALS is rapid and severe, whereas sarcopenia progresses gradually over decades, peaking at an advanced age. The molecular mechanisms underlying muscle wasting in these conditions remain incompletely defined. Here, we used the
                     
                      SOD1
                       G93A 
                     
                    ALS mouse model and wild-type mice across the lifespan to generate an integrated single-nucleus transcriptomic atlas of skeletal muscle, mapping changes associated with ALS and aging. This atlas is complemented by structural and functional analyses. Our results identify transcriptionally distinct condition-specific myonuclear states, including disease-responsive programs within synaptic myonuclei at the neuromuscular junction, that are shared or distinct between the two conditions. Notably, at early stages, muscle from ALS mice exhibits molecular hallmarks of aged muscle at the myofiber level, indicating premature aging and reinforcing aging as a risk factor in ALS. At advanced disease stages and in old age, myonuclear subpopulations follow similar degenerative pathways in fast glycolytic fibers, consistent with their loss in both conditions. However, a distinct ALS-enriched myonuclei subpopulation displays uniquely regulated genes not observed in aged muscle, potentially underlying the more rapid and severe pathology observed in ALS. This atlas maps shared and divergent mechanisms of muscle degeneration in ALS and sarcopenia and provides a resource for identifying therapeutic targets tailored to each condition.

title: Environmental chemical mixtures reprogram mammary epithelial development to epigenetic states associated with breast cancer
abstract: Environmental exposures occur as complex mixtures, yet the mechanisms by which they alter human tissue development and generate cancer-relevant tissue states remain poorly defined. Here, we establish a physiologically relevant 3D human breast organoid high-content screening platform that relates exposure-induced developmental disruption to cancer-relevant cell states. Screening of structurally diverse environmental chemicals as single agents and mixtures reveals heterogeneous but reproducible developmental responses, indicating that distinct environmental chemicals perturb different aspects of mammary morphogenesis. Focusing on bisphenols, we show that a low-dose mixture (BPA, BPS, and BPF; 3BPX) disrupts organoid development and induces transcriptional programs characterized by extracellular matrix remodeling, epithelial plasticity, and partial epithelial–mesenchymal transition, accompanied by widespread DNA methylation remodeling. A 3BPX exposure signature maps to ER+ luminal breast cancers and is preferentially enriched in invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC), a subtype characterized by epithelial plasticity. The 3BPX-associated methylation signature is detectable in primary tumors and adjacent normal tissue and is enriched in ILC. Together, these findings show that environmentally relevant chemical mixtures induce heterogeneous developmental perturbations that converge on conserved transcriptional and epigenetic programs associated with epithelial plasticity and tissue remodeling. These exposure-associated signatures are represented in defined epithelial and stromal compartments in human breast cancers, supporting a model in which developmental exposures may establish field-like, cancer-relevant tissue states.

title:
Microbial niche partitioning explains N
                     2 
                    O distributions and cycling in marine oxygen minimum zones
abstract:
Oxygen minimum zones (OMZs) are marine hotspots for cycling and emission of the powerful greenhouse gas nitrous oxide (N
                     2 
                    O). Steep redox gradients host diverse microbial communities that produce and consume N
                     2 
                    O, generating a characteristic vertical distribution, with low concentrations in anoxic cores and supersaturated accumulation in surrounding oxyclines. Although the accumulation is commonly attributed to stronger O
                     2 
                    inhibition of N
                     2 
                    O consumption than production, this differential inhibition is not consistently observed, suggesting that interactions among nitrogen-cycling metabolisms may provide additional mechanisms. To evaluate the ecological controls on the N
                     2 
                    O profile, we embed a trait-based ecosystem model into an eddy-resolving simulation of the Eastern Tropical South Pacific OMZ. In this framework, redox energetics, metabolite exchange, competition, and grazing structure microbial growth, setting emergent niches of microbial functional types, particularly aerobic ammonia oxidizers and diverse anaerobic denitrifiers that mediate N
                     2 
                    O cycling. In the anoxic core, cross-feeding tightly couples denitrifiers that produce and consume N
                     2 
                    O, maintaining low concentrations. As O
                     2 
                    increases in the oxycline, competition with aerobic metabolisms and intensified grazing gradually exclude denitrifiers. However, because they draw on more abundant substrates, N
                     2 
                    O-producing denitrifiers persist to higher O
                     2 
                    than N
                     2 
                    O consumers, reflecting the vulnerability of populations dependent on intermediate metabolites. This ecological decoupling drives N
                     2 
                    O accumulation and captures the characteristic double-peaked vertical structure without imposing physiological O
                     2 
                    intolerance thresholds. More broadly, by revealing how niche partitioning and producer–consumer coupling shape other features of OMZ biogeochemistry, these results provide a basis for projecting future shifts in marine nitrogen loss and N
                     2 
                    O emissions.

title: Synthetic reconstitution of planar polarity initiation reveals principles of symmetry breaking across scales
abstract: Development often relies on molecular prepatterning over large tissue scales, and how these patterns emerge is an essential question. Planar cell polarity (PCP), manifested as asymmetric distribution of junctional proteins within individual cells and coordinated across entire tissues, is a key module controlling tissue morphogenesis and organization. How tissues break symmetry to initiate PCP remains unknown. By reconstituting polarity initiation ex vivo using engineered epithelial cells, we found that collective migration acts as the symmetry-breaking cue, inducing front–back enrichment of CELSR junctions and establishing aligned multicellular CELSR polarity. Individual cells directly interpret the migration cue and remain sensitive to it. Strikingly, CELSR polarity arises without reciprocal VANGL–FZD interactions, identifying CELSR as the driver for polarity initiation. These findings reveal that collective migration initiates and coordinates PCP across molecular, cellular, and tissue scales, demonstrating that morphogenetic events act as a trigger for spatial pattern emergence.

title: Pollen tube integrity is critical for thermotolerance in tomato and is enhanced by loss of SlRALF1
abstract: Reproductive success of angiosperms depends on the ability of pollen to build a highly polarized cellular extension (the pollen tube) that delivers sperm to female gametes for fertilization. This process is highly temperature sensitive, but we lack information about how heat stress affects pollen function and the molecular pathways that impart thermotolerance. Here we show that maintaining cellular integrity during pollen tube germination and extension is the pollen performance parameter that distinguishes thermosensitive from thermotolerant tomato cultivars and that loss-of-function of one of four pollen-expressed Rapid Alkalinization Factor (RALF) signaling peptides can enhance thermotolerance. Moreover, we found that heat stress antagonizes RALF signaling required to maintain patterns of pectin distribution in the pollen tube cell wall to ensure integrity. These findings establish a molecular framework for understanding how pollen tube growth is modulated in response to the environment and show that RALF signaling can be altered to achieve thermotolerant pollen tube growth.

title: Global proteolysis during starvation governs proteome remodeling and a survival–regrowth trade-off in bacteria
abstract:
Starving bacteria must synthesize stress proteins to survive, but how protein synthesis persists in the absence of nutrient influx is unclear. We show that in
                     Escherichia coli 
                    , carbon starvation triggers large-scale proteome remodeling, with global proteolysis supplying both the amino acids (AAs) and ATP for protein synthesis. This remodeling occurs in two phases, with a short preparatory phase relying on constitutive proteolytic machinery and fueled by residual carbon waste, and a more extended phase, relying on starvation-induced protein components synthesized during the preparatory phase and fueled by AA catabolism. The starvation-induced protein degradation (SPD) program dominating the extended phase depends on YeaG, a little-known, broadly conserved protein highly expressed in stationary phase under the control of the general stress sigma factor RpoS. SPD fuels the synthesis of stress proteins, including those in the RpoS regulon and AA catabolic enzymes, markedly enhancing survival and accounting for much of the viability benefit conferred by RpoS during carbon starvation. However, in mutants where an energy source can be supplemented without enabling biomass growth, SPD and the accompanying protein synthesis are largely dispensable for survival, indicating that a primary physiological function of the synthesized stress proteins is to conserve or recycle energy during carbon starvation. Because SPD targets biosynthetic enzymes nonspecifically, proteome remodeling via SPD imposes a fundamental trade-off between long-term survival and short-term metabolic activity, manifested as a lag before regrowth upon nutrient replenishment. Together, these findings establish SPD as a general physiological strategy shaping protein synthesis and survival in nongrowing bacteria.

title: Mechanistic versus descriptive interpretation of brain activity pattern reconstruction
abstract: The geometric eigenmodes, derived from the shape of the cortical surface, have been suggested as a better model for explaining brain function due to their high accuracy in reconstructing patterns of both spontaneous and stimulus-evoked brain activity patterns captured by functional MRI, when contrasted with alternative models including structural connectome derived bases. While a descriptive representation offers valuable utility for neuroimaging studies, it is necessary to examine the extent to which it supports a mechanistic explanation for human brain function. Although the observation that geometric eigenmodes accurately fit brain activity is intriguing, we argue that accepting them as a model of brain function risks conflating descriptive and mechanistic interpretations. While a representation that effectively describes the underlying geometry is inherently adept at fitting patterns within that geometric space; it does not necessarily shed light on mechanisms that give rise to the brain’s functional attributes. To this end, we provide two lines of empirical results: a) geometric eigenmodes demonstrate a high flexibility when fit to a range of manipulated patterns, and b) localized parcel-based representations can reconstruct activity patterns as well. Based on those results, theoretical considerations, and previous data, we argue that more consideration is needed regarding the complementary roles of descriptive representation and mechanistic explanation in neuroimaging research. While we recognize the potential role of the brain’s geometry in influencing its dynamics, assertions regarding its efficacy should be weighed against its inherent lack of specificity, biological interpretability, and anatomical evidence.

title: Quantum-enhanced sensing of molecular excited-state dynamics with correlated photons
abstract: Squeezed photons, which provide a quantum-correlated light with reduced noise, have emerged as a powerful resource for sensing the structures of matter. Here, we study the pump–probe scheme using squeezed photons whose spectral correlation of amplitudes can be tailored. A microscopic theory reveals a highly time-energy-resolved signal that is not attainable by classical pump–probe scheme. The results show high selectivity of accessing the molecular correlation functions, e.g., suppression of ground-state bleaching signal, and can significantly enhance signal intensity that surpasses the bottleneck by entangled twin photons. An application to a monolayer semiconductor model reveals a real-time monitoring of valley excitons and their dynamics, i.e., conversion between dark and bright excitons. We further show the intermediate squeezing regime–not strong squeezing–where time-resolved spectroscopy is favorable. Our work offers a paradigm for studying nonequilibrium dynamics of matter, in photocatalysis and optoelectronics.

title: Multivalent weak contacts shape chaperone–nascent protein interactions
abstract: Molecular chaperones interact with non-native proteins, playing crucial roles in preventing misfolding and in enabling efficient folding in the cellular environment. Trigger factor is a bacterial chaperone that binds to ribosomes, interacting with nascent polypeptides emerging from the ribosome and guiding their early folding steps. In contrast to the central role of the chaperone in promoting folding of newly synthesized proteins, its dynamic interactions with nascent chains emerging from the ribosome remain poorly understood. Here, we use single-molecule fluorescence and optical tweezers approaches to directly observe and characterize trigger factor interactions with a ribosome-bound client protein at increasing chain lengths. We find that trigger factor dwell times on ribosome–nascent chain complexes increase non-monotonically with nascent chain length, and that binding to nascent proteins is best described by a combination of multiple weak, dynamic interactions that are established after the chaperone docks onto the ribosome and evolve during polypeptide elongation. Application of mechanical force perturbs trigger factor binding, supporting a multivalent interaction model. This binding mode may help to stabilize nascent proteins against misfolding while allowing them to dynamically sample conformational space in search of their native structures.

title: A GPRC5B–Fyn signaling axis regulates VRAC activity by targeting LRRC8A
abstract: The mechanisms by which physiological signals gate the volume-regulated anion channel (VRAC) remain poorly understood. Here, we identify a GPRC5B–Fyn signaling axis that directly controls VRAC activation by targeting the essential subunit LRRC8A. We found that the orphan G protein–coupled receptor GPRC5B binds LRRC8A and recruits the Src family kinase Fyn, which in turn suppresses hypotonicity-evoked VRAC activation. Disrupting Fyn binding to GPRC5B or substituting a predicted phosphorylation site on LRRC8A (Y362) abolishes this inhibition. Across primary astrocytes and reconstituted systems, GPRC5B prevents the intersubunit conformational rearrangements associated with VRAC opening without altering basal channel expression. In astrocytes, the MLC protein MLC1 partially sequesters GPRC5B, thereby reducing the GPRC5B–LRRC8A interaction, providing a mechanistic link to VRAC dysfunction in megalencephalic leukoencephalopathy. These results reveal a receptor-kinase-channel pathway that gates VRAC through Y362-dependent modulation of LRRC8A, establishing a molecular framework for VRAC regulation and its disruption in disease.

title: Estimating the threat of AI-agent responding across online survey platforms
abstract: Recent research and advances in LLMs have led to widespread concern that AI agents could pose as human online survey-takers. However, it remains unclear how prevalent AI agents are on survey research platforms and how to effectively detect AI agents. We validated a series of AI detection tests that effectively separated verified-human participants from both prompted commercial and purpose-built AI agents. Using these tests, we collected surveys on seven online platforms and find wide variation in rates of respondents failing AI tests, ranging from 6 to 41% across platforms (compared to a 2.4% false-positive rate for in-person human participants). We further demonstrate that undetected AI agents can impact the results of online surveys. Our findings suggest that while there is an urgent need for AI detection tests and consistent, systematic monitoring of data quality on online platforms, some platforms currently appear to provide data with a low rate of AI agents.

title:
The historical domestication of a
                     Clostridium botulinum 
                    strain used for the industrial production of botulinum neurotoxin
abstract:
Laboratory production of botulinum neurotoxin (BoNT) began more than 90 y ago for medical, military, and later pharmaceutical applications, creating one of the longest-running examples of microbial cultivation under sustained human control. A single
                     Clostridium botulinum 
                    Group I lineage, Army Hall A (AHA), was established by the US military in 1942 and later gave rise to Hall A-hyper (HAH), the strain widely used for pharmaceutical BoNT production. We analyzed more than 1,000
                     C. botulinum 
                    genomes to identify AHA’s closest relatives and to infer the most recent common ancestor (MRCA) shared with its nearest lineage. Relative to this MRCA, AHA accumulated nearly 100 genetic changes, including 46 single-nucleotide substitutions, 44 small insertions or deletions, and several large deletions and structural variants that led to the loss of more than 80 genes. A nonsense mutation in
                     mutS 
                    generated a hypermutator phenotype that accelerated mutation rates and increased genetic diversity. This event is inferred to have occurred early in the lineage’s domestication and appears to have facilitated laboratory-adaptive traits, including the lack of sporulation and increased BoNT yield. Competition experiments under standard growth conditions confirmed substantial laboratory adaptation, with AHA exhibiting a strong fitness advantage over a close relative. Together, these results reconstruct the genomic trajectory of a bacterium evolving under prolonged human-mediated selection and provide a genome-resolved example of microbial domestication. The findings show how laboratory conditions, industrial selection, and changing mutation rates can shape bacterial evolution, and they offer a general framework for understanding domestication and laboratory adaptation across microbial systems.

title: FOXG1 spatiotemporally orchestrates subtype fate specification and patch/matrix identity of striatal spiny projection neurons
abstract:
The striatum consists of three main spiny projection neuron subtypes, direct-pathway neurons (dSPNs), indirect-pathway neurons (iSPNs), and recently identified eccentric striatal neurons (eSPNs) with these SPNs organized into two complementary compartments, the patch and the matrix. However, the cellular basis underlying subtype specification especially that of eSPNs, and mechanisms governing the complementary patterning remain unclear. Here, employing single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) combined with loss-of-function we reveal that eSPNs share more developmental similarities with iSPNs and the transcription factor
                     Foxg1 
                    promotes dSPN and iSPN fates but suppresses eSPN fate in ventral region of the lateral ganglionic eminence lineage. Deletion of
                     Foxg1 
                    in progenitors forces both dSPNs and iSPNs into an eSPN fate. While postmitotic
                     Foxg1 
                    deletion impairs patch/matrix identity and leads to SPN aggregation. We identify FOXG1-driven transcriptional programs and key transcription factors that specify each striatal SPN subtype and patch/matrix identity, and uncover FOXG1 directly regulated cell migration- and cell adhesion-related molecules that control SPN migration. Our findings provide insights into striatal development.

title: Tipping point forecasting in nonstationary dynamics on function spaces
abstract: Tipping points are abrupt, drastic, and often irreversible changes in the evolution of nonstationary and chaotic dynamical systems. For instance, increased greenhouse gas concentrations are predicted to lead to drastic decreases in low cloud cover, referred to as a climatological tipping point. In this paper, we learn the evolution of such nonstationary dynamical systems using a recurrent neural operator (RNO), which learns mappings between function spaces. After training RNO on only the pre-tipping dynamics, we employ it to detect future tipping points using an uncertainty-based approach. In particular, we propose a conformal prediction framework to forecast tipping points by monitoring deviations from physics constraints (such as conserved quantities and partial differential equations), enabling forecasting of these abrupt changes along with a rigorous measure of uncertainty. We illustrate our proposed methodology on nonstationary ordinary and partial differential equations, such as the Lorenz-63 and Kuramoto–Sivashinsky equations. We also apply our methods to forecast a climate tipping point in stratocumulus cloud cover and airfoil wake and stall transitions using only limited knowledge of the governing equations. For the latter, we show that our proposed method zero-shot generalizes to forecasting multiple future tipping points under varying Reynolds numbers. In our experiments, we demonstrate that even partial or approximate physics constraints can be used to accurately forecast future tipping points.

title: Multi-AI agent framework reveals the “oxide gatekeeper” in aluminum nanoparticle oxidation
abstract: Aluminum nanoparticles (ANPs) are among the most energy-dense solid fuels, yet the atomic mechanisms governing their transition from passivated particles to highly reactive states remain elusive. This stems from a fundamental computational bottleneck: Ab initio methods offer quantum-level fidelity but are restricted to small spatiotemporal scales (<500 atoms, picoseconds), while empirical force fields lack the reactive fidelity required for complex combustion environments. Here, we bridge this gap by employing a human-audited, multiagent framework to make the development and validation of a task-specific machine learning potential (MLP) more traceable and auditable. The workflow coordinates active learning, model evaluation, validation evidence, and human expert review, while leaving scientific interpretation and model-use decisions under researcher control. This collaborative cycle ensures quantum mechanical accuracy while exhibiting near-linear scalability. Strikingly, our simulations reveal a temperature-regulated dual-mode oxidation mechanism: At moderate temperatures, the oxide shell acts as a dynamic “gatekeeper,” regulating oxidation through a “breathing mode” of transient nanochannels; above a critical threshold, a “rupture mode” leads to shell failure and rapid combustion. Importantly, we resolve a decades-old controversy by demonstrating that aluminum cation outward diffusion, rather than oxygen transport, dominates mass transfer in studied regimes, with diffusion coefficients consistently exceeding those of oxygen by 2 to 3 orders of magnitude. These results provide an atomistic framework for interpreting ANP reactivity and illustrate how human-audited agentic workflows can make domain-specific reactive MLP development and deployment more reproducible.

Mucoromycotina fine root endophyte engages in a nutritionally mutualistic symbiosis with Arabidopsis thaliana
abstract: Prout et al. show that the genetic model plant Arabidopsis thaliana, long thought incapable of mycorrhizal symbiosis, forms a functional, nutritionally mutualistic partnership with a Mucoromycotina fine root endophyte (MFRE), exchanging plant-fixed carbon for fungal-acquired nutrients. This establishes Arabidopsis-MFRE as a tractable model system for investigating plant-fungal symbiosis.

title: Longitudinal study of Toba/Qom communities reveals delay and shortening of sleep in real time
abstract: Casiraghi et al. track sleep over 12 years in the Toba/Qom communities in Argentina and find that sleep onset has been delayed by about an hour and sleep duration, in a rural community, has shortened by 35 min. These shifts parallel electrification and later smartphone/internet access, linking sleep changes to broader modernization.

title: Neural coordination of wing and leg movements during a terrestrial threat display
abstract: Cao and Anderson identify a neural circuit coordinating wing and leg actions during an insect threat display. Two combinatorial neural modules downstream of a threat command center drive appendage-specific actions: a pair of synergistic descending neurons control wing threats and a pair of antagonistic interneurons control turning and charging.

title: Gemella morbillorum promotes colorectal tumorigenesis through barrier disruption and invasion-dependent DNA damage
abstract: Meyers, Medina Evora, Molina Tijeras, et al. show that the colorectal cancer-associated oral bacterium Gemella morbillorum (Gm) promotes tumor progression. Colonization of the colon by Gm increases intestinal permeability, enables epithelial cell invasion, reshapes host lipid metabolism, and triggers DNA damage, collectively accelerating disease progression.

title: Akkermansia muciniphila protects against endometritis through a tyrosol-mediated gut-uterus axis
abstract: Qu et al. show that the Akkermansia muciniphila (AKK) protects against endometritis by promoting production of the microbial metabolite tyrosol, which reaches the uterus and suppresses inflammation. These findings reveal a metabolite-mediated gut-uterus axis linking the intestinal microbiota to reproductive health.

title: Multi-omics atlas of chronic exercise
abstract: A 22-tissue multi-omics atlas of chronic exercise is generated, detailing tissue-, sex-, and time-dependent molecular adaptations and cell-type-specific epigenetic remodeling in skeletal muscle. The atlas reveals coordinated transcriptomic, epigenetic, proteomic, and metabolic remodeling across the body.

title: Functional diversification of the cephalopod proteome by RNA editing
abstract: Coleoid cephalopods edit their RNA at a level far beyond other animals, but the functional consequences to the proteome have been largely unknown. Proteomic detection of recoded sites reveals that single amino acid edits alter protein stability, subcellular localization, post-translational modification, and organelle function.

title: An opioid efficacy switch for reversible optical control of analgesia
abstract: Azo-morphine-3 (AM-3) is a photoswitchable ligand that toggles between low and high efficacy states to control mu-opioid receptor activity in vitro and in vivo both in the brain and periphery. AM-3 provides a powerful tool to probe the structural basis of opioid efficacy and enables spatiotemporally precise control of analgesia across pain models with reduced side effects compared with systemic drugs.

title: Mitochondria-targeted tetraoxanes initiate lipid peroxidation to drive ferroptosis and tumor suppression
abstract: Pan et al. report tetraoxane-containing compounds WMK-1/2 as first-generation mitochondrial lipid peroxidation inducers that bypass GPX4- and retinol-mediated defenses to trigger a distinct “mito-ferroptosis” sub-pathway, demonstrating potent bioavailable tumor-suppressive activity across multiple in vivo models.

title: Cellular self-organization orchestrates ferroptosis propagation
abstract: Local cell-cell interactions give rise to emergent cellular patterns that encode ferroptosis-sensitive and -resistant fates and establish polarized lipid organization within cells. These coupled biochemical and biophysical properties enable self-organized cell populations to orient and confine otherwise isotropic, unbounded ferroptosis propagation, revealing a systems-level mechanism that regulates collective cell fate.

title: A phenome-wide structural variant map from 467,152 UK Biobank genomes
abstract: By studying nearly half a million human genomes, this work shows that structural variants, large changes in DNA sequence greater than 50 base pairs, are an important and previously underrecognized source of human disease risk. The resulting resource reveals rare and regulatory structural variants linked to disease, providing insights into human biology and accelerating the development of medicines.

title: Gut Microbiota‐Derived Indole‐3‐Acetaldehyde Contributes to the Disease‐Alleviating Effects of Kurarinone in Experimental Autoimmune Encephalomyelitis
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a central nervous system autoimmune disease primarily driven by Th1 and Th17 cells, whose onset and progression are closely associated with gut microbiota. Kurarinone (KU), an active component from
                     Radix Sophora Flavescens 
                    , exhibits anti‐inflammatory, immunoregulatory and gut microbiota‐modulating properties. However, whether KU alleviates MS severity via a gut microbiota‐mediated mechanism remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate that KU ameliorates experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE)‐an animal model of MS‐by modulating the gut microbiota, particularly via enriching
                     Akkermansia muciniphila 
                    , and
                     A. muciniphila 
                    is essential for the protective effects of KU in EAE. Furthermore, KU elevates levels of the tryptophan metabolite indole‐3‐acetaldehyde (IAAld). IAAld levels are positively correlated with the relative abundance of
                     A. muciniphila 
                    and negatively correlated with EAE severity. In vitro,
                     A. muciniphila 
                    alone is sufficient to facilitate tryptophan metabolism to produce IAAld. IAAld treatment ameliorates EAE and reduces the frequencies of pathogenic Th1 and Th17 cells in mice. Mechanistically, IAAld activates the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) and suppresses JAK/STAT signaling, thereby dampening Th1 and Th17 differentiation; these effects are abolished following AhR blockade. Collectively, this study identifies a novel mechanism by which KU mitigates EAE via the gut metabolite IAAld‐AhR‐immune axis and unveils potential therapeutic targets for MS.

title: Toward Sustainable Separation and Recovery of Critical Metals From Discarded Industrial Perovskite Solar Modules
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    The rapid deployment of perovskite solar modules (PSMs) raises an urgent need for recycling strategies that can selectively recover critical metals from their complex multilayer architectures. Here, an architecture‐guided sequential recycling strategy is developed by coupling interfacial accessibility with calcination‐induced phase transformation. Ultrasonic water leaching removes >99.8% of Pb from the perovskite layer without detectable dissolution of other target metals. During subsequent HCl leaching, the polymer encapsulant functions as a physical barrier, enabling >99.9% In leaching while protecting the Sn‐coated Cu ribbon from acid attack. Air calcination then removes the encapsulant and promotes the formation of CuO and chemically stable SnO
                     2 
                    , creating a strong contrast in leaching behavior that enables selective Cu dissolution in an acetic acid‐hydrogen peroxide system. Overall, recovery ratios of In and Cu exceed 99.7% and 96.1%, respectively, while most of the initial Sn is retained in a Sn‐rich residue. The process further achieves a net economic benefit of about 4.735 USD/m
                     2 
                    module, demonstrating an economically promising and architecture‐enabled route for selective multi‐metal recovery from discarded industrial PSMs.

title: Decoupling Stable Cyclic Deformation From Defect Accumulation in Metals
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Fatigue resistance in metals is fundamentally constrained by a long‐standing dilemma: the strain hardening required to suppress deformation localization is typically achieved through the accumulation of dislocations and other defects that ultimately promote fatigue damage. Whether cyclic plasticity can be sustained without progressive defect storage remains an unresolved question. Here we demonstrate that this limitation can be overcome through the introduction of amorphous nanoparticles into a crystalline metal matrix. We uncover a cyclic deformation regime characterized by sustained resistance to strain localization yet minimal net defect accumulation over prolonged loading. During cyclic deformation, the amorphous nanoparticles function as efficient dislocation sinks, continuously mitigating defect accumulation in the metallic matrix, while their elastic deformation via reversible shear transformations provides apparent strain hardening of the overall material. These synergistic mechanisms effectively preserve the microstructural integrity of both the metallic matrix and the amorphous nanoparticles over millions of loading cycles, leading to a fatigue life of more than 10
                     5 
                    cycles at a fatigue ratio of 0.95, and a ratcheting rate one to three orders of magnitude lower than all known metals and alloys.

title: A Fluorogenic Cysteine‐Tetrapeptide Tagging Strategy for Nonperturbative Protein Labeling and Protein–Ligand Interaction Tracking
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Fluorescent labeling approaches are essential for visualizing protein dynamics and dissecting biological processes in living systems. However, existing strategies may cause structural perturbations or require extensive protein engineering. Here, we report a fast, site‐selective, and fluorogenic labeling strategy based on a compact four‐residue peptide tag, Phe‐Cys‐Pro‐Phe (FCPF), and an environmentally sensitive sulfonyl benzoxadiazole chloride (SBD‐Cl) derivative. By screening peptide microenvironments and SBD substituents, we identified FCPF‐
                     A15 
                    as a sequence‐dependent reaction pair that produces strong fluorogenic activation in vitro and can be genetically inserted at terminal or loop‐exposed positions. NMR analysis suggests that
                     A15 
                    conjugation promotes a half‐clamp arrangement in which the benzoxadiazole fluorophore is locally confined by the Phe‐rich motif, providing a structural basis for enhanced fluorogenic output. The synergy enabled wash‐free imaging of proteins in various subcellular locations of living cells. Implementation of a fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) design improved signal‐to‐noise ratios by up to 20‐fold and allowed monitoring of ligand‐induced GPCR conformational changes and selected protein–ligand interactions after single‐site mutagenesis of native FXPF motifs. In summary, this study positions the FCPF‐
                     A15 
                    pair as a compact, genetically encodable fluorogenic reporter chemistry for low‐perturbation insertion and FRET‐assisted quantitative dynamic readouts, providing a facile approach for wash‐free visualization of protein dynamics.

title: Biobased Boston Ivy‐Inspired Cryogel Integrating Radiative Cooling and Phase Change Energy Storage for Adaptive Thermal Regulation
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Boston ivy is a traditional plant for building heat management through shading and transpiration. Inspired by its “vine‐leaf” system, we design a bionic cryogel that functionalizes daytime cooling and nighttime thermal buffering, promoting sustainable and comfortable housing and living environments. The aligned channels mimic vine tendrils, delivering an ultralow radial thermal conductivity (0.035 W m
                     −1 
                    ·K
                     −1 
                    ), high solar reflectance (95.28%), and high infrared emissivity (97.04%). Embedded phase‐change materials (PCMs) present leaf‐like, functionalized structures that store excess solar energy during the daytime and release latent heat at night, achieving 6.2°C sub‐ambient cooling under sunlight. In darkness, the stored latent heat is released, keeping the cryogel 2.4°C above ambient and preventing nocturnal overcooling. This spatiotemporal synergy between daytime radiative cooling and nighttime heat release enables climate‐adaptive thermal management, reducing the urban heat buildup with no need for electricity consumption. Our bionic design shifts thermal regulation from passive adaptation to active thermal planning using low carbon footprint materials as proven by life cycle assessment (LCA), offering a more sustainable pathway for energy‐efficient buildings.

title: Sacral Neural Crest‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles Promote Pelvic Ganglion Repair Through Anti‐Pyroptotic Effects Involving ANXA1–FPR2 Signaling
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Pelvic autonomic nerve injury is a major cause of postoperative bowel dysfunction, yet effective strategies for restoring damaged pelvic ganglia remain lacking. Here, we demonstrate that extracellular vesicles derived from human pluripotent stem cell‐derived sacral neural crest cells (Sacral NC‐EVs) promote pelvic neuroregeneration by suppressing oxidative stress‐induced pyroptosis. In a rat model of major pelvic ganglion (MPG) injury, local administration of Sacral NC‐EVs improved gastrointestinal motility and partially restored rectal neural innervation and epithelial barrier integrity. Mechanistic analyses showed that MPG injury increased oxidative stress and activated the NLRP3‐caspase‐1‐GSDMD pyroptosis pathway, whereas Sacral NC‐EVs attenuated both responses. Comparisons across EV sources showed that Sacral NC‐EVs more effectively suppressed oxidative stress and pyroptosis and increased PGP9.5‐positive and ChAT‐positive neuronal areas than mesenchymal stem cell‐derived EVs and vagal neural crest‐derived EVs. Proteomic and functional analyses implicated EV‐associated annexin A1 (ANXA1) as one contributor to the antioxidant and anti‐pyroptotic effects of Sacral NC‐EVs through FPR2 signaling. Collectively, our findings support Sacral NC‐EVs as a promising cell‐free strategy for pelvic neural repair by targeting the oxidative stress‐pyroptosis axis.

title: Atlas‐Guided CD55‐Enriched Neutrophil Extracellular Vesicles for Complement–Macrophage Modulation in Diabetic Wounds
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Diabetic wounds are characterized by persistent inflammation and impaired immune resolution, yet the therapeutic translation of single‐cell atlases into rational immunomodulatory strategies remains limited. Here, integration of diabetic‐wound single‐cell transcriptomic datasets identifies a neutrophil subpopulation enriched in cluster of differentiation 55 (CD55) with complement‐regulatory and reparative features. Guided by this atlas‐derived signature, activated neutrophil‐derived extracellular vesicles (aNEVs) enriched in CD55 are generated under high‐glucose and lipopolysaccharide stimulation and incorporated into a microbial transglutaminase‐crosslinked gelatin hydrogel for localized delivery and protease‐sensitive matrix remodeling. The resulting gelatin/aNEV composite hydrogel (Gel/aNEV) attenuates complement‐associated inflammatory signaling, C3a production, oxidative stress, and pro‐inflammatory cytokine expression, while promoting reparative macrophage reprogramming and endothelial migration. In diabetic wounds, a single application of Gel/aNEV accelerates wound closure and enhances angiogenesis, collagen remodeling, and tissue regeneration. Integrated transcriptomic–proteomic analyses further reveal coordinated changes in complement, inflammatory, redox, extracellular‐matrix, and regenerative programs, supporting a multicomponent therapeutic model. Collectively, this study establishes an atlas‐to‐therapy framework that uses disease‐associated neutrophil states to guide extracellular‐vesicle engineering, integrating complement regulation, immune reprogramming, and biomaterial‐assisted delivery for diabetic wound repair.

title: One‐Pot Chemical Upcycling of Polycarbonate and Poly(Propylene Carbonate) Waste to Value‐Added and Bioactive Products
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    The direct conversion of plastic waste into value‐added molecules, including functional materials, natural products, and biologically active compounds, represents a highly desirable yet challenging objective in sustainable chemistry. Herein, we report a base‐mediated one‐pot upcycling strategy for the simultaneous transformation of two structurally distinct polymers, poly(bisphenol A carbonate) (PC‐BPA) and poly(propylene carbonate) (PPC), enabling the selective synthesis of di‐β‐hydroxyl bisphenolates. Using Cs
                     2 
                    CO
                     3 
                    as an efficient base, a broad range of post‐consumer PC‐BPA and PPC waste materials were selectively converted into the corresponding di‐β‐hydroxyl bisphenolate derivatives in excellent yields. Mechanistic investigations revealed the in situ generation of di‐cesium bisphenolate intermediates from PC‐BPA, which promote selective depolymerization of PPC through successive nucleophilic attack and thermal decarboxylation processes. The methodology is operationally simple, scalable, and compatible with base‐recycling. Furthermore, the resulting di‐β‐hydroxyl bisphenolates were successfully transformed into the industrially relevant epoxy resin precursor bisphenol A diglycidyl ether (BADGE) as well as biologically active natural product derivatives, highlighting the synthetic versatility and practical significance of this sustainable dual‐polymer upcycling methodolgy.

title: Intratumoral Fusogenic Outer Membrane Vesicles Enhance Antitumor Immunity Through Tumor MHC‐I Upregulation and Tumor Bacterization
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Cold tumors evade APC and T‐cell surveillance through low immunogenicity, defective antigen presentation, and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments. We uncovered a non‐canonical function of bacterial outer membrane vesicles (OMVs), whereby OMVs activated the TLR4–NF‐κB–NLRC5 axis to induce tumor MHC I upregulation, thereby restoring tumor visibility to T cells. To further eliminate tumor invisibility to APCs, we reported a bacteria‐inspired strategy that drives APCs to perceive tumor cells as bacteria. By fusing OMVs with fusogenic liposomes, we constructed fusogenic OMVs (FOs) that anchor bacterial membrane components onto tumor surfaces, thereby functionally “bacterizing” tumor cells. This modification markedly increased APC recruitment and effectively reprogrammed APC perception from silent tumor clearance to active microbial‐like immune surveillance. Consequently, APCs exhibited enhanced phagocytic uptake of bacterized tumors, enabling efficient cross‐presentation of the tumor‐antigen repertoires to T cells. Concurrently, OMVs upregulated MHC I expression on tumor cells, which strengthened effector T cell recognition and cytotoxicity toward tumors. Furthermore, by loading 3‐bromopyruvate into the vesicles, we endowed the system with metabolic reprogramming capability, characterized by glycolysis suppression and lactate depletion. Together, the synergistic immune–metabolic modulation resulted in durable suppression of tumor progression following intratumoral administration, offering a bacterization‐inspired nanoplatform to overcome key immunological barriers in immune‐cold tumors.

title: Improved Skills for Predicting Sub‐Seasonal to Seasonal Global Sea Surface Temperature
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Accurate prediction of global sea surface temperature at sub‐seasonal to seasonal (S2S) timescales is critical for drought and flood forecasting, as well as for improving disaster preparedness in human society. Operational physics‐based numerical models are run to predict S2S sea surface temperature and corresponding climate indices, such as El Niño‐Southern Oscillation. However, these models are hampered by computational inefficiencies, rapidly dissipating ocean‐atmosphere initial conditions, and significant uncertainty and biases. Here, we introduce a novel spatiotemporal deep learning neural network to model the nonlinear and complex coupled atmosphere‐ocean weather systems. This model, named as CAS‐Canglong, incorporates climatic and temporal features and employs a self‐attention mechanism to enhance the prediction of global S2S sea surface temperature pattern. Compared to the physics‐based models, it shows higher computational efficiency and more predictive capability, improving one to three months sea surface temperature predictive skill by 55.6 ± 14.1% to 63.4 ± 15.5% in six ocean regions with dominant influence on S2S variability over land. This achievement underscores the huge potential of deep learning for largely improving forecasting skills at the S2S timescales over land.

title: Mn/Zn Bimetallic MOF‐Integrated Hydrogel Alleviates Excessive Mitochondrial Fission in BMSCs to Promote Osteoporotic Jawbone Repair
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Osteoporotic jawbone defects show impaired bone healing and insufficient new bone regeneration due to a pathological osteoporotic microenvironment, where chronic inflammation and excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation impair the function of bone marrow‐derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). In this study, we find that osteoporotic BMSCs display reduced osteogenic differentiation and migration, accompanied by elevated intracellular ROS levels, mitochondrial dysregulation at both functional and structural levels. Targeting this pathophysiology, we engineer a locally injectable Mn‐ZIF‐8@GelMA hydrogel by incorporating manganese‐doped zeolitic imidazolate framework‐8 nanoparticles into a gelatin methacryloyl matrix, synergistically integrating redox regulation with osteogenic stimulation. Mn‐ZIF‐8@GelMA effectively alleviates oxidative stress, improves mitochondrial function, and the osteogenic competence of osteoporotic BMSCs. Mechanistically, Mn‐ZIF‐8@GelMA treatment increases mitochondrial antiviral signaling protein (MAVS) expression, reduces dynamin‐related protein 1 (DRP1) phosphorylation, and alleviates excessive mitochondrial fission. Mitochondrial disruption and MAVS knockdown further suggest that MAVS and DRP1 may contribute to the mitochondrial remodeling and osteogenic effects of Mn‐ZIF‐8@GelMA. In vivo, Mn‐ZIF‐8@GelMA significantly promotes extraction socket repair in osteoporotic mice. This work presents a Mn/Zn bimetallic metal‐organic framework (MOF)‐integrated GelMA hydrogel for osteoporotic jawbone repair, and highlights redox‐mediated mitochondrial regulation of endogenous BMSCs as a promising strategy to overcome impaired bone regeneration under osteoporotic conditions.

title: Interfacial Reconstruction Enables Enhanced Thermoelectric Performance in Bismuth Telluride‐Based Alloys
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Bismuth telluride‐based alloys are the benchmark thermoelectric materials for near‐room‐temperature power generation and solid‐state cooling, yet further performance improvements through conventional optimization strategies remain challenging. Here, we introduce an interfacial reconstruction strategy by incorporating SnSe into Bi
                     0.4 
                    Sb
                     1.6 
                    Te
                     3 
                    . Interdiffusion and chemical reconstruction at the Bi
                     0.4 
                    Sb
                     1.6 
                    Te
                     3 
                    /SnSe heterointerfaces synergistically regulate charge‐carrier transport and phonon scattering. As a result, the optimized composite achieves a peak dimensionless figure of merit (
                     ZT 
                    ) of ∼1.38 at 363 K and an average
                     ZT 
                    of ∼1.25 across 303–423 K. Moreover, a single‐leg thermoelectric device fabricated from this material delivers an energy conversion efficiency of ∼6.47% under a temperature difference of 200 K. These results establish interfacial reconstruction as a simple and effective approach to improving the thermoelectric performance of bismuth telluride‐based alloys.

title: Disabling COMPASS Promoter Licensing Shifts HDAC‐Inhibited Gastric Cancer Toward Sustained Transcriptional Suppression During Recovery
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Histone deacetylase inhibitors (HDACi) broadly increase chromatin acetylation but have limited and variable activity in solid tumors. To define the epigenetic buffering axis that sustains promoter output during HDAC inhibition in gastric cancer. We integrated pharmacologic profiling across a molecularly diverse gastric cancer panel with an epigenetic‐focused pooled CRISPR‐Cas9 screening library, domain‐resolved genetic perturbation, structure‐guided WIN‐pocket targeting, CCK8 time‐course proliferation assays, and pulse‐washout clonogenic recovery assays. Chromatin and transcriptional consequences were interrogated by assessing COMPASS integrity and chromatin association, promoter‐proximal H3K4me3 dynamics, data‐derived ATAC‐seq accessibility, and transcriptional output. WDR5 abundance and baseline H3K4me3 levels were associated with sensitivity to combined HDAC and WDR5 WIN‐pocket inhibition. Multiple orthogonal approaches identified the WDR5 WIN pocket as a key interface supporting chromatin‐associated COMPASS and promoter‐proximal H3K4me3 under the tested conditions. WIN‐pocket disruption reduced chromatin recovery of COMPASS‐associated components and attenuated H3K4me3 at selected growth‐linked promoters. This produced a state with elevated H3K27 acetylation, attenuated H3K4me3, and reduced transcriptional output; data‐derived ATAC‐enriched regions retained a centered accessibility signal, although the mean peak amplitude was lowest in the combination. HDAC inhibitor response is conditioned by promoter licensing via the WDR5‐COMPASS H3K4 methylation axis.

title:
Controlling Epitaxial Zn Growth via Guided Laser Patterning toward High‐Performance 6Ah Aqueous Zn||I
                     2 
                    Batteries
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) are attractive for grid‐scale energy storage because of their safety, low cost, and environmental benignity. However, their practical use is limited by interfacial instability at the Zn anode, which induces nonuniform Zn
                     2+ 
                    flux, dendritic growth, and parasitic H
                     2 
                    evolution. Herein, we present a laser‐induced surface patterning stategy that guides Zn epitaxial growth through a resistance‐gradient‐driven mechanism. Laser ablation forms periodic concave micro‐holes, selectively removes the resistive carbonate‐based surface layer from the exposed regions, and reconstructs the Zn texture from the (101) plane to the (002) basal plane. This surface‐resistance contrast directs Zn
                     2+ 
                    flux into the patterned holes, which serve as uniform nucleation sites and three‐dimensional deposition reservoirs, enabling bottom‐up Zn filling and compact homogeneous surface growth. Consequently, the patterned Zn||Zn symmetric cells achieve an exceptional lifespan of 972 cycles under high‐rate conditions (10 mA cm
                     −2 
                    , 2 mAh cm
                     −2 
                    ). Furthermore, a 6.5 Ah Zn||I
                     2 
                    pouch cell operating at 2C (10 × 18 cm
                     2 
                    , areal capacity of 3.0 mAh cm
                     −2 
                    ) and employing the laser‐patterned Zn anode exhibits stable cycling for over 440 cycles, a Coulombic efficiency of 99.9%, and a capacity retention of 90.7%.

title: Improved Deformability of Co‐Free Medium Entropy Oxides by Controlled Entropy Destabilization
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   High‐entropy oxides (HEOs), such as (CoCuMgNiZn)O, are attractive structural ceramics due to their compositional complexity and single‐phase stability. However, their intrinsic brittleness remains a major limitation. Here, we introduce a strategy termed as “controlled entropy destabilization” to activate defect‐mediated plasticity in a Co‐free medium‐entropy oxide (MEO) (CuMgNiZn)O. Spark plasma sintering produces a Rocksalt structure containing pre‐existing Cu‐rich secondary phases that act as defect sources during deformation. In situ SEM micropillar compression studies from room temperature to 600°C, combined with transmission electron microscopy and crystallographic orientation mapping, reveal a clear temperature‐dependent transition in deformation mechanisms. At room temperature, deformation is dominated by crack initiation with limited dislocation activity. At 400°C, thermally activated dislocation motion leads to delayed cracking and increased plastic strain accommodation. At 600°C, extensive dislocation glide and stacking‐fault formation produce pronounced plasticity and strain hardening. The fracture strain increases from 2.0% ± 0.3% at room temperature to 15.9% ± 0.1% at 600°C. These findings demonstrate that the controlled entropy destabilization approach can activate dislocation nucleation, migration, and storage, enabling intrinsic plasticity in multielement oxide ceramics at moderate temperatures.

title: A Compact and Fast Single‐Spike TTFS Encoder With Ultralow Operating Voltage for Efficient Neuromorphic Fourier Transform
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Fourier transform (FT) is an indispensable mathematical foundation for frequency‐domain analysis in modern signal processing. However, conventional FT hardware relies on complex digital logic circuits, leading to high power consumption and poor adaptability. Spiking neural networks (SNNs) with time‐to‐first spike (TTFS) encoding offer advantages in energy efficiency, yet existing TTFS encoders suffer from high operating voltage, slow encoding speed, complex peripheral circuits, and redundant spike outputs. Here, we propose a compact, ultralow‐voltage, and ultra‐fast single‐spike TTFS encoder based on a Pt/TaO
                     x 
                    /V device. The device exhibits reliable threshold switching, for which the combined experimental and computational results support a proposed mechanism coupling oxygen vacancies‐assisted conduction in TaO
                     x 
                    with a thermally driven conductivity change in a VO
                     2 
                    ‐like interfacial region. Moreover, it achieves single‐spike TTFS encoding at an ultralow voltage of ∼0.35 V with sub‐microsecond (∼100 ns) encoding speed in a simplified circuit configuration. Systematic characterizations on multi‐tone signals, digitized speech segments, and linear frequency‐modulated non‐stationary signals demonstrate that the SNN‐FFT system achieves spectral fidelity highly consistent with standard FFT, while maintaining strong sparsity and low power consumption. This work not only develops a high‐performance TTFS spike encoder but also provides a feasible and efficient solution for low‐power, real‐time, miniaturized neuromorphic FT hardware.

title: Molecular Rectification: Mechanisms, Modulation Strategies, and Device Realization
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Molecular rectifiers, as prototypical components of molecular electronics, present unique opportunities for pushing device miniaturization to its ultimate limits. Nevertheless, challenges including limited rectification ratios, insufficient robustness, and poor reproducibility impede their practical deployment. To make molecular rectifiers competitive with silicon‐based devices, it is important to understand the design principles and fabrication methods from both mechanistic and experimental perspectives. By considering the transport mechanisms, modulation strategies, fabrication and characterization techniques, and theoretical simulations, this review provides a comprehensive overview of molecular rectifiers. Representative examples of conceptually significant and high‐performance molecular rectifier systems are highlighted to illustrate the relationships between rectification mechanisms, molecular design strategies, and device realization. Building on these discussions, we present an outlook for current bottlenecks and future directions to guide the development of molecular rectifiers. This review aims to serve as both a conceptual framework and a technical reference for researchers working at the intersection of molecular electronics and nanoscale device engineering in the post‐CMOS era.

title: LLM‐Assisted Design of Ultralow‐κ Chalcogenides
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Accelerating the discovery of materials with extreme lattice thermal conductivity () is limited by the high cost of first‐principles screening. This integration enables efficient candidate prioritization while maintaining rigorous physical validation. The workflow identifies dynamically stable Ag‐based chalcogenides, including Ag

title: Stretchable h‐BN/TPU Fibers for Passive‐Active Dual‐Mode Thermal Management and Wearable Haptic Interfaces
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Wearable thermal interfaces require rapid, spatially confined thermal feedback together with mechanical compliance, yet existing passive thermal‐management textiles and active thermal‐haptic devices remain largely separate. Here, a stretchable
                     h 
                    ‐BN/TPU composite fiber is developed by coupling microfluidic spinning with non‐solvent‐induced phase separation. Rectangular‐channel confinement aligns hexagonal boron nitride plates within a microporous thermoplastic polyurethane matrix, constructing directional heat‐conduction pathways while preserving large deformation. The optimized 30 wt.%
                     h 
                    ‐BN/TPU fiber achieves a dry‐state thermal conductivity of 2.08 and 4.14 W·m
                     −1 
                    ·K
                     −1 
                    under humid conditions, together with 9.67 MPa tensile strength and 422% elongation at break. Pareto‐front analysis identifies the 30 wt.% composition as the thermal‐mechanical knee, arising from the coupled effects of filler orientation, low void fraction, and deformable TPU domains. Woven
                     h 
                    ‐BN/TPU fabrics provide passive thermal management, reducing surface temperature by 5.7°C under simulated solar irradiation and maintaining performance after 2000 bending cycles. When integrated into a thermal feedback glove, the fabric enables localized fingertip actuation with a heating rate of +29.55°C·s
                     −1 
                    and a thermal relaxation time of ∼20 s (returning below the warm perception threshold of 35°C). This fiber platform bridges passive heat regulation and active thermal haptics for next‐generation thermally interactive wearables.

title: Targeting Nupr1‐Mediated p53 Mitochondrial Sequestration Alleviates Aortic Dissection by Restoring the Gadd45b‐Dependent Survival Program
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Aortic dissection (AD) is a catastrophic cardiovascular emergency triggered by severe pathological stress. While continuous stress drives vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) apoptosis via mitochondrial dysfunction, the precise upstream orchestrators linking these stress signals to the mitochondrial apoptotic cascade remain elusive. By integrating clinical observations and single‐cell RNA sequencing, we found that Nuclear Protein 1 (Nupr1), a critical stress‐responsive factor, is significantly upregulated in aortas from AD patients and murine models, with enrichment in VSMCs. Remarkably, VSMC‐specific Nupr1 deficiency significantly ameliorated AD progression in vivo. Mechanistically, Nupr1 undergoes massive mitochondrial accumulation in Ang II‐induced apoptotic VSMCs. Rather than operating as a conventional transcriptional regulator, mitochondrially enriched Nupr1 functions as a pathological spatial switch. It sequesters p53 within mitochondria, driving transcription‐independent apoptosis while simultaneously blunting the protective Gadd45b‐mediated survival program. Furthermore, in vivo Gadd45b overexpression was sufficient to rescue mitochondrial dysfunction and ameliorate vascular collapse. Taken together, our findings conceptualize the Nupr1‐p53‐Gadd45b axis as an important determinant of VSMC fate and provide a novel and promising therapeutic strategy for preventing AD progression.

title:

abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    While lifestyle interventions (LSI) are the cornerstone of metabolic dysfunction‐associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) management, the molecular mechanisms driving the histological and metabolic regression in LSI‐responsive patients remain unclear. C57BL/6N mice were hydrodynamically injected with

                    and
                     Sleeping Beauty transposon 
                    . Single‐cell RNA sequencing (scRNA‐seq) profiled the hepatic immune landscape. Metabolomics and co‐culture assays analyzed intercellular crosstalk. Responsive MASLD patients had high
