                     Slc25a4 
                    ‐mediated enhanced hepatic fatty acid oxidation (FAO), and hepatic PPARα knockdown abolished this effect as well. Slc25a4 orchestrates an LSI‐responsive hepatocyte–macrophage axis: Pannexin 1‐mediated ATP release recruits lipid‐eating macrophages, whose GDF15 activates PPARα‐driven FAO, establishing Slc25a4 as a therapeutic target to restore exercise response in MASLD.

title: Innovative Approach Reveals How Receptors Control G Protein State Equilibria
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   G protein‐coupled receptors (GPCRs) constitute the largest family of drug targets, acting through heterotrimeric G proteins. Agonist bound GPCRs promote GDP release from G proteins allowing their activation upon GTP binding. Here, we analyze this process with innovative tools that detect the main states of native Gi proteins: the GDP‐bound, the open nucleotide‐free and the active GTP‐bound states. We show that receptor activation increases the amount of open‐state Gi proteins, consistent with GDP release from inactive Gi proteins. We also observe that the active receptor can release GTP from the active Gi protein, to return to an inactive open state. Consistently, receptor activation also promotes the formation of the Gαβγ complex from the GTP‐bound state in cells, in agreement with the formation of the receptor‐G protein ternary complex. These data suggest that the amount of active GTP‐bound form produced upon GPCR activation can be controlled by the receptor‐induced GTP release. This control of G protein state equilibrium that depends on the receptor subtype may affect coupling efficacy. These data reveal receptor‐dependent G‐protein state equilibria and identify GTP release as an additional, context‐dependent control point that can shape apparent coupling efficacy.

title: Molecular Landscapes of Tumor Dormancy in Gynecologic Malignancies: From Survival Mechanisms to Precision Interception
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Late recurrence in gynecologic malignancies is associated with tumor dormancy and persistent minimal residual disease (MRD). Although current treatments reduce proliferating tumor burden, residual cells may survive therapy and drive delayed relapse. This Review examines dormancy in ovarian, endometrial, and cervical cancers using entry, maintenance, and awakening as an organizing framework rather than a universally demonstrated sequence. Direct evidence is concentrated in ovarian cancer, whereas evidence in endometrial and cervical cancers remains predominantly indirect. We delineate candidate biological dependencies—including redox control, lipid peroxidation buffering, mitochondrial plasticity, adaptive stress‐response programs, epigenetic and post‐transcriptional plasticity, immune regulation, and extracellular matrix remodeling—rather than established vulnerabilities. On this basis, we evaluate two biologically distinct investigational concepts: suppression of reactivation‐associated signals to prolong clinical latency, and state modulation followed by biomarker‐defined treatment, discussed within established disease‐specific care pathways. Finally, we propose a translational framework combining longitudinal liquid biopsy with spatial and single‐cell profiling for MRD monitoring, biological stratification, and future probabilistic inference of residual‐cell states. Together, these concepts support a shift from reactive relapse treatment toward evidence‐ and risk‐constrained recurrence‐interception research and provide a framework for validating residual‐state biomarkers and therapeutic dependencies in gynecologic malignancies.

title: Neuron‐Derived Vesicular circMagi1 Restrains Vascular Repair After Ischemic Stroke by Promoting TRIM65‐Mediated ANXA2 Degradation
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Circular RNAs (circRNAs) contribute to stroke pathogenesis, yet their intercellular functions within the ischemic neurovascular unit remain poorly defined. Profiling of plasma extracellular vesicles (EVs) revealed a higher abundance of circMagi1 in patients with acute ischemic stroke compared with healthy controls. This upregulation was recapitulated in the ischemic mouse brain, where cell‐type‐resolved analyses identified injured neurons as a primary source of circMagi1‐containing EVs that accumulate in endothelial cells. Mechanistically, endothelial circMagi1 binds ANXA2 and enhances its engagement with TRIM65, thereby promoting TRIM65‐mediated ANXA2 ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation and restraining angiogenesis. To therapeutically target this axis in vivo, treatment with siCircMagi1‐RVG‐EVs was initiated on post‐stroke day 1 and maintained thereafter, while siTrim65‐Ang2‐EVs were introduced from either day 1 or day 9. Among the schedules tested, adding siTrim65‐Ang2‐EVs from day 9 was associated with greater neurovascular recovery than sustained circMagi1‐targeted treatment alone or co‐initiation on day 1. Together, these findings delineate a vesicle‐mediated signaling axis linking neuronal injury to impaired vascular repair and support further evaluation of delayed TRIM65 inhibition during sustained circMagi1 suppression.

title: Highly‐Time‐Resolved Measurements of Tryptophan's Distribution and Homeostatic Regulation in Live, Intact Animals
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Current theories regarding tryptophan's homeostatic regulation, which are derived from in vitro, post‐mortem, and cell‐culture studies, lack any direct evidence supporting their occurrence in living subjects. In response, here we have used 20 s resolution, multi‐hour plasma measurements to confirm, for the first time, that the cooperativity and tryptophan‐induced stabilization of tryptophan 2,3‐dioxygenase (TDO) seen in vitro and in cell culture hold in live, intact animals. For example, a model coupling these regulatory mechanisms with a constant tryptophan production rate from tissue reservoirs describes our in vivo measurements quantitatively, and provides high‐precision estimates of tryptophan flux and tryptophan‐induced TDO up‐regulation in individual subjects. In bridging a longstanding gap between ex vivo, post‐mortem, and cell culture investigations and the physiology of live, intact animals, an advance that had previously only been reported for glucose, our results highlight the transformative power of applying only‐recently‐available, seconds‐resolved metabolite measurements to the study of metabolic regulation.

title:
Bone Marrow Macrophage STING Signaling is a Direct Nexus Linking Marrow Adipose Expansion to NAD
                     + 
                    Depletion and Osteogenic Decline in Skeletal Aging
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Reversing the destructive remodeling of the bone marrow microenvironment during aging remains a major challenge. Here, we reveal an age‐dependent dual role of bone marrow macrophage (BMM) STING signaling during skeletal aging. While BMM STING deficiency is detrimental during early bone development and maturation, it paradoxically confers protection against age‐related bone loss from middle age onward. Mechanistically, accumulating bone marrow adipocytes secrete substantial soluble dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (sDPP4). This sDPP4 functions as an extracellular ligand for Toll‐like receptor 4 on BMMs, thereby collaborating with endogenous mitochondrial DNA to activate STING signaling. This STING activation concurrently induces a CD38‐dependent salvage synthesis pathway. Importantly, this STING‐driven upregulation of CD38 not only amplifies bone marrow inflammation but also, through its ecto‐nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD
                     + 
                    ) activity, depletes the precursor nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) required for NAD
                     + 
                    salvage synthesis, thereby impairing NMN availability and osteogenic capacity in neighboring bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells. Finally, therapeutic intervention combining STING pharmacological inhibition with NMN supplementation effectively attenuated bone loss in preclinical models. Thus, we propose BMM STING signaling as a direct nexus connecting marrow adipose accumulation, innate immune inflammation, and diminished bone formation, and emphasize its targeting potential for managing the aged bone marrow microenvironment.

title: How compartmentalization and proliferation shape the splenic T cell repertoire during an immune response to a complex antigen in mice
abstract: The adaptive immune system recognizes billions of unique antigens using highly variable T cell receptors (TCRs). To what extent TCR features shape the spatial distribution of the TCR repertoire (TCR-R) within lymphoid organs remains unclear. Here, we compared the TCR-R composition in T cell zones (TCZ), B cell zones (BCZ), and germinal centers (GC) of the spleen by analyzing the complementarity-determining region 3 of the beta chain (CDR3β) in microdissected splenic compartments from naïve and immunized mice. While we found substantial differences in TCR-R composition between these compartments, these differences largely disappeared once the effects of compartment size and proliferation were accounted for: During steady state, the few T cells found in BCZs strongly resemble random subsets of those found in TCZs. After immunization, expanded clones started appearing in the TCZ at day 3 and later shifted to the BCZ. GCs harbored even further expanded clones that were grouped into clusters with high sequence similarity. TCR-R differences during the immune response were well explained by a Galton-Watson model of T cell proliferation, suggesting that this could be the central factor shaping the observed TCR-R differences. Similarly, while TCR length and closeness to germline initially showed more pronounced differences between the compartments, our models of random distribution and proliferation explained these differences almost entirely. Hence, our findings suggest that splenic TCR-Rs are shaped predominantly by compartment size and proliferation rates rather than TCR sequence features. This would imply that quantitative assessment of TCR-R dynamics across heterogeneous spatial compartments during an immune response is only possible when these effects are explicitly accounted for.

title: MEGH-DDI: MolT5-driven edge-aware graph learning with Hop2Token representation for drug–drug interaction prediction
abstract:
Drug-drug interactions (DDIs) are critical in pharmacology, as synergistic or antagonistic effects between co-administered drugs can enhance therapeutic outcomes or cause toxicity, posing major challenges for drug safety assessment and new drug development. Current molecular representation methods often fail to capture dynamic substructure relationships or semantic interactions among functional groups. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes MEGH-DDI, a multimodal framework that integrates complementary molecular representation learning with graph-structure dynamic perception. The framework employs a dual-channel semantic module that combines Mol2vec-based substructure representations with MolT5 chemical language embeddings, while SHAP-based dynamic feature selection reduces redundancy. For fine-grained structural modeling, we introduce an edge-aware GCNII equipped with bond-level attention to distinguish different types of chemical bonds. Furthermore, the Hop2Token module converts multi-hop neighborhoods into token sequences, enabling Transformer-based modeling of high-order substructure dependencies. Experimental results demonstrate that MEGH-DDI achieves competitive performance across both transductive and inductive settings. On the DrugBank dataset, MEGH-DDI attains an accuracy of 98.36% in the transductive task, outperforming earlier baselines and surpassing recent state-of-the-art methods, with both AUC and AP exceeding 99.7%. On the ChChMiner dataset, MEGH-DDI achieves an F1 score of 99.05%, improving over the best existing method by 2.74 percentage points. In the inductive settings, MEGH-DDI achieves competitive performance across most evaluation metrics on both datasets, showing advantages over competing methods on several key metrics. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of MEGH-DDI in predicting DDI involving previously unseen drugs and its potential to generalize to complex DDI prediction scenarios. To enhance interpretability, MEGH-DDI incorporates a three-level mechanism spanning atoms, chemical bonds, and topological paths, highlighting key atoms and bond contributions. Overall, MEGH-DDI provides an efficient, accurate, and interpretable solution for drug safety assessment and new drug discovery. Code and datasets are available at
                     https://github.com/Lilyjoys/MEGH-DDI 
                    , and a free web platform is provided at
                     http://www.edgh-ddi.com 
                    .

title: Poison exon splicing in the human brain provides a new paradigm for understanding and targeting neurological disorders
Pep2Net: an integrated peptide knowledge base and cross-attention model for multi-task prediction of peptides
RNA modular expression laboratory (RNAmel): an integrated R/Shiny platform for reproducible bulk RNA-seq analysis and interpretation
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Background 
                     Bulk RNA-sequencing is routine, but turning a gene-level count matrix into biological insight still requires combining specialised tools for quality control, differential expression, dimensionality reduction, enrichment, co-expression networks, and activity inference. These steps are typically performed either with bespoke scripts that are hard to reuse and audit, or with interactive applications that ease exploration but can obscure provenance and couple analysis logic to interface code, making the analytical core hard to test, script, or reuse. 
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     We present the RNA Modular Expression Laboratory (RNAmel), an open-source R/Shiny platform for reproducible downstream bulk RNA-seq analysis, from count matrix and sample metadata to biological interpretation. Its distinguishing feature is architectural: rather than a monolithic Shiny application, RNAmel is implemented as a tested R package whose analysis and figure-generation logic lives in a public function layer covered by more than 440 unit tests, with the Shiny interface acting as a thin wrapper over this API. The same tested functions therefore drive the interactive session, the exported R script, and the test suite. On a single loaded dataset, RNAmel spans differential expression (DESeq2), PCA and UMAP exploration, multi-contrast comparison, gene-set enrichment and over-representation analysis, WGCNA co-expression networks, transcription-factor and pathway activity inference (decoupleR), per-sample signatures (GSVA/ssGSEA), and optional, opt-in AI-assisted interpretation. Analyses are recoverable as portable sessions and exported as runnable R scripts, Methods text, and self-contained HTML reports, with a versioned Docker environment and an accompanying renv.lock file recording the exact package versions. We demonstrate RNAmel on two published human datasets, a glucocorticoid-treatment study and a 120-sample, eight-cancer-type TCGA subset, and report internal consistency and cross-method concordance checks (exact reproduction of exported analyses; agreement with independent DESeq2 and WGCNA reference implementations; concordance with limma-voom). 
                   
                   
                     Conclusions 
                     
                      By placing a tested, scriptable function layer beneath an interactive interface, RNAmel combines exploratory accessibility with script-level transparency and reproducibility for downstream bulk RNA-seq analysis. It is freely available under the MIT licence at
                       https://github.com/KmBioChemo/RNAmel 
                      .

title: CoMeDA: an integrated platform for compositional analysis of metabarcoding data with batch correction
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Background 
                     Metabarcoding data generated from 16S rRNA and internal transcribed spacer (ITS) amplicon sequencing are inherently compositional, with observed abundances representing relative rather than absolute information. Ignoring this compositional structure can lead to spurious results in downstream analyses. In addition, multi-cohort studies frequently suffer from batch effects arising from differences in sample processing or sequencing platforms, which may confound true biological signals if not properly addressed. Despite the availability of multiple microbiome analysis platforms, these analytical considerations are not always incorporated together as central components of user-accessible workflows. 
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     We developed CoMeDA, an integrated web-based platform that treats the compositional structure of metabarcoding data and batch effects as coordinated components of a single analytical workflow. The platform supports both raw FASTQ files and pre-classified taxa tables, making it compatible with both short-read and long-read sequencing technologies. CoMeDA performs zero handling through probabilistic estimation and applies centered log-ratio (CLR) transformation as the default normalization strategy, followed by automated batch effect correction that removes technical variation while preserving biological signals. Downstream analyses, comprising diversity assessment using compositionally appropriate metrics, differential abundance analysis with effect size estimation, co-occurrence network inference, and functional prediction for both bacterial and fungal communities, are performed within the same compositional framework. CoMeDA also implements split-CLR transformation for cross-dataset analyses, enabling cross-kingdom and paired-condition correlation analyses while reducing spurious correlations introduced by directly combining datasets with different compositional structures. Using simulated datasets and a mock community with known ground truth, we evaluated the contribution of individual analytical components, the behavior of the automated batch-correction strategy, and taxonomic classification accuracy. We further reanalyzed a published multi-cohort gout dataset, a pediatric Crohn’s disease bacterial-fungal dataset, and a PacBio long-read periodontitis dataset. Using these datasets, CoMeDA recovered biologically coherent patterns while also highlighting additional literature-supported findings across different study designs. 
                   
                   
                     Conclusions 
                     CoMeDA provides a compositionally coherent workflow in which normalization, batch correction, and downstream analysis follow a consistent analytical logic. The platform features an interactive web interface and requires no programming expertise. CoMeDA is freely available online without registration, and a standalone Docker image is provided for local deployment.

Pepper
                     RING 
                    ‐type
                     E3 
                    ligase,
                     CaANKR1 
                    , negatively regulates drought tolerance by modulating
                     CaMAPK1 
                    stability
abstract:
SUMMARY 
                   
                    Drought stress severely restricts plant growth and productivity, and abscisic acid (ABA)–mediated signaling plays a central role in coordinating adaptive responses to water deficit. Mitogen‐activated protein kinase (MAPK) cascades are widely involved in plant stress signaling; however, the ubiquitin‐mediated regulation of MAPK stability during drought responses remains poorly understood. In this study, we conducted a yeast two‐hybrid screening and identified CaMAPK1, a pepper (
                     Capsicum annuum 
                    ) MAPK, as an interacting partner of the RING‐type E3 ubiquitin ligase CaANKR1, which was further confirmed via
                     in vitro 
                    and
                     in vivo 
                    assays.
                     CaMAPK1 
                    expression was induced by dehydration, osmotic stress, salinity stress, and ABA treatment. Furthermore, CaMAPK1 exhibited kinase activity and was predominantly localized to the nucleus. Ubiquitination assays revealed that CaANKR1 promoted K48‐linked polyubiquitination of CaMAPK1 in a RING domain–dependent manner. Consistently, cell‐free degradation assays showed that CaMAPK1 protein stability negatively correlated with
                     CaANKR1 
                    expression levels, indicating that CaANKR1 promotes the proteasome‐dependent degradation of CaMAPK1. Phenotypic assays revealed that
                     CaMAPK1 
                    silencing in pepper reduced drought tolerance by altering ABA‐mediated stomatal responses and water retention, whereas
                     CaMAPK1 
                    overexpression in
                     Arabidopsis 
                    produced the opposite phenotype. Collectively, these findings suggest that CaANKR1 negatively modulates ABA‐mediated drought tolerance through ubiquitin‐dependent destabilization of CaMAPK1. Together, they reveal a mechanism underlying ABA‐driven drought responses and highlight a promising target for enhancing crop drought resilience.

title:
The plant longevity gene
                     AHL15 
                    delays leaf senescence by repressing
                     ORESARA1 
                    and cytokinin degradation
abstract:
SUMMARY 
                   
                    The
                     Arabidopsis thaliana 
                    (Arabidopsis)
                     AT‐HOOK MOTIF NUCLEAR LOCALIZED 15 (AHL15) 
                    gene is associated with various longevity phenotypes and extends the life span of plants when overexpressed. In this study, we show that, in addition to previously described longevity phenotypes, constitutive overexpression of
                     AHL15 
                    in Arabidopsis delays leaf senescence, whereas
                     ahl15 
                    loss of function accelerates this process. Dexamethasone‐induced nuclear localization of AHL15‐GR during dark‐triggered senescence results in a stay‐green phenotype and represses the expression of several early senescence‐associated genes. Among these, the
                     ORESARA1 (ORE1) 
                    locus is directly bound by AHL15, suggesting a direct delaying effect of AHL15 on senescence. Furthermore, we demonstrate that AHL15 acts by directly repressing the expression of several
                     CYTOKININ OXIDASE (CKX) 
                    genes involved in cytokinin inactivation, resulting in delayed degradation of cytokinins during dark‐induced senescence. Cytokinins are known to inhibit senescence, and this, together with the downregulation of
                     ORE1 
                    expression, explains the delaying effect of AHL15 on senescence.

title:
NLP6 
                    /7‐mediated nitrate signaling facilitates high‐affinity potassium uptake and enhances tolerance to low potassium environments in Arabidopsis
abstract:
SUMMARY 
                   
                    Balancing the acquisition of the macronutrients nitrogen (N) and potassium (K) is critical for plant growth, yet the mechanisms that balance N and K acquisition remain poorly understood. Here, we show that the NIN‐LIKE PROTEIN7 (NLP7) transcription factor, which mediates nitrate signaling, plays a crucial role in promoting K acquisition in Arabidopsis. K
                     + 
                    uptake activity was reduced in the
                     nlp7 
                    mutant and
                     nlp6nlp7 
                    double mutant but enhanced in the
                     NLP7 
                    ‐overexpressing line. Consistently, these mutants were hypersensitive to K deficiency, whereas the
                     NLP7 
                    ‐overexpressing line displayed increased tolerance. Transcriptome analysis of the
                     nlp6nlp7 
                    mutant suggested that NLP7 activates several critical K‐related genes, including
                     HAK5 
                    , a transporter gene essential for K
                     + 
                    uptake from soil, and
                     SKOR 
                    , a channel gene critical for root‐to‐shoot transport of K
                     + 
                    . Using co‐transfection assays, gel electrophoresis mobility shift assays, and chromatin immunoprecipitation assays, we demonstrate that NLP7 directly interacts with and activates the promoters of these two genes. Furthermore, the enhanced K
                     + 
                    uptake and improved K deficiency responses driven by
                     NLP7 
                    overexpression were mitigated in the
                     hak5 
                    and
                     skor 
                    mutants, demonstrating the significant physiological role of NLP7‐induced activation of these genes. Although
                     HAK5 
                    and
                     SKOR 
                    responded differently to K deficiency, both genes were activated similarly by NLP7 under K‐sufficient and K‐deficient conditions. Together, these findings suggest that K deficiency‐induced regulation and nitrate‐responsive regulation operate through independent transcriptional mechanisms but collaborate to ensure appropriate K acquisition under diverse N and K conditions, especially when K availability is limiting.

title:
The
                     RcDREB1E 
                    ‐
                     RcMYB28 
                    module improves drought tolerance in
                     
                       Rosa chinensis 
                     
                    via
                     
                       RcLAR 
                     
                    /
                     
                       RcCORA1 
                     
                    ‐mediated proanthocyanidin biosynthesis and stress responses
abstract:
SUMMARY 
                   
                    Drought is widely recognized as one of the most severe abiotic stresses limiting plant growth and productivity. Proanthocyanidins (PAs), as key functional secondary metabolites, are central to enhancing plant tolerance to abiotic stresses. Nevertheless, the specific mechanisms underlying PA‐mediated drought resistance in rose remain largely unclear. Herein, we demonstrate that drought‐induced PA accumulation constitutes a conserved evolutionary mechanism across the plant kingdom, ranging from unicellular algae to angiosperms. Specifically, according to the drought‐responsive transcriptome dataset of
                     Rosa chinensis 
                    ‘Old Blush’, an R2R3‐MYB transcription factor, RcMYB28, was identified. Overexpression of
                     RcMYB28 
                    remarkably enhanced drought tolerance and induced a significant increase in PAs accumulation, whereas plants with silenced
                     RcMYB28 
                    displayed the opposite phenotypic characteristics. Specifically,
                     RcMYB28 
                    directly regulated the expression of leucoanthocyanidin reductase (
                     RcLAR 
                    ) and a cold and drought regulatory‐protein encoding gene (
                     RcCORA1 
                    ), thereby promoting PA synthesis and enhancing the stress response. Moreover, we identified RcDREB1E as a potential upstream transcriptional regulator of
                     RcMYB28 
                    . RcDREB1E exerts a positive regulatory effect on drought tolerance and PAs accumulation via
                     RcMYB28 
                    expression. Collectively, our results demonstrate a new transcriptional regulatory module (RcDREB1E‐RcMYB28) underlying drought‐triggered PAs accumulation, which offers valuable genetic resources for engineering enhanced drought tolerance in rose.

title:
A
                     bHLH121 
                    /
                     URI 
                    –
                     ANAC017 
                    –
                     MAT1 
                    /
                     SAM1 
                    regulatory cascade controls iron homeostasis in
                     Arabidopsis
abstract:
SUMMARY 
                   
                    Iron (Fe) deficiency is a critical environmental constraint limiting plant growth, yield, and quality. Although plants have evolved sophisticated mechanisms to enhance Fe uptake, transport, and utilization, key components of the underlying regulatory network remain unclear. Here, we identify the NAM, ATAF1/2, and CUP‐SHAPED COTYLEDON 2 (NAC) transcription factor ANAC017 as an essential regulator of Fe homeostasis in
                     Arabidopsis 
                    .
                     ANAC017 
                    expression is strongly induced under Fe deficiency, and loss of
                     ANAC017 
                    function leads to reduced Fe accumulation in both roots and shoots, impaired root elongation, and pronounced leaf chlorosis. Notably,
                     anac017 
                    mutants show excessive Fe retention in the cell wall—particularly within the hemicellulose fraction—under Fe‐deficient conditions, suggesting that ANAC017 contributes to the mobilization and reutilization of apoplastic Fe. Mechanistically, ANAC017 functions within the canonical Fe signaling cascade. We show that the core Fe regulator, the BASIC HELIX‐LOOP‐HELIX (bHLH) transcription factor bHLH121/URI, directly activates
                     ANAC017 
                    transcription, and overexpression of
                     ANAC017 
                    partially rescues the Fe‐sensitive phenotype of the
                     bhlh121/uri 
                    mutant. Further experiments revealed that the transcription factor ANAC017 binds to the promoter of
                     MAT1 
                    /
                     SAM1 
                    (encoding
                     S 
                    ‐adenosylmethionine synthetase), potentially modulating its expression. In conclusion, this study reveals that ANAC017 functions downstream of the bHLH121/URI pathway to regulate Fe homeostasis via two separate mechanisms: facilitating cell wall Fe reutilization and mediating
                     S 
                    ‐adenosylmethionine synthetase metabolism by regulating
                     MAT1/SAM1 
                    .

title: Roots to simplicity: when evolution removes a key organ
abstract:
Summary 
                   The evolution of roots was an instrumental event in the colonisation of land by vascular plants. Roots have undergone extensive radiation and can take many diverse forms including taproots, fibrous roots, and adventitious roots. This includes specialist root types, such as pneumatophores in mangroves, that have allowed species to occupy new ecological niches. In some cases, the relationship between roots and soil has been broken, rendering roots unnecessary and ultimately resulting in loss of this organ in some species. We identify several ecological niches/life habits in which rootless vascular plants have evolved: aquatic environments, canopies, arid environments, and carnivory. Many of these plants are challenging to cultivate in a laboratory environment. The exception to this is duckweeds, which we propose as a powerful experimental model for studying organ loss in plants.

title: Single‐nucleus RNA sequencing reveals a key regulator RsHB8 affecting vascular cambium activity and xylem differentiation during radish taproot thickening
authors:
Feng Cui, 
Jingxue Li, 
Hongyu Bi, 
Sichen Zhao, 
Xiaoqi Yuan, 
Boya Zhao, 
Liang Xu, 
Yinbo Ma, 
Xiaoli Zhang, 
Sen Chen, 
Yuting Zhang, 
Yan Wang, 
Liwang Liu
abstract:
In xylem differentiation in radish taproots, HOMEOBOX 8 (RsHB8) is proposed to activate transcription of the xyloglucan endotransglucosylase/hydrolase gene  RsXTH22  and contribute to cell-wall remodeling, whereas the LOB domain-containing protein RsLBD21 interacts with RsHB8 and attenuates this transcriptional activation.

  
 ABSTRACT 
 Radish taproot thickening is primarily driven by vascular cambium (VC) activity. However, the transcriptional regulatory mechanisms underlying taproot thickening at a single-cell resolution remain unclear. In this study, single-nucleus isolation coupled with fluorescence-activated cell sorting was used to construct a cell atlas of radish taproots using microdroplet-based single-nucleus RNA sequencing. Through canonical marker gene profiling and validation using laser capture microdissection transcriptome data, 12 cell types were identified, and the first single-nucleus transcriptomic atlas was constructed for radish taproots. VC cells exhibited heterogeneous transcriptional states with varying levels of expression of cell cycle-associated genes. Pseudotime analysis inferred a transcriptional trajectory from VC cells toward xylem parenchyma cells in radish taproots. Integrating pseudotime analysis with predicted protein–protein interaction networks highlighted HOMEOBOX 8 (RsHB8) as a candidate regulator of the inferred VC–to–xylem parenchyma (XP) trajectory.  RsHB8m  overexpression increased taproot width and promoted xylem differentiation, whereas  RsHB8 -silenced plants exhibited a reduced taproot width and narrower xylem region.  Xyloglucan endotransglucosylase/hydrolase 22  ( RsXTH22 ) was identified as a target gene of RsHB8. LOB domain-containing protein 21 (RsLBD21) interacted with RsHB8, inhibited its transcriptional activity, and attenuated the RsHB8-mediated transcriptional activation of  RsXTH22 . Silencing  RsLBD21  significantly increased taproot and xylem width, whereas silencing  RsXTH22  resulted in the opposite phenotypes. Together, these findings establish a single-nucleus transcriptomic atlas of radish taproot development and provide insights into the transcriptional regulation of VC differentiation during taproot thickening.

title:
Coordination of lignin and pectin remodeling by a NAC transcription factor regulates seed abscission in sesame (
                     Sesamum indicum 
                    L.)
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Seed shattering, which facilitates seed dispersal, is essential for plant reproduction but causes substantial yield loss in sesame (Sesamum indicum L.). It occurs through capsule dehiscence and/or seed abscission from the placenta, either simultaneously or independently depending on the species. In this study, we investigated cell wall-associated factors underlying delayed seed abscission in the sesame cultivar Suwon195 (SW195) relative to the easy-shattering cultivar IT030100. Histological and transcriptome analyses indicated that cell wall remodeling, particularly involving pectin and lignin, contributes to the delayed abscission phenotype of SW195. SW195 showed higher pectin methylesterase activity and stronger accumulation of low-methyl-esterified homogalacturonan, together with lower polygalacturonase-associated pectin turnover, than IT030100. These changes are consistent with a pectin-remodeling state that favors wall stabilization in the SW195 abscission zone. Abscission zone lignification was also weaker in SW195. Pharmacological inhibition of lignin biosynthesis altered pectin staining and reduced seed abscission in IT030100, whereas monolignol supplementation restored both phenotypes, supporting a functional association between lignification, pectin-related wall remodeling, and abscission. Quantitative trait loci (QTL) mapping and whole-genome resequencing identified a major locus on chromosome 9 encompassing a NAC transcription factor (SiNAC; SIN_1025412) and a pectin methylesterase inhibitor (SiPMEI; SIN_1025380). Transient overexpression of SiNAC enhanced lignin biosynthesis in sesame. Together, these findings indicate that coordinated lignin deposition and pectin remodeling are associated with seed abscission in sesame and identify candidate genetic components for breeding reduced-shattering cultivars.

title: Distinct root apoplastic barrier distribution and conserved peroxidase function in desert trees
abstract:
Abstract 
                   The formation of extracellular barriers in roots plays a critical role in maintaining water balance and nutrient homeostasis; however, their molecular composition and physiological roles in desert-adapted plants remain largely unexplored. 
                   Here, we examine apoplastic barrier formation in the roots of 2 arid-adapted, ecologically and economically important tree species: date palm (Phoenix dactylifera) and gray mangrove (Avicennia marina). In date palm, lignin and suberin showed complementary distribution patterns within the outer root layers. In mangrove roots, lignin accumulated in the epidermis and exodermis, whereas suberin was concentrated in the exodermis. Label-free Raman spectroscopy imaging confirmed these spatial patterns. Noninvasive magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed that water distribution mirrored barrier localization: date palms retained water in the vasculature and outer tissues, whereas mangroves concentrated water in the xylem. Transcriptome analysis identified a type III PEROXIDASE (PER) highly expressed in the exodermis of both species. The PER protein localized to Golgi-derived vesicles and the plasma membrane and interacted with a component of the Golgi apparatus. Expression of date palm and mangrove PER in Arabidopsis thaliana leads to ectopic lignin deposition in the root epidermis. Together, our findings suggest that type III PEROXIDASES are transported to the plasma membrane through the Golgi vesicles and promote lignin deposition. Overall, this study reveals distinct root barrier distribution and identifies a conserved molecular component underlying structural adaptations that enable plants to thrive in challenging environments.

title:
Identification of photosynthesis-related genes in peanut (
                     Arachis hypogaea 
                    L.) by hyperspectral phenomics, GWAS, and RNA-seq
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Peanut (Arachis hypogaea L.) contributes importantly to the global food supply, and its yield potential is closely linked to leaf photosynthetic efficiency. However, conventional measurement of leaf net photosynthetic rate (Leaf Pn) is time- and labor-intensive, limiting its application to large breeding populations. We established a phenomics-driven framework integrating hyperspectral reflectance and genome-wide association studies for high-throughput evaluation and genetic dissection of Leaf Pn. Machine-learning models were trained on preprocessed spectral data from 1,200 leaf samples collected in 4 environments. Random forest performed best after Savitzky–Golay smoothing and first-derivative transformation (R2 = 0.81, root mean square error = 1.50), outperforming the vegetation index-based model (R2 = 0.66). Applying this model to a panel of 173 peanut genotypes identified 2 quantitative trait loci, qPn5.1 and qPn13.1, encompassing 7 candidate genes. Integrated analyses prioritized Arahy.K5L3ZW, which encodes protein kinase 2B. Silencing this gene increased Leaf Pn, whereas transient overexpression decreased it, indicating that Arahy.K5L3ZW negatively regulates Leaf Pn. This framework enables high-throughput genetic dissection of seedling photosynthetic capacity and identifies a candidate target for improving photosynthetic efficiency in peanut.

title:
RuBP availability contributes to the regulation of RUBISCO activity in
                     Synechocystis
abstract:
Abstract 
                   RIBULOSE-1,5-BISPHOSPHATE CARBOXYLASE/OXYGENASE (RUBISCO) and the Calvin-Benson-Bassham (CBB) cycle assimilate most of the inorganic carbon on earth. Conserved CP12 proteins control diurnal C-assimilation of the CBB cycle. Their function originated in cyanobacteria that deactivate GLYCERALDEHYDE 3-PHOSPHATE DEHYDROGENASE (GAPDH) and PHOSPHORIBULOKINASE (PRK) during darkness by redox-regulated complex-formation with CP12. This mechanism indicates metabolic regulation of C-assimilation. We measured C-assimilation in vivo at the day/night transition by dynamic 13CO2 labeling and 1-C-positional monitoring of 13C-incorporation into 3-phosphoglycerate (3PGA) and aspartate of Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 grown with high (5%) CO2 supply. Unlike wild type, a Δcp12 mutant accumulated ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate (RuBP) and assimilated 13CO2 in darkness. We validated these observations by proteome measurements and orthogonal quantifications of RUBISCO abundances and specific activities. Complementation of Δcp12 with native CP12 and point-mutants of its GAPDH- and PRK-binding domains demonstrated that defective complex formation is causal for aberrant C-assimilation during darkness and that RuBP accumulation correlates significantly with the time-shifted 13C-incorporation into 3PGA. RUBISCO carboxylase activity is present throughout the diurnal cycle and depends on CP12-controlled substrate availability. 13C-positional analyses suggest dysregulated RuBP regeneration in Δcp12 during darkness via futile metabolic cycling through gluconeogenesis and the oxidative pentose phosphate path. We propose that blocked regeneration and rapid depletion of RuBP contributes to the regulation of RUBISCO activity at day-night transitions.

title: Evidence of large-scale and room-temperature stair-stepped quantum spin Hall states in Bi4Br4
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Topological insulators host exotic quantum phenomena such as the quantum spin Hall (QSH) effect, which enables dissipationless one-dimensional edge conduction. Realizing such states at room temperature and on a macroscopic scale is essential for energy-efficient electronics and quantum technologies, yet remains a fundamental challenge due to material limitations. Here, using microwave impedance microscopy, we directly visualize robust conductive channels persisting up to 300 K in α-Bi4Br4 nanowires. Their stability and scalability are likely enabled by a “stair-stepped” stacking configuration on the side facets, a multilayer geometry in which QSH edge states from individual layers remain spatially decoupled. This configuration circumvents the stringent alignment and layer-number constraints of previous proposals, allowing robust stair-stepped QSH (SS-QSH) conduction in structures several micrometers long and hundreds of nanometers high. Magnetic-field- and temperature-dependent measurements are consistent with the topological nature of these conductive channels, as further supported by our theoretical analysis. Crucially, the conductance peaks and bulk signals scale with nanowire height, verifying the stair-stepped origin. Our results are also successfully reproduced by finite-element analysis simulations. This work establishes α-Bi4Br4 as a practical platform for high-temperature topological electronics and demonstrates a generalizable stacking strategy for designing scalable QSH systems.

title: Photonic half-semimetals with dual semimetal-insulator topology
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Topological wave systems have largely evolved along two distinct paradigms: gapless topological semimetals and gapped topological insulators. While topological semimetals support bulk transport, they generally lack intrinsic selectivity among propagation channels; topological insulators enable robust transport but confine it to narrow interfaces, limiting spatial utilization. Here, we theoretically demonstrate and experimentally realize time-reversal-invariant spin-valley photonic half-semimetals (HSMs), which exhibit a dual semimetal-insulator topology within a single bulk band structure. In HSMs, the bandgap closes selectively in spin-valley space: for a given spin (valley), one valley (spin) is semimetallic while the other remains insulating. This coexistence of spin- and valley-resolved gapless and gapped band structures makes HSMs fundamentally distinct from both conventional semimetals and insulators. As a defining bulk phenomenon, an HSM functions as a spin-valley-locked beam splitter, intrinsically enabling valley-selective spin routing. Moreover, when four complementary HSMs are assembled into a periodic superlattice, the same dual topology enables reciprocal spin-valley-resolved multilane helical transport with 100% spatial utilization. These results establish HSMs as a platform for selective bulk wave control and multichannel topological transport beyond conventional topological phases.

title: Unified structural origin of functionality in spiral skyrmions revealed by 3D electron tomography
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Ferroelectric skyrmions exhibit a range of emergent phenomena, including collective dynamics, negative capacitance, and a strong electric-field-induced second-harmonic generation response. However, three-dimensional (3D) atomic-scale configurations of skyrmions are unclarified yet, making the relationship between the physical functionalities and their underlying structural origin remains elusive. Here, using atomic-scale electron tomography, we experimentally resolve the 3D structure of polar skyrmion for the first time in PbTiO3/SrTiO3 superlattice. On the basis of large-data image acquisition with more than 95,000 3D coordinates of atoms, we visualize that the core of the skyrmions exhibit an upward spiraling morphology. By quantitatively analyzing the ferroelectric polarization and lattice distortion, we uncover an unconventional decoupling between the two at the skyrmion wall, where the polarization is suppressed, accompanied by a local enhancement of tetragonality exceeding 5% at the center of the wall. This increased tetragonality modifies the local free-energy landscape, enhancing the negative-capacitance response and field sensitivity at the skyrmion wall. The polar skyrmion wall hosts a concentration of emergent physical properties, thereby providing a unified structural origin for the functionalities and physical behaviors of skyrmions. This work establishes a real space basis for understanding the physical properties of polar skyrmions.

title:
Robust quasi-bound states in the continuum in bilayer terahertz metasurface with
                     S 
                    4 point-group symmetry
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Metasurface-based bound states in the continuum (BICs) enable exceptional spatiotemporal control of light and substantially enhance light–matter interactions, making them highly attractive for applications in sensing, nonlinear optics, and integrated photonics. However, conventional BICs in single-layer metasurfaces rely on in-plane symmetry and are highly susceptible to structural perturbations, offering limited design flexibility and constraining both their robustness and functional diversity. To overcome these limitations, we theoretically propose and experimentally demonstrate a new class of symmetry-protected quasi-BICs in bilayer terahertz metasurfaces. These states are realized by coupling in-plane rotational and out-of-plane reflective symmetries through S4 point-group operations. Moreover, we show that such QBICs exhibit strong robustness against structural defects and fabrication imperfections. This work overcomes the robustness limitations of conventional single-layer metasurface BICs and establishes a general design paradigm for photonic devices that harness BICs with enhanced stability and scalability.

title: Deciphering Critical Transition for AKI Deterioration by STIfuse: Fusing Dynamic and Static Representations
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a life-threatening condition with notably high in-hospital mortality, characterized by a three-phase progression: a relatively stable state (without imminent life threat), a critical pre-deterioration state (the time window which may be identified and in which timely intervention could prevent upcoming irreversible deterioration), and a deteriorated state (severe conditions such as death or rescue events). Accurate early prediction of AKI deterioration and deciphering the critical transition remain challenging because of complex, high-dimensional, noisy, and incomplete clinical data, as well as limited mechanistic understanding of disease progression. To solve this problem, we propose STIfuse (Spatiotemporal Information fusion), a unique dual-view framework that integrates deep learning (DL) and spatiotemporal information transformation (STI) based on Takens’ embedding theorem and critical slowing down (CSD) theory. The DL backbone encodes multi-dimensional static representations to capture structural dependencies, while the STI branch transforms high-dimensional spatial information into a low-dimensional dynamic representation. These views are fused by a multivariate Gaussian distribution: the means capture statistical levels for diagnosis, and the covariances reflect collective physiological fluctuations for early deterioration prediction. An optimal-transport-distance-based contrastive loss is employed to learn discriminative dynamic features between ˈcriticalˈ and ˈstableˈ states. Pretrained on the MIMIC-IV dataset and validated on five external cohorts (including MIMIC-III (with two independent cohorts), eICU, HiRID, and NWICU), STIfuse demonstrated superior performance in predicting 72-hour deterioration. Further analysis of single-cell multi-omics data study uncovered inflammatory cascades linking comorbidities to AKI. STIfuse provides an interpretable, robust and scalable framework for early warning of AKI deterioration prediction, highlighting its potential in utility and scalability for clinical foundation models.

title: How does the brain do more with less energy?
scChronos: hierarchical temporal context learning for missing snapshot prediction in single-cell time series
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Motivation 
                     Single-cell time-series atlases provide discrete cross-sectional snapshots of continuous developmental processes, making missing-snapshot prediction essential for reconstructing trajectories and dynamic programs. However, destructive scRNA-seq profiling prevents tracking the same cells across time, yielding unpaired population snapshots and making missing-snapshot prediction challenging. Existing methods typically rely on explicit dynamical propagation or transport-based coupling between snapshots, which may ignore the statistical constraints of the overall population distribution and be sensitive to sampling noise and cell-to-cell variability. 
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     We introduce scChronos, a hierarchical temporal context learning framework that formulates missing-snapshot prediction as target-conditioned population distribution prediction rather than individual-cell propagation. Unlike cell-centric propagation approaches, scChronos explicitly captures dual-level dynamics: (i) within each observed snapshot, scChronos compresses cell populations into cluster-representative cell representations with a transcriptomic encoder, preserving population information while reducing noise and (ii) across reference snapshots, the dual-branch temporal context integration module fuses information from all available and nearby time points into a temporal representation, which is then decoded with learnable cell-generation seeds to predict the target distribution. Extensive experiments demonstrate that scChronos improves both interpolation-style recovery and extrapolation-style forecasting compared with state-of-the-art methods. Beyond reducing distributional discrepancy, scChronos better preserves developmental topology and maintains cell-type-specific marker and pathway programs. 
                   
                   
                     Availability 
                     The code and data are available at https://github.com/yjs193/scChronos and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20933283.

title: CRISPR-HAWK: haplotype- and variant-aware guide design toolkit for CRISPR-Cas
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Motivation 
                     Current CRISPR guide RNA design tools rely on reference genomes, overlooking how genetic variation impacts editing outcomes. As genome editing advances toward clinical applications, incorporating population diversity becomes essential for ensuring therapeutic efficacy across diverse populations. 
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     We present CRISPR-HAWK, a framework integrating individual- and population-scale variants and haplotypes into gRNA design. Analyzing therapeutic targets across 79 648 genomes reveals that genetic variants substantially alter guide performance. For the clinically approved sickle cell disease therapeutic guide targeting BCL11A, we identify haplotypes that completely abolish predicted cutting activity. Across seven therapeutic loci, 82.5% of guides contain variants modifying on-target activity. Variants also create novel protospacer adjacent motif sites generating individual-specific guides invisible to reference-based design. These findings demonstrate that variant-aware selection is critical for equitable genome editing. 
                   
                   
                     Availability 
                     CRISPR-HAWK is available at https://github.com/pinellolab/CRISPR-HAWK and https://github.com/InfOmics/CRISPR-HAWK.

title: Autoimmunity induced by epigenome alteration affecting thymic Treg cell development
abstract:
Methyl-CpG-binding domain protein 3 (MBD3), an essential component of the nucleosome remodeling and deacetylase (NuRD) complex, controls chromatin accessibility at lineage-specific transcriptional enhancers and promoters during hematopoietic cell differentiation. Here, we have shown that MBD3 deficiency in the T cell compartment resulted in spontaneous development of T cell–mediated multiorgan autoimmune diseases including fatal autoimmune myocarditis. The MBD3-deficient mice notably showed a significant reduction of CD25
                     + 
                    Foxp3
                     + 
                    regulatory T (Treg) cells in both the thymus and periphery without much affecting the development and function of conventional T (Tconv) cells. Mixed bone marrow (BM) chimeras reconstituted with wild-type and MBD3-deficient BM revealed a cell-intrinsic defect in thymic Treg cell lineage differentiation in MBD3-deficient cells. Transcriptional, phenotypic, and functional analyses of thymocyte subsets further revealed that MBD3 deficiency particularly affected the activation of a Treg-specific enhancer of the
                     Il2ra 
                    gene encoding CD25, hence impaired CD25 expression in immature CD4 single-positive thymocytes (ImCD4SP) but not in peripheral T cells. The impairment markedly limited thymic Treg precursor cell generation and substantially reduced overall thymic Treg cell output. By contrast, MBD3 deficiency scarcely impacted the TGF-β/IL-2-dependent in vitro Treg cell generation from Tconv cells. Thus, Treg-specific developmental properties such as high IL-2/CD25 dependency of their thymic differentiation may render them more sensitive than Tconv cells to epigenetic changes of the whole T cell compartment. The results provide a mechanistic basis by which general epigenomic alterations in the T cell compartment can be causative of autoimmune and other immunological diseases through selectively affecting thymic Treg cell development.

title: Convergent genome streamlining accompanies independent miniaturization in the world’s smallest fishes
abstract: Miniaturization, the reduction of adult body size to an extreme degree, has evolved repeatedly across vertebrates. Yet its genomic underpinnings remain poorly understood. Cypriniformes, the most species-rich order of freshwater fishes, contains multiple miniaturized lineages that have evolved via contrasting developmental processes. Proportioned dwarfs are tiny-bodied but otherwise morphologically similar to larger relatives, while progenetic miniatures exhibit developmental truncation and retain larval-like anatomical features into adulthood. Using a new time-calibrated phylogeny of 309 cypriniform species and comparative genomic analyses of 33 high-quality genome assemblies, we investigated the evolutionary history and genomic correlates of miniaturization across this order. Ancestral state reconstruction revealed multiple independent origins of both miniature types, with reversals to the nonminiature state rarely recovered and miniature origins nonrandomly distributed across the phylogeny. The origins of the two types of miniatures differed in their timing. Progenetic miniatures arose predominantly in the Eocene whereas proportioned dwarfs arose mainly within the Miocene period. Genome size variation across Cypriniformes has been overwhelmingly driven by polyploidy. However, progenetic miniatures showed a directionally consistent, though nonsignificant, trend toward genome size reduction. Comparative genomic analyses revealed that all three independently evolved progenetic miniature lineages share convergent signatures of repeat loss alongside genome-wide intron shortening, patterns absent in proportioned dwarfs. Our study provides the broadest evidence to date that progenetic miniaturization, despite independent origins, is underpinned by predictable structural genomic changes, revealing a fundamental link between developmental truncation and genome architecture in vertebrates.

title: Ice-ray pentagonal packing of pseudo-fivefold helices
abstract:
While fivefold point symmetry is common in nature, fivefold spatial symmetry is seldom observed. Regular pentagons cannot tile a plane without leaving voids, and even the densest “ice-ray” packing is exceptionally rare. Fivefold helices are equally elusive. We report a small molecule that self-assembles into hydrogen-bonded pseudo-fivefold helices and adopts an ice-ray pentagonal packing motif over crystallographic length scales using peripheral disorder that partially occupies regions that would otherwise be void in an ideal pentagonal tessellation. The resulting structure exhibits weak and nondirectional interhelical interactions within the (
                     bc 
                    ) plane and comparatively strong and directional intrahelical hydrogen bonding along the
                     a 
                    axis. This structural anisotropy gives rise to single crystals with large aspect ratios and distinct mechanical behavior. This realization of two rare structural motifs within a single crystal shows the capability of simple organic molecules to form complex structures and highlights an untapped potential for symmetry engineering in molecular solids through the interplay of intermolecular interactions with pronounced differences in strength and directionality.

title: Shading enhances Se accumulation in tea leaves through promoting CsMYB7-like-mediated conversion of Se (VI) to Se (IV)
abstract:
Limited selenium (Se) accumulation in agricultural products contributes to widespread dietary Se deficiency, posing a global nutritional threat. Efficient agronomic strategies to enhance Se biofortification in crops are still lacking. Here, we reveal the synergistic effects of shading and Se nanoparticles application on Se biofortification in tea leaves. Field experiments demonstrate that shading enhances Se accumulation in tea leaves under sufficient Se supply, through activating Se metabolism pathway. We identify CsAPR1 functions at the early stage of Se assimilation, catalyzing the reduction of Se (VI). The transcription of
                     CsAPR1 
                    is activated by CsMYB7-like and is further promoted by shading through interaction with CsbHLH70. Under sunlight, CsHY5 competes with CsbHLH70 for binding to CsMYB7-like, thereby attenuating CsMYB7-like-mediated transcription of
                     CsAPR1 
                    and suppressing Se accumulation in tea plants. Our findings reveal the molecular mechanisms underlying shade-induced enhancement of Se biofortification, offering insights and strategies for Se-enriched crop production.

LoL-align: sensitive and fast probabilistic protein structure alignment
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                    The ubiquitous availability of protein structures permits replacing sequence alignment with more accurate and sensitive structure alignment algorithms. LoL-align maximizes a local log-odds score for proteins to be homologous, given their intra-protein
                     C

Engineered TYK2 dependence enables myeloid-selective IL-10 receptor agonism
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                    Interleukin-10 (IL-10) is a central anti-inflammatory cytokine that suppresses immune responses in myeloid cells but can also activate T cells, limiting its therapeutic use in chronic inflammatory diseases owing to narrow efficacy windows and dose-limiting toxicities
                     1–5 
                    . Here we show that myeloid and T cells differ in their dependence on JAK-family kinase pairing for IL-10 signalling and function. We took advantage of this differential kinase dependence to engineer a tetravalent nanobody-based myeloid-selective IL-10 receptor agonist (msIL-10R agonist) that fully recapitulates IL-10’s potent suppression of monocytes, macrophages and dendritic cells while avoiding stimulation of T cells. Cryo-electron microscopy structural analysis reveals a distinct receptor cross-linking geometry of the msIL-10R agonist compared with native IL-10 family cytokines. This tetravalent architecture renders signalling strictly TYK2-dependent and highly sensitive to IL-10Rα and IL-10Rβ receptor abundance, thereby conferring selective activity in myeloid cells. This msIL-10R agonist reduces inflammation in humanized mouse models of lipopolysaccharide challenge, delayed-type hypersensitivity and colitis. A humanized version exhibits IgG-like pharmacokinetics, sustained receptor occupancy and durable myeloid suppression up to 30 days without T cell activation or haematological toxicities in non-human primates. These findings establish a geometry-based strategy for achieving cell-type-selective cytokine signalling and identify the msIL-10R agonist as a therapeutic candidate for myeloid-driven inflammatory diseases, including inflammatory bowel diseases.

Sexual dimorphism in epidermal stem cell dynamics
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                    The epidermis is a stratified epithelium comprising proliferative basal cells and differentiated suprabasal cells that are continuously renewed throughout life. Conflicting theories have been proposed regarding the heterogeneity of the basal cell layer, with some studies proposing that all proliferative cells have self-renewal potential during homeostasis
                     1–5 
                    . Meanwhile, others posit a model in which stem cell differentiation occurs through an intermediate transit-amplifying-like progenitor state with strictly limited proliferative potential
                     6–10 
                    . Here, to determine the heterogeneity and pattern of cell fate, we performed intravital time-lapse imaging to track the fate of lineage-labelled cells in the skin interfollicular epidermis. Results from quantitative analyses of clonal dynamics support a two-compartment model of epidermal homeostasis, whereby basal cells are organized in a stem cell–transit-amplifying cell hierarchy. Critical to these conclusions was the discovery of sexual dimorphism in epidermal fate, with female mice showing a highly synchronized pattern of cell division, differentiation and delamination that contributes to accelerated wound healing. Single-cell RNA sequencing, transcriptional profiling and clonal analyses of castrated mice revealed that male sex hormones promote stem cell differentiation and delamination. In summary, our study provides insight into the functional identity of the stem cell population and identifies sex-specific differences in the regulation of epidermal stem cells and transit-amplifying cell fate.

title: Early tetrapod neck mobility modelled using an extant analogue
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                    Tetrapods arose from lobe-finned fishes with a notochord-dominated axial column
                     1–3 
                    . During this transition, the skull became separated from the shoulder girdle
                     4–6 
                    , giving rise to a neck region. This head–shoulder separation has generated hypotheses suggesting that neck mobility increased during the origin of tetrapods, facilitating the ecological transition towards more terrestrial habitats
                     4,5,7–9 
                    . However, incompletely co-ossified vertebral components
                     10 
                    have posed a challenge to modelling the mobility of these early tetrapod necks. Here we used material tests on the similarly configured axial columns of sturgeon to predict the capacities of the tetrapod neck region for lateral flexion, extension and rotation across the tetrapod stem. Our model indicates that the soft tissue-dominated axial column was surprisingly rigid, despite lacking co-ossified vertebral components. We estimate that most stem tetrapods could move their heads less than 6° laterally and less than 3° dorsally but could not rotate them. Notably, mobility did not shift in conjunction with the head–shoulder separation that occurred between the origin of tristichopterids (represented by
                     Eusthenopteron 
                    ) and that of more crownward stem tetrapods. Therefore, mobility in the tetrapod neck did not serve as a functional driver of head–shoulder separation. Instead, forelimb-driven locomotion, implicated in early tetrapods
                     11–14 
                    , provides a better functional explanation for the head–shoulder separation.

A microexon regulatory code reveals autism-linked genetic variation
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                    Neuronal microexons are a highly conserved class of alternative splicing events enriched in genes with critical functions in nervous system biology
                     1,2 
                    . Microexon splicing is often disrupted in the brains of autistic individuals, and mice with microexon deficiencies display autism-like phenotypes
                     1,3,4 
                    . However, the full landscape of microexons is not known, and the impact of genetic variation on these exons has not been systematically investigated. Here, through extensive transcriptome profiling, we detect hundreds of new microexons, including many with neuronal subtype-specific splicing patterns, and others that activate nonsense-mediated mRNA decay. Using machine learning, we define a sequence code predictive of neuronally spliced microexons and use this to identify critical regulatory elements surrounding the expanded microexon repertoire. This code further reveals genomic variants predicted to alter microexon splicing in individuals affected by autism, with rare variants having the strongest estimated impact. These variants are mostly detected in idiopathic individuals and are associated with autism status. They also converge on synaptic and other autism-linked genes, as well as genes not previously linked to autism. Our results collectively define an expanded repertoire of microexons, delineate their regulatory code, and pinpoint variants predicted to affect their splicing, with implications for the disruption of functions central to neuronal biology and brain disorders.

Competing mechanisms toughen bcc binary and medium-entropy alloys at 20 K
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                    Plastic deformation in body-centred cubic (bcc) metals and alloys is conventionally mediated by screw dislocations. Their temperature-sensitive motion is attributed to a steep rise in strength with decreasing temperature that constricts plastic zones at crack tips, leading to a ductile-to-brittle transition
                     1 
                    . Here we evaluated the mechanical properties of group IV–V bcc refractory alloys with similar electronic structures at 20 K and found that these materials instead exhibit a plateau in tensile yield strength and fracture toughness as a function of temperature, with no apparent ductile-to-brittle transition. This behaviour arises from the global activation of twinning and an ω-phase transformation, which nucleate dislocations at interfaces before global dislocation motion. The initial mechanism is temperature insensitive and controls yielding, thereby preventing a crack-tip plastic zone from constricting with decreasing temperature.

abstract: A short summary: Fast3VmrMLM, which considers all genetic effects and controls for all polygenic backgrounds, is a computationally efficient algorithm for large-scale marker-pair epistasis GWAS in sizable populations, integrating genome-wide pairwise scanning, machine learning, and big-data techniques. It outperformed plink, FaST-LMM, REMMA, and Next-Gen GWAS, achieving higher power and lower false-positives, identifying experimentally supported gene-by-gene interactions, and advancing genetic network construction and breeding-by-design.

title: SMXL neofunctionalization and small RNAs underlie the recent evolution of a plant sex-determining system in Sapindaceae
abstract: Using the dioecious Sapindaceae species Eurycorymbus cavaleriei, we identify a Y-linked non-coding allele, SUNMAO, that promotes male flower development by producing small RNAs that silence the X-linked SUN allele. In females, SUN and the HD-ZIP transcription factor KUN form a positive regulatory loop that represses anther development, and this regulatory module is conservated in monoecious litchi. Our findings establish a mechanistic framework for understanding flower sex differentiation and the evolution of dioecy in Sapindaceae.

title: A premitotic polarity program patterns the grass leaf epidermis
abstract: Korosteleva et al. show that premitotic polarization of BdPOLAR-like1 regulates cell-size asymmetry during early transverse patterning divisions in the developing grass leaf epidermis. Subsequently, a postmitotic, independent polarity module enforces cell fate asymmetry. Together, these two polarity modules ensure the formation of the short-long epidermal pattern typical of grasses.

title: A North American mycorrhizal fungus displays zinc tolerance intraspecific variation and protects pines from zinc toxicity
abstract: Fletcher et al. show that zinc tolerance in the mycorrhizal fungus Suillus tomentosus is a polygenic, constitutive trait decoupled from population structure or soil zinc levels. The fungus also protects pine seedlings from zinc toxicity, buffering its host against a widespread environmental stress.

title: Encrypting the message: Bacterium turns host RNA into a target
abstract: Pathogenic bacteria are remarkably inventive when it comes to manipulating their hosts. In this issue of Cell Host & Microbe, McCaffrey et al. identify a previously uncharacterized bacterial effector from Legionella pneumophila that modifies not host proteins but messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) to dampen the host inflammatory response.

title: Pleiotropic roles of microbial bile acid metabolism in intestinal health and diseases
abstract: Qi et al. review advances in diverse microbe-mediated modifications of bile acids (BAs) and the development of AI-assisted pipelines for discovering metabolic reactions. They examine microbiota-BA interactions and the multifaceted immunomodulatory effects of BAs in intestinal diseases, offering a roadmap for BA-based preventative and therapeutic strategies.

title: Plant virus-derived siRNAs stay a step ahead of viral short-range spread
abstract: Whether mobile virus-derived siRNAs can pre-immunize uninfected plant tissues has been a long-standing assumption in plant biology. In this issue, Albertini et al. demonstrate that they indeed establish an AGO1-dependent immune zone of adjacent uninfected short-range cells, and this mobile pre-immunization is impacted by viral suppressors of RNA silencing.

title: Mutant KRAS favors a microbe that signals back
abstract: Tumor genetics and the microbiome both shape colorectal cancer, but their reciprocal interplay remains poorly defined. In this issue of Cell Host & Microbe, Jiao et al. show that mutant KRAS favors Bacteroides acidifaciens, which signals back through a SusF-ARHGEF2 axis to reinforce RAS-MAPK signaling.

title: When microbial biofilms build kidney stones
abstract: Qi et al. identify Corynebacterium glucuronolyticum-like bacteria as urinary pathobionts that promote calcium oxalate crystallization through two complementary mechanisms: degradation of the crystallization inhibitor hippuric acid and biofilm-mediated crystal aggregation. The work reframes microbiome contributions to stones as discrete, targetable microbial functions rather than generalized dysbiosis.

title: A microbial signal rewires the adipose-ovary dialogue
abstract: In this issue of Cell Host & Microbe, Chen et al. show that a gut microbial metabolite reprograms adipose ceramide metabolism to influence ovarian function. By placing adipose tissue between microbial and reproductive signaling, the study reveals how inter-organ communication couples the metabolic and ovarian dimensions of polycystic ovary syndrome.

title: Candidozyma auris turns skin immunity to its advantage
abstract: Skin colonization is central to Candidozyma auris success as a healthcare-associated pathogen. In a recent Science paper, Merrill et al. show that during skin colonization, C. auris occupies hair follicles and exposes chitin, which is associated with induction of IFNγ responses that remodel follicular keratinocytes to promote fungal persistence.

title: From blunt to precision: Engineering microbiome therapeutics against cancer
abstract: Two recent papers in Cell Host & Microbe move microbiome therapeutics beyond selecting “beneficial” strains. By turning bacterial surfaces into oral vaccine couriers and resident microbial metabolism into a controllable reactor, they show how location, control, and measurable output can transform the gut into a precision platform for cancer immunotherapy.

title: Sensing endoplasmic reticulum redox state by ethylene receptors
A pseudoenzyme sensor of trehalose-6-phosphate directly represses the metabolic integrator SnRK1 in plants
abstract: In Arabidopsis, pseudoenzyme class II T6P synthase functions as a T6P sensor that directly represses the master metabolic regulator SnRK1, highlighting a conserved switch that couples carbon availability to metabolic homeostasis in plants.

title:
Chrysanthemum Morifolium– 
                    Derived Nanovesicles Reduce Lactate‐Associated Histone Lactylation and Modulate Microglia‐Mediated Neuroinflammation in Sepsis‐Associated Encephalopathy
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Sepsis‐associated encephalopathy (SAE)—a complication of the central nervous system in patients with sepsis—markedly diminishes cognitive functions and is linked to hippocampal neuritis–induced injury. Plant exosome‐like nanovesicles can transport proteins, lipids, and molecular compounds between neural cells and the periphery, thereby modulating target cells. This study examined the therapeutic potential of
                     Chrysanthemum morifolium 
                    –derived exosome‐like nanovesicles (CRELNVs) in an animal model of lipopolysaccharide‐induced SAE, revealing their ability to effectively cross the blood–brain barrier, be internalized by microglia, and alleviate nerve injury and memory impairment by reducing lactate levels in microglia at the hippocampus. CRELNVs decreased lactylation levels in microglia, thus promoting the conversion of microglial cells from the detrimental M1 metabolic phenotype to the protective M2 one. Mechanistically, our finding suggest CRELNVs reduced proinflammatory cytokine release is associated with the inhibition of NF‐κB activation. Thus, CRELNVs were concluded to exert their protective effects by modulating the H3K18la/NF‐κB axis and regulate microglia‐mediated neuroinflammation by responding to the hippocampal neuritis–induced injury in SAE.

title: A Fish MDA5 Integrates Canonical RIG‐I and MDA5 Ligand Recognition
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    RIG‐I and MDA5 are cytosolic RNA sensors that recognize distinct viral ligands in mammals, yet RIG‐I has been independently lost from multiple teleost lineages. How RIG‐I‐deficient vertebrates preserve recognition of RIG‐I‐associated viral RNA remains poorly understood. Here, we show that MDA5 from the large yellow croaker (
                     Larimichthys crocea 
                    ,
                     Lc 
                    ), a teleost species lacking RIG‐I, recognizes both 5′‐triphosphate dsRNA (5′ppp‐dsRNA), the canonical ligand of RIG‐I, and long dsRNA, the classical ligand of MDA5. Its C‐terminal domain (CTD) is essential for the recognition of both ligands, with residues specifically required for sensing the 5′ppp moiety. Structural modeling, molecular dynamics simulations, and mutational validation support a model in which a flexible RNA‐capping loop in the CTD confers
                     Lc 
                    MDA5 a conformational plasticity, allowing the CTD to cap the 5′ppp‐dsRNA terminus for RIG‐I‐like recognition or orienting the CTD parallel to long‐dsRNA axis for canonical MDA5 recognition. Disruption of 5′ppp recognition impaired
                     Lc 
                    MDA5‐mediated antiviral activity against a RIG‐I‐sensitive virus. Downstream,
                     Lc 
                    MDA5 signals through an integrated MAVS–STING–TBK1/IRF3 axis to drive type I IFN responses to both RNA ligands. Our findings reveal an unexpectedly flexible architecture of vertebrate cytosolic RNA sensing in which a single RLR combines ligand‐recognition and signaling properties classically partitioned between RIG‐I and MDA5.

title: Enzyme‐Linked Cycloaddition Assay (ELCA) for Rapid, Ultra‐Sensitive Monitoring of Secreted Sialoglycoproteins
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Glycosylation of proteins is central to cell signaling, immune function, and pathogen interactions, yet existing methods for monitoring glycan changes require specialized instrumentation and primarily report on membrane‐anchored, rather than secreted, glycoproteins. Here, we present the Enzyme‐Linked Cycloaddition Assay (ELCA), a click chemistry‐based platform for ultra‐sensitive detection and semi‐quantitative analysis of secreted sialoglycoproteins.
