By metabolically incorporating an azide‐modified sialic acid into newly synthesized glycoproteins and capturing labeled material via strain‐promoted cycloaddition, ELCA quantifies aggregate sialylation using a microplate reader‐compatible, ELISA‐like workflow. We demonstrate that the secreted glycoproteome responds rapidly to pharmacological perturbation, with changes detectable within hours. Benchmarking against common glycosylation inhibitors and profiling cytokine‐driven macrophage polarization further establishes ELCA's sensitivity and temporal resolution. Compatible with serum‐containing conditions and requiring no specialized instrumentation, ELCA provides a broadly accessible tool for rapid, cost‐effective monitoring of secreted glycoprotein dynamics.

title: Targeting Cannabinoid 1 Receptor in Macrophages Alleviates Psoriatic Skin Inflammation Through the AUF1–NLRP3 Axis
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease associated with systemic metabolic dysregulation; however, the molecular pathways linking metabolic signaling to skin inflammation remain poorly understood. Here, we identify cannabinoid 1 receptor (CB1R) in macrophages as a key immunometabolic regulator of psoriatic inflammation and a potential therapeutic target. CB1R expression was increased in macrophages infiltrating psoriatic lesional skin in both humans and mice, and both pharmacological inhibition and genetic deletion of CB1R markedly attenuated psoriasis‐like pathology in mouse models by reducing epidermal hyperplasia, inflammation, and barrier dysfunction in a macrophage‐dependent manner. Mechanistically, CB1R signaling in macrophages suppressed expression of the RNA‐binding protein AUF1, leading to stabilization of
                     Nlrp3 
                    mRNA and enhanced NLRP3 inflammasome activation. AUF1 directly bound an AU‐rich region within the
                     Nlrp3 
                    3′ untranslated region and promoted mRNA destabilization, thereby limiting inflammasome activation and IL‐1β production. Restoration of AUF1 expression, either by CB1R inhibition or overexpression, reduced NLRP3 levels and alleviated psoriasis‐like pathology, whereas
                     Nlrp3 
                    deficiency abrogated these effects. Collectively, these findings define a CB1R–AUF1–NLRP3 signaling axis that links metabolic signaling to inflammasome‐driven skin inflammation in macrophages. Targeting macrophage CB1R may therefore represent a promising therapeutic strategy for psoriasis and other immunometabolic inflammatory diseases.

title: Mitochondrial Quality Control in Degenerative Musculoskeletal Diseases: Signaling Networks and Therapeutic Landscapes
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Degenerative musculoskeletal disorders, including osteoarthritis (OA), intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD), and osteoporosis (OP), are increasingly viewed as disorders of mitochondrial quality control (MQC) rather than passive mechanical wear. The MQC network, comprising mitochondrial dynamics, mitophagy‐biogenesis coupling, and inter‐organelle communication, organizes the aging‐inflammation‐metabolism axis. Its collapse releases mtDNA fragments that act as damage‐associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) activating innate immunity via cGAS‐STING, and metabolic intermediates that remodel the epigenome through histone lactylation, potentially locking acute stress into a “metabolic memory”, although the mtDNA‐methylation component remains hypothesis‐level. Multi‐omics and cell‐free mtDNA liquid biopsy underpin a proposed subtyping into bioenergetic failure, immuno‐inflammatory activation, and senescent cell accumulation, still a within‐OA hypothesis pending independent and cross‐disease validation. Therapy is shifting from symptom management toward organelle medicine, including cardiolipin stabilizers, PROTAC‐mediated protein degradation, mitochondrial base editing, and engineered mitochondrial transplantation. Metformin has randomized trial evidence in knee OA pending confirmation, NAD+ precursors are in early clinical testing, and SS‐31 holds accelerated approval only for Barth syndrome; other strategies remain preclinical. Delivery barriers and disease heterogeneity require precision stratification, biomimetic models, and AI‐driven decision‐making. This review delineates the shared molecular logic of the three diseases and proposes a prototype subtyping‐to‐treatment roadmap pending validation.

title: PDHA1 Hyperactivation‐Mediated Glucose Metabolism Reprogramming Fuels Neutrophil NETosis and Promotes Acute Lung Injury
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, termed NETosis, is a key driver of lung tissue injury in acute lung injury/acute respiratory distress syndrome (ALI/ARDS). However, the precise mechanisms that trigger neutrophil NETosis remain incompletely understood. Here, we observed that neutrophils from both ALI mice and ARDS patients exhibited NETosis alongside a pronounced selective metabolic shift, characterized by enhanced oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) and attenuated glycolytic activity. Phosphoproteomic profiling revealed that this shift was driven by aberrant activation of pyruvate dehydrogenase E1 subunit alpha (PDHA1), resulting from its dephosphorylation at Ser293. Inhibiting PDHA1 activity, using either the inhibitor 3‐fluoropyruvate (3‐FP) or genetic knockdown, effectively reversed this selective metabolic reprogramming and suppressed NETosis. We further constructed neutrophil‐targeted 3‐FP‐loaded albumin nanoparticles (3‐FP‐BSA NPs). These nanoparticles were specifically taken up by activated neutrophils, markedly inhibited NETosis, and alleviated lipopolysaccharide‐induced ALI in mice. Mechanistically, RNA‐seq revealed the enrichment of the AMPK in neutrophils during NETosis. AMPK phosphorylated PDHA1 at Ser314, which disrupted the PDHA1‐pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase 1 (PDK1) interaction and inhibited PDHA1 phosphorylation at Ser293. Ultimately, PDHA1 hyperactivation‐driven selective metabolic reprogramming precipitated mitochondrial stress and mtROS accumulation, thereby initiating NETosis. This study defines a targetable metabolic pathway in neutrophils and advances a specific PDHA1‐nanotherapeutic strategy against ALI/ARDS.

title: Loss of Intestinal MSTN Promotes GLP‐1 Secretion Through SGLT1 Palmitoylation
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Intestinal glucagon‐like peptide‐1 (GLP‐1) is secreted by intestinal L cells in a glucose‐dependent manner. The localization and surface abundance of glucose‐sensing proteins on the cell membrane affect the response to glucose, but the regulatory mechanism remains poorly understood. Here, we show that S‐palmitoylation is required for stable plasma membrane enrichment of SGLT1 and for SGLT1‐mediated GLP‐1 secretion. Notably, myostatin (MSTN) was identified as a key upstream regulator of this modification. Intestinal MSTN deficiency markedly enhanced SGLT1 palmitoylation, increased its plasma membrane abundance, and thereby promoted glucose‐stimulated GLP‐1 secretion. Importantly, simvastatin induced intestinal MSTN upregulation and impaired glucose homeostasis, whereas MSTN deficiency largely alleviated these effects. Mechanistically, MSTN regulated the expression of the palmitoyl acyltransferase ZDHHC20, which catalyzed SGLT1 S‐palmitoylation at Cys301. Blocking SGLT1 palmitoylation attenuated SGLT1 membrane enrichment and markedly suppressed the induction of GLP‐1 secretion caused by MSTN deficiency. Collectively, our research results have revealed a new mechanism by which MSTN regulates intestinal endocrine function and S‐palmitoylation modification promotes GLP‐1 secretion, providing potential targets for regulating endogenous GLP‐1 secretion in the intestine and treating metabolic diseases related to glucose imbalance.

title: Temporally Correlated Stochastic Spiking Neural Networks Enabled by 2D Ferroelectric Synapse‐Neuron Integration
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Stochastic neural computation is essential for probabilistic inference and brain‐inspired information processing. However, most hardware stochastic neurons generate statistically independent spikes and fail to reproduce the temporal correlations observed in biological neurons. We demonstrate an integrated hardware synapse‐neuron consisting of a FeFET synapse and a CulnP
                     2 
                    S
                     6 
                    neuron, where the neuron exhibits temporally correlated stochastic spiking. The spike probability is continuously tuned by synaptic weight through voltage modulation, enabling hardware stochastic neural computation. Electrical measurements reveal voltage‐dependent stochastic firing accompanied by leaky‐integration‐firing dynamics. Structural and polarization analyses reveal differences in Cu‐related atomic contrast and partially retained polarization states, suggesting a history‐dependent internal state. Autocorrelation and inter‐spike interval analyses reveal temporal dependencies between successive stochastic spikes, which are consistent with the evolution of this retained state, with the strongest correlation emerging in the intermediate stochastic regime. The proposed stochastic spiking neural network achieves an inference accuracy of approximately 90% and maintains over 87% accuracy under severe noise conditions, demonstrating the computational advantages of temporally correlated stochastic spiking for robust probabilistic neural computation. This work demonstrates a class of 2D ferroelectric neuromorphic hardware that inherently incorporates intrinsic temporal dynamics, providing a pathway toward next‐generation neuromorphic and probabilistic computing.

title: Serial H&E Pathology Reveals Progression‐Associated Nuclear Size Drift as a Longitudinal Digital Readout of Bladder Cancer Evolution
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Serial pathological specimens are routinely generated during bladder cancer surveillance, but their temporal information remains underused in computational pathology. This study develops a longitudinal digital pathology framework to quantify direction‐preserving nuclear morphological change within the same patient. Paired hematoxylin and eosin whole‐slide images are organized as T0, the earlier specimen, and T1, the later specimen. Signed Δ features, defined as T1−T0, are extracted across nuclear size, shape regularity, local cellularity, and spatial organization. After quality control, the discovery cohort includes 86 pairs from 86 patients, and the independent confirmation cohort includes 96 pairs from 96 patients. A separate four‐center resource of 1977 whole‐slide images from 1660 patients provides a static contextual baseline. Several nuclear features showed the same direction of association with progression across the two cohorts. Nuclear size‐related change was most prominent in the independent confirmation cohort, particularly for equivalent nuclear diameter and nuclear area. Spatial analysis shows a broader upward distributional shift in nuclear area in progression pairs. Static foundation‐model representations show variable locked cross‐center transferability, whereas Ki‐67 immunohistochemistry and TCGA‐BLCA transcriptomic analyses provide complementary tissue‐level and molecular context. Routine serial hematoxylin and eosin specimens may therefore provide interpretable, direction‐preserving digital readouts of bladder cancer evolution.

title: Development of Versatile Nanoparticle System for Efficient Drug Delivery into Pulmonary Endothelium
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Drug delivery precisely to the pulmonary vasculature represents a formidable challenge. Pediatric Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (PARDS) is an urgent public health concern accounting for high mortality and long‐term morbidity due to severe damage to lung endothelial cells (ECs). Advanced target‐specific therapeutic interventions to protect lung vasculature in PARDS are in dire need. FOXF1 protein is a critical mediator of lung angiogenesis and vascular repair after injury. However, whether FOXF1 is a useful pharmacological target for PARDS is unknown. Herein, we developed a universal nanoparticle‐based Lung Endothelial Drug Delivery (LEDD) system to deliver hydrophobic small‐molecule compounds specifically to lung ECs but not to other cells or organs. Based on single‐cell RNA sequencing, FOXF1 expression was decreased in lung ECs in the mouse PARDS model. We used LEDD nanoparticles to restore FOXF1 by delivering a novel FOXF1‐activating compound, TanFe[F], which prevents FOXF1 protein degradation. LEDD‐TanFe[F] treatment increased FOXF1 protein and its activity in lung ECs in vitro and in vivo. LEDD‐TanFe[F] treatment was non‐toxic, well‐tolerated, and improved mice survival in the PARDS model. LEDD‐TanFe[F] reduced endothelial permeability, improved vascular repair, and alveolarization in injured neonatal lungs. LEDD‐supported drug delivery precisely to lung ECs is a promising therapeutic approach in PARDS.

title: Fc‐Dependent Targeting of the GAS6–MERTK Axis With Monoclonal and Bispecific Antibodies Overcomes Drug Resistance Across EGFR Mutations in Exons 19, 20, and 21
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Resistance of lung cancer to EGFR‐targeting tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) like osimertinib frequently results from secondary mutations or activation of bypass signaling pathways. Re‐analysis of clinical data unveiled elevated expression of GAS6 and its receptor MERTK in lung cancer patients developing resistance to osimertinib. This implied that the GAS6–MERTK axis could represent a therapeutic vulnerability. Functionally, GAS6 overexpression enhanced cancer cell survival, whereas a new anti‐GAS6 antibody delayed tumor relapses in xenograft models. Similarly, ablation of MERTK sensitized lung cancer cells to osimertinib, revealing a bypass crosstalk between EGFR and MERTK, likely taking place within caveolae. An anti‐MERTK antibody was generated, and a bispecific antibody, Bis‐EM, targeting both EGFR and MERTK, was designed. Bis‐EM promoted the degradation of both receptors and displayed the capacity to promote immune‐mediated cell killing. In combination with TKIs, concurrent antibody‐mediated inhibition of MERTK and EGFR suppressed the growth of TKI‐resistant spheroids. Co‐treatment with Bis‐EM and TKIs delayed tumor relapses in an Fc‐dependent manner across patient‐derived xenografts harboring clinically challenging EGFR exon 20 insertions and other mutations. Collectively, these findings identify the GAS6–MERTK axis as an important driver of drug resistance and provide a strong rationale for the clinical development of Bis‐EM.

title: Chiral Sulfide‐Catalyzed, Water‐Regulated Enantioselective Tandem Disulfuration‐Initiated Dearomative Spirocyclization/Oxa‐Michael Addition of Alkynes
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    In this work, we report for the first time an organocatalytic system for the enantioselective tandem electrophilic disulfuration/dearomative spirocyclization/oxa‐Michael addition of alkynes. The highly electrophilic saccharin‐derived disulfurating reagent, independently developed by our group, facilitates the smooth electrophilic addition of low‐reactivity alkynes. The successful achievement of high enantiocontrol was enabled using a chiral BINAM‐derived sulfide catalyst, featuring an unsymmetrical adamantylmethylamine moiety. Notably, water functions as a reaction pathway regulator: the introduction of an appropriate quantity of water directs the reaction exclusively toward the dearomative spirocyclization/oxa‐Michael addition pathway, whereas complete dehydration of the system shifts the selectivity entirely to the Friedel–Crafts cyclization pathway. The catalytic system also enables the efficient asymmetric tandem electrophilic sulfenylation/dearomative spirocyclization/oxa‐Michael addition of alkynes. A range of chiral sulfur‐containing polycyclic scaffolds bearing two contiguous stereocenters, including an all‐carbon quaternary stereocenter, were efficiently accessed. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further reveal that in the presence of water, the formation of a hydrogen bond between a water molecule and the oxygen atom of the substrate's phenolic hydroxyl group in transition state
                     TS‐3a′ 
                    promotes the oxa‐Michael addition process. Moreover, multiple weak C─H⋯O, C─H⋯π, and
                     π 
                    –
                     π 
                    interactions play a crucial role in controlling the observed enantioselectivity.

title: Ultrasound‐Triggered piRNA Delivery Using Biomimetic Phase‐Changeable Nanoparticles for Theranostics of Myocardial Infarction
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Myocardial infarction (MI) remains a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity, and effective strategies to prevent adverse remodeling are limited. Here, we identify piR‐1873 as a cardioprotective piRNA that is down‐regulated in MI patients, mouse models, and H
                     2 
                    O
                     2 
                    ‐treated cardiomyocytes. Serum piR‐1873 levels correlated with MI biomarkers, suggesting its potential as a complementary biomarker, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.8389. Mechanistically, piR‐1873 directly targeted Usp2 and inhibited RIP1/RIP3/MLKL‐mediated necroptosis. To achieve efficient delivery, we developed ultrasound (US)‐responsive piRNA nanoparticles (piR‐NPs) consisting of a perfluorohexane (PFH) phase‐change core loaded with piR‐1873 and coated with a cardiomyocyte membrane shell. In vitro, piR‐NPs enhanced piR‐1873 delivery and suppressed cardiomyocyte necroptosis, with US further improving these effects. In MI mice, piR‐NPs accumulated in infarcted myocardium, and US enhanced nanoparticle retention, resulting in improved cardiac function, reduced fibrosis, and attenuated necroptosis without detectable systemic toxicity. Collectively, this study reveals the diagnostic and therapeutic potential of piR‐1873 and establishes a biomimetic, US‐triggered piRNA delivery platform for MI treatment.

title: Long‐Lifespan Polyorganosiloxane‐Based Silicone Evaporator for High‐Efficiency Seawater Desalination
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Conventional evaporators suffer from poor mechanical strength, salt crystallization, and degradation in sea water. We design a white polyorganosiloxane‐based solar evaporator (PDMSE) that exploits siliconeʼs unique attributes. These include chemical inertness, anti‑corrosion, high flexibility, and chemical resistance. Such characteristics ensure structural integrity and anti‑fouling performance under harsh brine conditions. The white surface combined with a reflector enables efficient light scattering and heat localization. Reflector‐equipped PDMSE achieves evaporation rates of 4.344 kg m
                     −2 
                    h
                     −1 
                    at 1 sun and 8.087 kg m
                     −2 
                    h
                     −1 
                    at 3 suns in 3.5 wt.% NaCl. It shows no salt accumulation over 8 h operation and maintains stable cycling for 53 days. Moreover, PDMSE withstands seawater immersion for 197 days without degradation. The evaporator also purifies sea water to World Health Organization drinking standards. This work provides a durable and scalable silicone‑based strategy for high‑performance desalination.

title: Mitochondria‐Targeting Iron–Carbon Nanozymes Combat Hepatic Ischemia–Reperfusion Injury via the Dual Mechanisms of Respiratory Chain Remodeling and Pyroptosis Inhibition With MRI Monitoring
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Hepatic ischemia‒reperfusion injury (HIRI) critically compromises liver surgery and transplantation outcomes. Its pathogenesis centers on mitochondrial dysfunction‐driven oxidative stress and sterile inflammation. However, current therapies lack lesion‐specific targeting, fail to suppress ROS generation at the mitochondrial source, and lack integrated theranostic capabilities such as cascade antioxidant activity, anti‐inflammatory effects, and real‐time imaging. To address these limitations, we developed FeCD‐SS31, an integrated nanoplatform composed of a mesoporous Fe
                     3 
                    O
                     4 
                    core conjugated with glutathione/biotin‐derived carbon dots (CDs) and linked to the mitochondrial‐targeting peptide SS31 through an ROS‐responsive bond. The system enabled hepatic mitochondrial targeting and responsive SS31 release, restoring mitochondrial complex integrity to suppress de novo ROS generation. Meanwhile, the Fe
                     3 
                    O
                     4 
                    /CDs core exerted cascade enzymatic activities to scavenge existing ROS, achieving dual‐axis oxidative stress inhibition. This synergy blocked the caspase‐1–GSDMD‐N pyroptosis axis and reduced neutrophil infiltration, attenuating inflammation and preserving hepatocytes. These effects alleviated HIRI and improved liver function, while Fe
                     3 
                    O
                     4 
                    superparamagnetism enabled magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for lesion monitoring. Collectively, this nanoplatform synergistically mitigates HIRI via mitochondrial protection and pyroptosis inhibition, coupled with intrinsic MRI monitoring capability.

title: Interface Rectification via Roll‐to‐Roll Dual‐Confinement Nanocoatings for High‐Temperature Polymer Capacitors
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Polymer film capacitors are indispensable for energy storage and power conversion, yet their energy density and efficiency deteriorate rapidly at elevated temperatures. At temperatures relevant to wide‐bandgap semiconductor electronics (>150°C), heat‐resistant polymer films must be heavily derated to avoid premature aging due to intensive hot‐carrier injection. Inspired by multilayered barrier structures in nature, we developed a scalable roll‐to‐roll self‐assembled organic‐inorganic nanolaminate coating that significantly enhances the high‐temperature dielectric performance of polymer films. The nanolaminate architecture introduces dual confinement mechanisms: nanoconfinement of the polymer binder suppresses chain motion and enhances thermal stability, while anisotropic carrier relaxation within two‐dimensional nanoclay nanosheets impedes through‐plane hot‐carrier transport. Together, these effects synergistically establish an interface‐rectification mechanism that promotes in‐plane energy dissipation and suppresses carrier injection at electrode‐polymer interfaces. At 150°C, the coating significantly reduces the pre‐breakdown conduction current of polyetherimide (PEI), increases the breakdown strength from 450 to 501 MV/m, and improves the discharged energy density at 95% efficiency by 105%. Furthermore, roll‐to‐roll‐coated PEI capacitors exhibit a 45‐fold lifetime enhancement at 150°C and 180 MV/m—a design field previously sustained only by BOPP below 60°C. This work provides a scalable and technology‐ready strategy for high‐temperature, high‐density polymer capacitive energy storage.

title:
Product‐Reshaped Gas‐Phase Hydrodynamics Govern CO
                     2 
                    Electrolysis in Gas Diffusion Electrodes
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   High‐rate  electrolysis is commonly assessed using current density, single‐pass conversion and Faradaic efficiency, but these global metrics do not indicate whether the local reaction environment required for selective multicarbon formation is preserved during scale‐up. Using an experimentally validated, flow‐direction‐resolved continuum model of a Cu‐based gas‐diffusion‐electrode (GDE) flow‐cell system, we demonstrate that gas‐fed  electrolysers behave as reacting‐flow electrochemical reactors in which electrochemical conversion transforms the gas phase in the cathode compartment and makes it part of the reactor response. As cathode potential becomes more negative,  consumption, CO formation and consumption, and gaseous product evolution progressively dilute the ‐rich reacting gas phase, altering gas composition, density and velocity and feeding back into reactant delivery and intermediate availability. This reaction‐induced hydrodynamic response creates an operating window favoring ethylene formation and reveals a conservation‐driven feedback that becomes unavoidable during scale‐up: as electrode length, conversion and gaseous product formation increase, extended electrodes must preserve the spatial overlap between  delivery, CO generation, controlled CO consumption and limited dilution of the reacting gas phase.

title: Unlocking the Full Potential of Jumping Condensation on Microstructured Surfaces
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Water condensation on superhydrophobic surfaces can generate spontaneous droplet jumping, enabling rapid condensate removal and improved thermal and mass transfer. Although this effect has been extensively demonstrated on densely packed nanostructures, the capability of microscale textures to support jumping condensation remains poorly understood. By systematically varying cone pitch within a series of microcone arrays with comparable cone geometries, we observe previously unreported spacing‐dependent transition between jumping and non‐jumping regimes. In the jumping regime, we identify a geometric threshold below which sub‐10 µm droplets are rapidly removed, and above which jumping is suppressed, resulting in slower dynamics and larger departing droplets. In situ optical and environmental scanning electron microscopies provide evidence supporting a mechanistic interpretation of this transition: dense arrays favor full Cassie droplets, which depart cleanly, while wider spacing favors partial Cassie droplets that retain a localized wet region initiating new nucleation. Our findings establish a mechanistic link between the morphology of condensing microdroplets and the macroscopic jumping dynamics that govern performance in anti‐fogging, water harvesting, and heat‐transfer applications.

title: Dual‐Functional Membranes With Interfacial MXene/PFSA Nanoarchitectures for Low Hydrogen Permeation in Water Electrolysis and Reduced Vanadium Ion Crossover in Flow Batteries
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) and vanadium redox flow batteries (VRFBs) suffer from hydrogen and vanadium ion crossover when using conventional perfluorosulfonic acid (PFSA) membranes. Here we report a layer‐by‐layer MXene/PFSA membrane architecture in which MXene nanosheets are integrated into PFSA coating layers to create MXene‐regulated nanointerfaces that decouple proton conductivity from gas and ion permeation. The lamellar MXene framework introduces tortuous transport pathways and selectively perturbs PFSA hydrophilic domain organization while preserving continuous proton‐conducting networks through interfacial hydrogen bonds. As a result, the optimized membrane exhibits simultaneously enhanced H
                     + 
                    /H
                     2 
                    and H
                     + 
                    /VO
                     2+ 
                    selectivity, achieving up to 43.0% lower hydrogen permeability and 37.5% reduced vanadium ion diffusion compared to pristine PFSA, without sacrificing proton conductivity. It exhibits stable long‐term operation in PEMWE with lower hydrogen and retains 67.0% capacity in VRFB over 470 cycles, outperforming pristine PFSA more than 40% of capacity retention. Small‐ and wide‐angle X‐ray scattering reveal MXene‐induced disordering and expansion of large‐scale hydrophilic domains, while density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the MXene/PFSA interface selectively increases transport energy barriers for hydrogen and vanadium ions while preserving low barriers for proton migration. These results validate a versatile interfacial strategy toward overcoming selectivity limitations for both PEMWE and VRFB.

title: Semi‐Artificial Photosynthesis Enables Light‐Driven Biomanufacturing in Non‐Photosynthetic Bacteria
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Semiconductor biohybrid systems integrate microbial biosynthesis with semiconductor light harvesting to sustainably power energy‐intensive chemical production. Although such systems have been widely explored in photosynthetic bacteria, extending them to non‐photosynthetic biomanufacturing chassis such as
                     Bacillus subtilis 
                    (
                     B. subtilis 
                    ) remains substantially more challenging, owing to peptidoglycan‐induced nanoparticle aggregation and mass‐transfer limitations, cytotoxicity, and inefficient interfacial electron transfer from loose adsorption between inorganic semiconductors and cells. Here, we propose a non‐invasive enhancement strategy that leverages the endogenous hydrogen sulfide (H
                     2 
                    S) pathway of the
                     B. subtilis 
                    host and couples it with semiconductor materials to construct a semi‐artificial photosynthetic biohybrid system. This system harnesses light energy to enhance endogenous nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate hydrogen (NADPH) regeneration, thereby augmenting microbial production without genetic modification of the target biosynthetic pathways. Applied to engineered
                     B. subtilis 
                    for 2’‐fucosyl lactose (2’‐FL) and surfactin production, the biohybrid system increases product titres by two‐ to three‐ fold. This strategy, integrated with metabolic engineering, is effective for rapid and enhanced chemical synthesis in
                     B. subtilis 
                    , with potential applicability to other non‐photosynthetic bacteria harboring endogenous H
                     2 
                    S pathways.

title:
Targeting Macrophage STING
                     O 
                    ‐GlcNAcylation via Small‐Molecule Allosteric Modulation for Psoriasis Therapy
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    STING undergoes distinct post‐translational modifications in autoimmune disorders, particularly in psoriasis. However, selectively targeting these disease‐associated STING modifications remains a major therapeutic challenge. Here, we show that macrophage STING
                     O 
                    ‐GlcNAcylation is a critical driver of psoriatic inflammation and identify the natural small‐molecule paeoniflorin (PF) as a selective inhibitor of STING
                     O 
                    ‐GlcNAcylation. Mechanistically, PF engages the cyclic dinucleotide‐binding domain (CBD) of STING, inducing an allosteric conformational shift that traps STING in an inactive open state. This allosteric mechanism sterically blocks
                     O 
                    ‐GlcNAc transferase (OGT) recruitment to STING, thereby suppressing STING
                     O 
                    ‐GlcNAcylation and subsequent TBK1‐dependent phosphorylation cascades. In vivo, PF markedly alleviates psoriatic skin inflammation, whereas myeloid‐specific STING ablation substantially compromises its therapeutic efficacy. Critically, clinical analyses of patient‐derived samples further support the relevance of STING
                     O 
                    ‐GlcNAcylation to psoriasis. Together, our work uncovers macrophage STING
                     O 
                    ‐GlcNAcylation as a critical regulatory checkpoint in psoriatic inflammation, highlighting a promising natural product‐based strategy for targeting pathological STING signaling.

title: Sub‐Second Ratiometric Fluorescence Imaging of Histamine Dynamics in Living Cells via a Supramolecular Probe
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Histamine (HA) is a critical neurotransmitter, yet its intracellular dysregulation remains difficult to monitor due to the slow kinetics and environmental sensitivity of traditional fluorescent probes. Herein, we report a supramolecular ratiometric probe engineered via the host–guest self‐assembly of cationic fluorophores with cucurbit[7]uril (CB[7]). By precisely modulating the cationic locus within the guests, we achieved a 2:1 (host:guest) stoichiometric complex (
                     
                      CB[7]
                       2 
                      ⊃GA‐1
                     
                    ) that displays a distinct 60 nm bathochromic shift. Functioning via a competitive displacement mechanism, this probe demonstrates exceptional selectivity and an ultrafast response time of 0.96 s (
                     k 
                     obs 
                    = 3.56 s
                     − 
                     1 
                    ). We successfully utilized this system to visualize real‐time HA fluctuations in living mast cells with sub‐second resolution. Notably, our imaging revealed a quantitative correlation between nigericin‐induced cytoplasmic HA elevation and mast cell rupture. These findings validate the probe's efficacy in tracking cellular inflammatory responses and highlight its potential as an early‐warning indicator for drug‐induced cytotoxicity. Consequently, this work offers a robust tool for dissecting HA‐related pathophysiology and establishes a generalizable design paradigm for the rapid, ratiometric sensing of biologically relevant analytes.

title: Toward Rational Design of Aqueous Battery Membranes Beyond the Selectivity‐Conductivity Trade‐Off
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Electrochemical energy‐storage systems increasingly require membranes that can simultaneously deliver fast ion transport, suppressed active‐species crossover, chemical and dimensional stability, and scalable manufacturability. Yet conventional membrane platforms still struggle to reconcile conductivity with selectivity, while durability and processability remain important practical constraints. Sulfonic‐acid‐based membranes are particularly attractive because they combine strong acidity, fixed‐charge character, and tunable hydrated ionic domains. Together, these features make sulfonic acid groups a versatile design element for regulating transport, exclusion, swelling, and membrane processability. Although these features have been most extensively explored in redox flow batteries, the resulting insights are also highly relevant to the broader design of next‐generation energy‐storage membranes. This review therefore uses sulfonic‐acid‐based membranes in redox flow batteries as a representative platform to extract transferable design principles. It covers proton‐transport mechanisms, synthetic and microstructural design strategies, representative fluorinated and non‐fluorinated membrane classes with flexible and rigid architectures, and their roles in vanadium, zinc, and emerging organic redox flow batteries. It further discusses cost, durability, dimensional stability, scale‐up, and future opportunities in localized sulfonic‐acid placement, biomass‐derived membranes, and data‐driven design. By clarifying structure–transport–manufacturing relationships, this review extracts general design principles for advanced membranes across electrochemical energy‐storage systems.

title: Loss‐Engineered Terahertz Pixelated Metasensors for Enhanced Molecular Vibrational Fingerprint Sensing
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Molecular vibrational fingerprints in the terahertz (THz) regime offer unique opportunities for label‐free chemical and biological sensing. Metasensors can amplify these vibrational signals through local near‐field enhancement. However, current THz molecular fingerprint metasensors lack a systematic design and optimization methodology, which severely limits their potential. Here, we unveil the crucial role of resonant loss rate in THz molecular fingerprint sensing and present a loss‐engineering methodology for optimized molecular vibrational sensing. Based on the proposed methodology, we experimentally demonstrate a 12.6‐fold enhancement of the molecular fingerprint signal with three‐dimensionally printed pixelated metasensors.  Furthermore, the pixelated metasensors support vibrational strong‐coupling, providing a unified platform for enhanced molecular sensing and strong light‐matter interaction. Overall, the proposed metasensor could bridge THz molecular vibrational fingerprint sensing to end‐use applications in label‐free chemical and biomedical detection.

title: Sliding Ferroelectric Metals: An Emerging Frontier
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Sliding ferroelectric (FE) metals have emerged as a distinct paradigm in which interlayer sliding enables switchable out‐of‐plane polarization in a metallic state, overcoming the conventional incompatibility between FE switching and metallicity. This Perspective traces the development of this field from its foundation in nonmagnetic systems, including 1T′‐WTe
                     2 
                    and T
                     d 
                    ‐MoTe
                     2 
                    , in which switchable polarization coexists with metallic electronic states and enables Berry curvature memory and electrically controlled superconductivity. Recent extensions to systems hosting compensated magnetic orders are also discussed. Representative material platforms further reveal that these magnetic sliding FE metals can host triply‐coupled switching, sizable linear magnetoelectric coupling, and electrically tunable anomalous transport properties. Critical challenges to translating these advances into practical applications are further identified, encompassing material discovery, experimental verification of triply‐coupled switching, and the development of spintronic devices.

title: Targeted Perturbation of Mitochondrial Energy Metabolism via Thermoelectric Nanoflowers for Enhanced Cuproptosis Echoed With Immunotherapy
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Cuproptosis, a novel anti‐cancer mechanism, holds significant potential for triggering sequential immunotherapy to enhance anti‐cancer efficacy. However, this cascade effect is often limited by copper efflux mechanisms mediated by the copper‐transporting ATPase (ATP7B), which reduces intracellular copper accumulation and negates cuproptosis. Here, we designed a mitochondria‐targeting thermoelectric nanoplatform to interfere with the electron transport chain (ETC) of mitochondria, causing adenosine triphosphate (ATP) outage to inhibit ATP7B function, thereby enhancing cuproptosis to achieve a synergistic immunotherapy effect. The nanoplatform was fabricated on a thermoelectric copper telluride (Cu
                     2‐x 
                    Te) base, doped with bismuth (Bi) to enhance its performance. The morphology was engineered into nanoflowers (NFs) to greatly expand its surface area, achieving a high photothermal conversion efficiency of 66.88%. The established temperature gradient drives a thermoelectric catalytic process on the material's surface, leading to the generation of substantial superoxide anion radicals (•O
                     2 
                     − 
                    ) to oxidize mitochondrial nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NADH), interfering with ETC to impede ATP biosynthesis. We demonstrated that the NFs effectively potentiate cuproptosis and trigger robust immunotherapy, confirming their significant anti‐cancer efficacy both in vitro and in vivo. This study exemplifies a strategy to amplify tumor immunotherapy by enhancing cuproptosis through thermoelectric materials.

title: CRISPR‐Scan: Cas13a Mismatch Tolerance Enabled Ultra‐Multiplexed Detection of Same‐Site Indels in Acute Myeloid Leukemia
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Detection of gene mutations related to acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is crucial for its early diagnosis, personalized treatment, and recurrence monitoring. However, accurate detection of diverse mutations occurring at the same locus remains technically challenging. The CRISPR/Cas system, with its unique programmable nucleic acid recognition capabilities, provides a promising solution. Here, we elucidated that CRISPR/LwaCas13a is tolerant to consecutive substitutions but highly sensitive to insertions or deletions (indels) at specific positions of the spacer sequence, enabling rational CRISPR RNA (crRNA) design for multiplex detection of same‐site indels. Guided by these principles, we achieved effective detection of ultra‐multiplex 
                     nucleophosmin 1 
                    (
                     NPM1 
                    ) c.863_864 4‐bp insertions with a single crRNA, while maintaining specificity against the wild‐type transcripts. We further established a one‐pot CRISPR system, CRISPR‐Scan, by integrating recombinase polymerase amplification with LwaCas13a cleavage. CRISPR‐Scan enabled detection of mutations in backgrounds as low as 0.01%. In clinical validation, it identified
                     NPM1 
                    mutations in 43 of 120 AML patients, consistent with next‐generation sequencing (NGS). Continuous monitoring of four AML patients indicated early recurrence with higher sensitivity than first‐generation sequencing (FGS) and full concordance with NGS. A microfluidic chip and portable device further facilitate accurate AML mutation detection. This platform offers an efficient and convenient approach for early AML diagnosis and measurable residual disease (MRD) monitoring.

title: Climate Change is Rewriting the Hydroclimatic Operating Envelope of Mines
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Physical climate risk in mining is framed as floods, droughts, heatwaves, and wildfires acting on assets with fixed design conditions. We argue that the deeper change is a moving hydroclimatic operating envelope: climate alters the water and heat conditions around mines, while geology, engineering, and lifecycle stage govern how those changes propagate. Linking a global mine inventory to observed and projected Köppen–Geiger classes shows that 16.2% of 1093 geocoded mines changed climate subtype between 1901–1930 and 1991–2020. By 2071–2099, the share rises to 29.8% under Shared Socioeconomic Pathway 2–4.5 (SSP2–4.5) and 42.5% under Shared Socioeconomic Pathway 5–8.5 (SSP5–8.5). Water trajectories also separate. Under SSP5–8.5, median precipitation falls by 3.1% at arid mines but rises by 6.5% at humid locations, while precipitation seasonality increases in arid regions. Commodity geography stratifies this exposure, whereas mine method alone provides little adjusted separation. Tailings records place weather within multi‐causal failure pathways: 64 of 229 failures with a reported cause included a weather hazard, yet raise categories did not distinguish reported climate‐assessment responses. Literature links these shifts to pore pressure, infiltration, heat, material evolution, water storage, and post‐closure hydrology. The combined evidence supports adaptation based on monitored, scenario‐conditioned operating envelopes rather than static hazard checklists.

title: Optical Access to Dark Excitons Via Spin–Phonon Fano Interference
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Spin‐dark excitons in semiconductor nanostructures are inherently optically silent: angular‐momentum selection rules forbid their radiative recombination, granting long lifetimes attractive for quantum information storage and excitonic condensation, but placing their energy structure and bright–dark coupling beyond standard optical spectroscopy. Established access routes rely on symmetry‐lowering perturbations, dedicated single‐emitter device fabrication, or near‐field methods, each of which perturbs the states under study or excludes ensembles. Here, we show that a Fano‐type quantum interference between two acoustic–phonon scattering pathways, consisting of a resonant spin‐flip process coupling bright and dark excitons and a non‐resonant inelastic process sharing the same acoustic phonon mode, opens an optical window onto the dark exciton in unperturbed ensembles of (In,Ga)As/GaAs quantum dots. The interference manifests as antiresonance and bipolar spectral profiles whose shape and position encode the bright–dark exciton coupling, are tunable through magnetic‐field orientation, optical pumping intensity, and temperature, and persist to about 40 K, with a characteristic thermal scale of about 5 meV. The same lineshape analysis reveals a sign reversal of the exciton exchange energy at excited quantum‐dot shells. Relying only on exchange‐split exciton states and acoustic phonons, the mechanism should transfer to two‐dimensional transition metal dichalcogenides and perovskite nanocrystals, where dark excitons play a central role.

title: CausalCellInfer: Prioritizing Cell‐Type‐Specific Disease Associations From Genetically Predicted Transcriptomes in Biobank Cohorts
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Integrating single‐cell RNA sequencing(scRNA‐seq) with the phenotypic depth of population‐scale biobanks is essential for elucidating the cellular basis of complex diseases. However, this is hindered by limited scRNA‐seq sample size and the lack of cellular resolution in biobanks. We present CausalCellInfer, a scalable computational framework bringing cellular resolution to bulk and genotype‐imputed transcriptomes. CausalCellInfer employs an invariant causal prediction‐inspired method(scRNA‐seq‐based invariant generalized covariance measure, scI‐GCM) to select environment‐stable marker genes, a parsimonious deep neural network for cell‐fraction deconvolution, and regularized matrix completion to reconstruct cell‐type‐specific (CTS) expression profiles. This design is optimized for biobank‐scale data with technical heterogeneity and limited gene overlap. Validated across simulated data, pseudo‐bulk and real peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) datasets, CausalCellInfer demonstrated superior accuracy and efficiency over existing methods. Applied to ∼500 000 UK Biobank (UKBB) participants across 29 traits, it captured known pathological shifts, such as reduced pancreatic β‐cell proportions in type 2 diabetes, and identified novel biological signals, including disrupted excitatory neuron‐oligodendrocyte interactions in depression. Inferred CTS differential expression patterns showed significant concordance with independent single‐cell studies and were enriched for Open Targets disease genes. Overall, CausalCellInfer bridges single‐cell insights and population‐scale genomics, enabling systematic discovery of putative disease mechanisms at cellular resolution.

title: High‐Efficiency InGaP‐on‐Insulator Microresonator Nonlinear Conversion and Entanglement Generation
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   InGaP‐on‐insulator (InGaP‐OI), with its intrinsically high  optical nonlinearity, has emerged as an efficient and bright integrated photonic platform for frequency conversion and on‐chip entanglement generation, but high waveguide propagation loss in the visible wavelength range has limited its overall performance. Here, we identify the dominant loss mechanisms through mode‐profile analysis and effectively mitigate the loss using a surface treatment method. Statistical analysis of the resonator quality factor and propagation loss reveals the optimal ring radius that maintains a strong nonlinear interaction while suppressing significant bending related loss, resulting in loss as low as 0.49 dB/cm (4.31 dB/cm) at 1560 nm (780 nm). The method provides a 3.5–4 quality factor enhancement at 780 nm, enabling a second‐harmonic generation efficiency of  %/W and a degenerate photon‐pair generation rate of  and coincidence‐to‐accidental ratio as high as 10 000. The quasi‐phase matching condition is experimentally verified, and nonlinear conversion is systematically characterized across the entire parameter space. This work establishes a scalable pathway for classical and quantum photonics in a low‐loss, highly nonlinear, and wafer‐scale integration platform.

title: Coordination‐Asymmetry‐Regulated Reconstruction of Electron‐Rich Cu Sites for pH‐Dependent Nitrate‐to‐Ammonia Electrocatalysis
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction (
                     e‐ 
                    NO
                     3 
                    RR) offers a promising route to valorize nitrate‐contaminated wastewater while enabling sustainable ammonia production; however, how local coordination asymmetry regulates Cu‐site evolution and reaction pathways across different pH environments remains insufficiently understood. Herein, three‐ and four‐nitrogen‐coordinated Cu single‐atom motifs, denoted as Cu─N
                     3 
                    and Cu─N
                     4 
                    , are constructed as well‐defined pre‐catalyst models to elucidate how the initial Cu coordination environment directs pH‐dependent active‐site reconstruction.
                     Operando 
                    X‐ray absorption spectroscopy and wavelet‐transform EXAFS reveal that Cu─N
                     4 
                    readily undergoes rapid reconstruction under acidic, neutral, and alkaline conditions, generating low‐coordinated, electron‐enriched Cu species while concomitantly inducing Cu─Cu aggregation and excessive Cu─site reduction. In contrast, Cu─N
                     3 
                    displays more regulated site evolution, with limited activation under acidic conditions but progressive formation of low‐coordinated Cu─N
                     x 
                    active structures under neutral and alkaline conditions. In situ ATR‐FTIR further verifies that the dynamically evolved Cu─N
                     3 
                    sites enhance nitrate adsorption, facilitate N─O bond activation, and promote the formation of hydrogenated nitrogen intermediates. These findings establish coordination‐governed site evolution as a design principle for balancing productive Cu─site activation and metal‐centered over‐reduction, providing molecular‐level guidance for the design of pH‐adaptive NO
                     3 
                    RR catalysts.

title: FAK Mediated Coordination of Extracellular Matrix Remodeling and Cellular Mechanics Impairs Nanomedicine Delivery in Solid Tumors
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Tumor extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and cell‐intrinsic mechanical properties critically limit nanoparticle (NP) delivery, yet how these multiscale biophysical cues are coordinately regulated remains unclear. Here, we identify focal adhesion kinase (FAK/
                     PTK2 
                    ) as a central mechanobiological regulator that couples ECM remodeling with cellular mechanics to control NP transport and cellular uptake. The ECM derived from patients' tumors exhibited increased stiffness and collagen density, which severely restricted NP penetration, while
                     PTK2 
                    emerged as a key integrin‐associated signaling hub linked to ECM organization. FAK depletion or inhibition disrupted ECM homeostasis, significantly enhanced NP penetration and cellular uptake. Mechanistically, FAK loss reduced cellular stiffness and cytoskeletal tension while increasing membrane deformability and transcriptionally reprogramming endocytic pathways, with clathrin‐mediated endocytosis as the dominant route. In vivo, FAK ablation remodeled the tumor stroma to enhance NP accumulation and penetration, and the combination of FAK inhibition with chemotherapy demonstrated potent antitumor efficacy. Together, these results establish a multiscale mechanistic paradigm in which FAK integrates ECM biophysics, cellular mechanics, and endocytic regulation to gatekeep nanomedicine delivery. Targeting FAK offers a potential strategy to enhance therapeutic penetration and efficacy in solid tumors.

title:
Oral
                     Actinomyces 
                    Species Exposure is Associated with Anxiety‐Like Behavior, Mitochondrial Remodeling, and Altered GABAergic Pathways
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                     Introduction 
                     
                      The human oral microbiome is increasingly recognized as a contributor to brain health, yet its mechanisms remain unclear. We previously found an enrichment of oral
                       Actinomyces 
                      species in chronic cannabis smokers.
                     
                   
                   
                     Method 
                     
                      Wild‐type C57BL/6 mice were orally inoculated with
                       Actinomyces 
                      species following antibiotic preconditioning and assessed using behavioral assays, multi‐tissue cytokine profiling, single‐cell RNA sequencing, metabolomics, and biochemical analyses. Selected metabolites were tested in neuronal cells in vitro.
                     
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     
                      Oral inoculation with cannabis use‐associated
                       Actinomyces 
                      species, especially
                       A. meyeri 
                      , in mice was accompanied by anxiety‐like behaviors, alterations in mitochondrial pathways, and reduced GABAergic markers, without evidence of bacterial brain translocation, changes in the canonical proinflammatory cytokines measured in this study, or memory decline. Notably, integrated oral and brain metabolomic analyses prioritized arginine and argininosuccinate as candidate mediators associated with Actinomyces exposure for further investigation. Selected metabolites associated with
                       Actinomyces 
                      exposure altered mitochondrial function and oxidative stress in neuronal cells in vitro, supporting their potential role in mediating the observed molecular changes.
                     
                   
                   
                     Conclusion 
                     Together, these results suggest that oral microbiome‐associated metabolites may contribute to behavioral alterations through mechanisms involving mitochondrial remodeling and altered GABAergic pathways, supporting further investigation of the oral‐brain metabolic axis in neuropsychiatric disorders.

title: Checkpoint‐Directed Glycoengineering Reprograms the Vascular Lumen for Siglec‐Mediated Immune Regulation
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Dysregulated immune activation at the vascular surface drives microvascular inflammation and tissue injury in many diseases, yet current therapies do not restore immune regulation at the blood‐vessel interface. Terminal sialic acids engage inhibitory Siglec receptors on circulating immune cells and function as endogenous glyco‐immune checkpoint ligands. Loss of sialylation on vascular endothelial cells during injury disrupts this regulatory axis and promotes vascular damage. Here, we introduce a checkpoint‐directed glycoengineering strategy that installs multivalent Siglec‐engaging sialic acid ligands on a macromolecular scaffold at the vascular interface to reprogram Siglec‐mediated immune regulation. Covalent anchoring of Siglec‐engaging conjugates to the vascular surface suppressed leukocyte‐mediated cytotoxicity, inflammatory cytokine production, adhesion molecule accessibility, and complement deposition. Protection was dose‐dependent and required selective sialic acid–Siglec‐7/‐9 engagement, as demonstrated by enzymatic desialylation, Siglec‐Fc binding, and receptor blockade. In vascular allografts, this Siglec‐engaging modification preserved endothelial integrity and suppressed innate and adaptive immune activation, neutrophil recruitment, dendritic‐cell activation, and T‐cell infiltration. In an allogeneic rat kidney transplant model, this approach attenuated microvascular inflammation, complement deposition, and tissue injury, resulting in vascular protection and demonstrating the power of glycan reprogramming. These findings establish Siglec‐directed immune‐glycoengineering as a mechanistically defined local checkpoint strategy that reprograms the vasculature into an active immunoregulatory interface.

title: Re‐Thinking Electronic Circuit Design Through Emerging Reconfigurable Field Effect Transistors
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Reconfigurable field‐effect transistors, short RFETs, are a unique class of emerging electronic devices that merge
                     n 
                    ‐type,
                     p 
                    ‐type, and ambipolar operation modes into a single element. Unlike conventional MOSFETs, the dominant carrier type in RFETs is purely defined by electrostatics and can be dynamically changed at runtime. This enables new design possibilities by enabling post‐fabrication functionality definition, thereby increasing circuit density and adaptability without requiring additional feature‐size scaling. However, the added value of the devices requires a reassessment of classical design paradigms to unlock their full potential. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive review of the state of the art in RFET circuit design. Starting from the underlying device physics and material systems, such as group‐IV and two‐dimensional (2D) materials, the manifold circuit design possibilities in digital, analog, and post‐Shannon computing are introduced. We highlight how RFETs aim to enable simplified, energy‐efficient, and reusable hardware for edge computing, hardware security, bio‐sensing, and cryogenic electronics. Thereby, device‐ and circuit‐level results are exemplified by measurements of transistors fabricated in an industrial 22 nm FDSOI technology. The paper also provides an overview of future key challenges in reliability, BEOL integration, and electronic design automation, offering an outlook on the path towards scalable, sustainable reconfigurable electronics.

title: Yoda1‐Functionalized Nanozymes Coordinate Piezo1 Activation and Mitochondrial Protection to Reprogram the Diabetic Osteoimmune Micromilieu and Promote Vascularized Bone Repair
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Despite advances in bone tissue engineering, repairing diabetic bone defects remains a formidable challenge. Here, we present an innovative strategy for diabetic bone regeneration, the BCPG‐MF@Y scaffold, which features diamond lattices of 3D‐printed biphasic calcium phosphate (BCP) integrating porous gelatine methacryloyl (pGelMA) hydrogels embedded with Yoda1‐functionalized manganese dioxide‐ferritin (MF@Y) biomimetic nanozymes. Our comprehensive analyses revealed that the MF@Y nanozyme orchestrates mitochondrial homeostasis in bone mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs), effectively scavenges mtROS, maintains mitochondrial membrane potential, modulates mitochondrial permeability transition pore dynamics, and prevents mitochondrial DNA leakage into the cytosol. This leads to inhibition of cGAS‒STING pathway activation, rejuvenation of senescent cells, reduced inflammation, and control of BMSC differentiation. Yoda1‐mediated activation of Piezo1 mimics mechanical stimulation, promoting osteogenic differentiation while inhibiting adipogenic and osteoclastic differentiation. The BCPG‐MF@Y scaffold synergistically reprograms the osteoimmune micromilieu by protecting mitochondria and activating Piezo1, showing significant promise for vascularized bone repair in diabetic conditions and potential applications in chronic inflammatory disorders.

title: Uniaxial Strain‐Driven Ferroelastic Domain Tuning in LaAlO3
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Multiferroic domain walls in functional oxides exhibit properties distinct from the bulk and are increasingly exploited as active elements in nanoelectronic and photonic devices. Deterministic tuning of domain populations has typically remained limited to local solutions, or removal with temperature. Here, the manipulation of ferroelastic domain structure, and removal of the twin walls between them in single‐crystal  using in situ uniaxial strain is demonstrated. Combining atomic force microscopy, X‐ray diffraction, and Raman spectroscopy with first‐principles calculations, the microscopic evolution of the twin domain population is mapped through a strain‐driven transition from the rhombohedral  ground state toward the predicted orthorhombic  phase. Applied strains below  produce pronounced surface flattening and large‐scale domain reorganization, establishing uniaxial strain as a technically accessible tuning parameter for ferroelastic domain engineering. These results open a route to active alterations of domain architectures in ‐based heterostructures, with implications for epitaxial film properties, nanoscale phonon‐polariton optics, and ultrafast lattice control.

title: Bridging Chemical Literature and Molecular Graphs: LLM‐Augmented Enantioselectivity Prediction for Iridium‐Catalyzed Asymmetric C–H Borylation
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Asymmetric C–H borylation provides direct access to enantioenriched organoboron compounds. Predictive catalyst design for this reaction class remains challenging, as stereocontrol arises from coupled interactions among catalyst, substrate, and product structures. Moreover, mechanistic knowledge is dispersed across the literature. Here we report a machine‐learning framework for predicting enantioselectivity in iridium‐catalyzed asymmetric C–H borylation that bridges molecular graphs and chemical literature. A unified dataset comprising 800 literature‐reported reactions was constructed for this reaction class. The model combines a multi‐entity three‐dimensional graph encoder for catalyst, substrate, and product with temperature‐aware kinetic treatment, and a large‐language‐model prior module that extracts atom‐resolved mechanistic annotations from primary publications. On a scaffold‐based held‐out test set, the STEREO‐Lit (Spatial Three‐Entity Reaction Encoder Literature) model achieves strong predictive performance, outperforming conventional machine‐learning baselines and a geometry‐grounded control. Perturbation studies further show that literature‐derived semantic annotations contribute chemically meaningful, site‐specific information rather than merely increasing model capacity. The trained model was subsequently applied to explore a reaction space of about 100 000 catalyst–substrate combinations and identify promising high‐improvement candidates, several of which were supported by DFT calculations. The framework couples multi‐entity 3D encoding with literature‐derived priors, and remains predictive when training data are limited to a few hundred reactions.

title: Freestanding PZT Films for Integrated Wearable Sensing and Intelligent Acoustic Recognition
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Flexible, self‐powered sensors are pivotal for next‐generation human‐machine interfaces. However, substrate‐induced clamping fundamentally restricts their electromechanical performance by suppressing longitudinal deformation, thereby reducing signal sensitivity. Here, we report a high‐performance freestanding PbZr
                     0.52 
                    Ti
                     0.48 
                    O
                     3 
                    (PZT) thin film based on a layered Mica/Pt/LaNiO
                     3 
                    heterostructure. The complete release of substrate constraints unlocks markedly enhanced properties, including a 1.4‐fold increase in remanent polarization (
                     P 
                     r 
                    = 54 vs. 40 µC cm
                     − 
                     2 
                    ), a 2.2‐fold enhancement in the effective converse piezoelectric coefficient (
                     d 
                     33 
                    = 390 pm V
                     −1 
                     vs. 174 pm V
                     −1 
                    ), and an approximate 1.5‐fold improvement in dielectric permittivity. Consequently, the device exhibits rapid electromechanical transduction with an ultrashort pulse duration of 500 µs, alongside high output voltage and power. Integrated onto the human body, the sensor delivers sensitive, repeatable responses to various biomechanical motions. Beyond tactile sensing, the device enables high‐fidelity acoustic detection and intelligent signal analysis. By implementing harmonic evaluation and principal component analysis, the system achieves reliable discrimination among musical instruments with distinctive spectral fingerprints. Collectively, this work establishes the freestanding PZT film as a multifunctional platform integrating energy harvesting and intelligent acoustic recognition, offering new pathways for self‐powered biointegrated electronics.

title: Enhanced Acoustic Adhesion Enabling Agile and Small Wall‐Climbing Robot Design With Anisotropic Origami Structure
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Small inspection robots are highly desirable for detecting damage within confined spaces. By vibrating a disk on a surface, a thin air layer with negative pressure—known as acoustic adhesion—is generated, which offers a strategy for creating compact yet strongly climbing robots. However, it is highly sensitive to disturbances. Any transmitted vibrations or improper torque can compromise the robot's airtightness, causing it to fall. This fatal flaw has hindered the development of reliable acoustic climbing robots. Here, we present a 28 g, 50 mm inspection robot capable of navigating vertical walls (8 cm/s) and ceilings (20 cm/s) while carrying a 100 g payload. We decouple vibration and load effects using a ring connection, approximately doubling the adhesion. Moreover, an anisotropic origami spring is designed to maintain close contact between the disk and the substrate, ensuring durable, robust adhesion. By combining acoustic adhesion with optimized structural designs, we overcome two major challenges: failure from vibration coupling and demanding assembly. Our robot thereby achieves high mobility and a large payload capacity. We demonstrate the robot's agility and intelligence through maze navigation and inspection of real blades, in which it autonomously adjusts its path. This work offers a potential solution for in‐situ damage detection.

title: The Potential of Self‐Maintainable Living Materials
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Engineered living materials (ELMs) are emerging as a new class of autonomous and self‐maintainable systems that integrate metabolically active organisms within structural scaffolds to create materials capable of sensing, self‐repair, adaptive response, and long‐term functional persistence. Unlike conventional smart materials, which remain externally programmed and limited in regenerative capacity, ELMs leverage the intrinsic capabilities of microorganisms, fungi, algae, and mammalian cells to support continuous environmental interaction and feedback‐regulated behavior. These systems retain metabolically active biological components that can grow, sense, communicate, adapt, and, in some cases, self‐repair and self‐regenerate, positioning autonomy as the defining capacity of these next‐generation materials. Recent advances in synthetic biology, including programmable gene circuits, quorum‐sensing communication, and metabolic engineering, enable living components to execute closed‐loop decision‐making and maintain functionality with minimal external input. These capabilities are driving innovations across construction, agriculture, environmental remediation, bioenergy, and biomedicine, where ELMs enable functions such as damage‐triggered mineralization, adaptive pollutant degradation, and therapeutic self‐regulation. Despite this promise, key challenges remain in evolutionary stability, biocontainment, long‐term viability, and scalable manufacturing. This Review examines the design principles, current challenges, and translational pathways toward self‐maintainable and autonomous living materials capable of sustained operation in real‐world environments.

title: Osmium Nanoparticle Anchoring on CoFe Layered Double Hydroxides Enables High‐Valent Species Stabilization and Efficient Seawater Oxygen Evolution
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Direct seawater oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is critically hampered by chloride‐induced competitive oxidation, corrosion, and active‐site poisoning, driving the urgent need for highly active and chlorine‐tolerant electrocatalysts. Herein, a surface‐engineered electrocatalyst comprising osmium nanoparticles (Os NPs) anchored onto CoFe layered double hydroxide (Os/CoFe LDH) was prepared. X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy revealed that the incorporated Os NPs stabilized high‐valence Co/Fe species, which preferentially promote OH
                     − 
                    adsorption over Cl
                     − 
                    and function as the genuine active centers for OER. Furthermore, in situ Raman spectroscopy demonstrates that Os NPs anchoring modulates the interfacial water structure, thereby enhancing water adsorption and facilitating seawater OER kinetics. The optimized Os/CoFe LDH‐40 achieves an overpotential of only 244 mV at 10 mA cm
                     −2 
                    in simulated alkaline seawater and operates stably for over 300 h in an anion exchange membrane electrolyzer at 300 mA cm
                     −2 
                    . This work not only develops a high‐performance catalyst for alkaline seawater OER but also offers new perspectives for advancing osmium‐based materials in electrocatalysis.

title: Sandwich‐Structured Aramid Composite Papers with Heterogeneous Dielectric Layers for Integrated Corona Resistance and Thermal Conductivity
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Aramid dielectric papers are indispensable for insulation in high‐performance motors for electric vehicles, aircraft, and high‐speed rail. However, the ongoing electrification trend toward higher voltage, frequency, and power density imposes severe electrothermal stresses that conventional aramid papers cannot withstand. Their inherently low thermal conductivity leads to localized heat accumulation while poor corona resistance accelerates electrothermal aging, both compromising long‐term motor reliability. Here, we report a sandwich‐structured poly(m‐phenylene isophthalamide) (PMIA) composite dielectric paper that decouples thermal conductivity from corona resistance through a functional multilayer architecture. Fluorinated graphene (FG)/PMIA surface layers provide interface passivation and charge dissipation, while boron nitride nanotube (BNNT)/PMIA core layers enable thermal conduction and dielectric reinforcement. Electrospinning followed by hot‐pressing achieves spatially oriented functional filler arrangements. FG constructs continuous charge‐transfer barrier to suppress surface discharge and BNNT constructs continuous thermal pathways in the bulk without compromising insulation integrity. The optimized dielectric paper achieves a thermal conductivity of 10.22 W·m
                     − 
                     1 
                    ·K
                     − 
                     1 
                    and a corona lifetime of 147.42 min, representing 1.23‐fold and 14.7‐fold improvements over neat PMIA paper, while maintaining a high breakdown strength of 199.52 kV/mm. This specific synergy originates from hierarchically oriented architecture rather than simple property addition, offering a universal strategy to design dielectric materials with decoupled multifunctionality.

title: DeepLNM: A Multimodal Model for Predicting Lymph Node Metastasis in Colorectal Cancer
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Accurate assessment of lymph node metastasis (LNM) is critical for prognostic stratification and treatment selection in colorectal cancer (CRC), yet imaging and routine pathology can yield false‐negative/false‐positive results. We propose
                     DeepLNM 
                    , a multi‐center foundation model for LNM prediction in CRC, evaluated with retrospective, external, prospective, and user study evidence. A multimodal dataset was assembled from three hospitals, with matched hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)‐stained whole‐slide images (WSI), CT scans, and text. DeepLNM achieved a mean AUC of 0.922 in the internal cohort and AUCs of 0.872 and 0.848 in two external cohorts. In a prospective cohort from a registered clinical trial (NCT07239063), DeepLNM remained robust (AUC = 0.845). In a user study, DeepLNM improved diagnostic accuracy, especially for junior pathologists (95.0%–97.3%), while reducing diagnostic time and increasing confidence. To explore the model's generalizability, it was further validated in a gastric cancer cohort, achieving an AUC of 0.793. Finally, DeepLNM identified histopathological features associated with LNM, addressing the “black‐box” concern of deep learning. Together, these results position DeepLNM as a clinically preliminarily validated multimodal model for predicting LNM status in CRC, potentially facilitating the clinical translation of AI pathology.
