abstract: Terrestrial megafauna (animals >1,000 kg) have substantial impacts on ecosystems while alive; yet, we know little about the impacts of these ecosystem engineers after they die. Like whale carcasses in the ocean, terrestrial megacarcasses may leave ecological legacies via the nutrient pulses they create on the landscape. Here, we investigated the impact of elephant megacarcasses on savanna ecosystems in Kruger National Park, South Africa. To determine how elephant carcasses affect below- and aboveground biodiversity and ecosystem processes, we collected soil and plant samples from 40 carcass sites (pairing “on carcass” and “off carcass” samples) ranging from 8 d to 7.7 y postmortem. We found that elephant carcasses released enormous pools of nutrients into savanna soils, increasing ammonium by 31×, nitrate by 7×, and phosphorus by 3× on average. These extreme ammonium concentrations were negatively correlated with the biodiversity of bacteria and plants, which were both suppressed at elephant carcass sites. Despite these decreases in biodiversity, ecosystem processes were strongly elevated at elephant carcass sites, with soil microbial respiration elevated for 1 to 2 y and herbivore grazing >3× higher for 7+ y postmortem. These results demonstrate that elephant megacarcasses generate coldspots of biodiversity but hotspots of ecosystem processes, unveiling a cryptic ecological function of megaherbivores that is extreme in both magnitude and duration relative to carcasses of smaller animals. As humans drive terrestrial megafauna toward extinction, we risk losing not only their ecosystem engineering abilities while they are alive but also the ecological legacies their carcasses create after death.

title: Competing presynaptic protein assemblies coordinate basal neurotransmission with homeostatic plasticity
abstract:
Neural circuits establish a stable basal level of synaptic transmission that is maintained throughout life. When synaptic activity is perturbed, homeostatic mechanisms restore this set point, but how neurons reconcile long-term stability and rapid compensatory plasticity remains unclear. Here, we identify two competing presynaptic multimolecular complexes that control steady-state transmission and homeostatic potentiation and define the molecular switch that enables transitions between these functional states. At
                     Drosophila 
                    neuromuscular junction, the transmembrane protein PlexinB (PlexB) and the auxiliary subunit Neto-α regulate both basal synaptic function and homeostatic plasticity. PlexB association with presynaptic KaiR1D/Neto-α receptor complexes modulates channel properties and fine-tunes neurotransmitter release, whereas PlexB signaling with Semaphorin2b (Sema2b) and Neto-α drives homeostatic potentiation. KaiR1D and Sema2b/PlexB compete for a limited pool of presynaptic Neto-α. Motor neurons switch from steady-state transmission to homeostatic potentiation by exchanging KaiR1D/Neto-α/PlexB complexes for Neto-α/PlexB/Sema2b. Critically, Neto-α must dissociate from KaiR1D-containing complexes to initiate the homeostatic response. Variants of Neto-α or KaiR1D that fail to dissociate support normal basal neurotransmission but abolish homeostatic plasticity. These findings demonstrate that dynamic reorganization of competing presynaptic protein assemblies enables neurons to preserve stable baseline transmission while mounting robust compensatory responses to perturbations. Given the widespread roles of presynaptic receptors and Semaphorin/Plexin signaling in synaptic regulation, this mechanism may represent a conserved strategy for balancing stability and plasticity in neural circuits.

title: The honey bee stinger: An unusual pump with collapsible double pistons
authors: Fiorella Ramirez-EsquivelClaudia KloseHyun Chai LeeQuinn GracoAjay NarendraSridhar RaviaSchool of Engineering and Technology, University of New South Wales, Canberra, ACT 2612, Australiabhttps://ror.org/01sf06y89School of Natural Sciences, Macquarie University, Sydney, NSW 2109, Australiachttps://ror.org/01sf06y89Pollinator Futures Research Centre, Macquarie University, Sydney, NSW 2109, Australia
abstract:
Most stinging animals deliver venom by contracting muscles around a venom reservoir, but honey bees employ a fundamentally different strategy. The stingers of worker bees have the unique ability to autotomize, separating from the body, to continue to sting independently. Despite more than a century of anatomical descriptions, the mechanics of venom pumping have remained unresolved due to the challenges of observing them in action. We recorded high-speed videos of active, autotomized stingers, combined with micro computed tomography-based three-dimensional reconstruction to characterize the biomechanics of stinging in the honey bee
                     Apis mellifera 
                    . We reveal that the stinger functions as a unique double-piston micro-pump. Two lancets, each possessing a deformable valve, slide in antiphase within a bulb chamber. These valves dynamically deform to alternately form a seal during the downstroke and collapse during the upstroke, enabling pressure generation for pumping while potentially minimizing backflow during refilling. The inverted tear-drop shape of the bulb facilitates refill even while pumping proceeds. We explored valve deformations and flow behavior by constructing a dynamically scaled physical model of the bulb chamber confirming key features of the pumping cycle and propose mechanisms for valve deformations. The double piston design adds significant design complexity but enables continuous venom delivery in a compact, autonomous unit. These findings provide deeper understanding of venom pumping in honey bees and other Hymenoptera. This study also provides evidence of an axial piston pump within a biological system and offers inspiration for the design of microfluidic pumping devices.

title: Extensive glacier loss in the coterminous United States
authors: Andrew G. FountainBryce GlennChristopher McNeilBrian Menounosahttps://ror.org/00yn2fy02Department of Geology, Portland State University, Portland, OR 97201bhttps://ror.org/05ehhzx21United States Geological Survey, Alaska Science Center, Anchorage, AK 99508chttps://ror.org/025wzwv46Department of Geography Earth and Environmental Sciences, University of Northern British Columbia, BC V2N 4Z9, Canadadhttps://ror.org/02pry0c91Hakai Institute, Campbell River, BC V9W 0B7, Canada
abstract: Glaciers populate the mountain ranges of the western conterminous United States and despite their importance to alpine hydrology, their area and volume change have never been comprehensively evaluated. Our study shows that since the mid-twentieth century about one-quarter of the glaciers have disappeared and the overall area and volume are reduced by one-third. The pattern of glacier shrinkage suggests most glaciers in the conterminous United States are largely maintained by local topographic influences due to their small size. These results improve our understanding of evolving high alpine hydrology and importance to ecosystem processes.

title: Evolution shapes ecosystem resilience through spatial self-organization
abstract: Drylands are globally widespread and ecologically important but vulnerable to climate change. Many exhibit spatially self-organized vegetation patterns that enhance resilience by enabling vegetation to reorganize their patterns under drying, thereby optimizing water use and maintaining productivity. Plants can also undergo evolution in response to environmental change. Although both spatial self-organization and rapid evolution are fundamental mechanisms of resilience, their interaction remains largely unknown. Using a theoretical model, we examine how these mechanisms interact to shape vegetation transitions—abrupt or gradual—and ecosystem resilience under climatic drying. We find that pattern formation can suppress adaptation by maintaining soil moisture beneath vegetation patches despite rainfall decline, thereby limiting selection for increased drought tolerance. However, this suppression is largely alleviated under the variable rainfall typical of drylands. In turn, evolution feeds back on self-organization by increasing the spatial plasticity of vegetation patterns and their ability to reorganize under changing climate, although this positive effect weakens as evolutionary rate increases. Considering direct (adaptation) and indirect (pattern-mediated) effects, evolution enhances resilience, with indirect effects via pattern plasticity dominating. Within model scenarios spanning plausible rainfall variability and relative evolutionary-to-ecological rates, more than half of vegetation transitions are abrupt involving biomass losses exceeding 50%, highlighting a potential mechanism underlying recent global observations of widespread abrupt vegetation losses in drylands. These results demonstrate that evolution and spatial self-organization jointly determine dryland resilience under environmental change and highlight the unexpected role of evolution in patterned landscapes, calling for integrative approaches to predict ecosystem responses in a changing world.

title: Shedding light on left hippocampal mGlu5 in Alzheimer’s disease
abstract: Metabotropic glutamate receptor 5 (mGlu5) is essential for synaptic plasticity and memory, making it a potential therapeutic target in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). While hemispheric asymmetries in hippocampal function have been observed in AD patients, the lateralized contribution of mGlu5 signaling to cognitive decline remains unclear. Here, we show a physiological left-right asymmetry in hippocampal mGlu5 expression in wild-type mice, with higher levels in the left hemisphere, consistent with previous reports. This physiological asymmetry is lost in two distinct mouse models of AD, the J20 and 5xFAD mice, revealing a hemisphere-specific disruption of hippocampal mGlu5 regulation. Using the light-controllable negative allosteric modulator Alloswitch-1, we show that selective inhibition of left, but not right, hippocampal mGlu5 restores working and short-term memory in AD mice. This finding indicates that altered mGlu5 expression does not simply reflect receptor loss, but rather a dysregulated signaling state that remains functionally relevant and pharmacologically targetable. Left-specific modulation also normalizes pathological downstream signaling, including aberrant Pyk2 and GSK-3β activation and tau hyperphosphorylation, across both hemispheres, indicating a widespread impact of hemisphere-selective intervention. These findings establish a functional lateralization of hippocampal mGlu5 signaling and identify the left hippocampus as a critical site for mGlu5-dependent memory dysfunction in AD. They also highlight the therapeutic potential of region-specific photopharmacology for precise intervention in early AD pathology, providing a strategy for spatially targeted modulation of pathological synaptic signaling in neurodegenerative disease.

title: In mice, a population of male germ cells shows characteristics of nonapoptotic cell death during G0 arrest
abstract: In mammals, a small population of spermatogonial stem cells (SSCs) is established shortly after birth. These cells self-renew and produce sperm for the male’s reproductive lifespan, passing the genome on to the next generation. Establishment of a population of SSCs with high genomic integrity is essential. SSCs are derived from a much larger precursor population of male germ cells (MGCs) that differentiate during fetal life. During the last third of gestation, MGCs undergo a prolonged period of G0 cell cycle arrest during which they sustain high levels of transcription and acquire epigenetic programming for SSC fate. Although these differentiation steps can cause cellular and genomic damage, it has been unclear whether selection for germ cell quality occurs during G0 arrest since no classic markers of cell death have been detected. In this study, we used a mouse model to characterize a population of MGCs that begin to accumulate markers of cell death, such as AnnexinV (AnV) and propidium iodide (PI), at E16.5. The AnV- and PI-positive MGC population is characterized by low expression of the RNA-binding protein, Dead End 1, and exhibits dsDNA breaks and mitochondrial dysfunction. Interestingly, we do not see evidence of an active cell death cascade until the time of birth, when phosphorylation of MLKL, a hallmark of necroptotic cell death, occurs. Based on these findings, we propose that variable cellular health is an important basis for selection of SSC precursors.

title: Learning dissipative chaotic dynamics with boundedness guarantees
abstract: Chaotic dynamics, commonly seen in weather systems and fluid turbulence, are characterized by their sensitivity to initial conditions, which makes accurate prediction challenging. Recent approaches have focused on developing data-driven models that attempt to preserve invariant statistics over long horizons since many chaotic systems exhibit dissipative behaviors and ergodicity. Despite the recent progress in such models, they are still often prone to generating unbounded trajectories, leading to invalid statistics evaluation. To address this fundamental challenge, we introduce a modular framework that provides formal guarantees of trajectory boundedness for neural network chaotic dynamics models. Our core contribution is a dissipative projection layer that leverages control-theoretic principles to ensure the learned system is dissipative. Specifically, our framework simultaneously learns a dynamics emulator and an energy-like function, where the latter is used to construct an algebraic dissipative constraint within the projection layer. Furthermore, the learned invariant level set provides an outer estimate for the system’s strange attractor, which is known to be difficult to characterize due to its complex geometry. We demonstrate our model’s ability to produce bounded long-horizon forecasts that preserve invariant statistics for chaotic dynamical systems, including Lorenz 96 and a reduced-order model of the Kuramoto–Sivashinsky equation.

title: Laundering and evasion in response to antislavery policies in Brazil’s cattle sector
abstract: Modern slavery remains pervasive across many economic sectors. Progress toward eradicating it has been partially hindered by a lack of tested, comprehensive policy responses. Using data on millions of cattle transactions in Brazil, we evaluated how ranchers changed their selling behavior after being added to the “Dirty List,” a public registry that names and shames employers found to use modern slavery. Dirty Listed ranchers significantly reduced direct sales to slaughterhouses that signed sustainable supply chain commitments but evaded sanctions by laundering cattle through compliant intermediaries or selling to nonsignatory slaughterhouses. These responses weakened the financial cost of listing to ranchers, and likely allowed beef and leather linked to modern slave labor to enter international supply chains. Our findings highlight the limits of downstream enforcement and underscore the need to monitor upstream suppliers to ensure slavery-free supply chains.

title: AI-generated language remains systematically distinguishable from human communication
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in the social sciences to simulate human behavior and communication, yet validation methods for these applications remain limited. Existing evaluations often rely on human judgments of plausibility, a coarse, difficult-to-scale, and often unreliable benchmark for distinguishing AI-generated from human text. As a result, researchers lack robust tools for assessing the realism of LLM-generated language and for calibrating models to real-world data. We address this gap in two ways. First, we introduce the Conversational Human Authenticity Test (CHAT), a validation framework that combines aggregate metrics of detectability and semantic similarity with interpretable linguistic features, including stylistic markers and topical patterns, to assess how closely LLMs approximate human language in a given dataset. Second, we benchmark nine open-weight LLMs across five calibration strategies, including fine-tuning, stylistic prompting, and context retrieval, on user interactions from X, Bluesky, and Reddit. We find that even after calibration, LLM outputs remain clearly distinguishable from human text, especially in affective tone and emotional expression. Instruction-tuned models generally underperform base models, and larger models do not obviously improve human-likeness. We also identify a trade-off between realism and semantic fidelity: methods that make outputs seem more human often move them further from the content of human responses. Together, these results provide a scalable framework for validation and calibration in LLM-based social simulation while underscoring current limits in reproducing human communication.

title: Field experiments predict ecological response to a large-scale epidemic of an anti-keystone pathogen
abstract:
Knowledge of how pathogens, in the context of a changing environment, shape the structure of ecological communities remains limited, and little information exists on the ability of small-scale field experiments to predict the consequences of large-scale environmental impacts. We addressed these issues using the emergence of a widespread epidemic (sea star wasting disease, SSWD) on rocky intertidal shorelines. Prior experiments demonstrated strong reductions in sessile species diversity in response to the local experimental removal of the sea star
                     Pisaster ochraceus 
                    [R. T. Paine,
                     Am. Nat. 
                     100 
                    , 65–75 (1966); R. T. Paine,
                     Oceologia 
                     15 
                    , 93–120 (1974)] at our site. In surveys of sea star populations over 8 y spanning the onset of the SSWD epidemic,
                     P. ochraceus 
                    populations declined by 90%, then subsequently recovered to about one third of pre-epidemic size under an endemic disease phase. Using four different types of temporal data, we documented large increases in populations of the competitively dominant mussel
                     Mytilus californianus 
                    following
                     P. ochraceus 
                    decline, which were of similar magnitude to those observed in prior field experiments. As in the field experiments, sessile species richness and diversity declined strongly following the onset of the SSWD epidemic as mussels were released from predator control. Our results reveal a strong effect of a pathogen in regulating ecological community structure by disrupting the role of a keystone species, a result anticipated by prior small-scale field experiments.

title: Multidimensional vulnerabilities of informal settlements in the Urban South
abstract:
Informal settlements are widespread and rapidly growing, often associated with high vulnerabilities. However, global-scale understanding on their spatial distribution and complexity of vulnerability is limited. Here, we delineate the informal settlements across a sample of 1,914 cities of the Global South by integrating Sentinel-2 imagery with deep learning models, and we explore the heterogeneity of vulnerability using Urban Informal Settlement Vulnerability Index that encompasses living conditions, social infrastructure, and environmental risk. We found that Urban Informal Settlements cover 12.94 ± 2.52% of their total urban areas (approximately 34.04 × 10
                     3 
                    km
                     2 
                    ), especially in sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and Middle Asia. Sub-Saharan African cities have the highest vulnerability of informal settlements, with 31.75 ± 6.20% of total urban areas being occupied by informal settlements, while East Asian cities exhibit relatively low vulnerability across all dimensions. We also find that urban informal settlements with high environmental exposure are widespread in the Global South, and there is a significantly polarized distribution between “low” and “high” vulnerability categories. The findings highlight the disparate distribution of multidimensional vulnerability in informal settlements across the Urban South, providing a comparative evidence base for further local assessment and context-specific policy discussions related to SDG 11.

In this Review, the authors discuss how single-cell, spatial and functional omics are uncovering gene regulatory mechanisms underlying trophoblast differentiation and maternal interactions and how these insights are advancing understanding of healthy placentation and pregnancy disorders.

Deep single-cell proteomics reveals cellular heterogeneity in the cold response of Arabidopsis leaves
abstract: This study presents a deep single-cell proteomics (SCP) workflow for plant cells, integrating single-cell sorting, sample pretreatment, MS detection, and data processing, with plant-specific optimizations. The workflow quantified approximately 4,200 protein groups from a single mesophyll cell and revealed cell-type-specific cold response dynamics at single-cell resolution. This framework provides a powerful tool for comprehensive insights into plant biology.

title: The Arabidopsis TELLURITE RESISTANCE C is required for the functionality of both photosystems by supplying manganese and calcium
abstract: This study identifies a role for TerC in manganese and calcium homeostasis in chloroplast thylakoids, supporting the function of both photosystem II and photosystem I. Reduced TerC expression causes photosystem II and oxygen-evolving complex phenotypes similar to those of the thylakoid manganese transporter mutant pam71. TerC overexpression restores manganese levels and photosystem II function in pam71, while reduced TerC expression additionally affects photosystem I composition and state transitions.

title: Emerging Paradigms in Strigolactone Biosynthesis, Signaling, and Evolutionary Dynamics
abstract: Summary: This review integrates recent advances in strigolactone biosynthesis, structural diversification, perception, signal attenuation, and evolutionary specialization across plant lineages. It highlights emerging mechanistic links between endogenous and rhizosphere-directed SL pathways, D14-centered signaling, receptor evolution, and interorganismal functions, while identifying unresolved questions that remain central to SL biology.

title: The orchid Gastrodia-derived extracellular vesicles deliver miR535 to suppress a fungal effector and facilitate symbiosis with Armillaria.
abstract: Short Summary: The mycoheterotrophic orchid Gastrodia elata delivers gel-miR535 via its extracellular vesicles (GeEVs) to regulate its fungal partner Armillaria, where the miRNA silences the immunosuppressive effector gene Ag_07049. Ag_07049 encodes a secreted effector that suppresses plant immunity, and its downregulation by gel-miR535 curbs fungal pathogenicity and promotes balanced symbiosis. These findings reveal a previously unknown cross-kingdom RNAi mechanism by which a plant regulates its beneficial fungal partner, extending the RNAi paradigm from plant defense to symbiosis.

title: Functional recomposition of excitatory synaptic inputs to individual neurons in ferret visual cortex after the onset of visual experience
abstract: Jaepel, Tepohl, et al. show that the onset of vision drives rapid expansion and functional recomposition of excitatory synaptic inputs onto visual cortical neurons. Binocular inputs are amplified and aligned around a stable contralateral scaffold while ipsilateral inputs preserve diversity; also, co-tuned inputs become spatially clustered along dendrites.

title: Near‐Infrared Triggered Rechargeable Singlet Oxygen Battery for Sustained Phototherapy: Fast Charging and Long‐Lasting Discharging
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Photodynamic therapy (PDT) for deep‐seated tumors is fundamentally constrained by limited tissue penetration, the ultrashort lifetime of singlet oxygen (
                     1 
                    O
                     2 
                    ), and the lack of reusable oxygen delivery systems. Herein, we report a near‐infrared (NIR) triggered rechargeable “singlet oxygen battery” that enables sustained and cyclic
                     1 
                    O
                     2 
                    supply for enhanced phototherapy. A series of aza‐boron‐dipyrromethene (aza‐BODIPY) probes (NBDP, ABDP, and PBDP) are rationally engineered by integrating distinct
                     1 
                    O
                     2 
                    carriers, among which PBDP exhibits optimal performance. Upon 808 nm irradiation (5 min), PBDP nanoparticles (NPs), as the singlet oxygen battery, generate abundant
                     1 
                    O
                     2 
                    that is reversibly captured via [4+2] cycloaddition with 2‐pyridone to form endoperoxides (EPOs), while simultaneously enabling efficient photothermal conversion. After light cessation, stored
                     1 
                    O
                     2 
                    is thermally released from EPOs for up to 1 h, realizing sustained therapeutic action. Notably, the system supports multiple charging–discharging cycles with negligible performance decay. In vivo NIR‐II imaging reveals efficient tumor accumulation, leading to significant tumor suppression via synergistic sustained PDT/PTT (photothermal therapy) with excellent biocompatibility. This work provides a rechargeable
                     1 
                    O
                     2 
                    storage and release platform by integrating NIR activation, self‐heating‐assisted discharge, and cyclic phototherapeutic capability, offering a promising strategy to improve the efficiency and durability of phototherapy for tumor treatment.

title: Porcupine‐Quill‐Inspired Shape‐Morphing Biointerfaces Disassemble Biofilms
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Mature biofilms are difficult to eradicate because the extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) matrix shields embedded bacteria from chemical and mechanical attack. Here, we report a porcupine‐spine‐inspired photo‐responsive dynamic offensive bio‐interface that dismantles mature biofilms through electrically actuated mechanical penetration and light‐driven oxidative stress. A high‐aspect‐ratio nano‐dagger array undergoes reversible nanoscale deformation (∼110 nm) under an alternating electric field, while a photo‐responsive heterostructure generates a surface photovoltage (∼364 mV) that enhances reactive oxygen species production. Mechanical penetration continuously disrupts the biofilm–surface interface, exposing bacteria within the EPS matrix to oxidative attack. This synergistic mechanism enables nearly complete biofilm eradication under complete immersion in bacterial suspensions of 10
                     9 
                    CFU mL
                     −1 
                    , outperforming representative state‐of‐the‐art systems while maintaining stable antibiofilm activity for at least 10 days without chemical biocides. This work establishes a dynamic offensive strategy for durable self‐cleaning and antifouling interfaces.

title: Microstructure Evolution in Dry‑Coated Sulfidic All‐Solid‐State Battery Cathodes: Investigating Core–Shell Particle Morphology
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    This study investigates continuous extruder mixing and high‑shear batch mixing to promote the formation of core–shell‐like particle coatings for enhanced interfacial contact in dry‑coated sulfidic all‑solid‑state battery cathodes containing 82 wt.% high‐Ni NCM85 (LiNi
                     0.85 
                    Co
                     0.10 
                    Mn
                     0.05 
                    O
                     2 
                    , particle size D
                     50 
                    3.8 µm) cathode active material and 0.5 wt.% polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder. Particle morphology and electrode microstructure are analyzed by particle size measurements, electron microscopy, and X‐ray characterization. Morphological observations indicate that extrusion yields a robust PTFE fibril network and a more homogeneous electrode surface, where deformed Li
                     6 
                    PS
                     5 
                    Cl solid electrolyte particles suggest a core–shell‐like coating. Batch mixing resulted in reduced electrode quality, tensile strength, and microstructure homogeneity. Despite its dedicated mechanofusion process and higher specific mechanical energy input (∼ speed, time), a distinct core–shell‐like coating is not evident for such a small‐particle system. Charge transport features are analyzed in symmetric cells under blocking conditions. Batch‑mixed electrodes attain higher electronic conductivity, whereas extruder‑mixed electrodes achieve higher ionic conductivity. These differences likely arise from microstructural features. Electrochemical characterization of half‑cells demonstrates the enhanced performance of extruder‑mixed electrodes, including higher active material utilization, reduced overpotentials, and improved rate capability. Overall, extruder mixing provides a scalable and effective route for engineering the electrode microstructure.

title: Praseodymium‐Modulated NiFe Layered Double Hydroxide with Enhanced Oxygen Evolution Activity and Extended Durability
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in alkaline water electrolysis suffers from sluggish kinetics and limited catalyst durability. Here, we present a praseodymium (Pr) doping strategy that simultaneously tailors the electronic structure and pore architecture of nickel–iron layered double hydroxide (NiFe‐LDH). Atomically dispersed Pr
                     3+ 
                    expands the interlayer spacing from 0.76 to 0.81 nm and refines the mesoporous network, increasing Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface area by 13.4% and decreasing the average BJH desorption pore size by 12.8%. Strong Pr─O covalency downshifts the Ni 3d band center and reinforces Ni─O hybridization, as corroborated by X‐ray absorption spectroscopy and density functional theory (DFT). These synergistic effects switch the OER rate‐determining step (RDS) from
                     * 
                    O →
                     * 
                    OOH (ΔG = 0.74 eV) to
                     * 
                    OH →
                     * 
                    O (ΔG = 0.28 eV). The optimized Ni
                     2 
                    Fe
                     0.88 
                    Pr
                     0.12 
                    ‐LDH delivers an overpotential of 407 mV at 500 mA cm
                     −2 
                    and sustains 2190 h in half‐cell tests. When integrated into an anion exchange membrane (AEM) electrolyzer, it operates continuously for over 1000 h at industrially relevant current densities, with a moderate voltage drift of 0.202 V (average degradation rate ∼0.20 mV h
                     −1 
                    ). This work establishes a dual electronic and pore engineering route for durable LDH‐based OER catalysts.

title: Hybrid Spring‐Coupled Broadband Energy Harvester Integrated with CuSCN Functionalized Triboelectric Vibration Sensor for Self‐Sustainable Vehicular IoTs
A Dual‐Functional Nanoplatform Targeting the dsDNA–cGAS Axis to Mitigate Disc Degeneration and Aberrant Innervation
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Pathological sensory nerve ingrowth into degenerated intervertebral discs contributes to discogenic pain, yet strategies that concurrently mitigate disc degeneration and pathological innervation remain limited. Here, we found that senescent nucleus pulposus (NP) cells accumulated and released double‐stranded DNA (dsDNA), which reinforced NP cell senescence and matrix catabolism. The accumulated dsDNA also activated cGAS–STING signaling, increased Netrin‐1 expression, and promoted neuronal migration and neurite outgrowth. Guided by these findings, we developed RU@PEI‐ZIF, a dual‐functional nanoplatform combining PEI‐mediated dsDNA scavenging with ZIF‐8‐mediated delivery of the cGAS inhibitor RU.521. RU@PEI‐ZIF displayed dsDNA‐binding capacity, cytocompatibility, and pH‐responsive RU.521 release. In senescent NP cells, RU@PEI‐ZIF reduced extracellular and cytosolic dsDNA, attenuated cGAS–STING‐associated inflammatory and neurotrophic signaling, and reduced NP cell‐mediated neuronal migration and neurite outgrowth. In an animal model of disc degeneration, intradiscal RU@PEI‐ZIF reduced disc degeneration, NP cell senescence, pathological sensory innervation, and pain hypersensitivity. These findings support RU@PEI‐ZIF as a dual‐action nanotherapeutic strategy targeting both disc degeneration and pathological innervation.

title: A Living Multi‐Omics PDX Biobank of High‐Risk Sarcomas Reveals ecDNA‐Driven Oncogene Amplification in Osteosarcoma and Enables Preclinical Precision Oncology
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Sarcomas are rare, genomically heterogeneous malignancies for which prognosis has remained poor and largely unchanged over recent decades. Patient‐derived xenograft (PDX) models are an important tool for cancer research, but their availability and utility remain limited in sarcoma. Here, we establish the SGH sarcoma PDX biobank, a living multi‐omics resource comprising 155 xenografts from 132 patients across 11 sarcoma histotypes, with osteosarcoma as the predominant subtype. This cohort is enriched for high‐risk sarcomas characterized by poor prognosis and widespread copy‐number alterations. Using this biobank, we show that extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA) frequently drives high‐level oncogene amplification in osteosarcoma and that
                     MYC 
                    ecDNA may underlie aggressive disease trajectories. Analyses of paired patient and PDX samples demonstrate that ecDNA is preferentially retained over intrachromosomal amplicons during engraftment and is stably maintained in PDX models. In addition, the PDX models largely recapitulate the histopathological and molecular features of their matched patient tumors while exhibiting distinct clonal evolutionary trajectories during engraftment. Finally, we identified potentially actionable genomic alterations within this PDX cohort, demonstrated genotype‐matched targeted therapy in a KRAS G12C‐mutant PDX model, and prioritized several candidate antibody–drug conjugate targets. Together, this resource provides a platform for biological discovery and preclinical precision oncology for sarcoma.

title: LigHTS: Biomimetic Hydrogel Photo‐Fabrication for Imaging‐Based Ultra‐High‐Throughput Screening
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Imaging‐based ultra‐high‐throughput screening (UHTS) in pharma and biotech still relies on 384‐ and 1536‐well plates whose rigid, flat substrates limit biological fidelity and screening efficiency. Highly biomimetic organoids and organs‐on‐chips improve relevance but at a cost that is incompatible with early screening campaigns. Photopatterned hydrogel scaffolds are potentially scalable, but current approaches lack plate‐scale reproducibility and throughput. To address this gap, we present chemically‐mediated Light‐Intensity Gradients for structured hydrogel functionalization of ultra‐High‐Throughput Screening formats (LigHTS): an all‐optical, in‐well method for parallel photofabrication of biomimetic hydrogels in standard 384‐ and 1536‐well plates. Adding ultraviolet‐light absorber tartrazine to photo‐curable solutions enables hydrogel thickness control by tuning illumination dose without focusing optics. Entire plates are functionalized in parallel with soft (∼1–10 kPa), thin (∼10–200 µm) hydrogels. Simultaneously, film photomasks that encode anisotropies enable control of well‐level gel thickness and topography at UHTS scale. We demonstrate the utility of biomimetic gelatin‐methacrylate‐functionalized UHTS plates using mechanosensitive human cells (HT1080 fibrosarcoma cells, HaCaT epithelial cell colonies, and cardiomyocyte tissues derived from induced pluripotent stem cells), which display stiffness‐ and topography‐dependent phenotypes. Finally, geometric uniformity across the plate meets industry requirements (coefficient of variation <20%), providing a readily available route to enhanced biomimicry in imaging‐based UHTS pipelines.

title:
Low Threshold Vertical Cavity Surface Emitting Lasers Based on CsPbI
                     3 
                    Thin Films
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Metal halide perovskites are attractive gain media for compact coherent light sources. Although the all‐inorganic CsPbI
                     3 
                    is a particularly promising representative, low‐threshold laser operation remains challenging in CsPbI
                     3 
                    thin films due to phase instability and difficulties in preparing high‐quality thin films within low‐loss optical resonators. Here, we demonstrate the first vertical‐cavity surface‐emitting lasers (VCSELs) based on CsPbI
                     3 
                    thin films. The devices are fabricated via planar hot pressing using CsPbI
                     3 
                    thin films prepared through poly(vinylpyrrolidone)‐assisted phase stabilization, which enables simultaneous fabrication of smooth gain layers and well‐defined vertical cavities consisting of two distributed Bragg reflectors. Variable stripe length measurements on the CsPbI
                     3 
                    thin films are used for optical gain spectroscopy to guide the design of the VCSEL cavity mode by a rigorous coupled‐wave analysis. The optimized VCSELs afford optically pumped lasing at 720.4 nm coinciding with the maximum of the optical gain spectrum at a record‐low threshold energy density of only 2.8 µJ cm
                     −2 
                    . Moreover, the VCSELs provide an outstandingly stable operation even under ambient conditions, which is attributed to the encapsulation inherently provided by the VCSEL structure. These results establish a pathway toward practical, low‐threshold perovskite VCSELs and highlight the potential of this platform for next‐generation laser devices.

title: Flexible Integration of Structurally Diverse Spatial Multi‐Omics With AgaeSMO
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Spatial multi‐omics (transcriptome, epigenome, proteome, metabolome, morphomics), provide near‐panoramic omics profiles across tissues. However, cross‐integration of structurally unpaired and underutilized morphomic datasets (e.g., Hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)‐stained images), remains a bottleneck due to inherent differences in spot structures, feature dimensions, and cellular heterogeneities. Here, we present AgaeSMO, an adaptive graph auto‐encoder for versatile cross‐modality integration of both structurally paired and unpaired spatial multi‐omics data. AgaeSMO encodes each omics modality from a cell type‐aware KNN (k‐nearest neighbor) feature graph and a spatial adjacency graph, while leverages GATs (Graph Attention Networks) as the backbone to fuse modalities by learning joint representations through an attention‐weighted module. It specially fuses structurally unpaired modalities, which applies a morphological transformation strategy by designing a cross‐guidance alignment among modalities through graph cross‐attention learning. H&E images are treated as a standalone morphomic modality (rather than auxiliary features) is specially fused with other modalities through image patch embeddings to fully utilize cellular morphological heterogeneities. AgaeSMO is a powerful tool can effectively integrate diverse omics modalities with both paired and unpaired spot architectures. These unique capabilities enable precise spatial domain delineation, micro‐environmental heterogeneity detection, compatible across broad platforms, that outperforming pre‐existing tools. AgaeSMO offers a versatile, robust framework for integrative spatial multi‐omics analysis and facilitates multimodal, biologically interpretable mining.

title: Sex‐ and Time‐Resolved Physiological and Gut Ecosystem Responses to a Food‐Grade Microbiome‐Targeted Intervention in Collegiate Endurance Athletes
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Endurance athletes experience sustained physiological demands during high‐volume training, yet evidence for microbiome‐targeted interventions in real‐world settings remains limited. We conducted a two‐stage, randomized, double‐blind, placebo‐controlled trial in 150 athletes allocated 2:1 to combined probiotics‐yeast extract (CPYE) or placebo for 6 weeks; 44 completers confirmed for the 12th Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region University Games entered an exploratory 6‐week extension with intensified training. Integrating wearable‐derived phenotyping, field‐based cardiorespiratory indices, clinical assessments, fecal metagenomics, and metabolomics, we found that during the randomized short‐term phase, CPYE was associated with changes in device‐estimated maximal oxygen uptake, exercise heart‐rate indices, lactate, and redox biomarkers versus placebo. Exploratory sex‐stratified analyses suggested heterogeneous response patterns, while the selected long‐term extension indicated time‐dependent changes requiring confirmation. Multi‐omics identified sex‐ and phase‐associated differences in microbial taxa, functions, metabolites, and network topology. Indirect‐effect models nominated candidate features (
                     rmlD 
                    ,
                     PISD 
                    ‐linked phosphatidylethanolamine pathways,
                     Bacteroides ovatus 
                    , and folate‐related functions) as potential indirect correlates of host outcomes. These findings support further evaluation of CPYE‐associated responses in collegiate endurance athletes; subgroup, long‐term, network, and indirect‐effect results are hypothesis‐generating.

title: Ultrahigh Interfacial Thermal Conductance across GaN/BAs Interfaces via Atomic‐Level Engineering
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    The integration of gallium nitride (GaN) with ultrahigh‐thermal‐conductivity boron arsenide (BAs) substrates represents a promising pathway for developing next‐generation high‐power devices. The heat dissipation capability of such integrated systems is fundamentally governed by thermal transport across GaN/BAs interfaces, and buffer layers such as Al
                     2 
                    O
                     3 
                    have been widely adopted to accommodate lattice mismatch and facilitate heterointegration. However, the atomic‐scale structural factors governing thermal transport across GaN/BAs interfaces remain unclear, limiting further improvements in interfacial thermal conductance. Herein, we propose an atomic‐scale interfacial structural‐uniformity strategy for engineering ultrahigh thermal conductance across GaN/BAs interfaces using molecular dynamics simulations augmented by machine‐learning interatomic potentials. We show that interfacial structural uniformity plays a more important role than individual bond strength in determining thermal transport across the investigated GaN/BAs interfaces. For instance, the As‐N‐terminated coherent interface exhibits the highest interfacial structural uniformity and achieves an ultrahigh interfacial thermal conductance of approximately 2000 MW·m
                     − 
                     2 
                    ·K
                     − 
                     1 
                    , representing a nearly eightfold enhancement over the experimentally reported Al
                     2 
                    O
                     3 
                    ‐mediated interface (250 MW·m
                     −2 
                    ·K
                     −1 
                    ). Finite‐element analysis indicates that this atomic‐scale optimization directly translates into device‐scale performance, leading to a substantial improvement in overall heat dissipation efficiency. These findings suggest that engineering interfacial structural uniformity offers a promising strategy for achieving high‐efficiency thermal management in next‐generation high‐power electronic devices.

title: The role of methylation and structural variants in shaping the recombination landscape of barley
abstract:
SUMMARY 
                   Meiotic recombination is not only a key mechanism for sexual adaptation in eukaryotes but crucial for the accumulation of beneficial alleles in breeding populations. The effective manipulation of recombination requires, however, a better understanding of the mechanisms regulating the rate and distribution of recombination events in genomes. Here, we identified the genomic features that best explain the recombination variation among a diverse set of segregating populations of barley at a resolution of 1 Mbp and investigated how methylation and structural variants (SVs) determine crossover (CO) hotspots and coldspots at a high resolution of 10 kb. Hotspots were found to be in proximity to genes, and the genetic effects not assigned to methylation were found to be the most important factor explaining differences in recombination rates among populations, along with the methylation and the parental sequence divergence. Interestingly, coldspots were associated with the inheritance of a highly methylated genomic fragment from one parent only, but hotspots were identified at genomic segments where both parents were equally low methylated. The parental sequence divergence was shown to have a sigmoidal correlation with recombination, indicating an upper limit of mismatch among homologous chromosomes for CO formation. SVs were shown to be correlated with CO suppression, and their type and size were not found to influence that effect. The joint act of methylation and SVs was associated with the location of coldspots in barley, and the weight of their relative effect depends on the genomic region. Our findings suggest that recombination in barley is highly predictable, occurring mostly in multiple short sections located in proximity to genes and being modulated by local levels of methylation and SV load.

title:
The
                     SPL8‐YAB3/TCP19 
                    module integrates transcriptional and protein–protein regulatory mechanisms to orchestrate anther development in Arabidopsis
abstract:
SUMMARY 
                   
                    SQUAMOSA PROMOTER BINDING PROTEIN‐LIKE 8 (SPL8) is a plant‐specific transcription factor essential for anther development, but its regulatory partners and downstream mechanisms remain largely unknown. We identified 26 SPL8‐interacting transcription factors by yeast two‐hybrid screening and bimolecular fluorescence complementation (BiFC) assays, with YABBY (YAB) and TEOSINTE BRANCHED 1/CYCLOIDEA/PCF (TCP) family emerging as the predominant interactors. Among these, YAB3 and TCP19 were selected for detailed characterization. Their interactions with SPL8, as well as with each other, were confirmed in plant nuclei by fluorescence resonance energy transfer–fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FRET‐FLIM). Chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing (ChIP‐seq), ChIP‐qPCR, yeast one‐hybrid, and dual‐luciferase assays demonstrated that SPL8 directly binds the regulatory regions of
                     YAB3 
                    and
                     TCP19 
                    and activates their transcription. Dexamethasone‐inducible expression assays further showed that this induction occurs independently of de novo protein synthesis. Expression analyses revealed overlapping spatial and temporal patterns of
                     SPL8 
                    ,
                     YAB3 
                    , and
                     TCP19 
                    during early anther development, particularly in tapetal cells, microspore mother cells, and vascular tissues. Genetic and cellular analyses of promoter‐driven SRDX repression lines showed that
                     SPL8 
                    ,
                     YAB3 
                    , and
                     TCP19 
                    regulate anther morphogenesis, tapetal differentiation, meiotic progression, and microspore development. Although individual family members exhibited functional redundancy, their repression caused severe developmental defects and male sterility. Together, these findings establish the
                     SPL8 
                    –
                     YAB3 
                    /
                     TCP19 
                    module as a multilayered regulatory system in which
                     SPL8 
                    controls anther development through both transcriptional activation of
                     YAB3 
                    and
                     TCP19 
                    and physical interaction with these proteins, expanding the regulatory framework of
                     SPL 
                    ‐mediated reproductive development.

title: RBMS1 Contributes to Early Arteriovenous Fistula Neointimal Remodeling Through Modulation of VSMC Phenotypic Responses
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Arteriovenous fistula (AVF) creation initiates stage‐dependent remodeling of the venous outflow tract. Neointimal hyperplasia is a common component of this response, but its post‐transcriptional regulation remains unclear. Here, analyses of human AVF datasets and tissue specimens characterized RNA‐binding motif single‐stranded interacting protein 1 (RBMS1) expression in postoperative AVFs, whereas a day‐14 mouse AVF model and cultured vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) were used to investigate its role in early neointimal remodeling. Smooth muscle‐targeted RBMS1 overexpression aggravated neointimal formation, whereas conditional RBMS1 deletion attenuated it in murine AVFs. In cultured VSMCs, RBMS1 overexpression enhanced proliferation, migration, and the transition from contractile to synthetic marker expression, whereas RBMS1 silencing produced the opposite effects. Mechanistically, RBMS1 bound myelin protein zero‐like 1 (MPZL1) mRNA and promoted exon 5 skipping, generating the MPZL1‐Δ5 isoform. MPZL1‐Δ5 overexpression reproduced selected RBMS1‐associated VSMC responses and increased neointimal hyperplasia in vivo, including in RBMS1‐deficient mice. MPZL1‐Δ5 further interacted with GTPase‐activating protein SH3 domain‐binding protein 1 (G3BP1) and enhanced protein kinase B (AKT) activation, whereas G3BP1 silencing attenuated RBMS1‐ or MPZL1‐Δ5‐induced VSMC responses. Together, these findings identify the RBMS1–MPZL1‐Δ5–G3BP1–AKT pathway as an important VSMC‐associated mechanism contributing to neointimal remodeling during the early postoperative phase of experimental AVFs.

title: Hydrogen Production from Ammonia Electrochemical Cracking
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Utilizing NH
                     3 
                    as a H
                     2 
                    carrier has been proposed to address the storage and transportation bottlenecks of the green hydrogen supply chain. NH
                     3 
                    thermal cracking is a conventional technique for H
                     2 
                    recovery after transport, but its infrastructure‐intensive nature limits its application in decentralized H
                     2 
                    production scenarios. Consequently, ammonia electrolysis, coined “e‐cracking” in this article, is proposed as a complementary technique for such scenarios. This emerging technique couples hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) with ammonia oxidation reaction (AOR), which was previously studied in the context of ammonia fuel cells. While thermal cracking has been extensively investigated regarding catalyst development and economic feasibility, e‐cracking is at an early stage and lacks such efforts, as reflected by its lower technology readiness level (TRL). To bridge this gap, this Perspective provides a comprehensive analysis of e‐cracking addressing both aspects. We begin with an overview of catalyst development for both techniques and then conduct a techno‐economic analysis (TEA) based on reported performance data. By comparing the levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH), we demonstrate e‐cracking's theoretical potential for lower costs and identify the current limitations arising from catalytic performance. Finally, we provide an outlook on research directions and strategies to advance NH
                     3 
                    e‐cracking toward practical implementation.

title: Architecting Anisotropic Force‐Responsive Bidirectional High‐Contrast Three‐Color Fluorescence Switches via Effective Molecular Modulation for High‐Security Information Storage
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Although bidirectional three‐color fluorescent molecular switches triggered by anisotropic force are promising for enhancing the security of information storage, the engineering and development of such force‐responsive smart emissive materials face significant challenges, rendering them extremely rare. Here, 13 uncommon tricolored mechanofluorochromic luminogens were obtained through efficient molecular engineering strategies synergistically integrating substituent variation and positional isomeric approaches, three of which exhibited exceedingly scarce force‐induced hypsochromic and bathochromic bidirectional fluorescence responses. More specifically, employing dibenzofulvene as the core scaffold, a family of 20 fluorene‐based fluorogenic compounds was elaborately constructed by incorporating pyrene, tetraphenylethene, and three isomeric carbazole moieties at the conjugated extension sites, with phenyl and regioisomeric trifluoromethylphenyl groups respectively attached to the two flanking positions. Next, a three‐step high‐efficiency screening protocol was devised for these luminogens: first assessing mechanoresponsive fluorescence behaviors, then evaluating the three‐color mechanofluorochromic capabilities, and finally determining whether the selected force‐responsive tricolored fluorescence switches could realize bidirectional three‐color fluorescence switching after sequential grinding from gentle to vigorous. Ultimately, 3 luminogens featuring ultra‐rare bidirectional three‑color mechanofluorochromism were identified. Impressively, based on the screened force‐triggered bidirectional high‐contrast tricolor fluorescent switch
                     
                      TPE‐
                       o 
                      ‐CF
                       3 
                     
                    , two advanced dual‑layer information storage systems were established, which could effectively safeguard the security of the stored information.

title: Aged ZnO Nanoparticles Promote Breast Cancer Lung Metastasis by Remodeling the Pulmonary Microenvironment Through the CXCL10/Wnt/β‐Catenin Axis
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Our previous work demonstrated that zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO NPs) undergo physicochemical transformations during environmental aging, forming a composite mixture of zinc hydroxide carbonate, nanosized ZnO, and Zn
                     2+ 
                    (termed aged ZnO NPs). Compared to their pristine counterparts, aged ZnO NPs exhibit significantly enhanced mutagenicity and malignant transformation capacity in mouse embryonic fibroblasts. However, their potential role in cancer initiation and progression in vivo remains unresolved. Here, we provide the first evidence that subchronic pulmonary exposure to aged ZnO NPs markedly accelerates lung metastasis and colony formation in a mouse model of breast cancer. Single‐cell transcriptomic profiling (scRNA‐seq) revealed that aged NPs remodel the metastatic microenvironment by recruiting M2 macrophages and myeloid‐derived suppressor cells, and by activating cancer‐associated fibroblasts. These findings were corroborated by analysis of public scRNA‐seq datasets. Mechanistically, CXCL10 derived from macrophages and fibroblasts was identified as a key mediator of metastasis via activation of the Wnt/β‐catenin pathway. Notably, pharmacological inhibition of the CXCL10/CXCR3 axis effectively attenuated NP‐induced metastasis. Collectively, this study uncovers the cellular and molecular mechanisms by which aged ZnO NPs potentiate breast cancer metastasis, highlighting the need to incorporate environmental aging processes into the risk assessment of nanomaterials.

title: High‐Density‐Cluster Ru Catalyst Substitute for Pt/C Benchmark Improves Membrane Water Electrolysis
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    The hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is of great importance for the renewable energy conversion to hydrogen fuel via water electrolysis. However, the current benchmark Pt/C catalyst suffers from high cost, pH sensitivity, and deficient durability, severely restricting the large‐scale development of membrane water electrolysis. Herein, we develop a cost‐effective Pt‐free catalyst featuring high‐density, ultrafine Ru nanoclusters modified with CoP and uniformly dispersed on nitrogen‐doped carbon films (NCF). This catalyst achieves not only superior HER activity across a wide pH range but also robust stability at ampere‐level large current densities, manifesting as a competitive alternative to commercial Pt/C. Typically, Ru‐CoP/NCF exhibits an overpotential of only 22 mV at 10 mA cm
                     −2 
                    in acidic media, with the mass activity and price activity 1.21 and 2.18 times higher than Pt/C, respectively. A proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer using Ru‐CoP/NCF catalyst delivers a high current density of 1.0 A cm
                     −2 
                    at a voltage of merely 1.67 V and sustains long‐term operation for 780 h with a minimal decay rate of 84 µV h
                     −1 
                    . This Ru‐CoP/NCF catalyst thus demonstrates practical potential for the development of non‐Pt membrane electrodes.

title: A Dual‐Delivery System Designed to Overcome EV‐Mediated Ferroptosis Resistance for Efficient Solid Tumor Therapy
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Tumor‐derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) are emerging as critical mediators of metabolic adaptation, yet their role in orchestrating ferroptosis resistance within the tumor microenvironment remains poorly understood. Here, we show that highly malignant osteosarcoma (OS) cells respond to ferroptotic stress by secreting EVs enriched with Alpha‐enolase (ENO1). These EVs‐ENO1 not only bolster the antioxidant capacity of tumor cells but also confer widespread ferroptosis resistance to macrophages and neutrophils, fostering an immunosuppressive niche. To disrupt this metabolic defense, we developed an OS‐targeting lipid nanoparticle (LNP) system for the synergistic delivery of BAP1 mRNA and ENO1 siRNA. We demonstrate that this dual‐delivery platform enhances ferroptosis through two complementary regulatory pathways, BAP1/SLC7A11 and ENO1/GPX4, leading to potent lipid peroxidation and tumor cell death. In syngeneic orthotopic and lung metastasis models, these targeted LNPs significantly suppress tumor progression and catalyze anti‐tumor immunity by activating M1‐type macrophages and cytotoxic T cells. Our findings identify the secretion of EVs‐ENO1 as a key reactive mechanism against ferroptosis and provide a translatable nanomedicine strategy to overcome metabolic and epigenetic resistance in solid tumors.

title: Dual‐Dynamically Crosslinked Nanogels Enable Prolonged Ocular Retention for Multimodal Dry Eye Therapy
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Dry eye disease (DED), a chronic disorder affecting nearly half the global population, is perpetuated by oxidative stress, inflammation, and tear film instability. Constrained by short precorneal residence and monotherapy, DED therapies necessitate frequent dosing and polypharmacy, leaving unmet needs for prolonged ocular retention and multimodal intervention. Herein, we develop berberine (BBR)‐loaded dual‐dynamically crosslinked nanogels (BBR@MPN‐NGs) integrating tannic acid (TA)‐zinc metal‐polyphenol networks with carboxymethyl chitosan/aldehyde‐functionalized poly(ethylene glycol) Schiff base networks, enabling a single‐platform multimodal therapy combining antioxidant, anti‐inflammatory, and lubricating capacities. Capitalizing on dual‐dynamic synergy, BBR@MPN‐NGs exhibit 1‐year colloidal and antioxidant stability alongside lubricity, while leveraging TA‐mediated adhesion and Schiff base reversibility to sustain corneal BBR exposure for 24 h, enabling once‐daily dosing. In murine DED models, BBR@MPN‐NGs outperform first‐line cyclosporine A and dexamethasone in promoting corneal epithelial repair and tear secretion. Mechanistically, the nanogels reprogram the pathological microenvironment by scavenging reactive oxygen species, attenuating pro‑inflammatory macrophage polarization, and suppressing c‐Jun N‐terminal kinase signaling to reduce pro‐inflammatory gene expression. Notably, the preservative‐free nanogels passed sterility and endotoxin testing, showing no ocular or systemic toxicity, which supports biosafety. These dual‐dynamically crosslinked nanogels enable reduced‐frequency and shortened treatment duration, offering an integrated strategy for complex ocular surface diseases requiring sustained multimodal intervention.

title: Advancing Biotherapeutic Treatment of Ulcerative Colitis Using Lipid Mesophases: Formulation Design and Preclinical Validation
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Biotherapeutics are required to achieve high remission rates in patients with severe ulcerative colitis (UC); however, adverse effects, complex dosing regimens, administration routes, and low patient compliance limit their widespread clinical use. Given the localized nature of UC, this study aimed to develop localized delivery strategies for infliximab (IFX), an anti‐tumor necrosis factor‐α (TNF‐α) monoclonal antibody recommended for moderately‐to‐severely active UC. Exploiting the intrinsic biocompatibility, mucoadhesion, and protein‐entrapment capacity of lipid mesophases (LMPs), IFX was encapsulated within the gel matrix, providing protection against enzymatic and environmental degradation. IFX‐LMPs were designed for targeted delivery to inflamed colonic tissues via rectal or oral administration, with oral dosage forms manufactured either by 3D printing or by encapsulation into enteric capsules. A comprehensive physicochemical characterization was performed to elucidate mesophase self‐assembly and its relationship with IFX release profiles in biorelevant fluids. The rectal gel demonstrated strong mucoadhesion, while LMP‐loaded enteric capsules enabled effective colon targeting. In a prophylactic treatment setting, LMP‐based formulations significantly attenuated disease progression and the development of severe inflammation compared with subcutaneous IFX. Overall, this study establishes a biocompatible delivery platform that enables colon‐targeted IFX release, representing a promising therapeutic strategy for UC using biotherapeutics.

title: Ionically Counter‐Programmable Phase‐Separation of Superstable Star‐Biopolyamide Coacervates for Electrothermally‐Responsive Pseudosolid Smart Windows
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Thermoresponsive polymers are highly anticipated for passive thermochromic smart windows, yet the instability and too‐high mobility of their light‐scattering states for separated phases remain significant hurdles. To address these challenges, we report a design concept for pyrrolidone‐based star‐polyamides synthesized from itaconic acid and cadaverine, whose architecture provides exceptional sensitivity to external stimuli. In a stark departure from the classical Hofmeister series, Ca
                     2+ 
                    initiates an anomalous salting‐in effect that contrasts with the Na
                     + 
                    ‐induced salting‐out. DFT/MD calculations reveal that pyrrolidone moderately coordinates with Ca
                     2+ 
                    without disrupting its hydration shell, thereby imparting a dense positive charge to the coacervate surfaces. Crucially, the cationic surface charge endows the coacervates with light‐scattering bodies with superior dispersion stability, surpassing conventional PNIPAM by over 20‐fold. The system maintains robust stability at 5 mol/L, a regime where conventional thermoresponsive polymers inevitably fail. An applied electric field enables spatial control of transparency, creating a dual electro‐thermal responsive system for energy‐efficient, sustainable smart windows. Furthermore, the Ca
                     2+ 
                    salting‐in effects enable coacervation in a high polymer concentration range over 50% to establish pseudosolidity, which provides a versatile platform for next‐generation electro‐thermal soft systems, ranging from implantable biosensors to battery‐operated smart windows.

title: Mechanochemical Engineered Sulfur Copolymers Onto Group 13 and Related Fillers Through Lewis Acid‐Base Pairing
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Group 13 and related fillers are cornerstone components for advanced composites, yet their severe interfacial incompatibility with organic matrices inherently limits their practical efficacy. Conventional surface modification strategies remain fundamentally constrained by a heavy reliance on hazardous solvents, matrix curing inhibition, and structural degradation of the fillers. Herein, we report a solvent‐free mechanochemical copolymerization strategy that establishes an universal, non‐destructive interfacial engineering paradigm for diverse Group 13 and related fillers (nano‐Al, B
                     4 
                    C, and ZrB
                     2 
                    ). By directly architecting sulfur‐containing polymer coatings on filler surfaces, this approach elegantly exploits intrinsic Lewis acid–base pairing between electron‐deficient metal/metalloid sites and electron‐rich sulfur moieties. Mechanistically, the resulting electronic configurations and coordination chemistry are systematically elucidated via a synergistic combination of XPS, solid‐state
                     11 
                    B NMR, and DFT calculations, confirming the formation of robust S–Al and S–B coordinative networks. The extraordinary universality of this matrix‐agnostic platform is validated by incredible performance increments across three distinct frontiers, driving a staggering 666% surge in combustion enthalpy for nano‐Al fuels, a 33% ablation reduction for ZrB
                     2 
                    thermal shields, and concurrent ∼270% elevations in both strength and toughness for B
                     4 
                    C structural composites. Ultimately, this environmentally benign protocol paves a versatile avenue toward the green synthesis of high‐performance hybrids.

title:
Hepatic Lipid Stress Drives Metabolic Dysfunction‐Associated Steatohepatitis Progression through FTO
                     O 
                    ‐GlcNAcylation‐Induced m6A Demethylation of
                     HRAS
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Metabolic dysfunction‐associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is driven by nutrient stress through incompletely defined epigenetic mechanisms. This study demonstrates that lipid stress activates the hexosamine biosynthesis pathway (HBP), elevating
                     O 
                    ‐linked β‐N‐acetylglucosamine (
                     O 
                    ‐GlcNAc) modification of the N6‐methyladenosine (m6A) demethylase fat mass and obesity‐associated protein (FTO) at Ser195. This post‐translational modification recruits the deubiquitinase ubiquitin‐specific peptidase 20 (USP20), displaces the E3 ligase F‐box and WD repeat domain containing 7 (FBXW7), and enhances FTO protein stability and m6A demethylase activity.
                     O 
                    ‐GlcNAc‐dependent FTO activation removes m6A from Harvey rat sarcoma viral oncogene homolog (
                     HRAS 
                    ) mRNA, evades YTH N6‑methyladenosine RNA binding protein 2 (YTHDF2)‑mediated degradation, and prolongs transcript half‐life. Subsequent HRAS upregulation activates the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway, driving hepatic steatosis and inflammation. Administration of a novel cell‐penetrating peptide (CPP) designed to block FTO
                     O 
                    ‐GlcNAcylation at Ser195 effectively ameliorates MASH progression in vitro and in vivo. These findings establish FTO
                     O 
                    ‐GlcNAcylation as a druggable metabolic‐epigenetic checkpoint in MASH pathogenesis, revealing a promising therapeutic strategy for this increasingly prevalent liver disease.

title: Hardware‐Native Gaussian Sampling With Probabilistic Ising Machines for Modern Communication Paradigms
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Modern communication systems increasingly shift computation to edge devices, where post quantum signing, generative AI and semantic communication must operate under strict energy, latency and memory constraints. A central bottleneck in these workloads is Gaussian sampling. In Falcon class signatures, sampling accounts for about 25% of operations and about 65% of signing time. In diffusion inference, repeated Gaussian injection across denoising steps makes edge deployment costly. Here we show that probabilistic Ising machines provide a hardware native route to random Gaussian distributions with both tunable variance and sampling density with two independent parameters. We compare fully digital field‐programmable gate array (FPGA) and FPGA‐spintronic implementations with software implementation. At matched sampling precision, the proposed FPGA sampler reduces the dynamic power and logic utilization of the Gaussian‐sampling core by approximately 4.0‐fold and 4.4‐fold, respectively, relative to the isolated Falcon core. A projected ASIC implementation in 28 nm CMOS is estimated to consume approximately 8 mW. Image generation quality quantified with well‐established metrics is preserved in an open‐source diffusion pipeline. These results establish probabilistic Ising machines as an efficient and scalable platform for Gaussian sampling in post quantum cryptography, edge generative inference and semantic communication.

title: One‐Step Induction of Oogonia‐Like and Pro‐Spermatogonia‐Like Cells From Porcine Pluripotent Stem Cells
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Pigs share a germ cell regulatory network highly similar to that of humans, yet lack a robust system for inducing and expanding germ cells from pluripotent stem cells, impeding large‐animal gametogenesis research. Here, we established a modular platform capable of efficiently inducing and long‐term expanding porcine germ cell‐like cells directly from pluripotent stem cells. We first developed a one‐step method to induce pro‐spermatogonia‐like cells (activating SOX17) and oogonia‐like cells (activating SOX17/TFAP2C) from porcine pre‐gastrulation epiblast stem cells (pgEpiSCs) harboring a NANOS3‐tdTomato (NT) reporter, via activation of exogenous transcription factors. Single‐cell transcriptome profiling revealed a differentiation trajectory from pgEpiSCs through primordial germ cell‐like cells (PGCLCs) to pro‐spermatogonia/oogonia‐like cells, with concomitant differentiation of gonadal somatic cells. Functional analyses demonstrate that EGF activates core PGC network and is essential for porcine PGCLCs survival in a xenogeneic reconstituted ovary, BMP4 drives NANOS3 and DDX4 expression, and IWR1 enhances germ cell differentiation by suppressing mesodermal programs. Finally, to address the challenge of cell quantity, we established a long‐term expansion module based on FGF2, IWR1, and EGF that sustains NT‐positive cells for up to 120 days while preserving their early PGC and pro‐spermatogonia‐like molecular characteristics. Our study provides new insights into porcine gametogenesis and reproductive development across species.

title: Sequence‐Controlled Copolymers Through Selective Ring‐Opening Polymerization of Multiunit Macrolactones
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   A new strategy for the synthesis of sequence‐controlled polymers (SCP), in which increased ester reactivity by the introduction of neighboring glycolate units within a multiunit macrolactone, was developed. DFT calculations and model reactions show that the proximity of glycolate functionality adjacent to an ester group increases the reactivity, leading to a selective ring‐opening. By exploiting this feature, sequence‐controlled polymers were prepared from cyclic polyester‐containing macrolactones through ring‐opening polymerization (ROP) using transesterification catalysts (tBuOLi and 1,8‐diazabicyclo[5.4.0]undec‐7‐ene (DBU)).

title: Lattice Disorder in CuI Enables Filament‐Free Transparent Memristors
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    The realization of invisible neuromorphic electronics hinges on transparent memories that reconcile high optical transparency with stable analog tunability, which is a challenge unmet by conventional filamentary devices. Here, we introduce an alloyed Cu
                     1‐ 
                     
                       x 
                     
                    Ag
                     
                       x 
                     
                    I halide transparent semiconductor with dual ionic‐electronic character, which enables a filament‐free switching platform. Ag
                     + 
                    incorporation induces lattice distortions within the γ‐phase CuI matrix, expanding interstitial channels and lowering the migration barrier without phase transition. This activates room‐temperature ion migration to dynamically modulate the p‐type hole conductance. Asymmetric electrodes induce spatially distributed ion migration and interfacial modulation, avoiding localized metallic percolation. In situ TEM and EDS mapping confirm reversible Cu
                     + 
                    /Ag
                     + 
                    redistribution without continuous conductive pathways. Pt/Cu
                     1‐ 
                     
                       x 
                     
                    Ag
                     
                       x 
                     
                    I/Ag devices exhibit > 80% transparency, low‐voltage readout, and > 2‐year retention. They emulate synaptic plasticity and achieve high‐accuracy handwritten digit recognition. Our findings establish a design strategy for transparent memristors, enabling reliable neuromorphic hardware via ionically mediated electronic transport.

title: Meningeal Lymphatic LTBR Deficiency Links Spinal Cord Injury to Secondary Brain Pathology
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Spinal cord injury (SCI) induces secondary brain pathology, but the mechanisms linking spinal and brain injury remain unclear. Here, we identify meningeal lymphatic dysfunction as a contributor to secondary brain pathology after SCI. In mice, meningeal lymphatic vessels (mLVs) progressively deteriorated from 14 to 56 days post‐injury, accompanied by glymphatic dysfunction. In patients with SCI, diffusion tensor imaging along the perivascular space (DTI‐ALPS) revealed impaired glymphatic function, which correlated with motor cortical and hippocampal atrophy. mLVs ablation exacerbated neuroinflammation, neuronal loss, impaired hippocampal neurogenesis, and motor and cognitive deficits, whereas VEGF‐C‐mediated lymphatic restoration ameliorated these abnormalities. Integrated single‐cell and bulk transcriptomics identified reduced LTBR expression in meningeal lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs) after SCI.
                     Ltbr 
                    knockdown in LECs further exacerbated SCI‐induced lymphatic dysfunction and secondary brain pathology, whereas LEC‐specific
                     Ltbr 
                    overexpression promoted lymphatic repair and improved neurological outcomes. In human LECs, LTBR enhanced proliferation, migration, and tube formation, with PI3K‐AKT signaling potentially contributing to these effects. These findings establish meningeal lymphatic dysfunction as an important component of secondary brain pathology after SCI and identify LTBR as a potential regulator of lymphatic repair.

title: A Novel Reactive Oxygen Species‐Responsive Bone‐Targeted Nanoplatform Based on Cloperastine Attenuates Ovariectomy‐Induced Bone Loss by Inhibiting Osteoclast Oxidative Phosphorylation
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Postmenopausal osteoporosis is caused by excessive osteoclast‐mediated bone resorption. This study identifies mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) as a tractable metabolic target for antiresorptive therapy. A literature‐guided drug repurposing screen focused on compounds reported to affect OXPHOS or related energy metabolism identified cloperastine (Clo) as a potent suppressor of receptor activator of nuclear factor κB ligand‐induced osteoclastogenesis. Clo reduces mitochondrial respiration, downregulates OXPHOS complex proteins, decreases mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS), dissipates the mitochondrial membrane potential, disrupts mitochondrial dynamics, and collectively impairs osteoclast differentiation and bone resorption in vitro. Asp8‐modified methionine/lysine‐based ROS‐responsive polyethylene glycol micelles encapsulating Clo (Clo/Asp8‐PMK‐MCs) were developed for potential bone‐directed delivery. These micelles (∼220 nm; −3.60 ± 0.09 mV) exhibit ROS‐triggered disassembly and accelerated Clo release under oxidative conditions. Fluorescence tracking of DID‐labeled micelles shows stronger skeletal signals with Asp8 modification than without it. Clo/Asp8‐PMK‐MCs inhibit osteoclast differentiation and bone resorption, whereas bioactive Asp8‐PMK‐MCs simultaneously promote osteoblast differentiation and matrix mineralization. In ovariectomized mice, Clo/Asp8‐PMK‐MCs attenuate ovariectomy‐induced bone loss, preserve trabecular bone microarchitecture, reduce osteoclast‐related parameters and serum bone resorption markers, and enhance bone formation. These findings support Clo/Asp8‐PMK‐MCs as a potential OXPHOS‐targeted nanomedicine integrating Clo‐mediated antiresorptive activity with carrier‐mediated osteogenic activity to attenuate estrogen deficiency‐induced bone loss.

title: Structural Variants in the Human Genome Associated With Gut Microbiome and Blood Metabolic Traits With Potential Causal Links
abstract:
ABSTRACT
