                    Research on genetic variants affecting the gut microbiome and blood metabolites has mainly focused on single nucleotide variants (SNPs), leaving structural variants (SVs) largely unexplored. Here, we analyzed high‐coverage (∼42×) whole‐genome sequencing data from 2002 individuals and constructed a catalog of 138 859 high‐confidence SVs, including 44.3% variants not represented in public SV resources. Genome‐wide association analyses of 22 519 common SVs identified 30 microbiome‐associated and 48 metabolite‐associated SV loci, including 19 study‐wide significant associations. Notable signals included an Asian‐specific 6.5k deletion at
                     TENT2 
                    associated with
                     Coprobacillus sp. 29_1 
                    abundance (β = 0.158,
                     p 
                    = 2.5 × 10
                     −9 
                    ) and a deletion covering
                     HBA1/HBA2/HBM/HBQ1 
                    linked to nine blood metabolic traits (strongest for MCV; β = ‐0.570,
                     p 
                    = 1.22 × 10
                     −91 
                    ). Conditional and variance‐partitioning analyses indicated that SVs capture complementary genetic information beyond tested SNP signals. SV‐based Mendelian randomization delineated putative directional relationships, including
                     Clostridium ramosum 
                    with serum uric acid and hyperuricemia. In vitro experiments further supported three predicted metabolite–microbe interactions, showing that vitamin K1 inhibited
                     Coprococcus comes 
                    , hydroxyproline inhibited
                     Veillonella parvula 
                    , and cysteine promoted
                     Fusobacterium mortiferum 
                    growth. Together, our study provides a comprehensive SVs resource and highlights SVs as overlooked genetic determinants of host‐microbiome‐metabolome interactions relevant to human physiology and disease.

title: Sustainable Hydrogel‐Forming Microneedle‐Reservoir Patches for Transdermal Delivery of Hydrophilic Macromolecules: Biopolymers, Green Manufacturing and Translation
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Hydrophilic biomacromolecules, including insulin, peptides, proteins and vaccine antigens, have transformed modern therapeutics, yet their delivery remains dominated by injections because the stratum corneum (SC) severely restricts passive transport of large and polar molecules. Microneedles have created a route through this barrier, but many existing systems remain limited by low loading capacity, burst release, weak dose control, microbiological quality requirements, short‐term stability, and poor manufacturing scalability. This review critically examines hydrogel‐forming microneedle (HFMN)‐reservoir patches as an emerging architecture for controlled transdermal biomacromolecule delivery. Rather than treating microneedles as isolated projections, it positions the patch as an integrated multilayer device comprising a skin‐interfacing hydrogel conduit, a drug reservoir, a diffusion‐control layer, and a protective backing. Particular emphasis is placed on sustainable polymers, including cellulose derivatives, alginate, chitosan (CS), polyethylene oxide (PEO), carboxymethyl chitosan (CMCS) and oxidized polysaccharides, together with scalable manufacturing routes such as pressurized gyration (PG). The review also evaluates fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC)‐dextran and other model macromolecules, highlighting what they prove about physical transport and what they cannot prove about therapeutic bioactivity. Finally, design rules are proposed for next‐generation microneedle‐reservoir patches that integrate biomaterial selection, release control, green manufacturing, and translational requirements.

title: Low‐Density Lipoprotein Receptor‐Targeted Biomimetic Nanoplatform Suppresses Glioblastoma Stemness and Remodels Antitumor Immunity via Dual Metabolic Disruption
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Glioblastoma (GBM) remains one of the most lethal malignancies because durable tumor control is constrained by limited brain‐tumor drug exposure, metabolic plasticity, stem‐like tumor states, and an immunosuppressive microenvironment. We developed apolipoprotein B fragment‐decorated nanoparticles co‐loaded with regorafenib and erythrodiol (ApoBf‐R/E@NPs), a low‐density lipoprotein receptor‐oriented biomimetic nanoplatform that couples brain‐tumor delivery with coordinated dual‐drug exposure. Fixed‐ratio combination‐index analysis demonstrated synergy between the two agents. Regorafenib disrupts autophagy‐associated nutrient salvage and restricts angiogenic support, whereas erythrodiol stabilizes ATP‐binding cassette transporter A1 and depletes cellular cholesterol. These complementary perturbations converge on ATP depletion, mitochondrial dysfunction, and suppression of phosphoinositide 3‐kinase/protein kinase B and mitogen‐activated protein kinase signaling. Across established and patient‐derived GBM models, treatment broadly impaired tumor‐cell survival while suppressing stemness‐associated programs and reducing viability and tumorsphere persistence in patient‐derived glioma stem‐like cell cultures. Treatment also promoted an immunogenic cell death‐associated tumor‐cell state and antitumor immune remodeling. In immunocompetent GBM models, ApoBf‐R/E@NPs showed preferential intracranial tumor‐associated delivery, suppressed orthotopic and untreated distal tumor growth, and delayed postoperative regrowth, accompanied by systemic immune remodeling and expansion of memory‐associated T‐cell populations. These findings establish a blood‐brain barrier‐oriented nanodelivery strategy that couples complementary metabolic vulnerabilities to broad GBM control, stem‐like compartment suppression, and antitumor immunity.

title:
CW‐Pumped Amplified Spontaneous Emission From Thermally Evaporated CsPbBr
                     3 
                    Films
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Lead halide perovskites are widely reported as promising optical gain media for optoelectronic applications in the short‐pulse regime. However, their operation under continuous‐wave excitation remains severely limited by thermal accumulation and gain instability. Here, we present a systematic study of amplified spontaneous emission under long‐pulse and continuous‐wave excitation in thermally evaporated CsPbBr
                     3 
                    thin films, providing direct insight into the limits of sustained optical gain in perovskite materials. By correlating excitation pulse duration, substrate thermal conductivity, temperature‐dependent emission properties, and time‐resolved carrier dynamics, we establish a physical framework linking thermal dissipation to gain stability. We identify excitation‐time thresholds and define optimal operating regimes, demonstrating sustained amplified spontaneous emission for pulse widths up to 30 µs in films without encapsulation or additional post‐processing. Our results reveal that light‐induced thermal accumulation is the dominant mechanism limiting amplified spontaneous emission under extended excitation and highlight thermal management as a critical design parameter for steady‐state optical gain. These findings provide practical design rules for perovskite gain media and represent a key step toward electrically pumped, continuous‐wave‐performing perovskite superluminescent and laser diodes.

title: Mitochondrial Protection and Neural Repair via ROS‐Responsive Biomimetic Nanoparticles in Intracerebral Hemorrhage
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH)‐induced secondary brain injury is driven in part by oxidative stress, blood‐brain barrier disruption, mitochondrial dysfunction, and neuronal loss. Here, we developed a brain endothelial cell membrane‐coated ROS‐responsive biomimetic nanoplatform (NP@D+M) for co‐delivery of the VDAC1 inhibitor DIDS and the mitochondrial fission inhibitor Mdivi‐1. NP@D+M showed uniform size, preserved endothelial membrane proteins, and accelerated drug release under elevated H2O2. In ICH‐like neuronal injury models, NP@D+M enhanced uptake, protected neurites, reduced LDH release and apoptosis, restored mitochondrial membrane potential and ATP production, and suppressed mitochondrial ROS. Mechanistically, NP@D+M disrupted aberrant LPAR1‐VDAC1 interaction, inhibited mPTP opening, and restored mitochondrial homeostasis; LPAR1 gain‐ and loss‐of‐function experiments confirmed its role in the mitochondrial protective effect. Targeted metabolomics and single‐cell transcriptomics further supported improved energy metabolism and attenuated injury‐associated cellular responses. In vivo, NP@D+M crossed the BBB, accumulated in brain parenchyma, protected perihematomal neurons, improved mitochondrial function, and alleviated neurological and cognitive deficits without obvious systemic toxicity. These findings identify a LPAR1‐VDAC1‐mPTP‐targeted nanotherapeutic strategy for mitochondrial protection and neural repair after ICH.

title: Sea Cucumber‐Inspired Double‐Network Biopolymer Hydrogels for Programmable Soft Machines
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Engineering biopolymer‐based hydrogels with robust load‐bearing capacity, reversible mechanical programmability, and adaptive actuation remains difficult due to weak physical crosslinking and porous structure. Inspired by the mutable dermis of sea cucumbers, a collagen–alginate double‐network elastomeric (CoDE) hydrogel integrates a covalently crosslinked collagen cryogel scaffold with an ionically crosslinked alginate sacrificial network. This hydrogel system is inherently biocompatible and biodegradable. Compression‐induced scaffold densification and ionic locking enable broad tuning of the compressive response, sustaining programmable peak stresses up to 16 MPa. CoDE exhibits reversible lock–unlock states while fully preserving its peak stress, elastic modulus, and energy dissipation after repeated loading to 85% compressive strain. Cyclic compressive loading mechanically “trains” the biopolymer hydrogel by altering its microstructure. Chemically triggering the release of stored elastic energy in the biopolymer network generates actuation forces. Further, CoDE is tested as a bio‐inspired, externally driven swimmer that can be subjected to large‐scale, repetitive deformation with predictable kinematics that match finite‐element simulations at the device level. The CoDE platform has future applications for building soft‐material machines for adaptive soft robotics, dynamic biointerfaces, and mechanically instructive biomaterials.

title: Drug Repurposing for Treating NCOR‐Related Intellectual Disability
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Nuclear receptor corepressors (NCOR1/2) mediate the transcriptional activity of methyl‐CpG binding protein 2 (MECP2), and genetic variants in
                     NCOR1/2 
                    or
                     MECP2 
                    associate with autism or intellectual disability. However, it is unknown whether heterozygous NCOR mutations impair cognitive functions and how NCOR‐related intellectual disability can be treated. Here, we constructed a knock‐in (KI) mouse line carrying a heterozygous
                     NCOR1 
                    mutation (
                     NCOR1 
                    c.2182+2T>G) found in a pediatric patient. These NCOR1
                     KI/+ 
                    mice showed social avoidance, stereotypic behaviors, and memory deficits, similar to heterozygous
                     NCOR1 
                    knockout mice, demonstrating
                     NCOR1 
                    haploinsufficiency. snRNA‐seq revealed upregulated neuregulins (
                     Nrg1/3 
                    ) and downregulated γ‐aminobutyric acid (GABA) receptor subunit (
                     Gabra2 
                    ) in hypothalamic GABAergic neurons in NCOR1
                     KI/+ 
                    mice. In cultured neurons,
                     Nrg1 
                    overexpression is sufficient to downregulate
                     Gabra2 
                    . Spironolactone, an NRG antagonist, prevents
                     Gabra2 
                    downregulation induced by full‐length NRG1, but not by the NRG1 intracellular domain, suggesting that the noncanonical NRG backward signaling contributes to
                     Gabra2 
                    downregulation upon
                     NCOR1 
                    loss‐of‐function. Spironolactone and the GABA‐A receptor positive modulator allopregnanolone, both FDA‐approved drugs, mitigated cognitive impairments in NCOR1
                     KI/+ 
                    mice. Furthermore, spironolactone improved learning in an autistic patient bearing a pathogenic mutation in
                     MECP2 
                    . These findings elucidate the mechanism of NCOR‐related cognitive dysfunctions and provide preclinical proof‐of‐concept for treatment through drug repurposing.

title: LLMs as Representation Generators for Gradient‐Free Scientific Optimization: A Case Study in Battery Fast Charging
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Scientific optimization problems are often characterized by slow, expensive, and non‐differentiable evaluations, which severely limit efficient exploration of rich design spaces. In these settings, performance depends not only on the optimizer itself, but also on whether the chosen search space can represent good solutions and whether important design requirements are effectively incorporated into the search. Here, we introduce a gradient‐free optimization framework based on large language models (LLMs) that enables the generation and refinement of executable control policies directly from natural language. We propose two complementary paradigms: Prompt‐to‐Optimizer (P2O), which combines LLM‐based structural generation with gradient‐free parameter optimization, and Prompt‐to‐Protocol (P2P), which directly synthesizes fully specified control policies. We apply this framework to battery fast‐charging protocol design, a representative slow‐feedback optimization problem. Across multiple case studies, our methods outperform conventional approaches restricted to predefined functional forms. In a realistic fast‐charging scenario, both approaches improve battery state of health by approximately 4.2% over a representative baseline, with P2P achieving this under matched evaluation budgets. More broadly, our results suggest that LLMs can serve as representation generators that expand the hypothesis space of scientific optimization, enabling efficient search in domains where evaluations are costly, and gradients are unavailable.

title: PrOMet: Accurate and Robust Metal‐Binding Site and Type Prediction
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Metal binding to proteins is crucial for many biological functions, yet the prediction of metal‐binding sites and metal types remains underexplored compared to other biomolecular interactions. Despite advances in deep learning, computational methods have achieved limited success in this area; even the best‐reported approaches reach only moderate localization accuracy on high‐resolution crystal structures, and even worse when applied to medium‐resolution data. We hypothesize that the main challenge lies in the nature of metal binding. While the putative sites span the entire protein surface, actual binding requires the atomic‐level coordination geometry. We present a structure‐based metal binding site and type predictor, PrOMet, in this work, which leverages a Prune‐and‐Optimization strategy built upon two hierarchically connected machine learning architectures. This strategy allows the method to effectively narrow the search space while maintaining robustness to AlphaFold models and medium‐resolution cryo‐EM structures. PrOMet outperforms existing methods, including structure‐based and language model‐based predictors, achieving a PR‐AUC of 0.739 for metal ion localization and an average F1‐score of 0.743 for metal type classification—Zn, Ca, Mg, Mn, Fe, Cu, respectively. PrOMet can be an effective tool for allocating uncertain metal positions and types within protein structures, as well as for metalloenzyme design studies.

title: Optimized Land–Water Management Expands Afforestation Potential Under Land and Human Water‐Use Constraints
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Afforestation is a low‐cost and high‐potential climate change mitigation strategy, but its feasibility remains highly uncertain because most existing assessments focus primarily on biophysical suitability and land resource constraints, while largely overlooking the critical limitation imposed by human water demand. Here, we developed an integrated framework combining machine learning, statistical modelling, the Biome‐BGCMuSo model, and multi‐scenario analysis to quantify China's afforestation potential under coupled land and water constraints and explore how optimized land–water management can enhance afforestation potential and associated carbon sink. We found human water demand reduced China's feasible afforestation potential from 78.13 to 40.57 Mha, with climate change causing a further 15.23%–15.91% decline. Notably, optimized land management and water‐saving measures could individually increase feasible afforestation area by 6.04–7.05 Mha and 5.89–6.97 Mha, respectively. When combined, these measures would further increase afforestation potential by 14.95 and 13.66 Mha under SSP‐245 and SSP‐585, respectively, generating an additional carbon sink of 109.64 ± 12.08 and 125.92 ± 13.40 Tg C yr
                     − 
                     1 
                    by 2060. Our findings reveal that ignoring human water demand substantially overestimates afforestation potential and identify practical pathways to expand feasible afforestation potential while minimizing land‐use conflicts and safeguarding water security under future climate change.

title: An ATP7A‐Mediated Endogenous Regulation Bio‐Clay Enzyme Enables Self‐Amplified Copper Accumulation for Immunogenic Pyrop
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Tumor cells maintain abnormal metabolism to support their rapid proliferation, which often compromises the therapeutic outcomes, including pyroptosis. Inhibiting the copper transporter ATPase (ATP7A) effectively disrupts this metabolic balance, yet current exogenous ATP7A inhibition strategies suffer from poor delivery efficiency and low tumor selectivity. Herein, we developed an endogenous regulation strategy to downregulate ATP7A levels using a self‐amplifying bio‐clay enzyme (Bio‐Clayzyme), cupriferous Prussian blue/montmorillonite (CuPB/Mt). Upon tumor cell internalization, CuPB/Mt induces a robust reactive oxygen species (ROS) storm, accompanied by antioxidant depletion, mitochondrial dysfunction, and adenosine triphosphate (ATP) exhaustion. These metabolic disturbances are associated with reduced ATP7A expression, which may subsequently impair ATP7A‐mediated copper efflux. The resulting intracellular copper accumulation may further promote ROS amplification, supporting a positive feedback loop among ROS production, ATP7A downregulation, and copper retention. Specifically, the introduction of Mt optimizes the Cu d‐band center and strengthens tumor cell adhesion, thereby boosting the multi‐enzyme‐like catalytic activity and enabling efficient utilization of short‐lived ROS. Consequently, CuPB/Mt activates nucleotide‐binding oligomerization domain‐like receptor family pyrin domain‐containing 3 (NLRP3)‐dependent pyroptosis and elicits a potent anti‐tumor immune response, offering an ATP7A‐mediated endogenous regulatory paradigm for self‐amplified catalytic therapy and immunogenic pyroptosis.

title: Lactylation‐Mediated HER2 Stabilization Promotes Trastuzumab Resistance in Gastric Cancer
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Trastuzumab is the standard first‐line targeted therapy for human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)‐positive gastric cancer (GC). Unfortunately, its clinical efficacy is often compromised by the development of drug resistance. The Warburg effect, a hallmark of cancer metabolism, leads to substantial lactate accumulation. Nevertheless, the impact of metabolic reprogramming on the response to HER2‐targeted therapy remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that AARS1‐mediated lactylation of HER2 promotes trastuzumab resistance in GC. Mechanistically, lactylation at lysine 1171 (K1171) promotes USP11‐mediated deubiquitination and stabilization of HER2 and also enhances the interaction between HER2 and EGFR. Clinically, elevated HER2 K1171 lactylation levels are associated with poor prognosis in GC patients. Inhibiting HER2 K1171 lactylation with L‐alanine or stiripentol—a lactate dehydrogenase inhibitor (LDHi) clinically approved for epilepsy—significantly sensitizes tumor cells to trastuzumab. Furthermore, a cell‐penetrating peptide designed to specifically block HER2 K1171 lactylation potently enhances antitumor efficacy in vivo. In summary, our findings identify HER2 lactylation as a critical mechanism underlying trastuzumab resistance and highlight lactate metabolism as a promising therapeutic target for HER2‐positive GC.

title: Large Electrostrain and High Optical Transmittance via Oxygen Octahedron Rotation Disordering in KNN Ceramics
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Lead‐free K
                     0.5 
                    Na
                     0.5 
                    NbO
                     3 
                    (KNN)‐based ceramics are promising candidates for multifunctional electronic materials. Nevertheless, the synergistic optimization of electrostrain and optical transmittance in KNN polycrystalline ceramics remains a critical challenge, owing to the structural trade‐off between large strain and high transparency. Here, we employ chemical disorder engineering specifically through BaTiO
                     3 
                    (BT) substitution to manipulate the BO
                     6 
                    oxygen octahedron rotation disorder. BT incorporated into KNN gradually modulates the BO
                     6 
                    rotation mode from local ordering to a random distribution, which refines the size of cubic‐phase‐enriched polar nanoregions, facilitating high transparency in visible‐light range. The disordered BO
                     6 
                    rotation essentially lowers the thermodynamic switching barriers for polarization and strengthens the defect‐dipole pinning effect, thereby enhance the electrostrain synergistically. The optimal composition, i.e., KNN‐0.03BT exhibits a large electrostrain of 1.2% and an optical transmittance of 60% in visible‐light range. By overcoming the long‐standing bottleneck in traditional polycrystalline ceramics, this work elucidates the core mechanism of atomic‐scale disordering‐enhanced polarization response and reduced optical loss, thereby advancing multifunctional material applications such as transparent sensing and flexible electronics.

title: Tracking CDK1 Dynamics With a Novel Biosensor Mouse and Clinical Cohorts to Predict CDK4/6 Inhibitor Sensitivity in ER+ Breast Cancer
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    High‐risk estrogen receptor positive (ER+) early breast cancer (EBC) is managed with endocrine therapies and cyclin‐dependent kinase (CDK) 4/6 inhibitors, although no standard molecular markers clinically identify these tumors. CDK1 lies immediately downstream of CDK4/6 but has not been investigated as a prognostic marker for ER+ disease. Here, we integrate real‐time imaging of a novel Cdk1 activity biosensor mouse with clinical cohorts to establish CDK1 as a candidate biomarker of progression and therapeutic sensitivity. Using the MMTV‐PyMT;MMTV‐Cre;Cdk1‐FRET biosensor mouse, we visualized Cdk1 upregulation in situ during the transition to invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC). Clinically, we identified that pCDK1
                     T161 
                    is specifically upregulated in IDC, and that pCDK1
                     Y15 
                    is prognostic of poor relapse‐free survival in stage 1 disease. We further characterized CDK1 activity as part of a dynamic adaptive response to CDK4/6 inhibition: the CDK1/cyclin B1 complex was suppressed, then rebounded within 3 days. In the NeoPalAna trial, non‐responders incompletely suppressed
                     CDK1 
                    . Palbociclib‐resistant cells recovered basal CDK1 in vitro, non‐responsive tumors exhibited elevated Cdk1 activity in vivo, and
                     CDK1 
                    was elevated in CDK4/6 inhibitor‐resistant patient tumors. Together, our findings position CDK1 as a candidate biomarker for poor prognosis in early disease, and an indicator of adaptive responses and resistance to CDK4/6 inhibition.

title: Epigenetic Silencing of CYYR1 Promotes Lung Adenocarcinoma Progression Through TRIM21‐Dependent Regulation of HMMR Stability
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains a leading cause of cancer‐related mortality. Integrative multi‐omics and machine‐learning analyses across independent cohorts identified CYYR1 as a frequently downregulated transmembrane protein in LUAD, with low expression associated with poor prognosis and promoter hypermethylation. CYYR1 restoration suppressed LUAD cell proliferation, migration, invasion, tumor growth, and metastasis. Mechanistically, CYYR1 facilitated TRIM21‐dependent ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of HMMR, thereby reducing CDC20‐associated oncogenic signaling. Biochemical and cellular analyses supported this CYYR1–TRIM21–HMMR regulatory relationship, while a patient‐derived LUAD organoid model provided proof‐of‐concept evidence that CYYR1 restoration inhibited organoid growth and reduced HMMR, CDC20, and Ki67 expression. CYYR1 restoration also increased cisplatin sensitivity. Genistein treatment was associated with CDC20 modulation and enhanced cisplatin response, and cellular thermal shift assays provided evidence consistent with CDC20 engagement, although CDC20 dependence of the Genistein response remains unproven. Collectively, these findings identify CYYR1 as an epigenetically dysregulated tumor‐suppressive factor that regulates HMMR stability through a TRIM21‐dependent mechanism and reveal a potential therapeutic vulnerability in CYYR1‐deficient LUAD.

title:
Spatial Au
                     + 
                    Mapping Reveals a Self‐Amplifying Anti‐Tumor Immunity Loop Driven by Au(I) Complexes
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Although many metal complexes exhibit promising chemoimmunotherapeutic effects by inducing immunogenic cell death (ICD), the precise regulation of how these complexes interact with immune cells remains unclear. Herein, we introduced
                     Au9 
                    as the first representative gold complex to directly associate with immune cells in the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME). Our study delineated the mechanism underlying
                     Au9 
                    ‐driven anti‐tumor response and “hot” TIME remodeling, anchored in Au
                     + 
                    spatial mapping. Of note, macrophages, dendritic cells (DCs), and tumor cells ranked as the top three in Au
                     + 
                    enrichment. Further investigation showed that
                     Au9 
                    treatment stimulated the phagocytic activity of M1 macrophages, as confirmed by 3D scanning reconstructions. Importantly,
                     Au9 
                    treatment triggered a self‐amplifying anti‐tumor immunity loop. This study pioneered critical insights into the mechanisms of TIME‐remodeling and laid the groundwork for the rational design of next‐generation gold complexes with enhanced chemoimmunotherapeutic efficacy.

title: Aryl‐Tethered Pendant Sterically Shielded Imidazoliums for Durable Anion Exchange Membranes
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Conventional quaternary‐ammonium‐based anion‐exchange membranes (AEMs) with insufficient alkaline stability limit the durability of AEM water electrolyzers (AEMWEs). Here we report novel poly(arylimidazolium) membranes (QAI‐x) that overcome this barrier through an aryl‐tethered pendant sterically shielded imidazolium cation. This architecture sterically protects the imidazolium cation while avoiding the introduction of a benzylic cation–polymer linkage. Combined with ether‐free polyaromatic backbones, the QAI‐x membranes simultaneously achieve enhanced chemical stability and dimensional stability, with no measurable loss in hydroxide conductivity after 4000 h in 1 M KOH at 80°C, resistance to Fenton oxidation, and limited dimensional swelling despite relatively high water uptake. In AEMWEs, QAI‐x membranes support voltage decay rates as low as 9 µV h
                     −1 
                    over 5400 h in 1 M KOH and 16 µV h
                     −1 
                    over 2000 h in 5 M KOH at 80°C and 2.5 V, substantially outperforming commercial benchmarks. Cell operation is further demonstrated for more than 1000 h at 3 A cm
                     −2 
                    under a dry‐cathode configuration. These results highlight aryl‐tethered steric shielding as a promising molecular‐design strategy for durable AEMs.

title: scGEN: Leveraging an Adaptive Weighting Strategy for Challenging Cell Clustering in Single‐Cell RNA‐seq
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Recent advancements in single‐cell RNA sequencing (scRNA‐seq) have greatly enhanced our ability to dissect cellular heterogeneity. However, unsupervised clustering often struggles to identify transitional or developmental boundary cells, as existing methods rely on highly variable genes without considering expression levels, thereby overlooking subtle but crucial signals. To address this challenge, we developed a single‐cell gene‐aware embedded network (scGEN), which captures complex intercellular relationships. scGEN employs adaptive feature weighting and iterative fine‐tuning to prioritize ambiguous or transitional cells with overlapping transcriptional profiles. Evaluation across eight distinct scRNA‐seq datasets demonstrated that scGEN consistently outperformed nine leading clustering approaches. Additionally, scGEN generated refined assignments for approximately 10% of cells with ambiguous transcriptional profiles and revealed biologically meaningful differences, providing a more detailed view of cellular heterogeneity in the human fetal pituitary. Cell–cell communication analysis identified developmental signaling networks associated with the refined annotations, including a putative Pre.Gonado‐like population detected at 7 weeks with prominent involvement in BMP, NOTCH, and extracellular matrix remodeling pathways. Furthermore, histological analysis of 6–8‐week embryos provided orthogonal tissue‐level support for early gonadotrope‐lineage states and SOX2–GATA2–NR5A1 bridging populations. Together, these results highlight scGEN's ability to enhance cell‐type assignments and detect subtle biological differences.

title: Phosphorylated STYK1 Promotes Gemcitabine Resistance via Autophagy‐Mediated Cancer Stemness in Pancreatic Cancer
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is one of the most lethal malignancies, with gemcitabine resistance remaining a major clinical challenge. Although cancer stemness and autophagy have both been implicated in PDAC chemoresistance, the mechanism by which their crosstalk governs gemcitabine resistance remains poorly understood. Here, we identify serine/threonine/tyrosine kinase 1 (STYK1) as a critical mediator of gemcitabine resistance through autophagy‐ dependent maintenance of pancreatic cancer stemness. Mechanistically, gemcitabine activates AMP‐activated protein kinase (AMPK), which contributes to the enhancement of STYK1‐mediated autophagic flux, thereby promoting stemness‐associated chemoresistance. Furthermore, AMPK phosphorylates STYK1 at residues Ser91 and Ser304, thereby further potentiating STYK1‐mediated autophagy and cancer stemness. Importantly, we developed SAIDP5, a therapeutic peptide disrupting STYK1‐AMPK binding, which synergizes with gemcitabine to attenuate chemoresistance. This study reveals that gemcitabine‐induced AMPK activation amplifies STYK1‐driven autophagy and cancer stemness, thereby contributing to gemcitabine resistance, and highlights SAIDP5 as a promising peptide‐based strategy to improve gemcitabine efficacy in PDAC.

title: Gonadotropin‐Inhibitory Hormone (GnIH) and Its Receptor GPR147 Mediates Acute Stress‐Induced Activation of the Locus Coeruleus‐SAM Axis
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Gonadotropin‐inhibitory hormone (GnIH, also known as RFamide‐related peptide‐3, RFRP‐3) is a hypothalamic neuropeptide that regulates vertebrate reproduction via its receptor GPR147. Although GnIH is known to mediate stress‐induced reproductive suppression, its role in broader stress responses remains unclear. This study investigated the fuction of GnIH in acute stress and evaluated the mechanisms by which GnIH regulates norepinephrine (NE) release and activates the locus coeruleus‐sympathetic‐adrenal medulla (LC‐SAM) axis in mice. The results show that GnIH is co‐localized and co‐stored with NE in sympathetic nerve terminals and that it is associated with heightened LC‐SAM axis activity induced by acute stressors. Central or peripheral administration of GnIH potentiated acute stress responses and activated the LC‐SAM axis, accompanied by increased anxiety‐like behaviors. Conversely, genetic ablation of GnIH or GPR147 attenuated acute stress‐induced anxiety‐like behaviors and LC‐SAM axis activation. Mechanistically, both central and peripheral GnIH enhanced NE synthesis, transport and release. These findings indicate that GnIH mimics or augments endogenous NE signaling to activated the LC‐SAM axis during acute stress. Pharmacological modulation of the GnIH/GPR147 system may represent a therapeutic approach for the inhibiting maladaptive stress responses and stress‐related pathologies and infertility.

title: TurbOmics: a web-based platform for the analysis of metabolomics data using a multi-omics integrative approach
Temporal phenotypic responses of early vegetative maize to heat, drought, and combined stresses
abstract:
SUMMARY 
                   
                    Understanding how maize responds to heat, drought, and the combination of stresses is essential for developing resilient cultivars for future climates. We characterized temporal phenotypic responses of 47 genetically diverse
                     Zea mays 
                    inbred lines grown under control, drought, heat, and combined drought‐heat stresses for 13 days in a high‐throughput phenotyping platform. Plant area was modeled over time using Bayesian hierarchical growth analysis. Treatment explained the largest proportion of phenotypic variance, while genotype × treatment interaction accounted for up to 35% of color variation. Growth and development responses were strongly genotype‐dependent, and combined‐stress responses were more closely related to heat rather than drought responses. Heat primarily reduced height and impacted growth but not development, whereas drought reduced leaf number and greenness and impacted both growth and development, indicating distinct physiological effects. Despite strong genotype effects, subpopulation explained differences only in drought responses. In follow‐up experiments, these early vegetative stresses had a significant impact on days to anthesis and plant area even long after the stresses had stopped. Collectively, these results emphasize that combined‐stress tolerance cannot be inferred from a single‐stress, and that there is potential for improving early environmental stress tolerance that will impact later plant phenotypes.

title: A wheat‐specific proline‐rich protein regulates grain weight through a ubiquitin‐mediated delay of endosperm cellularization
abstract:
SUMMARY 
                   
                    Grain weight is a key determinant of wheat yield, yet the developmental mechanisms that define this trait remain poorly understood. Here, we identify
                     TaPGW1‐A1 
                    , a wheat‐specific proline‐rich gene that regulates grain weight.
                     TaPGW1‐A1 
                    is a recently evolved gene found only in wheat. It is highly expressed in early developing grains, and its overexpression delays endosperm cellularization and prolongs the syncytial phase, resulting in an 8% increase in field‐based grain weight.
                     Ta 
                    PGW1‐A1 protein directly interacts with the ubiquitin receptor
                     Ta 
                    DSK2a (Dominant Suppressor of KAR2 homolog)
                     via 
                    its N‐terminal signal peptide, and the protein–protein complex localizes to the cell periphery. Biochemical assays show that
                     Ta 
                    DSK2a binds both K48‐ and K63‐linked polyubiquitin chains. Loss‐of‐function of
                     Ta 
                    DSK2a leads to reduced grain size, confirming its essential role in grain development. The E3 ligase
                     Ta 
                    RGLG2 inhibits the binding of
                     Ta 
                    PGW1‐A1 to
                     Ta 
                    DSK2a. Together, these findings define a
                     Ta 
                    PGW1‐A1–
                     Ta 
                    DSK2a–
                     Ta 
                    RGLG2 regulatory module that links developmental timing with ubiquitin‐mediated protein turnover, revealing a previously unrecognized mechanism controlling endosperm cellularization and grain yield in wheat.

title:
The degree and direction of subgenome expression bias in
                     Brassica napus 
                    vary between cultivars, tissues and developmental stages
abstract:
SUMMARY 
                   
                    Most extant plant lineages show evidence of past polyploidisation events in their genomes. Allopolyploids arise from hybridisation, resulting in polyploid genomes comprising subgenomes from different ancestors. Adaptation to their environment, pre‐ and post‐hybridisation and selection for specific traits has led to several allopolyploids exhibiting an unequal contribution from their subgenomes to phenotypic traits. Associated regulatory changes may have given rise to cultivar‐specific subgenome dominance that contributes to the diversity of phenotypes. Likewise, different tissues and developmental stages have distinct expression profiles that may exhibit higher contributions from one subgenome relative to the other. Here, we investigate different metrics for quantifying the contribution of each subgenome to expression in cultivars of
                     Brassica napus, 
                    in space (tissue) and time (development).
                     Brassica napus 
                    inherited two subgenomes, A and C, from its ancestors
                     Brassica rapa 
                    (A) and
                     Brassica oleracea 
                    (C). We find that the C subgenome has a larger contribution to transcript abundance than the A subgenome, whereas the mean abundance per expressed gene is higher for the A subgenome. Direct comparison of homoeologous pairs reveals higher expression of genes on the C subgenome. We find that the degree and direction of expression bias can change substantially within a homoeologous pair between cultivars, tissues and across development, suggesting that subgenome dominance is highly dynamic. The quantification of expression bias reveals a strong dependence on the metric and on classification thresholds. These findings help explain contradictory reports on expression bias and subgenome dominance.

title:
CsSSU I differentially modulates plastidial prenyltransferases linked to coloration and aroma in sweet orange (
                     Citrus sinensis 
                    L.)
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Coloration (carotenoids) and aroma (volatile terpenoids) are major determinants of citrus fruit quality, but their coordinated improvement is challenging because carotenoid and volatile-terpenoid biosynthesis draw on a shared isoprenoid precursor network. Here, we used chimeric fruits of the sweet orange (Citrus sinensis L.) bud mutant “Zongcheng” to investigate this metabolic coordination. Metabolomic analyses revealed coordinated accumulation of carotenoids and volatile terpenoids in the brown peel sectors. We systematically characterized the sweet orange trans-prenyltransferase (TPT) family and identified CsGGPPS4, CsGGPPS6, and CsGGPPS8 as plastid-localized enzymes catalyze geranylgeranyl diphosphate (GGPP) biosynthesis. Comparative transcript profiling, biochemical assays, and in vivo functional analyses revealed distinct functions among these enzymes. Expression profiling and in vivo experiments demonstrated that CsGGPPS6 and CsGGPPS8 promote carotenoid accumulation, whereas CsGGPPS4 exerts only minor effects under the tested conditions. Notably, CsGGPPS6 exhibited substrate-ratio-dependent product specificity, producing predominantly farnesyl diphosphate (FPP) under equimolar substrate conditions but both FPP and GGPP when isopentenyl diphosphate (IPP) was enriched; its manipulation in vivo also altered sesquiterpenoid accumulation. CsSSU I directly interacted with CsGGPPS6 and CsGGPPS8 and differentially modulated their catalytic properties: association with CsGGPPS6 favored FPP formation and restricted further elongation to GGPP, while association with CsGGPPS8 enabled geranyl diphosphate (GPP) production and enhances GGPP production. Manipulation of CsSSU I in vivo coordinately affected monoterpenoid, sesquiterpenoid, and carotenoid accumulation. Collectively, these results establish that CsSSU I acts as a protein-binding modulator that remodels product output of plastid-localized TPT enzymes and indicate that this regulatory network orchestrates terpenoid-derived pigmentation and aroma traits in citrus.

title: Franks and Farquhar (2007) and beyond: the influence of guard and subsidiary cell biomechanics on stomatal function
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Stomata are the gatekeepers to leaf gas exchange and as such are essential for CO2 uptake for photosynthesis, water loss for evaporative cooling, and ultimately plant growth and productivity. Research has long focused on understanding the mechanisms that govern stomatal aperture adjustments, in particular how changes in turgor pressure in guard cells (GCs) are achieved and how these cause the reversible cell shape distortion that leads to pore opening and closing. Here we discuss the immense impact the paper by Franks and Farquhar (2007) has had on this research field, both in the past and more recently, by stimulating new angles of exploration of stomatal mechanics. As new techniques have emerged, the impact of the mechanical advantage of epidermal/subsidiary cells and how this is overcome by GCs has inspired novel studies into the importance of subsidiary to stomatal function, the effect of different cell shapes (dumbbell- vs kidney-shaped) on stomatal kinetics, the significance of cell geometries and cell complexes, as well as the underlying biochemical cell wall composition responsible for GC deformation. While many questions remain unanswered, we summarize the take-home messages from the key literature on stomatal biomechanics.

title: Metal-organic frameworks for separation of organic compounds in liquid phase
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Liquid-phase separation underpins numerous sectors of modern chemical industry, yet achieving high selectivity for separation of mixtures of organic compounds remains a persistent challenge. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), showing exceptional tunability in composition, topology and pore environment, hold unique promise to address this challenge. This review surveys recent progress in studies of MOFs for the selective extraction and purification of organic substrates in liquid phase, with a focus on elucidating the mechanism of selectivity. Function-directed design principles, encompassing tailored bonding interactions, programmable supramolecular environments and pore-confinement effects, are discussed as enabling precise control over transport processes. These concepts are examined across key application domains, including removal of pollutants in water treatment, the separation of structurally similar hydrocarbons in petrochemical refinery and the selective discrimination of daily pharmaceuticals. Opportunities for the next generation of MOF-based sorbents are outlined, highlighting challenges associated with scalability and long-term operational stability, and the growing roles of artificial intelligence (AI)-guided discovery in developing sustainable separation technologies are further projected.

title: Taking a BREATH (Bayesian Reconstruction and Evolutionary Analysis of Transmission Histories) to simultaneously infer phylogenetic and transmission trees for partially sampled outbreaks
abstract:
Abstract 
                   We introduce and apply Bayesian Reconstruction and Evolutionary Analysis of Transmission Histories (BREATH), a method to simultaneously construct phylogenetic trees and transmission trees using sequence data for a host-to-host outbreak. 
                   BREATH's transmission process that accounts for a flexible natural history of infection (including a latent period if desired) and a separate process for sampling. It allows for unsampled individuals and within-host evolution. It also accounts for the fact that an outbreak may still be ongoing at the time of analysis, using right truncation adjustment. 
                   We perform a simulation study to verify our implementation and explore sensitivity to unknown or misspecified parameters. We then apply BREATH to a previously-described 13-year outbreak of tuberculosis. We find that using a transmission process to inform the phylogenetic reconstruction results in better resolution of the phylogeny (in topology, branch length and tree height) and a more precise estimate of the time of origin of the outbreak. Considerable uncertainty remains about transmission events in the outbreak, but our reconstructed transmission network resolves two major waves of transmission consistent with the previously-described epidemiology, estimates the numbers of unsampled individuals, and describes some high-probability transmission pairs. 
                   An open source implementation of BREATH is available from https://github.com/rbouckaert/BREATH as the BREATH package to BEAST 2.

title: Diversity and divergence of two sympatric, sibling octopus species
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Coleoid cephalopods have convergently evolved many traits shared with vertebrates, including camera-type eyes, large brain-to-body size ratios, and complex behaviors. Most evolutionary studies of cephalopods have compared individual genomes of taxa that diverged tens to hundreds of millions of years ago; yet, very few have examined more recent evolution from a population genetics perspective. Here, we present a comparative population genomic analysis of the sympatric sister species Octopus bimaculatus and Octopus bimaculoides using whole-genome resequencing. Despite similar morphologies, these species differ substantially in their life histories, ecologies, and geographic distributions. Using demographic inference, we estimated that the two species diverged on the order of one million years ago, with point estimates from independent methods spanning roughly 0.4 to 1.3 million years, and that O. bimaculatus has maintained a consistently larger effective population size since divergence. Consistent with these demographic histories, we found stronger signatures of positive selection in O. bimaculatus, including a positive correlation between recombination rate and nucleotide diversity, more selective sweeps, and a higher proportion of mutations fixed by adaptation—all consistent with more efficient natural selection in larger populations. Protein-coding genes overlapping with selective sweeps were enriched for various functions that included many related to brain and eye development, suggesting that traits characteristic of coleoid cephalopods continue to be shaped by positive selection on recent timescales in these species. Comparing coding-sequence divergence on the Z chromosome to the autosomes, we also find evidence for a female-biased mutation rate, consistent with an independent estimate from a deeper-timescale cephalopod comparison.

title: FunFOLD5: combining localised templates and structural homology for accurate predictions of biologically relevant protein–ligand interactions
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Motivation 
                     A central challenge in protein–ligand modelling is to predict not only the presence of an interaction but also the correct ligand identity, binding-site location, and biologically relevant bound conformation. While recent deep learning approaches such as AlphaFold3 and Boltz-2 have demonstrated impressive accuracy in modelling protein–ligand complexes, these methods typically require prior knowledge of the ligand, focus on a single dominant binding pose, and rely heavily on large training datasets. Template-based methods offer a complementary solution by leveraging experimentally resolved protein–ligand complexes to transfer both binding-site architecture and ligand chemical identity, enabling function inference even for uncharacterised or engineered proteins. However, conventional template-based methods are limited by their dependence on global fold similarity, which can miss local binding features critical for ligand specificity. Localised template search strategies may overcome this limitation by capturing conserved pocket-level interactions, enabling more accurate and functionally relevant ligand-binding predictions across diverse protein families. 
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     We present FunFOLD5, a template-based method for predicting protein–ligand binding sites. Whereas its predecessor FunFOLD4 relied on global fold similarity to identify templates, FunFOLD5 combines local and global searches, integrating rapid structural template retrieval with a local targeted protocol to improve interaction accuracy. The pipeline combines Foldseek-based template searching, curated ligand annotations from BioLiP2, and ligand superposition followed by spatial clustering to identify associated ligands and consensus binding sites. Benchmarking on blind targets from CASP15 and CASP16 demonstrates robust performance across a wide range of biologically relevant ligands, including nucleotides, metal ions, cofactors, and small metabolites. FunFOLD5 achieved high-accuracy predictions for 81.2% of ligand instances (56 of 69). Importantly, the local targeted protocol consistently improved ligand identification, residue-level recall, and binding-pose accuracy. 
                   
                   
                     Availability and implementation 
                     FunFOLD5 is freely available as a Dockerised pipeline at https://hub.docker.com/r/radiyaman/funfold5_template, providing a scalable and reproducible framework for large-scale protein–ligand interaction analysis and functional annotation.

title: LoGicAl: local ancestry and genotype calling uncertainty-aware ancestry-specific allele frequency estimation from admixed samples
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Motivation 
                     In admixed groups, it is of interest to estimate allele frequencies of their ancestral contributing populations. These ancestry-specific allele frequencies inform genetic drivers of disease etiologies, facilitate genome-wide association study interpretations, enhance polygenic risk prediction and portability, and provide insights into demographic history. Their estimation leverages inferred locus-specific ancestry background, i.e. local ancestry, generated by tools like RFMix. However, existing estimation methods lose accuracy and incur biases by failing to model uncertainty from upstream local ancestry inference and genotype calling. 
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     Here, we introduce LoGicAl (Local ancestry and Genotype calling uncertainty-aware ancestry-specific Allele frequency estimation), a novel likelihood-based method for estimating ancestry-specific allele frequencies from admixed samples, simultaneously accommodating uncertainty from ancestry calling, genotyping, and statistical phasing. We demonstrate that modeling these uncertainties substantially reduces estimation errors, resulting in superior accuracy for both sequence-based and array-based genotyping with different levels of local ancestry inference quality. By integrating an accelerated fixed-point algorithm, LoGicAl achieves high scalability and enhanced computational efficiency compared with existing approaches. Applying LoGicAl to admixed cohorts in the 1000 Genomes Project, we illustrate the benefits of local-ancestry-based allele frequency estimates. Together, LoGicAl contributes to genomic analyses of admixed samples by providing precise and rapid ancestry-specific allele frequency estimates, and to constructing the spatial landscape and dynamics of genetic variations in admixed populations at a finer scale. 
                   
                   
                     Availability and implementation 
                     The LoGicAl software is available at https://github.com/student-jw/LoGicAl.

title: An importin-α IMA8 facilitates nuclear import of COI1 to promote jasmonate-mediated defense responses in Arabidopsis
abstract: Jasmonate signaling requires the nuclear localization of its receptor COI1, but the mechanism underlying COI1 nuclear import remains unclear. Here, we identify IMPORTIN ALPHA ISOFORM 8 (IMA8) as a nuclear transport receptor for COI1 and demonstrate that IMA8-facilitated nuclear import of COI1 is essential for proper jasmonate responses, revealing a previously unrecognized spatial regulatory step in plant hormone signaling.

title: Transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulation of OsNHX2 encoding a tonoplast-localized transporter controls intracellular K+ accumulation to regulate cold tolerance in rice
abstract: Short Summary: OsNHX2 is a tonoplast-localized K+ transporter that modulates intracellular K+ accumulation through transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulation. It maintains reactive oxygen species homeostasis under cold stress and promotes osmolyte accumulation, thereby enhancing cold tolerance in rice.

title: Hyper-mutational processes provide a head-start for weak cancer drivers: Explaining atypical KRAS variants
abstract:
Hypermutant cancers frequently contain atypical driver gene variants, which may provide sub-optimal oncogenic advantages. The reason why weak cancer drivers prevail and are not outcompeted by stronger alternatives is unclear. Here, using mathematical modelling, we show that aberrant mutational processes alone can account for the detection of weak, rather than canonical, driver mutations. We find that simply increasing the mutation rate per cell division, without altering selection or mutational biases, can lead to the dominance of weak drivers due to rapidly occurring further driver events. This effect can be further enhanced by mutational biases towards specific nucleotide sequence contexts. Focusing on
                     POLE 
                    -mutant (DNA polymerase epsilon proofreading-deficient) colorectal cancers, we quantify the mutation bias for varied
                     KRAS 
                    drivers under both
                     POLE- 
                    mutant and non-hypermutant mutational processes. In
                     POLE 
                    -mutant cancers, the combination of the bias coupled with an elevated mutation rate is sufficient to explain the enrichment of atypical
                     KRAS 
                    drivers. Furthermore, model predictions are consistent with the observed prevalence of atypical
                     KRAS 
                    drivers observed in mismatch repair deficient colorectal cancers. Thus, differential selection across these cancer types need not be invoked to explain the variation in driver mutations. Our study clarifies the interplay of mutation and selection during the evolutionary dynamics of tumourigenesis.

title: A statistical damage model for coupled mechano-electrophysiological axonal injury
abstract: Deformation-induced injury of white matter nerve bundles is prevalent in central nervous system injuries, leading to a series of neurological dysfunctions. To describe the effect of deformation injury on the physiological electrical signals of neurons, several axonal electrophysiological damage models based on the Hodgkin-Huxley equations have been proposed. However, none of these models can fully characterize the results of white matter nerve stretching experiments under different rates and amplitudes. Building on previous work by peers, we propose a novel axonal deformation damage model that comprehensively considers the coupled effects of sodium and potassium channel damage on gating variable rate constants, as well as the differences in mechanical properties and injury among individual axons during deformation—with these differences continuously modeled by a statistical distribution. The proposed model can not only reasonably describe the sodium left-shift phenomenon (a key post-injury feature) but also accurately reproduce the neuro-electrophysiological responses of nerve fascicles under various stretching conditions. This new neuro-electrophysiological model for nerve fascicle injury exhibits good universality and provides a mechanical mechanism-based reference for future clinical treatment strategies of nerve injury.

title: Process bigraphs and the architecture of compositional systems biology
abstract:
Building multiscale biological models requires the integration of independently developed submodels, which means moving shared variables between them and coordinating when each submodel runs. Existing tools typically address isolated biological mechanisms with specific numerical methods, rarely specify which variables each model reads and writes, how those variables are translated, and how model updates are synchronized. We present Process Bigraph, a framework for composing and simulating multiscale models. Process Bigraph generalizes the architectural ideas previously used in the Vivarium software into a shared specification that describes process interfaces, hierarchical data structures, composition patterns, and orchestration patterns. The paper explains how the framework is organized and why it makes biological models easier to understand, reuse, and build on; S1 Text provides the formal specification. We introduce Vivarium 2.0 as an open-source implementation of the process bigraph framework. We demonstrate its utility with Spatio-Flux, a standalone library of microbial ecosystem simulations that combine kinetic equations, dynamic flux balance analysis, and different spatial processes. These simulations illustrated how the framework effectively integrates diverse biological processes, leading to emergent spatially organized population dynamics. Finally, we discuss implications for emerging multiscale modeling standards.
                     Availability and implementation: 
                    Vivarium 2.0 is a suite of software libraries that include: (1) bigraph-schema, for defining and operating on data types within a hierarchical JSON-based format; (2) process-bigraph, for defining process interfaces, composite simulations, and executing them; and (3) viva-superpowers, for AI-assisted construction and composition of process bigraphs. Spatio-Flux is a reference application used in this paper to demonstrate the framework’s utility. S1 Text provides detailed descriptions of these software libraries. All software is open-source and available at:
                     https://github.com/vivarium-collective 
                    .

title: How does explicit reliability guide choices? Effect of trustworthiness on choice and metacognition
abstract: A key challenge in today’s fast-paced digital world is to integrate information from various sources, which differ in their reliability. Yet, little is known about how explicit probabilistic information about the likelihood that a source provides correct information is used in decision-making. Here, we investigated how such explicit reliability markers are integrated into decisions and the extent to which individuals have metacognitive insight into this process. We developed a novel paradigm where participants viewed predictions from sources of varying explicit reliability to help them make a choice between two options. After each decision, they rated how much they felt a given source influenced their choice. Using computational modelling, we estimated the effective reliability that participants assigned to each source. Overall, we found that participants did not take source reliability at face value, inappropriately using the stated probabilities of source correctness to make a choice. Interestingly, even sources that were explicitly labelled as unreliable biased choices, as if these were treated as moderately reliable. Additionally, the presence of sources flagged as lying ones and known to be reliably predicting the incorrect answer impaired performance by increasing leakiness in evidence accumulation. Despite these biases, participants showed some metacognitive awareness of what influenced their choices: they were aware of the impact unreliable sources had on their decisions and could evaluate how much a given source had increased the likelihood of their response. These results suggest that people distort explicit source reliability but have some awareness of this process.

title: Dynamic workforce modulation and foraging efficiency in Eusocial insect colonies
abstract:
Understanding the fitness advantages conferred by eusociality remains a central challenge in behavioral ecology. One promising approach is to identify collective strategies that shift efficiency within social groups. Here, we explore the hypothesis that reserve workforces in ant colonies represent an adaptive mechanism that enhances flexibility and foraging efficiency under fluctuating environmental conditions. We examine how departure and return rates of foragers modulate such reserve workers and how these time-dependent dynamics shape the colony’s overall energetic balance. By integrating an energetic-balance framework with stochastic search simulations inspired by empirical results from four colonies of
                     Aphaenogaster senilis 
                    ants, we quantify the energetic requirements for colony viability, incorporating energy intake, search costs, and basal metabolic demands. Our results show that as colonies grow, maintaining a positive energy balance requires a disproportionately larger relative workforce. By modulating departure and return rates over time, colonies control the synchrony of their collective search and efficiently activate or suppress their reserve workforce to scale foraging effort as needed. These findings suggest that the “lazy” or weakly engaged workers commonly observed in large colonies function as an essential reserve that stabilizes colony energetics and enhances responsiveness. Together, our results provide a functional explanation for sublinear metabolic scaling in eusocial groups and highlight workforce modulation as a key factor underlying their energetic stability and evolutionary success.

title: Identification of regulators of aryl hydrocarbon receptor signaling in human cells by genome-scale CRISPR screening
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Background 
                     The human aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) integrates chemical signals derived from the environment, gut microbes, and endogenous sources to regulate processes ranging from intestinal barrier integrity to xenobiotic detoxification. Despite strong evidence that dysregulation of AHR signaling is a causal factor in metabolic and autoimmune disorders, we currently lack a comprehensive understanding of the factors that regulate AHR activity in human cells. 
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     Here, we use genome-scale CRISPR screening to systematically identify regulators of AHR signaling in a model of human hepatocytes. The resulting datasets recapitulate the core AHR signaling pathway and identify a large network of regulators. Many of these factors have roles beyond AHR signaling, reflecting that AHR signaling is deeply integrated into human cell biology. We further dissect this network to reveal novel modes of regulation of AHR expression, protein levels, and signaling. For example, we find that the E3 ubiquitin ligase UBR5 sustains AHR signaling by counteracting degradation of ligand-bound AHR. Finally, we identify components of the AHR regulatory network that are specific to cell types and ligands as potential nodes to manipulate AHR signaling in a targeted manner for therapeutic benefit. 
                   
                   
                     Conclusions 
                     Overall, our results define the regulatory network that underpins AHR activation, with implications for our understanding of host-microbe interactions and integrative chemosensation and the etiology of metabolic and inflammatory disorders.

title: Integrating physiological and proteomics signatures for understanding drought, salinity and alkalinity stress tolerance mechanisms in lentil
Wild-AC: A fast, index-free multi-pattern string matching algorithm with wildcard support for proteomics
abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                     Background 
                     
                      Efficient multi-pattern string matching with wildcard support is essential in proteomics, where peptides must be mapped to protein databases containing ambiguous amino acids (e.g.,
                       B 
                      ,
                       Z 
                      ,
                       X 
                      ). Existing approaches either require preprocessing (e.g., FM-index) or fail to handle wildcards in the text.
                     
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     
                      We present Wild-AC, a modified Aho-Corasick algorithm that supports wildcards in the text by branching the search into parallel ‘scout’ paths, one per possible wildcard representation, while the unmodified primary search continues unaffected in the common, wildcard-free case. Wild-AC outperforms the FM-index (wildcard case) and matches or exceeds Wu-Manber (exact search) in speed for realistic proteomics workloads, i.e., 1000–500 000 peptide patterns (average length ∼18 amino acids) searched against protein databases (texts) of 3 × 10
                       6 
                      –2.1 × 10
                       8 
                      characters. On databases masked to a wildcard rate of 5%, Wild-AC retains its advantage for large peptide sets, while the FM-index becomes preferable for small ones. It requires no index, scales well with pattern count, and supports multi-threading. The C++ implementation is open source at
                       https://github.com/Wild-AC/Wild-AC 
                      .
                     
                   
                   
                     Conclusion 
                     Wild-AC extends the Aho-Corasick algorithm to support wildcards and outperforms FM-Index and Wu-Manber in the task of peptide-protein mapping while considering ambiguous amino acids.

DNA nanodevice-engineered macrophages as living sensors for dual-mode in vivo monitoring of tumor-associated macrophage polarization
abstract: Exploiting macrophages as cell-autonomous reporters of their polarization states represents a promising strategy for interrogating tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) phenotypes in cancer. Here, we develop a macrophage-based sensing platform, termed eMφ. This platform is created by engineering macrophages with a modular and multiplexable DNA origami nanodevice to report TAM polarization states within the tumor microenvironment. Upon tumor infiltration, microenvironmental cues drive macrophage polarization, triggering the engineered system to convert endogenous signals (e.g., Arg1 or iNOS mRNA) into distinct, state-specific reporter outputs. The integration of local and circulating reporters enables compartment-resolved, multiscale readouts of macrophage state. Following intravenous administration, eMφ facilitates tumor detection across multiple murine models, including B16F10 melanoma and lung metastasis, and enables precise evaluation of macrophage-reprogramming immunotherapy. Overall, this work establishes DNA nanodevice-programmed macrophages as a novel class of synthetic-living hybrid systems, paving the way for programmable and precise immune-state diagnostics and therapy.

title: SMCHD1 is a target for gene activation therapy to treat Prader-Willi syndrome
abstract:
Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS) is a neurodevelopmental disorder caused by loss of expression from the active paternal allele at an imprinted cluster on chromosome 15. Current treatments address individual symptoms rather than the underlying cause of disease. Because all patients preserve a normal but epigenetically silenced maternal copy of these genes, activation of this copy offers a potential disease-modifying therapy. Here, we investigated the epigenetic regulator SMCHD1. First, we demonstrated that SMCHD1 represses the PWS locus in both mice and humans, supporting its relevance as a therapeutic target. Second, we found that SMCHD1 represses the entire PWS locus in neural lineages, extending its previously known role beyond only part of the cluster. Deleting
                     Smchd1 
                    after early development in vivo activated PWS genes in disease-relevant mouse tissues including hypothalamus and improved phenotypes in a PWS mouse model. Despite broader genome-wide binding, postearly development targeting of SMCHD1 appeared remarkably safe, supporting its potential for gene activation therapy for PWS.

title: A solid magnesium zincate for hydrogen-methane evolution
MIMAS: An open-source microlens-array miniature microscope for accessible large-field cortical imaging in freely behaving mice
abstract:
Large-scale cortical dynamics during natural behavior are difficult to measure because head-mounted imaging systems must balance field of view, spatial resolution, weight, and optical complexity. Existing wide-field miniature microscopes often rely on compound or custom-corrected optical assemblies, which increase device complexity and limit accessibility for laboratories without specialized optics expertise. Here, we present the Miniature Integrated Microlens Array System (MIMAS), an open-source head-mounted fluorescence microscope that replaces conventional multi-element optics with a 4 × 5 microlens array as its sole imaging element. By combining modular subfield acquisition with computational registration and stitching, MIMAS achieves cellular-resolution imaging across an approximately 4 × 4.5 mm
                     2 
                    field of view while weighing only 2.31 g. In freely behaving mice with sparse labeling of layer 2/3 cortical neurons, MIMAS enabled simultaneous calcium imaging across multiple dorsal cortical regions, with signals extracted from thousands of neurons. This broad sampling captured distributed cortical activity related to locomotor state and sparse position-modulated responses during open-field exploration without detectable disruption of locomotion or loss of signal quality over 30 min of recording. Beyond neuronal imaging, MIMAS also supported wide-field vascular imaging and resolved vessel caliber-dependent hemodynamic responses to isoflurane. These results establish MIMAS as a lightweight, accessible, and versatile platform for large-scale fluorescence imaging in freely behaving mice and demonstrate an alternative strategy for wide-field cortical imaging that lowers the optical complexity barrier for individual laboratories.

title:
Escalating soil CO
                     2 
                    degassing correlates with ground uplift and seismicity during the ongoing unrest of Campi Flegrei (2005–2025)
abstract:
The mechanism driving accelerating unrest at the densely populated Campi Flegrei caldera since 2005 remains debated. Analyzing an unprecedented two-decade geochemical dataset, we show that escalating soil CO
                     2 
                    fluxes closely tracks caldera uplift, revealing magmatic fluid pressurization at 3- to 4-kilometer depth and heating as the fundamental driver of the unrest. A critical magmatic gas pulse occurred between 2018 and 2022 specifically focused this outgassing beneath the Solfatara crater. Thermodynamic modeling demonstrates that an increasing mass of ascending fluid pressurizes the hydrothermal system, forcing vapor condensation within the upper kilometer. This condensation transfers latent heat to the crust. We calculate that this released thermal energy is an order of magnitude greater than that required for the 1.6-meter uplift since 2005. Ultimately, this fluid pressurization and heating drive accelerating deformation and seismicity; alongside the 2021 emergence of seismic sequences with short inter-event times, it directly signals an escalating phreatic or magmatic eruption risk.

title: Multiscale insights into screw dislocation-driven growth mechanisms
abstract:
Spiral growth in two-dimensional (2D) materials has conventionally been explained by single screw dislocation mechanisms, yet a complete multiscale understanding remains elusive due to the intricate nature of screw dislocation structures. Here, we present a stabilization approach through metallic transition metal dichalcogenides (m-TMDs) overlayers on spiral semiconducting TMDs (s-TMDs), which enables unprecedentedly robust atomic-resolution imaging of screw dislocations in cross-sectional van der Waals heterostructures. Our multiscale investigations identify nanoscale substrate undulations as critical nucleation sites for screw dislocations and uncover a multi-screw dislocation-driven (MSDD) growth paradigm, characterized by periodic stress stripes with linear densities approaching ∼10
                     6 
                    cm
                     −1 
                    . Furthermore, we establish that dislocation interactions govern stacking sequence reconstruction, while the kinetic competition among multiple screw dislocations determines the ultimate spiral architectures. These insights fundamentally transform our understanding of defect-mediated growth in 2D materials.

title: Sensory receptor expansion and neural accommodation in butterfly color vision
abstract:
The evolution of complex brains required the incorporation of newly evolved neurons into existing circuits, yet the genetic and developmental mechanisms enabling their integration remain poorly understood. Butterflies expanded their color vision by adding a second R7 photoreceptor per ommatidium, a rare departure from the conserved insect eye ground plan. Because each R7 makes an independent stochastic fate choice, this duplication increased the number of ommatidial types from two to three. We identified the genetic basis of this expansion and demonstrated how the brain accommodates the new input. R7 duplication was achieved by converting R3/4 cells to an R1/6 fate, triggering the R7 recruitment program on both sides of the ommatidium. By manipulating transcription factor expression in
                     Drosophila 
                    , we engineered a “butterfly-fly” that recapitulates this ancient R7 duplication and three-type stochastic mosaic. In the fly brain, two R7 subtypes connect to specific types of Dm8 neurons, which are born in excess and undergo apoptosis if they fail to find synaptic partners. In our butterfly-fly model, these surplus Dm8s are immediately rescued and form subtype-appropriate connections. These findings suggest that population-level variation maintains a reservoir of potentially interacting neurons, providing a developmental substrate that allows the brain to immediately accommodate newly evolved neurons.

title: A biohybrid mesh harvester for distributed energy harvesting in living tissues
abstract: Harnessing bio-origin resources for energy conversion offers a promising pathway toward energy sustainability matched to biosystems, addressing a fundamental limitation in powering bio-integrated electronics. However, existing approaches by integrating harvesters onto continuous substrates follow a “centralized” paradigm that differs markedly from the inherently distributed energy conversion found in living tissues, limiting both biocompatibility and scalability. We demonstrate a distributed harvesting strategy by integrating individual harvesting units within a mesh network that closely mimics the structural and mechanical properties of biological tissues. This architecture enables seamless embedding within in vitro cardiac tissue to form a bio-hybridization with cellular-scale intimacy across both device and substrate, transcending conventional approaches limited to a surface contact. This strategy achieves effective energy density more than an order of magnitude higher than that of existing approaches based on the centralized paradigm. While the concept is currently demonstrated in an in vitro cardiac system for converting biomechanical energy, the approach can provide a generalizable framework for integrating diverse energy-harvesting modalities and offers a pathway toward in vivo biohybrid systems.

title: Exposure route, not dose, is the primary driver of infection patterns for a respiratory virus
abstract: Infectious disease severity, shedding, and within-host kinetics can vary substantially with exposure dose, inoculation route, and host factors. However, the relative contributions of these variables to infection heterogeneity remain poorly quantified because small sample sizes in controlled in vivo experiments limit their statistical power and scientific scope. Here, by compiling and jointly analyzing the largest published database of nonhuman primate challenge experiments (107 studies; 721 animals), we show that exposure route drives SARS-CoV-2 infection kinetics more strongly than dose, age, sex, or species. Aerosol inoculation yields kinetics distinct from all other respiratory exposure routes.
